title: Correct the failed-run message in run-migrations.sh (:187-188): it still names the applied-counts-skips defect that PR #1436 fixed
description:
**ACTION (owner): change the failure message at** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh:187-188` **so it stops naming a defect the runner no longer has.**

**What the code says.** Read at develop `4aa5cb38bd52449b08e08a77bc6bebca04751c2b`, which contains PR #1436 (the KS-808 fix, squash `ae9bf6828f88`):

* Line 188 is printed on **every** failed-migration run. It sits inside the `failed_count > 0` branch that opens at `:180`, and reads: `applied=N-counts-skips defect is KS-808. Exit 3 - the code this`. With `:187`, the sentence says the applied=N-counts-skips defect is still open.
* That counting was changed by PR #1436. `:121`, `:147` and `:173-174` now count a skip on its own (comments marked `KS-808 (2)`), and `:176` prints `Summary: applied=$applied_count failed=$failed_count skipped=$skipped_count`.
* So at runtime the script tells an operator about an open defect that the code no longer has.

**Scope.** Text only: the two `echo` lines at `:187-188`. No behaviour change; the exit code (3) and the counting stay as they are.

**How it was found.** gate77 finding N-1436-1, graded Minor by the gate, recorded during the merge of PR #1436. Board search by symbol before filing, team-scoped, title or description: the filename returns 8 tickets (KS 808, KS 1296, KS 1443, KS 1305, KS 1401, KS 1376, KS 1054, KS 1031), none of which owns these two lines; the exact phrase `applied=N-counts-skips` returns 0; `:187-188` returns 0; a fabricated control term returns 0.

**Related:** KS-808. It stays In Progress for its live sweep; this ticket does not move it.

title: Anchor schema: accept and anchor platform-s's signatureHash (the plain SHA-256 of a detached .p7s) on the sign verb
description:
## What platform-s needs

Platform-S can now sign any file type **detached** ([PS-1043](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1043/signing-formats-p1-detached-signing-baseline-signformatpolicy)): a CAdES `.p7s` is stored beside the **unchanged** document. The signing anchors through the flat `/api/anchors` path, with `metadata.documentType = sign` and `contentHash` = the document's own hash. That hash is the same as the upload's, because the bytes did not change.

So the chain proves *a signing happened on this document at this time*, but **not which signature**. The `.p7s` hash never leaves S. A `.p7s` deleted or swapped on S's side (a substitute needs a signing key, and S holds uploaded keys) cannot be caught from outside S.

**Stuart's ruling (2026-10-09):** put the signature's hash *"in the chain with the document information as part of the signing verb"*, as a **plain SHA-256**, not a keyed commitment. Anyone holding the `.p7s` should be able to check it against the chain on their own.

## Suggested work

1. Accept `metadata.signatureHash` in the anchor request schema: optional, `^[a-f0-9]{64}$` (lowercase hex SHA-256). Today `anchorSchema.ts` strips unknown metadata keys, so S will not send it until this ships. A silently dropped field would make detached signatures look anchored when they are not.
2. Carry it into the on-chain CIP-674 metadata beside `documentType` / `occurredAt` (a 64-character string is within the 64-byte metadatum limit, [KS-1284](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1284/cardanotransactionts-add-json-metadatum-with-schema-throws-on-any)).
3. Return it on **both** reads S and a verifier use — see *Clarified 10 Oct* below (the [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) read-back pattern), so S can show "signature anchored" and a verifier can compare.
4. **Restrict it to** `documentType = sign` and answer 400 to it on any other verb (a requirement, not an option — a stray hash on another verb must not be anchored as if it named a signature).

## Clarified 10 Oct 2026 (from the S-side review of the signing-formats branch)

**How S sends it.** A detached `sign` is anchored as a **standalone flat anchor**: `POST /api/anchors` with `documentId` = S's transaction id (a fresh GUID per event), `contentHash` = the document's own hash (unchanged by a detached signature), `metadata.documentType = sign`, the identity block when enabled, and — once this ticket is live — `metadata.signatureHash`. It is deliberately **not** sent through `/lifecycle-events` (`sign` is not in that enum, and K's lifecycle anchors drop S's metadata and identity today — [KS-1385](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1385/ks-1175-follow-on-the-anchors-k-emits-for-share-transfer-custody)). So on K it is a **second anchor over the same content hash** as the originate / upload anchor, linked to the K document by that hash only.

**Read-back, precisely (item 3):**

* **By id** — `GET /api/anchors/{id}`: S stores and polls this anchor's id, so "signature anchored" on S's Verify comes from here. This is the read [KS-723](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-723/declare-the-remaining-157-routed-but-undocumented-api-operations-in) still leaves undeclared; declare it and carry `signatureHash` on it together.
* **By hash, with multiplicity** — `GET /api/anchors/verify/{contentHash}` (and the provenance surface): the public check is someone holding the `.asics` (document + `.p7s`) hashing the document and asking K by that hash. If that answer collapses to one anchor (the [KS-596](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-596/architecture-p1-registration-accepts-optional-s-supplied) shape [PS-611](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-611/s-verifies-through-v1-which-collapses-the-multiplicity-ks-596-ruling-b) records), they may be shown the upload anchor and no signature hash. Either list **every** anchor for the hash, each with its `documentType` and `signatureHash`, or state on this ticket that the public path is the by-id read only.

**Size:** a lowercase-hex SHA-256 is exactly 64 bytes — at, not over, the metadatum limit [KS-1284](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1284/cardanotransactionts-add-json-metadatum-with-schema-throws-on-any) chunks beyond. Worth one cell that it is anchored as a single string, not a two-element array.

**One value, never an array:** S allows one detached signature per document iteration, so there is one `.p7s` and one hash per `sign` anchor. Several signers would be parallel SignerInfos inside that one `.p7s`, still one hash.

**Linkage to the K document — a question for** [KS-1384](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1384/one-anchor-row-per-document-id-network-a-repeat-post-apianchors-resets)**'s ruling, not this ticket.** Today the sign anchor is outside K's document record (standalone, hash-linked). When [KS-1384](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1384/one-anchor-row-per-document-id-network-a-repeat-post-apianchors-resets) rules on one anchor per document versus per event, it should also say how a flat anchor relates to a K document: either K accepts an optional K-document reference on `FlatAnchorRequest` and records it on the anchor row, or (once per-event rows exist) S sends K's document id as `documentId`. This ticket can land on today's shape as written; nothing here waits on that ruling.

**What S checks after this lands:** `AnchorSignatureHash` is switched on per environment only after the paired K serves a spec declaring `FlatAnchorRequest.metadata.signatureHash` (the [PS-981](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-981/do-not-deploy-develop-to-uat-ps-until-demo-pk-carries-ks-117211731175) served-spec gate reads it), and S's k-live cell asserts the by-id read-back carries the hash and that it equals the downloaded `.p7s`'s SHA-256.

## [KS-240](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-240/strict-by-default-on-chain-minimisation-strip-issuername-any-human) (on-chain minimisation)

The value is the hash of a `.p7s`. A `.p7s` contains the signer's X.509 certificate (name, possibly email), but **the hash is not reversible and identifies nothing by itself**. It is also the integrity value of a public signature object. The signer's identity already rides separately as the **keyed** `identityCommitment` ([KS-721](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-721/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-opaque-identitycommitment)), which S crypto-shreds on erasure. Stuart ruled the plain hash acceptable on these grounds. If K's minimisation review disagrees, please say so on this ticket before building, and do not narrow it silently.

## Ordering

**K deploys first** (the [KS-721](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-721/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-opaque-identitycommitment) / [PS-612](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-612/rename-the-certify-verb-to-declare-across-s) lesson). The S side is tracked on the linked PS ticket: S records the hash in its own ledger now, and starts sending `metadata.signatureHash` only after this is live on the K it pairs with. Acceptance is observable from S (sign detached → anchor read-back carries the hash), so it tests in the [KS-772](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-772/review-stream-s-k-integration-contract) review stream like [KS-721](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-721/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-opaque-identitycommitment).

title: originate declares handlebars as a direct prod dependency that no source file imports
description:
## Finding

`services/originate/package.json` declares `handlebars` `^4.7.9` under `dependencies` (prod), and 0 files in the repo import or require it. Measured 2026-10-08T23:4xZ at develop `1e7f90e26137` with `git grep` for `require('handlebars` and `from 'handlebars`; positive controls on the same instrument: express 339 files, ts-jest 14.

## Why it matters

originate is the only service image that carries handlebars at runtime. Its runner stage re-installs from originate's own lock with `npm ci --ignore-scripts --omit=dev` (`services/originate/Dockerfile:79`), and handlebars is prod there. governance and referral prune dev deps before the runtime copy (`:54`, `:61`); vc-issuer installs `--omit=dev` (`:86`), where handlebars is dev; the Dev root lock reaches no image.

So the three handlebars advisories have image reach only because of this declaration, and no code path goes into it. Removing the declaration removes the reach; the lock refresh only patches it.

## Not done

NOT done in the lock-refresh PR, and the removal is not built. Unmeasured: whether anything loads handlebars dynamically (a string-built require, a templating config read at runtime). That check comes first.

Duplicate search, shared with the lock-refresh ticket: `handlebars` 0 hits in Linear including archived (control `pbkdf2` 3).

## Cross-reference

The lock refresh that clears the three advisories without removing this declaration: KS-1452.

title: Three new advisories freeze every push: in-range lock refresh for handlebars 4.7.9 -> 4.7.10
description:
## What is broken

Three `handlebars` advisories, published 2026-10-08T17:52Z, make the pre-push preflight refuse EVERY Secuura push on develop `1e7f90e26137`: leg 6 (npm-audit, KS-470) and leg 7 (standalone-lock advisories, KS-531). Trigger: Seat F 6th's KS-808 push was refused at 2026-10-08T23:26Z with `PREFLIGHT FAILED on leg(s) 6 7 - fix the above before pushing. (12/15 legs ran)`. Seat R 21st's #1427 merge-in push was refused the same way.

## Base control (Seat V 1st, 2026-10-08T23:45Z, clean scratch clone at develop 1e7f90e26137, 0 dirty locks asserted first)

* leg 6, `node scripts/audit/audit-gate.mjs`, rc 1: "FAIL — 3 NEW advisories not in the baseline": GHSA-xw65-4hp5-5hc7 \[moderate\], GHSA-8r5x-fm3f-whwj \[critical\], GHSA-p8wg-vrv2-v86f \[critical\].
* leg 7, `node scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs`, rc 1: "FAIL — 3 advisories in standalone locks and NOT in the baseline", each `pinned: 4.7.9`, each `in 4 lock(s): services/governance, services/originate, services/referral, services/vc-issuer`.

## Census: 45 tracked locks, 5 handlebars entries in 5 locks

| Lock | Pinned | Flag | resolved / integrity | Parents (declared range) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Blockchain/Dev (workspace root, leg 6) | 4.7.9 | prod | no / no | ts-jest `^4.7.9`; member services/originate `^4.7.9` |
| services/governance | 4.7.9 | dev | yes / yes | ts-jest `^4.7.9` |
| services/originate | 4.7.9 | prod | yes / yes | root DIRECT `dependencies` `^4.7.9`; ts-jest `^4.7.9` |
| services/referral | 4.7.9 | dev | yes / yes | ts-jest `^4.7.9` |
| services/vc-issuer | 4.7.9 | dev | yes / yes | ts-jest `^4.7.9` |

## The fix: in-range, lock-only refresh 4.7.9 -> 4.7.10

* 4.7.10 clears all three. Leg 7's own instrument (the npm bulk advisory endpoint): 4.7.9 returns the three, each `>=4.0.0 <=4.7.9`; 4.7.10 returns `{}`. 4.7.10 is `latest` and the only release above 4.7.9.
* 0 of the 7 declaring parents refuse 4.7.10 (semver, with must-fail controls 5.0.0 and 4.7.8). So: no manifest edit, no `overrides`, no baseline row.
* The change is not version-only. 4.7.10 moves its own `dependencies.minimist` from `^1.2.5` to `^1.2.8`; every other lock-relevant field is equal. All five locks already resolve minimist at 1.2.8, so no other entry moves.
* Planned change set: 5 locks, 5 entries, 18 field writes, 0 manifests, 0 baseline, 0 source. Root entry: `version` + `dependencies.minimist` (it carries no resolved/integrity). Each standalone: `version`, `resolved`, `integrity`, `dependencies.minimist`.
* Integrity is taken from the downloaded 4.7.10 tarball (712,317 B); its sha512 equals the registry's `dist.integrity`. The same pipeline reproduces the 4.7.9 value the four locks carry today.

## Runtime reach

* services/originate: handlebars 4.7.9 IS in the runtime image. The runner re-installs from originate's own lock with `npm ci --ignore-scripts --omit=dev` (`services/originate/Dockerfile:79`), and handlebars is prod there.
* governance, referral: not at runtime. Both prune dev deps before the runtime copy (`npm prune --omit=dev`, `governance/Dockerfile:54`, `referral/Dockerfile:61`).
* vc-issuer: not at runtime. The runner installs `--omit=dev` from its own lock (`vc-issuer/Dockerfile:86`), where handlebars is dev.
* The Dev root workspace lock reaches no image (0 Dockerfile references; control: `package-lock.json` 8).
* 0 files in the repo import or require handlebars (controls on the same instrument: express 339, ts-jest 14). Present in one image; no code path found into it.

## Authority

Standing direction to BUMP rather than accept: Kam's cards `secuura-four-advisories-ruled-after-measurement` = bump (2026-09-09T10:30), `secuura-five-new-advisories-freeze-every-push-1006` = a, and `secuura-advisory-freeze-3-ghsa-1007` = a (G 3rd's round). No card exists for THIS freeze: 0 hits for `handlebars` in the decision store. This round rests on the standing direction plus Wednesday's ANSWER to F 6th. Ticket creation, one ticket per TEST PASS (Kam 2026-09-07 13:23): this is one pass, one ticket.

## Not done here

* No baseline row. Leg 6's 15-entry CLEANUP advisory block stays out (disposition KS-767).
* No platform-doc change. The test-discipline skill's §4 binds a test change (backend unit, integration or systemTest); a lock-only dependency refresh changes no test, so neither platform doc moves.
* The PR ends at READY FOR QA, tier 1 (security). The merge is a later seat's, on a gate.

## Precedent

KS-1437 (#1406) and KS-1425 (#1397): the same in-range lock-refresh shape for earlier advisory freezes.

## Cross-reference

The vestigial direct declaration in services/originate that gives handlebars its only image reach is filed separately as KS-1453 (not built here).

title: A bare `slot-literal-ok:` marker DOES exempt a quoted value in all five slot guards — the closing quote satisfies the "has a reason" test, contradicting systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1169
description:
**BLUF:** the platform rule says a bare `slot-literal-ok:` marker exempts nothing, but on a **quoted value** (JSON, or any line where the marker is not last) the value's own closing quote satisfies the "has a reason" test, so **a bare marker DOES exempt**. Measured in all five harness guards' shared regex shape. Found while fixing KS-1450; not introduced by it.

## The rule it contradicts

`systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1169`, verbatim:

> A deliberate exception carries `slot-literal-ok: <reason>` on the same line; a bare marker exempts nothing.

## The defect

Every implementation tests for "marker, optional whitespace, then one non-whitespace character":

```
no_hardcoded_slot_literals.test.sh   grep -vE 'slot-literal-ok:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]'
playwright/.../no-hardcoded-slot-literals.test.ts:79    const MARKER = /slot-literal-ok:\s*\S/
performance/.../noHardcodedSlotLiterals.test.ts:49      const MARKER = 'slot-literal-ok:'
schemathesis/.../test_no_hardcoded_slot_numbers.py:50   _OPT_OUT = "slot-literal-ok:"
akto/tests/unit/config/noTypedSlotValues.test.ts        (same shape)
```

`[^[:space:]]` / `\S` is satisfied by **any** non-space character, including `"`. So:

```
  "reason": "x 6982 slot-literal-ok:",      -> EXEMPTED   (wrong: the reason is empty)
const p = 6982; // slot-literal-ok:          -> reported   (right)
```

Driven both ways in one call against the same regex. The only reason this has never shown up is that every existing marker sits in a `#` or `//` comment at true end-of-line, where nothing follows the colon — which is also why the suites' own controls pass: each plants its bare-marker fixture into a comment, never into a quoted value. `test_no_hardcoded_slot_numbers.py:263` asserts "the bare marker does not \[exempt\]" and passes for exactly that reason.

## Why it matters now

KS-1450 is the first change to put `slot-literal-ok` markers inside JSON string values (the six `accepted.*.reason` entries of `systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis-baseline.json`). Before it, that file carried **zero** markers, so the gap was latent. It is recorded as a named limitation in KS-1450's PR Test Evidence rather than fixed there, because a one-guard fix would make the five guards disagree about what a bare marker means.

## Suggested fix

Require a reason character that is not structural, e.g. tighten the class to `[^[:space:]",]` (and the JS/Python equivalents) in **all five** implementations in one change, so they stay in agreement.

**Blast radius, measured before proposing it:** exactly **2** existing marker lines repo-wide would lose exemption, and **neither needs it** — `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/unit/test_no_hardcoded_slot_numbers.py:50` (`_OPT_OUT = "slot-literal-ok:"`, a constant; the line holds no slot literal) and the shell guard's own bare-marker control line (its port is computed, not typed). So nothing that passes today would go red.

Each implementation should also gain a control that plants the bare marker into a **quoted value**, not only into a comment — the absence of that control is what hid this.

## Provenance

* Both-way measurement and the blast-radius count: Seat R 16th, 2026-10-08, during KS-1450.
* The rule: `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1169`.
* The guard: KS-1386 (Done, Peter).

title: develop fails pre-push preflight leg 14 since 89dff83aa: 8 unmarked slot-2 literals in schemathesis-baseline.json block every push carrying a Blockchain/Dev path
description:
**BLUF:** `develop` **fails its own pre-push preflight on leg 14, and has done since** `89dff83aa` **merged. Every push carrying a** `Blockchain/Dev/` **path is blocked.** The failing cell is `systemTest/__tests__/no_hardcoded_slot_literals.test.sh` (the KS 1386 guard). It reports 8 unmarked slot-2 literals, all in `systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis-baseline.json`. Peter — two of the eight cannot take the guard's exemption marker, so this needs a design call from you, not a mechanical edit. Nothing has been changed: no edit to the guard, the baseline, or anything else.

## Measured, both ways, on the same suite

Run in a worktree, restoring the file byte-identically afterwards:

| baseline file taken from | leg 14 suite | lines matching `slot2` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `ed346e6d9ff8` (develop before #1424) | rc 0, **9 passed, 0 failed** | 0 |
| `eae08a3f441c` (develop now) | rc 1, **8 passed, 1 failed** | 8 |

The suite's own positive control fires in both runs (`CONTROL: all 54 planted literals are reported`), and a fabricated token (`slot9`) reads 0 in both, so the instrument discriminates and the difference is the file, not the harness. The file is byte-identical at both ends of the PR that hit this, so the failure is `develop`'s, not the PR's.

## What the guard reports, verbatim

```
FAIL unmarked slot 2..4 values (8 lines) — derive them from support/slot-expect.sh, or mark 'slot-literal-ok: <reason>'
PREFLIGHT FAILED on leg(s) 14 - fix the above before pushing. (12/15 legs ran)
```

The 8 lines in `systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis-baseline.json`: **10, 11, 854, 859, 864, 869, 874, 879**. There are **0** `slot-literal-ok` markers anywhere in the file.

## The two that cannot carry a marker

Six of the eight are prose inside `"reason"` strings, which can take an inline marker. Lines 10 and 11 are **run-id strings inside a JSON array**:

```
"pre-merge-ks-1445-2026-10-07T14-01-26Z-slot2",
"pre-merge-ks-1445-2026-10-07T14-30-16Z-slot2"
```

A marker cannot be added to those without changing the id itself. All eight values are descriptive provenance — which sweep produced the row — not hardcoded targets.

## Why it reached develop

The pre-push hook selects the full preflight only when the push changes a `^Blockchain/Dev/` path. #1424 was systemTest-only, so leg 14 — which scans systemTest — never ran on the change that broke it. A systemTest-only merge can therefore land a leg-14 regression that only a later `Blockchain/Dev/` push discovers.

## What it blocks

Any push whose changed set includes a `Blockchain/Dev/` path. Confirmed on one: the full preflight ran 7.5 minutes, reported `shell suites: 70 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped (of 71)`, and refused. `--no-verify` was advertised by the hook and not taken.

## Question for Peter

Which remedy do you want for lines 10 and 11 — exempt recorded provenance inside the guard (a run id that ends `-slotN` is a record of where a row came from, not a target), or rename the ids so they carry no slot token? The six `"reason"` lines can take `slot-literal-ok` either way. **We will not touch your guard or the baseline file without your word.** Related, for context only: KS 1386 is the guard, KS 1445 the sweep whose triage added the rows, KS 1361 the earlier baseline reconciliation.

title: POST /api/nft/ipfs/upload: the spec doesn't mark the request body required, so a bodyless POST is "valid" and its 400 fails positive_data_acceptance
description:
## BLUF

`positive_data_acceptance` fails on `POST /api/nft/ipfs/upload`. The pair is **not** in `schemathesis-baseline.json` at `develop` b280b74ff, so it is untriaged. It is [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks)**'s class** (positive_data_acceptance at scale), on an operation [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks) doesn't name. It was raised separately, not appended, because Peter's rule is that only Backlog/Todo tickets are updated, and [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks) is In Progress.

## Evidence (re-verified from source at `develop` b280b74ff, 2026-10-07)

* **Spec** (`Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`): `POST /api/nft/ipfs/upload` has a `requestBody`, but `requestBody.required` is **unset**. Under OpenAPI an empty body is therefore spec-valid. Compare `POST /api/auth/wallet/authenticate`, where `required: true`.
* **Runtime:** a request with **no body** is answered `400 {"code":"BAD_REQUEST","message":"Validation error","details":[{"path":["data"],"message":"Required"} …]}`.
* **Live result:** Schemathesis 4.29.4, `pre-merge`, slot 2 on Peter's Mac, stack built from the [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is) branch (no service changes), run `pre-merge-ks-1445-2026-10-07T14-30-16Z-slot2`, test case `P8GPsj`. Reproduce with `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer …' http://localhost:6982/api/nft/ipfs/upload`.
* **Counts are a floor:** it fired in that run and not in the run before it on the same commit.

## Fix direction

The runtime clearly requires a body (`data` is required), so declare `requestBody.required: true` in the route's OpenAPI source. Then run `npm run generate-openapi`, restart or recreate api-gateway (it serves the spec), and check whether sibling `nft` operations have the same omission.

## Done when

- [ ] The spec marks the body required, and a bodyless POST is no longer generated as a positive case.
- [ ] The pair stops firing, or is baselined against this ticket.

Found while running [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is)'s pre-merge gate.

title: Security: POST /api/notifications still creates a notification for ANY userId (BOLA) — its owning ticket KS-486 is closed and archived
description:
## BLUF

The notification BOLA recorded in Review A ([KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor), row 1: "`POST /api/notifications` takes `userId` from body … any authenticated user pushes spoofed `security`/`system` notifications with an `actionUrl` to any user") is **still live on** `develop`. [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor) is **Deployed to UAT and archived**, so the defect has **no open owner**. This ticket is that owner. It was raised separately, not appended to [KS-1015](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1015/sweeps-2026-09-08-28-checkoperation-pairs-have-no-live-owner-18), because Peter's rule is that only Backlog/Todo tickets are updated, and [KS-1015](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1015/sweeps-2026-09-08-28-checkoperation-pairs-have-no-live-owner-18) is In Progress.

## Evidence (re-verified from source at `develop` b280b74ff, 2026-10-07)

* **Create:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/notifications.ts:242`. `POST /` reads `userId` from `req.body` (`:244`) and stores the row under that user. There is no self-or-admin check against the caller's token.
* **Read:** `PATCH /:id/read` (`:155`) looks only in the **caller's** rows (`getUserId(req)` → `notifications.get(userId)`).
* **Live result.** Schemathesis 4.29.4, `pre-merge`, slot 2 on Peter's Mac, stack built from the [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is) branch (no service changes), run `pre-merge-ks-1445-2026-10-07T14-01-26Z-slot2`:
  * The systemTest xfail `test_notification_bola.py::TestNotificationBola::test_cannot_create_notification_for_another_user` still gets **201**. It is marked xfail citing "[KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor)-A", a closed ticket.
  * The stateful sweep's `ensure_resource_availability` pair failed. `POST /api/notifications` created a row for a generated `userId`, then `PATCH /api/notifications/{id}/read` as the caller answered `404 Notification not found`, test case `X8K02g`. That 404 is a symptom of the BOLA: the row went to someone else.
* That stateful pair is **not** in `schemathesis-baseline.json` at b280b74ff, so it is untriaged.

## Why it matters

Any authenticated user can place a `security` or `system` notification with an arbitrary `actionUrl` in **any** user's inbox: in-app phishing.

## Done when

- [ ] `POST /api/notifications` refuses a `userId` other than the caller's, unless the caller is an admin or internal service (decide which; the route comment calls it "internal").
- [ ] The xfail in `test_notification_bola.py` flips to a pass, and its marker and the systemTest reason text stop citing closed [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor). Peter owns that change ([KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-all-tools-security-regression-coverage)).
- [ ] The stateful `ensure_resource_availability` pair stops firing, or is baselined against this ticket.

Found while running [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is)'s pre-merge gate.

title: systemTest (Schemathesis): implement Kam's 2026-08-26 ruling on GET /api/users/admin/list as a check-scoped guard, so its baseline entry can retire
description:
## Summary

**BLUF.** Kam ruled on 2026-08-26 that the `negative_data_rejection` **check** on `GET /api/users/admin/list` is tolerated. The Schemathesis harness has never implemented that ruling. The pair is kept quiet only by a baseline entry (re-pointed to [KS-1015](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1015/sweeps-2026-09-08-28-checkoperation-pairs-have-no-live-owner-18) by [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing) on 2026-10-07), and `tests/test_by_design_permissive.py` still describes the operation as having "no stated ruling". This ticket builds the check-scoped guard, so the ruling lives in code and the baseline entry can retire. systemTest only; no platform change.

+++ Evidence and what the guard must and must not do

### The ruling, verbatim

KAMIL, VERBATIM, [KS-592](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-592/negative-data-rejection-recurs-176-failures-across-10-ops-ks-266-ks) (2026-08-26), Linear comment `11ea84ac-7623-4b91-943c-f0aeb72c726d`:

> **The second is operative.** The tolerated thing is the `negative_data_rejection` **check** on `GET /api/users/admin/list` — **not the operation**.

The same comment, on what must stay live:

> 🔴 **The two** `offset=-1` **HTTP 500s on this operation stay LIVE.** A whole-operation exclusion would have swallowed them, and a ruling can settle a 200-where-a-400-was-wanted but cannot make an unhandled 500 correct.

Both quotes are already in `systemTest/schemathesis/config/baseline_kamil_verbatim.py` (`KAMIL_VERBATIM["KS-592"]`), added by [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing).

### Where things stand (re-read on `develop` `b280b74ff`, 2026-10-07)

* `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_by_design_permissive.py` (module docstring, scope note) lists `GET /api/users/admin/list` among the operations "deliberately absent — no stated ruling covers them, so they stay armed under `negative_data_rejection` ([KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the))". That was true before 2026-08-26; it isn't now.
* `config/check_predicates.py`, `config/checks.py` and `schemathesis.toml` carry no tolerance for this operation.
* `config/schemathesis-baseline.json` entry `negative_data_rejection::GET /api/users/admin/list` (ticket [KS-1015](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1015/sweeps-2026-09-08-28-checkoperation-pairs-have-no-live-owner-18)) is the only thing keeping the pair from failing the gate. Measured in [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing)'s three slot-1 sweeps (Schemathesis 4.29.4): **10 / 10 / 11** failing cases.

### Done looks like

1. A guard scoped to **this check on this operation only**, following the existing by-design guard shape ([KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the) / `by_design_input_tolerance_guard`). Kam's quote goes verbatim in the source and test docblocks, labelled `KAMIL, VERBATIM, KS-592 (2026-08-26)`.
2. **Red → green**, proven by a test that fails on today's code and passes after.
3. A test proving the `offset=-1` **500s still fail** `not_a_server_error` (owned by [KS-593](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-593/not-a-server-error-recurs-17-raw-5xx-across-8-ops-ks-431-ks-449-ks-497) / [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) §2). A whole-operation exclusion would fail this test.
4. `test_by_design_permissive.py`'s scope note updated to say the ruling exists and where it is implemented.
5. The baseline entry retired once a live sweep shows the pair no longer fails, with before/after counts.

+++

Raised from [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing)'s close-out (PR 1419 notes). Refs as KS-NNN text. Filed by agent on Peter's behalf; left unassigned as asked.

title: Renovate cannot bump base-image-watch.sh EXCLUDED_BASES — Blockchain/Dev/** is in ignorePaths (split from KS-1367; needs Kamil's agreement)
description:
## BLUF

Split from [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not) at Peter's request (2026-10-07). [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not)'s branch (`feature/ks-1445-…`, shared with [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is)) makes Renovate see `systemTest/performance/config/observability.yml` `k6Image`. The remaining part needs a change to the repo's `ignorePaths`, which sits in Kamil's work-stream E ([KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490/review-e-deployment-containers-and-cicd-supply-chain)). **This ticket waits on Kamil's agreement.** He has not commented on [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not), so there is nothing of his to quote yet.

## Re-verified from source (2026-10-07, worktree at `origin/develop` 652cf5f6e)

* `renovate.json:4` has `"ignorePaths": ["Blockchain/Dev/**"]`. Renovate skips every manager, including a `customManagers` regex, under that path.
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/base-image-watch.sh` `EXCLUDED_BASES` names `grafana/k6:2.3.0` and every `observability/docker-compose.yml` image tag.
* Two tests fail when that list disagrees with the files Renovate does bump:
  * `systemTest/performance/tests/unit/config/k6ImagePinParity.test.ts` (k6)
  * `observability/test/compose-image-pins.test.mjs` (observability, added in [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is))
* So a Renovate PR is red until a person edits the list by hand. That is safe, because nothing slips through, but it is noise.
* Renovate app: `gh pr list --state all --author app/renovate` returns no PR ever. That is consistent with the app not being installed. The installation itself could not be read with the available token.

## Options for Kamil

1. Narrow `ignorePaths` so `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/base-image-watch.sh` is visible, and add a regex `customManagers` entry for its quoted `"image:tag"` lines, grouped with `k6 runtime` and `observability stack images`.
2. Leave it as a hand edit. The red parity tests are the prompt, and that is documented in `systemTest/performance/docs/quick-start.md`.

## Done when

- [ ] Kamil has chosen 1 or 2. Quote his reply verbatim here.
- [ ] If 1: the config passes `renovate-config-validator --strict`, and a dry run shows one grouped update covering all three k6 sites.

title: Pin systemTest k6 to the latest release (or later) — the Mac's native k6 is 0.48.0, the suite needs ≥ 2.3.0
description:
## Problem

The only native k6 on Peter's Mac is **v0.48.0** (`k6 version`, 2026-10-07). The performance suite expects the k6 2.x `--summary-export` shape and, per `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` (\~line 88), **needs k6 ≥ 2.3.0** (`--features freeze-env`). The [KS-1439](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1439/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4293-4294-fixes-only-35-entries-incl) run used 2.3.0. A run on 0.48.0 would not be comparable and risks the parser reading missing fields as zeros — i.e. a result that cannot be trusted.

Repo state today: the pinned image is `grafana/k6:2.3.0` (`systemTest/performance/config/observability.yml`, `docker/k6/Dockerfile`, `@types/k6` 2.3.0), set by [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) (Done). [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not) (Backlog) covers Renovate not seeing the `observability.yml` pin.

## Wanted

1. **Determine the latest k6 release from the vendor's release page at bump time — not from memory** (the latest was not verified when this ticket was raised; 2.3.0 is only the newest version the repo has recorded).
2. If the latest is newer than 2.3.0: bump the image pin, Dockerfile tag, `@types/k6`, and the summary fixture (`tests/unit/fixtures/smoke-summary.k6-<ver>.json`), as [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) did. If 2.3.0 is still latest: no bump, only item 3.
3. Make the host k6 version a checked precondition: the runner fails loudly (naming the found and required versions) when the native k6 is older than the pin, instead of running and parsing a mismatched summary. Extend `k6ImagePinParity.test.ts`-style coverage; the fix needs a test red on 0.48.0 and green on the pinned version.
4. Document the Mac install (`brew install k6` / `brew upgrade k6`) in the performance docs; re-baseline timings if the version changes.

## Out of scope

Renovate coverage of `observability.yml` ([KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not)).

## Test Evidence expectations

Quote results as measured on the pinned k6 version; state it in the evidence block.

title: start-secuura.sh --rebuild leaves ~30 untagged images per slot per rebuild (and interrupted rebuilds pin them)
description:
Raised from platform-s ([PS-1012](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1012/dep-ssd-local-systemtest-make-stack-slots-safe-across-two-dropbox>)) rather than fixed from there, because `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` is platform-k's.

## What happens

`docker compose` names each built image `<compose project>-<service>`: `platform-k-*` for slot 1, `secuura_slot2-*` for slot 2, and so on. `start-secuura.sh --rebuild` builds every service again (the serial per-service `docker compose build` from [KS-345](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-345/start-secuurash-rebuild-hangs-on-the-full-33-service-compose-bake)). Each rebuild moves those tags to new images, and the previous image of each service is left untagged as `<none>`. That's about 30 images per slot per rebuild, some of them 0.6–2.2 GB. Nothing in the script prunes images or the build cache. A grep of `start-secuura.sh` for `prune`, `rmi` and `image rm` finds nothing.

**The worse case is an interrupted rebuild.** On 2026-10-02 the Pro had 29 `<none>` images, every one held by a container in K slot 1's project (`platform-k`) that was `Created` **but never started**: `secuura-auth`, `secuura-api-gateway`, `secuura-originate` and others. Docker won't prune an image a container uses, so those stayed until someone removed them by hand (Stuart did).

## Measured (MacBook Pro, Docker Desktop, 2026-10-07)

* `docker system df`: images 20.7 GB, of which 1.76 GB is reclaimable. The **build cache is 39.6 GB, of which 22.65 GB is reclaimable**, mostly entries last used in the previous two days by slot rebuilds.

## Suggested fix (for Kamil's judgement)

The platform-s side is doing this in [PS-1012](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1012/dep-ssd-local-systemtest-make-stack-slots-safe-across-two-dropbox) / [Secuura/platform-s#909](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1012-stack-slots-safe-across-two-dropbox-synced-machines-994c737d0439):

* **Label every build with its owner:** for compose, a `labels:` entry under each service's `build:` such as `com.secuura.slot-image=<project>-<service>`, or one label per project.
* **Before rebuilding,** run `docker image prune -f --filter label=…` scoped to this compose project. Without `-a`, this removes only dangling, unused images from earlier builds of this slot. It never touches another slot, platform-s, a tagged image, or an image a container still uses.
* **After an interrupted rebuild,** remove that slot's `Created`-but-never-started containers, so they stop pinning old images.
* **Don't prune the build cache automatically.** It's shared by every slot on both platforms, so pruning it makes everyone's next build cold. Documenting a manual `docker builder prune --filter until=168h -f` is enough.

title: Two shell tests assume a macOS host and fail on the Linux runner: bootstrap_login_diagnosis never finds its node stubs (lsof shows `MainThrea`), and run_migrations Cell 5 can't hide pg_isready (it sits in /usr/bin)
description:
## BLUF

Two of the six suites that fail in **Code Security Gates** (0 green in 197 runs) aren't covered by [KS-1148](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1148/ci-runner-environment-gaps-one-class-two-jobs-security-scanning-runs), [KS-1138](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1138/ci-shell-suite-step-pr-security-gatesyml-step-11-manifest-readers) or [KS-1330](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1330/run-shell-suitessh-re-land-the-round-2-signal-handling-with-a-sigint). Neither is a product bug. Each test makes an assumption that holds on macOS and fails on the Ubuntu runner. Both fixes are small and stay inside the tests.

Raised from the [KS-1440](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1440/akto-image-23610-2371-release-v2371-2026-10-06-both-local-tags) session's investigation of Code Security Gates (2026-10-07). Re-read against `origin/develop` at `eb67b9659`.

## 1. `systemTest/__tests__/bootstrap_login_diagnosis.test.sh`: the stub counter can't see Node on Linux

* `:82` `count_my_stubs()` finds the stubs with
  `lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN | awk '/node/{print $2}'` (`:84`).
* `:163` / `:166` compare that count before and after (`K1201_WITH`, `K1201_AFTER`).
* **On the Linux runner,** lsof's COMMAND column shows the thread name, not the binary. Node's main thread is named `MainThread`, which lsof truncates to `MainThrea`. So `/node/` never matches, the count is always 0, and the assertion fails. On macOS lsof prints `node`, so it passes locally.
* **Fix shape:** select by the stub's own PIDs (capture `$!` when the stub starts) or by the stub's port, rather than by the process name.

## 2. `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/run_migrations_failure_exit_code.test.sh` Cell 5 ([KS-1296](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1296/run-migrationssh-readiness-probe-discards-command-not-found-and-blames)): pg_isready can't be made absent

* `:110` `NOPG_PATH="$WORK/bin_nopg:/usr/bin:/bin"`. The intent is a PATH where `pg_isready` can't be found.
* `:111` asserts that precondition, and `:124` fails the cell when it doesn't hold. The guard is working as designed: it refuses to report a pass it can't prove.
* **On the runner,** the image installs the PostgreSQL client into `/usr/bin`, so `pg_isready` is still on the PATH. The precondition fails and the cell goes red. On macOS (Homebrew, outside `/usr/bin`) it passes.
* **Fix shape:** build `bin_nopg` from symlinks to only the tools `run-migrations.sh` needs, and drop `/usr/bin:/bin` from that PATH. Don't weaken the precondition: it's what stops this cell from passing without testing anything.
* This cell belongs to [KS-1296](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1296/run-migrationssh-readiness-probe-discards-command-not-found-and-blames) **(In Progress)**. It's linked here rather than reopened there; fold it in if that's tidier.

## Not run

No fix has been written or run. The causes above come from the runner logs and from reading the code at the lines cited. A fix should be proven red→green on Linux bash, not only on the Mac.

## Assignment

This ticket covers code both inside `systemTest/` (item 1) and outside it (item 2). It's assigned to Kamil per the team rule for fixes outside systemTest. Item 1 is systemTest code, so Peter can take it if preferred.

title: Schemathesis stateful: one generated POST /api/did case is recorded with no request and no response and a skipped scenario — identical in 4.29.3 and both 4.29.4 runs (skipped, then errored)
description:
**BLUF.** On seed 1439 every `full` sweep records one stateful case, `POST /api/did`, with **no interaction at all** (no request, no response) inside a scenario whose status is `skip`. Schemathesis 4.29.3 counted it as skipped; 4.29.4 counts it as **errored** (the one `errored` in the [KS-1439](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1439/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4293-4294-fixes-only-35-entries-incl) runs). The platform may never have been asked, so this is not yet a platform finding. It is a deterministic oddity worth one look, filed so it has a home, not a defect report.

+++ Evidence, what is established and what is not

### Seen (verified in the NDJSON of all three runs, `develop` `147ae4420`, slot 4, seed 1439)

| Run | Case | Scenario status | Interaction recorded |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `full-ks-1439-2026-10-07T07-58-16Z-slot4` (4.29.3) | `POST /api/did`, stateful | `skip` | none |
| `…T08-19-25Z-slot4` (4.29.4) | the same case | `skip` | none |
| `…T09-11-58Z-slot4` (4.29.4, repeat) | the same case | `skip` | none |

* It is the **same generated case** every time (same body prefix and keys), so it is determined by the seed, not by load or timing.
* The scenario holds exactly one case. It carries an `Authorization` header and a JSON body of 2,556 characters with many non-ASCII keys, among them one named `method`.
* Counted `skipped` at 4.29.3 and `errored` at 4.29.4. The 4.29.4 release notes say test cases that hit network errors are now reported as errored instead of skipped; the tool's own statistic also counts a case with no recorded interaction as errored, so the label alone does not say a network error happened.
* The spec declares `POST /api/did` with a `DidCreateRequest` body (not marked required) and responses 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 415, 429, 500, 502, 503.

### Checked and ruled out

* **Not a lone-surrogate encoding failure:** every string in the body encodes to UTF-8 (0 unencodable strings).

### NOT established

* Whether the request was ever sent. No interaction is recorded, and the scenario is `skip`, which points to "never sent", but that is an inference.
* Whether the platform would answer this exact body. Not tried: no live probe was run, by design (the planned runs were finished).
* Whether it is a Schemathesis stateful-engine behaviour (a skipped step) or something about this body.

### Suggested first step (not done)

Replay the single recorded case against slot 4 and see whether `POST /api/did` answers and with what; if it answers, the oddity is in the stateful engine and belongs with [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete)'s "a stateful count is a sample" note; if it hangs or resets, it belongs to platform-k and goes to Kamil.

### Why it matters at all

It is the only thing 4.29.4 counts as errored on this estate, so it is the first signal a reader sees when the new Errored row is non-zero, and it reads like a network failure when it may be a skipped step.

Related: [KS-1439](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1439/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4293-4294-fixes-only-35-entries-incl) (the bump that surfaced it), [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) (stateful sampling), [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) (register addendum 2026-10-07).

+++

Refs as KS-NNN text. Posted by agent on Peter's behalf.

title: Akto full scan reports three LOW HEADER_ALL_KEYS_INVALID_VALUES results (wallet-status ×2, GET /api/settings/notifications) that no ticket or allowlist covers — classify them: by-design or a finding
description:
## BLUF

The one `test:security` run on 2026-10-07 reported three **LOW** results from `HEADER_ALL_KEYS_INVALID_VALUES` on two public routes. No ticket covers them and no allowlist mechanism can express them. They are probably expected for public routes that ignore request headers, but that is **not established**, and today they fail the Full OWASP workflow on their own because the gate fails on any severity, LOW included.

## Measured (slot 1, Mac, Akto 2.37.1, 2026-10-07, run `security`, full OWASP summary `6ac60a95a141e9203079d8bf`, 50,450 result docs)

| Result |  |
| -- | -- |
| Template | `HEADER_ALL_KEYS_INVALID_VALUES`, category INPUT, severity LOW, CWE-20, nature INTRUSIVE |
| Docs for the template | 350; **90 executed** (a captured exchange); **3 flagged** (raw `vulnerable: true`); 347 not |
| Flagged 1 | `GET /api/auth/wallet/status/dt-seed-7` |
| Flagged 2 | `GET /api/auth/wallet/status/STRING` (the `{walletAddress}` placeholder) |
| Flagged 3 | `GET /api/settings/notifications` |

**What the template does** (read from the library file): it selects a 2xx, non-error response, replaces **every request header value** with invalid values, and flags the result when an attempt still returns 2xx with a body more than 90% identical to the original and the same schema.

**What the data shows.** Each flagged result has 4 attempts. Attempts 0–2 returned **400** (102-character body, 0% match). **Attempt 3 returned 200** (50 characters for wallet-status, 83 for settings/notifications) with a **100% match** — that attempt is what tripped the template. The altered request carried 3 headers for wallet-status (`host`, `x-akto-ignore`, `authorization`) and 2 for settings/notifications (`host`, `x-akto-ignore`). Which values attempt 3 used was **not examined**.

## Why this needs a ticket

* The two routes are already known to be public: `wallet/status` is public by necessity and cannot be allowlisted ([KS-1009](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1009/security-get-apiauthwalletstatus-returns-userid-role-to-any-anonymous); Kamil, PR #802, quoted in `endpointFalsePositives.ts`: "the registry has no representation for a parameterised route"), and `GET /api/settings/notifications` keeps optional auth by ruling ([KS-719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-719/security-put-apiprivacysettings-and-apisettingsnotifications-accept), quoted in the same file from `routes/admin.ts`: "The GET above keeps optional auth so anonymous readers still get the documented defaults").
* No existing allowlist mechanism fits. `KNOWN_FALSE_POSITIVE_ENDPOINT_TESTS` admits two ruled kinds with compile-time bounds (`public-by-design` only for `REMOVE_TOKENS`; `similarity-undiscriminating` only for three templates — Kamil's [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) bound), and a LOW from an INPUT template is neither. The wallet-status URL also carries a path parameter the registry cannot express.
* The gate (`assertNoVulnerabilities`) fails on any severity. So even after [KS-1009](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1009/security-get-apiauthwalletstatus-returns-userid-role-to-any-anonymous)'s HIGH is fixed, any of these LOWs that recurs will keep the Full OWASP workflow red.

## Not established

* **Whether it is a real input-validation gap (CWE-20) or expected** for routes that never read the headers being altered. For `settings/notifications` the altered headers do not include `authorization`, so "it ignores a bad token" does not explain it.
* **Why it was not reported before.** The 2026-10-05 full runs on slots 2 and 4 listed only the nginx LOW ([KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low)). This stack's collection also carried authenticated samples for these URLs (a `feed-har` added them, 343 → 349 endpoints). Not shown to be the cause.
* Related, not claimed: [KS-1207](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1207/security-an-unknown-sk-key-on-an-optional-auth-mount-skips-the) (In Progress, Kamil) covers an unknown key on an optional-auth mount skipping the Bearer check.

## Proposed next steps (smallest first)

1. Re-run **only** this template on those three URLs with a targeted Akto `CUSTOM` run (`apiInfoKeyList`; the technique used for [KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low)) and read attempt 3's actual request: which headers, which values.
2. Classify each: by design, or a finding. Kamil's call for the platform side.
3. If by design: accept it by a **narrow** rule with the ruling quoted verbatim (the [KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low) pattern), and a control showing another endpoint or template still fails. Extending the allowlist's compile-time bound needs Kamil's ruling first. If a finding: a platform ticket for Kamil.

## Done means

1. Each of the three results has a recorded classification, with the attempt-3 evidence.
2. If by design: the Full OWASP workflow no longer fails on them, a control still fails, and Console = Akto = HTML agree on the known-FP and vulnerable counts.
3. If a finding: it is ticketed for the owner and the test keeps failing honestly.

Found while verifying [KS-1440](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1440/akto-image-23610-2371-release-v2371-2026-10-06-both-local-tags) (PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1411](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1440-akto-23610-2371-with-the-ks-1416-ks-1421-and-ks-724-fixes-it-5f3e7f62426b), merged; history entry PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1412](https://linear.app/secuura/review/docs-project-history-for-the-2026-10-07-akto-2371-batch-one-pr-merged-06305b942330)). Nothing was changed for this finding.

title: Akto image 2.36.10 → 2.37.1 (Release v2.37.1, 2026-10-06; both _local tags verified 2026-10-07)
description:
**BLUF:** Akto published **Release v2.37.1** on 2026-10-06 at 18:10 UTC. systemTest pins **2.36.10** ([KS-1411](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1411/akto-image-2364-23610-release-v23610-2026-10-05-both-local-tags), 2026-10-05). `2.37.1_local` returns 200 for **both** the dashboard and testing images, so it is a valid pair. Across 2.36.10 → 2.37.1 upstream changed **0 files under** `apps/testing`, **0** `pom.xml`/`package.json` files, and **none** of the Struts actions the harness calls. The one change that reaches the harness's path is the **RBAC rework**: the dashboard's `RoleAccessInterceptor` now runs role checks on sessions used straight from the API, which it used to skip. Our `init-user.sh` seeds the Akto user directly into Mongo and writes **no RBAC row**. So this looks like a low-risk bump, with one specific thing to prove live. It is **not** proven until the three tiers run on a slot.

## Current → new versions

| Item | Current (develop) | New |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Akto dashboard image | `aktosecurity/akto-api-security-dashboard:2.36.10_local` | `…:2.37.1_local` |
| Akto testing image | `aktosecurity/akto-api-testing:2.36.10_local` | `…:2.37.1_local` |
| Canonical pin | `systemTest/akto/package.json` → `config.aktoImageVersion: "2.36.10"` | `"2.37.1"` |
| Mongo | `mongo:6.0.28` | unchanged (no `pom.xml` changed, so the Mongo driver did not move) |

### Docker Hub `_local` tags (checked 2026-10-07)

| Version | Released (UTC) | dashboard | testing | Valid pair? |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 2.36.10 (current) | 2026-10-05 06:26 | 200 | 200 | yes |
| 2.36.11 | 2026-10-05 11:46 | 200 | 200 | yes |
| 2.37.0 | 2026-10-05 14:55 | 200 | **404** | no (dashboard only) |
| **2.37.1** | 2026-10-06 18:10 | 200 | 200 | **yes (latest)** |

The GitHub release bodies for v2.36.11, v2.37.0 and v2.37.1 are **empty**. The change list below comes from the compare between the two tags, not from release notes.

## Upstream changes from v2.36.10 to v2.37.1

There are **56 commits** and **242 files** (GitHub compare v2.36.10...v2.37.1). 155 of the files are the dashboard's React frontend (`apps/dashboard/web/polaris_web`).

| Area | Files | What changed |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `apps/dashboard` (Java + UI) | 192 | **RBAC upgrade, phases 1–7** (PR 6574) — see below. Argus posture page: sensitive-data events and guardrail-violation KPIs/drills (`ArgusPostureService`, `ArgusAgentPostureDrillService`, `InsightUtil`, `InsightDataBundle`, `HostCollectionResolver`, `KpiGrid`; PRs 6592, 6605). New posture shown to all users (PR 6595). Guardrail activity fixes (undefined values, missing previous messages in violations; PRs 6602, 6604). Guardrail policies limited to the servers a collection-limited user can see. Threat actions scoped by host for collection-limited users. A new Roles & Users UI (role editor page, access summaries, Polaris dropdowns) |
| `apps/threat-detection` | 11 | **Impossible-travel** detection (aggregation groupBy + distinct country, PR 6583). **VPN/Tor detection policy** backed by a merged IP intelligence DB (PR 6588). Duplicate threat report fix |
| `apps/threat-detection-backend` | 6 | Guardrail charts aggregated by host scope for collection-limited users. Failed threat-event fetches are no longer cached as empty results |
| `apps/guardrails-service` (Go) | 10 | Session-based vs single-prompt guardrail separation, with two parallel LLM calls (with and without summary) (PR 6591). **Final image moves from** `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian11:nonroot` **to** `alpine:3.22` with `bash` added, keeping UID/GID 65532 (PR 6598). A trace-envelope fix (PR 6600) was merged and then reverted (PR 6601) inside the range |
| `libs/dao` | 15 | RBAC DAOs and DTOs: `RBACDao` (+148/−49), `CustomRoleDao`, new `RbacCacheVersionDao`, `CollectionRule`, `RuleCollections`, `RbacEnums`, `UsersCollectionsList`, `SAMLConfig` |
| `libs/utils` | 5 | New `IpAnonymizerLookup` (VPN/Tor). `UsageMetricCalculator`. Two new **Liquibase Mongo changelogs**: `account/027-api-collections-rule-indexes.xml` (host and tag indexes on `api_collections`) and `common/006-create-rbac-cache-versions.xml` (`rbac_cache_versions` collection) |
| `protobuf` | 1 | `threat_detection/.../dashboard_service/v1/service.proto` |
| `.github` | 2 | Akto's own prod/staging workflows |

### RBAC upgrade in detail (the part to watch)

* Phase 1: **deny-on-error**, report-only by default. It is switched on only by `AKTO_RBAC_DENY_ON_ERROR=true`, which our compose does not set. Role checks added on integration actions that had none. Tolerant role-name parsing. RBAC feature cache fix.
* Phase 2: per-feature permission overrides on custom roles, and a new `THREAT_SETTINGS` permission.
* Phase 3: host and tag collection rules on custom roles.
* **Security fix:** role escalation in `updateUserScopeRoleMapping`, and a cross-account password reset (commit `20b1bb345`).
* Phase 4: team admins limited to collections can only assign roles their custom role lists.
* Phase 5: time-bound user access, and opt-in SSO access removal for users in no mapped group (Okta, Azure, SAML now share one mapping, `SsoRoleMapping`).
* Phases 6–7: audit logs for role, custom-role and SSO-mapping changes.
* Hardening: one access-change check for every path, the last admin is kept, deleted roles give no access, and role changes reach every dashboard instance (`RbacCacheVersionDao.syncIfChanged`, polled every 10 s).
* **"Role checks no longer skipped for sessions used straight from the API without an account set"** (commit `b0e5a7c71`). `RoleAccessInterceptor` now fills the account id from `Context.accountId` when the session has none. Before, the checks below that point were skipped for such requests.
* New endpoints: `api/fetchUserPermissions` (`UserPermissionsAction`) and `api/fetchAssignableRoles`.
* Accounts without the paid RBAC feature are still relaxed to full access, **except admin actions**, which need the Admin role.

### Dependency changes inside the images

| Dependency | Before | After |
| -- | -- | -- |
| guardrails-service base image | `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian11:nonroot` | `alpine:3.22` (+ `ca-certificates`, `bash`) |
| `golang.org/x/image` | v0.43.0 | v0.45.0 |
| `golang.org/x/sync` | v0.21.0 | v0.22.0 |
| `golang.org/x/sys` (indirect) | v0.45.0 | v0.47.0 |
| `golang.org/x/text` (indirect) | v0.39.0 | v0.41.0 |

No `pom.xml` or `package.json` changed in the range. That means swagger-parser and mongodb-driver-sync did not change either, so the Mongo 6.0 hold stands. We do not run guardrails-service, so its base-image change does not reach our stack.

### Checked against what the harness depends on

These are the [KS-1363](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1363/akto-a-skipped-har-replay-is-only-a-warn-the-tier-runs-on-synthetic) / [KS-1411](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1411/akto-image-2364-23610-release-v23610-2026-10-05-both-local-tags) checks, re-run for 2.36.10 → 2.37.1:

* `apps/testing`: **0 files changed.**
* `TestRunStatusHelper`, `TestRunStatusAction`, `TestResultsStatsAction`, `StartTestAction` and the testing-run DTOs are **not in the diff**. The copied regexes, the 3,000-sample cap and `api/stopTest` should still hold.
* `tests-library-master.zip` is **not in the diff**, so the test templates should be the same.
* The Struts actions the harness calls (`startTest`, `stopTest`, `fetchTestRunStatusSummaries`, `fetchTestRunLogs`, `fetchTestingRunResults`, `fetchTestingRunResultSummaries`, `saveTestEditorFile`, `uploadHar`, `importDataFromOpenApiSpec`, `importSwaggerLogs`, `fetchSwaggerImportLogs`, `getAllCollections`, `fetchApiInfosForCollection`, `fetchAllSubCategories`) do **not** appear in the `struts.xml` diff.
* **Liquibase:** `LiquibaseStartupMigrator.java` is not in the diff. [KS-1411](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1411/akto-image-2364-23610-release-v23610-2026-10-05-both-local-tags) verified that changelogs run only when `AKTO_RUN_DB_MIGRATIONS=true`, which our stack never sets. So 027 and 006 should not run on our stack. Confirm on the slot: no `rbac_cache_versions` collection and 0 Liquibase lines in the dashboard log.
* **Open risk — RBAC on the seeded user:** `systemTest/akto/scripts/init-user.sh` seeds the user, account and organisation into Mongo and writes **no RBAC row**. With 2.37.1, the interceptor's checks now run for API-driven sessions, and `RBACDao.getCurrentRoleForUser` is read for every guarded action. The live run must show that the seeded user still reaches every action above, with no 403 / `FORBIDDEN` / "You don't have access to this product" / "Your role was removed" response. If it does not, the fix belongs in `init-user.sh` (seed an ADMIN RBAC row), with a red→green test.

## Work

1. Bump the pin in every place that mirrors it, all from 2.36.10 to 2.37.1, and add a KS ref and date to the comments:
   * `systemTest/akto/package.json` (`config.aktoImageVersion`)
   * `systemTest/akto/docker-compose.yml` (dashboard and testing fallbacks, and their comments)
   * `systemTest/akto/.env.example` (the three commented examples)
   * `systemTest/akto/src/report/reportServiceLogs.ts` (empty-state string)
   * `systemTest/akto/docs/configuration.md`
   * `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` (the *Akto pin* paragraph)
   * `Projects Documents/QA_Tool_Cheat_Sheet_Secuura_API_Testing.html`
   * `Projects Documents/API_Security_Functional_Testing_Architecture_Flow_Diagrams.html`
2. Run `npm run update-images` to confirm 2.37.1 is still the latest valid pair when the work starts.
3. Run the unit and quality gates for `systemTest/akto` (`aktoPinMirrors.test.ts` and `aktoVersionNotTyped.test.ts` must stay green).
4. Do a live run on the named slot: `test:pr`, then `test:pre-merge`, then `test:security`. Compare finding counts, run counts, the status histogram, the test catalog (194 ids / 20 categories at 2.36.10) and wall-clock against the 2026-10-05 2.36.10 baseline (pr 24 s / pre-merge 3 m 57 s / security 11 m 1 s). Report the before and after as numbers.
5. Check the RBAC risk above explicitly: count any 403 or role-denial responses from the dashboard during the runs, and check for the Liquibase and `rbac_cache_versions` absence.

## Not done in creating this ticket

* No image has been pulled or run, and no suite has been run against 2.37.1.
* The upstream commits were read by title and by changed path. Only `RoleAccessInterceptor.java`, `SignupAction.java`, `struts.xml`, the guardrails `Dockerfile` and `go.mod` were read as diffs. The GitHub compare API returned no line counts for the `libs/` files, so those were read by path only.
* Known findings already tracked are unchanged by this ticket: [KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low) (the accepted `Server: nginx` LOW), [KS-1416](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1416/akto-the-three-code-injection-sqli-scans-run-0-sqlnosql-templates-akto) (0 SQL/NoSQL templates), [KS-1374](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1374/akto-scans-are-now-paced-to-fit-the-platforms-rate-limit-test-times) (pacing).

title: Bump systemTest schemathesis pin 4.29.3 → 4.29.4 (fixes only: 35 entries incl. 8 negative_data_rejection, network errors now errored, NDJSON credentials sanitised) + refresh every pyproject package to latest
description:
**BLUF:** Upstream released **4.29.4 on 2026-10-06**, a fixes-only patch (35 entries, no features, no changes marked breaking). `develop` pins `==4.29.3` ([KS-1408](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1408/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4280-4293-four-releases-4290-4293), Done). This ticket records every change, tracks the pin bump, and refreshes every package in `systemTest/schemathesis/pyproject.toml` to its latest release. Correction to the first draft of this ticket: it said 31 entries and 4 `negative_data_rejection` entries; the upstream CHANGELOG has **35** and **8**.

## Upstream 4.29.4 (2026-10-06), verbatim from the upstream CHANGELOG

### Fixed

`st run` (8)

* Show a single `Coverage` block in `st run` output under `--max-time`.
* Report test cases that hit network errors as errored instead of skipped.
* Report test cases interrupted by crashed checks as errored.
* Missing `Network Error` details in stateful runs that also report a failure.
* Keep test runs successful when crash recording cannot write to the cache directory.
* Sanitize credentials in recorded test cases in NDJSON reports.
* Name the config section and key when a list or string is too short.
* Show the compact `[auto, 1-64]` range when `--workers` gets an out-of-range value.

**Hooks** (3)

* Report all-rejecting `filter_case` hooks as hook errors during fuzzing.
* Report `filter_case` hooks that start rejecting mid-run during fuzzing as hook errors.
* Report `SystemExit` raised in hooks as an error instead of skipped operations or success.

**Data generation** (5)

* Crash in the coverage phase on non-numeric `default` values of numeric schemas.
* Binary `default` of a non-string parameter sent as the default positive value in coverage.
* Report invalid schema keywords in negative mode as schema errors.
* Invalid values generated for `\S` patterns, e.g. non-breaking spaces.
* Generate ECMA-literal `&&`, `~~` and `[` inside character classes in `pattern`.

**Request serialization** (6)

* Send multipart form booleans, nulls, and objects as `true` / `false` / `null` and JSON.
* Send non-file multipart fields as plain form fields instead of file uploads.
* Encode multipart parts with nested multipart or form-urlencoded content types.
* Use the part's own schema for the root element of XML-encoded multipart parts.
* Crash when serializing an XML body for an operation that does not declare XML.
* Send `text/plain` object and array bodies as JSON instead of Python text.

**Schema handling** (3)

* Use the file name as the discriminator value for whole-file `$ref` branches.
* Accept response discriminator values derived from whole-file reference names.
* Resolve external `$ref` pointers in `response_schema_conformance` failure schemas.

`negative_data_rejection` (8)

* False positive for form body fields that become valid strings when sent.
* False positive for `null` sent to nullable query parameters.
* False positive for `null` in query parameters alongside unsent extra parameters.
* False positive for DRF validation errors wrapped in `detail`.
* False positive for path parameters whose `anyOf` / `oneOf` accepts any string.
* Missed failure when a nullable query value is sent beside an invalid header.
* Missed failures for type mutations of nullable or `allowEmptyValue` parameters.
* Crash when cases use string query values.

**Others** (2)

* Report GraphQL errors with multiple source locations without crashing.
* False "Network Error" on Windows when servers close reused keep-alive connections.

## What reaches our estate (read from the spec and harness; to be confirmed by the sweep, not asserted)

* **Skipped → errored:** network-error and crashed-check cases change bucket. Our skipped/errored panels, `src/sweep_outcome.py` and `report_reconciliation.py` read these counts. Expect counts to move; every move is explained.
* **NDJSON credential sanitising:** touches the `recorder.cases[]` readers (pinned by `test_ndjson_writer_shape.py`, `test_ndjson_completeness.py`).
* `negative_data_rejection` **(8):** the spec has 249 `null`-typed schemas and 2 form-urlencoded bodies. None of the 8 describes the [KS-1414](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1414/schemathesis-429x-reports-negative-data-rejection-on-requests-that-are) pool-draw mechanism, so the [KS-1414](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1414/schemathesis-429x-reports-negative-data-rejection-on-requests-that-are) count (55 and 61 at 4.29.3) is **not expected to fall**. Measured, not assumed; the harness already reports it as a section (PR 1403).
* **Schema handling:** the spec has 3 discriminator uses, so a small `response_schema_conformance` change is possible.
* **Inapplicable by inspection:** 0 multipart, 0 XML and 0 `text/plain` bodies in the spec; the harness registers no `filter_case` hook (`map_case`, `before_add_examples`, `after_call` only); GraphQL and Windows items.

## Scope

1. Pin `schemathesis==4.29.4`; sync the venv; regenerate `constraints.txt` via `update-deps`; update the `schemathesis_tests.yaml` header (parity-tested).
2. **Refresh every package in** `systemTest/schemathesis/pyproject.toml` (`[build-system]`, `[project] dependencies`, `[project.optional-dependencies] dev`, `requires-python`) to the latest release, checked against PyPI at bump time. Any hold is named with its resolver error.
3. Six-surface audit against 4.29.3: checks, phases, warnings, `run --help` flags, `--report` formats, NDJSON writer fields.
4. New tests, each red on 4.29.3 and green on 4.29.4: network error counted as errored (console == results.json == HTML); NDJSON credentials sanitised.
5. Gates: ruff format and lint, mypy, pip-audit, full unit suite, Prettier where applicable.
6. Live on platform-k slot 4 (K only): `full` before (4.29.3) and after (4.29.4), same seed, same stack; `integration`; Akto; Playwright; k6. Counts quoted before and after.
7. Docs: systemTest `CLAUDE.md`, schemathesis `docs/`, and the two HTML documents in the repo root.

## Status (2026-10-07)

Done and tested locally; PR 1414 is open against `develop` (head `3e3185e4d`, not merged). Results, the Test Evidence block and what was NOT run are in the comment of 2026-10-07 on this ticket. Follow-ups: [KS-1442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1442/schemathesis-stateful-one-generated-post-apidid-case-is-recorded-with) (the one errored case) and the [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) addendum. Correction to the scope above: the `negative_data_rejection` fixes did not reduce the [KS-1414](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1414/schemathesis-429x-reports-negative-data-rejection-on-requests-that-are) false positives (39 / 25 / 35 across the three runs), and the bump broke the console and verdict parsers (errored cases left `skipped`), which is now fixed and pinned.
