title: gate63 minors on the KS-1404 trust-anchor wiring (PR 1388): six Minors carried forward, and the image proof was never run
description:
gate63 returned **GO** on #1388 (KS-1404, the trust-anchor wiring) with six Minor findings, none
blocking and none Major. The PR has merged; this ticket carries the findings forward with the
fix-shape the gate gave for each. Report `a68b1497f421c496…`, 276 lines.

Refs KS-1404

## The six findings

**N-1388-1 — the tsc figure does not reproduce, and no host is named.** The claim "a single
pre-existing tsc error (`rfc3161-verify.ts` TS2345), its line moving 344→349" appears in the commit
message, the PR body and flow 11.4. The gate measured TypeScript 5.9.3 on standalone member
installs and got **rc 0, zero** `error TS` **lines at both** `f01c1da5717f` and `3ce575eeb63c`; the brief
expected 59. Three different counts for one figure, none with a host. The substance holds — **0 NEW**
**errors either way** — but it sits in a client-facing doc with nothing that lets a reader
re-measure it. *Fix-shape:* name the host and install recipe beside each figure, or restate as
"0 new tsc errors (base N / head N on <host>, <recipe>)". The "1937 packages" figure in the PR body
is the same class (the gate measured 349+267 standalone, 346+311 as workspace members; I measured
1,393 package directories in the worktree — three units, one number).

**N-1388-2 — the cheat sheet's corrected note points the wrong way.** The note after the KS-1404
table (`:3776-:3779`) says the wiring row is "below"; it is at `:3748`, **above**. "is now covered"
also reads as though some environment already has the anchor in effect — none does, because no
deploy has happened. *Fix-shape:* "below" → "above", and say "this change wires every
compose-launched box; in effect once deployed". This could not be fixed in the merge-in: Q-M's M1
pins the head's section byte for byte.

**N-1388-3 — cell A does not bind the default's variable name.** Tamper T-NAME
(`${OTHER_VAR:-/app/config/tsa-trust-anchors-dtrust.crt}`) stays **6/6 green**. The default still
pins D-Trust so verification is unaffected; what breaks silently is the documented override path.
*Fix-shape:* anchor the regex to `^\$\{TSA_TRUST_ANCHORS_PEM:-(.*)\}$`. *Regression test:* T-NAME
must red cell A.

**N-1388-4 — no PR cell parses the REAL per-provider file inside the verifier.** C1 hashes the PEM
with the test's own decoder; C2 uses a synthetic root. At the base C1 reds only through A's
precondition, so its own conjunct has no independent red-first. The gate's probe P1/P2 closes the
gap at runtime for this head, as does pre-existing cell 17 (the bundle's block 1 is byte-equal to
this file). *Fix-shape:* commit P1 and P2 as cells —
`parseTrustAnchors(readFileSync(<real file>)).length === 1` at the digest, and a synthetic token with
the real file by path refused "does not chain", never "no trust anchor configured".

**N-1388-5 — a missing anchor is silent until a verify, and** `/health` **carries no anchor state.**
Fail-closed is the safe direction, but a wiring failure reproduces today's "everything refused"
state behind a green `/health`. *Fix-shape:* an `anchors: {configured, count, sha256[]}` block in
`/health`, or a boot-time log line. **Operational consequence now:** the deploy sweep must use the
in-container checks in the gate's C7(a), never `/health`.

**N-1388-6 — the image also ships the two-root bundle** (DigiCert included) at
`/app/config/tsa-trust-anchors.crt`. Q-SCOPE holds and no new privilege is created.
*Fix-shape (optional):* COPY only the per-provider file, or note it in `config/README.md`.

## OWED to the kintsugi deploy round, not done here

**C6, the local image proof, is NOT RUN — the Docker daemon was unreachable (c6 rc 20).** So the
claim that the built image actually contains `/app/config/tsa-trust-anchors-dtrust.crt` is
unverified. It is owed to the deploy round, which is a separate seat on its own GO. Nothing in
#1388 has been deployed: `TSA_URL` is present-but-empty on both live boxes, which resolves to
D-Trust by code default, and `TSA_TRUST_ANCHORS_PEM` is absent on both, so every real RFC 3161
token is still refused with `no trust anchor configured` until a deploy happens.

## Also worth recording, found while merging

`merged8.py` requires nine `targets` as (blob, mode) pairs that the gate's `## MERGE ADDENDUM` line
does not publish. I sourced each by reading `ls-tree` at the head so the mode comes from git rather
than from me, but the gap between what the gate publishes and what the merge tool demands is an
invitation to guess at a value that lands on `develop` permanently.

title: revoke answers 400 "already revoked" where 404 belongs if the document is deleted mid-race
description:
**Pre-existing, and narrowed rather than introduced by the KS 1278 change.** Found while building PR #1393.

`updateDocument` in originate's document repository returns `null` for **two** different outcomes:

1. the document was not found — the inner `getDocument` read came back empty (the pre-existing path, `documentRepo.ts:538`);
2. the guarded write changed no row — the KS 1278 `ifStatusIsNot` guard refused it because the row was already in the target status.

The revoke route maps `null` to **400 BAD_REQUEST "Document is already revoked"**. For the ordinary case that is right, and deliberately so: the route 404s and 403s before the write, and 400s on the read, so by the time the guarded write runs the document exists and was not revoked at read time — a `null` can only mean the row became revoked in between, which is exactly the race KS 1278 closes.

**The residual:** if the document is **deleted** between the route's read and the guarded write, outcome 1 fires instead, and the caller is told **"Document is already revoked" with a 400** when the correct answer is **404 Document not found**. The window is narrow — it is a race, not a reachable sequential path — and nothing here is a security or data-integrity problem: no write happens, no provenance row is recorded and no anchor is emitted in either case. It is a response-classification defect only.

**Before KS 1278** the route did not read the write's result at all, so this particular confusion could not arise there; the same single `null` was already ambiguous for every other caller of `updateDocument`, which is why this is recorded as pre-existing in shape and merely surfaced at a new call site.

**What a fix would need.** Separate the two meanings rather than overload one `null` — for example a discriminated result (not-found vs guard-refused vs updated), or a cheap existence re-read on the `null` path before choosing the status code. Both touch every caller of `updateDocument`, which is why it was explicitly left out of KS 1278's scope rather than bolted on.

**Not measured.** No live sweep and no two-session test ran against a real PostgreSQL. The claim above is read off the control flow in `documentRepo.ts` and `routes/documents.ts` plus the mocked cells in PR #1393, not reproduced against a running stack.

Refs KS-1278

title: Flow doc block 18.3 states a suite reading with no seat, date or host, beside a PR body reporting a different run at the same sha
description:
## BLUF

Flow-diagram block 18.3 states a `services/auth` suite reading as "at head" with no seat, no date
and no host, while the PR body for the same sha reports a different run. A reader of the document
cannot tell that more than one reading exists at that commit, or whose machine produced the one
they are looking at.

Raised from gate60's review of PR #1384 (KS 1210) as finding N-1384-2.
**Pre-existing in that PR's documentation, not introduced by its merge-in.**
Severity Minor (D9) / Polish (D8); it blocked
nothing, and a documentation change at the time would have moved the head and forced a re-gate,
which is why it was deferred to a follow-up rather than fixed in place.

## What is actually wrong

Three readings of the same suite exist at sha 852fc9276320, and the document presents one of them
as if it were the only one:

* Seat E 2nd measured 864 of 864 with zero ks949 timeouts.
* The PR body reports a red run 1 at the same sha.
* The gate's own run on its host, 2026-10-05 at 08:05:51Z under load 2.35 rising to 6.46, also
  measured 864 of 864 with zero ks949 timeouts.

The document's sentence is **not false** — it is true of Seat E 2nd's run. The defect is that it is
unattributed, so a reader cannot reconcile it with the red run the body describes, and cannot tell
which host or load the green figure came from.

## What to do

* Attribute block 18.3's figures: name the seat, the date and the host that produced them.
* Add the run-1 reading alongside, or point the reader at the PR body where it is recorded.
* The companion D8 note is weaker and can be closed with it: the "5000 ms" figure in that block is
  a vitest timeout VALUE, not a stated suite timing, so the skill's stated-timings rule is barely
  engaged there. Polish only.

## Not covered

No live sweep. This is a documentation-attribution defect, measured by reading the committed
documents and the gate's report; nothing was exercised against a running service for it.

Refs KS-1210

title: Dead config: API_GATEWAY_PORT=6882 in both env templates is read by nothing — the gateway's port is GATEWAY_PORT (stack_env.sh), so editing it silently does nothing
description:
## BLUF

Hi Kamil, a small one for your call. Both platform-k env templates set `API_GATEWAY_PORT=6882` under an `# API GATEWAY` heading. Nothing in the repository reads that key. The gateway's published host port comes from a different key, `GATEWAY_PORT`, which `stack_env.sh` derives per slot. Today the line does no harm, but it reads as live config:

* Someone moving the gateway port would edit it, and nothing would change.
* `bootstrap-env.sh` copies it into every clone's `Blockchain/Dev/.env`, slot 2's included. That puts a slot-1 port literal in every slot's `.env`, which the CLAUDE.md slot MUST says should not happen.

## Verified from source (develop `0f2422925`, 2026-10-05)

* `Blockchain/Dev/env.example:361`: `API_GATEWAY_PORT=6882`. This is the canonical template since [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap).
* `Blockchain/Dev/env.local.example:56`: `API_GATEWAY_PORT=6882`.
* `git grep -n API_GATEWAY_PORT` across the whole repository returns **those two lines and nothing else**. No compose file, service, script, test or doc reads it.
* The key that actually sets the gateway's host port is `docker-compose.yml:2276`, `"${GATEWAY_PORT:-6882}:80"`. `GATEWAY_PORT` is exported per slot by `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh` (`6882 + 100*(N-1)`).
* Live: on a fresh slot-2 worktree, `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=2 bash scripts/bootstrap-env.sh` wrote `API_GATEWAY_PORT` into the generated `.env` (checked by key name only), and the gateway still came up on `:6982`. So the key is inert.

## Fix (your call)

1. **Delete both lines.** This is the simplest option, since nothing reads them.
2. **Or replace them** with a comment pointing at `GATEWAY_PORT` / `stack_env.sh`, so the `# API GATEWAY` heading tells a reader where the port really comes from.

Either way, a static check like the "no literal slot port outside `stack_env.sh`" guard proposed on [KS-1381](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381/slot-1-urls-outside-ks-1355s-four-spots-m365s-entra-redirect-uri) would stop it coming back.

## Not in this ticket

The other slot-1 literals in templates and scripts are on [KS-1381](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381/slot-1-urls-outside-ks-1355s-four-spots-m365s-entra-redirect-uri). Template drift between `env.example` and `.env.example` is on [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap).

Found while checking slot-2 port keys during [KS-1411](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1411/akto-image-2364-23610-release-v23610-2026-10-05-both-local-tags) (Akto 2.36.10 bump), Peter's Mac.

title: Akto: the three "code injection (SQLi/…)" scans run 0 SQL/NoSQL templates — Akto files those under NO_AUTH/VEM, and the SQL_INJECTION / NOSQL_INJECTION categories they map to do not exist
description:
## BLUF

Three Akto scans are named for SQL injection but run **no** SQL or NoSQL template. `CODE_INJECTION_TEST_IDS` maps the scans to category names `SQL_INJECTION`, `NOSQL_INJECTION`, `OS_COMMAND_INJECTION` and `LFI_RFI`, and **none of those exist in Akto's library**. Akto files its 8 SQL/NoSQL-injection templates under `NO_AUTH` and one more under `VEM`. The tier-level scans (pre-merge and full OWASP) do run them, so the platform is not unscanned for SQLi. But each of these three scans reports a PASS for SQLi that it never tested:

* `[slow] KYC submit: code injection (SQLi/XSS/RCE/LFI/SSTI/CRLF)`
* `[slow] analytics: code injection (SQLi/XSS/RCE/LFI/SSTI/CRLF)`
* `[slow] verifier: code injection on payload fields (SQLi/XSS/RCE/LFI/SSTI/CRLF)`

This is the [KS-709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-709/akto-reports-a-pass-for-a-test-that-executed-nothing-clean-0-not) false-zero family: the scan never selected the templates, so it could not have found anything.

## Measured (slot 2 of the Mac, 2026-10-05, Akto 2.36.10, branch [KS-1411](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1411/akto-image-2364-23610-release-v23610-2026-10-05-both-local-tags) at `a964e962c`)

`generate-test-ids` warns on every run: \*"expected categories absent from this library: OS_COMMAND_INJECTION, SQL_INJECTION, NOSQL_INJECTION, LFI_RFI — the matching *\_TEST_IDS in constants.ts will be empty"* (`bin/generate-test-ids.ts:271-277`). The warning was already present before 2.36.10, because the library is the identical blob (`c6fd9c0c…`). The catalog has 20 categories and 194 ids.

| Category in `CODE_INJECTION_TEST_IDS` (`src/core/constants.ts:503-514`) | ids in the catalog |
| -- | -- |
| COMMAND_INJECTION | 23 |
| **OS_COMMAND_INJECTION** | **0** (absent) |
| **SQL_INJECTION** | **0** (absent) |
| **NOSQL_INJECTION** | **0** (absent) |
| XSS / SSTI / INJECT / LFI / CRLF | 6 / 2 / 3 / 11 / 2 |
| **LFI_RFI** | **0** (absent) |
| **Total** | **47**, which matches "templates initiated 47" on each of the three scans |

Where Akto actually files the SQL/NoSQL templates:

* `NO_AUTH` (8): `AUTH_BYPASS_SQL_INJECTION`, `NOSQLI_ERROR_BASED_REPLACE_BODY_MONGO`, `SQLI_ERROR_BASED_PARAM_APPEND_PAYLOAD_MYSQL`, `…_APPEND_PAYLOAD_POSTGRESQL`, `…_APPEND_PAYLOAD_SQLITE`, `SQLI_ERROR_BASED_PARAM_MYSQL`, `SQLI_ERROR_BASED_PARAM_POSTGRESQL`, `SQL_INJECTION_REFERER_HEADER`
* `VEM` (1): `SQL_INJECTION_URL_PATH`

Results read directly from Akto's Mongo (`testing_run_result`, filtered on `testSubType` matching SQLi/NoSQLi):

| Scan | SQL/NoSQL templates run | Result docs | Without error | Vulnerable |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| pre-merge (through `NO_AUTH`) | 8 | 2,776 | 334 | 0 |
| full OWASP | 9 | 3,132 | 425 | 0 |
| KYC code injection | **0** | **0** | 0 | 0 |

The analytics and verifier code-injection scans use the same 47-id set (`tests/securityWorkflows.test.ts:200, 260, 317`), so they also run 0.

Losing `OS_COMMAND_INJECTION` and `LFI_RFI` costs nothing: command injection runs through `COMMAND_INJECTION` (23) and LFI through `LFI` (11). Only SQL and NoSQL are actually missing from these scans.

## Not established

* `SQL_INJECTION_USER_AGENT_HEADER` is in `yaml_templates` but not in the catalog. [KS-717](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-717/akto-test-id-catalog-and-the-loaded-template-library-drift-silently) §3 listed it as producing zero results on 2.22.2. I have not re-checked why it is missing.
* Whether Akto has ever filed these templates under `SQL_INJECTION` / `NOSQL_INJECTION` (for example in an older library) has not been checked. So when the mapping went stale is unknown.

## Proposed fix (systemTest only)

1. Select by **template id**, not only by Akto's category, for the SQL/NoSQL members of `CODE_INJECTION_TEST_IDS`. Akto's category for a template is not a stable taxonomy, so the selection should name what each scan claims to test.
2. Turn the `generate-test-ids` warning into a failure when a workflow set loses a family its scan's name claims. A warning that every run prints is a warning nobody reads.
3. Correct the scan names, or the `constants.ts:502` comment, to match what actually runs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The three code-injection scans select the SQL and NoSQL templates. Measured live: the run's result docs include those `testSubType`s.
- [ ] A test fails if `CODE_INJECTION_TEST_IDS` contains 0 SQL-injection or 0 NoSQL-injection ids. It must be shown red on the current code first.
- [ ] The per-scan time budget ([KS-441](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-441/akto-ci-scan-throughput-21-s-local-vs-10-min-in-the-isolated-pr-akto) / the testing discipline doc's tier table) is re-checked with the added templates.
- [ ] Console = Akto = HTML parity holds on the changed scans.

title: #1387 gate62 minors: the two platform-k docs claim "all three cmp-equal" and that is false, and the new status-URI cell's first-line pin is blind to a later active :6882 line
description:
Two Minors from gate62's review of PR #1387 (KS 1388 §1, merged on Wednesday's GO of
2026-10-05T10:04:00Z). Neither is a regression introduced by that PR: both are properties of the
documentation and of the test cell it added. Filed as a later row on Wednesday's instruction — **not**
**fixed in that round.**

## 1. Both platform-k documents claim "all three cmp-equal", and that is false

**Where:** the KS 1388 block in `Projects Documents/API_Security_Functional_Testing_Architecture_Flow_Diagrams.html` and the corresponding section in `Projects Documents/QA_Tool_Cheat_Sheet_Secuura_API_Testing.html`.

**What the documents say vs what is true.** The applied-equals-held claim is written as all three files
being `cmp`-equal to an independent apply. Measured: only the **suite file** is `cmp`-equal. Each of
the two env examples differs from the held hunk by **exactly one added line** — its `# KS 1388:` §5d
WHY comment, which the skill requires and the held patch does not carry. So the honest claim is
"one file cmp-equal, two files equal plus exactly one declared comment line each", and that is
materially different from "all three cmp-equal": a reader auditing the PR against the held artefact
would find two mismatches and have no way to tell they were intended.

**Why it matters beyond wording:** this is a claim about an *equality gate*, in the two documents a
reviewer reads instead of re-running the gate.

## 2. The new test cell's first-line pin is blind to a later active `:6882` line

**Where:** the cell added to `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/prometheus_targets.test.sh`.

**Symptom.** The cell pins the **first** occurrence of the status URI in each env example. A file
whose first line is correct but which carries a **later, active** (uncommented)
`nginx-gateway:6882` line passes. The cell cannot see the second line at all, so the regression it
exists to catch can be reintroduced below the line it reads and stay green.

**Fix shape (not applied here):** a per-file count cell —
`grep -c 'nginx-gateway:6882' <file>` asserted `== 0` — which is blind to position and therefore
cannot be satisfied by ordering. Keep the existing first-line pin as well: it carries the
positive statement about what the first line should be, which a count cannot express.

## Dup search before filing

All **543** KS issues enumerated across every state (not `searchIssues`, which saturates at 50 and
cannot prove a zero) and substring-matched locally. `"all three cmp-equal"` 0 hits, `"cmp-equal"` 0
hits; `"nginx-gateway:6882"`, `"stub_status"` and `"SECUURA_NGINX_STATUS_URI"` each hit exactly 1 row
and it is KS 1388 itself, the parent, not a duplicate of either finding. Controls fired both ways: a
must-hit probe for the parent key returned 1 (KS 1386 cites it) and a nonsense string returned 0.

Refs KS-1388. KS 1388 stays OPEN: only §1 shipped, and its §5f live sweep has not run.

title: Schemathesis 4.29.x reports negative_data_rejection on requests that are VALID — a pool-drawn value overwrites the negative body (55–61 false failures per full sweep, 12 ops; 2 at 4.28.0)
description:
## Summary

Since the 4.29.3 bump ([KS-1408](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1408/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4280-4293-four-releases-4290-4293)), every `full` sweep reports **55–61** `negative_data_rejection` **failures that are false**. Schemathesis mutates only the request body to make it invalid, then a value it draws from its pool of earlier responses overwrites that mutation. The request actually sent is **valid under the published schema**, the platform rightly accepts it, and the check still reports *"Invalid data should have been rejected"*. At 4.28.0 the same mechanism produced 2 such cases on 1 operation. These are tool false positives, not platform defects, and they're kept **visible**: no harness filter, no baseline masking (systemTest/CLAUDE.md truthful-gate rule). This ticket records the class so nobody triages them as platform bugs, and tracks re-checking each upstream release.

+++ Evidence, method and what to do

### Measured (slot 4, `develop` `46c3e20cf`, seed 1408, same stack)

| Run | `negative_data_rejection` failures | **False positives** (only body negative, sent body valid) | Operations |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 4.28.0 (before) | 209 | **2** | `POST /api/analytics/exports` |
| 4.29.3 | 251 | **55** | 12 |
| 4.29.3 re-run | 253 | **61** | 12 |

Operations seen in both 4.29.3 runs: `POST /api/governance/participants/register` (12/12) · `POST /api/security/events` (8/8) · `POST /api/security/rate-limit/reset` (6/6) · `POST /api/transfers` (5/5) · `POST /api/notifications` (4/14) · `POST /api/analytics/exports` (2/2) · `POST /api/m365/connections/init` (1/1) · `POST /api/status/{id}/allocate` (1/1). In one run only: `POST /api/timestamps` (11), `PATCH /api/gdpr/dsr/{dsrId}` (3/1), `PATCH /api/platform/tenants/{id}/status`, `POST /api/referrals/qualify`, `POST /api/delegations` (9), `POST /api/teams/notify`, `POST /api/delegations/validate`.

### How a case is classified

For each failing `negative_data_rejection` case in the NDJSON:

1. `meta.components`: **only** `body` has `mode: negative`. Path, query and headers are positive.
2. The body actually sent validates against the operation's request schema from `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` (`jsonschema_rs`, `$ref`s resolved, YAML timestamps kept as strings).
3. Typically `meta.pool_draws` carries a body entry (44 of 55 in the first run). Example, `POST /api/governance/participants/register`: body `{"walletAddress": "0", "stakedAmount": 1}` with `walletAddress` drawn from `POST /api/nft/record`. The spec requires `walletAddress` string `minLength: 1` and `stakedAmount` number 0…1e12, so it's **valid**, and the platform's 201 is correct.

The phase description on these cases reads *"Positive test case"*, which is itself a tell. Cases where the body is genuinely invalid (189–193 per run), or where no body was sent ([KS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1364/spec-85-of-145-request-bodies-are-not-marked-required-true-so)'s class), are **not** counted here.

### What to do

* **Re-check on every upstream release.** The classifier is a \~100-line script ([KS-1408](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1408/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4280-4293-four-releases-4290-4293) scratch `classify_run.py`). Worth turning into a harness report section so the count is visible per run rather than worked out by hand.
* **Upstream:** a candidate report to the Schemathesis project ("negative body mutation overwritten by a pool draw, case still judged negative"). It's not raised; that's an outward-facing post and Peter's call. In any commit or PR text, refer to it in plain words only (no other organisation's issue URLs).
* **Baseline:** don't baseline these as platform defects. If they're baselined at all, it should be with this ticket as the reason and an `expires`.

Related: [KS-1408](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1408/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4280-4293-four-releases-4290-4293) (the bump; evidence comment there) · [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing) (baseline lag) · [KS-752](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-752/schemathesis-baseline-gate-is-unreachable-runpy-skips-it-whenever-the) (the gate that would have caught the jump is skipped on failing sweeps) · [KS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1364/spec-85-of-145-request-bodies-are-not-marked-required-true-so) (no-body class, kept separate).

+++

title: start-secuura.sh and start-local.sh print the demo issuer password in their startup banners
description:
## BLUF

**Two platform-k start scripts print a password in clear on every successful start.** Both echo the demo issuer account's email *and its password* in their closing "Credentials" banner:

| Script | Line (`develop` `0f2422925`) | Last change |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` | `:711`, `echo -e "    Issuer:  demo@secuura.io / <password>"` | `7b14f84ff`, 2026-09-22 |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/start-local.sh` | `:251`, `echo "    Issuer:  demo@secuura.io  / <password>"` | `48641bda3`, 2026-09-05 |

The value is not reproduced here. The banner goes to the terminal, and from there into anything that captures stdout: CI logs, `nohup` / background-run logs (it is in this session's `$TMPDIR` start log), pasted bug reports and screenshots.

The platform-s rule (platform-s `CLAUDE.md` → *Security Considerations*) is: *"platform-k: a script or service there that prints or logs a password is raised as a **Critical** defect, assigned to Kamil."* That is why this is raised Urgent and assigned to you.

## Measured (5 Oct 2026)

* **The printed credential is live.** The same script's own login check (`start-secuura.sh:603`, which uses the same literal in a `curl` body) logged `Issuer login (demo@secuura.io)` as a success on a fresh K slot 3 (`46c3e20cf`, `--rebuild --fresh-db`).
* **Re-verified on the current** `origin/develop` `0f2422925`**:** both lines are still present, and no other `*.sh` under the repo echoes the literal.

## Severity context (stated so it can be weighed, not used to wave it through)

* This is the **published demo sample login**: platform-k `CLAUDE.md:107` names it, and [KS-668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-668/compose-seeds-published-123-credentials-by-default-and-the-11-rotation)'s scope note calls the demo logins deliberate, documented sample credentials. So the secret itself is already public.
* What the banner adds: it makes a known-default credential the thing every operator reads at the end of every start, on **every** compose deploy that runs these scripts. [KS-668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-668/compose-seeds-published-123-credentials-by-default-and-the-11-rotation) shows the same compose path seeds these defaults by default (`ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` defaults to `true`), and that rotating them through `.env` is silently ignored. So on a box where an operator *thinks* they rotated it, the banner still prints the old value, and the old value may still work.
* It also undercuts the "never print a password" rule both platforms hold. A script that prints one is the precedent the next script copies.

## Not covered by existing tickets (checked)

* [KS-972](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-972/start-secuurash-banner-prints-adminsecuuracom-admin123-which-has) (In Progress, PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1180](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-972-banner-start-secuurash-no-longer-prints-the-retired-admin-850ff68f818a)) fixed the **Admin** half of the same banner and explicitly left the Issuer half: *"the issuer half is correct and only the admin half is stale."* Its concern was a stale credential, not a printed one. It wasn't updated here because it is In Progress.
* [KS-668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-668/compose-seeds-published-123-credentials-by-default-and-the-11-rotation) (Backlog) covers compose seeding of the `*123` defaults and the broken rotation channel, not scripts printing them.
* [KS-951](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-951/the-default-password-ci-gate-catches-one-shape-and-calls-it-clean-16) (Backlog) covers the default-password CI lint. That lint scans only `.ts/.tsx/.js` under `services/` and `packages/`, so it cannot see a `.sh` banner. That's why nothing has flagged these lines.
* [KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a) retired the published SYSTEM_ADMIN credential. Its item 3 covers scripts that *read* a fallback, not scripts that *print* one.

## Suggested fix (your call)

1. Print the mechanism, not the value, as [KS-972](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-972/start-secuurash-banner-prints-adminsecuuracom-admin123-which-has) did for the admin line. For example: `Issuer: demo@secuura.io (password: DEMO_ISSUER_PASSWORD, or the published demo default; see CLAUDE.md)`.
2. Make `start-secuura.sh:603`'s login check read the password from the environment instead of a literal, so the script doesn't carry the value at all.
3. Extend the [KS-951](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-951/the-default-password-ci-gate-catches-one-shape-and-calls-it-clean-16) gate, or add a small `.sh` check, so a script that echoes a known seeded password fails the gate.

## Acceptance

* Neither banner prints a password value. A stack start's captured stdout contains no seeded password.
* A guard fails if a `.sh` under `Start_Up/` or `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/` echoes one.

---

*Found 5 Oct 2026 while bringing up K slot 3 for platform-s* [PS-1003](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1003/verification-policies-leaves-a-deployment-wide-block-policy-which) *(*`up-slot.sh 3`*). No K code was changed. Related:* [KS-972](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-972/start-secuurash-banner-prints-adminsecuuracom-admin123-which-has)*,* [KS-668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-668/compose-seeds-published-123-credentials-by-default-and-the-11-rotation)*,* [KS-951](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-951/the-default-password-ci-gate-catches-one-shape-and-calls-it-clean-16)*,* [KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a)*.*

title: gate61 round-2 follow-ups on migration 049: X7 backfill order, the flow doc's stale suite figures, an ungated arm, and 039 failing for a non-superuser owner
description:
Filed by the Seat F 3rd session at the close of PR #1383. Wednesday ruled all four items **not required before that merge**. Refs KS-1401.

**Searched first** (Linear `searchIssues`, 2026-10-05): `N-1383`, `gate61 round 2`, `backfill after CREATE POLICY`, `11 cells 53 assertions`, `permission denied to create role`, `flow doc block 22`, `tenant_scope_bypass`. That endpoint is **fuzzy** — it returned five relevance-ranked hits for every term, so this is weak evidence of absence rather than proof. The nearest existing tickets are **KS-1376** (certifications ends FORCE with no policy — related, different defect), **KS-889** (a different COALESCE backfill window) and **KS-1281** (a different `permission denied` on `vc_credentials_store`). None covers the four below.

---

### r2-1 (Minor) — in the constructed X7 state the NULL row stays NULL

In gate61 round 1's constructed X7 state (`certifications` with RLS FORCE and **no** policy), migration 049's backfill leaves the `tenant_id IS NULL` row still NULL.

**Unreachable on the repo's own paths**, which is why it is Minor: the gateway runner backfills, then sets NOT NULL, then FORCEs, in that order.

* Fix shape: perform the backfill **after** `CREATE POLICY`, not before.
* Regression arm: X7's owner arm.

### r2-2 (Minor) — the FLOW document still carries the pre-fix suite figures

Block 22 of the architecture flow document still reads `11 cells, 53 assertions.` and `13 s, 13 s, 12 s`. The suite is now **12 cells, 62 assertions, 19/18/19 s**. The QA cheat sheet **is** correct, so the two platform-k documents disagree with each other.

Verified at the close of the session, both lines, with the cheat sheet as a control (zero occurrences of `53 assertions` there against one of `62 assertions`, so the check discriminates between the documents).

**Deliberately not fixed in PR #1383:** a content commit on a head that already holds a signed GO would re-gate it. This is a **docs-only** follow-up.

### r2-3 (Polish) — the COMMITTED arm does not gate the count arms

In the suite's cell 12, the assertion that the migration run committed (`rc 0`, zero `ERROR` lines) is reported **beside** the row-count assertions rather than **gating** them. If a run fails to commit, the count assertions still execute and report against a rolled-back database.

Today all three pass together so nothing is hidden, but the arrangement means a future rollback would be reported as a count failure rather than as a non-committed run. A `RAISE NOTICE` is not transactional, which is the whole reason the COMMITTED arm exists.

### r2-6 (Info, pre-existing) — 039 fails every boot for a non-superuser owner

Run as a non-superuser owner, the gateway runner fails migration 039 on every boot with `permission denied to create role`. Pre-existing, not introduced by 049.

**Why it matters here:** it bears directly on the one fact nobody has measured on the kintsugi database — the connecting role's superuser / BYPASSRLS / owner status — which is the input that decides whether gate61's N-1383-1 would have bitten that database at all. Read that role before the 049 apply round.

---

**Not a blocker for PR #1383.** Its merge is held on a separate Kam ruling (the KS-1404 anchor wiring must merge first), not on any of these.

title: Akto image 2.36.4 → 2.36.10 (Release v2.36.10, 2026-10-05; both _local tags verified that day)
description:
**BLUF:** Akto published **Release v2.36.10** on 2026-10-05 at 06:26 UTC. systemTest pins **2.36.4** ([KS-1363](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1363/akto-a-skipped-har-replay-is-only-a-warn-the-tier-runs-on-synthetic), 2026-09-30). `2.36.10_local` returns 200 for **both** the dashboard and testing images, so it is a valid pair. Across 2.36.4 → 2.36.10 upstream changed **0 files under** `apps/testing` and **0 files that the harness reads**. All changes are in agent-guard, guardrails, posture/insights, and Prometheus metrics. This looks like a low-risk bump. It is **not** proven until the three tiers run live on a slot.

## Current → new versions

| Item | Current (develop `46c3e20cf`) | New |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Akto dashboard image | `aktosecurity/akto-api-security-dashboard:2.36.4_local` | `…:2.36.10_local` |
| Akto testing image | `aktosecurity/akto-api-testing:2.36.4_local` | `…:2.36.10_local` |
| Canonical pin | `systemTest/akto/package.json` → `config.aktoImageVersion: "2.36.4"` | `"2.36.10"` |
| Mongo | `mongo:6.0.28` | unchanged (the upstream Mongo driver did not move) |

### Docker Hub `_local` tags (checked 2026-10-05)

| Version | dashboard | testing | Valid pair? |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 2.36.4 (current) | 200 | 200 | yes |
| 2.36.5 | 200 | 200 | yes |
| 2.36.6 | 200 | 200 | yes |
| 2.36.7 | 200 | 200 | yes |
| 2.36.8 | 200 | **404** | no (dashboard only) |
| 2.36.9 | 200 | **404** | no (dashboard only) |
| **2.36.10** | 200 | 200 | **yes (latest)** |

## Upstream changes from v2.36.4 to v2.36.10

There are **34 commits** and **70 files** (GitHub compare v2.36.4...v2.36.10). By area:

| Area | Files | What changed |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `apps/agent-guard` | 29 | Agent-guard work, including Bedrock agent support |
| `apps/dashboard` | 23 | Argus/agentic posture score calculation and bands, posture names and the approved section, the insight cards, guardrail policy replay ("policy respect for replay"), multi-lingual prompt blocking and sentiment detection in the guardrails UI, endpoint-shield filters, LLM observability (longer LLM timeout, new default date range), issue names shown in display format, and `ModuleInfoAction` (+39) |
| `apps/data-ingestion-service` | 8 | New Prometheus `/metrics` endpoint, gated on `PROMETHEUS_METRICS_ENABLED` (InfraMetrics action, filter and listener), plus outbound HTTP client metrics |
| `apps/akto-gateway` | 3 | Counter for guardrails validation decisions (with a redaction "modified" tag), and a new test |
| `apps/guardrails-service` (Go) | 4 | Field-mapping validator changes. `akto-endpoint-shield` moves from 20260929073208-b978541dc4f9 to 20261002113503-022da8dfea71 |
| `libs/dao` and `libs/utils` | 3 | New `AllowVendorAllowlistDao`, plus a Liquibase **Mongo changelog** `026-allow-vendor-allowlist.xml`. It creates the `allowvendorallowlist` collection and 3 indexes, guarded by MARK_RAN preconditions. Vendor approvals move out of `mcp_allowlist`, and existing `__vendor__` rows are **not** migrated |

### Dependency changes inside the images

| Dependency | Before | After |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `io.micrometer:micrometer-core` (akto-gateway) | not present | **1.17.1** (new) |
| `io.micrometer:micrometer-registry-prometheus` (data-ingestion-service) | not present | **1.17.1** (new) |
| `akto-endpoint-shield` / `mcp-endpoint-shield` (Go) | v0.0.0-20260929073208-b978541dc4f9 | v0.0.0-20261002113503-022da8dfea71 |

No other `pom.xml`, `go.mod` or `package.json` changed in the range. That means swagger-parser and mongodb-driver-sync did not change either, so the Mongo 6.0 hold stands.

### Checked against what the harness depends on

These are the [KS-1363](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1363/akto-a-skipped-har-replay-is-only-a-warn-the-tier-runs-on-synthetic) checks, re-run for 2.36.4 → 2.36.10:

* `apps/testing`: **0 files changed.**
* `TestRunStatusHelper`, `TestRunStatusAction`, `TestResultsStatsAction`, `StartTestAction` and the testing-run DTOs are **not in the diff**. The copied regexes, the 3,000-sample cap and `api/stopTest` should still hold.
* `tests-library-master.zip` is **not in the diff**, so the test templates are the same.
* ~~The new Mongo changelog runs on the dashboard's account DB at startup.~~ **Corrected 2026-10-05 (verified):** Akto runs its Liquibase changelogs only when `AKTO_RUN_DB_MIGRATIONS=true` (`libs/utils/.../LiquibaseStartupMigrator.java:28-35`, the same blob `521c44759b` at both tags). Our compose and `docker.env.example` never set it, and it is not set inside the slot-2 dashboard container. So no changelog has ever run on our stack, at 2.36.4 or now. 026 changes nothing for us: `allowvendorallowlist` is absent on slot 2, and the dashboard log has 0 Liquibase lines.

## Work

1. Bump the pin in every place that mirrors it, all from 2.36.4 to 2.36.10, and add a KS ref and date to the comments:
   * `systemTest/akto/package.json` (`config.aktoImageVersion`)
   * `systemTest/akto/docker-compose.yml` (dashboard and testing fallbacks, and their comments)
   * `systemTest/akto/.env.example`
   * `systemTest/akto/docs/configuration.md`
   * `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` (the *Akto pin* paragraph)
   * `Projects Documents/QA_Tool_Cheat_Sheet_Secuura_API_Testing.html`
   * `Projects Documents/API_Security_Functional_Testing_Architecture_Flow_Diagrams.html`
2. Run `npm run update-images` to confirm 2.36.10 is still the latest valid pair when the work starts.
3. Run the unit and quality gates for `systemTest/akto`.
4. Do a live run on the named slot: `test:pr`, then `test:pre-merge`, then `test:security`. Compare finding counts, run counts, the status histogram and wall-clock against the 2026-09-30 2.36.4 baseline (30 s / 3 m 42 s / 13 m 46 s). Report the before and after as numbers.

## Not done in creating this ticket

* No image has been pulled or run, and no suite has been run against 2.36.10.
* The upstream commit list was read by title and by changed path only. The agent-guard files were not reviewed line by line, because the harness doesn't use them.

## Result — slot 2, the Mac, 2026-10-05 (branch `feature/ks-1411-…`; PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1392](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1411-akto-image-pair-2364-23610-every-pin-mirror-and-test-version-02c1883784bf) open at head `b10545dac` after merging develop `32e058975`. Not merged.)

**BLUF:** 2.36.10 is a clean bump for the harness. There are **0 new tests**. The catalog is byte-identical at 194 ids / 20 categories, and there is **no result-field drift** (16 DOC + 14 RES). `otherError` is **0%** across 15 runs (147,816 results). **Console = Akto's own Mongo = HTML report** reconciles run by run for all 15 scans. `test:security` exits **1**. The cause is the one LOW `UNWANTED_RESPONSE_HEADERS` (`Server: nginx`) result that Kamil accepted on [KS-1397](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1397/the-gateway-answers-every-request-with-server-nginx-aktos-unwanted); the bump did not cause it.

| Tier | 2.36.4 (slot 4, 2026-09-30) | 2.36.10 (slot 2, 2026-10-05) | Result docs | 429s | Verdict |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| pr | 30 s | **24 s** | 8,677 → 8,552 | 0 → 0 | PASS |
| pre-merge | 3 m 42 s | **3 m 57 s** | 20,851 → 20,851 | 182 → **944** | PASS |
| security | 13 m 46 s | **11 m 1 s** | 50,018 → 50,162 (full scan) | 0 → 0 | FAIL (LOW 1, [KS-1397](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1397/the-gateway-answers-every-request-with-server-nginx-aktos-unwanted)) |

* **Pre-merge 429s:** all 944 landed in one \~2 s window, across 48 endpoints and 33 templates. The testing engine is byte-identical to 2.36.4, so the bump is not the cause. Pacing versus bursts is the open question on [KS-1374](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1374/akto-scans-are-now-paced-to-fit-the-platforms-rate-limit-test-times), which I did not update because it is In Progress.
* **Parity:** Akto's 57 `vulnerable:true` rows = 1 vulnerable + 56 known false positives (`COMMAND_INJECTION_WINDOWS`, 14 in each of 4 code-injection scans). HTTP 429 = 944 on all three surfaces when counted with Akto's own `TestRunStatusHelper` rule (last attempt, first 4xx/5xx code).
* **New guards:** `aktoPinMirrors.test.ts` covers both compose fallbacks and the three `.env.example` examples. The old guard read only the dashboard's fallback, and a stale testing fallback passed it. `aktoVersionNotTyped.test.ts` covers test metadata: no test may type an `aktoVersion`. It flagged `harReplaySurfaces` (2.36.4), `vulnerableCount` (2.9.9) and `reportGolden` (2.8.5); all three now read `PINNED_AKTO_VERSION`. Each guard was red first, then green.
* **Gates:** format:check, lint, knip, audit and check-test-ids are green. Unit tests: 105/105 files, 1,901/1,901 tests.

**Open, for Peter's decision:** (1) the [KS-1397](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1397/the-gateway-answers-every-request-with-server-nginx-aktos-unwanted) allowlist entry (harness side, [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-all-tools-security-regression-coverage)), so the security tier stops exiting 1 on an accepted finding; (2) ~~the missing-categories warning, untracked~~ now [KS-1416](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1416/akto-the-three-code-injection-sqli-scans-run-0-sqlnosql-templates-akto): the three "code injection (SQLi/…)" scans run 0 SQL/NoSQL templates, because Akto files them under NO_AUTH/VEM. Also raised: [KS-1417](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1417/dead-config-api-gateway-port6882-in-both-env-templates-is-read-by) (dead `API_GATEWAY_PORT`, Kamil).

title: 28 unguarded err.message values land in 500 response bodies across six services - no NODE_ENV guard in any of the six files
description:
**BLUF:** **28 handlers across six services put a thrown error's own message straight into a 500 response body, and none of the six files carries a** `NODE_ENV` **guard.** That is a production information leak. KS 1334 and KS 1341 are the same defect, already fixed per-file; this ticket covers the remaining six files as one pass.

Measured by me at develop `f01c1da5717fdcb80a5e1aeeaa8ff9f0f00edd80`. Instrument: a per-line regex `\b(?:err|error)\.message\b` for the message expression, then a separate check that the enclosing statement answers 500. Positive control: `originate/src/routes/webhooks.ts` at the same sha reads `NODE_ENV` **1** time, so a zero below is a measurement and not a broken reader.

## Sites, by file

`api-gateway/src/routes/notifications.ts` (blob `7945e1b01837`) — **6**: :126 :147 :176 :204 :234 :290
`api-gateway/src/routes/batch.ts` (blob `f2f48dca32e5`) — **3**: :166 :214 :262
`api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts` (blob `d87c04979e2b`) — **1**: :196
`transfer/src/routes/delegations.ts` (blob `33dd1f110f66`) — **1**: :283
`tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts` (blob `82a6f8d4b623`) — **7**: :311 (500 at :330) :353 :392 :422 :483 :544 :564
`mcp-server/src/http-server.ts` (blob `fce4a31793b3`) — **10**: nine `INTERNAL_ERROR` envelopes at :61 :76 :110 :169 :182 :192 :202 :212 :265, plus :134, which is a non-envelope 500 body (`res.status(500).json({ verified: false, error: message })`)

`NODE_ENV` **occurrences in all six files: 0.**

## Four more leaks that are NOT in a 500 and are NOT counted above

Listed so the count is not mistaken for the whole surface:

`api-gateway/src/routes/batch.ts:118` — returned into a per-item result inside a 200
`api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts:163` — a **502** body, `Failed to reach security service: ${err.message}`
`mcp-server/src/http-server.ts:104` and `:163` — pushed into a `results` array that is returned with 200

## UNMEASURED

* **Which errors actually reach these handlers in production.** Whether any carries a database string, a file path, an internal hostname or a credential fragment is not measured here, and settling it needs a running system, not a source read.
* No live reach. No request was issued against any of these routes.

## Why one ticket and not six

One test pass, one ticket. The per-file precedents (KS 1334 for adminConfig, KS 1341 for the webhooks routes) each closed a single file because each was found on its own; this set was found in one screening pass over the same class.

## Scope note on the neighbouring tickets, each read before filing

* KS 730 is the **guarded** remainder — its own wording is "71 response-side sites still return `err.message` verbatim **unless** `NODE_ENV === 'production'`". The sites above have **no** guard at all, so they are a different class and do not belong on it.
* KS 1346 is a **logging** defect (a non-Error throw logged as `[object Object]`), not a response-body leak.
* KS 1214 covers the mcp-server `POST /hash` route specifically, as an authentication defect; it overlaps one file here but not this class.

Searched before filing: all 522 open Secuura-PK issues, title and description, by exact substring on each of the six paths and on the message expression. Controls: a must-hit probe for the webhooks routes returned KS 1341, a must-hit probe for adminConfig returned KS 1334, and a deliberately absent string returned 0. No open ticket covers this set.

title: webhooks routes reject connector principals (userId connector:<id>) - 500 after KS 1345, silent 200 before
description:
**BLUF:** a caller authenticating with an API key becomes a **connector principal** whose `userId` is non-UUID (`connector:<connectorId>`), and the webhooks routes cast that value to `uuid`. `GET /api/webhooks` answered **200** `{webhooks: []}` for such a principal before KS 1345 and answers **500 INTERNAL_ERROR** after it. `POST /api/webhooks` already answered 500 for the same principals.

Filed from gate57 finding N-1381-1 (Minor) on PR 1381. Facts only; nothing here was measured live.

## The principal class, traced at source

Measured at `3ce8cd4026a6` by reading the source, with no live reach and no database read:

* the gateway sets the connector userId: `api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:301`
* it exchanges the key for an RS256 JWT minted with the same userId by `generateConnectorToken`: `auth/src/services/jwt.ts:289`
* originate's `authenticate()` accepts that token with no `type` check: `originate/src/middleware/auth.ts:82-104`
* the gateway mounts the webhooks routes behind the `webhooks:manage` scope: `api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:442-446`

So a key holding `webhooks:manage` reaches a `${userId}::uuid` cast carrying `connector:...`.

## Behaviour

* before KS 1345: **200** with an empty list, which is a silent wrong answer
* after KS 1345: **500**, logged as an error on every call
* create (`POST`, the `${userId}::uuid` cast in its INSERT, no catch) already answered 500 for these principals, so the list route is now consistent with create

## UNMEASURED

* whether any **issued** API key actually holds `webhooks:manage` — this needs a database read and was not done
* whether any other path mints a non-UUID userId
* live reach: the class was traced at source only

## The open question for the owner

A 500 for a principal-class condition is arguably a mis-mapping. It could reasonably be a 4xx, or the list could be keyed on the organisation rather than the user. That decision is the owner's and was explicitly out of scope for PR 1345, which replaced a silent wrong answer with a loud one.

Related: KS 1345 (the PR that flipped the status), KS 1341 (the same file's error-body work), KS 1256 (connector allow-list failing open — a different defect in the same principal class).

title: Bump systemTest schemathesis pin 4.28.0 → 4.29.3 (four releases: 4.29.0–4.29.3; BREAKING exit codes, per-operation seeding, negative cases break a random subset of locations)
description:
## BLUF

Upstream released **4.29.3 on 2026-10-05**. The pin on `develop` is `schemathesis==4.28.0` ([KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9), merged 2026-09-28), so the gap is **four releases: 4.29.0 (2026-10-02), 4.29.1, 4.29.2 (both 2026-10-04) and 4.29.3**. There is no 4.28.x patch release.

This is the behavioural bump [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) warned about ("The NEXT bump will be breaking"). 4.29.0 has **three BREAKING exit-code changes** that land directly on `run.py`'s verdict handling. It also has **per-operation seeding**, which changes what a fixed seed means for our before/after comparisons, and **negative cases now break a random subset of request locations**. 4.29.1–4.29.3 then rework `negative_data_rejection` in both directions: many false positives removed, several missed failures now caught. Expect our failing-pair counts to move both ways, so every vanished pair needs classifying as *not generated* vs *fixed*, never *passed*.

Count of entries (upstream `CHANGELOG.md`, quoted verbatim below):

| Release | Date | Added | Changed | Fixed | Performance |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 4.29.0 | 2026-10-02 | 7 | 12 (3 BREAKING) | 92 | 2 |
| 4.29.1 | 2026-10-04 | 2 | 0 | 44 | 0 |
| 4.29.2 | 2026-10-04 | 0 | 0 | 23 | 0 |
| 4.29.3 | 2026-10-05 | 0 | 0 | 3 | 0 |

## Where the pin lives (checked on `origin/develop`, 2026-10-05)

* `systemTest/schemathesis/pyproject.toml:99`: `"schemathesis==4.28.0"`
* `systemTest/schemathesis/constraints.txt:110`: `schemathesis==4.28.0`
* `systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis_tests.yaml` header, lines 2–3 (the tripwire pinned by `tests/unit/test_config_header_pin_parity.py`)

## Items most likely to move our results (to be measured, not asserted)

 1. **Exit codes (4.29.0, BREAKING):** `st run`/`st fuzz` exit **2 when nothing is tested** and **2 on schema, configuration and internal errors**. `st run`/`st fuzz`/`st replay` exit **130 on Ctrl+C**. Audit every place the runner maps an exit code to a verdict. A run that tested nothing must read INVALID, never green ([KS-684](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-684/schemathesis-4243-4251-bump-plus-harden-the-harness-against-the) / [KS-1270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1270/schemathesis-4273-ndjson-writer-thread-deadlocks-on-a-lazy-import) silent-truncation class).
 2. **Per-operation seeding (4.29.0):** *"Fuzzing and pytest seed each operation separately"*. A seed-fixed before/after taken across this bump compares different inputs. Take the **before** at 4.28.0 and the **after** at 4.29.3 knowing the seed no longer reproduces the same cases ([KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) note: the seed moves the op count).
 3. **Negative-case shape (4.29.0):** *"Negative test cases break a random subset of request locations instead of all of them"*, plus *"Linked stateful steps send negative requests as often as scenario-starting steps"*. Affects every `negative_data_rejection` count and the [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the) by-design tolerance scoping.
 4. `negative_data_rejection` **rework (4.29.0–4.29.3):** about 20 entries. False positives removed (repeated scalar query params, boolean spellings, omitted optional query params, empty `allowEmptyValue`, values that change during serialization, numeric path/query) and missed failures now caught (array/object query/header/cookie params, single-element arrays, numeric strings violating `minimum`). Cross-check against `schemathesis-baseline.json` ([KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing)) and the open per-endpoint tickets ([KS-1359](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1359/get-apiplatformaudit-log-accepts-wrong-type-and-out-of-range-query), [KS-1371](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1371/post-apistatusidunrevoke-accepts-index-1-below-the-declared-minimum)).
 5. **Rate limiting (4.29.1, 4.29.2):** no more false `unsupported_method` when a limiter answers an undeclared method with `429`, and `429` is no longer counted as rejected data in `low_valid_rate` (decided INFORMATIONAL in [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9)). Relevant to the gateway's rate limiter and the cooldown rule.
 6. **Stateful (4.29.0, 4.29.1, 4.29.2):** scenarios over 6 steps now run, `phases.stateful.max-steps = 50` no longer silently caps at 6, dependency inference widens (envelopes, `PUT` creators, `allOf`, form bodies), and unbounded memory growth on time-limited runs is fixed. Stateful op counts and duration will move.
 7. **Reports (4.29.0):** `--report json` `exit_code`/`stop_reason`/`errors` semantics fixed for aborted runs; Allure/JUnit status mapping corrected. Our HTML report and `baseline_gate` read these, so check the parsers.
 8. `ignored_auth` **(4.29.0):** stops probing once an op rejects missing and invalid credentials; false positives removed for redirects, cookie API keys and undeclared `Authorization`. Check the `ignored_auth` wording surface.
 9. **New** `--report wfc` (4.29.0): adds to the `--report` list, which is one of the six audit surfaces (was 6 at 4.28.0).
10. **Warnings:** `validation_mismatch` / `missing_test_data` / `missing_auth` no longer fire from undeclared-method or negative requests, and `missing_deserializer` now names media types. Re-run `TestAllInstalledWarningsAreAccountedFor` and confirm the registry count.

## Bump gate ([KS-1268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1268/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4271-4272-retargeted-from-4273-whose) / [KS-1285](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1285/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4272-4275-the-ks-1270-ndjson-hold-is) / [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) shape)

1. **Acceptance, the one-op NDJSON line-count check** ([KS-1270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1270/schemathesis-4273-ndjson-writer-thread-deadlocks-on-a-lazy-import)): `ScenarioFinished` count = console `Tested:`, `EngineFinished` present (`tests/functional/config/test_ndjson_completeness.py`, inside `quality`).
2. `setup` at the **old** pin (through `systemTest/run-in-slot.sh N`, on the slot Peter names) → **before** `full` sweep (fixed seed) → pin + WHY comment + yaml header + the two HTML docs → `update-deps` → `quality` → **after** `full` sweep → pair diff via `baseline_gate.extract_failure_pairs`. `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` exported on every run.
3. **Audit the six surfaces**: `--help` diff (54 flags at 4.28.0; 4.29.0 adds `st replay` flags), `--report` list (6 at 4.28.0, `wfc` new), check registry, phase list, warning registry (12 at 4.28.0), `ignored_auth` wording.
4. **Exit-code audit** (new for this bump): every runner path that reads Schemathesis's exit code, red→green tested for 2 (nothing tested), 2 (config/schema/internal error) and 130.
5. Fixed-seed stateful comparison, with the per-operation-seeding caveat recorded.
6. Pre-push preflight ([KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight)), `npm ci` in `Blockchain/Dev` first ([KS-691](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-691/pre-push-preflight-cannot-run-from-a-git-worktree-legs-1-and-6-fail)); point provisioned legs at the slot with `GATEWAY_URL`.
7. **Three-way parity (Peter, 2026-10-05): console output == Schemathesis results == HTML report.** For the after sweep, the console summary, Schemathesis's own results (NDJSON / `--report json`) and our HTML report must show the same numbers: operations tested, checks run, failures per check, warnings, errors, exit code / stop reason and verdict. Any mismatch is a defect to fix (red→green) before the bump is TESTED, not a caveat. It matters most here because 4.29.0 changes `exit_code` / `stop_reason` / `errors` in `--report json`, adds exit codes 2 and 130, and remaps Allure/JUnit statuses. Every one of those is a place where the three views can drift apart without anyone noticing.

## Working rules

Plan first against `CLAUDE.md`, `systemTest/CLAUDE.md`, the `secuura-test-discipline` and `peter-local-environment` skills and this ticket. Code comments carry the WHY + ticket number and state the prior behaviour. Honest results: no change may mask a failure, and every fix is proven red→green. One slot, the one Peter names. **No other organisation's issue/PR URL or** `owner/repo#N` **in any commit message, PR title or PR body**: refer to upstream in plain words.

---

## Full upstream changelog, 4.28.0 → 4.29.3 (verbatim from `CHANGELOG.md`)

### 4.29.3 (2026-10-05)

**🐛 Fixed**

* False `negative_data_rejection` failures for nested values sent as repeated scalar query parameters.
* False `negative_data_rejection` failures for boolean spellings such as `0`, `yes`, or `True`.
* False `negative_data_rejection` failures for omitted optional query parameters beside other serialized values.

### 4.29.2 (2026-10-04)

**🐛 Fixed**

* Crash in the coverage phase for large arrays of binary strings.
* Missing inferred links for paths with generic identifier parameters such as `{identifier}`.
* Missing inferred links for body fields returned under differently named response schemas.
* Positive cases violating negated Unicode property patterns such as `\p{L}`.
* `FutureWarning` printed to stderr for some schema `pattern` values.
* Broken shell quoting for truncated request bodies in generated `curl` commands.
* Display report write failures with the format, path, and operating-system error.
* Missing `anyOf` negative coverage cases when a referenced schema contains invalid keywords.
* Missing invalid-format coverage cases for Open API 3.1 `$ref` with sibling keywords.
* Request bodies dropped when referenced through a plain-name `$anchor` in Open API 3.1.
* Empty schema location in failures when a `$ref` points at a whole external file.
* Negative cases never breaking query or cookie parameters given explicit values differing in name case.
* Unsupported regex patterns inside `contains` reported as Hypothesis `Unsatisfiable`.
* Config errors for invalid HTTP method values show the section and the valid values.
* Raw `ValueError` for non-JSON values such as `datetime.date` in schemas passed to `from_dict`.
* False `negative_data_rejection` failures for empty query values of parameters with `allowEmptyValue: true`.
* False `negative_data_rejection` failures for query values that become valid or disappear during serialization.
* Formatted schema errors for invalid SSE `itemSchema` definitions in response validation.
* `phases.stateful.max-steps = 50` silently capping scenarios at 6 steps.
* Report the document URL when a fragment is missing in a remote `$ref` document.
* Crash fetching a dynamic token when the client certificate file does not exist.
* Rate-limited (`429`) responses counted as rejected data in the `low_valid_rate` warning.
* Report `409` responses as conflicts, not rejected data, in the `low_valid_rate` warning. (upstream issue 4932)

### 4.29.1 (2026-10-04)

**🚀 Added**

* Dependency inference unwraps `result` / `data` envelopes that carry metadata such as `status` or `time`.
* Dependency inference treats `PUT /items/{name}` as the creator when nothing `POST`s to `/items`.

**🐛 Fixed**

*CLI*

* Return exit code 2 for run-wide configuration errors.
* Report custom handler startup errors with a clean message.
* Stateful worker hangs after Ctrl-C from custom handlers.

*pytest plugin*

* Keep reports separate for identical schemas with different report configurations.
* Reports including results from an identical schema that did not configure reports.

*Python API*

* `ImportError` on `from schemathesis.checks import content_type_conformance` (and other built-in checks) before schema loaded.
* `schemathesis.check` return type: decorated functions and classes keep their own type.
* `base_url` passed to `Case.call` ignored for WSGI applications.

*Stateful testing*

* Memory growing without bound during long runs with a time limit.
* Crash in dependency inference for Open API 3.1 references to boolean schemas.
* Crash in dependency inference for Open API 3.1 boolean schemas inside `anyOf` and `oneOf`.
* Crash in dependency inference for response references targeting non-object values.
* Inferred links reading foreign keys from responses that do not declare them.

*Data generation*

* Hanging, or failing a health check, on arrays with a large `minItems`.
* Crash while processing patterns beside string length bounds too large for regex engines.
* "Failed Health Check" in negative mode for string path parameters carrying keywords of other types.
* Missing negative multipart bodies for binary fields with multiple content types.
* Preserve case-sensitive cookie parameter names.
* Dictionary bindings on body paths ignored through recursive `$ref` schemas.

*Coverage phase*

* Hanging on unique arrays with a large `minItems`.
* Crashes and invalid positive cases from YAML binary keyword values.
* Invalid positive cases for large arrays and objects beside `prefixItems`, `if`, or `unevaluatedProperties`.
* Missing positive cases for satisfiable numeric `multipleOf` schemas with large bounds.

*Request serialization*

* Send binary Open API 3.2 `querystring` parameters as percent-encoded raw queries.
* Captured array path parameters ignoring their declared Open API style.

*Schema handling*

* Report malformed Open API `servers` definitions as clean loading errors.
* Report infinite recursive and unresolvable references as clean errors.
* Report empty or non-object Open API parameter `content` as a clean error.
* Stalls of up to 30s per document carrying an unreachable `$schema` URL.

`negative_data_rejection`

* False positive when path and query numeric values are both valid on the wire.
* Missed failures for invalid single-element arrays in query, header or cookie parameters.
* Missed failures for invalid array or object query, header and cookie parameters.
* Missed failures when an array parameter with a valid element accompanies invalid ones.
* Missed failures for invalid path parameters beside undeclared query parameters.
* Missed failures for numeric strings violating `minimum` or other bounds.

*Others*

* False `unsupported_method` failures when a rate limiter answers an undeclared method with `429`.
* `checks.enabled = false` not disabling custom checks.
* Report undecodable JSON response bodies as JSON parsing errors.
* Missing closing delimiter in reproduce cURL commands for empty multipart bodies.

### 4.29.0 (2026-10-02)

**🚀 Added**

* WFC Report output via `--report wfc` or `--report-wfc-path`.
* Dependency inference links body fields named after a collection to its items' `code`.
* `st replay` options `-H`/`--header`, `--auth`, `--auth-wfc` and `--auth-wfc-user` for replayed requests.
* Coverage Content-Type probes for malformed multipart and undeclared request media types.
* `format: binary` values include small valid PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, PDF and ZIP files.
* Multipart file names carry the extension of the detected file format, e.g. `image.png`.
* `use_after_free` and `ensure_resource_availability` failures note responses served from a cache.

**🔧 Changed**

* Negative test cases break a random subset of request locations instead of all of them.
* Name the pattern that stops the analysis when test data cannot be generated.
* **BREAKING**: `st run` and `st fuzz` fail with exit code 2 when nothing is tested.
* **BREAKING**: `st run` and `st fuzz` exit 2 on schema, configuration and internal errors.
* **BREAKING**: `st run`, `st fuzz` and `st replay` exit 130 when interrupted with Ctrl+C.
* Linked stateful steps send negative requests as often as scenario-starting steps.
* `st replay` step chains show each linked value as `recorded -> replayed`.
* `st replay` removes fixed crash files with masked credentials once config or CLI supplies them.
* Fuzzing and pytest seed each operation separately, so operations with identical parameters explore different inputs.
* Stateful testing targets only metrics from `generation.maximize` or explicit `hypothesis.target()` calls.
* `ignored_auth` stops probing an operation once it rejects missing and invalid credentials.
* `missing_deserializer` warning names the response media types that go unvalidated.

**🐛 Fixed**

`st run` *and* `st fuzz`

* Fuzzing phase dropping data generation errors when several distinct errors occur.
* `st fuzz --help` omitting that fuzzing stops at the first failure without `--continue-on-failure`.
* `st fuzz` omitting schema errors of individual operations.
* `st fuzz` workers continuing after the first failure and reporting `Stop reason: Completed`.
* `Stop reason: Time limit reached` for runs stopped by a failure shortly before the deadline.
* `continue-on-failure` in the config file ignored.
* WFC auth skipping users in the coverage phase and settling operations on the wrong one.
* WFC auth never retrying users rejected before the API created their accounts.
* Crash when writing a baseline file into a directory that does not exist.
* Raw traceback for unreadable or malformed baseline files.
* Python spelling in config type errors, e.g. `bool: True` instead of `boolean: true`.
* Crash on TOML dates and times in the config file.

`st replay`

* Ignoring auth providers and `[auth.openapi]` credentials, resending masked values instead.
* Reporting a crash as fixed when its credentials were missing or rejected.
* Deleting fixed crash files that sent a masked request body value.
* Reproduce commands for stateful chains using stale recorded IDs.
* Flagging stateful steps as changed when only re-extracted IDs differ.
* Resending stale `User-Agent` and test case ID headers, or dropping `-H` headers.

*Reports*

* Schemathesis check failures marked as broken instead of failed in allure-pytest.
* Wrong Allure status for pytest errors (broken) and skips (skipped).
* Duplicate pytest Allure results for the same operation.
* pytest errors and skips marked as passed in JUnit.
* `from_fixture` tests missing from pytest Allure and JUnit results.
* Operations with schema errors missing from pytest Allure and JUnit results.
* Missing `epic` label with the API title in CLI Allure results.
* `exit_code` of `0` in `--report json` for runs aborted by a fatal error.
* `stop_reason` of `interrupted` and empty `errors` in `--report json` for runs aborted by an error.

*Hooks*

* Raw traceback and exit code 1 for errors in `before_load_schema` and `after_load_schema`.
* Keep schema example values that data generation hooks change in the examples phase.
* Apply test-scoped `filter_case` and `map_case` in the pytest coverage phase.
* Call test-scoped `after_validate`.
* Apply `apply_to` and `skip_for` filters on hooks registered by name, e.g. `hook("before_call")`.

*Stateful testing*

* Scenarios with more than 6 steps running rarely or failing with `Unsatisfiable`.
* Dependency inference ignoring `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `multipart/form-data` and `formData` request bodies.
* Inferred links with `*` wildcards never filling request body fields.
* Inferred links passing names as identifiers, parent names to new resources, or scalars to arrays.
* Keep operations in dependency inference when a response has an unresolvable `$ref`.
* Missing inferred links for path parameters named after a resource field, e.g. `/projects/{code}`.
* Inferred links reading response fields the schema does not define.
* Missing inferred links for fields and nested foreign keys inherited through `allOf`.
* Crash when a link fills the body of an operation accepting `*/*`.

*Data generation*

* Keywords next to a root `$ref` applied in Open API 3.0 and Swagger 2.0 schemas.
* Coverage phase sending positive custom media type bodies in negative-only mode.
* Coverage phase missing positive cases for multipart bodies with custom-encoded properties.
* Negative test data unsatisfiable for operations with plain string headers, such as FastAPI's `Header(None)`.
* Open API 3.1 `$ref` siblings dropped when the target defines the same keyword.
* Coverage phase crash on malformed `contains` keywords in Open API 3.0 schemas.
* `format: binary` strings ignoring `minLength` and `maxLength`.
* Crash instead of a schema error on malformed keywords like `minLength: "x"`.
* `--generation-unique-inputs` treating inputs that differ only in sensitive parameter values as duplicates.
* Coverage phase skipping negative cases for optional parameter combinations under `--mode negative`.
* Integer path parameters violating `enum`, `multipleOf` or `not` in positive test cases.
* Coverage phase ignoring captured identifiers for request body properties defined via `$ref`.
* False positive `negative_data_rejection` in coverage phase for parameters with unanchored `pattern` and `maxLength`.
* Coverage phase generating different values for an operation depending on how many operations were loaded before it.
* Fuzz dictionary bindings overridden by path, query or header values captured from earlier responses.

*Request serialization*

* Multipart parts for arrays of primitives labelled `application/json` while carrying raw text.
* Booleans and nulls sent as `True`/`False`/`None` in `label`, `matrix` and object-style parameters.
* Parameter styles ignored for Open API 3.1 `type` lists and implicit object or array schemas.
* Nested objects and `encoding` styles ignored in `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` bodies.
* Coverage phase stringifying nested values of JSON-encoded `content` parameters.
* Coverage phase sending a declared `Content-Type` header that names another body media type.
* Percent-encoded delimiters, missing names and dropped falsy values in `matrix`/`label`/`simple` path parameters.
* Examples and fuzzing phases sending a declared `Content-Type` header that names another media type.
* Missing multipart `boundary` when `Content-Type: multipart/form-data` is set explicitly.

*Unsatisfiable schema messages*

* Property names holding `/` or `~` printed unescaped.
* Plural `1 more branches` for a single branch.
* Name the `prefixItems` element that admits no value.
* Name conflicting keywords inside `$ref` branches of a `oneOf`.

*False positives*

* `ignored_auth` when unauthenticated requests redirect to a sign-in page.
* `ignored_auth` when an API-key cookie is passed via the `Cookie` header.
* `ignored_auth` when credentials are passed in an `Authorization` header the schema does not declare.
* `negative_data_rejection` for numeric array path parameters sent as a single number.
* `negative_data_rejection` for multipart bodies with `--generation-unique-inputs`.
* `negative_data_rejection` for string parameters declared as `anyOf`/`oneOf` with a `false` branch.
* `validation_mismatch`, `missing_test_data` and `missing_auth` warnings from undeclared-method requests.
* `validation_mismatch` and `missing_test_data` warnings from negative test cases.
* `negative_data_rejection` for repeated string query parameters whose every value is valid.
* `negative_data_rejection` for request bodies referencing a schema of a newer draft.

*Others*

* Memory exhaustion from large `workers` values; reject values below 1.
* Crash files lost when a negative mutation stored a `bytes` value.
* Wrong or crashing request URLs for GraphQL schemas loaded from files or dictionaries.
* Crash on non-string property names from YAML 1.1 parsers, e.g. `on:`, passed to `from_dict`.
* Network errors when a server closes a keep-alive connection without `Connection: close`.
* Raw or misleading config errors for wrong value types, duplicate list items and non-string choices.
* Broken `curl` reproduction commands for request data with C1 control or Unicode line-separator characters.
* `curl` reproduction commands sending wrong bytes in fish, or `\$` for `$` in bash.
* Equal `Case` objects hashing differently when header names differ only in case.
* Oversized `curl` reproduction commands for non-ASCII request data.

**🏎️ Performance**

* Coverage phase \~1.6x faster on schemas with many `enum` or `const` positions.
* Coverage phase \~4x faster on recursive request bodies with `maxItems`.

## Related

[KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) (→ 4.28.0; flagged this bump as breaking) · [KS-1285](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1285/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4272-4275-the-ks-1270-ndjson-hold-is) (→ 4.27.5) · [KS-1268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1268/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4271-4272-retargeted-from-4273-whose) (bump ritual shape) · [KS-1270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1270/schemathesis-4273-ndjson-writer-thread-deadlocks-on-a-lazy-import) / [KS-1271](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1271/systemtest-guards-after-ks-1268ks-1270-ndjson-completeness-gate-writer) (NDJSON completeness gate) · [KS-684](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-684/schemathesis-4243-4251-bump-plus-harden-the-harness-against-the) (warnings guard) · [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the) (`negative_data_rejection` by-design tolerance) · [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing) (baseline lags the registers) · [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) (stateful links / seed)
