title: a password change or reset leaves the account's other sessions live
description:
## BLUF

A successful password change does not revoke the account's other sessions, and neither does the reset
flow. Raised from gate59's review of PR #1382 (KS 1005). **Pre-existing — not introduced by that PR.**

## N-1382-1 — no session revocation on a successful password change

A successful change makes **zero** `revokeAllUserSessions` calls. The reset flow does not revoke
either. So after a password change — including a change prompted by suspected compromise — every
other authenticated session on that account stays live.

Scope of the evidence, stated so it is not over-read: this was **measured on mocked calls only**, not
against a running stack. The count of zero is a count of calls the handler makes, not a live
observation of a surviving session.

## N-1382-2 — the e2e test for this can never fail

- [ ] Fix the e2e case so it can fail. Case 12.5.3, "other sessions should be invalidated", POSTs to
      `/api/auth/change-password` — **a route that does not exist** — and asserts only inside
      `if (status === 200)`. Because the request cannot return 200, the assertion body never runs, so
      the test passes unconditionally. It has therefore never tested the behaviour in N-1382-1, and
      the correct route is the one KS 1005 fixes.

## Adjacent, and deliberately not merged into this ticket

KS 257 ("Session revocation only enforced at the auth service") is adjacent but different — it is
about *where* revocation is enforced, not *whether* a password change triggers it — and it is
archived. Noted here so the connection is not lost.

title: Cross-tenant guard fails open for tenantless tokens (connector on /lookup and /stub; access tokens likewise)
description:
## BLUF

**The cross-tenant 404 on** `GET /api/users/lookup` **and** `POST /api/users/stub` **is skipped entirely when the caller's token carries no tenant claim.** Filed from gate54a's finding **N-1374-1** on PR #1374 (KS-1402). **Not reachable through the token exchange today** — read in the code, the exchange always issues a tenant claim — so this is a latent fail-open, not a live hole. It is filed so the guard's shape is fixed rather than left depending on a property of a different component.

## What the gate measured

* **P5: 200 at the head.** A token with no tenant claim reaches the handler and the cross-tenant branch does not fire.
* **P5b: 200 at the base too.** So this is **not a regression introduced by PR #1374** — the behaviour predates it. PR #1374 only widens which token *types* reach the route; it does not change the tenant guard.
* The guard lives at `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:759`, and it has applied to `POST /api/users/stub` since **KS 564**. `GET /api/users/lookup` joins it with PR #1374.
* **Access tokens are in scope too**, not just connector tokens: the guard keys on the presence of a tenant on the caller, not on the token type.

## Why it is not reachable today

The token exchange always issues a tenant claim. That was established **by reading the exchange code, not by exercising it** — so "unreachable" is a code reading, and a change to the exchange (or any other issuer, including a test-only or future path) could make it reachable without anything here changing.

## Fix shape

**Fail closed when the caller has no tenant**: refuse rather than fall through to the unscoped read. The route-level 404-not-200-empty convention should be preserved, so a tenantless caller gets the same 404 a cross-tenant caller gets, and the absence of a tenant is never the thing that widens a read.

## Provenance

* gate54a on PR #1374, finding N-1374-1. Report: `2026-10-05-ks1402-1374-g54a/report.md`.
* Duplicate search before filing (all 571 KS issues, title + description, searched locally): `tenantless` **0 hits**; `cross-tenant` 22; `fails open` 8; `no tenant claim` 1. Must-hit controls `connector` **86** and `tenantId` **24**, impossible-token control `zzqqxx` **0** — so the 0 is a measurement. The two closest neighbours were read and are **different mechanisms**: KS-1091 is an `x-tenant-id` header honoured on originate's direct path; KS-1119 is a `crossTenantLookup` hash fallback in verification.
* **Who builds this is not decided here.**

title: A Blockchain/Testing run drops an untracked schemathesis.json in the repo root, and it is not gitignored
description:
**BLUF:** running any `Blockchain/Testing` entry point from the repo root leaves an untracked
`Blockchain/Testing/schemathesis.json` behind. It is not covered by any `.gitignore`, so the next
`git add -A` stages a run artefact. Caught during KS-1382 when `git add -A` staged it into a PR.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Testing/ci/tools/run-schemathesis.sh` — it writes
`$FINDINGS_DIR/schemathesis.json`, and `FINDINGS_DIR` defaults to `.` in the same file. Run from the
repo root, `.` is the repo root.

**Reproduce:**

1. From a clean worktree, run anything that reaches the Schemathesis wrapper (the KS-1382 harness
   drives it under stubs, which is enough — no live target needed).
2. `git status --porcelain` shows `?? Blockchain/Testing/schemathesis.json`.
3. `git check-ignore -q Blockchain/Testing/schemathesis.json` exits non-zero: not ignored.
4. `git add -A` stages it.

**Observed content:** `[]` — the wrapper's empty-findings fallback, i.e. pure run output with no
source value.

**Why it matters:** a staged run artefact is the kind of thing that reaches a PR unnoticed. It did
not reach one here only because the staged file list was read line by line before committing.

**Measured on the board before filing** (team Secuura-PK, exact-substring filters, not the fuzzy
search): description contains `Testing/schemathesis.json` → 0; title contains `schemathesis.json`
→ 0; description contains `not gitignored` → 0; description contains `FINDINGS_DIR defaults` → 0.
Must-hit control, description contains `stack_env.sh` → 5, so the filter is not blind.

**Suggested fix (not prescribed):** either add the artefact path to `.gitignore`, or default
`FINDINGS_DIR` to a run directory outside the tracked tree. Whoever picks it up should decide which,
since `FINDINGS_DIR` is also passed in explicitly by the orchestrator.

Filed by the Platform K board account during the KS-1382 round, unassigned. Not fixed in that PR:
the artefact was unstaged and deleted, and nothing in KS-1382 changes `FINDINGS_DIR`.

title: Timestamping accepts an UNSIGNED timestamp token as valid: verifyRealToken verifies no signature
description:
**BLUF:** `verifyTimestamp` returns `valid: true` with `isQualified: true` for a token whose signature was never checked. Any blob whose ASN.1 contains the expected hash as an OCTET STRING plus a GeneralizedTime passes. Kam ruled on 2026-10-04 that this is filed and fixed in a seat with red-first tests.

## What the code does

Instrument: source read of `services/timestamping/src/tsa/qualified-tsa.ts:365-456` at develop `88e8877a2a0d`, line by line.

`verifyRealToken(tokenDer, expectedHash)`:

1. parses the DER with `forge.asn1.fromDer`
2. walks the tree to depth 30 looking for an OCTET STRING byte-equal to the expected hash, setting `foundHashMatch`
3. takes the first GENERALIZEDTIME as `genTime`
4. optionally reads signer certificate fields via `forge.pkcs7.messageFromAsn1`, inside a `try/catch` whose own comment reads *"Certificate extraction is optional — token can still be valid"*
5. returns `valid: true` if `foundHashMatch`, with `tsaCertificate.isQualified` set to the literal `true`

There is **no** `publicKey.verify` and no `forge.pki.rsa` verification in either TSA file. `rfc3161-client.ts` matches `verify` **zero** times (instrument: grep; control: `forge.` matches 40+ lines in the same file, so the grep reads).

## Why it matters

The hash-presence test proves the blob **contains** the hash. It does not prove a TSA ever signed it, that the signature is valid, that the certificate chains to a trusted root, or that the certificate was valid at `genTime`. `isQualified: true` is asserted rather than established.

## Not covered / unmeasured

* **Unmeasured at runtime.** This is a source reading. No forged token was constructed and submitted, and no running timestamping service was exercised.
* Whether any caller treats `valid: true` as a compliance assertion is unmeasured.
* Whether this is deliberate for demo purposes is a product question, not a measurement.

## Relationship to the advisory freeze

`node-forge` 1.4.0 carries GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv, a HIGH integrity flaw in **RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification** with no upstream fix. We are outside its reach only because we never call that operation — the same gap this ticket is about. Kam's ruling on the freeze card states node-forge is removed from timestamping **in this rework**, and carries a baseline row until it lands.

## Kam's ruling, 2026-10-04 21:05:17 AEDT (card secuura-tsa-accepts-unsigned-tokens-1004 = a)

"File a High ticket on our board, fix in a seat with red-first tests."

## Suggested fix shape (not implemented here)

Real RFC 3161 verification: verify the SignedData signature over TSTInfo against the signer certificate, chain that certificate to a configured trust anchor, check validity at `genTime`, and compare the message imprint from the parsed TSTInfo rather than from a tree-wide search. Removing `node-forge` in favour of a maintained ASN.1/CMS path retires the advisory as a side effect.

title: Three range-widened HIGH advisories freeze every push; two have no upstream fix
description:
**BLUF:** every push on this repo is refused by the pre-push preflight on legs 6 and 7. Three HIGH advisories are reported and not baselined. **Two of the three have no upstream fix in existence.** Kam ruled option (b) on 2026-10-04.

## The refusal

Measured on a real push attempt (Seat B 55th, 2026-10-04 08:49:12 to 08:56:04Z, push rc 1, no `--no-verify`): `PREFLIGHT FAILED on leg(s) 6 7 - fix the above before pushing. (12/15 legs ran)`. The other 10 legs that ran were clean; 3 skipped for "local stack not up". Nothing reached origin.

| advisory | package | pinned | locks |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm | braces | 3.0.3 | 11 standalone + workspace root |
| GHSA-ch52-4w7c-c8xp | http-cache-semantics | 4.2.0 | services/anchoring, services/nft-certificate |
| GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv | node-forge | 1.4.0 | services/timestamping |

## The mechanism is a RANGE WIDENING, not a new publication

Instrument: GitHub advisory API, read 2026-10-04.

* GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm published 2026-09-18T18:31:41, **updated 2026-10-02T22:36:34**
* GHSA-ch52-4w7c-c8xp published 2026-09-18T18:31:44, **updated 2026-10-02T22:36:44**
* GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv published 2026-09-03T21:31:15, **updated 2026-10-01T21:09:10**

All three were published weeks ago. All three were updated **after** the last green push (2026-10-01 \~16:0xZ, whose preflight ran these same two legs and reported "Nothing failed"). The pinned versions never moved; the advisories' affected ranges moved onto them. A repo nobody touched for 2 d 19 h froze itself.

## Two of the three cannot be fixed by any bump

Each affected range is `<=` exactly the version we pin, and each has `first_patched_version: none` (advisory API). Cross-checked against the npm registry:

* braces: latest published **is** 3.0.3 — no newer version exists
* node-forge: latest published **is** 1.4.0 — no newer version exists
* http-cache-semantics: latest **4.3.0**, which is outside `<= 4.2.0`

## Shipped exposure is FOUR paths, not fourteen

Instrument: lockfile `dev` / `devOptional` flags read from develop `88e8877a2a0d`, plus each service Dockerfile. Control: `express` in services/api-gateway reads PROD.

* braces is **DEV in 10 of 11 locks** and PROD in exactly one, services/api-gateway
* http-cache-semantics is PROD in both anchoring and nft-certificate
* node-forge is PROD in services/timestamping

Every runtime stage omits dev (api-gateway, anchoring and timestamping all `npm ci --omit=dev`; nft-certificate builds with dev then `npm prune --omit=dev` and the runner copies that tree). So the ten dev-only braces locks do not ship it.

## Reachability of the vulnerable code

Instrument: `git grep` over product code at `88e8877a2a0d`. Control: the same grep shape finds `from 'express'` in 326 files, so a zero is a reading.

* braces (CWE-674, availability): **0 direct callers**
* http-cache-semantics (CWE-524, confidentiality): **0 direct callers**; transitive, declared by `cacheable-request`
* node-forge (CWE-347, integrity, forged RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signatures): not transitive. `services/timestamping` declares `"node-forge": "^1.3.3"` and imports it at `src/tsa/qualified-tsa.ts:18` and `src/tsa/rfc3161-client.ts:12`. **The vulnerable operation is not invoked:** `verifyRealToken` performs no signature verification, and `rfc3161-client.ts` matches `verify` zero times. That is tracked separately — see the timestamping ticket.

## Kam's ruling, 2026-10-04 21:05:25 AEDT (card secuura-freeze5-high-no-fix-1004 = b)

"Fix what can be fixed, remove node-forge, accept only braces". Card option text, verbatim: *"One T1 PR: the http-cache-semantics refresh + a braces baseline row (reason, ticket, expiry no later than 31 Oct). node-forge gets removed from timestamping in the same rework the separate unsigned-token card needs; until that lands it carries a baseline row with the same expiry."*

## The fix, as ruled

1. http-cache-semantics: in-range lock refresh on services/anchoring and services/nft-certificate only, 4.2.0 to 4.3.0, **no manifest change needed** — `cacheable-request` declares `^4.0.0`. Dry resolution in scratch copies of the base manifests and locks moved exactly 1 entry per lock, 0 added, 0 removed, and npm then reported `found 0 vulnerabilities`. Contrast control: the same command for braces, whose latest is our pin, moves the lock not at all. **These are host-npm figures; the Docker daemon was down, so the containerised cleanroom re-take is outstanding.**
2. A baseline row for braces, reason and expiry per the ruling.
3. A baseline row for node-forge, with removal tracked on the timestamping ticket.

## Not covered

No containerised cleanroom re-take (Docker not running). Whether an attacker-controlled input can reach a brace pattern in api-gateway is **unmeasured**. The 15 baseline rows the same leg reports as no longer reported are out of scope here.

title: auth GET /api/users/lookup refuses connector tokens, so every Platform-S transfer-custody 401s and falls back to a flat anchor — KS-739's users:read ruling cannot take effect
description:
## BLUF

**No Platform-S rights-assign or rights-reassign reaches** `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` **successfully.** originate resolves `newHolderEmail` by calling auth's `GET /api/users/lookup` with the **caller's** `Authorization` header, and `/lookup` accepts only access tokens (`authenticate()`). Platform-S authenticates per Organisation with a **connector** token, so auth answers 401 *"Invalid token"*, originate passes it through ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)'s 4xx rule), and S degrades to a flat `/api/anchors` anchor. No `custody_events` row is written and `documents.owner_user_id` never moves.

[KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) (Done, archived) ruled 2026-09-02 that *"Platform S provisions* `users:read` *on its connector key; K does not widen* `ALLOWED_LOOKUP_ROLES`*"*. That ruling cannot take effect: the scope check sits behind an authenticator that rejects the token type before any scope is read. A missing scope would answer **403**; what S receives is **401 Invalid token**.

## Code (platform-k `develop` `0736d8b78`)

* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1665-1671` — email-only path: `fetch(${AUTH_SERVICE_URL}/api/users/lookup?email=…, { headers: { Authorization: <caller's header> } })`.
* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1708-1730` — a 4xx from the lookup is passed through; 401 → *"The credential on this request was rejected by the user lookup. Re-authenticate and retry."* ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)).
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:266` — `userRoutes.get('/lookup', authenticate(), …)` — access tokens only.
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:357-359` — "[KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) *(Option A): this ONE route also accepts a connector token — see authenticateAccessOrConnector. Every other route keeps plain authenticate()."* — `/stub` was widened; `/lookup` was not.
* Platform-S side: `ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs` `TransferCustodyAsync` sends `{ newHolderEmail, reason }` + `onBehalfOf` with `Authorization: Bearer <connector access token>` (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:1527`).

## Measured — local pair, slot 3, 2026-10-01

platform-s `f370236c` (+ [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) systemTest changes only) ↔ platform-k `0736d8b78`, fresh databases, 33/33 K containers up, `/health/deep` 200, S provisioning key accepted, 10/0/0 organisations registered.

**4 of 4** transfer-custody calls refused, identical body, under Organisation 3's connector key:

```
transfer-custody status=401 body={"success":false,"error":{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"The credential on this request was rejected by the user lookup. Re-authenticate and retry. Upstream said: Invalid token"}} … using /api/anchors fallback.
```

* 09:21:55Z — 2 calls ([PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914)'s date-sort seed: two documents delegated to a same-org colleague).
* 09:22:55–09:31:06Z — 2 calls during `npm run test:k-live` (`verb_matrix.spec.ts` rights-assign + rights-reassign on K document `7af2374a-dd61-47e7-be50-122dcb5e412b`).

In the same window, Organisation 3's connector token **succeeded** on `originate` (201) and on lifecycle events (`rights-unassign`, `delete`) — so the key is valid; only the auth-service lookup refuses it.

## Why nothing went red

The platform-s `@k-live` cell "rights-assign and rights-unassign each reach K" asserted only that the S edge carries an anchor K resolves as not-failed — which the flat fallback also satisfies. It passed (17 passed / 1 skipped) while both custody calls 401'd. [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) tightens that cell to assert the custody transfer K records — `GET /api/documents/{id}` `owner.id` must move off its pre-assign value (measured: it reads `""` before and after today's refused transfers). The cell is **red until this ticket ships**, deliberately, and turns green once K records the transfer. Platform-S's `TransferCustodyAsync` carries a comment naming this ticket.

## Options (Kamil's call — no K code changed)

1. **Widen** `/lookup` **to** `authenticateAccessOrConnector()`, as [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) did for `/stub` — makes [KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)'s `users:read` ruling effective (the connector key then needs that scope).
2. **originate resolves the holder with its own service credential**, not the caller's header — removes the dependency on the caller's token type.
3. **Platform-S sends** `newHolderId` — requires S to know the K user id of the recipient (S-side; it does not today).

Whichever is chosen, a recipient with no K account still gets the typed 404 `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) measurement A) — worth confirming the S holder exists in K once the 401 is gone.

## Related

[KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) (Done, archived — ruling this ticket shows cannot take effect) · [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) (Option A connector scoping) · [PS-681](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-681/systemtest-k-live-every-share-and-rights-verb-times-out-waiting-for) (Done — Stuart's original 502 report) · [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) (platform-s: the k-live cell that hid this).

title: charge_events has RLS off entirely on the kintsugi database (already past 039), and 8 rows are in it — a redeploy cannot fix it
description:
## BLUF

**On a database that recorded** `039_rls_fail_closed.sql` **before** `charge_events` **existed, that table ends with row-level security not enabled at all — no RLS, no FORCE, no policy — and a redeploy cannot change it.** Measured on the kintsugi database, which holds **8 rows** in that table. Both migration runners skip any file already recorded, so 039's edits are inert there, and `038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` only helps a database whose 039 has not yet run. This ticket does not write the fix; "What done means" below states the constraints it must meet.

## Measured

Read on the kintsugi main database before and after the 2026-09-30 deploy, identical both times:

| table | exists | rows | RLS enabled | RLS forced | policies |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| charge_events | yes | **8** | **false** | **false** | **0** |
| certifications | yes | 0 | true | true | 0 |
| oauth_apps | yes | 0 | true | true | 2 |
| svc_webhooks | yes | 0 | true | true | 1 |

Controls: both readings showed `users` with RLS enabled and 2 policies, and a policy name that does not exist returning 0; the after-deploy reading also showed `to_regclass` on a table that does not exist returning false. So the zeros above are readings, not a blind query.

`charge_events` **is the row of that table with no ticket.** It is also the only one of the four holding data.

## Why a deploy does not fix it

* Both runners skip a migration already recorded in `_secuura_migrations`: `scripts/run-migrations.sh:118-122`, and api-gateway's startup stage at `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts:137-141`, which reads `SELECT 1 FROM _secuura_migrations WHERE filename = $1 LIMIT 1` and `continue`s when a row comes back. Both were read at `91a8f6b721bc`.
* `039_rls_fail_closed.sql` has listed `charge_events` since KS 458. It skips any listed table that does not exist yet, or that has no `tenant_id` column. Nothing that runs later enables RLS on `charge_events`: no migration numbered after 039 names it, and the startup stage's RLS loop does not list it.
* `038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` creates these tables **before** 039 runs, so on a fresh database 039 gives `charge_events`, `oauth_apps` and `svc_webhooks` their policies on the first boot (`certifications` is the exception recorded in KS-1376). On this database, 038a ran on 2026-09-30 **after** 039 was already recorded; its only effect there was one tracker row, the four tables already existing.
* So 038a cannot help a database where 039 has already run, and editing 039 itself reaches nothing — the edit to it inside the deployed range was inert on this box for exactly that reason.

**Unmeasured:** why `charge_events` was skipped when this database first ran 039. The consistent reading is that it did not exist yet, as 038a's own header describes for a bare database, but the original run's log was not read, and whether the table had a `tenant_id` column at that moment was not read.

## Relationship to the existing tickets — read before filing

* **KS-1376** covers `certifications` ending RLS FORCE with no `tenant_isolation` policy, and its fix shape is *"a migration numbered after 039 that applies 039's* `tenant_isolation` *block to* `certifications`*"*. A migration numbered after 039 is unrecorded on **every** database, including ones already past 039 — so that fix, once written, should reach the `certifications` row above as well; confirm it on an already-migrated database when it lands. The `certifications` half is therefore not re-filed here.
* **KS-1054** covers fresh databases being fail-open until the second boot, addressed by Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1332 (merged).
* **KS-1055** covers per-tenant databases never receiving the file migrations.
* **What none of them states** is the case this ticket is for: `charge_events` **on an already-migrated database, with RLS never enabled and rows already present.** Searched team KS with `includeArchived`, on title and description, by `charge_events` (7 hits, none about RLS), `039_rls_fail_closed` (6), `relforcerowsecurity` (1, KS 959, which is KS 597's org-context fallback and cites forced RLS only to explain why a zero row-count needs a control), `certifications` (50, paginated) and `tenant_isolation` (20). Positive control `migration` returned 50, so the query shape works.

## Other environments

* A fresh database from `91a8f6b721bc`: when #1332 was reviewed, `charge_events` was measured with RLS enabled and forced and one fail-closed `tenant_isolation` policy on all three bare-database paths, and 038a, 039 and both runners are unchanged since. Not re-measured here.
* **demo: unmeasured.** The instrument that closes it is the same read-only catalog query — `pg_class.relrowsecurity` and `relforcerowsecurity`, the `pg_policies` count, the row count — against demo's main database.
* Any other database created before #1332 and already past 039: unmeasured.

## What done means

1. On every already-migrated database this applies to, `charge_events` has RLS enabled and forced with the `tenant_isolation` policy 039 defines, shown by the same catalog read before and after.
2. It is delivered by a path an existing database actually runs on deploy — a migration numbered after 039 — not by editing a recorded file.
3. A regression check that is red on a database where 039 was recorded before `charge_events` existed, and green after. Driven as the application role, not as a source-text assertion: the failure mode here is a runtime one, and only a driven probe separates "policy present" from "table reachable because the reader owns it".
4. The **8 existing rows stay readable to their own tenant** after the change, tested rather than assumed. This is the part that makes the change riskier than the `certifications` case, where the table is empty.

Related: KS-1054 (fresh databases, addressed by #1332). See also KS-1376 (the `certifications` row above, whose fix shape should cover it) and KS-1055 (per-tenant databases).

title: 13 new advisories block every push: axios 1.18.1 ×12 (7 high — SSRF, proxy bypass, ReDoS, prototype pollution; runtime in services/kyc) and dompurify 3.4.13 — all fixed in range (axios 1.20.0, dompurify 3.4.16)
description:
## BLUF

**The push preflight fails legs 6 and 7 on** `develop`**'s own dependencies again, so no push on this repo succeeds until this lands.** Thirteen advisories published on 2026-09-30 are absent from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`: **twelve against axios 1.18.1 (7 high)** and one against dompurify 3.4.13 (low). **No lock changed to cause this.** No `axios`/`dompurify` line in any lock moved between `377989cf3`, where both legs were rc 0 on 2026-09-30 \~02:45Z, and `4f18c59a8`.

**Every one is fixed inside the declared ranges, so this is a lock refresh, not a manifest bump.** That was checked against each advisory's `vulnerable_versions`, not inferred. `frontend/issuer` already pins axios 1.20.0 / dompurify 3.4.16 and is flagged by neither leg.

Measured at `develop` `4f18c59a8`, twice (2026-09-30 \~22:55Z and 23:11Z, identical ID sets), on Stuart's Mac: `npm run audit:gate` rc 1 (`24 distinct advisories reported, 26 baselined` → 13 NEW); `npm run audit:locks` rc 1 (`1611 distinct packages pinned — 18 advisories match, 6 already baselined` → 12 NEW).

## The thirteen, and the fix version measured for each

Each advisory's `vulnerable_versions` comes from the npm bulk-advisory endpoint, the same data the gates read, and was checked with `semver.satisfies` against both the pinned version and the candidate fix.

| advisory | sev | summary (from the gate) | vulnerable | 1.18.1 | 1.20.0 |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `GHSA-r4gj-5m52-g5wh` | high | `maxRedirects: 0` not enforced by fetch adapter → redirect-based SSRF | `>=1.17.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-mghh-pgcx-3jjj` | high | ReDoS in `shouldBypassProxy`, reachable via untrusted redirect `Location` | `>=1.15.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-3pq3-5fj3-cg6v` | high | HTTP/2 adapter bypasses configured DNS lookup and proxy controls | `>=1.13.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-542g-h47m-68v8` | high | DoS via unhandled `error` in HTTP/2 session init | `>=1.13.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-c29m-xwm3-cm6r` | high | ReDoS in `fromDataURI` data: URL parser | `>=1.16.1 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-x97p-jq2g-jp4f` | high | prototype-pollution gadget in `toFormData` options | `>=1.15.1 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-m8m8-qj5v-23w3` | high | Node HTTP adapter prototype-pollution gadget → request socket hijack | `>=1.15.2 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-44g4-m2mj-wpvx` | moderate | CIDR-form `NO_PROXY` entries ignored → proxy exclusion bypass | `>=1.15.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-vh66-26gq-q6x8` | moderate | prototype-pollution gadget in fetch adapter alters outbound requests | `>=1.7.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-9fr6-4gfg-395g` | moderate | prototype pollution in default instance overrides HTTP method | `>=1.0.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-j8rh-479h-cp32` | moderate | header injection via inherited headers after minimal interceptor | `>=1.0.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-4hqw-qxg8-jxx2` | moderate | fetch adapter header injection via inherited FormData `getHeaders` | `>=1.12.0 <1.20.0` | VULN | ok |
| `GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p` | low | **dompurify** `IN_PLACE` hook leaves detached event handlers armed → DOM XSS | `>=3.4.13 <=3.4.15` | 3.4.13 VULN | 3.4.16 ok |

## Where, and why a lock refresh reaches it — measured

| lock | pinned | declared range | leg |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `services/kyc` | axios 1.18.1 | `^1.8.2` (`dependencies`) | 7 |
| `frontend/admin` | axios 1.18.1 | `^1.6.5` | 7 |
| `frontend/verifier` | axios 1.18.1 | `^1.6.2` | 7 |
| `Blockchain/Dev` root (workspace) | axios 1.18.1 (one copy, hoisted) | admin/issuer/verifier/kyc as above + `@meshsdk/provider` `^1.7.2` | 6 |
| `Blockchain/Dev` root (workspace) | dompurify 3.4.13 | `frontend/issuer` `^3.4.13` | 6 |
| `frontend/issuer` | axios **1.20.0**, dompurify **3.4.16** | — | not flagged |

Every range admits axios 1.20.0 and dompurify 3.4.16, `@meshsdk/provider`'s `^1.7.2` included, so the root lock can stay on a single copy.

`services/kyc` **is runtime exposure, not build-tree only.** axios is in `dependencies`, the image installs with `npm ci --omit=dev` (`services/kyc/Dockerfile:63`), and `src/providers/microsoft-entra-client.ts` imports it for outbound calls. The redirect-SSRF and proxy-bypass rows are the ones to read against that client. Reachability was **not** assessed here. The frontends' exposure (browser bundle vs build tree) was not measured either.

## Done means

1. axios ≥ 1.20.0 in `services/kyc`, `frontend/admin`, `frontend/verifier` and the root lock, and dompurify ≥ 3.4.16 in the root lock. Each lock is regenerated **containerised** (`node:24-alpine`; host npm 11.5.1 dies with `edgesOut`, see [KS-1379](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1379/pr-1339s-standalone-locks-were-re-resolved-from-bare-manifests-1000)), with a no-target control run as [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1358](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1380-15-locks-agree-with-packagesshared-on-types-esc-4199-pg-8231-020075b0edd2) did so that every move is attributable.
2. Legs 6 and 7 green at the PR head with **no** baseline row for any of the thirteen.
3. The `services/kyc` suite and image build at the head, since it is the runtime consumer.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd Blockchain/Dev
npm run audit:gate    # leg 6
npm run audit:locks   # leg 7
```

Found on 2026-09-30 while verifying [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1358](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1380-15-locks-agree-with-packagesshared-on-types-esc-4199-pg-8231-020075b0edd2) ([KS-1380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1380/develop-does-not-build-since-ks-1378-1339-analytics-billing-and)) for Stuart. [KS-1395](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1395/two-advisories-published-after-ks-1378-block-every-push-again-undici), the previous batch, is closed. This is the next one.

title: Thirteen advisories published 2026-09-30 block every push: axios 1.18.1 in four locks and dompurify 3.4.13 in the workspace root
description:
## BLUF

**The push preflight fails legs 6 and 7 on** `develop`**'s own dependencies, so no push on this repo succeeds until this is triaged.** Thirteen advisories published 2026-09-30 between 15:01:07Z and 15:37:57Z (GitHub advisory API) are absent from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`. Measured at `develop` `4f18c59a89db16cb8b06b7850aeb64e6f81f95ee`: `npm run audit:gate` and `npm run audit:locks` from `Blockchain/Dev`, **both rc 1**; `npm run audit:contract` rc 0.

**None of these is one of KS-1378's five**, and none is one of the two KS 1395 names. This is the fourth separate batch since 2026-09-29: KS-1378's five, KS 1395's two, six more cleared by an in-range lock refresh under KS-1378 (Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1356), and these thirteen.

## The thirteen (summaries from the GitHub advisory API)

Twelve are **axios**, every one fixed in **1.20.0** on the 1.x line (`GHSA-x97p-jq2g-jp4f` and `GHSA-9fr6-4gfg-395g` also name 0.34.0 for the 0.x line, which no lock here uses). Seven high, five moderate (GitHub labels the five `medium`):

| advisory | sev | summary |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GHSA-c29m-xwm3-cm6r` | high | ReDoS in the `fromDataURI` `data:` URL parser freezes the Node event loop |
| `GHSA-mghh-pgcx-3jjj` | high | ReDoS (O(N²)) in `shouldBypassProxy` host normalization, reachable via untrusted redirect `Location` |
| `GHSA-x97p-jq2g-jp4f` | high | Prototype pollution gadget in `toFormData` options |
| `GHSA-3pq3-5fj3-cg6v` | high | HTTP/2 adapter bypasses the configured DNS lookup and proxy controls |
| `GHSA-542g-h47m-68v8` | high | DoS via an unhandled `error` event in HTTP/2 `ClientHttp2Session` initialization |
| `GHSA-m8m8-qj5v-23w3` | high | Node HTTP adapter prototype-pollution gadget allows request socket hijack via inherited `createConnection` |
| `GHSA-r4gj-5m52-g5wh` | high | `maxRedirects: 0` is not enforced by the fetch adapter, allowing redirect-based SSRF |
| `GHSA-vh66-26gq-q6x8` | moderate | Prototype pollution gadget in the fetch adapter can alter outbound requests |
| `GHSA-9fr6-4gfg-395g` | moderate | Prototype-pollution gadget in the default instance allows an inherited `Object.prototype` method to override the HTTP method |
| `GHSA-j8rh-479h-cp32` | moderate | Header injection via inherited `headers` after a minimal interceptor |
| `GHSA-4hqw-qxg8-jxx2` | moderate | Fetch adapter header injection via inherited `FormData` `getHeaders` |
| `GHSA-44g4-m2mj-wpvx` | moderate | CIDR-form `NO_PROXY` entries are ignored, causing proxy exclusion bypass for internal IP ranges |

One is **dompurify** `GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p` (low): `IN_PLACE` node-removing `afterSanitize` hook leaves detached subtree event handlers armed, causing DOM XSS. Vulnerable `>= 3.4.13, <= 3.4.15`; `first_patched_version` **3.4.16**.

## Where they are pinned — measured across all 45 tracked locks at `develop`, not assumed

| lock | axios | dompurify |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` (workspace root) | **1.18.1** | **3.4.13** |
| `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/admin/package-lock.json` | **1.18.1** | — |
| `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/verifier/package-lock.json` | **1.18.1** | — |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/kyc/package-lock.json` | **1.18.1** | — |
| `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/issuer/package-lock.json` | 1.20.0 (already patched) | 3.4.16 (already patched) |
| `systemTest/akto/package-lock.json` | 1.20.0 (already patched) | — |
| `Blockchain/Dev/mobile/secuura-app/package-lock.json` | 1.13.2 (inside six of the twelve ranges; see below) | — |

No other tracked lock pins either package.

**Four locks need the change, not the three leg 7 names.** The workspace root lock pins both packages and is covered by leg 6, not leg 7. `mobile/secuura-app` is out of scope under KS 769 (expires 2026-10-19), and leg 7 excludes it under that ruling. Its axios 1.13.2 sits inside six of the twelve axios ranges (`GHSA-3pq3-5fj3-cg6v`, `GHSA-542g-h47m-68v8`, `GHSA-vh66-26gq-q6x8`, `GHSA-9fr6-4gfg-395g`, `GHSA-j8rh-479h-cp32`, `GHSA-4hqw-qxg8-jxx2`). After the refresh, that is the only copy of any of the thirteen left in the 45 tracked locks, and it is KS 769's to decide.

**Why leg 7 never reported the dompurify advisory:** leg 7 scans the 43 standalone locks, and the only standalone copy of dompurify is `frontend/issuer`'s, which is already at the patched 3.4.16. The vulnerable copy is in the workspace root lock, which is leg 6's. Both instruments are behaving correctly.

## The route — an in-range lock refresh, not a manifest bump

Every affected manifest already admits the patched version, so no `package.json` changes:

* `frontend/admin` declares `axios ^1.6.5`
* `frontend/verifier` declares `axios ^1.6.2`
* `services/kyc` declares `axios ^1.8.2`
* `frontend/issuer` declares `dompurify ^3.4.13` (the root lock's copy is the workspace hoist of this)

Neither package is declared at the workspace root itself. The refresh is Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1363: those five lock entries move and nothing else. Each moved axios entry also records axios 1.20.0's own `form-data ^4.0.6` range; form-data 4.0.6 was already locked everywhere.

## Reachability

* `services/kyc`: **one** source file imports `axios` (`src/providers/microsoft-entra-client.ts`). A real service path, and the image ships `node_modules`.
* `frontend/admin`: **zero** source files import `axios`. `frontend/verifier`: **zero**. Declared but unused; their final images are nginx plus the built `dist/`, and the builder stage is discarded.
* `frontend/issuer/src/utils/sanitize.ts` imports `dompurify`. **No test anywhere covers that file** — searched `frontend/`, `services/` and `packages/` for a spec naming `sanitize` or `dompurify`.

## Done means

1. Legs 6 and 7 both rc 0 at the PR head, with `audit:contract` still rc 0, and **no baseline row added, removed or changed** (26 baselined before and after).
2. Each of the thirteen advisories shown absent from both legs, against the lock entry that cleared it.
3. Every lock move proved by `cmp` plus a lock parse against a pristine control tree at the same base — never by npm's `up to date` banner, which has read as success on this repo before while nothing moved.
4. Locks regenerated containerised in `node:24-alpine`, with the container's npm version recorded.
5. The images and suites that consume the moved locks built and run.

## Not in scope

* The three frontends declare no `test` script at all, so "suites before and after" cannot be satisfied for them — that is KS 1391.
* `services/kyc`'s suite needs `packages/shared` built first, or one file fails to load with `Failed to resolve entry for package "@secuura/shared"`. That is the same class as the stale-`packages/shared/dist` entry at `BACKLOG.md:6`: there the dist is stale, here it is absent.
* The fourteen grandfathered dead baseline rows (thirteen undici plus `GHSA-v2v4-37r5-5v8g`) among the fifteen entries leg 6's cleanup list names on every run; the fifteenth, `GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr` (KS 729), is not grandfathered.

title: Suggested: move platform-k (outside systemTest + observability) to TypeScript 7.0.2 — five current tools fail on TS 7 (tested), so they would be replaced first
description:
**Owner:** Kamil; the order of work is his call. **Raised:** 2026-09-30, split from [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint). **Base:** `develop` @ `4f18c59a8`.
**Companion ticket:** [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint) (Peter) covers `systemTest/` + `observability/`. The two tickets reference each other and never overlap.

## 1. Summary

**Suggestion (Peter, 2026-09-30): move the rest of platform-k to TypeScript 7.0.2**, the version systemTest and observability are moving to on [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint). This ticket covers the rest of platform-k: 43 `package.json` files, 38 of them on TypeScript 5.x. Whether and when to move is Kamil's decision.

**We can't just change the TypeScript version number and keep our current tools.** Five of the tools we use today **stop working** when TypeScript 7 is installed. This was tested, not assumed (§2). Those tools have to be replaced (or, for tsup, fixed) before TypeScript 7 can go in. The replacements were tested too, and they work.

## 2. Why the tools have to change

### In plain English

The `typescript` package on npm has always contained two things:

1. **The compiler** (`tsc`): you run it to check and build code.
2. **A library**: other tools load it *inside their own code* to compile or check TypeScript for you. Our test runner, our script runner, our linter and our SDK bundler all work this way.

**TypeScript 7 is a rewrite, and it ships only the compiler. The library is gone.** In the `typescript@7.0.2` package the library exports exactly **2** things: `version` and `versionMajorMinor`. In 6.0.3 it exports **2,248**. Microsoft says a new, *different* library will come with TypeScript 7.1, and gives no date. The tools that depend on the old library would then have to be rewritten against the new one.

So any tool that loads TypeScript as a library crashes when TypeScript 7 is installed. It asks for functions that no longer exist. Nothing in our config can fix that, because the code the tool needs is not in the package.

### Proof: the same test on TypeScript 6 and TypeScript 7 (2026-09-30)

**Method:**

* Two fresh projects on Node 24.18.0, identical apart from the TypeScript version.
* Each tool at the version we use today.
* The same two-file source in each: one module and one test.
* Tools installed with `--legacy-peer-deps`, because npm refuses to install ts-jest next to TypeScript 7 at all.
* **TypeScript 6.0.3 is the control:** every tool must pass there, so that a failure on 7 can only be caused by 7.

| Tool (version we use) | What we use it for | Where | Its declared TypeScript support | **TypeScript 6.0.3** | **TypeScript 7.0.2** |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **typescript-eslint** 8.71 (parser) | Linting TypeScript | `Blockchain/Dev` workspace root | `>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`: **excludes 7** | ✅ lints | ❌ `typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0.` |
| **ts-jest** 29.4 + jest 29.7 | Running unit tests | governance, originate, referral, vc-issuer | `>=4.3 <7`: **excludes 7** (npm refuses the install) | ✅ 1/1 passed | ❌ `does not expose the JavaScript compiler API required by ts-jest` |
| **ts-node** 10.9 | Running `.ts` scripts | referral, vc-issuer, staking, `connectors/whatsapp-bot`, `deployment/cardano` | `>=2.7`: claims open support | ✅ ran | ❌ `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'fileExists')` |
| **ts-node-dev** 2.0 | Dev server with reload | governance | `*`: claims open support | ✅ ran | ❌ same `fileExists` crash (it runs ts-node underneath) |
| **tsup** 8.5 (`--dts`) | Building the SDK's type declarations | `sdk/javascript` | `>=4.5.0`: claims open support | ✅ `.d.ts` written\* | ❌ `TypeError … (reading 'useCaseSensitiveFileNames')`; no `.d.ts` |

\* **tsup has a second, separate problem.** Its d.ts step injects a `baseUrl` option that TypeScript 6 already rejects as deprecated (`TS5101`) and TypeScript 7 removes entirely. The control passed only with `"ignoreDeprecations": "6.0"`. tsup's JS build works on both versions; only the type-declaration step fails.

**Result: 5 of 5 tools pass on TypeScript 6 and fail on TypeScript 7.** Two of them say so up front in their declared ranges. The other three *claim* support but crash when run.

### Proof: the replacements work on TypeScript 7

| Replacement | Replaces | Loads the TypeScript library? | **TypeScript 7.0.2** |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **oxlint 1.86 + oxlint-tsgolint 7.0.2003** | typescript-eslint | No. Its own parser, plus TypeScript 7's Go compiler for type-aware rules | ✅ lints ([KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint) spike: 4 harnesses, 9/9 planted checks) |
| **Vitest 5.0.3** | ts-jest + jest | No (not a dependency or peer) | ✅ 1/1 passed |
| **tsx 4.23.15** | ts-node, ts-node-dev | No (not a dependency or peer) | ✅ ran |
| **tsc 7.0.2** itself | — | — | ✅ type-checks the same source clean |

## 3. Options (Kamil's call)

| Option | What it means | Trade-off |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **1. Replace the tools, then TypeScript 7.0.2** (this plan) | typescript-eslint → oxlint; ts-jest → Vitest; ts-node / ts-node-dev → tsx; fix or replace tsup's d.ts step | Same TypeScript version as [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint). The most work, but every replacement is proven above |
| **2. Keep the tools, run two TypeScripts side by side** | TypeScript 7 for `tsc`; TypeScript 6 installed under the name `typescript` for the tools. ts-jest's own error message recommends this | Two compilers in one tree, which can disagree. **Unproven:** the TypeScript 7 package name ts-jest suggests, `@typescript/native`, **does not exist on npm** (checked 2026-09-30); `@typescript/typescript6` does (6.0.2). Needs its own proof first |
| **3. Stay on TypeScript 6.0.3 for now** | Bump 5.x → 6.0.3, which every current tool supports; revisit when the tools support TypeScript 7.1's new library | The least work now, a second migration later. Leaves platform-k on two TypeScript versions (6.0.3 here, 7.0.2 in systemTest/observability) |

## 4. Scope

**In scope: everything in platform-k except** `systemTest/` **and** `observability/`**.** That is 43 tracked `package.json` files: the `Blockchain/Dev` workspace (services, packages, frontends, sdk, tests, connectors, deployment) and `secuura-website-package`.

**Out of scope:** `systemTest/` and `observability/` → [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-observability-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint).

## 5. The work, in the proposed order (Option 1)

1. **Linting:** `Blockchain/Dev` root typescript-eslint → oxlint + tsgolint.
2. **Tests:** Jest / ts-jest → Vitest in governance, originate, referral and vc-issuer. [KS-1051](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1051/develop-is-red-on-the-servicesoriginate-jest-suite-and-nothing-catches): originate's Jest suite is already red on `develop`. Also `sdk/javascript` Vitest 1 → 5, and the rest of Vitest 4 → 5.
3. **Scripts:** ts-node / ts-node-dev → tsx in the six packages above.
4. **SDK types:** fix or replace tsup's d.ts step (both problems in §2).
5. **TypeScript 5 → 7.0.2**, in batches that each build clean with `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild` ([KS-1380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1380/develop-does-not-build-since-ks-1378-1339-analytics-billing-and) shows how easily lock drift breaks a clean build). Review [KS-920](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-920/shared-ships-the-typescript-compiler-and-a-267-mb-dev-tree-into-all-24) alongside this: `/shared` ships the TypeScript compiler into 24 runtime images, and TypeScript 7's compiler is a native per-platform binary.
6. **Playwright → 1.63.0** in the `Blockchain/Dev` root (^1.61.1; workspace-root lock), `tests/e2e` (^1.40.0, **npm-deprecated**) and `tests/e2e-v2` (1.58.2; `RUNBOOK.md:26` ties it to a cached chromium). Settle [KS-1393](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1393/repo-hygiene-31-spec-files-under-blockchaindevtests-that-no-playwright) row 1 (with [KS-1390](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1390/the-e2e-v2-harness-is-platform-ks-only-browser-portal-and) / [KS-734](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-734/the-e2e-playwright-suite-cannot-run-from-a-clean-checkout-testse2e-is)) first, because some of these test corpora may be retired.
7. **Other currency items:**

| -- | -- | -- |
| `secuura-website-package` ESLint | ^8.56.0 (**EOL, npm-deprecated**) | Off ESLint 8, or retire the package ([KS-1393](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1393/repo-hygiene-31-spec-files-under-blockchaindevtests-that-no-playwright) row 3) |

| vite / @vitejs/plugin-react | ^5 to ^8 / ^4 to ^6 | 8.3.1 / 6.1.1 |
| prettier | ^3.2.4 | 3.9.9 |
| `.claude/skills/secuura-test-discipline/SKILL.md:463-465` | Describes the 400-line cap as ESLint `max-lines` | Reword once linting moves |

## 6. Done when

* Each batch builds clean from `--rebuild`, and its packages' own gates pass.
* Lock changes are scoped to the target packages. [KS-1379](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1379/pr-1339s-standalone-locks-were-re-resolved-from-bare-manifests-1000): an unscoped re-resolve moved \~1,000 non-target entries.

title: The gateway answers every request with `Server: nginx` — Akto's UNWANTED_RESPONSE_HEADERS flags it (LOW); decide: remove the header, or accept it with a recorded reason
description:
## BLUF

Hi Kamil — a small one from the Akto full scan, for your call rather than a defect report. The nginx gateway sends `Server: nginx` on every response. The version is already hidden and upstream `Server` headers are already stripped; what remains is nginx's own header name, which stock nginx cannot drop. Akto's `UNWANTED_RESPONSE_HEADERS` template (LOW, CWE-16) flags its mere presence, so the full OWASP scan now reports one vulnerable result. Would you prefer to remove it (headers-more module), or accept it with a reason so the harness can allowlist it honestly?

## What was seen

Akto `security` tier, slot 4, 2026-09-30, Akto 2.36.4 (found while verifying [KS-1363](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1363/akto-a-skipped-har-replay-is-only-a-warn-the-tier-runs-on-synthetic)): the **Full OWASP API Top 10** run reported `LOW 1 · vulnerable results 1` — `UNWANTED_RESPONSE_HEADERS` (category MHH) recorded against `POST /api/anchors`; the probe's request went to the gateway root and got 200 with, among others, `Server: nginx`. The other 12 security scans passed. This tier is report-only, so it gates nothing.

## Verified from source and live (not inferred)

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker/nginx-gateway/nginx.conf:24` — `server_tokens off;` (no version in the header). Also set in `nginx-demo.conf:196` and `nginx-production.conf:288`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/docker/nginx-gateway/nginx.conf:142` — `proxy_hide_header Server;` (an upstream service's `Server` never reaches the client).
* Live on slot 4: `GET /api`, `GET /health` and `GET /api/anchors` all return `Server: nginx`.
* The template's list is presence-based — `Server` sits in its `response_headers` `key.contains_either` list beside `X-Powered-By`, `X-AspNet-Version` and friends — so any value matches.

## Why it surfaced now (inference, not proven)

The template file is the identical blob at Akto 2.35.6 and 2.36.4, so the bump did not add it. This run had **0** rate-limited results, where the 2026-09-28 run at the old fixed 1,500/min pace had 8,730 refused; the header template plausibly executed against this endpoint for the first time because the scan was no longer throttled ([KS-1374](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1374/akto-scans-are-now-paced-to-fit-the-platforms-rate-limit-test-times)). I have not re-run 2.35.6 to prove it.

## Options

1. **Remove the header** — add the headers-more module to the gateway image and `more_clear_headers Server;`. Clears the finding for real; costs an image change on every nginx target (local, demo VM, production template).
2. **Accept it** — a name-only `Server` header discloses little once the version is hidden. If you rule this way, the harness side (mine, [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-all-tools-security-regression-coverage)) adds it to the Akto known-false-positive allowlist with your ruling quoted as the reason, so it stops reading as a vulnerability without silencing anything else.

No change is made on either side until you choose.

title: platform-k systemTest + observability → TypeScript 7.0.2 + oxlint/tsgolint (Option A, the PS-990 counterpart)
description:
## BLUF

**This ticket covers** `systemTest/` **and** `observability/` **in platform-k, and nothing else. Owner: Peter.** The four TypeScript harnesses (akto, api-explorer, performance, playwright) and `observability/` move to **TypeScript 7.0.2 + oxlint 1.86.0**, with oxlint-tsgolint 7.0.2003 where type-aware lint is needed. ESLint and typescript-eslint are removed. The Playwright Test runner stays at 1.63.0. This is Option A from [PS-990](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-990/systemtest-move-to-typescript-7-702-replace-eslint-typescript-eslint).

**Why:** ESLint 9 is end-of-life and typescript-eslint refuses TS 7. For the rest of platform-k, the same move to TypeScript 7.0.2 is **suggested** (not ruled) in [KS-1398](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1398/platform-k-product-tree-typescript-702-one-ts-version-across-platform) (Kamil), and that decision is his. The two tickets reference each other and never overlap.

**The full plan is attached as** `ks-1396-plan.md`**.** It holds the toolchain inventory, matrices A–D, per-harness steps, observability, decisions, verification, and the spike results as an appendix.

## Scope

| Ticket | Covers |
| -- | -- |
| [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint-option-a-the-ps) **(Peter)** | `systemTest/`: 4 harnesses, root wiring, `fixtures/` typecheck, docs. Plus `observability/`. |
| [KS-1398](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1398/platform-k-product-tree-typescript-702-one-ts-version-across-platform) **(Kamil)** | Everything else in platform-k. Referenced only. |

**Guard:** `git diff --stat origin/develop -- . ':!systemTest' ':!observability'` must be empty before every commit.

## Status

* **Spike (offline, 2026-09-30): done.** Summary below; full results are in the attached plan's appendix.
* **Plan: approved by Peter, 2026-09-30.** Attached.
* **Implementation: not started.** Worktree `~/dev_Obeden/wt/ks-1396` @ `develop` `4f18c59a8`, Docker slot 2.

## Spike summary (full detail: attached plan, Appendix)

| Harness | tsc 6.0.3 → 7.0.2 | ESLint → oxlint (lint time) | Rules migrated / skipped | oxlint findings on today's tree |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| playwright | 0 → 0 errors (0.99 → 0.31 s) | 2.87 → 1.67 s | 127 / 8 | **0** |
| akto | 0 → 0 (1.44 → 0.36 s) | 6.99 → 2.43 s | 95 / 9 | 3 oxlint JSDoc false positives (D2) |
| performance | 0 → 0 (1.72 → 0.64 s) | 4.07 → 1.91 s | 91 / 8 | 36 → **0** with nested tsconfigs |
| api-explorer | 0 → 0 (1.43 → 0.46 s) | 2.73 → 1.30 s | 92 / 10 | 44 → **0** with nested `tests/tsconfig.json` |

* **Planted checks: 9/9 pass.** The `process.env` slot gate is caught where gated and silent in the `config/` exemptions. `no-explicit-any`, `no-unsafe-member-access` and `no-restricted-imports` all fire.
* **Sequencing:** run `@oxlint/migrate` **before** bumping TS, because typescript-eslint throws on TS 7.
* **dotenv 17 → 18:** [PS-990](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-990/systemtest-move-to-typescript-7-702-replace-eslint-typescript-eslint)'s R1 trap does not apply here. On 18, a bare `config()` follows `DOTENV_CONFIG_PATH`; nothing sets it, and a pinning test is planned.
* **observability** was not part of the spike. It has no TS dependency, tsconfig or tests, and moves to oxlint without type-aware rules.

## Decisions (Peter, 2026-09-30)

* **D1:** rules oxlint lacks follow [PS-990](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-990/systemtest-move-to-typescript-7-702-replace-eslint-typescript-eslint) §8. A `tests-unit` JSDoc-presence scan replaces `require-jsdoc` / `require-description`; the other gaps are accepted and listed in the PR.
* **D2:** the akto oxlint JSDoc false positives (`src/core/constants.ts:355`, `src/report/skipBuckets.ts:409`). Isolate a minimal reproduction, then add one line-scoped suppression per site citing [KS-1396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1396/platform-k-systemtest-typescript-702-oxlinttsgolint-option-a-the-ps). No docblock rewrites just to please the linter.
* **D5:** the [KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and) / [KS-1363](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1363/akto-a-skipped-har-replay-is-only-a-warn-the-tier-runs-on-synthetic) "TS held at 6.x" note in `akto/package.json` meant packages outside this ticket ([KS-1398](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1398/platform-k-product-tree-typescript-702-one-ts-version-across-platform)). It is rewritten in the akto step.
* **Scope:** `systemTest/` + `observability/` only. Everything else is [KS-1398](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1398/platform-k-product-tree-typescript-702-one-ts-version-across-platform).

## Done when

* Each harness's `npm run quality` passes, with identical unit counts before and after, unslotted and with `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=2` / `STACK_SLOT=2` exported.
* `observability/`'s `npm run quality` passes and its planted checks are recorded. It has no unit tests; that coverage gap is stated in the PR.
* The root `npm run typecheck` (7 configs, including `fixtures/`) is clean on TS 7.
* The planted checks are recorded, each lock diff is scoped, and `audit:locks` is clean.
* Live runs on slot 2 pass (Playwright suite, Akto pr tier, api-explorer generation, perf smoke), each with branch, SHA and slot.
* The guard above is empty, and a Test Evidence block is recorded on this ticket.

## Record

* Before the 2026-09-30 split, this ticket also surveyed the rest of platform-k: TS 5.x packages, ESLint 8, Jest, Vitest 1, the Playwright versions. That content now lives in [KS-1398](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1398/platform-k-product-tree-typescript-702-one-ts-version-across-platform).
* The pre-spike line "akto sets no `types`" was wrong and was corrected. akto sets `["vitest/globals","node"]`, and the spike measured 0 errors.
* The spike results and the plan were first posted as comments, then consolidated into this description and the attached plan on 2026-09-30.
