title: Two advisories published after KS-1378 block every push again: undici GHSA-r53p (low, issuer + root lock) and js-yaml GHSA-r3ph (moderate, systemTest/performance)
description:
## BLUF

**The push preflight fails legs 6 and 7 again on** `develop`**'s own dependencies, so no push on this repo succeeds until this is triaged.** Two advisories published after [KS-1378](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1378/five-new-advisories-block-every-push-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address) merged ([Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1339](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1378-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address-and-undici-off-five-815a0a16d4c7), squash `2cb858335`, 2026-09-29 06:17Z) are absent from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`. **Neither is one of** [KS-1378](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1378/five-new-advisories-block-every-push-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address)**'s five — those are still clear** (no gate reports any of them, and every in-scope lock pins morgan 1.12.1 / nodemailer 10.0.12 / ip-address 10.7.x).

Measured at `develop` `37205947d` on 2026-09-30 \~02:45Z (Stuart's Mac): `npm run audit:gate` and `npm run audit:locks` from `Blockchain/Dev`, **both rc 1**.

## The two, verbatim from the gates

| advisory | sev | package (pinned) | where | leg |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `GHSA-r53p-7pc4-xj5r` | low | **undici 5.29.0** | `frontend/issuer` lock + `Blockchain/Dev` root lock | 6 and 7 |
| `GHSA-r3ph-w7gj-g6xm` | moderate | **js-yaml 5.2.3** | `systemTest/performance` | 7 |

* undici: *"undici vulnerable to downstream response splitting via retry interceptor"*
* js-yaml: *"maxTotalMergeKeys does not limit CPU use for empty merge sources"*

Leg 6 reads `audit-gate: 24 distinct advisories reported, 25 baselined.` → FAIL, 1 NEW. Leg 7 reads `43 standalone lockfiles … 1612 distinct packages pinned — 20 advisories match, 18 already baselined.` → FAIL, 2 NEW.

## Routes — measured from the locks, not assumed

* **undici 5.29.0 is on the** [KS-559](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-559/dep-batch-2026-08-04-11-new-advisories-undici-5-ip-address-3-hono-cors) **path, unchanged.** In both locks the only 5.29.0 copy resolves `@meshsdk/provider` → `@utxorpc/sdk` → `@connectrpc/connect-node` (`^5.28.3`) → `undici`. Kam ruled on 2026-08-05 (recorded on [KS-559](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-559/dep-batch-2026-08-04-11-new-advisories-undici-5-ip-address-3-hono-cors)) that undici advisories on this path are a **permanent build-tree-only acceptance**: the issuer image ships no `node_modules`, the browser bundle resolves connect-web, and there is no safe-range fix (connect-node 2.x is a major). Three baseline rows already cite that ruling (`GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524`, `GHSA-m8rv-5g2x-5cg5`, `GHSA-v3r7-h72x-cjcm`); nine more on the same path cite [KS-470](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-470/npm-audit-25-transitive-advisories-on-the-develop-lockfile). The other undici copy in both locks (jsdom's nested 7.30.0) is not flagged.
  → **Decision for Kam:** does the [KS-559](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-559/dep-batch-2026-08-04-11-new-advisories-undici-5-ip-address-3-hono-cors) ruling extend to `GHSA-r53p` (a reasoned baseline row citing it), or does this one want a fix? [KS-1378](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1378/five-new-advisories-block-every-push-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address)'s "no baseline entry" was ruled for its five specifically, so it does not decide this one.
* **js-yaml 5.2.3 is a direct runtime dependency of the k6 harness.** `systemTest/performance/package.json:55` declares `"js-yaml": "^5.2.1"` under `dependencies`; the lock pins 5.2.3. It is the parser behind the k6 YAML loader ([KS-1117](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1117/k6-yaml-loader-a-bom-immediately-followed-by-a-comment-is-a-marked)'s `readYaml()`). Test harness, not a shipped image — but it is in the standalone-lock corpus, so it gates every push. **Not measured:** whether a patched 5.x exists inside `^5.2.1` (the gate does not print the patched version, and nothing beyond the gate's own registry query was run). systemTest is Peter's area ([KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-all-tools-security-regression-coverage)), so this half may want to go to him.

## Also printed by leg 6 (cleanup, not a failure)

`2 baseline entries are no longer reported — remove: GHSA-v2v4-37r5-5v8g (ip-address, KS-470), GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr (ip-address, KS-729)`. Cleared by [KS-1378](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1378/five-new-advisories-block-every-push-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address)'s ip-address bump; [KS-1378](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1378/five-new-advisories-block-every-push-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address)'s merge comment already names this as a separate follow-up. It could ride with this PR.

## Done means

1. Legs 6 and 7 green at the PR head, each naming neither advisory as new.
2. Any baseline row carries `reason` + `ticket`, and `expires` unless Kam rules it permanent as [KS-559](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-559/dep-batch-2026-08-04-11-new-advisories-undici-5-ip-address-3-hono-cors) did.
3. Any lock regen is containerised (`lockfile-cleanroom.sh` / `node:24-alpine`) — host npm 11.5.1 dies with `edgesOut` on this fleet's Macs (see [KS-1379](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1379/pr-1339s-standalone-locks-were-re-resolved-from-bare-manifests-1000)).

## Reproduce

```bash
cd Blockchain/Dev
npm run audit:gate    # leg 6
npm run audit:locks   # leg 7
```

Found while checking [KS-1378](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1378/five-new-advisories-block-every-push-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address)'s state for Stuart, 2026-09-30.

title: audit-locks' refusal points at a regen command that cannot regenerate systemTest/performance's lock
description:
**Priority:** Medium — it sends a reader to a command that fails or silently does nothing.

When leg 7 (`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs`) refuses an advisory in any of its 43 standalone locks, its message at `:352` says: "bump the pin (containerised per-dir regen — see [lockfile-cleanroom.sh](<http://lockfile-cleanroom.sh>))". The command `lockfile-cleanroom.sh:120` prints, for the 35 locks that script itself checks (`find services packages frontend scripts -maxdepth 2`, none under `systemTest/`), is:

```
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/<dir>":/app -w /app node:24-alpine npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts
```

Two measured problems when a reader follows that pointer for an advisory in `systemTest/performance/package-lock.json` (2026-09-30):

1. The per-directory mount cannot work for a lock with a `file:` link outside its directory. That manifest carries `"secuura-observability": "file:../../observability"`, and the command fails with `npm error code EMISSINGTARGET` / `Missing target in lock file: "../observability" is referenced by "node_modules/secuura-observability" but does not exist.`, rc 1, lock unchanged. Mounting the parent (`-v "$PWD/systemTest":/app -w /app/performance`) succeeds, rc 0.
2. `npm install --package-lock-only` does not move a pin off a vulnerable range while the pin still satisfies the manifest range (`^5.2.1` here): measured in a scratch copy, 0 entries moved, `js-yaml` still 5.2.3. `npm update js-yaml --package-lock-only` moved exactly one entry, 5.2.3 -> 5.4.2.

A reader following the pointer on an advisory-driven regen therefore gets either a hard failure or a silent no-op, and the gate still refuses. Suggested shape: have `audit-locks.mjs` print its own per-lock command, mounting the lock's parent when the lock has a `file:` link that escapes its directory and using `npm update <package>` for an advisory-driven move; and note that no preflight leg clean-rooms the `systemTest/` locks.

Measured on: `develop` at `37205947ddd2775a72a417beb5b7ac8e3240fbf3`, npm 11.19.0 in `node:24-alpine`.

title: Repo hygiene: 31 spec files under Blockchain/Dev/tests that no Playwright config covers, 708 branches on the remote, and a duplicated website package a major React version behind
description:
## BLUF

Three separate bits of accumulated debt, none urgent, all cheap to decide and none of which anyone will notice until it misleads someone. Grouped because they are one afternoon together and three tickets apart. Measured on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026 — branch count taken from the GitHub API, not the local clone, which is shallow here.

| \# | Where | Seen | Suggest |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `Blockchain/Dev/tests/*.spec.ts` | **31 spec files** sitting directly in that directory, covered by no Playwright config. The repo has exactly three configs — `systemTest/playwright` (`testDir: ./tests`), `tests/e2e-v2` (`testDir: ./tests/tierN`), `tests/e2e` (`testDir: ./tests`) — and none of them resolves to `Blockchain/Dev/tests/` itself. Names read as exploratory leftovers: `admin-sidebar-collapse-{test,fresh,final}.spec.ts`, `issuer-portal-{quick,full,detailed,complete}.spec.ts`, several near-identical variants of one check | Delete, or move the ones worth keeping into `tests/e2e-v2/tests/tierN/` where a config can see them |
| 2 | The remote | **708 branches** (`gh api repos/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/branches --paginate`), of which 706 are neither `main` nor `develop`. The oldest carry no commit since March; ten are Dependabot branches whose PRs are open and stale | Prune merged and abandoned branches. Worth agreeing a rule — delete-on-merge, plus a sweep for anything with no commit in N months |
| 3 | `secuura-website-package/` | A hand-off bundle whose `source/` duplicates `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/website/` under the **same package name** `@secuura/website` v1.0.0, drifted to React 18 / Vite 5 / eslint 8 against the live copy's React 19 / Vite 8 / eslint 10; `diff -rq` over the two `src/` trees reports 19 differing files. Nothing outside itself references it — no compose service, no CI, no script | Decide: is it a deliverable that should be generated from `frontend/website` on demand, or dead weight? Either way it should not be a second copy of a shipped app under the same name |

## Why it matters

Each one is a small lie the repository tells a reader.

* **Row 1** — 31 files named `*.spec.ts` look like test coverage. They are not run by anything, cannot fail, and sit next to `tests/e2e`, `tests/e2e-v2` and `tests/connectors`, which are real. Someone counting specs to answer "how well is the admin portal covered?" gets a wrong answer. Same class as `KS-718`, where gitignored snapshots meant a fresh clone wrote its own expectations and passed.
* **Row 2** — 706 stale branches makes `git branch -r` useless for finding live work and slows every clone and fetch. It also hides the ten stale Dependabot branches behind noise.
* **Row 3** — two packages with the same name and different major versions of React is the shape that produces "it works in my build" confusion. `.planning/codebase/STRUCTURE.md:94` is the only place that mentions it, so nothing in the live docs explains why it exists.

None of this is a defect in the running platform, which is why Low.

## Suggested shape

1. Row 1 is a judgement call per file, but the duplicated-variant names (`-quick`, `-full`, `-detailed`, `-complete`, `-fresh`, `-final`) suggest most can go. Anything worth keeping earns a home under a config; anything else is deleted in one commit.
2. Row 2: agree the retention rule first, then sweep once. GitHub's automatic delete-on-merge setting would stop the recurrence.
3. Row 3: if the bundle is a customer deliverable, generate it from `frontend/website` at release time and stop tracking the copy. If it is not, delete it.

## Acceptance

* Every `*.spec.ts` in the repo is either reachable from a Playwright config or gone.
* Branch count is back to something a person can read, and the rule that keeps it there is written down.
* `@secuura/website` names exactly one package.

## Note to Kamil — please scan before fixing

Suggest doing row 1 together with `KS-1390` (the e2e-v2 harness is in no gate) and `KS-734` (the `tests/e2e` corpus cannot install from a clean checkout) rather than separately — all three are about which Playwright corpus is real, and the answer to "which of these three trees survives" settles all of them at once. Row 2 is independent and can go any time.

## References

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/*.spec.ts` (31 files) · `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts` · `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/playwright.config.ts` · `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts` · `secuura-website-package/source/package.json` vs `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/website/package.json` · `.planning/codebase/STRUCTURE.md:94` · related: `KS-1390`, `KS-734` (In Review), `KS-1038` (Backlog), `KS-718` (Done).

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — file counts and the package comparison read from the tree at that commit; the branch total came from the GitHub API because the local clone is shallow and its own count differs. Nothing was executed and nothing was deleted.

title: ci.yml's contract job cannot work — all three Aiken steps use `contracts/secuura` from the repo root, where no such directory exists; deploy-demo.yml has the same steps correct
description:
## BLUF

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` builds and tests the Aiken contracts with `cd contracts/secuura`, relative to the repo root. There is no `contracts/` at the repo root — the project is at `Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura` — and the workflow sets no `working-directory` and no `defaults.run.working-directory`. All three steps are wrong the same way: `aiken build` (`:205-208`), `aiken check` (`:210-213`), and the artifact path `contracts/secuura/plutus.json` (`:219`). The job would fail on the first `cd`. Latent today because Actions executes nothing on this repo, and wrong the moment it returns. The fix already exists in the tree: `deploy-demo.yml` does the identical steps with `working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura`. Verified on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026.

## What was seen

Aiken appears in exactly two workflows, and they disagree.

**Broken —** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
      - name: Build contracts
        run: |
          cd contracts/secuura        # :207  — no such directory from the repo root
          aiken build

      - name: Run contract tests
        run: |
          cd contracts/secuura        # :212
          aiken check

      - name: Upload contract artifacts
        with:
          path: contracts/secuura/plutus.json   # :219
```

`grep -n "working-directory\|defaults:" .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns nothing, so there is no job-level default to rescue the relative path.

**Correct —** `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml:84-100`, same steps:

```yaml
      - name: Build contracts
        working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura
      - name: Run contract tests
        working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura
      - name: Upload contract artifacts
        with:
          path: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura/plutus.json
```

So this is a straight port of a fix that was already made once, into the file that did not get it.

## Why it matters

The contracts are the best-covered thing in platform-k and the least exercised. Measured on this commit: **10 validators, 13 test modules, 378 test blocks**, including property/fuzz modules built on `aiken-lang/fuzz` v2.2.0 (`contracts/secuura/aiken.toml:20-23`). The only routes to running them are:

* `ci.yml` — broken as above, and dispatch-only anyway (`on: workflow_dispatch`, header *"CI/CD PIPELINE (DISABLED — DEPLOY VIA CURSOR)"*).
* `deploy-demo.yml` — correct, but fenced behind an explicit opt-in input because it targets the Azure Container Apps estate that was deleted in the 2026-07-08 cost pivot (`:35-39`, `:52-70`).
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/deploy-contracts.sh:45,76,87` — by hand, as a deploy prerequisite.

`KS-637` (Backlog, High) already records that the nightly Internal Audit has failed 40 runs straight and that *"the Aiken tests run nowhere else"*. This ticket is the narrower, immediately-fixable half: even if a runner came back tomorrow, the general-purpose job would still fail on the `cd`, so the contract tests would still not run. On-chain validators are the one area where a regression is unrecoverable after deploy — `KS-246` (Backlog) holds the external Aiken audit as the mainnet-readiness gate, and an audit is worth much less if the suite it rests on has no working automated home.

## Suggested shape

1. Port `deploy-demo.yml`'s shape into `ci.yml`: `working-directory: Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura` on both run steps, and `Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura/plutus.json` as the artifact path. Three lines.
2. Consider a job-level `defaults.run.working-directory` if other steps in that job are also root-relative — worth a read of the whole job rather than patching three lines blind.
3. While there: `contracts/secuura/TESTING.md` instructs the reader to `cd /Volumes/KK_DEV_Local/NEW STRUCTURE/…`, a former machine's absolute path, and recommends `aiken test` where every script and workflow in the repo uses `aiken check`. Same defect class — a documented path that cannot work anywhere but one laptop.
4. Add a contracts row to the manual-gate table in `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143`, which has none, so `aiken check` has a named local home while Actions is down.

## Acceptance

* `ci.yml`'s contract job reaches `aiken check` from a clean checkout — provable today by running the same commands locally from the repo root, without needing a runner.
* `TESTING.md` contains no machine-specific absolute path and names `aiken check`.
* `DEV-PROCESS.md` lists the contract command with its measured wall-clock, like the 13 rows already there.

## Note to Kamil — please scan before fixing

Recommend one grep across `.github/workflows/` for every root-relative `cd ` and every `path:` in an upload step, rather than fixing this instance alone. The repo moved to the `Blockchain/Dev/` layout at some point and `deploy-demo.yml` was evidently updated while `ci.yml` was not, so other files may carry the same stale assumption — and none of them can fail visibly while Actions is retired, which is exactly the condition in which this class accumulates.

## References

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:198-219` · `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml:79-100` · `Blockchain/Dev/contracts/secuura/` (10 validators, 13 test modules, 378 test blocks) · `contracts/secuura/aiken.toml:20-23` · `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/deploy-contracts.sh:45,76,87` · `contracts/secuura/TESTING.md` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143` · Aiken docs: [https://aiken-lang.org/](<https://aiken-lang.org/>) · related: `KS-637` (Backlog), `KS-246` (Backlog), `KS-552` (Done — the Container Apps pivot that fenced deploy-demo.yml).

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — the two workflow files were read and compared at that commit; nothing was executed and no runner was invoked. GitHub Actions on this repo answers every job with *"The job was not started because recent account payments have failed…"*, so the defect cannot surface until billing is restored.

title: No frontend declares a `test` script — six package.json files, none with one, so the issuer's vitest setup and its 12 component assertions are unreachable from any runner
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/frontend/` has nine directories, six of them with a `package.json`, and **not one declares a** `test` **script**. The root workspace runner is `"test": "npm run test --workspaces"` (`Blockchain/Dev/package.json:17`), so it cannot reach them. The issuer went further than the others — it has `vitest` + `@testing-library/react` + `jsdom` in devDependencies, a `test:` block in `vite.config.ts:8-12`, and two real spec files carrying 12 assertions — and none of it can be run without typing a `vitest` invocation by hand. This is unit/component coverage only; the portals themselves are covered by the e2e-v2 browser tier, which has its own problem (`KS-1390`). Read from the tree on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026.

## What was seen

Every `scripts` block under `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/*/package.json`:

| Frontend | `scripts` | Test files present |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `admin` | `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint` | 0 |
| `issuer` | `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint`, `check:bundle` | **2** (`blockchain-card.test.tsx`, `provenance-timeline.test.tsx`) |
| `verifier` | `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint` | 0 |
| `website` | `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint` | 0 |
| `outlook-addin` | `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint` | 0 |
| `demo-overlay` | `build`, `dev` | 0 |
| `status`, `gmail-addon`, `shared` | no `package.json` | 0 |

So the two issuer specs are dead weight: present, maintained-looking, and executed by nothing. `frontend/issuer/vite.config.ts:8-12` configures the vitest environment for them, which makes it look deliberate rather than abandoned — the missing piece is one line in `package.json`.

## Why it matters

* **It is a silent zero.** `npm run test --workspaces` at `Blockchain/Dev` looks like it covers the workspaces, and `frontend/*` is a workspace glob (`package.json:6-10`). A reader has no signal that the frontend leg of that command is empty.
* **It is the same class already ticketed one layer down.** `KS-634` (Backlog) — *"No CI gate runs the services' unit suites — a 73-test suite sat dead on develop and every PR stayed green"* — and `KS-652` (Backlog) — *"1219 tests across 23 services are ungated"*. Those are about services having suites nothing runs; this is frontends having no suite to run, plus one that exists and cannot be reached. Same failure mode, opposite end.
* **The precedent for cost is in the repo.** `KS-649` had 31 auth tests dead since 6 Aug because two suites failed at module load and reported "no tests"; `KS-718` had golden-master snapshots gitignored, so a fresh clone wrote its own expectations and passed. Tests that cannot fail are worse than absent — they read as coverage.
* Four shipped admin pages import types from `frontend/admin/src/__mocks__/` (`DocumentTypes.tsx:20`, `DocumentTypeDetail.tsx:22`, `VerificationQueue.tsx:11`, `Workflows.tsx:12`) — a `__mocks__` directory on the production path, in an app with no test framework to justify the name. Worth a look in the same pass.

## Suggested shape

1. Add `"test": "vitest run"` to `frontend/issuer/package.json` so the 12 assertions that already exist can run and fail. One line; it is the whole fix for the unreachable half.
2. Decide for the other five whether a unit tier is wanted at all. "No unit tests for admin/verifier, the browser tier covers them" is a legitimate answer — but it should be written down rather than inferred from an absence, because today the two states are indistinguishable.
3. If the answer is none, make `npm run test --workspaces` honest: `--if-present`, or a note in `Blockchain/Dev/package.json` saying the frontend leg is intentionally empty.
4. Rename or relocate `frontend/admin/src/__mocks__/` if it is production data, so the name stops implying a test fixture.

## Acceptance

* `npm test -w frontend/issuer` runs and reports 12 passing assertions.
* A planted failure in one of those specs turns the command red (the `KS-718` lesson — prove the suite can fail before trusting it).
* The intended unit-test posture for the other frontends is stated in the repo, whatever it is.

## Note to Kamil — please scan before fixing

Suggest checking the same shape across every workspace in one pass rather than ticket by ticket: which `package.json` files declare `test`, which declare it and are never invoked by a gate, and which have test files with no script. `KS-634` / `KS-652` already hold the services half, so a single audit would close the family. The `sdk/javascript` and `sdk/python` client SDKs are a third instance — no tests at all, and not workspace members, so nothing would reach them even if they had some.

## References

`Blockchain/Dev/package.json:6-10`, `:17` · `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/*/package.json` · `frontend/issuer/vite.config.ts:8-12` · `frontend/issuer/src/__tests__/` · `frontend/admin/src/__mocks__/` · related: `KS-634` (Backlog), `KS-652` (Backlog), `KS-649` (Done), `KS-718` (Done), `KS-1390`.

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — the scripts blocks above were read from the tree at that commit; nothing was executed.

title: The e2e-v2 harness is platform-k's only browser, portal and accessibility coverage — 222 tests, runnable by hand, named in no gate and absent from the gate inventory
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/` holds **24 spec files and 222 tests** across four tiers — including every browser journey and the only accessibility coverage platform-k has — and it is wired into nothing. It is not in `.githooks/pre-push`, it has no row in the "Manual CI-gate equivalents" table that `KS-685` commissioned, and the workflow its own README points at (`.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`) does not exist on `develop`. Meanwhile the suite people *are* pointed at, `systemTest/playwright`, is API-only: 3 spec files, 11 tests, no browser. So the documented estate says platform-k has a Playwright tier, and the thing that actually opens a browser is the one nobody is told to run. Counted on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026. Nothing was executed — this is about wiring, not results.

## What is there

Measured from the tree, not from the docs:

| Tier | Specs | Tests | What it covers |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `tier1-api` | 12 | 174 | API over HTTP |
| `tier2-smoke` | 5 | 43 | Smoke journeys |
| `tier3-e2e` | 4 | 40 | **Real browser journeys** — issuer, admin, verifier |
| `tier4-a11y` | 3 | 6 | **axe on admin, issuer and verifier** |
| **Total** | **24** | **222** |  |

It is runnable today. `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/package.json` declares `test`, `test:api`, `test:smoke`, `test:e2e`, `test:a11y`, `install:browsers` and `report`, and `playwright.config.ts` defines the four matching projects (`api`, `smoke`, `e2e`, `a11y`). `@axe-core/playwright` is a devDependency there.

## What is missing

1. **No gate names it.** `grep -rn "e2e-v2" .githooks/pre-push Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` returns nothing. The manual-gate table at `DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143` maps *former CI job → local command* for 13 rows and has no row for e2e-v2, and none for accessibility at all.
2. **Its README cites a workflow that does not exist.** `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/README.md:4` sends the reader to `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`; `git ls-tree origin/develop .github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml` is empty.
3. **The plan doc under-reports it.** `Blockchain/Dev/docs/E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:324` still says *"only the verifier portal has a tier-4 spec. Issuer + admin coverage is a follow-up."* That follow-up is `KS-44`, which is **Done** — there are three tier-4 specs in the tree today. The row understates the coverage that exists.

## Why it matters

* It is the whole UI answer. Without it the honest statement about platform-k is that no browser opens anywhere in the estate — `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts:12-18` says so itself, and `DEV-PROCESS.md:141` spells it out: *"Despite the name, this suite drives no browser… Read a green here as '12 API assertions passed', not as 'the portals work'."*
* It is the whole accessibility answer. There is no `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` anywhere in the repo and no axe inside any frontend, so `tier4-a11y` is the only thing that would catch a regression against WCAG 2.2 / EN 301 549 — relevant to the same obligations the platform-s side tracks. WCAG 2.2: [https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/](<https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/>) · EN 301 549 v3.2.1: [https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/03.02.01_60/en_301549v030201p.pdf](<https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/03.02.01_60/en_301549v030201p.pdf>) · EAA Directive 2019/882: [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj](<https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj>)
* An ungated suite rots quietly. `KS-557` / `KS-560` are the precedent — the tier reported 126 failures, of which only 11 were real, and the cause was a harness defect that had gone unnoticed. `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:358` keeps that lesson as a standing rule.
* Actions being retired makes this the *only* route to the coverage, not a redundant one.

## Suggested shape

1. Give e2e-v2 a row in the `DEV-PROCESS.md` manual-gate table: the exact command, the pass criterion, and a measured wall-clock — matching the 13 rows already there.
2. Decide the tier split deliberately. `tier4-a11y` is 6 tests and needs only a running stack; it is the cheapest thing in the estate to make routine. `tier3-e2e` is slower and flakier (single-session collisions, `E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md` § "Worker-session collisions") so it may belong in a nightly/manual tier rather than a per-push one.
3. Fix the two stale pointers: the dead workflow reference in `tests/e2e/README.md:4`, and the tier-4 row in `E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:324` that `KS-44` has already overtaken.
4. Say in `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` where the browser tier actually lives, so "Playwright" stops meaning two different things in the same repo.

## Acceptance

* `DEV-PROCESS.md`'s gate table has an e2e-v2 row (or rows) with a command and a measured time.
* A named person can run the a11y tier from the runbook without reading source.
* No document points at `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`, and the tier-4 row reflects the three specs that exist.

## Decision needed before fixing — naming the three Playwright estates

Worth settling the naming in the same pass: `systemTest/playwright` (API-only, 11 tests) and `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2` (browser, 222 tests) are both "Playwright", and a third corpus sits at `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e` (`KS-734`, In Review — not a workspace member, cannot install from a clean checkout; `KS-1038`, Backlog — races its own lockout). Three Playwright estates with one name is the reason a reader can believe the portals are covered when the suite in the gate never opens a browser. One decision about which survives, which is gated, and what each is called would close this ticket and shrink two others.

## References

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/package.json` · `playwright.config.ts:29-73` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143`, `:141` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:316-345` · `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/README.md:4` · `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts:12-18` · `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:358` · related: `KS-1076` (Urgent, Todo — no Playwright e2e on a PR since 7 Sep), `KS-734` (In Review), `KS-1038` (Backlog), `KS-44` (Done), `KS-637` (Backlog), `KS-685`.

## Environment

title: Sourcing systemTest/slot-target.sh with no slot named silently exports slot 1's targets — and preflight leg 13 + the pre-push hook depend on that, so it cannot be fixed in systemTest alone
description:
## BLUF

**No action is needed today, and nothing is broken on the trunk.** This asks for your view on one coordinated change that sits across your files and systemTest.

`systemTest/slot-target.sh`, sourced with **no** slot named, silently exports slot 1's targets. Every harness now refuses an unslotted local run in its own code, so the export itself is the last place a slot is silently defaulted. It can't simply be made to refuse, though: **preflight leg 13 and the pre-push hook source it with no slot, on purpose**, and leg 13's positive control would then refuse every push.

Found by the [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) systemTest slot audit (2026-09-29). Re-checked against `develop` @ `8ba2da02d`, code and docs, not from memory.

## What happens today

* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh` resolves `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT="${SECUURA_STACK_SLOT:-${STACK_SLOT:-1}}"`: an unnamed slot becomes **1**.
* `systemTest/slot-target.sh:51` records whether a slot was actually requested (`SECUURA_SLOT_REQUESTED`), then sources `stack_env.sh` and exports slot 1's `SECUURA_GATEWAY_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `SECUURA_BASE_URL`, `SECUURA_API_URL`, `PERF_BASE_URL`, the `AKTO_*` set and `SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX=-slot1`. `SECUURA_SLOT_REQUESTED` is only used by `retarget()`.
* The TypeScript harnesses still refuse an unslotted local run, because `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` itself is never exported. Akto and Schemathesis read several of these exports directly, though. [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) is adding their own entry-point guards so they no longer depend on this.

## Why it can't be fixed in systemTest alone

* `.githooks/pre-push:273-285` ([KS-691](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-691/pre-push-preflight-cannot-run-from-a-git-worktree-legs-1-and-6-fail)) sources it deliberately, `|| true`, so the stack-dependent legs probe *this* slot's gateway rather than preflight's own `localhost:6882` default. When the developer's shell names no slot, that is the slot-1 export.
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:589-630` (leg 13, [KS-786](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-786/stack-env-and-slot-target-read-the-values-they-unit-test-out-of-the)) **measures** the variables `slot-target.sh` exports under `env -i`, **with no slot named**, and has a positive control: an empty list refuses the leg. If `slot-target.sh` refused (exported nothing) when unslotted, that control would fire and **every push would be refused.**

So the three pieces have to move together, and the hook and preflight are yours.

## A possible shape (entirely your call)

1. `slot-target.sh`: when `SECUURA_SLOT_REQUESTED` is empty and `CI` is not truthy, export nothing target-bearing and print a one-line notice, or `return 2`, matching the refusal the TS harnesses use (`systemTest/fixtures/slot-required.ts:76-91`).
2. **Leg 13:** measure the export set with an explicit slot (e.g. `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=1` inside the `env -i` subshell) rather than relying on the unslotted default. Its purpose, the full clear-list, is unchanged.
3. **Pre-push:** when no slot is named, say so and let the stack-dependent legs report SKIPPED (the [KS-1046](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1046/preflight-passed-is-printed-identically-whether-13-legs-ran-or-10-the) verdict), rather than probing slot 1.

Related: [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (stack tooling not slot-derived end to end), [KS-786](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-786/stack-env-and-slot-target-read-the-values-they-unit-test-out-of-the) (leg 13's origin), [KS-691](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-691/pre-push-preflight-cannot-run-from-a-git-worktree-legs-1-and-6-fail) (why the hook sources it).

## Not done here

No change to `slot-target.sh`, the hook or preflight on the [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) branch. Peter's ruling (2026-09-29): raise it for you rather than change your files.

Thank you, and apologies for another slot ticket. This one felt worth raising because the obvious fix would have quietly blocked every push.

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** points 2 and 3 — `slot-target.sh` refusing when unslotted is point 2; leg 13 is coordinated with [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s spot 4. This ticket had no acceptance section of its own, so these points are its acceptance, together with the three steps of its possible shape.

title: observability/ reaches the platform by slot 1's container names (documented), and both .env examples suggest the nginx stub_status on :6882, a port that does not exist on the container network
description:
## BLUF

`observability/` is **slot 1 only by a documented decision**, and that decision stands. This ticket records what would need to change to make it slot-aware, so the work is ready when [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never)'s `/metrics` lands. It also covers **one real error to fix now**: both example env files suggest a gateway status URL on a port that does not exist inside the container network.

Found by the [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) systemTest slot audit (2026-09-29). Re-checked against `develop` @ `8ba2da02d`, code and docs, not from memory.

## 1. The concrete error (small, fix any time)

* `observability/.env.example:47` and `observability/config/alerting.env.example:55` both say:
  `# SECUURA_NGINX_STATUS_URI=http://secuura-nginx-gateway:6882/stub_status`
* **6882 is the host-side port of the gateway's** `6882:80` **publish.** Inside the container network only **80** exists. The compose default already uses it (`docker-compose.yml:331`: `${SECUURA_NGINX_STATUS_URI:-http://secuura-nginx-gateway:80/stub_status}`), and `prometheus/prometheus.yml:48-52` explains why the old `:6882` scrape job was removed for exactly this reason.
* Anyone who uncomments the example gets an nginx exporter that cannot connect. **Fix:** change both examples to `:80`.

## 2. Where observability assumes slot 1 (documented, for when [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never) lands)

| Where | What | Documented as |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `scripts/observability.sh:57` | `docker inspect secuura-nginx-gateway` to discover the platform network | override `SECUURA_PLATFORM_NETWORK` |
| `scripts/observability.sh:96-100` | `docker exec "${SECUURA_PG_CONTAINER:-secuura-postgres}"` to read DB credentials | "SLOT 1 ONLY, deliberately" (`:88-90`) |
| `scripts/observability.sh:137-138` | `docker inspect "${SECUURA_REDIS_CONTAINER:-secuura-redis}"` | same limitation |
| `docker-compose.yml:296, 311, 331` | exporter defaults name `secuura-postgres`, `secuura-redis`, `secuura-nginx-gateway` | same |
| `prometheus/prometheus.yml:82-92` | `secuura-services` static targets `secuura-auth:4003` … labelled `slot: slot1` | "⚠ SLOT 1 ONLY" (`:74-78`) |
| `loki/alloy.river:84-92` | default `slot = "slot1"` for **every** container, then more specific rules override | README "Which stack slot am I looking at?" |

The README states the position clearly ("What is NOT per-slot: application metrics"), and the reasoning in `prometheus.yml:74-78` is sound: slot discovery needs either a Docker socket inside Prometheus or a generated targets file plus per-slot `docker network connect`, and neither is worth it while the job collects nothing ([KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never)).

**One small thing worth considering, independent of** [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never)**:** `alloy.river`'s default labels non-platform containers (Akto, observability's own, a k6 container without its label) as `slot1`. A neutral default such as `unslotted` would stop those logs appearing under slot 1 in the picker. That matches the rule the [KS-1386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1386/systemtest-api-explorer-hard-codes-slot-1s-gateway-6882-a-slot-n) systemTest fix adopts: an unslotted run is labelled `unslotted`, never `slot1`.

## Suggested shape (when [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never) is picked up)

* Derive container names from `STACK_PREFIX` (`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh:58-64`: `secuura` on slot 1, `secuura-s<N>` above) rather than typing `secuura-<svc>`.
* Revisit the static scrape job together with [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never)/[KS-985](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-985/eight-dashboards-show-a-slot-picker-that-filters-nothing-latent-today), as `prometheus.yml:74-78` already proposes.

## Not done here

No code changed. The observability stack was not started; this is a read of the files at `8ba2da02d`.

title: A clean image build of platform-k develop fails: services/governance does not compile (TS2742 on router's inferred type) — a new slot cannot start until the image exists from an older build
description:
## Seen (2026-09-29, develop `0aa9b52c6`; origin/develop `b4461d1e2` is three commits ahead, none touching governance)

Starting a fresh stack slot with no cached images (`Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` via platform-s's `up-slot.sh 4`) fails at the governance image:

```
docker compose -p secuura_slot4 build --progress=plain governance
#19 1.611 src/routes/governance.ts(19,7): error TS2742: The inferred type of 'router' cannot be
      named without a reference to '@secuura/shared/node_modules/@types/express-serve-static-core'.
      This is likely not portable. A type annotation is necessary.
#19 ERROR: process "/bin/sh -c npm run build" did not complete successfully: exit code: 1
```

Reproducible: the same `docker compose build governance` fails the same way on a second run. Slots 1–3 on this machine start only because they hold `secuura_slot{1,2,3}-governance` images built up to two weeks ago; slot 4 had no image and could not be built. A new developer machine, or a slot torn down with `--rmi all` (the test-discipline teardown), hits this.

The first attempt on the same slot failed one image earlier — `nft-certificate` at `npm ci --ignore-scripts` — and that one built cleanly on retry, so it was transient; governance is not.

## Suggested fix

`services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts:19` — give `router` an explicit type (`const router: Router = express.Router()`), the usual TS2742 remedy when a workspace package (`@secuura/shared`) carries its own `@types/express-serve-static-core`. Worth a `tsc --noEmit` over every service in the PR gate so a non-portable inferred type cannot land again.

## Impact on platform-s

Blocks pairing an S slot with a fresh K slot for the gate run on platform-s PR #889 (the S↔K remediation branch); recorded there and on [PS-928](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-928/k-live-goes-red-on-the-second-full-run-on-a-slot-the-anchor-refresher). Related: [KS-955](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-955/a-fresh-clone-cannot-run-the-four-platform-suites-and-fails-in-a-way) (a fresh clone cannot run the suites).

title: systemTest: no stack slot is hard-coded or silently defaulted, in any harness — api-explorer first, then fixtures/shell suites, Playwright, Performance, Akto, Schemathesis
description:
## Scope widened 2026-09-29 (Peter: "everything fixed on this branch", one ticket)

**BLUF:** this ticket now covers every systemTest harness, not just api-explorer. One branch (`feature/ks-1386-…`), **one commit per harness** so it can be reviewed commit by commit. Rule adopted (Peter, 2026-09-29): every entry point that touches a stack **refuses** a local run that names no slot (CI and remote targets stay exempt), and an exempt run is labelled `unslotted`, never `slot1`. Every slot value in code, tests and example files is **derived from the slot-1 base**, never typed per slot.

**Audit (read-only,** `develop` **@** `8ba2da02d`**; highest-risk items re-checked in the code by hand):**

* **Silent slot-1 fallbacks in code (highest risk):**
  * Schemathesis `setup` (`scripts/setup_paths.py:65`, exempt at `run.py:364`) mints an admin API key and IDOR tokens against slot 1 when no slot is named.
  * Schemathesis hooks' `BASE_URL` (`config/settings.py:48`) logs personas into slot 1 on the bare `st run` path.
  * Akto checks only the scan target for a slot (`src/config/validate.ts:58`), not its own dashboard URL. `OVERRIDE_APP_URL`, the real scan target, is not in the coherence check. `npm run db:ui` runs compose unguarded. `src/setup/templateLibrary.ts:27` uses slot 1's dashboard container.
  * `scripts/setup-env.sh:34` offers slot 1's URL as the default. `performance/scripts/prove-slot-isolation.sh:47` defaults its victim slot to 3 and stops that slot's containers.
  * Root cause: five slot resolvers return 1 when unset (fixtures, Playwright, Performance, Akto, Schemathesis).
* **Tests that type slot 2-4 values:** about 40 files across all harnesses. About 15 tests pin "unset means slot 1" as correct.
* **Example and config files:** `akto/.env.example` (a per-slot port table, plus live slot-1 defaults), `playwright/.env.example` ("unset means slot 1", now false), and a dead, wrong port block in `schemathesis/config/schemathesis_tests.yaml`.

**Split out, outside systemTest:** [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (`slot-target.sh`, pre-push and preflight leg 13, for Kamil) and [KS-1388](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1388/observability-reaches-the-platform-by-slot-1s-container-names) (`observability/`).

---

## Original scope (api-explorer)

## BLUF

`systemTest/api-explorer` is the one systemTest package that still does not resolve the stack slot. Its local server URL is a slot-1 literal, so an explorer generated for a slot-N stack points its "Local" server entry and both quick-start `curl` examples at **slot 1's** gateway. This is the `api-explorer` row of [KS-1056](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1056/systemtest-slot-isolation-is-opt-in-only-4-files-read-the-slot-every)'s per-suite table. [KS-1056](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1056/systemtest-slot-isolation-is-opt-in-only-4-files-read-the-slot-every) was closed as a Duplicate into [KS-687](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-687/akto-slot-targeting-dump-result-fieldssh-resolves-the-un-prefixed), and that row was recorded there, but [KS-687](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-687/akto-slot-targeting-dump-result-fieldssh-resolves-the-un-prefixed) closed without fixing it, so nothing tracks it now.

## Where (develop @ `0aa9b52c6`)

* `systemTest/api-explorer/src/config/servers.ts:8`: `const LOCAL_GATEWAY_HOST = 'http://localhost:6882';` The package never reads `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT`. `git grep -E "slot|SLOT" -- systemTest/api-explorer` finds nothing.
* `LOCAL_API_BASE_URL`, `HEALTH_CHECK_URL` and `AUTHENTICATED_HEALTH_CHECK_URL` are all built from that literal. They reach the generated page through:
  * `src/generator/render/configBannerSection.ts:16`: the server-selector dropdown (`SERVER_OPTIONS`)
  * `src/generator/render/quickStartSection.ts:24-31`: the two copyable `curl` health checks
* `tests/unit/config/servers.test.ts:24` asserts the literal `'http://localhost:6882/health'`. That typed per-slot literal is what CLAUDE.md's "every slot value is CALCULATED from slot 1" rule forbids.

## Consequence

An operator working on slot N who copies the explorer's curl, or picks the "Local" server, talks to slot 1. If slot 1 is up, they get another stack's answers. A token minted there fails on slot N as `401 Invalid or expired token`: the cross-slot contamination recorded as instance 3 on [KS-1056](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1056/systemtest-slot-isolation-is-opt-in-only-4-files-read-the-slot-every). If slot 1 is down, it looks like the stack is broken.

## Fix direction

* Derive the local gateway from the slot through the shared resolver (`systemTest/fixtures/slot.ts` / `target.ts`, as the other harnesses now do), not a literal. Slot 1 stays `:6882`.
* A LOCAL generation that names no slot fails loudly, per the systemTest no-slot rule, rather than defaulting to slot 1.
* Replace the `servers.test.ts:24` literal with an expectation computed from the slot-1 base, and add cells for slots 1–4 (the `start_secuura_slot_names.test.sh` shape).
* Red→green: those cells fail on the current code and pass after the fix.

## Out of scope

`PRODUCTION_API_BASE_URL` in the same file is not a slot concern and is not covered here.
