title: KS-1175 follow-on: the anchors K emits for share / transfer-custody / lifecycle-events carry no documentType and drop Platform-S's identity block — only originate and the flat anchor anchor identity
description:
## Found by

The S↔K compatibility review of 2026-09-29 (platform-k `0aa9b52c6`, platform-s `477eb57`).

## The gap

[KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) (merged `cbae988db`, `910687394`) accepts the `identity` block on `POST /api/anchors` and anchors it beside `documentType` / `occurredAt` (`services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts:128-151, 261-315`). Platform-S sends that block on **every** write once `CardanoAnchor:AnchorIdentity` is on — flat anchors, originate, version, certifications, share, transfer-custody and lifecycle-events (`ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.cs:1606-1631`).

On K, three of those routes never carry it to the anchor:

* `POST /api/documents/{id}/lifecycle-events` reads only `action` and `payload`; an `identity` key in the body is ignored (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:2440-2545`).
* `POST /{id}/share` and `POST /{id}/transfer-custody` likewise.
* All three anchor through `emitLifecycleAnchor`, whose body is `{documentId, contentHash, network}` — no `metadata.documentType`, no `identity` (`documents.ts:1275-1297`).

Result: for every non-mutating verb (delete, share-revoke, the share-\* edits, rights-unassign, note, certified, verified, share, rights-assign/reassign) the chain record has no verb and no actor/organisation identity, whatever S sends. Only `upload` (originate) and the flat-anchor fallback carry them.

## Ask

1. Carry `identity` (and the verb as `metadata.documentType`) from the share / transfer-custody / lifecycle-events request bodies into the `emitLifecycleAnchor` call, so the anchor records them — subject to the per-document-anchor ruling on the companion ticket (a reset row would not keep them anyway).
2. Declare `identity` on `DocumentShareRequest`, `TransferCustodyRequest` and `LifecycleEventRequest` in `originate.openapi.ts` so S's [PS-614](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-614/check-ss-verb-vocabulary-against-platform-ks-openapi-enum-at-gate-time) gate can see it (today S's `k_openapi_vocabulary.test.ts` only checks `onBehalfOf` placement).
3. Echo what was anchored on the lifecycle-event response, so S's read-back ([PS-870](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-870/6-send-the-identity-record-to-platform-k-on-every-anchored-verb) item 5) works on these verbs too.

## Verify

Paired slot with `AnchorIdentity=true` on S: a `share-revoke` on an originated document → the anchor read (`GET /api/anchors/{id}`) returns `identity.actorDid` and `metadata.documentType = share-revoke`. Today it returns neither.

Related: [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss), [PS-870](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-870/6-send-the-identity-record-to-platform-k-on-every-anchored-verb), [PS-864](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-864/epic-id-status-stored-and-shown-throughout-the-system-actor-and), the [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one) companion ticket (one anchor per document).

title: One anchor row per (document_id, network): a repeat POST /api/anchors resets the existing row to pending and nulls its transaction hash — so Platform-S's per-event anchoring collapses to one anchor per document (PS-895 companion)
description:
## Found by

The S↔K compatibility review of 2026-09-29 (platform-s `477eb57`, platform-k `0aa9b52c6`; origin/develop `b4461d1e2` is three commits ahead, none touching this). Companion to [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one), which asked the question from the S side after seeing six lifecycle events on one document share one External Ref, and one on-chain transaction for register + declare on dev-ps.

## What the code does

`dbPersistAnchor` upserts on the composite key and rewrites the chain columns from the **new** request:

```
services/anchoring/src/index.ts:1334-1372
  INSERT INTO anchor_store (...)
  ON CONFLICT (document_id, network) DO UPDATE SET
    status = EXCLUDED.status, transaction_hash = EXCLUDED.transaction_hash,
    block_hash/block_number/slot/fee/confirmations/confirmed_at = EXCLUDED.…,
    error_message, retry_count, simulated, updated_at = EXCLUDED.…
  RETURNING id
```

`metadata_payload` and `content_hash` are **not** in the update list, so the first event's label and hash stay on the row. Every `POST /api/anchors` builds the anchor with `status: 'pending'` and a null hash (`index.ts:463-560`), so on a conflict the existing row goes back to `pending` with `transaction_hash = NULL`, and `processAnchor(persistedId)` runs again (`:535`).

K's own share, transfer-custody, revoke and lifecycle-event routes all go through `emitLifecycleAnchor`, which posts only `{documentId, contentHash, network}` to that same flat endpoint (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1275-1297`). So every non-mutating verb S records re-enters the same row for the document.

Migration 031 records the one-row-per-(document, network) decision. `anchorSubmission.ts:383-386` (guard 1) reads the row's `transaction_hash` to avoid a second fee-paying transaction — the upsert has just nulled it.

## What this means for the S↔K contract

* Platform-S's user-facing promise (`docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §1, §7) is that every declare, sign and share event is anchored. K anchors **one row per document version per network**; later events reset and re-process it.
* For every verb S routes through `/lifecycle-events`, `/share` or `/transfer-custody`, the chain record carries **no** `documentType` **and no** `identity` — `emitLifecycleAnchor` sends neither, and the lifecycle-events handler reads only `action` and `payload` (`documents.ts:2440-2545`). That is a [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) gap; filed separately.

## Decisions needed (Kamil)

1. Is one anchor per (document, network) the intended contract? If yes, S will label its External Ref column "anchor for version X" and group events ([PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one) item 2), and the USER-MANUAL wording changes.
2. If events should each anchor, the upsert key needs an event dimension and `emitLifecycleAnchor` needs the verb.
3. Either way: **what happens on the reset.** Trace whether `processAnchor` after a conflict mints a second Cardano transaction for the same document (guard 1 cannot see the previous hash any more), or is caught by another guard. Not verified live in the review; [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one)'s dev-ps observation was one transaction for two events.

## Verify

* Unit: a second `POST /api/anchors` for the same `(documentId, network)` returns the existing id **and** either leaves a confirmed row's `transaction_hash` intact (per-document contract) or creates a distinct row (per-event contract) — whichever is ruled.
* Live on a paired slot: originate → declare → share on one document; count anchor rows and Cardano transactions; quote both on this ticket.

Related: [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one) (the S-side question), [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) (identity block), [PS-870](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-870/6-send-the-identity-record-to-platform-k-on-every-anchored-verb).

title: Verify is not bound to the credential's proof: a revoked credential resubmitted with another LIVE id still verifies true
description:
`Refs KS-1375`

## BLUF

Credential verification is not bound to the credential's own proof. A **revoked** credential
resubmitted carrying **another live credential's id** verifies `true` on **both** verify routes. This
is pre-existing: it reproduces at the merged head of PR #1341 *and* at develop before it. A forged
subject also verifies.

No DID resolver is wired, so the proof is not validated on these routes (structurally checked only,
outside production). PR #1341's fail-closed change covers ids that **no authority holds**, which is
why it is partial against its ruling's phrase "closes the id-edit trick": an id that *is* held by a
live credential is not an unknown id.

## Provenance

The ruling card for the unknown-id policy said this work was coming, and said it goes ahead either
way: "Separately, a ticket is being filed to bind the check to the credential's proof (wire the
issuer's DID resolver), which would close the edit trick whatever you choose here" and "The
proof-binding ticket goes ahead either way."

That ticket was never filed — searched by symbol (`didResolver`, `DID resolver`, `resolver`,
`proof-binding`) with two positive controls that each found a ticket known to exist. The only match
for `didResolver` was KS 1375 itself. This ticket is that filing.

Adjacent but **not** this: KS 624 (prism issues VCs with random bytes as the proof), KS 625
(`/presentations/verify` never checks the holder signature), KS 627 (wallet CIP-8/COSE verification).
Each was read before filing; none covers the credential-verify path's proof binding.

## Evidence

QA finding N-1341-1 (Major, not blocking), gate43 batch #1341-#1345, evidence under
`evidence/07_probe1341_*idswap*` in that gate's report directory.

## Not measured

The production path was not driven: the vc-issuer app refuses to boot without `DATABASE_URL` and
`PRISM_AGENT_URL`, so the finding is measured on the structural path only. The fix shape is
deliberately blank — it needs a decision on where the resolver lives and what it costs a stack with
no network to an issuer's DID document.

title: Blockchain/Testing: five audit/DAST/tenant-isolation entry points default TARGET_BASE to slot 1's gateway (:6882) — an unslotted run on a slot-N worktree attacks slot 1
description:
## BLUF

Five `Blockchain/Testing` entry points fall back to `http://localhost:6882` **— slot 1's gateway — when** `TARGET_BASE` **is not passed**, instead of deriving it from `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT`. On a slot-N worktree, forgetting the variable points ZAP (active scan), the tenant-isolation job and the internal audit at whichever stack owns slot 1, which on this host is usually someone else's. That is the [KS-1373](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1373/schemathesis-full-run-named-slot-3-but-871-of-its-requests-incl) failure shape (a run named for one slot reaching another), in the shell harness rather than the Schemathesis Python readers [KS-1373](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1373/schemathesis-full-run-named-slot-3-but-871-of-its-requests-incl) fixed.

## The spots (platform-k `develop` `0aa9b52c6`)

| File:line | Default |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Testing/ci/orchestrate.sh:37` | `TARGET_BASE="${TARGET_BASE:-http://localhost:6882}"` |
| `Blockchain/Testing/ci/tools/run-schemathesis.sh:23` | same |
| `Blockchain/Testing/jobs/05-dast-zap.sh:23` | `TARGET="${TARGET_BASE:-http://localhost:6882}"` |
| `Blockchain/Testing/jobs/06-tenant-isolation.sh:31` | same |
| `Blockchain/Testing/run-internal-audit.sh:30` | `TARGET_BASE="${TARGET_BASE:-http://localhost:6882}"` |

## Verified from the code (29 Sep, re-read)

None of the five sources `stack_env.sh`, `slot-target.sh` or reads `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT`. The only callers that set `TARGET_BASE` are `.github/workflows/nightly-platform-suites.yml:558` and `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml:351` (CI, unslotted, explicit) plus two script unit tests with fixture values; `orchestrate.sh:138/159` and `run-internal-audit.sh:103` just forward whatever they resolved. `Blockchain/Testing/README.md` and `ci/README.md` never mention slots — their only `TARGET_BASE` example is `TARGET_BASE=https://secuura.com ./run-internal-audit.sh 05` — so a local run following the docs on a slot-N worktree takes the `:6882` default.

## Fix (Internal Audit Harness — Kamil's call)

Source `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh` (with `PROJECT_ROOT` set — it refuses otherwise) and default `TARGET_BASE` to `http://localhost:${GATEWAY_PORT}`; locally, refuse to start with no slot named (the [KS-1016](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1016/test-anchor-read-honesty-hardcodes-docker-exec-secuura-postgres-fails) rule), so a missing variable is an error, not a silent slot-1 run. CI stays unslotted and passes `TARGET_BASE` explicitly. Add a static check that no `Blockchain/Testing` script carries a literal slot port.

## Acceptance — comprehensive slot unit tests in the same PR

Slots are dynamic: a developer picks, drops and re-picks them at will, several sessions share one host, and slot numbers are never fixed. These five scripts run ZAP active scans, tenant-isolation probes and the audit — aimed at the wrong slot they attack another session's stack, silently. That makes this a high-risk area; `Blockchain/Testing` has no slot tests today (its only test is `ci/aggregate.test.mjs`), so the PR is not done without them:

* For each of the five entry points and `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` = 1, 2, 3, 4: with no `TARGET_BASE`, the resolved target is that slot's gateway (`6882 + 100*(N-1)` from `stack_env.sh`, not a copy of the arithmetic).
* Locally with no slot named: the script refuses with the example command — it never falls back to any slot. With an explicit `TARGET_BASE` (the CI path): it is used unchanged.
* `TARGET_BASE` and the named slot disagreeing (the [KS-1373](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1373/schemathesis-full-run-named-slot-3-but-871-of-its-requests-incl) split-target shape) refuses.
* A static guard over `Blockchain/Testing/**` failing on any literal published port of ANY slot 1..4 — bite-checked: plant one, see it red, remove it.
* Hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

## Not in this ticket

`Blockchain/Testing/` is the Internal Audit Harness (its README: "standalone, free-tools-only security and compliance harness"), not the `systemTest/` test estate — every commit to it in the last 90 days is Kamil's, hence the assignment. Product-code and template slot-1 values → [KS-1381](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381/slot-1-urls-hard-coded-outside-ks-1355s-four-spots-the-three-frontends) (Kamil) and [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a). Schemathesis Python readers → [KS-1373](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1373/schemathesis-full-run-named-slot-3-but-871-of-its-requests-incl) (done in [KS-1353: Schemathesis 4.27.5 → 4.28.0, every floor to latest, harness fixes red→green, and KS-1373 one-run-one-stack guard](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1353-schemathesis-4275-4280-every-floor-to-latest-harness-fixes-45629328f369)).

## Environment

Found 29 Sep 2026 auditing platform-k for fixed-slot URLs while pairing slot 2 for platform-s [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views).

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** points 1, 2 and 4 — the `Blockchain/Testing/**` guard in this ticket's acceptance is the point-1 guard extended over this tree, not a second one; and the CI-path criterion follows [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals)'s decision.

title: Slot-1 URLs outside KS-1355's four spots: m365's Entra redirect URI defaults to :6882 (compose + three code fallbacks), bootstrap leaves FRONTEND_URL / CORS_ORIGINS / LLM_BASE_URL at slot 1, 20 service .env.examples and two smoke scripts pin slot 1, and dead VITE_* compose values name :6882
description:
## BLUF

On a slot-N stack, **platform-k's M365 integration builds its Entra OAuth redirect URI on slot 1's gateway** (`http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback`) unless someone sets `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` by hand — the compose default and three fallbacks in `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts` all name `:6882`. And `bootstrap-env.sh` **derives only** `DATABASE_URL` **/** `REDIS_URL` **per slot**, so a fresh slot-N `.env` keeps slot 1's `FRONTEND_URL`, has no gateway origin in `CORS_ORIGINS`, and keeps `LLM_BASE_URL` on slot 1's Ollama — all three had to be edited by hand on slot 2 today. This is the remainder after [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (compose `FRONTEND_URL` / `CORS_ORIGINS` defaults, `preflight.sh:94`, `start-local.sh`, `dev-reload.sh` — excluded here). Slots are dynamic; each value should derive from `stack_env.sh`'s exported ports.

## The spots (platform-k `develop` `0aa9b52c6`, tracked files, re-read line by line 29 Sep)

**Runtime — the M365 callback points at slot 1**

| File:line | Value |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:888` | `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI=${ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI:-http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback}` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:481, 595` | `process.env.ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI \|\| \`${process.env.FRONTEND_URL || '[http://localhost:6882](<http://localhost:6882>)'}/api/m365/callback\`\` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:993` | `… \|\| 'http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback'` |

**Bootstrap — derives two URLs per slot, not the rest** (`scripts/bootstrap-env.sh:229` `DATABASE_URL`, `:240` `REDIS_URL`; nothing writes these)

| Template (`env.example` is canonical since [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap); `.env.example` is its fallback) | Key | Slot-1 value |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/env.example:146` | `CORS_ORIGINS` | `:6100–:6102` only — no gateway / website origin on any slot |
| `Blockchain/Dev/env.example:372` | `LLM_BASE_URL` | `:11434` (Ollama is offset per slot in `stack_env.sh`) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local.example:117` | `FRONTEND_URL` | `:6882` (lines 23–63 also document every social-login callback on `:6882`) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example:92, 95, 190` (fallback template) | `FRONTEND_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS` | `:6882`, `:6881` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/*/.env.example`, `services/billing/env.example` — **20 files** | `DATABASE_URL` `:6432`, `REDIS_URL` `:6379`; api-gateway `CORS_ORIGINS`; m365 `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI`; billing `API_GATEWAY_URL` | slot 1 |

**Scripts — default to slot 1**

| File:line |  |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/auth-matrix-smoke.sh:31` | `API_URL="${API_URL:-http://localhost:6882}"` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh:15` | `GATEWAY="http://localhost:6882"` — no override |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/setup-dev-environment.sh:323–324`, `start-environment.sh:241` | print slot-1 URLs whatever the slot (display only) |

**Dead config — inert, but a slot-1 literal that reads as live**

`Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:1841, 1876, 1910–1912` set `VITE_API_URL` / `VITE_ORIGINATE_URL` / `VITE_ANALYTICS_URL` to `http://localhost:6882/…` in the issuer, verifier and admin frontends' **runtime** `environment:`. Those images are static Vite builds (`RUN npm run build`, then nginx — `frontend/{issuer,verifier,admin}/Dockerfile`), `import.meta.env.VITE_*` is fixed at build time, and no build arg or `.env` supplies it, so the bundles use their relative `'/api'` fallback — correct on every slot. The values are never read; delete them so nobody takes them as the source of truth.

## Fix shape (Kamil's call)

Pass `GATEWAY_PORT` into compose for `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` and drop the three `:6882` fallbacks in m365 (fail if neither `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` nor `FRONTEND_URL` is set); have `bootstrap-env.sh` write `FRONTEND_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS` (gateway + website origins) and `LLM_BASE_URL` from `stack_env.sh` as it does `DATABASE_URL`; source `stack_env.sh` in the two smoke scripts; remove the dead `VITE_*` lines. [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s proposed `check-stack-safety.sh` pin could take a "no literal slot port outside `stack_env.sh`" rule to hold all of it.

## Acceptance — comprehensive slot unit tests in the same PR

Slots are dynamic: a developer picks, drops and re-picks them at will, several sessions share one host, and slot numbers are never fixed. A value right for the slot it was checked on is wrong on every other — and the failure is silent (a request lands on someone else's stack, or an OAuth callback on the wrong gateway). That makes this a high-risk area, so the PR is not done without unit tests that prove every changed value **for every slot 1..4, not only slot 1 or the slot the author used**:

* `scripts/__tests__/bootstrap_env_slot_ports.test.sh` extended: for `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` = 1, 2, 3, 4, a fresh bootstrap writes `FRONTEND_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS` (gateway + website origins) and `LLM_BASE_URL` on that slot's ports from `stack_env.sh` — and no other slot's port appears in the output.
* A render test (`docker compose config` per slot) asserting `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` resolves to that slot's gateway, and a unit test that `services/m365-integration` has no `:6882` fallback left (no-`ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI`, no-`FRONTEND_URL` case refuses rather than defaulting).
* The two smoke scripts target the named slot's gateway for 1..4 and refuse locally when no slot is named.
* A static guard (e.g. in `check-stack-safety.sh`) failing on any literal published port of ANY slot 1..4 outside `stack_env.sh` — bite-checked: plant one, see it red, remove it.
* Tests are hermetic: run unslotted AND under each slot's environment with identical results (the offline-suite rule), never spawned with the shell's slot variables leaking in.

## Not in this ticket

[KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s four spots. `Blockchain/Testing/**` `TARGET_BASE` defaults → [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default) (the Internal Audit Harness, Kamil). The build break → [KS-1380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1380/develop-does-not-build-since-ks-1378-1339-analytics-billing-and). `docker-compose.production.yml` (deployed, not slotted).

## Correction history

First filed 29 Sep 08:29 UTC with the `VITE_*` values as the headline ("the frontends call slot 1's gateway"). Re-checked against the Dockerfiles the same morning: they are build-time variables never supplied at build, so that claim was wrong and is now listed as dead config; the template counts and canonical-template references were also corrected.

## Environment

Peter's Mac, fresh K worktree at `0aa9b52c6`, slot 2, 29 Sep 2026. Found while pairing platform-k slot 2 for the platform-s [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views) run.

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** points 1, 2 and 5 — the static guard in this ticket's acceptance is the point-1 guard, shared with [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s `docker-compose.yml` pin (both tickets edit that file), and the two smoke scripts follow point 2.

title: develop does not build since KS-1378 (#1339): analytics, billing and governance images fail `tsc` — packages/shared now locks @types/express-serve-static-core 4.19.9 / @types/pg 8.23.1, those three services still lock 4.19.8 / 8.20.0
description:
## BLUF

A clean build of platform-k `develop` at `0aa9b52c6` fails: `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild` stops with *"Build FAILED for: analytics billing governance — not starting containers"*, so no stack comes up. The previous clean build on this Mac, at `d9ce1403d` (28 Sep), succeeded. Between the two, no `package.json` or Dockerfile of those three services changed; what changed is [KS-1378](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1378/five-new-advisories-block-every-push-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address) **(**[Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1339](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1378-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address-and-undici-off-five-815a0a16d4c7), `2cb858335`**)**, which refreshed `packages/shared/package-lock.json` and several services' locks — but not these three.

## Evidence

`packages/shared/package-lock.json` (top-level `node_modules/@types/*`):

|  | before `2cb858335` | after | `services/analytics` lock at `0aa9b52c6` |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `@types/express-serve-static-core` | 4.19.8 | **4.19.9** | 4.19.8 |
| `@types/pg` | 8.20.0 | **8.23.1** | 8.20.0 |
| `@types/express` | 4.17.25 | 4.17.25 | 4.17.25 |

Each service image copies the built `/shared` (with its own `node_modules`) beside the service's `node_modules`, so `tsc` sees two copies of the same declarations:

```
analytics  src/index.ts(34,7): error TS2742: The inferred type of 'app' cannot be named without a reference to '@secuura/shared/node_modules/@types/express-serve-static-core'. This is likely not portable.
           (also routes/analytics.ts:20, routes/dashboard.ts:12, routes/health.ts:7)
billing    src/db.ts(45,32): error TS2345: Argument of type 'import("/app/node_modules/@types/pg/index").Pool' is not assignable to parameter of type 'import("/shared/node_modules/@types/pg/index").Pool'.
           (plus TS2742 on index.ts:33, routes/billing.ts:26, routes/webhooks.ts:29)
governance same TS2742 family
```

`#1339`'s file list refreshes the locks of queue, security, timestamping, prism and others; `services/analytics`, `services/billing` and `services/governance` are not in it.

**The mismatch is wider than the three that fail (re-checked from every lock at** `0aa9b52c6`**).** Eleven service locks still carry `@types/express-serve-static-core` 4.19.8 / `@types/pg` 8.20.0 against shared's 4.19.9 / 8.23.1: analytics, billing, governance (fail) and **kyc, nft-certificate, referral, staking, tenant-provisioning, tokenisation, transfer, wallet-connector** (built fine in the same run — none of their exported types is inferred across the boundary today, so they are latent, one annotation-less `const app = express()` away from the same error). `services/shared` locks 4.19.8 and `vc-issuer` a third `@types/pg` (8.21.0). At the last good commit `d9ce1403d`, `packages/shared` itself locked 4.19.8 / 8.20.0 — every lock agreed, which is why that build passed. All 35 images were attempted in this run; exactly these three failed.

## Likely fix (Kamil's call)

Refresh the failing three — and the eight latent ones — to the same `@types/express-serve-static-core` / `@types/pg` versions `packages/shared` now pins (or pin those `@types` in shared to what the services use). A check that every service lock agrees with `packages/shared` on the `@types` it re-exports would stop the next bump doing this — [KS-953](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-953/class-editing-api-gatewaysrcindexts-silently-reddens-packagesshared) is the same class (a change in one package silently reddening another).

## Reproduce

```bash
git worktree add --detach <path> origin/develop      # 0aa9b52c6
cd <path> && SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=<N> ./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild
```

## Environment

Peter's Mac, Docker Desktop 8 CPU / 31.3 GiB, fresh K worktree at `0aa9b52c6`, slot 2, 29 Sep 2026 \~09:25–09:50 BST. Found while bringing up a paired K for the platform-s [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views) gate run. Not caused by that work (no platform-k change on it).

title: PR #1339's standalone locks were re-resolved from bare manifests: ~1,000 non-target moves, incl. runtime bullmq/msgpackr 2 and @azure/identity/msal-node 6
description:
Raised from **gate41's finding N-1339-2** (Major, non-blocking) on PR #1339 (KS-1378, the four-package advisory bump). Wednesday ruled this a ticket rather than a fold-in for round 2, because the only mechanism the gate's own fix-shape offers is `npm install --package-lock-only`, and host npm 11.5.1 dies with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')` on this machine — measured by Seat B 43rd even on a bare `package.json` in an empty temp dir, so it is the host npm build and not the workspace layout.

## What happened

#1339's 13 standalone `package-lock.json` files were regenerated **from their bare manifests** rather than from their committed locks. That resolved every dependency afresh, so about **1,000 versions moved that the bump did not target**. All are inside their declared ranges, so nothing is a range violation — but nothing exercises them either: the suites run from the **root** lock, which moved **0** non-target versions.

## The moves that matter (gate-measured)

* `services/queue`: **bullmq 5.76.2 → 5.81.5**, pulling **msgpackr 1 → 2** — runtime.
* `services/m365-integration` and `packages/shared`: **@azure/identity 4.13.1 → 4.13.3**, pulling **@azure/msal-node 5 → 6** — runtime.
* `services/originate`: minimatch 3 → 10, plus dev-only eslint-cache majors.

## Fix-shape, quoted verbatim from gate41's report

> Fix-shape: regenerate each standalone lock FROM its committed lock (`npm install <pkg>@<ver> --package-lock-only`), or declare the drift and add a standalone-install smoke (build + boot) per service.

## The condition attached to #1339 merging without this

Wednesday's ANSWER to Seat B 44th, 2026-09-29T03:54:40Z: the two runtime moves above **get a clean standalone** `npm ci` **plus that service's own suite in the next gate**, so what ships untested by the root-lock suites is tested once. **Merged is not deployed:** no deploy carries these until this ticket is done or Kam says otherwise.

## Blocked on, and why it is not just "run the command"

`npm install` in any form is unavailable on this host. Seat B 43rd's workaround for #1339 was `node:24-alpine` (npm 11.19.0), mounted at `/src` — **never** `/dev`, which clobbers the container's `/dev/null` and dies rc 127 before starting. Whoever takes this needs either that container route explicitly permitted, or a working host npm.

## Neighbours (cross-reference only)

KS-1290 (an npm command inside a workspace member moves platform discriminators silently) and KS-1154 (the root lock carries only the darwin rollup binary) are the same family — lockfile regeneration doing more than it was asked to — but neither covers this drift.

Discovered 2026-09-29 by gate41 on PR #1339; ticketed by the Platform K build seat under Wednesday's ruling.

title: Five new advisories block EVERY push: bump morgan, nodemailer, ip-address and undici (Kam ruled (a))
description:
**BLUF — the push preflight FAILS legs 6 and 7 on develop's own dependencies, so NO push on this repo succeeds until this lands.** Five newly published advisories are absent from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`. Verified ABSENT from the baseline at develop `8af6ab8216007462e596daed6b0adcd1e87e34ee` itself, so this is not caused by any open branch.

Kam ruled card `secuura-five-new-advisories-block-every-push-0929` = **(a)** on the live board 2026-09-29 11:43:09 AEST: *"Bump all four packages, with a quick reachability check in the same round."* **No baseline entry for any of the five.**

## The five, verbatim from preflight leg 6

| advisory | package | where |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GHSA-6vj9-mwq6-2f5v` | **nodemailer** | process-global DNS cache reuses the TLS `servername` across transports -> **cross-tenant SMTP credential disclosure**. 2 locks: services/auth, services/originate |
| `GHSA-9f6g-j8ch-79g4` | **morgan** | log injection via an unescaped double quote in quoted log fields. **10 service locks** |
| `GHSA-rpw4-54j3-4h4q` | **ip-address** | `Address6.isLinkLocal()` reads `fe80::/64` not `fe80::/10` -> SSRF / trust-boundary bypass. 3 locks incl. packages/shared |
| `GHSA-2vr4-cq9g-pvrc` | **ip-address** | no classifier for the NAT64 local-use range `64:ff9b:1::/48` -> SSRF / trust-boundary bypass |
| `GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v` | **undici** | DoS via an unhandled error in WebSocket permessage-deflate decompression. frontend/issuer |

Leg 6 reads `30 distinct advisories reported, 25 baselined`; leg 7 reads `26 match, 21 already baselined` across 43 standalone locks / 1591 pinned packages. Both name the same five.

## The routes are NOT uniform — measured, not assumed

* **morgan** — declared `^1.10.0` in 10 services, pinned 1.12.0, **1.12.1 published and inside the caret**: a lock refresh reaches it.
* **ip-address** — `packages/shared` declares `^10.2.0`, pinned 10.4.0, **10.7.2 inside the caret**: a lock refresh reaches it there. The `@cardano-sdk/dapp-connector` and `@cardano-sdk/key-management` nested 10.4.0 copies and a 9.0.5 are TRANSITIVE: `overrides` or a parent bump.
* 🔴 **nodemailer — a lock refresh CANNOT fix it.** The highest published 9.x **IS** `9.1.1`, exactly what is pinned; `^9.0.3` is at its ceiling and latest is `10.0.12`. It needs a **MAJOR** bump in `services/auth` and `services/originate`. This is the most expensive of the four *and* it is the credential-disclosure one.
* **undici** — TRANSITIVE only, under `jsdom` (a test dependency) plus a 5.29.0. `overrides` or a jsdom bump.

## Not to be confused with

`KS 729` is a **different** ip-address advisory (GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr). A bump here may also satisfy it; that is a bonus, not this ticket's claim.

## Scope

Bump, plus a per-advisory **reachability read** recorded in the PR body (FOUND / TESTED / HOW). **The proof is preflight legs 6 and 7 passing on the PR.** No baseline entry, no `--no-verify`. Filed by the Platform K build seat on Wednesday's instruction after Kam's ruling.

title: validate route follow-ups from the KS-1370 gate: usage_count lost update, a cache-miss read fault mislabelled, and D1 pins no write
description:
Three gate40 findings on the merged KS-1370 change (#1338, squash `8af6ab8216007462e596daed6b0adcd1e87e34ee`). One logical path: the `POST /api/keys/validate` route in `services/security`. Each item is copied verbatim from the gate40 report (`2026-09-29-batch1338-g40/report.md`, sha256 prefix `372924904c1f`). Facts only; none of the three blocks anything that shipped.

- [ ] **N-1338-3 (Minor, TICKET — MEASURED AT RUNTIME; LOST-UPDATE-CANDIDATE):** the seat's "`usage_count` written from a stale copy is a lost update" is **narrowed by half (ii) but not closed**. Two processes validating one key in sequence (B, B2, B, B2): **head 0 → 4 (exact); base 0 → 2 (the stale-copy loss)**. Twenty CONCURRENT validates (10 on each process): **head 0 → 12 (run 1: 11); base 0 → 9 (run 1: 10)**. The remaining loss is a read-modify-write race: `usage_count = $3` is written from a value read one statement earlier. Fix-shape: `SET usage_count = usage_count + 1, last_used_at = GREATEST(last_used_at, $2)`. Regression cell: two instances × N concurrent validates on the real DB, asserting usage_count == N. Usage is telemetry, not an auth decision, so this is a ticket, not a block.
- [ ] **N-1338-4 (Minor, TICKET — MEASURED AT RUNTIME; pre-existing, unchanged by this PR):** a failed read on a cache MISS answers **200** `valid:false, 'Key not found'` (plus a warn line). The same fault on a cache HIT now answers **503**. Both are refused, and through the gateway both become a 30 s cached 401, so this is **coherent with "A revoked key is never honoured"**. But the miss branch mislabels a database fault as an unknown key, and auth's connector-token returns 401 there instead of 502. Fix-shape: give the cache-miss branch the same 503 on a failed read (a product decision; outside card-2's scope). Cell: miss + read fault → 503.
- [ ] **N-1338-5 (Minor, TICKET — PROBED; NOT-PINNED):** D1 asserts the answer and the eviction but **not that no write was issued**. The base's vanished-row RESURRECTION therefore has no cell. The head prevents it structurally (early return), but nothing pins that. Cell: in D1, assert the mock recorded no INSERT/UPDATE (`state.usageSql.length === 0`).

Adjacent, not duplicated: KS 1174 covers the gateway collapsing every API-key failure into 401, which is the gateway half of N-1338-4's symptom, not the security route's miss branch.

Refs KS-1370

title: Security: certifications ends RLS FORCE with no tenant_isolation policy on every fresh database, permanently
description:
**Found by the gate39 QA pass over PR #1332 (N-G39-1, Major). Facts only.**

## What is wrong

On a **fresh bare database**, `public.certifications` ends with row-level security **ENABLED and FORCED but with no** `tenant_isolation` **policy**. RLS with no policy is **default-deny**, so the table is unreadable and unwritable by the application role — and unlike the defect #1332 fixed, **this does not heal on a later boot**. It is permanent for the life of that database.

Measured across all four head paths (gateway runner boot 1 and boot 2, `scripts/run-migrations.sh`, and both combined): identical, `4c59e2ebdc37`. The **merge-base differs** (`fd91b0ab5a48`) and **does** carry `CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON public.certifications` — so the merge-base heals it and the current tip does not. An app-role `INSERT` carrying the tenant GUC is **refused**.

## Why it changed

`migrations/038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` (added in #1332) creates `certifications` **before** 039 runs. 039 then finds the table present and applies its RLS `ENABLE`/`FORCE` block to it — but the branch of 039 that creates the `tenant_isolation` policy does not cover it on that path. Before #1332, `certifications` did not exist when 039 ran, so 039 skipped it entirely and a later boot created it with its policy intact.

## A FALSE CLAIM IN THE MERGED CODE, filed here deliberately rather than separately (N-G39-4)

`038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` lines **16-17** describe this exact condition — `certifications` with RLS forced and no `tenant_isolation` policy — as one of the things the migration **fixes**. **It does not fix it; it is the cause of it.** The same header's claim that the schema equality is "proved … across … the docker/init seeded path" is also **wider than true**: the equality holds for `certifications` only, and fails for `oauth_apps` and `svc_webhooks` because of a pre-existing docker/init DDL difference (extra indexes and the `svc_webhooks_app_id_fkey` foreign key). Both header claims need correcting in the same change that fixes the policy, so the file does not keep asserting a fix it does not deliver.

## Fix shape (from the gate)

A migration numbered **after 039** that applies 039's `tenant_isolation` block to `certifications`, plus a **real-PostgreSQL cell driven as the application role** (`secuura_app`) asserting that an `INSERT` carrying the correct tenant GUC succeeds and one carrying a foreign tenant is refused. A source-text assertion is not sufficient here: the defect is a runtime default-deny, and only a driven app-role probe distinguishes "policy present" from "policy absent but table reachable as owner".

## Scope

Not fixed in #1332 — that PR was round 2 of 2 under the class cap and shipped GO WITH FINDINGS with this as named residue. No board ticket covered it before this one (searched by symbol: `certifications` + `tenant_isolation`, `tenant_isolation policy certifications`, `038a`, `certifications RLS force default-deny`, `certifications no tenant_isolation` — zero title-relevant results; three positive controls each returned their expected ticket first, so the search was working).

Refs KS-1054

title: Security: a revoked credential resubmitted with any other id verifies TRUE — neither verify route wires a didResolver, so the proof's id binding is never checked outside production
description:
**BLUF — the gate measured this at runtime on the merged code (gate38 finding N-1330-1, Major). A credential revoked through** `POST /api/credentials/:id/revoke`**, resubmitted with any other** `id`**, answers** `verified: true` **with** `checks.status: true`**.** Measured at the PR head and at the merged END.

This is not a defect of #1330 against its ruling — an edited id *is* an unknown id, and pass-through for unknown ids is the open card's default. It is filed because the measured cost of that default is **wider than the card prices it**.

**The mechanism, as the gate read and drove it:**

* Both revocation resolvers key on the caller-supplied `credential.id`, and the stored-record arm abstains on `found: false` (`services/vc-issuer/src/services/revocationResolvers.ts`; `packages/shared/src/vc/verifier.ts` :478-:484).
* **Neither verify route wires a** `didResolver`, so an Ed25519 proof gets a structural check only unless `NODE_ENV === 'production'` (`verifier.ts` :372-:396, read).
* The proof payload **does** cover `id`, so a wired didResolver would catch the edit.
* In production every Ed25519 credential already fails with `No DID resolver configured…` (pre-existing, read, not driven).

**Why it matters more than the card says.** The card `secuura-ks1352-unknown-credential-id-verify-policy` (open, `ruled_ts` null) prices its option a as "a revoked credential whose record was lost still verifies true" — an accident. The measured behaviour is deliberate and trivial: **any holder of a revoked credential can un-revoke it on a development-mode stack by editing one field.**

**Fix-shape (the gate's, quoted):** "wire the issuer's DID resolver on both verify routes so the proof binds `id` (then an edited id fails signature), or key revocation on a proof-bound value."

**Regression cell (the gate's, quoted):** "revoke R1, submit `{...doc, id: 'urn:x'}`, expect `verified: false`."

**Relation to the shipped work.** #1330 (squash `9caa42ad05f145251db820ba43eaf7941316668f`) is what makes revocation reachable at all; before it, verify consulted no authority. This finding is the remaining hole in the id-keyed approach. The unknown-id policy question itself is KS 1368; this ticket is the measured cost that should inform it.

**Board search before filing, with controls:** `didResolver`, `revocationResolvers`, `id-edit`, `edited id`, `No DID resolver` all returned **0**; the positive control `statusListResolver` on the same literal query shape returned **1** (KS-1352), and a nonsense control returned 0.

title: Akto scans are now paced to fit the platform's rate limit — test times went up; which way should we go?
description:
## BLUF

Kamil, when you have a moment: **we need your decision on how the platform's rate limit should treat our Akto scans.** To stop 429s being counted as passes, the scans are now slowed to 1,500 requests/min using Akto's own rate limit (systemTest only, no platform code changed). Coverage is honest, but **pre-merge went from 47 s to 19 m 28 s, and the security tier now takes about an hour.** Six options are below, most of them gateway-side, which is yours. Once we've agreed one, either of us can make the change. **Reducing test coverage is not an option.** Thank you.

+++ What was added, and what it costs (measured)

**The pacing** ([KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and) branch; [KS-709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-709/akto-reports-a-pass-for-a-test-that-executed-nothing-clean-0-not) for the false passes it fixes)

* Akto reads a per-account `globalRateLimit` from its Mongo once a minute. `systemTest/akto/tests/tierPacingSetup.ts` sets it per tier: **pr unthrottled; pre-merge and security at 1,500/min** (0.75 × the platform's 2,000/min, derived in `src/setup/aktoRateLimit.ts`), restored to unthrottled afterwards. `AKTO_GLOBAL_RATE_LIMIT=N` overrides it.
* Before any setup login, the harness also waits (≤61 s, probing `GET /api/auth/me`) for the 60-second window to have room, since back-to-back tiers were having their setup logins refused ([KS-1362](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1362/back-to-back-tiers-setup-logins-land-in-the-platforms-spent-60-second)).

**Measured on slot 2 of the Mac, 2026-09-28, Akto 2.35.6**

| tier | unpaced | paced at 1,500/min |
| -- | -- | -- |
| pr | 29 s — 8,702 results, 129 refused | (left unpaced) |
| pre-merge | **47 s** — only 1,057 actually tested, **8,129 refused** | **19 m 28 s** — 192 refused |
| full OWASP scan | 423.8 s — **8,730 of 50,162 refused** | **\~27 min — 0 of 50,306 refused** |
| whole security tier | — | **60 m 52 s** |

Two things to expect at any pace: Akto overshoots its setting by about 10%, and it releases each minute's allowance as a \~5 s burst, so the first minute of a paced run still sees a few refusals.

**The platform side as it stands** (read-only)

* Global limiter: `api-gateway/src/index.ts:472-485` — 60 s window, `max = RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS || (non-prod ? 10000 : 300)`; `.env.example:205` sets **2000**. Keyed per address, and every caller on the host shares `192.168.65.1` ([KS-618](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-618/client-ip-is-invisible-platform-wide-on-demo-every-ip-keyed-control)).
* Skip rules: `middleware/rateLimitSkip.ts` — read-only paths; an operator override `DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT=true` in non-prod envs; and a `Bearer test_token_` bypass when `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS=true` in `development`/`test`.
* nginx (`nginx-demo.conf:171-172`, VM demo) adds `limit_req` at 50 r/s (api) and 5 r/s (auth).

+++

+++ The options, as I see them

1. **Keep things as they are** — harness-side pacing only; no platform change. *Cost:* pre-merge \~20 min and security \~1 h locally. The limiter stays exactly as deployed.
2. **Raise** `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS` **for local stacks only** (e.g. back to the code's non-prod default of 10,000, or a figure you choose), leaving demo and production alone. The harness would pace to the new figure automatically, since it derives its rate from this value. *Cost:* local stacks stop matching the demo's limiter, so a limiter regression would be less likely to show locally.
3. **Use the existing operator override** — `DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT=true` on local non-prod stacks during scans. *Cost:* the global limiter is out of the picture entirely, including the verifier rate-limiting test's realism; easy to leave on by accident.
4. **Key the limiter per authenticated principal** (user or token) instead of per address — so the scanner's personas, k6 and a human each get their own budget. *Cost:* a real design change with security implications; overlaps [KS-618](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-618/client-ip-is-invisible-platform-wide-on-demo-every-ip-keyed-control).
5. **A dedicated, higher budget for a scanner identity in non-prod only** (e.g. a service account or a signed header, gated like the existing test-token bypass). *Cost:* a new bypass surface that has to be airtight to non-prod.
6. **Tune the harness further, no platform change** — pace closer to 2,000 (e.g. 0.85×) to save a few minutes at the price of a few more first-minute refusals, or pace fewer tiers. *Cost:* marginal gains; the limiter still sets the floor.

+++

## Where I'd love your guidance

1. Which option (or combination) fits how you want the limiter to behave?
2. Should local stacks match the demo's limits exactly, or is a looser local limit acceptable for testing?
3. Is \~20 min for pre-merge and \~1 h for security acceptable as a local gate, or is it worth a platform change to bring those down?

Once we've agreed a direction, either of us can make the change — whichever is more convenient. The one thing that isn't on the table is reducing test coverage: every option above keeps the same templates, tiers and endpoints, and changes only how fast they run or how the limit is set. No platform code has been touched so far.

## Checklist item added after the merge of PR #1347 (squash `8c810023f9c9`)

- [X] **N-1347-11 — the residue of the target-keyed pacing.** Closed by PR #1349, merged to `develop` as squash `691bb93e5c530c845ba0926ab0f369d5dc502720`: `isLocalScanTarget()` now reads `OVERRIDE_APP_URL` first and falls back to `SECUURA_API_URL`, the same precedence `systemTest/akto/src/scan/scanOptions.ts:98` uses for the host the scan attacks. With `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS=10000` reaching the harness (a raised local `.env`), a scan aimed at a remote stack through `OVERRIDE_APP_URL` alone was paced at 7500/min and is now paced at 1500, and an `OVERRIDE_APP_URL` pointing at localhost is paced at 7500. Without that raised value, and without `AKTO_PLATFORM_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE`, every target is paced at 1500, as before. Checked by unit tests only (9 cells: 4 that fail on the previous code, 5 controls); no Akto scan was run against any stack, and the demo's own `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS` has not been read.

description:
## Summary

Thank you for flagging this; it was worth chasing. The evidence now points **away** from the slot-3 sweep itself and towards a legitimate slot-1 run of the same harness's pytest tier in another session. That can't be proven from what's left on disk, though. Separately, the investigation surfaced a **real way one run could address two stacks**, and that is now fixed on the [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) branch with red → green tests.

**Status by section:**

| Section | Status |
| -- | -- |
| Fix: one resolver for every reader, and refusing a split target | ✅ **Done**: commits `d3d95efb0`, `1f3f054c0`, in PR [KS-1353: Schemathesis 4.27.5 → 4.28.0, every floor to latest, harness fixes red→green, and KS-1373 one-run-one-stack guard](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1353-schemathesis-4275-4280-every-floor-to-latest-harness-fixes-45629328f369) |
| Regression tests (red on the old code, green after) | ✅ **Done**: 136 new tests (33 red on the old readers) |
| Name the responsible leg with proof (reproduction) | ☑️ **Closed on correlation (2026-09-30)**: not reproduced; the ticket was accepted as Done on the timing and User-Agent evidence below. See *Suggested next step* if certainty is wanted later |

## What the evidence says (measured 2026-09-28)

* **The User-Agent belongs to the harness's pytest client, not the Schemathesis engine.** `secuura-schemathesis-test` is `TEST_USER_AGENT` in `src/http_client.py`, used only by `tests/conftest.py` and the pytest suites. The Schemathesis subprocess and its hooks never import it.
* **The slot-3 sweep's own traffic all reached slot 3.** Every interaction recorded in sweep 6's NDJSON went to `localhost:7082` (24,976 of 24,976), and the same holds for sweeps 1–5.
* **Timing.** Sweep 6's pytest suites finished at 14:37:27 BST (IDOR 14:32:58, integration 14:33:49, anchoring 14:37:25, preconditions 14:37:27). After that only the Schemathesis subprocess ran, which can't send that User-Agent. The stray requests arrived at 14:37:54–14:38:21 BST.
* **A likely source.** The [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) session's note on [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) records running `run.py quality` **through** `run-in-slot.sh 1`, which drives this exact pytest tier against slot 1, as intended. That tier makes the logged calls (login, register, `users/me`, then undeclared-method DELETEs across `admin/api-keys`, `analytics`, `anchors` from `test_undeclared_method_safety.py`), and it takes 25–48 s. That matches 871 requests in 27 s.
* **Not provable now.** The [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) worktree has been removed, so there's no artefact to timestamp against. This stays a strong correlation, stated as such.

## ✅ Done: what was found and fixed ([KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) branch, commits `d3d95efb0`, `1f3f054c0`, PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1335](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1353-schemathesis-4275-4280-every-floor-to-latest-harness-fixes-45629328f369))

Four readers chose the target gateway differently from the project's one resolver (`resolve_gateway_url()`, which prefers `SECUURA_BASE_URL`):

| Reader | Drives | Before |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `src/config.py` | the pytest suites' client | `API_BASE_URL`, else an import-time default |
| `src/anchoring/config.py` | the anchoring suite | same |
| `scripts/setup_paths.py` | `setup.py` provisioning | same |
| `scripts/runner/config.py` | the runner's env default | `API_BASE_URL` before `SECUURA_BASE_URL` (latent) |

So a shell where the two variables differed could send the sweep and persona logins to one stack and the pytest suites to another, with no error. The pytest client also never applied the "name your slot" rule, so an unslotted `pytest tests/` quietly drove slot 1.

**Now:**

* All four readers go through the one resolver, at call time.
* A new coherence check (`gateway_signal_conflicts()` / `assert_gateway_signals_agree()` in `src/slot.py`) refuses to start when the slot variables and the two URL variables disagree.
* The check is enforced in the runner's startup guard, `load_config()` and the anchoring config.
* A targeting refusal is no longer turned into a quiet credentials skip.

**Tests (✅ done):** 136 new, across two modules:

* the conflict matrix over every slot pair;
* all six readers agreeing for every slot and every environment shape;
* a derived source scan that allows direct reads in only three named modules.

They were red on the old readers (33 failed) and are green now. The offline suite is **2,825/2,825** unslotted and under the full slot-wrapper environment for slots 1–4; the live integration tier is 386 passed on the pushed head.

## ⏳ Open: suggested next step, when convenient

The ticket's own "done means" asks for the responsible leg to be named. If you'd like certainty, a short reproduction on an idle pair of slots (a closed listener on one, a run on the other) would settle it. The coherence check now makes the most plausible in-run mechanism refuse to start, so a repeat would show up as an error rather than stray traffic.

Related: [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) · [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) · [KS-1016](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1016/test-anchor-read-honesty-hardcodes-docker-exec-secuura-postgres-fails) · [KS-672](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-672/schemathesis-integration-suite-escapes-slot-targeting-a-slot-3-pre) · [KS-1362](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1362/back-to-back-tiers-setup-logins-land-in-the-platforms-spent-60-second)

title: api-gateway failed-login lockout is inert: createBruteForceProtection installs recordFailure, but no production code ever calls it — it can never block
description:
## Summary

For when you have a moment, Kamil. The gateway's failed-login lockout (`createBruteForceProtection`, `api-gateway/src/middleware/security.ts:146-192`) looks as though it never engages: it only blocks once `recordFailure()` has run, and nothing outside its own unit test seems to call it. The auth service's per-account lockout is still doing its job, so this is about the edge layer only. Either wiring it up or retiring it would be fine; whichever you prefer. Thank you.

+++ Evidence, and the two options

**What the code shows** (read-only, 2026-09-28)

* `security.ts:173-189` attaches `req.bruteForce = { recordFailure, recordSuccess }` and calls `next()`; nothing on the login's response path calls either helper.
* Searching `services/api-gateway/src` for `recordFailure` outside `middleware/security.ts` finds only `__tests__/security.test.ts:261`, which checks the helper exists.
* So `attempts` is never incremented, `blockedUntil` is never written, and the `429 "Too many failed attempts"` branch can't be reached.

**What the logs show**

* Slot 2's gateway, six hours of traffic including failed logins: **0** `BRUTE_FORCE_LOCKOUT`, **0** `BRUTE_FORCE_BLOCKED`.
* The lockout that does work is the auth service's (`services/auth/src/services/accountLockout.ts`: (email, /24), 5 failures in 15 min → 15-min lock). It answers **401** (`routes/auth.ts:339-342`).

**Why it came up:** [KS-1362](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1362/back-to-back-tiers-setup-logins-land-in-the-platforms-spent-60-second) first put some refused setup logins down to this lockout; on a closer look they were the global request window. It seemed worth recording that this layer isn't active, so no one leans on it.

**Options**

1. Wire it: call `recordFailure` / `recordSuccess` from the login proxy's response handling (401 / 2xx), with a test that shows a block after `freeRetries` failures.
2. Retire it: remove the middleware, its `bruteForce` config in `config/services.ts`, and the doc line at `security.ts:8`.

[KS-618](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-618/client-ip-is-invisible-platform-wide-on-demo-every-ip-keyed-control) (every IP-keyed control is shared behind one address) applies either way.

**Done means:** a test red on today's code shows N+1 failed logins from one address aren't blocked at the gateway; after the change they are — or the middleware and its claims are gone.

+++

title: POST /api/status/{id}/unrevoke accepts `index: -1` (below the declared minimum) with 200 and performs the unrevoke — outside the KS-662 ruling, which tolerates only a non-string `reason` here
description:
## Summary

When you have a moment, Kamil; this one touches revocation records, so it's worth a look. `POST /api/status/{id}/unrevoke` with `index: -1` answers 200 and completes the unrevoke, in every one of the six [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) sweeps. The [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the) ruling only tolerates a non-string `reason` on unrevoke, so this sits just outside it, much like [KS-1269](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1269/post-apistatusidrevoke-accepts-index-object-where-integer-is-declared) on revoke. Validating `index` before the write, or deliberately widening the ruling, would settle it. Thank you.

+++ Full evidence

Body `{"credentialId": "example-credentialId", "index": -1}` → **200** `{"statusListId": "…", "credentialId": "example-credentialId", "revoked": false, "unrevokedAt": "…"}`. Coverage phase, *"index: Value smaller than minimum"*, ×1 in each sweep:

| Sweep | Stack | Result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1–5 | `d9ce1403d` | 200 `revoked:false`, every sweep |
| 6 (merged `develop`) | `8a3413f26` | 200 `revoked:false` |

* The ruling's unrevoke allowance is `_tolerated_non_string_reason` at `systemTest/schemathesis/config/check_predicates.py:499`; below-minimum `index` is tolerated on **revoke** only.
* All six sweeps already include [KS-692](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-692/security-apistatus-revokeunrevoke-has-no-tenant-ownership-check-an)'s narrowing (status-list writes limited to platform admins).
* The credential id is the spec's placeholder, and it still answered 200. That *may* mean unrevoke doesn't check the credential exists. It's an observation from the response, not verified against the database.

**Reproduce** (platform admin, local slot):

```bash
curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"credentialId": "example-credentialId", "index": -1}' "$GATEWAY/api/status/0/unrevoke"
```

**Options:** validate `index` against its declared bounds before the write (the guard stays as the regression pin), or widen the ruling deliberately and update `check_predicates.py` with it. Listed for baselining against this ticket in [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing).

+++

title: Security: validate reads API keys from a boot-only memory map, so a revoked key keeps authenticating AND its usage write rewrites is_active = true over the revoke
description:
**BLUF — measured from the source path at develop** `0d156d12`**, and it is worse than a multi-replica write-back concern: it is also a live authentication bypass on a single process.**

`POST /api/keys/validate` in `services/security/src/index.ts` resolves the key from an **in-memory map first** and reads the database **only on a cache miss**:

* `:1326` `let apiKey = Array.from(memApiKeys.values()).find(k => k.keyHash === keyHash);`
* `:1328-1334` the code's own comment states the map "is populated **only at boot** from svc_api_keys".
* `:1335` the DB fallback (`security_find_api_key_by_hash`) runs **only** `if (!apiKey)`, and `:1347` warms the cache.

So once a key is in memory, this process never re-reads its row. Two consequences follow, and the second is the one the KS-888 validate brief raised:

**1. A revoked key keeps authenticating.** `:1358` `if (!apiKey.isActive)` is evaluated against the **stale memory copy**. If the row is set inactive by anything this process did not do — the revoke route on another replica, an operator UPDATE, a future admin tool — this process answers `valid: true` until it restarts.

**2. The usage write then UNDOES the revoke for everyone.** `:1369` `await dbSaveApiKey(apiKey);` and the upsert at `:316-318` is `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET last_used_at = EXCLUDED.last_used_at, usage_count = EXCLUDED.usage_count, is_active = EXCLUDED.is_active`. `EXCLUDED.is_active` comes from the in-memory `k.isActive`, which is still `true`. So a validate on a stale copy writes `is_active = true` over a persisted revoke. The revoke is lost in the database, not merely missed locally.

**What is measured and what is not.** Every line above is read at `0d156d12` and quoted. The control flow is decisive on its own: memory-first, DB-on-miss-only, boot-only population, and the upsert asserting `is_active` from that copy. What is **NOT** done is a driven two-process run demonstrating the lost revoke end to end — that needs two memory maps over one database and is the natural first step for whoever takes this.

**Why it is not KS-888.** KS-888 is about what happens when the usage write *fails* (mint refuses, revoke answers 503, validate logs and continues — all shipped or pinned). This is about the write *succeeding* and carrying a stale field. The pin for validate's log-only behaviour is PR #1334; it does not touch this and must not be read as covering it.

**Board search before filing, with controls:** `EXCLUDED.is_active`, `populated only at boot`, `security_find_api_key_by_hash`, `stale memory`, `revoked key still validates` all returned **0**; positive controls on the same literal query shape returned `memApiKeys` 4, `dbSaveApiKey` 3, `is_active` 2, and the nonsense control 0. The four `memApiKeys` hits (KS-1174, KS-889, KS-888, KS-869) were each read and none covers this: they are the gateway's 401 collapsing, the connector_id backfill window, the KS-888 save-failure family, and connector_id persistence.

**Shapes worth considering (not a recommendation).** Narrowest: drop `is_active` from the upsert's SET list, so a usage write can never assert liveness. That closes consequence 2 and leaves consequence 1. Wider: re-read the row (or invalidate the cache entry) before answering, which closes both and costs a query per validate on a deliberately unauthenticated hot path.

title: api-gateway crashes under load: onProxyReq calls setHeader after the proxied request's headers were sent — uncaught exception, 13 restarts, 502s on /api/auth/login
description:
## Summary

When you get a chance, Kamil — this one does hurt under load. During the [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) k6 runs, the api-gateway process exited on an uncaught exception thrown from its own proxy hook, and Docker restarted it 13 times in about five minutes. nginx answered 502 while it was down. The hook calls `setHeader` on a request whose headers were already sent, and nothing guards or catches that. A small guard plus an error path would likely settle it; your call on the shape. Thank you.

+++ Evidence, impact and a suggested direction

**The throw** (31 occurrences in the gateway log)

```
Uncaught exception {"error":"Cannot set headers after they are sent to the client"}
  at ClientRequest.setHeader (node:_http_outgoing:684:11)
  at ProxyServer.onProxyReq (/app/dist/routes/proxy.js:254:26)
  at ProxyServer.emit (/app/node_modules/eventemitter3/index.js:184:35)
  at ClientRequest.<anonymous> (/app/node_modules/http-proxy/lib/http-proxy/passes/web-incoming.js:133:16)
  at tickOnSocket (node:_http_client:1116:7)
```

`dist/routes/proxy.js:254` is the hook's first statement, `proxyReq.setHeader('X-Request-ID', requestId)` — source `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:246` (mapped by reading the compiled file in the running container). None of the hook's later header writes (vouch `:276`, policy headers, `Authorization`, the [KS-453](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-453/did-endpoints-getpatchdelete-apididdid-return-502-on-malformed-did) body re-stream) checks `proxyReq.headersSent` either.

**Where:** local slot 1, api-gateway built from develop `63db8a383` ([KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) changes no service code); Apple M2 Max, four stacks up. Load: k6 `scalability` (12:54–13:15Z) then `auth-spike` (13:15–13:17Z, 150 VUs on `POST /api/auth/login`). First crash 13:12:11Z; `restartCount=13`, last start 13:17:36Z; healthy afterwards.

**What callers saw**

| Signal | Value |
| -- | -- |
| nginx, `POST /api/auth/login` during auth-spike | **11,362 × 502** + 6,123 × 429 |
| scalability | thresholds 6/6, but **14.8 %** `http_req_failed`, 65,192 failed checks |
| auth-spike | INVALID — all 17,788 logins failed |
| auth service, same second as the first crash | `DB getUserByEmail failed … timeout exceeded when trying to connect` |

The auth DB-pool timeout looks like the trigger; the gateway turning it into a process exit is the defect.

**Ruled out:** slots sharing a database (each has its own Postgres + pgbouncer network), and the harness/k6 version (the trace is inside api-gateway; other k6 scenarios pass).

**Suggested direction**

1. Return early from the hook when `proxyReq.headersSent` (or the request is destroyed).
2. Let the proxy's error path answer 502/503 rather than letting a handler throw reach `uncaughtException` (the class [KS-1242](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1242/t-1-authenticatetoken-is-an-async-express-4-middleware-with-no-catch-a) describes for `authenticateToken`).
3. A regression test driving `onProxyReq` with an already-sent `proxyReq`, red on today's code.

**Reproduce:** `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD=… systemTest/run-in-slot.sh 1 bash -c 'cd systemTest/performance && npm run test:scalability'`, then `npm run test:auth-spike`; watch `docker inspect secuura-api-gateway --format '{{.RestartCount}}'` and `docker logs secuura-api-gateway | grep "Cannot set headers"`.

**Related:** [KS-1242](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1242/t-1-authenticatetoken-is-an-async-express-4-middleware-with-no-catch-a) (async middleware without a catch — same class, different site) · [KS-744](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-744/gateway-500s-on-every-proxied-route-for-a-token-lacking) (unguarded header set in `auth.ts:377`) · [KS-1362](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1362/back-to-back-tiers-setup-logins-land-in-the-platforms-spent-60-second) (back-to-back tiers' setup logins refused inside a spent request window — the 429 side of busy runs) · [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) (where it was found) · [KS-491](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-491/review-f-edge-waf-ddos-and-anti-automation) (Review F — availability under load).

+++

## Checklist item added after the merge of PR #1342 (squash `67c73393dfa0`)

- [ ] **N-1342-1 (Major, not blocking):** under keep-alive agent saturation (more than 128 requests in
  flight to one upstream), a **body-parsed** POST whose headers were already sent is delivered to the
  upstream with its `Content-Length` and **zero body bytes**. The guard skips the re-stream, so the
  upstream waits and the client gets a TCP reset at exactly 60.0 s, with **no 502 and no log line**.
  At develop before #1342 the same request **crashes** the process, so the merged change is strictly
  better — this is residue, not a regression. The raw-stream `/api/auth/login` route is unaffected
  (140/140 delivered). Evidence: `evidence/runs/probe1342b.log` and `probe1342c.log` in the gate43
  batch #1341-#1345 report directory.

title: Verify policy for a credential id with NO stored record — KS-1352 ships pass-through, and the unknown-id case is unruled
description:
**BLUF — a policy question, not a defect report. Nothing is built for this.**

KS-1352 made `POST /api/credentials/verify` refuse a credential that its stored issuer record **or** the status list marks revoked. It deliberately does **not** change the answer for a credential id that **no authority holds a record for**. That case needs a ruling.

**What ships today (pass-through).** The stored-record arm ABSTAINS when `credentialRepo.getById()` returns nothing: the status-list arm and the cryptographic proof still decide, so an unknown id verifies exactly as it did before KS-1352.

**Why it was not decided in KS-1352.** The ruling on that ticket is that a *revoked* credential fails. An unknown credential is a different case, and failing closed would have widened the ruling with a measured cost: `credentialRepo.loadFromDb()` returns silently when the database is unavailable (`credentialRepo.ts:212`) and the memory store then starts empty, so a fail-closed rule would refuse **every** credential on a process with no database.

**The gap this leaves, stated plainly.** A credential that was genuinely revoked but whose stored record was lost — the swallowed-DB-write path at `credentialRepo.ts:78`, or a replica that never issued it — still verifies as valid. That is a thinner version of the defect KS-1352 fixed.

**The options.**

1. **Pass-through (today).** An unknown id verifies on its proof alone. Preserves availability; keeps the gap above.
2. **Fail-closed with a distinct reason.** `verified: false`, `checks.status: false`, reason `no issuer record` — deliberately not the word "revoked", so `determineStatus()` does not mislabel it. Closes the gap; refuses every credential wherever the store cannot answer.
3. **Conditional.** Fail closed only when the store is known-answerable (database reachable), pass through otherwise. Closes the gap in normal operation but is itself fail-open during an outage.

**Where the boundary is pinned.** Cell `C2` in `services/vc-issuer/src/__tests__/ks1352-revoked-credential-fails-verify.test.ts` asserts that an id with no stored record still verifies true, so option 1 cannot be changed by accident — whichever option is chosen, that cell is the one to edit.

Measured on develop `0d156d12`. A literal board search found no existing ticket covering this (`unknown-id`, `not in the store`, `unknown credential`, `verify policy`, `storedRecordResolver` all 0; positive controls on the same query shape returned 1, 2 and 23).

title: Renovate's k6 rule sees only the Dockerfile FROM, not config/observability.yml — the pin the runner actually launches
description:
## Summary

A gentle tidy-up, not urgent. Renovate's k6 rule only sees the Dockerfile's `FROM`, while the runner actually launches the image pinned in `config/observability.yml`. So a Renovate PR would bump the file we don't run. [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released)'s pin-parity test already turns such a PR red, so nothing slips through; it would just be noise. The config itself is repo-level supply chain (Kamil's stream E), so it's worth agreeing the shape with him first.

+++ Where k6 is pinned, and what done looks like

Found in [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) (k6 2.1.0 → 2.3.0, 2026-09-28).

| Site | Role |
| -- | -- |
| `systemTest/performance/config/observability.yml` `docker.k6Image` | the pin the runner launches (`runner/k6_docker.ts`) |
| `systemTest/performance/docker/k6/Dockerfile` `FROM` | never built by the runner; read by the CVE gate |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/base-image-watch.sh` `EXCLUDED_BASES` | CVE-gate disposition |

`renovate.json` has one k6 rule — `{"matchDatasources":["docker"],"matchPackageNames":["grafana/k6"],"groupName":"k6 runtime"}` — and no `customManagers`, so only the `FROM` line is seen.

**Already in place:** `systemTest/performance/tests/unit/config/k6ImagePinParity.test.ts` fails when the three sites disagree.

**Open questions**

* Is the Renovate GitHub App installed? `systemTest/performance/docs/quick-start.md` calls it a one-time prerequisite; nothing records that it was done.
* The config change sits in Kamil's work-stream E ([KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490/review-e-deployment-containers-and-cicd-supply-chain)).

**Done when**

- [ ] A Renovate `customManagers` regex covers `observability.yml` `k6Image` and `base-image-watch.sh`, grouped with the Dockerfile rule so one PR moves all three.
- [ ] Whether the Renovate app is installed is recorded.
- [ ] Kamil has agreed the config change (stream E).

+++
