description:
## Summary

For when you have a moment, Stuart. Two small bits of drift in the merge-flow paperwork you own, spotted while preparing the [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) PR. The PR template still suggests dispatching the retired `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` and has no Test Evidence block. And the Test Evidence templates in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `DEV-PROCESS.md` have drifted apart. Nothing has been changed. Thank you.

+++ Evidence (develop `63db8a383`, 2026-09-28) and what "done" could look like

**1.** `.github/pull_request_template.md` **and the adopted merge flow**

* It asks authors to dispatch `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml`. Root `CLAUDE.md` (*Merge flow*), `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` and [KS-441](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-441/akto-ci-scan-throughput-21-s-local-vs-10-min-in-the-isolated-pr-akto) say not to: Actions is retired, and the gate is a local four-suite run.
* It has no Test Evidence block (touched / ran / NOT run / migrations+config), which the merge flow relies on. `grep -ci 'Test Evidence' .github/pull_request_template.md` → **0**.

**2. The two Test Evidence templates**

`DEV-PROCESS.md` says it uses the same wording as `CONTRIBUTING.md`, but:

* `grep -c 'Cross-cutting guards' Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` → **2**
* `grep -c 'Cross-cutting guards' Blockchain/Dev/CONTRIBUTING.md` → **0**

`CONTRIBUTING.md` also lacks DEV-PROCESS's Schemathesis "failing SET + diff vs develop" wording.

**Why here:** it belongs to the process [KS-685](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-685/define-the-work-test-commit-manual-merge-process-while-ci-is) set up (now Deployed to UAT), so there was no open ticket to add it to.

**Related:** [KS-1049](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1049/a-prs-test-evidence-must-state-whether-the-preflight-ran-the-hook) (Kamil — Test Evidence should say whether the preflight ran; the template would be its home) · [KS-1012](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1012/the-require-pr-gates-ruleset-survived-the-actions-retirement-7) (the `require-pr-gates` ruleset outlived Actions).

**Done when**

- [ ] The PR template no longer mentions dispatching the retired workflow.
- [ ] The PR template seeds the Test Evidence block, including a preflight-ran line ([KS-1049](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1049/a-prs-test-evidence-must-state-whether-the-preflight-ran-the-hook)).
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `DEV-PROCESS.md` share one Test Evidence template (one canonical copy; the other points at it).

+++

title: systemTest docs still describe GitHub Actions as live, and the history + test-discipline skill have gone stale
description:
## Why

Found while re-checking [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) (k6 2.1.0 → 2.3.0) on 2026-09-28, measured on its branch at `7d98a4f1d` (develop `63db8a383`). None of it is caused by the k6 bump, and it spans every suite, so it was deliberately kept out of that branch: folding it in would have added \~14 more edits to the two HTML docs that [KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and) also changes, widening a merge conflict that already exists.

## 1. "k6 live on the PR tier" after Actions was retired

GitHub Actions is retired for this repo (Kam, 2026-08-27; `CLAUDE.md` → *Merge flow*; `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md`). The two QA HTML docs still say k6 (and the other suites) run live on the PR tier.

* `Projects Documents/QA_Tool_Cheat_Sheet_Secuura_API_Testing.html` — **1** hit
* `Projects Documents/API_Security_Functional_Testing_Architecture_Flow_Diagrams.html` — **13** hits, including the status banner and Mermaid nodes labelled `K6 ✅ Live (pr gate)`

Reproduce:

```bash
grep -niE 'live on the pr tier|live \(pr gate\)' "Projects Documents/"*.html
```

Fix: say what actually gates a PR today — the author's local four-suite run + Test Evidence block (DEV-PROCESS.md §Manual CI-gate equivalents) — for every suite, not just k6.

## 2. `5_Project_History/history.md` is missing entries

No entry for [KS-396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-396/systemtest-validate-weekend-platform-fixes-bring-tool-pins-current) (k6 2.0.0 → 2.1.0, commit `aa8624a26`, PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#457](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-396-validate-weekend-platform-fixes-bring-systemtest-tool-pins-05837283bca9)) or [KS-1285](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1285/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4272-4275-the-ks-1270-ndjson-hold-is) (Schemathesis 4.27.2 → 4.27.5, `b6959f291`). `grep -c` returns 0 for both. Tool-bump entries follow the `### <date> — <Tool> X → Y` shape.

Note: open PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1129](https://linear.app/secuura/review/docshistory-2026-09-21-local-rebuild-on-develop-7be81d5c9-oom-e8a16926a4df) (Stuart, `chore/history-2026-09-21-local-rebuild-preflight`) and [KS-1354](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1354/bump-systemtest-k6-210-230-grafanak6-v220-v230-released) both insert at the top of `## Entries`, so they will conflict with each other and with this.

## 3. `secuura-test-discipline` skill is stale

`.claude/skills/secuura-test-discipline/SKILL.md` (tracked; the source of truth is `~/.claude/skills/`):

* **line 131** still reads "Slots isolate containers, not database credentials ([KS-731](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-731/local-slots-share-one-postgresredis-credential-pair-any-slot-can-read)**, OPEN**)". [KS-731](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-731/local-slots-share-one-postgresredis-credential-pair-any-slot-can-read) has been **Done since 2026-09-13**, and the skill itself says to *rewrite* that bullet when [KS-731](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-731/local-slots-share-one-postgresredis-credential-pair-any-slot-can-read) closes (keep the reachability rule, replace the read/write/DROP capability with the authentication failure that supersedes it).
* **line 194** says "Docker has **6** CPUs". `docker info --format '{{.NCPU}}'` reports **8** on the Mac today, and `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` already records 6 as stale.

## Done when

- [ ] Both HTML docs describe the local gate, not a live PR tier, for every suite (both docs in one commit, per the skill §4).
- [ ] `history.md` carries [KS-396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-396/systemtest-validate-weekend-platform-fixes-bring-tool-pins-current) and [KS-1285](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1285/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4272-4275-the-ks-1270-ndjson-hold-is) entries.
- [ ] The skill's [KS-731](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-731/local-slots-share-one-postgresredis-credential-pair-any-slot-can-read) bullet is rewritten per its own instruction and the CPU figure is re-measured and dated.
- [ ] Merge order agreed with [KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and) / PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1129](https://linear.app/secuura/review/docshistory-2026-09-21-local-rebuild-on-develop-7be81d5c9-oom-e8a16926a4df) so the doc hunks are rebased once.

title: Spec: 85 of 145 request bodies are not marked `required: true`, so Schemathesis sends "valid" empty bodies the handlers reject — 17 ops, 35 cases per sweep, 15 of them baselined against Done KS-255
description:
## Summary

One for the spec when convenient, Kamil. 85 of the spec's 145 request bodies aren't marked `required: true`, so Schemathesis reasonably sends "valid" requests with no body at all, and 17 operations answer 400 (35 cases per sweep). It isn't a blanket fix: 23 operations happily accept an empty body. So the likely shape is marking `required: true` where the Zod schema rejects an absent body. 15 of these pairs are still baselined against [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints), which is closed, so this would give them a live home. Thank you.

+++ Full evidence

**Sweep 4** (slot 3, seed 1353, 4.28.0, toml loaded): 85 operations with a non-required `requestBody`; 40 were sent a no-body positive case (237 cases); **17 operations / 35 cases** failed `positive_data_acceptance`.

| Operation | No-body cases | Status | Baseline today |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `PATCH /api/platform/tenants/{id}` | 4 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |
| `PATCH /api/users/admin/{id}` | 2 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |
| `POST /api/analytics/reports` | 1 | 400 | not baselined |
| `POST /api/billing/checkout/custom` | 1 | 400 | not baselined |
| `POST /api/billing/customers/{customerId}/default-payment-method` | 2 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |
| `POST /api/issuer-certs` | 2 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |
| `POST /api/m365/documents/sync` | 2 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |

| `POST /api/m365/sites` | 2 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |
| `POST /api/nft/estimate` | 1 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |
| `POST /api/nft/record` | 2 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |
| `POST /api/nft/verify/asset` | 1 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |
| `POST /api/nft/verify/transaction` | 2 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |
| `POST /api/onedrive/files/{id}/sync` | 5 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |
| `POST /api/referrals/generate` | 2 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |
| `POST /api/users/me/change-password` | 3 | 400 | [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) |

Example, `POST /api/billing/checkout/custom` (all four sweeps): body `null` → 400 `"path":["quantity"],"message":"Required"`.

**Direction:** mark `requestBody.required: true` where the handler's Zod schema rejects an absent body, at the generator (`*.openapi.ts` → `npm run generate-openapi`). Optionally, a spec-lint rule: a body whose schema has a non-empty `required` list must itself be `required: true`.

Related: [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done) · [KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks) · [KS-1015](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1015/sweeps-2026-09-08-28-checkoperation-pairs-have-no-live-owner-18) (finding 2) · [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing).

title: Akto: a skipped HAR replay is only a WARN — the tier runs on synthetic samples and the report never says its authz coverage was weakened
description:
## Summary

A small visibility gap in our own Akto harness. When `feed-har` can't get an issuer session, it logs a WARN, skips the HAR replay and carries on, and the tier then scans with synthetic samples. Nothing in the console, report JSON, HTML or gate mentions that its authz coverage was thinner, so a PASS reads the same either way. It would be kind to our future selves to make that visible.

+++ Detail, measurement and a suggested shape

**Seen** on slot 2, 2026-09-28, `test:pre-merge` at 11:49:37Z:

```
[secuura-auth] WARN   Could not obtain issuer (HAR replay) session: AxiosError: Request failed with status code 429
[har-traffic] WARN   No issuer token — skipping HAR traffic generation (endpoints keep their synthetic samples).
```

The tier then reported **PASS**. That particular 429 came from the platform's spent request window ([KS-1362](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1362/back-to-back-tiers-setup-logins-land-in-the-platforms-spent-60-second), now fixed on the [KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and) branch); this ticket is about the skip being invisible, whatever causes it.

**Why it matters:** the HAR replay gives Akto's BOLA/BFLA/authz templates real authenticated samples. Without it those templates match less, or run against placeholders. [KS-716](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-716/the-whole-super-admin-surface-is-silently-unscanned-no-system-admin) shows how big that can get (0 of 16 super-admin endpoints scanned, reported green). It's the same family as [KS-709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-709/akto-reports-a-pass-for-a-test-that-executed-nothing-clean-0-not): coverage quietly lost.

**Suggested shape**

1. `feed-har` writes its outcome (fed N endpoints / skipped + reason) into the run directory.
2. The run artifact carries it, and the console summary, HTML report and cross-check show it in one wording (the three-way parity rule).
3. The gate shows a visible DEGRADED line (like COVERAGE DEGRADED) rather than a hard fail, so a passing blip doesn't block a merge — but never silent.

**Done means:** a tier whose replay was skipped says so on all three surfaces, red on today's code and green after; a tier whose replay succeeded is unchanged.

It stands apart from [KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and) because `feed-har` runs before vitest, so it needs a small handoff and new gate behaviour worth reviewing on its own.

+++

title: Back-to-back tiers: setup logins land in the platform's spent 60-second window and are refused — HAR replay and provisioning lost
description:
## BLUF

When `test:pre-merge` (or `test:security`) starts straight after `test:pr`, its two setup logins can be refused with 429, so the tier runs without its HAR replay and with seeded accounts instead of provisioned ones — and still reports PASS. The cause turned out to be the gateway's **global request window**, not the failed-login lockout this ticket first suggested. A fix is on the [KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and) branch and has been seen working live.

## What we see

Measured on slot 2, 2026-09-28. Every refused setup login that day came straight after `test:pr`'s unpaced traffic had filled the window:

| refused logins | 429s in that minute (mostly Akto) | answered in |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 09:52:45Z (2) | 1,986 | 0 ms |
| 11:49:37Z (2) | 493 | 0–1 ms |
| 13:51:02Z (2) | 518 | 0 ms |

## Why it is the window, not the lockout — a gentle correction to the first version of this ticket

* The gateway's lockout (`api-gateway/src/middleware/security.ts`) can't be the source: nothing in production calls its `recordFailure()`, and slot 2 logged no `BRUTE_FORCE_*` events in six hours. That is now its own ticket, [KS-1372](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1372/api-gateway-failed-login-lockout-is-inert-createbruteforceprotection).
* The auth service's lockout answers **401**, not 429 (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:339-342`).
* At 13:51 six logins had just **succeeded** (13:50:38), which would have reset any lockout count anyway.
* A 0–1 ms answer means the gateway replied itself, before any proxying — which is how its rate limiter behaves.

The earlier reading ("nothing else was refused") was fair at the time; it's just that the logins were the only requests arriving in those seconds.

## What's changed

On the [KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and) branch (`feature/ks-1286-…`, squashed into `4f7766a3e`): before any setup login, `feed-har` and the first vitest `globalSetup` hook probe `GET /api/auth/me` (a 401 that carries `RateLimit-Remaining` — not a login), and wait for the window to reset (at most 61 s) when fewer than 200 requests remain. Unit-tested, plus a wiring test that fails if the hook order changes.

Seen live on slot 2, 14:11Z: `pr` left the window at 0; pre-merge waited 6 s, found 1,999 left, then uploaded 84 HAR samples and provisioned normally. Pre-merge passed.

## Done means

Once [KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and) merges: a tier started right after another shows no 429 on either setup login, the HAR is fed, and provisioning reports PROVISIONED. The live run above already shows this; it just needs to land.

## Related

[KS-1372](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1372/api-gateway-failed-login-lockout-is-inert-createbruteforceprotection) (the gateway lockout never engages) · [KS-1363](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1363/akto-a-skipped-har-replay-is-only-a-warn-the-tier-runs-on-synthetic) (a skipped HAR replay should be visible in the report) · [KS-618](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-618/client-ip-is-invisible-platform-wide-on-demo-every-ip-keyed-control) (every caller on a host shares one address).

title: schemathesis-baseline.json lags the Linear registers: 37 of 90 failing pairs untriaged (all now tracked on Linear; 39 across sweeps 4–5) and 44 entries unseen in the configured sweep
description:
## Summary

A housekeeping job for the systemTest side, and no platform change is needed. `config/schemathesis-baseline.json` has fallen behind Linear. In the configured sweeps, 37 failing pairs per sweep aren't in the file (39 distinct across sweeps 4 and 5), though every one is already carried on a ticket. Meanwhile 42–44 of the file's 97 entries didn't fail at all. Bringing the file in line, with a reason, ticket and `expires` on each entry, would let the baseline gate be read again. [KS-752](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-752/schemathesis-baseline-gate-is-unreachable-runpy-skips-it-whenever-the) is why this went unnoticed: the gate is skipped whenever a sweep fails.

+++ Full evidence and the working list

### Gate results across the [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) sweeps

| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1: 4.27.5 | no | 160 | 63 | 97 | 1,587 |
| 2: 4.28.0 | no | 158 | 59 | 99 | 1,572 |

| 4 | yes | 90 | 53 | 37 | 963 |
| 5 | yes | 92 | 55 | 37 | 994 |

title: DELETE /api/wallets/session/{sessionId}: the 200 body omits the declared `success` field
description:
## Summary

A quick one, Kamil, whenever it suits. A successful `DELETE /api/wallets/session/{sessionId}` returns `{"message": "Session disconnected"}`, while the published 200 schema expects a boolean `success`. It's consistent whenever a live session id is drawn (1 of 1 in sweeps 1–4 and 6), so it's a small contract gap rather than anything intermittent. Adding `success: true`, or adjusting the schema if the bare body is intended, would close it. Thank you.

+++ Full evidence

| Sweep | Interactions | Statuses | Result |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1: 4.27.5 | 16 | 401×8, 404×7, **200×1** | 1 of 1 200s fails the schema |
| 2: 4.28.0 | 8 | 401×4, 404×3, **200×1** | 1 of 1 |
| 3: + deps | 8 | 401×4, 404×3, **200×1** | 1 of 1 |
| 4: toml loaded | 16 | 401×8, 404×7, **200×1** | 1 of 1 |

Sweep 5 drew no live session id; sweep 6 matched sweeps 1–4. Fuzzing phase, *"Positive test case"*.

```
"success" is a required property
Schema:  { "required": ["success"], "properties": { "success": {"type": "boolean"}, "message": {"type": "string"} } }
Value:   { "message": "Session disconnected" }
```

**Options:** add `success: true` to the handler's success body (keeps the envelope consistent), or correct the published schema if the bare body is deliberate. Listed for baselining against this ticket in [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing).

+++

title: GET /api/platform/audit-log accepts wrong-type and out-of-range query values with 200 — beyond its ruled by-design tolerance
description:
## Summary

A small one for when you have a moment, Kamil. `GET /api/platform/audit-log` seems to accept a few more query shapes than the [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) / [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the) ruling allows: wrong-type and out-of-range `offset` / `limit` values come back **200**. It's been steady at 30 cases per sweep across all six [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) sweeps, so it's long-standing rather than new. Either tightening the validation or widening the ruling would settle it, and which is your call. Thank you.

+++ Full evidence and options

### Results across the [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) sweeps

Slot 3, seed 1353, 2026-09-28, read from each run's `schemathesis-output.ndjson`.

| Sweep | Interactions | Statuses | `by_design_input_tolerance_guard` | `negative_data_rejection` |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1: 4.27.5 | 188 | 200×60, 401×121, 405×6, 204×1 | **30** (all 200) | 32 |
| 2: 4.28.0 | 188 | same | **30** | 32 |
| 3: + deps | 188 | same | **30** | 32 |
| 4: toml loaded | 181 | 200×60, 401×121 | **30** | 0 |

Sweeps 5 and 6 match sweep 4.

* The guard lives in `config/check_predicates.py` (hook-loaded), so it ran in every sweep and never moved.
* `negative_data_rejection` ×32 = the guard's 30 + 2 unknown-parameter cases (the ruled shape). It reads 0 from sweep 4 because the toml exception is finally loaded. That's the ruling being applied, not a fix.

### The 30 cases (identical every sweep)

| Phase | Case | Count |
| -- | -- | -- |
| coverage | Incorrect type (whole query) | 10 |
| coverage | `offset`: Incorrect type | 5 |
| coverage | `limit`: Incorrect type | 5 |
| coverage | below minimum / above maximum (`offset`, `limit`) | 6 |
| fuzzing | `offset` / `limit` wrong type or below minimum | 4 |

Smallest repro: `GET /api/platform/audit-log?offset=-1` as a platform admin → **200**. The ruled shape `?offset=0&x-schemathesis-unknown-property=42` → 200 is allowed.

### Options

1. **Validate the query** (types and declared bounds) and keep the ruling narrow. The guard stays as the regression pin.
2. **Widen the ruling** on [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) / [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the), with `check_predicates.py` following it.

Sibling: [KS-1371](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1371/post-apistatusidunrevoke-accepts-index-1-below-the-declared-minimum) (unrevoke `index: -1`). Baseline side: [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing).

+++

title: Undeclared methods now answer 405 + Allow before authentication — does this supersede the KS-406 auth-first ruling?
description:
## Summary

A question rather than a finding, Kamil, and there's no rush. Undeclared methods now get **405 + a route-specific** `Allow` before authentication, while the [KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of) ruling says unauthenticated callers should see 401 so the method surface stays hidden. The current behaviour looks like [KS-3](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-3/discussion-schemathesis-implementation-readiness-see-ks-50)'s spec-aware method filtering, and it's RFC-correct. Could you let us know which posture should stand? The harness will follow either way. Thank you.

+++ Full evidence and the two options

### Measured (slot 3, `develop` `d9ce1403d`, 2026-09-28, no credentials)

```
DELETE /api/analytics/overview   (undeclared)          → 405   Allow: GET
PUT    /api/referrals/0          (undeclared)          → 405   Allow: DELETE, …
GET    /api/analytics/overview   (declared — control)  → 401
```

Across one full sweep's undeclared-method probes: **405 ×1,760**, 204 ×307 (OPTIONS), 404 ×29, **401 ×2**.

* Authentication itself is intact (the declared-method control is 401); only the order changed.
* `/api/referrals/0` is the route [KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of) used as its own 401 evidence.
* Source: `api-gateway/src/specRouteMap.ts` ([KS-3](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-3/discussion-schemathesis-implementation-readiness-see-ks-50) DRIFT-METHOD-405-EXPANSION) and the method allowlist at `api-gateway/src/index.ts:284`. `TRACE` is stopped by nginx with a global `Allow` (as [KS-404](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-404/gateway-answers-trace-with-bare-405-no-allow-header-rfc-9110-282) expects).

### Options

1. **405 +** `Allow` **before auth is now intended.** [KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of) is superseded; the harness retires its probe suppression (`[phases.coverage] unexpected-methods = []`) and asserts 405. That turns \~1,760 requests per sweep into real coverage.
2. [KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of) **still stands.** Method filtering moves behind auth (or answers 401 to unauthenticated callers), and the same probes, expecting 401, become the regression guard.

Recorded as `DRIFT-METHOD-405` in `systemTest/schemathesis/docs/known-issues-and-baseline.md`. The harness keeps [KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of)'s suppression until this is decided.

+++

title: KS-962 seed-idempotence suite skips all 27 cells on hosts without Postgres binaries — would an opt-in Docker runner help it run anywhere?
description:
## Summary

No rush at all on this one, Kamil. The [KS-962](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-962/the-api-gateway-user-seed-throws-42p10-on-every-boot-and-has-never) seed-idempotence suite (`ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh`) skips all 27 of its cells on any machine without Postgres binaries, and it does so honestly and loudly, exactly as designed. The only gap is that on such hosts the guard never runs. An opt-in Docker runner might let it run anywhere, but it's your suite, so whichever approach you'd prefer is the one to go with. Happy to help build or test it.

+++ Details and options

**Observed 2026-09-28** during the [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) preflight: `SKIP — no PostgreSQL binaries (initdb pg_ctl postgres psql) found; … 0/27 cells run`. Shell suites 59 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (of 60).

**What the suite needs** (read from the file): the Postgres binaries (via `KS949_PG_BIN`, then the Homebrew / Debian paths); Node ≥18, tsx and a built `packages/shared`; and auth's path includes the native `argon2`, so a macOS `node_modules` can't simply be mounted into Linux.

**One possible shape:** an opt-in container runner (Postgres 15 + Node, repo mounted read-only, `node_modules` in a named volume), off by default (e.g. `KS949_PG_DOCKER=1`). The suite already searches `/usr/lib/postgresql/15/bin`, so it would need no change itself.

**Other options, equally welcome:** connect to an already-running Postgres instead of `initdb`; reuse the stack's own `postgres` container; or document `brew install postgresql@15` as a prerequisite. (Not suggested: wrapping `pg_ctl` into a container, because Postgres's 0700 data-dir check is fragile across Docker Desktop's bind mounts.)

No defect was found; this is a coverage gap on Postgres-less hosts. Related: [KS-962](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-962/the-api-gateway-user-seed-throws-42p10-on-every-boot-and-has-never) · [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9).

+++

title: Stack tooling is not slot-derived end to end: stack_guard lists a project twice under mixed marker labels, dev-reload.sh / start-local.sh bypass stack_env.sh, and compose defaults FRONTEND_URL / CORS_ORIGINS to slot 1
description:
## Summary

For when you have a moment, Kamil; it matters most on a busy host. A few pieces of stack tooling still assume slot 1 instead of deriving from `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT`, so on slots 2–4 they can double-report a stack, miss its containers, carry slot-1 URLs, or preflight the wrong gateway. Each fix is small and follows the existing `stack_env.sh` pattern. The four spots are below. Thank you.

+++ The four spots, evidence and fix shapes

1. `stack_guard.sh` `list_other_stacks` **(lines 105–111)** reports one line per label tuple (`sort -u` on `project|owner|branch`), so a project with one `owner=unknown` container (the [KS-1011](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1011/ks-666-stack-marker-reads-unknown-for-ownerbranchcommitstarted-at) case) shows up twice. *Fix:* group by project and append an `unknown` count; add a case to `scripts/__tests__/stack_guard.test.sh`.
2. `dev-reload.sh` **(**`:45` `CONTAINER="secuura-$SVC"`**) and** `start-local.sh` don't source `stack_env.sh`, so they only find slot 1's containers and stamp `unknown` markers on anything they create. *Fix:* source `stack_env.sh` and use `${STACK_PREFIX}` (or retire `start-local.sh` if unused); extend `check-stack-safety.sh` so every script running `docker compose up|run|restart` must source it.
3. `docker-compose.yml` **defaults** `FRONTEND_URL` (`:767`) and `CORS_ORIGINS` (`:503`, `:2179`) to slot 1's ports. *Fix:* derive them from the exported `GATEWAY_PORT` / `WEBSITE_PORT`, so an unedited `.env` is right on every slot; pin it in `stack_env.test.sh` or `check-stack-safety.sh`.
4. **The** [KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight) **preflight's PROVISIONED legs** default to `:6882` (`preflight.sh:94`). On a slot-N worktree they probe slot 1 unless `GATEWAY_URL` is passed. *Fix:* derive from `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` via `stack_env.sh`, and fail loudly with an example command when no slot is named locally.

**Seen 2026-09-28** (Peter's Mac, `develop` `d9ce1403d`), bringing up slot 4 with slots 2 and 3 running:

```
Other Secuura stacks running on this host (NOT affected by this operation):
  secuura_slot2 — owner peterdouglas, branch feature/ks-1286-…
  secuura_slot3 — owner peterdouglas, branch feature/ks-1353-…
  secuura_slot3 — owner unknown, branch unknown
```

The `owner unknown` container came from a bare `docker compose` call in the [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) worktree at about 09:33 UTC. That's the same mechanism as spot 2, reached by hand, and slot 3 was restored through `start-secuura.sh` afterwards.

**Verify:** the guard prints a mixed-label project once; `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=N ./scripts/dev-reload.sh api-gateway` finds `${STACK_PREFIX}-api-gateway`; an untouched `.env` renders slot-N URLs (`docker compose config`); the preflight probes slot N; `check-stack-safety.sh` goes red on a revert of any of the four.

Related: [KS-1011](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1011/ks-666-stack-marker-reads-unknown-for-ownerbranchcommitstarted-at) (unknown markers; PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1181](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1011-markerwarn-start-secuurash-warns-loud-and-named-on-unknown-bc1340b4bef0) warns in `start-secuura.sh` only) · [KS-666](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-666/prevent-destructive-rebuilds-of-the-shared-vm-stack-from-destroying) (slot design) · [KS-1034](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1034/check-stack-safetysh-resolves-the-wrong-repo-root-inside-a-git-hook) · [KS-1373](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1373/schemathesis-full-run-named-slot-3-but-871-of-its-requests-incl) (the same slot-derivation theme, harness side).

+++

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** points 1, 2 and 3 — the spot-3 pin in `check-stack-safety.sh` is a natural home for the point-1 guard, and spot 4 is coordinated with [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports)'s leg 13.

title: Bump systemTest k6 2.1.0 → 2.3.0 (grafana/k6 v2.2.0 + v2.3.0 released)
description:
## Why

`systemTest/performance` ran **k6 2.1.0** (`grafana/k6:2.1.0`, [KS-396](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-396/systemtest-validate-weekend-platform-fixes-bring-tool-pins-current)). Upstream released **v2.2.0 (2026-08-10)** and **v2.3.0 (2026-09-21)**. Both sets of release notes were read in full: 2.2.0 states "There are no breaking changes in this release"; 2.3.0 has no breaking-changes section.

## What was measured against both images (Mac, arm64, 2026-09-28)

* Same container user (uid 12345).
* `k6 run --help`: 53 → 56 flags — `--once`, `--scenario`, `--log-ns-timestamps` added; none removed or renamed. Root help identical.
* `native-histograms` is still `lifecycle=experimental` on 2.3.0.
* **Trap:** k6 only *logs* `Unknown feature flag` for a `--features` name it does not know, and runs on with exit 0 — a renamed flag switches itself off silently.
* The `handleSummary()` summary is identical in shape on both (169 key paths, the same 22 metrics).
* The runner's `--tag scenario=<name>` is overwritten by k6's built-in `scenario` tag (`default`) on **both** versions — pre-existing, not caused by the bump.

## Where the version lives (corrected)

| Site | Role |
| -- | -- |
| `systemTest/performance/config/observability.yml` `docker.k6Image` | **the pin the runner launches** (`runner/k6_docker.ts`; `runner/setup.ts` pulls it) |
| `systemTest/performance/docker/k6/Dockerfile` `FROM` | never built by the runner; read by the CVE gate |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/base-image-watch.sh` `EXCLUDED_BASES` | CVE gate — its `--self-test` fails if the tag is missing |
| `systemTest/performance/package.json` `@types/k6` | typings, own release line (2.0.1 → **2.2.1**; no 2.3 typings exist) |

The three test fixtures that name the image assert nothing about it. Before this ticket nothing checked the sites agreed.

## New k6 features — applicability

| Feature | Decision |
| -- | -- |
| `freeze-env` (2.2.0) | **Enabled on every run** — no script writes `__ENV`; a future write now throws |
| `K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_LABELS` (2.3.0) | **Approved, to enable**: `perf_scenario` + `k6_image` labels (also restores a usable scenario label in Grafana) |
| `--log-ns-timestamps` (2.3.0) | **Approved, to enable** (verified offline on 2.3.0; 2.1.0 rejects it, so the runner then requires ≥ 2.3.0) |
| `native-histograms` | stays opt-in — blanks the gauge-based Grafana latency panels |
| `--scenario` / `--once` | N/A — no script declares `options.scenarios`; every run is k6's single default scenario |
| `async-metric-context` | N/A — every `group()` is synchronous |
| `merge-run-tags` | N/A — the runner's `--tag` values already contain the script's own tags |
| `tlsAIAFetch`, `handleSummaryTimeout` | N/A — local HTTP; the summary is fast |

## Done (branch `feature/ks-1354-…`)

* Pins moved in all three sites; `@types/k6` 2.2.1.
* `tests/unit/config/k6ImagePinParity.test.ts` — the three image sites must agree (red on a one-sided bump, then green).
* `freeze-env` on every run; `runK6` command tests pin that the flags reach `docker run`.
* The k6 image is recorded in the console banner, `run-metadata.json` and the HTML report banner.
* A real 2.3.0 summary fixture + gate test (the older fixtures predate `handleSummary()`).
* Live smoke before/after on slot 1, same commit: both **PASS 5 of 5**, 37 requests, 0 failed, 118 of 118 checks.
* `npm run quality` exit 0 (1,129 of 1,129); `base-image-watch --self-test` PASS; preflight 15 of 15.
* Docs: `quick-start.md` bump procedure, `systemTest/CLAUDE.md`, both QA HTML docs, `DEV-PROCESS.md`, `history.md`.

## Remaining on this ticket

- [ ] All seven scenarios on slot 1 with Grafana up (nightly excluded) — in progress.
- [ ] Enable the two approved features; flag an unknown `--features` name as an INVALID run; correct the summary types in `types/index.ts` to the real 2.3.0 shape.
- [ ] Remove the k6-specific stale doc claims (`quick-start.md` `ci_gate.ts` references, observability "k6 2.0" comment, cheat-sheet subtitle date).
- [ ] Quality gate + confirmation smoke; PR with Test Evidence (incl. preflight line, [KS-1049](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1049/a-prs-test-evidence-must-state-whether-the-preflight-ran-the-hook)); QA GO; merge.

## Split out

* [KS-1365](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1365/systemtest-docs-still-describe-github-actions-as-live-and-the-history) — stale docs not caused by this bump (Actions-retirement wording, history entries, skill text).
* [KS-1366](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1366/pr-template-still-says-to-dispatch-pre-merge-platform-suitesyml-and) — PR template / Test Evidence templates (Stuart).
* [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not) — Renovate sees only the Dockerfile side of the pin.

## Merge order

[KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and)'s branch and PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1129](https://linear.app/secuura/review/docshistory-2026-09-21-local-rebuild-on-develop-7be81d5c9-oom-e8a16926a4df) (Stuart) touch the same doc lines — sequence before merging.

title: Bump systemTest schemathesis pin 4.27.5 → 4.28.0 (first minor since 4.27.x: 9 additions, 10 fixes, 3 changes) + refresh every pyproject floor/constraint to latest
description:
## BLUF

Upstream released **4.28.0 on 2026-09-22** (the CHANGELOG dates it 2026-09-23), the first **minor** since the 4.27.x line, with **no intermediate release** after 4.27.5 ([KS-1285](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1285/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4272-4275-the-ks-1270-ndjson-hold-is), merged `b192ffd4a`). At filing, the pin `schemathesis==4.27.5` lived in three places: `systemTest/schemathesis/pyproject.toml`, `constraints.txt:110`, and the `config/schemathesis_tests.yaml` header (lines 2–3, a tripwire pinned by `tests/unit/test_config_header_pin_parity.py`). All three now read **4.28.0** on the branch.

Two things made this bigger than the last two bumps:

1. **4.28.0 is where** [KS-1285](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1285/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4272-4275-the-ks-1270-ndjson-hold-is)**'s "Unreleased" items landed.** `low_valid_rate` is a **new warning**, so `TestAllInstalledWarningsAreAccountedFor` went red on the bump commit, as designed. **Decided: INFORMATIONAL** (opt-in; it fired 0 times, and it isn't enabled). Making a new warning fatal unmeasured is what `unmatched_filter` and `unresolvable_reference` weren't allowed to do.
2. **Scope addition (Peter, 2026-09-28): the rest of** `pyproject.toml` **comes up to latest too.** See *Scope 2*.

## Scope 1: what 4.28.0 contains, measured against our spec

Exposure was measured against `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` (343 operations: get 157, post 154, delete 16, patch 12, put 4) and the upstream `CHANGELOG.md` verbatim, not the release page's prose.

**🚀 Added (9)**

| \# | Upstream entry | Our exposure |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Fuzz dictionary bindings for GraphQL arguments | **No**: OpenAPI 3 REST only |
| 2 | Opt-in `low_valid_rate` warning | **Yes, the headline item.** Trips the [KS-684](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-684/schemathesis-4243-4251-bump-plus-harden-the-harness-against-the) guard. **Decided INFORMATIONAL**; fired 0 times in the sweeps (opt-in, not enabled). Adopting it is a later, measured decision. |
| 3 | A server that stops accepting connections ends the run with one `Server Unavailable` error | **Yes (behavioural)**: a new run-ending condition that must read INVALID, not short-and-green (the [KS-1270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1270/schemathesis-4273-ndjson-writer-thread-deadlocks-on-a-lazy-import) / [KS-684](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-684/schemathesis-4243-4251-bump-plus-harden-the-harness-against-the) silent-truncation class) |
| 4 | `missing_test_data` for GraphQL | **No** |
| 5 | `st replay` FLAKY retries | **No**: we don't invoke `st replay` |
| 6 | Dynamic auth `extract_from = "cookie"` | **No**: bearer tokens via our own hook |
| 7 | `FailureGroup` for `validate_response` | **No**: Python API |
| 8 | pytest 8.4 support | **No**: we're on pytest 9.1.x; not capped |
| 9 | `validate()` / `is_valid()` on parameters | **No**: Python API |

**🐛 Fixed (10)**

| \# | Upstream entry | Our exposure (measured) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `negative_data_rejection` false positives for `regex`, `uri-reference` "and similar string formats" | **Plausible, measure rather than assert.** The spec declares no `regex` or `uri-reference` format. The nearest surface is 22 `uri`, 56 `pattern:` keywords (also `uuid` 48, `date-time` 33, `email` 18) |
| 2 | `response_schema_conformance` false positives for HEAD | **N/A**: 0 `head:` operations |
| 3 | `negative_data_rejection` for unknown query params next to boolean ones | **N/A**: **0 boolean query parameters** (62 query, 136 path, no cookie/header params) |
| 4 | Parameter examples sent together under one name / `examples` maps | **N/A**: 0 `examples:` maps, 0 media-level examples, 0 duplicate parameter names. Our examples are 47 schema-level `example:` scalars |
| 5 | GraphQL resolver errors | No |
| 6 | OpenAPI link validation for missing operations | **N/A**: **0 responses carry** `links:`. [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) is still Todo, so stateful chains come from *inferred* links only |
| 7 | Partial request-body examples under `examples` | **N/A**: same measurement as row 4 |
| 8 | Protocol-relative `$ref`s | No: local `$ref`s only |
| 9 | XML namespace prefixes | No: JSON only |
| 10 | Cookie generation + JSON body serialization | Cookie half **N/A** (no cookie parameters). The JSON half is *"send a JSON string, not raw bytes, for top-level* `format: binary` *JSON bodies"*, which touches **exactly 2 operations** |

**🔧 Changed (3)**

| \# | Upstream entry | Our exposure |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Constraint naming / conflict reporting for generation failures | Parser risk only; readers key on check *names*, not wording |
| 2 | GraphQL non-nullable → "GraphQL schema violation" | No |
| 3 | Enhanced `missing_test_data` operation identification | Low; informational here |

**Net:** what can move our numbers is the `low_valid_rate` warning (the guard), the `Server Unavailable` run-ending error, the string-format `negative_data_rejection` fix, the 2 binary-body operations, and `missing_test_data`'s identification. Everything else is GraphQL, `st replay`, Python-API, or a surface we don't have.

## Scope 2: bring every pinned package up to latest (Peter, 2026-09-28)

**Every** `>=` **floor in** `systemTest/schemathesis/pyproject.toml` **and every line in** `constraints.txt` is re-verified against PyPI and raised to the current release, in the [KS-684](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-684/schemathesis-4243-4251-bump-plus-harden-the-harness-against-the) / [KS-1169](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1169/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4252-4271-seven-negativecoverage) shape (floors record what was verified, not history). That covers `[project.dependencies]` (hypothesis, httpx, pytest, pytest-cov, pytest-html, python-dotenv, jinja2, pyyaml, allure-python-commons) and `[project.optional-dependencies].dev` (ruff, mypy, pytest-xdist, pytest-timeout, pip-audit, cssutils, html5lib, types-pyyaml).

* `python3 scripts/run.py update-deps` is the mechanism; floors are then edited to what it resolved, each with its WHY comment.
* **Toolchain bumps are the risk, not the libraries.** Fix what a new ruff/mypy rule flags; never widen an ignore.
* Outcome: `hypothesis` 6.168.3, `ruff` 0.16.9, `allure-python-commons` 2.16.1. `jsonschema_rs` 0.57.1, forced by 4.28.0's `<0.58.0,>=0.57.1` (so not the latest 0.58.1).

## Working rules for whoever picks this up

* **Plan first, against the sources**: `CLAUDE.md`, `systemTest/CLAUDE.md`, the `secuura-test-discipline` and `peter-local-environment` skills, this ticket and its parents.
* **No god files**: the 400-line cap applies to every file created or edited here.
* **Code comments carry the WHY + the ticket number**, stating the prior behaviour.
* **Honest results.** No change may mask a failure. A failure that vanishes because upstream stopped generating an invalid case is *not generated*, not *passed*.
* **One slot, the one Peter names.** Don't start another stack.
* `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` exported on every suite run; run `scripts/setup.py` **through** `systemTest/run-in-slot.sh N`.

## Bump gate ([KS-1268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1268/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4271-4272-retargeted-from-4273-whose) / [KS-1285](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1285/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4272-4275-the-ks-1270-ndjson-hold-is) shape)

1. **Acceptance, the one-op NDJSON line-count check** ([KS-1270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1270/schemathesis-4273-ndjson-writer-thread-deadlocks-on-a-lazy-import)): `ScenarioFinished` count = console `Tested:`, `EngineFinished` present. Automated by `tests/functional/config/test_ndjson_completeness.py` inside `quality`.
2. `setup` at the **old** pin → **before** `full` sweep (fixed seed) → pin + WHY + yaml header + the two HTML docs → `update-deps` → `quality` → **after** `full` sweeps → pair diff via `baseline_gate.extract_failure_pairs`. **Launch the sweep so** `schemathesis.toml` **is loaded**: since [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) the runner pins `cwd=PROJECT_ROOT`; before it, a sweep started from `systemTest/` silently ran without the toml. The `/api/auth/register` limit is **100/hr/IP on local and non-prod stacks** (5/hr only in production), so two sweeps inside an hour are fine locally.
3. **Audit the six surfaces**: `--help` diff (54 flags; byte-identical at 4.28.0), `--report` list (6; SARIF still absent), check registry, phase list, warning registry (11 → 12 with `low_valid_rate`), `ignored_auth` wording.
4. Fixed-seed stateful comparison ([KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete): the seed moves the op count, not the version).
5. Pre-push preflight ([KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight)), with `npm ci` in `Blockchain/Dev` first ([KS-691](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-691/pre-push-preflight-cannot-run-from-a-git-worktree-legs-1-and-6-fail)). On a slotted stack, point its provisioned legs at the slot with `GATEWAY_URL`; the script defaults to `:6882` ([KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) finding 4).

## ⚠ The NEXT bump will be breaking: upstream *Unreleased* already carries it

Read on 2026-09-28, after 4.28.0: `st run` / `st fuzz` **exit 2 when nothing is tested**, **exit 2 on schema, configuration and internal errors**, **exit 130 on Ctrl+C**, and **fuzzing and pytest seed each operation separately**. The last changes what a fixed seed means for our before/after comparisons, and the exit codes land directly on `run.py`'s verdict handling. Treat the 4.29 bump as a behavioural change.

## Environment prerequisite hit on 2026-09-28 (not a defect of this ticket)

A fresh worktree couldn't bring up a usable stack. `bootstrap-env.sh` copies `.env` from `env.example` (canonical under [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap)), which omits five keys compose consumes with an empty default: `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED`, `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS`, `TSA_URL`, `TSA_AUTH_KEY`. Two of them bit here:

* `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` gates the **whole** demo-user seeder (`services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:1230`); unset, no seeded account is written.
* `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` unset leaves `admin@secuura.com` with an unusable hash and `status = 'suspended'` (commit `023acccf8` retired its published default; see the `docker-compose.yml` comment above line 811), so there's no genuine platform admin.

`LOCAL_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED=true` ([KS-191](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-191/schemathesis-gate-rank-2-disable-login-limiter-in-cilocal-to-stop)) was also needed. Resolved locally by setting the keys by hand; the repo-side fix belongs to [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap) (noted there), and [KS-915](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-915/a-clean-stack-has-no-supported-way-to-obtain-its-first-privileged) is the ticket for the missing first-privileged-account procedure.

## Related

title: Security: a revoked credential still verifies as valid by EITHER route — POST /credentials/verify wires no statusListResolver, so checkStatus reports status:true and can never fail
description:
**A credential revoked through EITHER route still verifies as valid, and the verify response affirmatively reports** `checks.status: true`**. Measured at runtime, both arms, on a local stack at develop** `d9ce1403d1581ff1584ab799fbbf7fc6f9f8d817`**.**

Revocation is currently unenforceable at `POST /api/credentials/verify`. This is not "the credentials route forgets to update the status list" — it is that the verify route wires no `statusListResolver`, so `VerifiableCredentialVerifier.checkStatus()` cannot return anything but valid, whichever route did the revoking.

## What was measured

Local stack from a worktree at `d9ce1403`, services `vc-issuer` + `pgbouncer` + `postgres` + `redis` (all healthy, `migrations` completed). Requests issued from inside the `vc-issuer` container against `http://localhost:4014`. `POST /credentials/verify` is a `publicOps` exemption, so the verify arms carry no bearer.

### ARM 1 — revoke through `POST /api/credentials/:id/revoke`

| step | request | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| issue | `POST /api/credentials` | `201`, id `https://secuura.io/credentials/2b8015ca-…`, `statusListIndex "4"` |
| baseline verify | `POST /api/credentials/verify` | `200` · `verified: true` · `checks {signature:true,status:true,expiration:true,issuerDID:true,blockchain:true}` |
| revoke | `POST /api/credentials/<urlencoded id>/revoke` `{"reason":"…"}` | `200` `{"success":true,"message":"Credential revoked successfully","revokedAt":"2026-09-28T07:03:11.724Z"}` |
| re-read | `GET /api/credentials/<urlencoded id>` | `200`, `credentialStatus` now carries `"revoked": true, "revokedAt": "…", "revocationReason": "…"` — **the revocation IS persisted** |
| verify as-issued doc | `POST /api/credentials/verify` | `200` · `verified: true` · `errors: []` |
| verify the RE-READ doc | `POST /api/credentials/verify` | `200` · `verified: true` · `checks.status: true` · `errors: []` |

The last row is the sharp one: a document whose own `credentialStatus` reads `"revoked": true` is submitted to verify, and verify answers `verified: true` **with** `checks.status: true` — an affirmative claim that the status was checked and passed.

### ARM 2 — positive control, revoke through the STATUS route

| step | request | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| issue | `POST /api/credentials` | `201`, id `…/65f34225-…`, `statusListIndex "5"` |
| baseline verify |  | `200` · `verified: true` |
| allocate | `POST /api/status/default/allocate` | `200`, `index: 1` |
| revoke | `POST /api/status/default/revoke` | `200` `{"revoked":true,"revokedAt":"2026-09-28T07:03:11.740Z"}` |
| confirm recorded | `GET /api/status/default/revoked` | `200` `{"revokedIndexes":[0,1],"totalRevoked":2}` — **genuinely recorded in the status list** |
| verify | `POST /api/credentials/verify` | `200` · `verified: true` · `errors: []` |

**The positive control does NOT discriminate — and that is the finding.** The control was built to show that a "correct" revocation reaches verify. It does not. Revocation reaches verify by **neither** route, so the defect is broader than the credentials route: it is the verify route's missing resolver.

## Why, in code (read at `d9ce1403`, all paths under `Blockchain/Dev/`)

* `packages/shared/src/vc/verifier.ts:435` — `checkStatus()` consults revocation **only** inside `if (this.config.statusListResolver) { … }`. It is the only branch that can push an error.
* `packages/shared/src/vc/verifier.ts:449` — with no resolver the method falls through to `return { valid: errors.length === 0, errors }` with `errors` empty, i.e. **valid**.
* `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts:338-342` — `POST /verify` calls `verifyCredential(credential, { checkStatus: true, checkExpiration: true, checkBlockchain: false })`. `checkStatus: true` is passed; **no** `statusListResolver` **is**.
* `git grep statusListResolver` over the whole tree returns **3 hits, all inside** `verifier.ts` **itself** (`:24` the optional declaration, `:435` the guard, `:437` the call). Nothing anywhere supplies one.
* `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts:284-309` — the credentials-route revoke calls only `credentialRepo.revoke(id, reason)`; it never touches the status list. That part of the original read is correct, but it is not what makes verify wrong.
* `services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts:232-265` — `revoke()` writes `revoked` / `revokedAt` / `revocationReason` onto `credentialStatus`. Nothing reads them at verify. (Those three fields are also undeclared on the type — that is KS 1351, a different ticket.)

`checkStatus: true` therefore reads as a request for a check that structurally cannot fail.

## Board search before filing

Literal substring over title + description, `includeArchived: true`, team Secuura-PK: `statusListResolver` **0**, `checkStatus` **0**, `StatusList2021` **0**, `revoked credential still verifies` **0**, `statusListCredential` **1** (KS 1351, the type declaration + prefer-const ticket — it does not mention verify). Positive control `credentialRepo` returned **7** including one archived, so the scan can see; negative control `zzzq-b38-none` returned **0**. `searchIssues` was not used for the verdict: it is fuzzy and returned 20 unrelated rows for an exact worktree name.

## NOT TESTED / NOT DONE

* **No fix built.** Measurement only, per the brief. No PR, no product change.
* The api-gateway verify path (`POST /api/verification/verify`, `/api/v2/…`) was **not** measured — only vc-issuer's own `POST /api/credentials/verify`.
* Whether the demo or any deployed environment supplies a `statusListResolver` by another route was **not** checked; the grep above is over the repo at `d9ce1403` only.
* Presentation verification (`POST /api/presentations/verify`) was not measured, though it is the same `publicOps` class and likely shares the verifier config.
* Issuance required an ephemeral `VC_SIGNING_KEY` (Ed25519 PKCS8 hex) supplied through a local compose override for the measurement; it was never committed and the credential contents are throwaway.
* No assertion is made about what the *right* behaviour is (resolve the status list at verify, read `credentialStatus.revoked` directly, or refuse when `checkStatus: true` and no resolver is configured). That is a design call.

## Definition of done

* A credential revoked through `POST /api/credentials/:id/revoke` verifies as **not** valid, or `POST /api/credentials/verify` refuses to claim `checks.status: true` when it has no way to check status.
* The same holds for a credential revoked through `POST /api/status/:id/revoke`.
* A cell that fails before the fix and passes after, driving the real routes end to end rather than the verifier in isolation.

Found by runtime measurement, not code reading; the code read alone predicted only the ARM 1 half.

title: vc-issuer: VCCredentialStatus declares no revocation fields, so four credentialRepo cells are TS2339 — plus the prefer-const left by KS-1121's deletion
description:
**One test pass's residue from #1313 (KS-1121), both measured there and neither fixed in it.**

**Searched the board first, literally, over all 1340 Secuura-PK issues including archived** (`searchIssues` is fuzzy, so this was a literal substring match over every page): `VCCredentialStatus` — **0 open hits**; `prefer-const` — **0 hits**; `credentialRepo` — 6 hits, none about either item (KS-1295 store fallback, KS-1281 table permissions, KS-1204 allowedDocumentTypes, KS-1121 itself, KS-1116 ownership, KS-149 archived tooling); `vc-issuer/src/repositories` — 2 hits (KS-1281, KS-1121). Positive control: `credentialRepo` returned 6, so the scan can see.

## Item 1 — `VCCredentialStatus` has no `revoked` / `revocationReason` / `revokedAt`, and four cells read them

`packages/shared/src/vc/types.ts` declares `VCCredentialStatus` as `id`, `type`, `statusPurpose?`, `statusListIndex?`, `statusListCredential?`. Nothing else. But `services/vc-issuer/src/__tests__/credentialRepo.test.ts` reads `credentialStatus?.revoked`, `?.revocationReason` and `?.revokedAt`, and `tsc --noEmit` over a program that includes the test files reports **TS2339 at four sites** after #1313 (three before it):

```
src/__tests__/credentialRepo.test.ts(72,63):  error TS2339: Property 'revoked' does not exist on type 'VCCredentialStatus'.
src/__tests__/credentialRepo.test.ts(142,39): error TS2339: Property 'revoked' does not exist on type 'VCCredentialStatus'.
src/__tests__/credentialRepo.test.ts(143,39): error TS2339: Property 'revocationReason' does not exist on type 'VCCredentialStatus'.
src/__tests__/credentialRepo.test.ts(144,39): error TS2339: Property 'revokedAt' does not exist on type 'VCCredentialStatus'.
```

Three of the four pre-date #1313 (they sit at 118-120 at its base and shift to 142-144); the fourth, at `72:63`, is added by its new revoke cell. **The runtime path sets these fields** — `revoke()` writes them — so either the type is missing three fields it should declare, or the repository is writing fields the contract does not have. That is the decision this ticket asks for; it is not obviously a one-line type edit.

**Observation, not a conclusion:** line 32 of the same file writes `revoked: false` INSIDE a `credentialStatus` object literal at every tree and does **not** error, so the gap is reachable on a read and not on that construction. Worth one minute from whoever picks this up; it may say something about how the fixture is typed.

Note the package tsconfig excludes `src/__tests__`, so the package's own `tsc` never sees any of this. It is only visible through a program built with `exclude: []`.

## Item 2 — the same pass's cleanup: a `prefer-const` warning created by the ruled deletion

`services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts:95:11` — `warning  'result' is never reassigned. Use 'const' instead  prefer-const`.

Before #1313, `let result` was assigned twice: the exact lookup, then the `LIKE '%id%'` fallback. The owner's 2026-09-16 ruling deletes the fallback, so `result` is now assigned once. `npm run lint` in vc-issuer: **0 problems at #1313's base, 1 warning at its head**; rc 0 either way, because it is a warning.

## Why this is one ticket and not two

Both are residue of the same test pass (#1313) in the same package, and both are cleanup rather than behaviour. Split them if whoever picks it up finds the type question is a shared-package decision — it may be.

## Definition of done

* `VCCredentialStatus` and the repository agree about the revocation fields, decided rather than patched, and the four TS2339 sites go to zero over an `exclude: []` program.
* `credentialRepo.ts:95` is `const`, and vc-issuer lint is back to 0 problems.
* A note on whether the package tsconfig should stop excluding `src/__tests__` — this class is invisible until it does not.

Refs KS-1121

title: originate production file logs are a column of `undefined` — the File transports carry no format
description:
**BLUF: under** `NODE_ENV=production` **originate's two File transports write the literal string** `undefined` **on every line, so** `logs/error.log` **and** `logs/combined.log` **contain no usable information.** Found by the gate30T1 review; reproduced independently here.

## Measured

`services/originate/src/utils/logger.ts:45-46` constructs both File transports with **no** `format`:

```
new winston.transports.File({ filename: 'logs/error.log', level: 'error', maxsize: 10_000_000, maxFiles: 5 }),
new winston.transports.File({ filename: 'logs/combined.log', maxsize: 10_000_000, maxFiles: 5 }),
```

The logger-level format is `combine(errors({ stack: true }), timestamp(...))` — it has no `json()` and no `printf()`, so nothing renders the entry. The Console transport is fine because it is given its own format (`json()` in production, `colorize()+devFormat` otherwise); the File transports were never given one.

Rebuilding that exact logger and emitting one error:

* File transport **without** a per-transport format -> the file contains `undefined`
* the same transport **with** `format: combine(json())` -> `{"error":"boom","level":"error","message":"Admin config request failed (POST /api/admin/refresh-tenants)","service":"originate","timestamp":"..."}`

## Why it matters

Production is the only environment that creates these transports, so this is invisible in development and in tests. Every server-side error this service logs to file — including the `fail500` route context lines that KS-1341 and KS-1334 just routed there deliberately — lands as `undefined`.

## Fix shape

Give each File transport `format: combine(json())` (or hoist a shared `json()` into the logger-level format and let Console keep its override). Add a regression cell that builds the production logger against a temp directory, emits one error, and asserts the written line parses as JSON and carries `message` and `service`.

## Not covered

This is a reproduction of the mechanism, not a read of a real production log file on a deployed host. Scope is `services/originate`; other services' loggers were not examined.

title: The URL.pathname percent-encoding class also exists in 2 Blockchain/Dev files, outside KS-1337's scope
description:
## BLUF

The `new URL(..., import.meta.url).pathname` class that KS-1337 fixes in `systemTest/performance` **also exists outside** `systemTest/`**, in two files under** `Blockchain/Dev` — out of KS-1337's stated scope, so it is filed separately. A URL pathname is percent-encoded, so any of these resolving a path from a directory whose name contains a space yields `%20` and an `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`-class failure. **This fleet has such a directory.**

## The sites (gate29 sweep D, `git grep` over the clone at develop)

* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/openapi-examples/proxy/server.ts:31`
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/__tests__/ks732-mfa-disable-proof.test.ts:293, :296, :316`

**4 lines in 2 files.** KS-1337 fixed 1 of the 3 occurrences inside `systemTest/` (`performance/runner/cli.ts:162`, merged `3f70224a069b`); its other two — `systemTest/akto/tests/preSuiteSetup.ts:36` and `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts:42` — stay on that ticket. **These two are not on it.**

**Fix shape:** `fileURLToPath(new URL(...))`, as merged in `runner/cli.ts`. Red-proof shape: resolve from a temp directory whose name contains a space and assert the resolved path equals the real file, as the KS-1337 cell does — that shape reds even from a checkout without a space, which matters because most checkouts do not have one.

## A second, related gap, recorded here rather than split (the GO capped this at one ticket)

**Neither** `ks860` **nor** `ks879` **walks** `systemTest/` — `ks879`'s `DEV_ROOT` is `Blockchain/Dev` and `ks860`'s `WALK_ROOTS` are `services/` and `packages/` (gate29 N-1291-4, read at source). So that whole tree has **no raw-control-byte and no loopback-bind guard**, and nothing structural would have caught this class there either. That is arguably a separate workload from the four lines above; it is named here so it is not lost, and it can be split out.

## Done when

- [ ] the 4 lines in the 2 `Blockchain/Dev` files take their path through `fileURLToPath`
- [ ] at least one cell pins the spaced-directory case for them
- [ ] a decision is recorded on whether `ks860`/`ks879` should walk `systemTest/` (or a separate ticket exists for it)

## Provenance

Gate29 report `2026-09-26-batch1290-g29/report.md` (sha256 `c3a273b3a582c088d3d088a3ac21a954c562ac8735cc679ec7979c12553f1e52`, measured by this seat), notes **N-1291-2** (its sweep-D half) and **N-1291-4**.

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1335 issues (includeArchived) and 3780 comments**. Control token `b31nonce-9wq4tx-never-written` -> 0, while known terms returned hits, so the search discriminates in both directions. `import.meta.url).pathname` -> 2 (KS-1337, scoped to `systemTest/`; KS-847 Done, a NUL-byte/grep issue) · `WALK_ROOTS` -> 3 (KS-1319 and KS-1155, both about walk TIMEOUTS, not coverage; KS-876 Done). **Neither half of this is filed.**

title: fail500 family: a non-Error throw is logged as [object Object], so its content is lost from the log
description:
## BLUF

The `fail500` family helper logs a **non-Error** throw as `'[object Object]'`, so the thrown object's content is **lost from the log** — the body stays correctly constant, but the diagnosability the helper exists to preserve is gone. Measured at runtime by the gate29 probe on the routes #1290 converted.

## Detail

`fail500(res, context, err)` logs `err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)`. `String({...})` is `'[object Object]'`. So:

* an **Error** throw logs its message — correct;
* a **string** throw logs itself — correct;
* an **object** throw logs `[object Object]` — the content is gone.

At the merge-base neither kind leaked, because `err.message` on a non-Error is `undefined`; the helper is what made the log the only place the detail could live, and for objects it does not live there either.

**Fix shape:** in the family helper, log `err` itself, or `JSON.stringify` / `util.inspect` it for non-Errors.

**Family:** this is the same helper shape merged for KS730 in `routes/gdpr.ts` and `routes/systemErrors.ts`, so a fix belongs in all of them rather than in `webhooks.ts` alone.

## Also not pinned by the shipped cell (gate29 N-1290-3, measured: all green at head)

* (a) **non-Error throws** (string / object) on the three routes part B converted;
* (b) **rotate-secret throwing AFTER** `newSecret` **exists** — a rejected `$executeRaw` UPDATE, with the real `encryptField` and the key loaded. The gate probe drove this (S1) and measured the new secret **absent** from the 500 body and from every logger call, with a positive control — so today's behaviour is safe, but **no committed cell pins it**;
* (c) the **secret's absence from every log level** as an assertion.

## Done when

- [ ] the family helper preserves a non-Error throw's content in the log, in every file carrying the helper
- [ ] a cell pins a non-Error throw on at least one converted route
- [ ] a cell pins rotate-secret throwing after `newSecret` exists, asserting the secret is absent from the body and from every logger call

## Provenance

Gate29 report `2026-09-26-batch1290-g29/report.md` (sha256 `c3a273b3a582c088d3d088a3ac21a954c562ac8735cc679ec7979c12553f1e52`, measured by this seat), notes **N-1290-2** and **N-1290-3**; carries gate28's **N-1288-6**. Filed by the merging seat on that GO's instruction.

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1335 issues (includeArchived) and 3780 comments**. Control token `b31nonce-9wq4tx-never-written` -> 0, while known terms returned hits, so the search discriminates in both directions. `[object Object]` -> 3 (KS-1341, which is this seat's own gate28 record that it was NOT filed; KS-744, a gateway/verificationLevel issue; KS-440 Done) — **none is this defect.**

Refs KS-1341

title: GET /api/webhooks swallows a FAILED list query into 200 with an empty list - a DB failure reads as 'no webhooks'
description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/webhooks` swallows a **failed** list query into `200 {"success":true,"webhooks":[]}`, so a database failure is indistinguishable from "this organisation has no webhooks" — to the client and, on one of the two routes, to the log as well. Pre-existing; PR #1288's `control KS-1341 A0` currently **pins this as intended behaviour, which it is not.**

## The measurement

* `routes/webhooks.ts:196`: the list query carries `.catch((e: any) => { logger.warn('webhooks list query failed', { error: e?.message }); return []; })`. A rejected `$queryRaw` never reaches the catch under test; `fail500` is never called. Reproduced in all four `NODE_ENV` values by the gate28 probe.
* **The code's own comment records the harm.** `:187-190` (the KS-466 note) says a missing `::uuid` cast raised 42883 and "was silently swallowed by the `.catch` below, so this list ALWAYS returned `[]` (a pre-existing bug, independent of RLS)". The swallow hid a real defect once already.
* `GET /:id/deliveries` has the same shape at `:412` — `.catch(() => [])` — **with no log at all**, so that one is silent even server-side.

## Fix shape

Drop the `.catch` on both list queries so a rejection reaches the router's `fail500`: the thrown text logged server-side with the route named, and a constant 500 to the client.

## Regression cell

Flip `control KS-1341 A0` in `ks1341a-webhooks-500-never-answers-err-message.test.ts` from "swallowed into 200 `[]`" to expect **500 + the constant body + the logger call**. That cell exists today and asserts the opposite, so it is the pin that must move with the fix — it is deliberately recorded here so the change is not read as a regression.

## Board search before filing

Gating is TRUE; "off everywhere" is TRUE for the repository and **UNVERIFIABLE for live app settings** (no `az` in the gate). It re-widens the "in the repository" qualifier the neighbouring sentence had just added.
* **N-1286-8** (Polish) — `MT:40`, "a distinction the first version of this correction got wrong", is change-log prose about the correction itself. It will puzzle any reader who never saw the first version. Its home is the commit message, where it already is.
