title: ks597 integration guard: `?host=` and `?port=` query overrides in the DSN pass the no-database guard
description:
**BLUF: the guard that refuses a non-disposable database can be bypassed by putting the host or port in the DSN's QUERY STRING instead of its authority.** `?host=` and `?port=` overrides pass it. Minor — but the guard's whole purpose is that a cell writing to a database cannot reach a shared one, and a bypass in the connection string is exactly the shape that purpose is about.

## What was measured, and what holds

The guard itself works on the authority form, measured at runtime: `203.0.113.7`, port `6432` and port `5432` are each **refused with 0 TCP attempts**, and a free loopback port fails with `ECONNREFUSED` rather than being accepted. So the guard is real and it fires early, before any connection is attempted.

**The gap:** libpq-style DSN query parameters (`?host=`, `?port=`) are not part of the authority the guard inspects, so a DSN can name a forbidden target there and pass.

## Fix shape (not chosen here)

Parse the DSN's query parameters as well as its authority, and apply the same host and port predicate to whichever finally wins. Whatever resolution order the client uses is the one the guard must model — otherwise the guard is checking a different DSN than the one that connects.

## Stated so the record is not read as stronger than it is

The **INSERT path of that cell was not run** in the grading round, and its red proof is READ ONLY. That is a separate limit on what the round established, recorded here because anyone picking this up will be working in the same cell.

## Board search before filing

Searched over **486 open issues** on this team, matching literally against identifier + title + description: `QUERY-OVERRIDE`, `?host=`, `query override` — **0 open hits each**. `rolbypassrls` returned 2 (KS-1306 the parent, KS-980 a different subject). Controls as above: fresh token **0**, `ssrf-guard` **2**.

Refs KS-1306

title: entrypoint-corpus guard: a parenthesised return of a guarded call reads `guarded:false`, and the file's own rule-3 comment claims both return shapes are covered
description:
**BLUF: the guard reads** `guarded:false` **for call shapes the file's own comment says it covers.** Its rule-3 comment states *"Both return shapes are covered: a concise arrow body, and an explicit* `return`*"* — yet `return (() => g())` and `() => (() => g())`, when called, both read `guarded:false`, while the truth and `develop` both read **true**. `(() => g()).call(null)` reads false as well, and is not named anywhere.

This is the residue of a capped round. Nothing shipped for it; the pull request that attempted it stays open and its disposition sits with the repository owner.

## What is wrong, precisely

The defect is **parenthesisation**. A guarded call wrapped in parentheses — whether returned explicitly or as a concise arrow body — is not recognised, so a correctly-guarded call site is reported as unguarded. The reading is wrong in the **unsafe-looking** direction: it accuses safe code.

Three shapes, measured at runtime:

| shape | guard reads | truth / develop |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `return (() => g())` then called | `guarded:false` | true |
| `() => (() => g())` then called | `guarded:false` | true |
| `(() => g()).call(null)` | `guarded:false` | true |

The third came from a call-shape table the round was commissioned to make **"read as the truth or be NAMED"**. It does neither: it reads false and is unnamed.

**Evidence produced by the gate:** `evidence/1268/probe_readings_head.jsonl`, rows 23, 40 and 41.

## Why this is its own ticket

It is the same defect **class** as the round's first attempt, which is why the round capped. The fix is a reader change: recognise a parenthesised expression as transparent when deciding whether the inner call is guarded, and either read `.call`/`.apply` invocation forms as the truth or name them as unsupported. **A guard whose own comment claims coverage it does not have is worse than one with a stated limit**, because the comment is what the next reader trusts.

## Not in this ticket

The round's other work — the `entrypoint-corpus.test.ts` change at blob `8a4ce36a3a96` — is sound and is being re-raised separately by its author. This ticket is only the reader defect.

## Board search before filing

Searched over **486 open issues** on this team, matching literally against identifier + title + description: `guarded:false`, `parenthesised`, `rule-3`, `concise arrow` — **0 open hits each**. `entrypoint-corpus` returned 3 (KS-1155, KS-1142, KS-1140), none of them this reader defect. Controls: a fresh nonsense token **0**, `ssrf-guard` **2**, so the instrument discriminates in both directions.

Refs KS-1316

title: k6 runner: the pre-suite path is taken from URL.pathname, so a checkout directory containing a space fails ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND
description:
## BLUF

`systemTest/performance/runner/cli.ts:162` resolves the pre-suite step with
`new URL('../../fixtures/pre-suite.ts', import.meta.url).pathname`. `URL.pathname` **is**
**percent-encoded.** A checkout whose directory contains a space yields `.../Testing%20Agent%20MAIN/...`,
which is passed to the spawn as a literal path, and the run dies with
`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND … %2520 …` (the `%25` is the second round of encoding).

**This is not hypothetical on this fleet.** The QA gate's own checkout lives at
`/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/` — a path with **two spaces**. Any performance run
driven from a checkout like that cannot start its pre-suite step.

Found as a develop-own finding during the tier-2 gate on #1268 (report lines 214-219). **Not built**
**there**, and not built here: it is develop's, not that PR's.

## Measured at `00de57baeb405d0081fe8b6f192bd40d35acef61`

```
$ node -e "const u=new URL('../../fixtures/pre-suite.ts','file:///Volumes/Dev/Testing%20Agent%20MAIN/x/runner/cli.ts');
           console.log(u.pathname); console.log(require('url').fileURLToPath(u));"
/Volumes/Dev/Testing%20Agent%20MAIN/fixtures/pre-suite.ts     <- .pathname, what the code uses
/Volumes/Dev/Testing Agent MAIN/fixtures/pre-suite.ts         <- fileURLToPath, correct
```

`cli.ts:162` **is the only** `.pathname` **use of an** `import.meta.url` **URL in the package.** The fix-shape
already has precedent **in the same directory**, so this is a consistency fix rather than a new idea:

* `runner/actor_manifest.ts:60` — `dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`
* `runner/paths.ts:12` — `path.dirname(url.fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`
* `gate/cli.ts:31` — the same

## Done means

1. `cli.ts:162` uses `fileURLToPath(new URL('../../fixtures/pre-suite.ts', import.meta.url))`.
2. **A regression cell in the gate's own shape: run the CLI from a copy of the tree whose path**
   **contains a space**, and assert the pre-suite step resolves and spawns. A cell that only asserts
   the string has no `%20` would pass for a path that is wrong in some other way.
3. A sweep for any other `.pathname` on an `import.meta.url` URL across `systemTest/`, so the fix is
   the class and not the one line. ~~Measured today: **1** occurrence, this one.~~ **CORRECTED 2026-09-26 (gate29, and the PR agrees): the count is 3, not 1.** Measured by `git grep` over the clone at develop: `systemTest/performance/runner/cli.ts:162` (**fixed** by PR #1291, squash `3f70224a069b`), `systemTest/akto/tests/preSuiteSetup.ts:36` and `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts:42` — the last two remain open on this ticket. The original figure came from a sweep scoped to the performance package, while this DoD names `systemTest/`. Two wider sweeps add nothing to the class. The same class ALSO exists in 2 files under `Blockchain/Dev`, outside this ticket's scope — filed as KS-1347.

## Why it was not fixed in the round that found it

It is **develop's own defect**, not #1268's. #1268 touches `packages/shared`; folding an unrelated
`systemTest/performance` fix into it would widen a fix round past its declared scope and past the
files its gate reviewed.

## Search before filing

`searchIssues`, KS team, `includeArchived: true`, every page literal-matched client-side:
`preSuiteStep` **0**, `cli.ts:162` **0**, `%2520` **0**. `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` returns 3 (KS-691,
KS-149, KS-1148 — all unrelated: worktree preflight, vc-issuer tooling, CI-runner gaps).
`pre-suite.ts` returns 7, all about the step's own behaviour rather than path encoding.
Controls: `performance` **37** literal hits and `runner` **44** (the matcher fires); a nonce token
never written anywhere **0**.

title: Per-tenant DB readiness: the dormant per-tenant-database path, and the five tickets that each break it
description:
## BLUF

**Every tenant shares one database today.** Isolation comes from a `tenant_id` column plus
fail-closed RLS. A per-tenant-database path exists in the code and is **switched off**. This is the
parent for the five tickets that each break that path in a different way, so the work has one place
rather than five.

**Nothing is built by this ticket.** It exists because Kam ruled option (c) on KS-1304 — *"Leave it*
*until per-tenant databases are actually planned. Nothing changes. The ticket keeps the measurement for*
*whoever builds per-tenant databases"* (2026-09-26 07:19) — with the note **"start planning the**
**database"**. This ticket is the artefact that carries that ruling onto the board.

## Measured at `00de57baeb405d0081fe8b6f192bd40d35acef61` (develop's tip), by this seat

Re-measured here rather than carried over from the planning document, which read an older tree.

1. **The flag is set in 0 config files.** `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` occurs in exactly **two source**
   **files** — `packages/shared/src/db/tenant-pool-manager.ts:152` and
   `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:245` — and in **no** `.env`, `.example`, `.yml`,
   `.yaml` or `.json` config file. *Control: 25 config files do mention* `DATABASE_URL`*, so the*
   *config-file search is not blind.*
2. **Every tenant is seeded onto the shared database, and the code says so in its own comment.**
   `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts:1116-1144` writes all eight `tenant_config` rows
   with the same `db_name`, `db_host` and `db_port`, derived from `DATABASE_URL`. The comment at
   `:1116-1117` reads: *"Ensure all tenants have a tenant_config entry pointing to the shared*
   *'secuura' database. On Azure there is a single DB; per-tenant DBs are not provisioned."*
3. **The docs state the opposite.** `docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md:13` — *"Each client (tenant) receives an*
   *isolated PostgreSQL database"* — and `:16` — *"Each tenant has its own PostgreSQL database*
   *(*`secuura_tenant_{slug}`*)"*. `docs/RLS-FAIL-CLOSED-PLAN.md:35` — *"Real isolation is per-tenant*
   *databases."* **The second of those is internally contradictory**: the two lines immediately above
   it say RLS is *"permanently on its fail-open branch — inert today"*, so that document simultaneously
   says isolation comes from per-tenant databases and that the mechanism which would route to them is
   not in use. A reader of either doc will overestimate the isolation that exists.

A docs PR correcting both files is raised separately and links here.

## The five tickets, and why each blocks switching the path on

* **KS-1304** — `documents.ts` mixes a tenant-pool read with a default-pool write. Ruled (c): left
  until per-tenant databases are planned. `adminConfig.ts` carries 9 of the 11 `withTenant(` sites.
* **KS-1235** — auth's tenant-pool statements carry no tenant GUC.
* **KS-1055** — per-tenant databases never receive the file migrations. Measured on that ticket: a new
  tenant database comes up with RLS forced on and **zero policies**, so the app can read nothing.
* **KS-1054** — migration-runner ordering and exit status.
* **KS-598** — the MULTI_TENANCY registry upsert silently collapses. **KS-598 keeps KS-772 as its**
  **parent** (Stuart's review stream — re-parenting it would silently remove an item from a human's
  queue) and is linked here as *related* instead.

## What this ticket is NOT

* It does not choose between building the opt-in dedicated-database tier and deleting the dormant path
  and hardening RLS. **That decision is Kam's**, and it turns on whether a named customer or contract
  needs physical separation (data residency, per-tenant restore or deletion, customer-held keys) or
  whether this is defence in depth.
* It carries **facts only**. The planning document's recommendations and phasing are deliberately not
  reproduced here, so the board does not record a plan as though it were agreed.

## Search before filing

`searchIssues`, KS team, `includeArchived: true`, every page literal-matched client-side:
`per-tenant DB readiness` **0**, `tenant database readiness` **0**, `dedicated database tier` **0**;
`PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` returns **3** — KS-1055, KS-1304, KS-1235, i.e. the children, **no parent**;
`per-tenant database` returns 2, both children. Controls: `tenant` **49** literal hits and
`multi-tenancy` **8** (the matcher fires), a nonce token never written anywhere **0**.

title: POST /api/teams/notify: a permanently failing webhook is never rotated past, because last_sent_at is written only on success
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/teams/notify` now bounds its row set and **rotates** it, so a repeat call reaches rows the
previous call did not (#1274, F-1274-1). The rotation key is
`ORDER BY last_sent_at ASC NULLS FIRST, created_at ASC`.

`last_sent_at` **is written only after a SUCCESSFUL send.** A webhook that always fails — a dead peer,
or one the SSRF guard blocks — keeps a NULL `last_sent_at` for ever and therefore sorts to the **head**
**of every call**. With `TEAMS_NOTIFY_MAX_ROWS` or more permanently-failing rows, the starvation
F-1274-1 identified **returns in full**: the healthy rows past the limit are never reached by any
number of calls.

This is a **known, pinned limit of the F-1274-1 fix**, not a regression it introduced. Before that fix
the order was a fixed `created_at ASC` and *nothing* rotated.

## Where

`services/m365-integration/src/index.ts`, the notify route. The write is inside the success branch:

```ts
if (resp.ok) {
  sent.push(wh.id);
  await query('UPDATE svc_teams_webhooks SET last_sent_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1', [wh.id]);
} else {
  failed.push(wh.id);       // <- no write, so last_sent_at stays NULL
}
```

The `!result.ok` branch (guard-blocked or request-failed) likewise does not write.

## It is already pinned in code

`R3` in `src/__tests__/ks934-teams-notify-request-path-bound.test.ts` asserts the CURRENT behaviour:
with `MAX_ROWS` permanently-failing rows, a second call attempts **exactly the same set** and never
reaches the last five. **R3 is a pin, not a fix.**

⚠ **When this ticket is built, R3 WILL RED. That is the intended signal, not a breakage** — it must be
rewritten to assert the new behaviour in the same change.

Red-proved: writing `last_sent_at` on a failed attempt too (one of the fix shapes below) reds **R3 and**
**only R3** — 1 of 8 cells. So R3 discriminates today rather than passing vacuously.

## Why it was not fixed in #1274's fix round

Both available shapes reach past a fix round's declared scope:

1. **write** `last_sent_at` **on every ATTEMPT.** This changes the meaning of a **published** field —
   `lastSentAt` is returned by `GET /api/teams/webhooks` (`index.ts`, the list route) — so "last sent"
   would start meaning "last tried". A consumer cannot tell the difference and is not warned.
2. **add a** `last_attempted_at` **column.** DDL in **two** places (`docker/init/06-m365-tables.sql` and
   `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`) plus an `information_schema`-guarded backfill for
   existing deploys, then order by it.

Shape 2 is the honest one — it leaves the published field alone — but it is a schema change and
belongs in its own pass with its own review.

## Done means

1. A rotation key that advances on an ATTEMPT, not only on a success, by whichever shape is chosen.
2. A cell: `MAX_ROWS` permanently-failing rows, two calls, the second REACHES the rows past the limit.
3. `R3` rewritten in the same change (it pins the behaviour being replaced).
4. If shape 1 is chosen, the published `lastSentAt` field's meaning is documented where it is
   returned, or renamed.

## Search before filing

`searchIssues`, KS team, `includeArchived: true`, every page literal-matched client-side:
`last_sent_at`, `last_attempted_at`, `svc_teams_webhooks`, `teams/notify starvation`,
`permanently failing webhook`, `NULLS FIRST`, `teams notify rotation` — **0 literal hits each**.
Controls: `webhook` **43**, `adminConfig` **19**, `teams` **11** (the matcher fires); a nonce token
never written anywhere **0**. Noted for a later reader: KS-934's own description contains neither
`svc_teams_webhooks` nor `last_sent_at`, so those zeros are a property of the corpus, not of the
matcher.

Refs KS-934

title: adminConfig: four admin routes return err.message in a 500 body with no NODE_ENV guard (production info leak)
description:
## BLUF

Four handlers in `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts` put the thrown error's `message`
straight into a 500 response body **with no** `NODE_ENV` **guard at all**, so they leak internal text in
**production** as well as everywhere else. This is a different and worse class than KS-730, which is
about the off-production ternary shape (`NODE_ENV === 'production' ? constant : err.message`).

Found while finishing KS-730 PR 3 of 3. **Not fixed there**: KS-730 enumerated 46 ternary sites and
converted exactly those; these four were never in its list, and folding four unlisted admin routes
into a tier-1 fix round would widen it well past its declared shape.

## The four sites, measured at base `d7cdecf1d2ee`

| line | route |
| -- | -- |
| `:113` | `POST /api/admin/refresh-tenants` |
| `:1859` | `POST /api/admin/backfill-certification-metadata` |
| `:2031` | `POST /api/admin/seed-demo-users` |
| `:2158` | `POST /api/admin/migrate-tenant-data` |

Each is the same shape:

```
res.status(500).json({ success: false, error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: err.message } });
```

(`:113` is `message: err?.message || 'Refresh failed'`, the same leak with a fallback.)

**Pre-existing, not introduced:** the count is **4 at the base** `d7cdecf1d2ee` **and 4 at the KS-730 PR 3**
**head**. KS-730 PR 3 neither added nor removed any of them.

## Why it was invisible to KS-730's own guard

KS-730 PR 3's source cell asserts `liveTernaries: 0` and `helperCalls: 46`. Both are TRUE with these
four present, because the cell counts the `NODE_ENV === 'production'` shape — which these four do not
have. A green KS-730 cell therefore says nothing about them, which is exactly why they are pinned
separately rather than left to be rediscovered.

## The regression guard that already exists

`KS-730 C4 SOURCE`, in
`services/originate/src/__tests__/ks730c-adminconfig-500-never-answers-err-message.test.ts`, pins these
four **by enclosing route name**. A fifth site reds it. **Fixing one of these four will also red it** —
that is deliberate: the list is then updated as part of the fix rather than drifting silently.
**Whoever builds this ticket must update that cell's** `KNOWN` **list in the same change.**
Red-proved: adding a fifth unconditional site reds C4 and nothing else (1 of 14).

## Done means

1. The four sites answer the constant body and log the message server-side, as KS-730's 46 do
   (`fail500` already exists in this file and is the obvious vehicle).
2. `KS-730 C4 SOURCE`'s `KNOWN` list is emptied, or the cell retired with its reasoning recorded.
3. A cell drives at least one of the four end to end and proves the thrown text is absent from the

title: anchorStateSync's four persisting writers pass anchor.blockNumber through unshaped — the KS-1129 class on GET /api/anchors/:id
description:
## BLUF

`services/anchorStateSync.ts` has **four** writers that persist `blockHeight: anchor.blockNumber || 0` without shaping it. `anchor.blockNumber` comes from `GET /api/anchors/:id` — a **different endpoint** from the one #1220 fixed — so whether it arrives as a raw `pg` int8 **string** is **UNMEASURED**. If it does, all four persist a string into the document blob, and the gateway's tier-1 read refuses a string (`typeof persistedBlockHeight === 'number'`), so a document that IS on chain answers off-chain-only.

Filed on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-09-25 21:00Z, which was explicit that this must **not** be folded into KS-1074: being in the same file makes it cheap, but it does not put it in scope, and folding it in would change what KS-1074 claims and what its gate grades.

## The four sites, each traced to its write (read at develop `d7cdecf1d2ee`)

| site | writer | persists via |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `anchorStateSync.ts:231` | poller, real txHash — the **SUCCESS** path | `updateDocument(documentId, tenantId, { blockchain: … })` |
| `:266` | poller, simulated declaration | same |
| `:346` | read-time reconcile, heal-to-confirmed | same |
| `:382` | read-time reconcile, heal-to-simulated | same |

All four restate the blob wholesale, so the value they compute is the value stored: `updateDocument` replaces the `blockchain` column via a top-level spread (`documentRepo.ts`, `{ ...doc, ...updates }`).

## What is measured, and what is NOT

**Measured:** the four sites exist, all four reach `updateDocument`, and `|| 0` does **not** protect against a string — `'4242' || 0` is `'4242'`. `pg` 8.x returns int8 as a string by default and there is no `setTypeParser` for int8 anywhere in `Blockchain/Dev`.

**NOT measured, and it is the whole question:** whether `GET /api/anchors/:id` returns `blockNumber` as a number. #1220 (`847159dccd1e`) fixed `anchoring/src/anchorReadback.ts`, which serves the **verify** endpoint. The `AnchorReadState` interface in `anchorStateSync.ts` declares `blockNumber?: number | null`, which is a **declaration, not a measurement** — the same shape of assumption KS-1129 was filed against.

**So the first step is a measurement, not a fix:** read what `GET /api/anchors/:id` actually returns for a real anchored row. If it is already a number, the correct outcome is a recorded reason and a cell pinning it, not a coercion.

## Done when

- [ ] `GET /api/anchors/:id`'s `blockNumber` type is measured at source (or against a running anchoring service) and the reading recorded here.
- [ ] If it can be a string: all four sites shape it, using the same refusals as `toBlockHeight` / `toBlockNumber` — an empty string becomes null rather than `Number('') === 0`, an unconvertible value becomes null rather than `NaN`, and a real `0` is preserved.
- [ ] One cell per writer, each red before the fix, because four separate object literals are four separate claims. That is how four writers survived KS-1058 on the neighbouring `threadToken` defect.
- [ ] `|| 0` is reviewed per site while there: it also turns a legitimate `0` height into `0` by a different route, which is harmless, and turns `null` into `0`, which fabricates a height. Whether that should become `??` is part of this ticket.

## Sequencing

**Build this AFTER KS-1074 merges.** It touches the same file (`anchorStateSync.ts`) as KS-1074's five-writer change, and four of its sites are lines KS-1074 edits the immediate neighbourhood of.

## Board searched before filing

Literal match over **1,322** issues including archived and **3,737** comments:

* `blockHeight: anchor.blockNumber` → **1** hit, KS-1129 itself;
* `anchor.blockNumber || 0` → **2** hits, KS-1129 and KS-1130 (Done, archived);
* `anchorStateSync` → 14 hits, none owning these four sites;
* `GET /api/anchors/:id` → 9 hits, none owning them.

**No open ticket owns this.** Controls: the nonsense token `QQZX7VNOSUCHTOKEN29` → **0** hits (now spent by being written here), and `withTenant` → **14**, so the search discriminates.

Raised from the #1280 build (KS-1129's originate half).

Refs KS-1129

title: pre-push fixture guard: re-land GUARDGAPS with a call-site reader that passes the aborting `||` / `if` / `&&` shapes and flags multi-line `$(` and group openers
description:
**BLUF: the fixture guard's round-2 work was measured correct in cells 7 and 8 and shipped nothing, because cell 9's reader flags shapes that DO abort and passes shapes that swallow the abort — wrong in both directions.** This ticket re-lands the work with a reader that discriminates, and it resolves a contradiction in the earlier hold text.

## What is on `develop` today

Guard blob `52c852203edc2d7b64c3e23bc2ab3f077cf07cc6` at 6 cells, with three gaps all open: unanchored abort counts, a `repo_state` blind to the worktree, and no call-site pin. **Reach is 0 today** — all 12 of 12 call sites are bare — so nothing is currently mis-scored; the guard simply cannot see a regression.

## What the reader must do

Through the real guard, cell 9 currently **FLAGS** the named aborting shapes:
`bf || true` · `false || bf` · `if bf; then :; fi` · `bf && :`
and **PASSES** the named swallowing shapes: a multi-line `x=$(` / call / `)` and `( : noop` / call / `)`.

That is backwards. `build_fixture` aborts with an explicit `exit 2`, so only a **subshell** call site swallows it; `|| true`, `if` and `&&` do not.

## Scope

Re-land the anchored counts (cell 7), the widened `repo_state` (cell 8) and cells 11-12 from blob `5189cf31a098a62c485367beedb78def2428d787`, with `c9_scan` **admitting** `bf || true`, `false || bf`, `if bf; then :; fi` and `bf && :`, and **flagging** a previous line ending in `$(` / `(` or holding an unclosed `(`. Cell 10 computes `c9_scan`; cell 12 asserts on a subject copy.

## The contradiction to resolve, named by the gate to the filer

The earlier hold asked for a **strict whitelist** AND for the `||` shapes to be **unflagged**. Those two contradict each other. **The admitting whitelist is the one to pick** — that is the gate's own note to whoever picks this up.

## A limit worth carrying forward rather than rediscovering

Do not attempt to track shell nesting by counting parentheses. A paren-depth counter over lines called 11 of 12 real call sites offending, because a subshell can close with `) > "$WORK/c0.out" 2>/dev/null` and a multi-line `$( … )` can end with `)"`. A guard that half-parses shell is worse than one with a declared limit: read one line of context and write the limitation down.

## Evidence produced by the gate

`evidence/reader1253/reader_rows.json` · `evidence/reader1253/guard_*.stdout` · `behav_*.stdout` · `evidence/g1253/garms_rows.json`.

title: run-shell-suites.sh: a suite's untrapped background grandchild survives a signal to the runner
description:
**BLUF: signalling the runner does not reach a suite's own background grandchild.** `develop` leaves the whole suite behind; the fix is to forward the signal to the suite's **process group** rather than to the suite's pid alone.

## Why this is a separate ticket from the runner's signal handling

It is **pre-existing on** `develop` and it is a different fix. The runner's trap work decides what the *runner* does on a signal; this decides what the *suite's descendants* do. One can land without the other, and neither proves the other, so they are separate workloads.

Forward the signal to the suite's process group, so a suite that forks a background child does not leave that child running after the runner has been told to stop.

title: run-shell-suites.sh: re-land the round-2 signal handling with a SIGINT-to-pid arm that asserts under `set -m`
description:
**BLUF: the round-2 signal handling for** `run-shell-suites.sh` **was measured CORRECT and shipped nothing, because its suite's SIGINT-to-pid arm is gated as a constant UNREACHABLE while it in fact measures REACHABLE and DISCRIMINATING under the harness's own** `set -m`**.** The runner fix is not in dispute — the arm's reachability gate is. This ticket re-lands the runner with the gate corrected. One test pass proves all three items below, which is why they are one ticket and not three.

## What is on `develop` today, and what it costs

Runner blob `85920863d70454db21b0198cc66fc06e92ff8223`, with no trap:

* a `/tmp/rss.*` directory left behind per long-TMPDIR run;
* a `| tee` wait on a suite's background child;
* a lone SIGINT to the runner pid exiting **rc 0 with a green verdict**;
* SIGTERM leaving both the directory and the running suite.

The round-2 runner fixes all four, and SIGTERM was measured to STOP.

## Item 1 — re-land the runner and correct the arm's gate

Re-land the round-2 runner, measured correct at blob `8eef1c4877b30f7dfeb485dbb1955a53a6122fd5`: EXIT-only cleanup; INT/TERM clean up, untrap, kill the child and **re-raise**; suites run background plus `wait`; no pipe.

The suite's INT-to-pid arm runs `signal_run INT pid` **gated only by** `sig_installable` **(rule 1)**, and the PR matrix states that rule 2 holds only **without** job control. Under the harness's own `set -m` the arm is reachable, so the constant UNREACHABLE is wrong and the matrix needs correcting with it.

The two shell rules this rests on, both measured on `/bin/bash` 3.2.57:

1. **A signal IGNORED ON ENTRY to bash cannot be trapped** — `trap -p INT` comes back empty. The in-hook preflight is such a parent.
2. **bash ignores SIGINT in any ASYNCHRONOUS (background) job**, whatever the parent's disposition. The identical trap in the **foreground** gives rc 130.

Rule 2 is the one that does not hold under job control, and that is the whole point of this item.

## Item 2 — pin that a signal interrupts the runner promptly

With the suite back in the foreground all three signal arms still pass. Add a **kill-to-exit latency bound relative to the fixture suite's sleep**, so "it stopped" is measured rather than assumed.

## Item 3 — the background launch changed behaviour; document it or preserve both

Suites now start with **SIGINT ignored and stdin at** `/dev/null`. Reach is 0 today, so nothing is broken — but it is an undocumented behaviour change of the background launch and should either be stated or reverted to preserve both.

## Evidence produced by the gate

`evidence/trapprobe/trapprobe_rows.json` · `evidence/r1250/RE_head.stdout` · `RE_r1.stdout` · `RE_dev.stdout` · `RE_head_intign.stdout` · `1250_shellprobe.out` · `evidence/r1250/V_RF.stdout` · `evidence/trapprobe/latency_RF.out` · `evidence/r1250/maskprobe.out` · `census_int_stdin.out`.

Searched over **483 open issues**, matching literally against identifier + title + description rather than by fuzzy search: `set -m`, `signal_run`, `sig_installable`, `trapprobe`, `8eef1c4877b3` — **0 open hits each**. `SIGINT-to-pid` returned 1 (the pseudo-terminal harness ticket, a different workload). A fresh nonsense control token returned **0** and `run-shell-suites.sh` returned **16**, so the instrument discriminates in both directions.

title: packages/shared does not type-check src/__tests__, hiding 10 errors — add a test-inclusive tsc leg and fix them
description:
## BLUF

`npx tsc -p . --noEmit` in `packages/shared` returns **rc 0**, and always has. That is not health: `tsconfig.json` carries `"exclude": ["node_modules", "dist", "src/__tests__"]`, so **the package's own type-check never sees a test file**. Under a program that does include them there are **10 errors across 6 files**. The exclusion is the defect; the 10 are its consequence.

Filed from KS-1179's TYPECHECK-DEBT item on the coordinator's ruling (one ticket, not two: a single test pass proves it, because the new leg goes green only once the errors are gone).

## The 10, measured

| file | errors |
| -- | -- |
| `src/__tests__/ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts` | 2x **TS2345** (`Express` not assignable), 1x TS2741 |
| `src/security/ssrf-guard.ts` | 1x **TS2349** (see below), 1x TS7006 — **TS7006 fixed in KS-1179** |
| `src/__tests__/openapi-operation-ids.test.ts` | 1x TS2352 |
| `src/__tests__/openapi-415-injection.test.ts` | 1x TS2352 |
| `src/__tests__/ks914-pinned-address.test.ts` | 2x TS6133 (unused `vi`, unused `safeOutboundRequest`) |
| `src/__tests__/walkTimeouts.test.ts` | 1x TS5097 (`.ts` import extension) |

⚠ `ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts`**'s three are blocked until PR #1268 merges.** That PR is open and changes the same file; two branches on one file needs a declared merged-blob equality target. Do them after it lands.

## TS2349 — carried here because it does NOT fix cleanly

`mod` is `typeof https | typeof http` and calling the union of their overloads is the error. Four shapes were measured and **each relocated it**:

| attempt | result |
| -- | -- |
| no change | **TS2349** not callable |
| cast the callee `(mod.request as typeof https.request)` | **TS2769** no overload matches — `agent` is `https.Agent \| http.Agent` |
| callee cast + `agent: agent as https.Agent` at the call site | errors 10 -> 8, clean, **but the emit changes**: `agent,` expands to `agent: agent,` |
| callee cast + the assertion on the declaration | emit identical again, **TS2352** — the two Agent types "neither sufficiently overlaps" |

The only remaining shape is `as unknown as https.Agent`. **It was refused deliberately:** in an SSRF guard, a type the compiler stops checking is the risk to avoid. The honest fix is narrowing at the branch (`isTls ? https.request(...) : http.request(...)`), which **duplicates the call and changes the emit** — a real change to the request path, and not something a type error alone justifies. Decide it here, with the guard's owner.

## Method, so this is reproducible

A probe config **outside the repo**, extending the package's own `tsconfig.json` and overriding only:

```json
{ "compilerOptions": { "noEmit": true, "module": "esnext", "target": "ES2022" },
  "include": ["<pkg>/src/**/*.ts"], "exclude": [] }
```

`module`/`target` are raised only because the tests use top-level `await`; leaving them at the package's `commonjs` produces **9x TS1343 and 5x TS1378 that are artefacts of the probe**, not of the tree.

**Controls, because two earlier probes gave wrong answers:**

* **A** — the probe must SEE the file: `--listFilesOnly | grep <file>` returns 1.
* **B** — the probe must REPORT an error in it: planting `const x: number = "not a number";` takes it from **10 -> 11**, the new one naming the file and line. *(First read of this control grepped for the variable name and found 0 — tsc prints the file and line, not the identifier. The probe was fine; the grep was not.)*
* A probe adding `types: ["vitest/globals","node"]` reported **2 errors, both TS2688** — its own type-resolution failure silencing everything else. A probe that reports almost nothing looks like a clean tree.
* The same 10 reproduce under `moduleResolution: node` (the package's own) as under `bundler`, so they are not a resolution artefact. *(A duplicate-*`@types/node` *theory was raised and withdrawn: the tree holds 30 copies at three majors, but this program loads exactly one.)*

## Definition of done

- [ ] `packages/shared` type-checks `src/__tests__` — a leg or script that fails on a type error in a test file, with a positive control proving it can fail
- [ ] the 10 above resolved, or each recorded with the reason (TS2349 is a decision, see above)
- [ ] the ks781 three done after #1268 merges

⚠ **The leg touches the push gate**, which is not in the KS-1179 lane. That is why this is a separate ticket rather than more of that PR.

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1,318 issues (includeArchived) and 3,718 comments**: `tsconfig` -> 67 total / 30 open · `src/__tests__` -> 178 / 93 · `TS2345` -> 5 / 4 (KS-1313, KS-1179, KS-932, KS-872 — the F-3 lineage and L6's, none this subject) · `TS2349` -> **0** · `type-checks` -> 23 / 14. **No open issue is about the exclusion itself.** Controls: `readYaml` -> 13 total / 11 open, fires; a fresh token never written anywhere -> **0**.

Refs KS-1179

title: services/kyc db.retry.test.ts exceeds vitest's 5 s default under fleet load — 11498 ms loaded vs 675 ms alone; KS-1155's fix covers only packages/shared's walkers
description:
## BLUF

`services/kyc/src/__tests__/db.retry.test.ts` → `db availability retry (KS-377) > reports available immediately when the probe succeeds at boot` fails `Test timed out in 5000ms` when the box carries fleet load, having taken **11498 ms**. The assertion holds: the same cell passes in **675 ms** alone. This is the KS-1155 load class in a **service** suite, which KS-1155's delivered fix does not reach.

## Why KS-1155 does not cover it

KS-1155 shipped as #1254: *"the seven tree-walking guard suites get a 60 s budget from config; **every other suite keeps the 5 s default**."* That scope is `packages/shared`'s repo-tree-walking guards. `db.retry.test.ts` is in `services/kyc`, is not a tree-walking guard, and therefore still runs on the 5 s default.

KS-1053 names the same class for the `services/auth` ks949 cell — related, a different subject.

## The measurement (2026-09-26, Seat L8, on a tree where this file is blob-identical to develop `4db87c3e4b98`)

Four ways, because a timeout must be proven load-induced rather than called flaky:

| run | result |
| -- | -- |
| full kyc suite, **while a push's shell suites ran concurrently** | **1 failed / 29 passed (30)**, 13.11 s; the failure is `Test timed out in 5000ms`, the cell having taken **11498 ms** |
| `db.retry.test.ts` **alone** at develop | **5/5, 675 ms** |
| `db.retry.test.ts` **alone** in a worktree carrying an unrelated `kyc/src/index.ts` change | **5/5, 658 ms** |
| full kyc suite re-run **once the push finished and the box was quiet** | **30/30, 965 ms** |

The suite's own reported test time in the loaded run was **428–536 ms**; the overrun is scheduling, not work.

**Not caused by any change:** the worktree's diff touches `services/kyc/src/index.ts` and adds one new test file. `db.retry.test.ts` imports `../db` dynamically and never reaches `index.ts`.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

A red `Test timed out in 5000ms` here is indistinguishable, from the run alone, from a real regression in the DB boot latch (KS-377's subject). A seat that trusts it re-runs and loses minutes; a seat that does not trust it may dismiss a genuine failure in the same file later. The class needs a home in `services/` as it now has in `packages/shared`.

## Fix shapes, not chosen here

1. Extend KS-1155's config approach to the affected `services/*` suites — a named budget for the cells that are scheduling-sensitive, with every other cell left on the 5 s default.
2. Give this file its own `testTimeout` at the `describe`/cell level, which is the smallest change and keeps the budget beside the code that needs it.
3. Make the cell insensitive to scheduling (it uses fake timers around a retry loop), if that can be done without weakening what it pins.

**Not built this round** — outside Seat L8's queue; filed on the coordinator's instruction.

## Board search before filing (1,316 issues **including archived**, 3,705 comments; literal match)

* `db.retry.test.ts` → KS-419 and KS-382, **both archived** and both about the DB boot latch, not timeouts.
* `testTimeout` → KS-1155 only. `Test timed out` → KS-1155 only (+6 comments). `fleet load` → KS-1155, KS-1324, KS-1181, KS-1182.
* KS-1155 read in full: scoped to `packages/shared` tree-walking guards; its merged fix explicitly leaves every other suite on the 5 s default.
* **Controls:** `KS-1155` → 4 / 7 and `KS-849` → 1 / 1 both fire; a nonsense token → **0 / 0**.

No open ticket covers kyc's timeouts, so this is a new ticket rather than a comment on KS-1155.

Refs KS-1155

title: kyc verification writes are a whole-row read-modify-write: two timers, or a timer and an admin review, can still race
description:
## BLUF

`services/kyc` persists a verification by reading the **whole row**, mutating the object, and writing the **whole row** back through an upsert whose `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET` names `status`, `current_level`, `documents`, `liveness_completed`, `liveness_score`, `checks`, `overall_score`, `risk_level`, `reviewed_by`, `review_notes`, `updated_at` and `completed_at`. Nothing serialises those writers. So any two of them overlapping — two mock timers, or a timer and an admin review — can still lose one side's changes.

KS-849's fix (re-reading inside each mock timer) **narrows the window from 1500/3000 ms to the read-modify-write's own microseconds, and that is all it can do.** It does not make the write atomic.

## The part KS-849 explicitly does NOT close, measured

The 3000 ms auto-approve timer at `services/kyc/src/index.ts` sets `status = 'approved'` and `currentLevel = requestedLevel` **itself**. So after the re-read:

* **FIXED** — every field the timer does not own survives an admin review landing inside the window: `reviewedBy`, `reviewNotes`, `documents`, `livenessCompleted`, `livenessScore`, and checks that are no longer `pending`.
* **NOT FIXED** — an admin **rejection** through `POST /api/kyc/:id/review` inside those 3 seconds is **still overwritten to** `approved`, and a `newLevel` supplied by the reviewer is still replaced by `requestedLevel`.

This correction matters because the KS-849 ticket's own fix-shape text ("re-read the verification inside the timer") reads as though it addresses the admin-overwrite case. **It does not**, and the ticket should not be read that way.

## Where it is pinned rather than left to be rediscovered

PR for KS-849 adds `services/kyc/src/__tests__/ks849-mock-timer-stale-write.test.ts`, whose cell **S3 asserts** `status === 'approved'` **after a rejection**, with a comment stating this is not fixed and is tracked here. A later reader cannot mistake the limit for closed.

## Fix shapes, not chosen here

1. A **single-statement partial UPDATE** per writer, naming only the columns that writer owns, instead of the whole-row upsert. Removes the class for non-overlapping column sets; two writers to the *same* column still race.
2. **Row locking** (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` inside a transaction) around read-modify-write.
3. Move the mock auto-approve **off the request path** entirely, which removes the 3 s window but not the class.

Both (1) and (2) are behaviour changes to a persistence path and want their own gate, which is why this is a ticket rather than part of KS-849.

## Scope

The mock/demo path gates the timers (`KYC_PROVIDER === 'mock'`), but **the whole-row upsert is not mock-gated** — `/review`, `/complete`, `/document` and `/selfie` all write through it in every mode. So the timers are the reachable trigger today; the class is wider than the trigger.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,316 issues **including archived**, 3,705 comments; literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `auto-approve` → 0 titles/descriptions, 2 comments · `autoApprove` → 0 · `row locking` → 0 · `read-modify-write` → 0 titles, 1 comment · `stale write` → 0.
* `partial UPDATE` → 1 (KS-938, TOTP seed retention — unrelated).
* `svc_kyc_verifications` → KS-851 (column ordinal drift, a different defect) and KS-386 (archived, image payload).
* `KYC_PROVIDER` → KS-849 itself and KS-626 (archived, Entra callback).
* **Controls that fire:** `KS-1155` → 4 titles / 7 comments; `KS-849` → 1 / 1; a nonsense token `zzqx-l8-never-written-anywhere-7731` → **0 / 0**. So the search discriminates. (That token is now spent by appearing here.)

Nothing on the board describes this class in kyc.

Refs KS-849

title: childSuiteCounts reads a child KILLED by its own 180 s spawnSync timeout as a PASS - a lookalike summary pair is accepted as {7,0}
description:
**BLUF:** `childSuiteCounts` **can report a clean pass for a child process that was killed.** When a child is terminated by its own 180 s `spawnSync` timeout *after* it has already logged a summary-shaped pair, the reader takes that pair as the verdict and returns `{7,0}`. The kill is invisible to it. **Measured on both sides** - at PR #1245's head `65eb964271b0d6895e90fe8f5ffcbbbb9a484050` **and** on `develop` `4db87c3e4b98b8e366c3dd60d5f399917bad5086` - so this is a property of the code on the mainline, not of one branch.

This is the residue of a capped round. Nothing shipped for it; the pull request that attempted it stays open and its disposition sits with the repository owner.

## The lookalike that is accepted

A child that logs

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

and is then killed still presents that pair to the reader. `childSuiteCounts` returns `{7,0}` - seven passed, zero failed - and nothing downstream can tell that outcome apart from a genuine completion. **A verdict composed separately from the work reproduces here exactly:** the summary text is not evidence that the run finished.

## Three residues, one test pass, one ticket

1. **KILLED-AFTER-LOOKALIKE** - the defect above.
2. **CALLSITE-STILL-TEXT** - the call site still reaches the summary through text. The shape asked for is a pure `countsFromSpawn(result)` sitting behind `childSuiteCounts`, fed a synthetic spawn result, so the decision is made from the spawn outcome rather than from scraped output.
3. **JOINED-CLAIM** - the sentence *"measured to hold on the JOINED text"* should be dropped. It is not true: **10 real shapes are misread on joined text, 3 of them silently.** A claim about where a reader is safe, which is false, is worse than no claim.

## Fix shapes, any one of which closes the first residue

* **Refuse when the spawn says so:** `result.error` or `result.signal` set, or `result.status` not `0`/`1`.
* **Require vitest's trailing** `Start at` **/** `Duration` **block**, which a killed child never reaches.
* **Use the JSON reporter** instead of parsing human output.

## Cells the next attempt should carry

* The **H1 stdout capture** returns `null`.
* A spawn result of `{status 143, ETIMEDOUT}` **throws** rather than yielding counts.

Signal 143 is SIGTERM; a status of 143 with `ETIMEDOUT` is precisely the killed-child case, and it is the discriminating fixture.

## Reusable from the capped attempt - do not rebuild these

The round-2 **stdout-only reader**, the **whole-run cells**, and the `{3,2}` **row** are sound and are the parts to start from.

## Not covered

Preflight legs 3, 4 and 8 were not run for that attempt (no local stack). They are owed by nothing here; recorded so the absence is not mistaken for a pass.

## Board search before filing

Searched over **481 open issues** on this team, matching literally against identifier + title + description rather than by fuzzy search: `countsFromSpawn`, `KILLED-AFTER-LOOKALIKE`, `CALLSITE-STILL-TEXT`, `JOINED-CLAIM`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `status 143`, `capturedChildOutput` - **0 open hits each**. `spawnSync` returned 2 (KS-1111, KS-1098), neither about this reader. A fresh nonsense control token returned **0** and `childSuiteCounts` returned **1**, so the instrument discriminates in both directions.

**Not duplicates, deliberately:** KS-1313 is the parent this residue falls out of, and KS-1226 is its own parent. Both stay open and neither is closed by this ticket.

Refs KS-1313

title: A PTY harness so SIGINT can be asserted for run-shell-suites.sh in the foreground, in both the standalone and in-hook environments
description:
**BLUF: there is currently no way to assert that** `run-shell-suites.sh` **handles SIGINT, because every available harness either backgrounds the runner or runs with SIGINT already ignored - and bash discards the signal in both cases.** A pseudo-terminal harness is the only route to closing that gap. Nothing is broken today; the runner's INT/TERM arms exist and are correct. What is missing is the ability to *prove* the INT arm, and today that is recorded as UNREACHABLE rather than tested.

## The two measured rules that create the gap

Both measured on `/bin/bash` 3.2.57, which is the only bash on this drive - there is no Homebrew bash cellar and every local project image is busybox/Alpine with no `bash` at all.

1. **A signal IGNORED ON ENTRY to bash cannot be trapped.** `trap '...' INT` is silently not installed and `trap -p INT` comes back empty. **The in-hook preflight runs with SIGINT ignored**, so an INT arm inside the hook cannot exist at all.
2. **bash ignores SIGINT in any ASYNCHRONOUS (background) job**, whatever the parent's disposition: `trap -p INT` empty, the signal discarded, rc 0. The identical trap in the **foreground** gives rc 130.

Between them, SIGINT-to-pid is unassertable by any harness that backgrounds the runner, which is what a test harness naturally does in order to hold its pid.

## Current state, so this is not read as a defect report

The runner's signal arms were built and accepted on the ruling that each arm **probes its own reachability** and either asserts all four properties or reports UNREACHABLE naming the rule above. That is the right behaviour given the constraint. TERM is assertable and is asserted. INT is not, and says so.

## What this ticket asks for

One harness that runs `run-shell-suites.sh` **in the foreground of a pseudo-terminal** so a real SIGINT can be delivered to it and its disposition observed, usable from:

* a standalone run, and
* the in-hook environment, where the parent's disposition is the thing being worked around.

Candidate mechanisms, none chosen here: `script -q` (present on macOS and on Linux with different argument orders), a small `openpty`/`forkpty` helper, or Python's `pty` module driving the runner. The acceptance criterion is the discriminating one: **the same harness must give rc 130 on a foreground INT and must show the arm reporting UNREACHABLE when the signal is ignored on entry** - a harness that only ever produces one of those has not measured anything.

## Proposed tier

**Tier 2.** It is test-infrastructure with no runtime surface, but it is the only path to converting a standing UNREACHABLE into an assertion, and the rules above will otherwise be re-derived by whoever next touches the runner's signal handling.

## Board search before filing

Searched, over 479 open issues on this team, matching literally against identifier + title + description: `pseudo-terminal`, `pseudoterminal`, `SIGINT`, `script -q`, `openpty`, `forkpty`, `PTY harness` - **0 open hits each**. A fresh nonsense control token returned **0** and `run-shell-suites` returned **14**, so the instrument discriminates in both directions.

Note for anyone re-running this search: the bare term `pty` is useless here - it is a substring of "empty" and returned **69** open hits on this corpus. Use a word boundary or a longer term.

Refs KS-1302

title: run_shell_suites.test.sh KS-1303 cell: a `-lt 6` WALL-CLOCK margin against a 15 s child is load-sensitive - assert from the verdict, not the clock
description:
**BLUF: the KS-1303 cell in** `run_shell_suites.test.sh` **decides pass/fail on a wall-clock reading, so heavy machine load can red it for a reason that has nothing to do with the code under test.** Non-blocking: the cell is correct, its control is sound, and it was green on every run observed. This is about what reddens it in future, not about the fix it guards.

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/run_shell_suites.test.sh`, lines 570-575 at PR #1250's head `2b8dcb824dd2c5cd4b92757934d7de9d28813a22`. Line numbers move once that PR merges; the anchor is the `T1303_START` / `T1303_ELAPSED` block.

## What it asserts

```
T1303_START="$(date +%s)"
( cd "$R1303/Blockchain/Dev" && bash scripts/run-shell-suites.sh > "$TMP/t1303.out" 2>&1 )
T1303_RC=$?
T1303_ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - T1303_START ))
check 'KS-1303: a suite leaving a background child does not hold the runner (under 6 s; `| tee` waited the full 15)' 1 \
  "$( [ "$T1303_ELAPSED" -lt 6 ] && echo 1 || echo 0 )"
```

The fixture forks a child that outlives its suite by **15 s**. Before the fix, `tee` could not see EOF while that child held the write end of the pipe, so the runner waited the full 15 s. After the fix it returns as soon as the suite does.

## Why it is load-sensitive

The pass window is **0-5 s of wall clock**, measured on a whole `run-shell-suites.sh` invocation inside a freshly built scratch repository. Nothing in that window is reserved for the runner's own startup, so the cell's verdict is a race between the fix working and the machine being busy. The `-lt 6` figure is a proxy for "returned without waiting on the child"; it is not the property itself.

This is the same family as KS-1155, where tree-walking guards exceeded vitest's 5 s default under fleet load. Different file and different suite, so not a duplicate - the shared trait is a fixed time budget standing in for a behavioural claim.

## What is already right, and should not be removed

* The cell has a **control** at lines 578-579 pinning that the forking suite actually RAN and scored a pass (`shell suites: 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (of 1)`), so "the runner was fast" cannot be satisfied by a skipped or crashed suite.
* The fixture deliberately does **not** redirect the child's output. Holding the write end of the pipe is the whole mechanism; a tidied `sleep 15 >/dev/null 2>&1 &` made the cell pass against the *unfixed* runner. The reason is written into the suite beside the fixture and must stay there.

## Fix shapes (not chosen here)

1. Assert from the **runner's own verdict plus a child-held marker** - the child writes a marker, the runner's completion is compared against the marker's absence - so the claim is "did not wait for the child" rather than "took under 6 s".
2. Or keep the clock but widen the margin to something well below 15 s and far above any plausible startup (for example 10 s), so the cell still discriminates the 15 s wait while tolerating a loaded machine.

Shape 1 removes the timing dependency; shape 2 keeps it and only reduces the false-red rate.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed

The cell sits on a pull request whose next gate verdict is its cap. Re-cutting that head to change a cell nobody has called wrong would add a variable to a review already in flight.

## Board search before filing

Searched, over 479 open issues on this team, matching literally against identifier + title + description: `run_shell_suites.test.sh` (3 open hits - KS-1135 long-TMPDIR tsx socket, KS-1127 exit-0 SKIP counted as passed, KS-1089 `--list` polish; none is this cell), `-lt 6`, `load-sensitive`, `timing cell` - **0 open hits each**. A fresh nonsense control token returned **0**, and `run-shell-suites` returned **14**, so the instrument discriminates in both directions. The control token is deliberately not quoted here: a token written into a ticket body becomes findable and stops being a control.

Refs KS-1302
Refs KS-1303

title: Seat push tooling reuses one push-log name per worktree, so a push record is overwritten and the earlier STOP-count evidence is lost
description:
## BLUF

`push24.sh` (and its predecessors `push22/23.sh`) name the push log by the **worktree basename**: `<worktree>-push.out`. A seat that pushes twice from the same worktree **overwrites the first push's log**, and with it the in-hook evidence — the fleet STOP counts, the leg-by-leg preflight output and the `FIXTURE BUILD FAILED` check for that push.

Confirmed by the tier-2 gate on #1255 (report `2026-09-26-batch1249-t2b`, finding **N-1255-a**, READ): `raise/s-b28-cells-push.out` held a push from `15:50:24Z` to `15:57:03Z`, overwritten again afterwards — **#1255's own push record is gone.** Non-blocking; nothing shipped wrongly, and the counts were quoted into the PR from the run at the time.

## Why it matters

A PR's Test Evidence block quotes the STOP counts from that push's log. If the log has been overwritten by a later push from the same worktree, the evidence behind a merged PR is no longer re-readable — the claim survives and its source does not. That is an evidence-integrity gap, not a correctness one, which is why it is non-blocking and still worth closing.

## Fix shape (the gate's)

Name the push log by the **head sha** (or append `-push-<n>`), never reused. Same for the `.start`, `.end`, `.rc` and `-stubs.txt` siblings, which share the defect.

## Done when

- [ ] two pushes from one worktree leave two distinct logs, both readable afterwards
- [ ] the naming includes something that cannot repeat (head sha preferred)
- [ ] a control: push twice from one worktree and assert both files exist with different names

## Board search before filing

Literal match over 1,310 issues incl. archived and 3,687 comments: `push24.sh` → 0; `-push.out` → 0; `push log` → 4 total / 3 open (KS-1201, KS-1047, KS-948), each about other things (login_stub orphans, the hook's leg naming, an unrelated script) — **none about log-name reuse.** No existing home. Controls: `withTenant` → 12, `ZZZNOSUCHSYMBOLZZZ` → 0.

Raised from the #1255 merge (develop `4db87c3e4b98b8e366c3dd60d5f399917bad5086`).

title: Published spec descriptions carry internal ticket keys ("KS-1275:", "KS-1118 F-3", "KS-1133 — HASH ALIAS ORDER") — the owner's call
description:
## BLUF

The **served** OpenAPI description text now carries internal ticket keys. #1252 added `"KS-1275:"` and `"KS-1118 F-3"` to two descriptions in `originate.openapi.ts`, and they are published into `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` and served from `/api/docs`.

**This is a pre-existing style, not a new one** — `"KS-1133 — HASH ALIAS ORDER"` was already in the same file's v2 verify description before #1252.

Recorded by the tier-2 gate on #1252 (report `2026-09-26-batch1249-t2b`, finding **N-1252-b**, READ) as Polish and explicitly **the owner's call**.

## The decision, stated plainly

Ticket keys in a published description are useful to us and meaningless to an integrator reading the contract. Two defensible positions:

* **Keep them.** They make the reason for a wording discoverable, and the convention is already established in this file.
* **Strip them.** The published contract is customer-facing; internal identifiers belong in the source comment, not the served text. The source comment above each description can carry the key instead.

**No change should be made on a seat's own judgement** — hence a ticket rather than a fix. If the answer is "strip", it is a sweep across the spec (three known instances and possibly more), not a one-line edit.

## Scope, measured

Instances found in the published description text: `KS-1275:` and `KS-1118 F-3` (added by #1252), `KS-1133 — HASH ALIAS ORDER` (pre-existing). A full sweep of `originate.openapi.ts` description strings has not been done and is part of the work if the ruling is to strip.

## Done when

- [ ] a ruling is recorded: keep, or strip
- [ ] if strip: every instance in the published description text removed, the key moved to the adjacent source comment, and the yaml regenerated
- [ ] if keep: the convention written down where the next editor will find it, so it is a decision rather than an accident

## Board search before filing

Literal match over 1,310 issues incl. archived and 3,687 comments: `HASH ALIAS ORDER` and `SPEC-PROSE` searched alongside `originate.openapi.ts` (30 total / 11 open) and `docs/VOCABULARY.md` (13 / 7) — the path hits are about spec content generally, none about **internal keys in the published text**. No existing home. Controls fire as above.

Raised from the #1252 merge (develop `49bc69abae1528d8da76018aaa68b04749e5d93b`).

title: Nothing tells a PR author the 92-char squash-subject limit until a gate reads the PR — 3 of 4 titles over it in one round
description:
## BLUF

Three PR titles in one round exceeded the 92-character squash-subject limit, so the gate had to supply a subject for each. Raised as TITLE-99 (#1249, 99 chars), TITLE-93 (#1251, 93) and TITLE-94 (#1254, 94). Same defect three times in one round: **nothing tells an author the limit until a gate reads the PR.**

## Why it is worth recording rather than just doing better

The squash subject must be <= 92 chars and ASCII (MG-11). A PR title that breaks it is **not rejected anywhere** — not by GitHub, not by the pre-push hook, not by any local check. It surfaces only when a QA gate writes the merge addendum, at which point a human or a coordinator has to compose a replacement. The cost lands on the reviewer, one PR at a time, every time.

Measured this round: 3 of 4 titles over the limit, 93-99 chars. The two that were under it were under it by accident, not by check.

## Fix shapes (the reporter's proposals, not ratified)

1. A line in `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `DEV-PROCESS.md` stating the limit where authors look before opening a PR — cheapest, and catches nothing automatically.
2. A local check the author can run (a `scripts/` one-liner over `gh pr view --json title`) — catches it before the gate, still opt-in.
3. A pre-push or PR-body check — the only shape that cannot be skipped, and the most intrusive; it also does not apply cleanly, since the *title* is set after the push.

Shape 3 is noted for completeness and is probably wrong: the title is not knowable at push time. Shape 1 plus 2 is the realistic pair.

## Done when

- [ ] the 92-character limit is stated where a PR author will see it before opening the PR, **or** a check the author can run reports it, **or** a line records that supplying the subject at gate time is the accepted cost

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1,307 issues (includeArchived) and 3,684 comments**: `TITLE-99` -> **0** · `92 chars` -> **0** · `squash subject` -> 2 open (KS-1294, the hook's own CI sentence; KS-871, an audit-log path) — **both read in full, neither is this**. **Searched those three terms, 0 open hits for this defect.** Controls: `readYaml` -> 10 hits, fires; `qqx7-fresh-control-never-written-anywhere` -> 0.

## Provenance

Tier-2 gate `QA/Secuura-batch1249`, non-blocking (N-1249-b, N-1251-a, N-1254-c), recorded at the merges of #1249, #1251 and #1254.

title: walkTimeouts guard: the wiring pin passes on a commented-out line, and the derivation misses nested and async tree-walkers
description:
## BLUF

Three non-blocking findings from the tier-2 gate on PR #1254 (KS-1155, merged `ac38dc21dba4`). All three are in the `walkTimeouts` pair added by that PR — one file family, one test pass, one ticket.

**The first two matter more than their Polish severity suggests: they are limits of the thing that keeps the walker list honest**, which is the part of that change doing the real work. The budget itself is cheap; the guard that stops the list going stale is the point.

## The three items

1. **WIRING-PIN-SCRAPE.** The cell that proves `vitest.config.ts` wires the setup file is a **source scrape** — `expect(config).toContain('setupFiles')`. It would pass on a **commented-out** `setupFiles` line. That cell exists precisely because removing the wiring reddened nothing otherwise, so a scrape that a comment satisfies is a thin guard on the one thing nothing else covers.
2. **NESTED / DERIVE-MARKERS.** The derivation reads `src/__tests__/*.test.ts` one level deep and looks for `readdirSync`, `DEV_ROOT` or `WALK_ROOTS`. It therefore does **not** see a tree-walking guard in a **sub-directory**, nor one that walks via **async** `readdir` (or `fs/promises`, or `glob`). Either would get the 5 s default and start flaking under load — the exact state KS-1155 exists to end — while the drift guard stays green.
3. **TS1343** (Polish).

## Done when

- [ ] the wiring check cannot be satisfied by a commented-out line (parse the config, or assert the setup file is actually loaded at runtime)
- [ ] the derivation covers sub-directories and async tree-reading spellings, or names the spellings it deliberately does not cover so the blind spot is stated rather than latent
- [ ] TS1343 resolved or recorded as accepted

## Not in scope here

KS-1155's own `load >= 30` bar stays open on that ticket and is not addressed by any of the above.

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1,307 issues (includeArchived) and 3,684 comments**: `WIRING-PIN-SCRAPE` -> 1 (KS-1155, this finding's own record) · `DERIVE-MARKERS` -> 1 (same) · `walkTimeouts` -> 1 (same). **Searched those three terms, 0 open hits outside KS-1155 itself.** Controls: `readYaml` -> 10 hits, fires; `qqx7-fresh-control-never-written-anywhere` -> 0.

Tier-2 gate `QA/Secuura-batch1249`, non-blocking (N-1254-a, N-1254-b, N-1254-d), recorded at the merge of #1254.

title: packages/shared runs vitest without declaring it: npm ci inside the member exits 127 and reads like a broken tree
description:
## BLUF

`packages/shared` **runs** `vitest` **but declares it nowhere.** `npm ci` run inside the member installs 7 packages and no `node_modules/.bin`, so `npm test` exits **127** — which reads like a broken tree rather than a missing install. The working install is `npm ci` at the `Blockchain/Dev` workspace root, from whose lockfile `vitest` is hoisted.

Found while taking a baseline for KS-1143; cost about fifteen minutes of looking in the wrong place.

## Measured (2026-09-25, develop `6e2a00bfe`)

* `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/package.json` declares `"test": "vitest run"`. Its `dependencies` and `devDependencies` contain **no vitest**; neither does `Blockchain/Dev/package.json`.
* `vitest@4.1.11` resolves only from the workspace root: `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` has one `"node_modules/vitest"` entry.
* `npm ci` **inside** `packages/shared`: "added 348 packages", and the resulting `packages/shared/node_modules` holds **7 entries and no** `.bin`. `./node_modules/.bin/vitest` -> rc **127**.
* `npm ci` at `Blockchain/Dev`: 1,936 packages, `node_modules/.bin/vitest` present, `vitest/4.1.11`.
* **Control:** three other seats' worktrees (`s-b25-ks1140`, `s-b16-ks1133`, `s-l2-ks975`) also have **no** vitest binary under `packages/shared`, so this is the tree's normal state and not one bad install.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a habit

The failure mode is a **misleading** one. rc 127 with no `.bin` looks like a corrupted checkout; the actual cause is that the member's own `package.json` describes a command it cannot run alone. Anyone who installs the way the script implies gets a broken tree and no hint of why.

Related but **not** the same as KS-1292, which is about nothing running `tsc -p packages/shared` (a missing type-check leg). That ticket discusses `npm ci` nesting; it does not cover an undeclared test runner.

## Done when

- [ ] `packages/shared`'s own `package.json` declares the runner it invokes, **or**
- [ ] its `test` script fails with a message naming the workspace-root install, **or**
- [ ] a line in the package's README/CONTRIBUTING states that it is installed only from the workspace root

**Out of the finder's lane:** every shape above touches `package.json`, which is under the no-package.json hold for the seat that found it.

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1,305 issues (includeArchived) and 3,677 comments**: `vitest undeclared` -> **0** · `exits 127` -> **0** · `does not declare vitest` -> **0** · `npm ci` -> 104 total / 41 open and `hoisted` -> 39 / 13, both far too broad to settle it, so the likeliest open candidates were **read in full**: KS-1292 (no `tsc` leg; discusses `npm ci` nesting, not an undeclared runner) and KS-1284 (cardano metadata, unrelated). **Searched those five terms, 0 open hits for this defect.** Controls: `readYaml` -> 8 hits, fires; `zzz-nonexistent-token-l6-control` -> 0.

## Provenance

Environment gap found by the seat building KS-1143; raised by the tier-2 gate on PR #1248 as N-1248-b ENV-GAP and filed on the coordinator's instruction after that batch's verdict.

title: ks781 LEG F: a guard DEFINED but never called inside the parser continuation still reads guarded true (over-reports)
description:
## BLUF

Pre-existing limit of LEG F's guard walk, recorded by the tier-2 gate on PR #1248 (KS-1143 GF-2, merged `fa25c9b10fb4`). **A guard that is DEFINED but never CALLED inside the parser's continuation still reads** `guarded: true`**.**

This **over-reports**, which is the **unsafe** direction: the leg says something inspects the parsed body when nothing does. It is the same asymmetry KS-1143's own GF-1 was about, one step further in.

## Mechanism

GF-2 moved the walk's start from the whole wrapper body to the parser call's **continuation** — the function-valued arguments of the parser call. Inside that continuation the walk still hits on a **call node whose callee name is a known guard**. It does not establish that the call is reached: a guard call sitting in a branch that never executes, or bound and shadowed, is indistinguishable from one on the path.

Not introduced by #1248 — the predicate it replaced had the same property over a wider region, so GF-2 narrowed the region without changing this. Recorded so the remaining looseness has a name.

## Relationship to what is already open on KS-1143

KS-1143 stays In Progress for the **indirect-invocation false negative**, which is the *opposite* direction (under-reports: a continuation passed by NAME is not followed, so a genuinely mounted guard reads unguarded). **This one over-reports.** Two different directions, two different risks; they are not the same defect and should not be closed by one change without saying which each fix addresses.

## Done when

- [ ] a fixture where the guard call inside the continuation is unreachable reads `guarded: false`, **or**
- [ ] a line in the file records why reachability is deliberately out of scope for a text-level walk, so the limit is stated rather than latent

## Board search before filing

Literal match over **1,305 issues (includeArchived) and 3,677 comments**: `CONT-DEFERRED` -> 1 (KS-1143, this finding's own record) · `parserContinuations` -> **0** · `defined but never` -> 1 (KS-1143) · `never called` -> 17 total / 5 open, each read and none this subject (KS-1291 a stale comment, KS-1185, KS-843, KS-1143 itself). **Searched those four terms, 0 open hits for this defect.** Controls: `readYaml` -> 8 hits, fires; `zzz-nonexistent-token-l6-control` -> 0.

## Provenance

Tier-2 gate `QA/Secuura-batch1243`, non-blocking, recorded at the merge of #1248.

title: readYaml routing cells: a multi-line import evades parserImportSites (prettier produces it), the loaders are unpinned, and the canary pays a child spawn per run
description:
## BLUF

Three non-blocking findings the tier-2 gate raised against PR #1243 (KS-1300 items 2-4, merged `a9ae94edbed3`). All three are cells in the same `readYaml` routing/canary family in `systemTest/performance`, so they are **one test pass** and one ticket, per Kam's 2026-09-07 rule.

`Refs KS-1300` — this does **not** close it. KS-1300's own remaining item (READYAML-UNGATED: no gate runs this suite) is a different workload — wiring a suite into the hook or the preflight — and is deliberately left there rather than folded in here.

## The three items

1. **MULTILINE-IMPORT.** `parserImportSites()` reads four import positions — static at any indent, re-export, `require()`, dynamic `import()` — but each pattern is anchored per LINE. **A multi-line import is invisible**, and that is not hypothetical: this package's own prettier config wraps a long import across lines, so the formatter itself produces the evading shape. Measured at the merged tree: the guard's own positive control passes every single-line spelling and has no multi-line row.
2. **T2C-ROUTING-HOME.** The routing cells prove the SUITE does not import a parser directly. Nothing proves the **loaders** (`runner/config_loader.ts` and friends) reach `readYaml()` — the property the whole family exists for. The gate recorded this as homeless; this is its home.
3. **CANARY-IN-PACKAGE.** The retained canary spawns a `tsx` child to run the raw parse, because importing the parser into the suite would (correctly) trip the routing cell. That costs \~2.5 s of the suite's wall-clock. A cheaper in-package form — for example a child-free comparison against a captured raw-parse error — would keep the standing witness without the spawn.

## Done when

- [ ] `parserImportSites()` sees a multi-line parser import, with a positive-control row carrying the exact shape prettier produces
- [ ] a cell proves the loaders call `readYaml()`, so the property is pinned where it is actually relied on
- [ ] the canary keeps its guarantee without a per-run child spawn, or a line records why the spawn is the cheapest honest form

## Board search before filing

title: KS-1226 residue: readSuiteCounts is null on real fail-only, skip-only and todo-only lines
description:
Residue from the tier-2 review of PR #1241 (round 2 of 2, **NO GO at the cap** — gate report sha256 `b6b2c0f1ae210d92`). **#1241 is the unmerged attempt; KS-1226 is the parent.** Nothing from that attempt shipped.

## The defect

`readSuiteCounts` requires a `passed` segment, so it returns **null** on every real summary that has none. Captured verbatim from vitest 4.1.11, `--reporter=default`, piped:

```
      Tests  1 failed (1)      -> null   (correct: { passed: 0, failed: 1 })
      Tests  1 skipped (1)     -> null   (correct: { passed: 0, failed: 0 })
      Tests  1 todo (1)        -> null   (correct: { passed: 0, failed: 0 })
```

**Cost.** `childSuiteCounts` throws `could not read the child vitest summary` with the output tail. Loud, but it misattributes a zero-pass child as a parser defect — and a child where everything failed is exactly the case the reading must survive.

## Root cause

vitest renders the **final** summary with `getStateString` in `dist/chunks/utils.BS4fH3nR.js`, where `passed` is **conditional**:

```js
passed ? c.bold(c.green(`${passed} passed`)) : null,
```

There is a **second** `getStateString`, in `dist/chunks/index.UpGiHP7g.js`, belonging to the TTY-only live reporter, where `passed` is unconditional. The round-2 head comment quotes that one, and the "passed is always emitted" premise — and the refusal built on it — came from reading the wrong renderer.

## Also in this residue

* `tsc -p tsconfig.node.json` is **red at head**: `TS2532` at :79 and `TS2345` at :86, so `npm run lint` exits 2. `npm run lint` runs **both** tsconfigs; only `tsconfig.json` was run, and it is clean.
* The call site (:157 / :161) is **unpinned** — no cell reds if it stops calling `readSuiteCounts`.
* First-match reads an earlier `Tests  N passed (N)` console line as the summary: a silent `{5,0}` on a run that had 1 failure.

## Fix shape

Name-read with an **allowed-label set** and a **sum-equals-total** check instead of "require passed". Take the **last** `Tests` line, not the first. Narrow the indexed accesses so the stricter tsconfig passes. Correct the doc comment, C5's title, and the :156 citations.

## Regression cells

The three lines above to `{0,1}`, `{0,0}`, `{0,0}`. `      Tests  2 failed | 3 passed (5)` to `{3,2}`. A sum-not-equal-total line to null. The two-line output (an earlier `Tests  5 passed (5)`, then `      Tests  1 failed | 1 passed (2)`) to `{1,1}`. One cell that **reds when :157 stops calling** `readSuiteCounts` — for example by exposing the spawn result to a pure `readChildOutput(output)` that `childSuiteCounts` calls and a cell calls with real captured fail-only output. `tsc -p tsconfig.node.json --noEmit` rc 0.

Refs KS-1226

title: KS-980 N-5: an anonymous Docker volume was left behind by a disposable test Postgres
description:
Raised as a non-blocking finding by the review of PR #1242 (merged as `33ccff807eb2`).

**What it is.** A disposable Postgres container used for the integration cells was removed, but its **anonymous volume** `0ec12181` was not, and remains on the host.

**Why it matters.** `docker rm -f` removes the container, not its anonymous volume. Volumes accumulate silently across sessions and are invisible to a `docker ps -a` check, so a teardown that looks complete is not.

**What a fix looks like.** Tear down with `docker rm -f -v`, or prove the volume gone as part of the teardown check rather than proving only the container gone.

Refs KS-980

title: KS-980 N-3: a squash body named a base commit that is not an ancestor of the squash
description:
Raised as a non-blocking finding by the review of PR #1242 (merged as `33ccff807eb2`).

**What it is.** The PR body's base line named `d9515f4a06e0`, which is **not an ancestor** of the merged result. The actual base at merge time was `e68e2f0e837df86da527d775a3a49c631b0f5b17`, and the squash's parent is that commit.

**Why it matters.** The base line is how a reviewer reconstructs what a change was measured against. A base that is not an ancestor cannot be the one the work was tested on, so any figure quoted against it is unverifiable after the fact.

**What a fix looks like.** Take the base from the same read that pins the head, at the moment the evidence is produced, rather than from an earlier draft of the body.

Refs KS-980

title: KS-980 N-2: the PR body claimed a 14/14 full run over 2 suites when the integration config runs 3
description:
Raised as a non-blocking finding by the review of PR #1242 (merged as `33ccff807eb2`).

**What it is.** The PR body reported a full run as **14/14 over two suites**. `jest.integration.config.js` matches **three** suites. The number quoted is therefore not the full run it is presented as — it is a subset, described with the words of a complete one.

**Why it matters more than the number.** A count is a claim about what executed. A subset reported as a full run makes coverage look wider than it is, and the next reader has no way to tell from the body alone.

**What a fix looks like.** Quote the runner's own ratio and name the suites it covered, or say plainly which suite was excluded and why.
