title: No fresh worktree can run a withTenant integration cell in single-tenant mode - the generated Prisma client is absent and `prisma generate` cannot resolve @prisma/client from the schema's directory
description:
## BLUF

**No fresh clone or worktree of this repository can run a** `withTenant` **integration cell in single-tenant mode.** The generated Prisma client does not exist, and `prisma generate` cannot produce it from the obvious invocation.

Measured 2026-09-25 against a real disposable PostgreSQL:

```
Cannot find module '.prisma/client/default' from 'node_modules/@prisma/client/default.js'
  at getPrismaClient (src/db.ts:116)
  at withTenant (src/db.ts:329)
```

The callback never runs, so the cell reports a **module** error where a reader expects a database result. In one cell `{ code: "MODULE_NOT_FOUND" }` arrived where `{ code: "SHARE_TARGET_NOT_FOUND" }` was expected — **that reads as a product defect and is not one.**

## The mechanism, each part measured

1. `@prisma/client` **and the** `prisma` **CLI are declared and installed ONLY in** `services/originate` (`^7.8.0`). `Blockchain/Dev/package.json` declares none of them; `Blockchain/Dev/node_modules/@prisma/client` is **absent**.
2. **The generated client is never produced:** `npm ci` here runs with `ignore-scripts`, so the `postinstall` that would run `prisma generate` never runs. `node_modules/.prisma` is absent.
3. **Schema and package sit in different** `node_modules` **roots.** Schema: `Blockchain/Dev/prisma/schema.prisma`. Client: `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/node_modules`. From `services/originate`, `prisma generate --schema ../../prisma/schema.prisma` fails with `Error: Could not resolve @prisma/client` — generate resolves the client relative to the **schema's** directory. From `Blockchain/Dev` it fails earlier: `sh: prisma: command not found`.
4. **Node resolves** `@prisma/client` **fine** from `services/originate`. So this is generate's resolution rule meeting the layout, not a broken install.

## Why it matters now

`MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` picks the branch: **false** (the local-compose default) takes the **Prisma** branch of `withTenant`; **true** takes the pg-pool branch. So every `withTenant` integration cell is unrunnable in the **local default** mode. It stayed invisible because the existing integration suites (`ks597*`) use raw `pg` clients and never call `withTenant`.

**Not one bad tree:** a second, independently created worktree also has no generated client, and its suite passed only because it never touches `withTenant`.

## NOT claimed

Nothing about deployed environments — service images are built by their own Dockerfiles and were not examined. No claim any runtime is affected. This is about running these tests in a developer or agent worktree.

## Fix shapes, not chosen here

1. Make the layout resolvable — declare `@prisma/client` at the `Blockchain/Dev` root, or set an explicit generator `output`.
2. Add a discoverable `generate` script, rather than relying on a `postinstall` that `ignore-scripts` disables.
3. Regardless of 1/2: make `getPrismaClient()` fail with a sentence naming the cause and the command, as `run-shell-suites.sh` does for a missing `packages/shared` build. That is the difference between a module error and a diagnosis.

## Board search before filing (1294 issues incl. archived, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `.prisma/client` -> 1 total / 0 open \[\]
* `prisma generate` -> 3 / 1 \['KS-763'\] · `Could not resolve @prisma/client` -> 0 / 0
* `ignore-scripts` -> 16 / 7 \['KS-1290', 'KS-1216', 'KS-918', 'KS-763', 'KS-729', 'KS-664', 'KS-530'\] · `@prisma/client` -> 9 / 1 \['KS-664'\]
* Control, a nonsense token -> **0**. So the search discriminates.

## Provenance

Found running #1239 KS-1263's shipped cells against a disposable PostgreSQL built from `docker/init` + `scripts/run-migrations.sh`. Filed on the coordinator's ruling (b): round 2 ships proven in MODE T with MODE F a named residual, and this gap gets its own ticket rather than repo-tooling work inside a test PR.

title: originate documents.ts is the first router to mix a tenant-pool READ with a default-pool WRITE — on a dedicated-DB tenant it fails closed
description:
## BLUF

At #1239's head the `/share` and `/transfer-custody` handlers **read** through `req.db` (the tenant pool set by `extractTenantContext`) and **write** through `withTenant`, which always uses `tenantManager.getDefaultPool()`. **On a tenant whose config resolves to a dedicated database those are two different databases.**

`documents.ts` **is the first router to do this.** Every other non-test `withTenant` call site — 9, all in `routes/adminConfig.ts` — sits under `adminConfig.ts:30` `(req as any).db = prisma // Always shared DB`, so that router reads and writes one database by design.

## Reach, measured

* A pool other than `getDefaultPool()` **is** reachable in code: `getPool` returns a dedicated `Pool` when `perTenantDbEnabled` (`PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB === 'true'`) **and** the tenant's config resolves elsewhere.
* `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` **appears in 0 tracked config files** — compose, deployment and bicep; bicep sets only `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED`. So it is **latent and gated on a variable no template sets**.

## Behaviour on a dedicated-DB tenant, by reading

It **fails closed** rather than misplacing rows: `/share`'s target subquery runs in the default DB → NULL → `SHARE_TARGET_NOT_FOUND` → 404. `/transfer-custody`'s INSERT names a `document_id` absent from the default DB's `documents` → 23503 → rollback → 500.

**That is the right failure direction**, and it is why this is Minor rather than Major. It is still a router whose read and write disagree about which database it is talking to.

## NOT claimed

**Live proof NOT RUN** — no slot was available, and no per-tenant-DB tenant was provisioned. The reach above is static: read from `tenant-context.ts:93`, `tenant-pool-manager.ts:152/201-260` and `db.ts:308`, not executed.

## Related, and NOT a duplicate

**KS-1235** concerns **auth**'s `db.ts` sending tenant-scoped statements through `getPool(tenantId).query()` with **no tenant GUC** under fail-closed RLS. Same neighbourhood — tenant pool versus default pool — but a different service and a different mechanism (a missing GUC there, a read/write pool mismatch here). Read in full before filing.

## Fix shape

`withTenant` checks out from `getPool(tenantId)` (or takes the request's pool). Cell: a manager stub whose `getPool(t) !== getDefaultPool()` must see **both** writes on `getPool(t)`'s client.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,291 issues incl. archived, 3,644 comments, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` -> 5 total / 3 open (**KS-1235**, KS-1055, KS-1054); `getPool(` -> 2 / 1 (KS-1235). **KS-1235 read in full — related, not a duplicate** (see above).
* `getDefaultPool` -> 1 total / **0 open**. `tenantPool` -> **0**.
* Control that fires: `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` -> 5. Nonsense control -> **0**.

`Refs KS-1263`; does not close it. Ruled TICKET (Minor) by the tier-1c gate, explicitly **not** part of #1239's round 2.

title: run-shell-suites.sh now waits on orphaned children: tee keeps the pipe open until a suite's background child exits
description:
## BLUF

Suite output in `run-shell-suites.sh` is now piped through `tee` (the KS-1127 headline-per-cause fix). A consequence shipped with it: **a suite that leaves a background child holding stdout or stderr delays the runner until that child exits.** `tee` cannot see end-of-file while any process still holds the write end of the pipe.

Non-blocking, recorded in #1234's squash body (merged `e68e2f0e837d`). A separate fix from the `/tmp/rss.*` residue also recorded there, hence a separate ticket.

## Why it matters

The runner is the gate on every push. A suite that forks something and returns cleanly now makes the **whole runner** hang for as long as that child lives — and the symptom is "the push is slow", attributed to the runner rather than to the suite that forked. The runner's own verdict is unaffected, which is what makes it hard to trace: nothing fails, it just stops for a while.

## NOT claimed

No suite is known to do this today. The finding is the **mechanism** the `tee` introduces, measured by the gate at the merge — not an observed hang. I have not surveyed the 60 suites for background children.

## Fix shape

Redirect the child's stdout/stderr explicitly rather than inheriting the pipe, or bound the wait (read with a timeout and report the suite that held it, so the symptom names its own cause instead of looking like runner slowness).

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,291 issues incl. archived, 3,644 comments, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `tee` -> 142 total / 60 open and `orphan` -> 73 / 20, both far too generic to indicate ownership; the open rows were scanned and none concerns the runner's pipe.
* `run-shell-suites.sh` -> 29 total / 14 open — read for an existing owner; none names this.
* Control that fires: `run-shell-suites.sh` -> 29. Nonsense control -> **0**.

`Refs KS-1127`; does not close it.

title: run-shell-suites.sh leaves one empty /tmp/rss.* directory behind on every run under a long TMPDIR
description:
## BLUF

`run-shell-suites.sh` creates a short-path working directory when `TMPDIR` is long (the KS-1135 fix, so tsx's IPC socket path stays under the platform limit) and **does not remove it**. Every such run leaves **one empty** `/tmp/rss.*` **directory** behind.

## Why it is worth tracking

The runner is executed on every push, and now also by hand in fresh worktrees (the only place these suites run since Actions was retired). One directory per run accumulates silently in `/tmp` — harmless individually, and exactly the kind of residue nobody attributes later because the creating process is long gone and the directory is empty.

## NOT claimed

No failure, no disk-pressure incident, and no measurement of how many have accumulated on any machine. This is the mechanism, recorded at the merge that introduced it.

A `trap` that removes the directory on exit, including the abort paths — the runner already has abort paths (rc 2 on a fixture build failure, per #1218), so the trap must cover those and not only the clean exit.

title: The relabel guard's presence-not-truthiness rule is pinned on /version only — sign-cert and sign-wallet have the same rule and no cell
description:
## BLUF

PR **#1237** (KS-1229, merged `e119781ac993`) added four cells pinning that the **/version** route's relabel guard refuses a *present* `null`, empty-string or `false` `documentType`, and waves through only an **absent** one. Under a truthiness tamper of that guard, exactly the three new cells go red — so the pin is real.

**The same presence rule exists on** `sign-cert` **and** `sign-wallet`**, and neither is pinned.**

## Why this is the interesting half

A truthiness bug here is invisible to ordinary testing, because `null`, `''` and `false` all *look* absent to a `if (!documentType)` check while being present in the request. That is precisely the confusion #1237 proved the /version route does **not** have. The two sibling routes make the same distinction and nothing holds them to it — so the guard that was hardest to get right is the one with the least coverage on two of its three call sites.

## The fix shape

Port #1237's four cells to `sign-cert` and `sign-wallet`: a present `null`, a present empty string, a present `false`, and an absent field — with the same truthiness tamper as the red proof, which must redden exactly the new cells.

## NOT claimed

Not a measured defect on either route. Nobody has shown `sign-cert` or `sign-wallet` mishandles a present-falsy `documentType`; the finding is that **nothing would notice if they did**, which is a coverage claim, not a behaviour claim.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,286 issues incl. archived, 3,631 comments, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `sign-wallet` -> 20 total / 7 open; `sign-cert` -> 25 total / 7 open; `documentType` -> 52 total / 18 open. The nearest open rows (KS-1229 itself, KS-1213, KS-1202, KS-1133) were read for overlap: **KS-1229** is the parent this residue comes from, and the others concern other properties of those routes, not the presence-vs-truthiness rule.
* Controls that fire: `consumeResetToken` -> 3; nonsense control (`zzz-nonexistent-zzz`) -> 0.

`Refs KS-1229`; does not close it.

## Provenance

Tier-2c QA gate `2026-09-25-batch1218-t2c` (report sha256 `70dc4c987f04…`), raised as a **non-blocking** finding and recorded at the merge. Filed on the coordinator's instruction after the batch landed; it did not hold the merge.

title: k6 readYaml adoption: the unit suite that proves it is run by no gate, and three coverage gaps the new self-read cells leave
description:
## BLUF

PR **#1236** (KS-1110, merged `2208acc0638a`) routed both k6 unit tests through `readYaml()`, so a malformed scenarios file fails them **without printing its content** — measured: the old path printed the whole file. The gate recorded **four** non-blocking findings alongside it. They are one file and one fix pass, so they are items of one ticket rather than four, per Kam's 2026-09-07 rule.

## The four items

1. **READYAML-UNGATED — the one that undoes the rest.** **No pre-push leg and no PR workflow runs this unit suite.** The cells that prove the property exist, and nothing executes them. A regression here is caught only if someone runs the suite by hand.
2. **READYAML-CANARY.** The canary that proves the old path leaked file content was measured for items A and B; it is not retained as a standing cell, so the property "a malformed file does not print its content" has no permanent witness.
3. **READYAML-ROUTING.** An **indented or dynamic** parser import would pass the new self-read cells — they read the file's own source for a top-level import, so a `js-yaml` import that is indented, conditional or dynamic is invisible to them.
4. **READYAML-SHAPES.** The shapes covered are those the two tests use; other config shapes are unasserted.

## Why item 1 leads

The other three are ordinary coverage limits. Item 1 is different in kind: it means the suite's verdict is **never produced** in the normal flow. That is the "a verdict nobody runs" shape the repo already tracks elsewhere — and it makes items 2-4 moot in practice, because even a perfect cell that nothing runs protects nothing.

## NOT claimed

Not a live failure. `systemTest/performance` reads 1088/1089 at the merged tree, and the single red is the pre-existing path-dependent `PRESUITE-URLPATH`, identical at base, head and end — not this PR.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,286 issues incl. archived, 3,631 comments, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `readYaml` -> 5 total / 3 open (**KS-1117**, KS-1110, KS-485). **KS-1117 read in full and is NOT a duplicate** — it is js-yaml 5.2.3 rejecting a BOM followed by `#`, a parsing defect in the loader itself.

title: OpenAPI v2 verify description still says v1's legacy bodies keep their answer — it overstates, for bodies pairing hash with a document id or data
description:
## BLUF

PR **#1233** (KS-1133 + KS-1229, merged `1f1da7f35040`) documented the v1/v2 hash-alias split in the served spec. **The v2 description still carries the older claim that v1's legacy bodies keep their answer** — and that is exactly the sentence #1223 had to narrow in the *code* comment on the same day, for the same reason.

**It overstates for one case:** a body pairing `hash` with a document id **or** document data now takes the hash strategy, as v2 already does. So the spec tells an integrator something the route no longer does.

## Why this one matters more than an internal comment

It is in `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` — the served spec. An integrator reading it has no other source, and the S5 probe on #1233 confirmed the served yaml is byte-identical to the merged blob, so this text is what clients actually receive.

## The fix shape

Both routes' descriptions should say the same thing, since the point of #1233 was to stop them disagreeing.

description:
## BLUF

PR **#1218** (KS-897 + KS-896, merged `1609ecbf61e1`) made the pre-push base suite abort with rc 2 and a named line when a fixture build step fails, and added a six-cell guard that runs on every push. **Three gaps in that guard were measured by the gate and left open**, all non-blocking, all in the same suite and the same fix pass — so they are items of one ticket rather than three tickets, per Kam's 2026-09-07 rule that the unit is the test pass.

## The three items

1. **NB-1218-a — GUARD-UNANCHORED.** The guard counts the abort line **unanchored**, so an abort line that is *prefixed* by anything still satisfies it. This is the same shape the fleet's own STOP predicate had to be sharpened for on 2026-09-25 (line-start `^FIXTURE BUILD FAILED`, superseding the loose substring). **A guard that matches mid-line can be satisfied by output it did not cause.**
2. **NB-1218-b — FIXTURE-GITENV-WORKTREE.** The fixture can no longer write to the caller's repository *by the path the gate tested*, but a **worktree-only write** to the caller's repo is not pinned by any cell. The fix closed the shape that was found, not the class.
3. **NB-1218-c — FIXTURE-ERREXIT-EXEMPT.** `errexit` suspended **at a call site** is not pinned. This matters because the original KS-897 defect was exactly an errexit assumption that did not hold — `( … ) || { exit 2; }` tests only the subshell's last command.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a note

The guard runs on **every push by every author** and costs about ten seconds. Its value is entirely in what it would catch; each item above is a way the property it asserts can be false while it stays green. Item 1 in particular makes the guard satisfiable by a line it did not produce.

## NOT claimed

None of these is a live failure. The suite passes 6/0 at the merged head, and the shipped behaviour is an improvement on what preceded it. These are **coverage** gaps in a new guard, measured by the gate at the same time it approved the change.

title: run-migrations.sh readiness probe discards "command not found" and blames the database — a missing pg_isready reads as "PostgreSQL did not become ready"
description:
## BLUF

`run-migrations.sh`**'s readiness probe throws away the one message that says what is wrong, then blames the database.** When `pg_isready` is not installed, the probe's `2>/dev/null` discards *"pg_isready: command not found"*, the loop runs its full 30 attempts against a command that never executed, and the script exits 2 with:

```
ERROR: PostgreSQL did not become ready after 30 attempts.
```

**The database was up and answering the whole time.** The reader is sent to the database, the network and the DSN — none of which is the fault.

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh`, the wait loop (`MAX_RETRIES=30`, `RETRY_INTERVAL=2`):

```sh
if pg_isready -h "$PG_HOST" -p "$PG_PORT" -q 2>/dev/null; then
```

`-q` silences `pg_isready`'s own output and `2>/dev/null` silences the shell's *"command not found"*. Between them, a missing binary and an unreachable server are **byte-indistinguishable** from the script's output — and they have opposite fixes.

## Measured, 2026-09-25

On a disposable `postgres:15-alpine` instance on `127.0.0.1:55432`, built from `docker/init`:

* Host run: **exit 2**, `ERROR: PostgreSQL did not become ready after 30 attempts` (60 s of retries).
* **Control, same instant, same instance:** `pg_isready -U secuura -d secuura` **inside** the container returns `accepting connections`, **rc 0**. So the server was ready throughout.
* `which pg_isready` on the host: **absent**. `which psql`: **absent**.
* **Positive control that the script is otherwise fine:** copying the same script and `migrations/` into the container (where both binaries exist) and running it there gives `applied=49, failed=0`, rc 0, against that same database. **Only the host tooling differed.**

## Why it matters more than a cosmetic message

1. **It costs 60 seconds before it lies.** The loop cannot succeed, but it still burns all 30 attempts.
2. **The failure is attributed to the wrong system.** This is the class the repo already takes seriously — a verdict composed separately from the work (`STANDING_LINES.md`, *"a verdict line is a claim about what ran"*). Here the verdict names a component that was never consulted.
3. **It is a first-run experience.** A developer or a fresh VM without the Postgres client tools meets this before anything else, and the message points away from the fix.

## NOT claimed

* **Not a product defect and nothing shipped on it.** The script exits **2**, so it fails loudly; this is about *which* cause it names, not about a silent pass. It is **not** the same defect as KS-808 (`applied=N` counting skips / exit 0 on failure) — that is the summary lying about success, this is the probe lying about the cause.
* Whether any deployed environment or image lacks `pg_isready` was **not** measured. In the compose `migrations` service the binary is present, so this is reached by host/dev runs and by any image that drops the client tools.

## Fix shapes, not chosen here

1. **Check the binary exists first** and say so: `command -v pg_isready >/dev/null || { echo "ERROR: pg_isready is not installed — install the postgres client tools"; exit 4; }`. A distinct exit code keeps the two causes distinguishable to callers.
2. **Keep the stderr on the last attempt** so the real message survives into the log.
3. Fall back to a `psql -c 'SELECT 1'` probe (the script already depends on `psql`), which at least fails with a message about the thing it could not do.

(1) is the smallest and removes the misattribution entirely.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,285 issues incl. archived, 3,631 comments, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `pg_isready` -> 3 total / 2 open: **KS-1161** and KS-485. **KS-1161 is NOT a duplicate** — read in full, it is the redis healthcheck exposing `REDIS_PASSWORD` via `docker inspect`.
* `run-migrations.sh` -> 13 total / 7 open (KS-1054, KS-1031, KS-980, KS-808, KS-772, KS-601, KS-485). The two nearest were read in full: **KS-1054** is fail-open RLS from migration *ordering* on boot 1; **KS-808** is the runner's `applied=N` summary counting skips. Neither owns the readiness probe.
* `did not become ready` -> **0**. `command not found` -> 8 total / 1 open (KS-1137, a different script).
* Controls that fire: `KS-808` -> 4; `run-shell-suites.sh` -> 28 / 13 open. So the search discriminates.

## Provenance

Found on 2026-09-25 while provisioning a disposable PostgreSQL for KS-980's red proof (PR #1242), on the coordinator's instruction to file it rather than carry it. Tier 3 when picked up; not this round.

title: vc-issuer credentialRepo.store() falls back to memory SILENTLY when the database is unavailable — the caller is told it was stored
description:
## BLUF

`credentialRepo.store()` **in vc-issuer writes to the in-memory map and returns SILENTLY when the database is unavailable.** The caller is told the credential was stored. Nothing is logged, so there is no artefact anywhere that the write did not reach PostgreSQL — and on restart the credential is simply gone.

**Pre-existing, and deliberately NOT counted against PR #1231** (merged 2026-09-25 as `b83f986fd3e4`). That PR made the *table-absent* fallback LOUD — two WARNs per store. **This is the sibling path it did not touch:** `store()` then `if (!isDbAvailable()) return;` with no log at all. Raised by the tier-2b QA gate as **P-1** and ruled by the coordinator to be tracked separately rather than folded into #1231's scope.

## Why it matters, stated without overclaiming

A silent success on a durability-critical write is the failure mode that cannot be investigated after the fact: there is no line to grep, no counter, no artefact. The credential is served from memory for the life of the process and then disappears. Every other symptom (a verifier 404, a revoke that finds nothing) surfaces far from the cause.

**What is NOT claimed here:** that this is currently happening in any deployed environment. It is a code path, found by reading, with the trigger condition (`isDbAvailable()` false) unmeasured in Azure or on kintsugi.

## UNMEASURED — stated rather than glossed

Carried verbatim from the gate's findings on #1231, because they bound what this ticket knows:

* **Azure reach UNMEASURED.** Whether this path is reachable in the deployed environment was not measured; the Azure role and the table's state were not read.
* **The least-privilege SELECT is UNMEASURED.** Whether the runtime role can even perform the existence check that gates the fallback is unknown.
* The **kintsugi log observation** owed against KS-1281 would, if done, also say whether the loud sibling path fires there. That observation has not been made.

So the *severity* of this ticket rests on an unmeasured reach. **Measure the reach before choosing a fix shape** — if the path is unreachable in every deployed environment, a log line is the whole fix; if it is reachable, the question is whether a silent memory write is acceptable at all for credentials.

## Fix shapes, not chosen here

1. **Log it** — match what #1231 did for the table-absent path: a WARN naming the credential id and the reason. Smallest change; makes the event investigable.
2. **Refuse it** — treat a store with no database as an error the caller must handle, rather than a success. Correct if credentials must be durable, and a behaviour change that needs its own decision.

(1) is strictly an improvement and does not foreclose (2).

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,284 issues incl. archived, 3,620 comments, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `isDbAvailable` -> 14 total / 7 open (KS-1120, KS-1018, KS-953, KS-871, KS-851, KS-843, KS-577). Read for overlap; all concern other services or other call sites.
* `credentialRepo` -> 7 total / 5 open. The two nearest were read in full and are **NOT** duplicates: **KS-1121** is `getById` resolving by SUBSTRING (a disclosure defect, different function); **KS-1120** is presentations test-coverage gaps from #966.
* `vc_credentials_store` -> 3 total / 2 open (KS-1281, KS-1121). `services/vc-issuer` -> 30 total / 14 open. `memory fallback` -> 13 total / 5 open, none on this path. `falls back to memory` -> 0.
* Controls that fire: `KS-1281` -> 1; `consumeResetToken` -> 2. So the search discriminates.

## Provenance

Tier-2b QA gate `2026-09-25-batch1225-t2-r1` on PR #1231, finding **P-1**, at head `bd1d2daec2bf`. Filed at the merge of #1231 onto `develop` `b83f986fd3e47b66054d23a350e5aef6d80d0550`, on the coordinator's instruction. `Refs KS-1281`; it does not close it.

title: .githooks/pre-push still says "CI is the hard gate" (:8) and leaves "use sparingly" unexplained (:12) — KS-789's executable half
description:
## BLUF

`.githooks/pre-push` **still tells every contributor that a degraded leg or a bypassed push is caught by CI. There is no CI.** The same false premise was removed from `Blockchain/Dev/CONTRIBUTING.md` under KS-789; this is the half that lives in the **executable file every push runs**, and it was deliberately left out of that PR because a doc-only change and an edit to the live hook are different risk classes.

## The two lines

1. `.githooks/pre-push:8` — `"normal push is never blocked by infrastructure being off - CI is the hard gate."`
   GitHub Actions is retired for this repository (Kam, 2026-08-27). Nothing re-checks a leg that degraded. The line should say what actually catches it: the PR's Test Evidence block and its reviewer, with `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` section *Manual CI-gate equivalents* as the cross-reference.
2. `.githooks/pre-push:12` — `--no-verify` is described as *"use sparingly"*, with no reason given. One clause on *why* costs nothing and is the difference between a rule people follow and a rule people route around. This is item 4 of KS-789's fix shape, which that ticket scoped out.

## Why this is its own ticket and not part of KS-789's PR

KS-789's PR is **doc-only, one file, tier 3**. `.githooks/pre-push` is the hook that runs on every push from every author, so editing it is tier 2 and changes push behaviour's documentation at the point of use. Folding it into a doc PR would widen that PR's review for no reason, and PR #1218 (the pre-push suite) was still in a gate when this was written.

## The measurement worth carrying — why the doc copy looked like it had already moved

KS-789's own 2026-09-07 comment reported that `git grep "CI is the hard gate"` returned **exactly one hit, and it was this hook**, and concluded the CONTRIBUTING passage had moved or been rewritten. **It had not.** In `CONTRIBUTING.md` the phrase is **line-wrapped** — `...never blocks a push; CI is` / `the hard gate.` — so a single-line grep cannot see it. Both copies were live the whole time. Measured at `cf3de2c4cef5`: the joined form `"never blocks a push; CI is\nthe hard gate."` occurs exactly once in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and the unwrapped form occurs exactly once in `.githooks/pre-push`.

**The general point, which outlives this ticket:** a line-oriented grep silently under-reports any phrase a text wrapper may have split, and the under-report reads as an absence.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, 1,283 issues incl. archived, 3,620 comments, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `.githooks/pre-push` -> 40 total / 18 open. Read for overlap; none owns this text.
* `CI is the hard gate` -> 5 total / 2 open: **KS-789** (the doc half, its PR is open) and **KS-1012**. **KS-1012 is NOT a duplicate** — it is about the `require-pr-gates` *ruleset* enforcing seven unsatisfiable status checks, not about the hook's own comment.
* `use sparingly` -> 1 total / 1 open (KS-789 itself). `pre-push:8` -> 1 / 1 (KS-789). `pre-push:12` -> 4 total / 2 open (KS-789, KS-1063 — KS-1063 is a different gate's vacuous exit 0).
* Controls that fire: `KS-789` -> 5 / 4; `consumeResetToken` -> 1 / 1. So the search discriminates.

## Scope

Two one-line comment edits in one file. No behaviour change: the bypass stays, the degradation stays. `Refs KS-789`; this does not close it.

## Provenance

* Kam's ruling, card `secuura-ks789-ci-is-the-hard-gate-with-no-ci`, option **a**, 2026-09-22 20:53, delivered as KS-789 comment `227b9737`: *"Both: strike the CI clause AND require --no-verify pushes to say so on the PR"* — both halves. The doc half ships under KS-789; this is the rest.
* Premise re-read at the raise from the GitHub **rules** API (`/rules/branches/develop`, since `/branches/develop/protection` 403s this token): **3 active rules, 0 of type** `required_status_checks` -> *no required status check on develop* CONFIRMED, not assumed.

title: HERMETIC-UNPINNED: no cell in the originate suite pins the hermetic property KS-1266 established — reverting ks1213's env line stays green
description:
## BLUF

**KS-1266 stopped seven originate unit files reaching the network, and nothing in the suite would notice if that regressed.** The tier-2 gate on #1221 measured it: revert `ks1213`'s `ANCHORING_SERVICE_URL` line and the suite stays **green**. The property was proved by an **external probe**, not by a cell, so it is protected by nobody once the PR is merged.

## What #1221 established, and how

Seven files under `services/originate/src/__tests__/` now set `ANCHORING_SERVICE_URL` to `http://127.0.0.1:2` at import scope. Measured with a `--require` probe recording every `dns.lookup` and `net.connect`, bare vs patched, **157 tests green on both sides**:

|  | DNS `anchoring` | TCP `anchoring:4005` | TCP `127.0.0.1:2` |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| bare | **17** | **17** | 0 |
| patched | **0** | **0** | **26** |

The probe is not blind in either direction: 8 lookups of `127.0.0.1` on both sides. **But none of that lives in the suite** — it was an out-of-band measurement, and the suite's own 863 cells are indifferent to it.

## Why it matters more than it looks

The failure is **silent and slow**. A future edit that drops or overrides the env line puts the unit suite back on the host's resolver: it still passes, just non-deterministically and with a DNS lookup per anchoring call. That is precisely the state KS-1266 was filed to end, and it would return without any red.

It also erodes the port-1 half: `ks1228` and `ks520` were on `127.0.0.1:1`, which undici refuses **before opening a socket**, so their "closed port" never happened. Nothing pins that they must not drift back.

## Fix shape (the owner's call)

1. **A cell per file, or one shared helper cell**, asserting the module-scope base is a refused loopback port — cheap, but it pins the CONFIG rather than the PROPERTY.
2. **One probe-backed cell**: run the anchoring-touching files under a `dns.lookup` spy and assert **zero** lookups of a non-loopback host. That pins the actual property (hermeticity) and would red on any regression, however it arrives. It needs the probe to live in the repo rather than in a seat's scratch.
3. Keep it out of the suite deliberately and record that hermeticity is asserted only at the gate — honest, but then it must be written down somewhere a reader will find.

(2) is the one that matches what the ticket set out to guarantee.

## Done when

- [ ] a regression that removes or overrides `ANCHORING_SERVICE_URL` in any of the seven files **reds** the originate suite
- [ ] the port-1 shape is covered too: a change back to a Fetch-spec bad port is caught, not silently accepted

## SEARCHED BEFORE FILING

Literal census over **1,282** KS issues (archived included) and **3,625** comments: `127.0.0.1:2` → **1** hit (KS-1266 itself); `ANCHORING_SERVICE_URL` → 8, none owning this property; `hermetic` → 7, none this; `no cell pins` → 17, a generic phrase rather than this finding. Controls: `KS-1263` → 3 (so the instrument matches), a nonsense token → **0** (so it discriminates). **Unfiled.**

## PROVENANCE

Tier-2 gate `2026-09-25-batch1215-t2-r1` on #1221 (KS-1266), verdict GO with this as a disposition (`NEW: HERMETIC-UNPINNED (TICKET)`). Filed by Seat L1 on Wednesday's instruction of 2026-09-25 05:36:36Z, after the merge of #1221 as `9e744421ada2166c8944764017cad76d94737286`.

Refs KS-1266.

title: Nothing runs `tsc -p packages/shared` — the push preflight has no project type-check leg, so a type error is invisible (KS-872 acceptance, second half)
description:
## BLUF

`npx tsc -p packages/shared --noEmit` is **not run by anything**. Not by the push preflight's fifteen legs, not by vitest (which does not type-check), not by any remaining CI. A type error in `packages/shared` is therefore red in `tsc` and **invisible everywhere the team actually looks**.

KS-872 was filed when exactly that happened: `crypto.JsonWebKey` vanished in `@types/node` 26.1.0 and the project tsc went red on develop with nobody noticing. That ticket's acceptance has two halves. The fix is one; **this is the other** — *"either the preflight gains a shared project type-check leg, or a ticket says explicitly why it should not."*

## Measured today (2026-09-25, at develop `6ab9d5021e96`)

`npx tsc -p packages/shared --noEmit` exits **rc 0**, zero output, on a clean `npm ci` at `Blockchain/Dev`. A planted `const x: number = 'not a number'` gives **rc 2 / TS2322**, and removing it returns rc 0 — so the check is live, and the original error genuinely does not reproduce.

**Why it is green is the point, and it is fragile.** `npm ci` NESTS `packages/shared/node_modules/@types/node@20.19.43` (the package declares `^20.11.5`) beside the hoisted `@types/node@26.1.0`. The nested 20.x still carries `crypto.JsonWebKey` at `crypto.d.ts:513`; in 26.1.0 that interface moved to `webcrypto.JsonWebKey` (`crypto.d.ts:3630`). **Nothing pins that nesting.** A hoist change, a dedupe, or a lockfile refresh can remove it, and the error returns — to a check that still nobody runs.

## Ask

Add a `packages/shared` project type-check leg to the push preflight (`.githooks/pre-push`), **or** record here why it should not exist. If it is added it needs a planted-error control, like every other leg — a type-check that cannot fail is the failure mode this ticket is about.

## Searched before filing

Six terms, `includeArchived: true`, every page literal-matched on the title: `type-check leg` (50 fuzzy / **0** literal), `tsc` (50 / **12**), `preflight leg` (50 / **8**), `project type-check` (50 / **0**), `packages/shared tsc` (50 / **0**), `noEmit` (50 / **1**). **KS-872 itself has zero relations, zero inverse relations and zero children.**

Nearest, and all a different class:

* **KS-892** and **KS-933** — both *Duplicate/ARCHIVED* — say the project tsc is VACUOUS for `src/__tests__` because the tsconfig excludes it. That is *"the tsc does not cover enough"*, not *"no leg runs the tsc"*. Named rather than linked: archived issues refuse relations.
* **KS-1000 / KS-1122 / KS-848 / KS-1090** — the same excludes-`__tests__` class in auth, vc-issuer, kyc and api-gateway.
* **KS-910 / KS-1040** — preflight *leg* tickets, but legs 12 and 4.

**No open home; filed new.**

---

*Filed by Seat L3, 2026-09-25, on Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER Q1b). Carries the second half of KS-872's acceptance;* `.githooks/` *is in no seat's lane this round.*

description:
## BLUF

**#1174 (KS-1265) added an** `@`**-guard on** `issuerName` **at** `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:611`**, before** `saveDocument` **at** `:695`**. The older guard it superseded is still at** `:844` **and can no longer be reached for that case.** #1174's own merge message says so, verbatim:

> *"The older post-save guard is now unreachable for that case and can be removed in a later cleanup."*

That cleanup was never filed. This ticket is it.

## Measured at develop `6ab9d5021e96ea1481cb6c6ff2d6d33b414aecb7` (read-only)

* `:611-618` — `const topLevelIssuerName = typeof req.body?.issuerName === 'string' ? req.body.issuerName.trim() : '';` then `if (topLevelIssuerName.includes('@')) { return res.status(400)... }`, **before** the save.
* `:695` — `const saved = await saveDocument(document, tenantId, (req as any).db, {`.
* `:838-844` — `const suppliedIssuerName = ...` then `if (suppliedIssuerName.includes('@')) {` — **after** the save, so for a top-level `issuerName` carrying `@` the request has already returned at `:611`.
* Commit: `fd6335f08` *"KS-1265 EARLYGUARD: refuse an email-shaped issuerName before the document is saved (#1174)"*, +8/-0 in `documents.ts`.

## Why it matters

A dead guard is a claim. A reader auditing the create path finds two `@` refusals at different points and cannot tell from the file which one bites — and the `:844` copy reads as though a document can still be saved before an `@` is refused, which is exactly the behaviour #1174 removed. Same class as KS-1277: a correct rule beside a stale copy of itself is worse than the stale copy alone.

## Fix shape, and the proof the work must carry

Remove the `:838-851` post-save `@` branch (keeping the `issuerName` default assignment that follows it), and **prove the removal is safe before making it**:

1. A cell showing an `@`-carrying top-level `issuerName` is refused 400 at `:611` with `saveDocument` never called.
2. **Paired mutation:** delete the `:611` guard and that cell must fail. A guard whose removal reds nothing is not a guard, and a removal justified by an unproven check is not justified.

If the mutation shows `:844` is in fact still reachable by some other shape (a non-top-level `issuerName`), the guard stays and this ticket closes with that measurement recorded instead.

## SEARCHED BEFORE FILING

Literal census over **1,280** KS issues (823 archived; titles + descriptions) and **3,594** comments: `suppliedIssuerName.includes` → **1** hit (KS-1265, the ticket that created the situation); `suppliedIssuerName` → **1** hit (same); `#1174` → 2 hits (KS-772, KS-485 — both review-stream roll-ups, neither owns the cleanup). Controls: `KS-1265` → 4 hits, so the instrument matches; `zzqq-no-such-token-zzqq` → 0, so it discriminates. **Unfiled.**

## PROVENANCE

Found by Seat L1 on 2026-09-25 during the ITEM 0 residual measurement of KS-1265, from #1174's own merge message. Filed on Wednesday's ANSWER of 2026-09-25 02:20:37Z (Q6: *"Search first ... If unfiled, file one ticket assigned to the board account"*).

Refs KS-1265.

title: Lockfile edits move platform discriminators silently: an npm command inside a workspace MEMBER rewrites the ROOT lock (0 version changes, 12 lines of dev/devOptional churn), and an isolated resolve on darwin/arm64 strips os/cpu/libc markers (26 entries from frontend/issuer, 30 libc lines from services/mcp-server incl. the musl markers node:24-alpine needs, 103 entries on a full root re-resolution) — cause side of KS-1154; push-gate leg PROPOSED for Kam
description:
## BLUF

Two measured hazards in how this repo's lockfiles get edited on a developer host. Both produced wrong bytes in a working tree on 2026-09-25 before a per-file check caught them; neither is visible in `git diff --numstat` as anything but a small diff.

**TRAP 1 — an npm command run inside a workspace MEMBER rewrites the workspace ROOT lock, not the member's own lock.** `Blockchain/Dev/package.json` declares `workspaces: ["packages/*","services/*","frontend/*"]`, so `services/originate`, `services/mcp-server` and the frontends are members — while each also carries its own tracked standalone `package-lock.json`, which is what `scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs` reads (43 of the 45 tracked locks). Measured: `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts` run **inside** `services/originate` left `services/originate/package-lock.json` **byte-unchanged** and instead rewrote `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` — 12 lines, eleven `lightningcss-*` platform binaries plus `magicast` flipping `devOptional` → `dev: true`, with **0 packages added, 0 removed, 0 version-changed**. `npm update @hono/node-server` inside `services/mcp-server` moved **nothing at all**. So the in-place route silently misses its target and dirties a file the change must not touch.

**TRAP 2 — resolving a standalone lock in an isolated copy STRIPS platform discriminators for every host but the one resolving.** The isolated route writes the right file, but re-resolves optional platform deps for the current host (Darwin/arm64) and drops the rest. Measured, same session, npm 11.5.1 / node 24.7.0:

| lock | collateral |
| -- | -- |
| `frontend/issuer/package-lock.json` | **26 entries removed** — `emnapi/runtime` plus **25** `rollup/rollup-<platform>` **binaries** |
| `frontend/admin`, `frontend/verifier` | 1 entry removed each |
| `services/mcp-server/package-lock.json` | **30 lines of** `libc` **blocks deleted** — ten `"libc": ["glibc"]` / `["musl"]` markers |
| `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` (full re-resolution) | **103 entries removed** — esbuild 75, rolldown 13, lightningcss 10, cbor-extract 5. **103 of 103 carry an** `os`**/**`cpu` **constraint; 0 do not.** |

**Every service Dockerfile is** `node:24-alpine`**, i.e. musl**, so removing a `"libc": ["musl"]` discriminator is not cosmetic. And the frontends are built in Linux containers, so removing `rollup-linux-*` breaks their build.

*(npm scope sigils are omitted above —* `rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu` *means the scoped package; the symbols stay searchable.)*

## Relation to KS-1154 — read both; they are cause and symptom

**KS-1154** (Backlog) is *"Root package-lock.json carries only rollup-darwin-arm64 — npm ci on ubuntu installs no Linux rollup binary…"*. That is **one symptom**: a binary already absent from the root lock. This ticket is the **mechanism that keeps removing them**, in both directions and across every lock, plus TRAP 1, which KS-1154 does not mention at all.

KS-1154's own "Ancestors" paragraph states the link in its own words: *"The lock has lost a platform binary set three times now; the regen-on-one-host shape is what keeps re-creating it."* Its ancestors KS-653 and KS-376 (both Done, archived) are the two earlier recurrences. KS-1154's guard proposal is a **lockfile cell pinning the rollup set**; this ticket's proposal below is a **push-gate leg covering every discriminator in every lock**, which would have caught all three past recurrences and this one.

**Not a duplicate, and KS-1154 should not be closed by this:** KS-1154 has its own "Done when" (add `rollup-linux-x64-gnu`, green the advisory job's step 6). This ticket does not add that binary.

## The proven workaround, in use now

Both scripts live at `5_Project_History/2026-09-25_seatB-25th/raise/` and were used to build the KS-530 and KS-528 lock changes:

* `lockresolve21.sh` — copies a member's two manifests into an isolated dir **outside every workspace**, resolves there, copies the lock back. Fixes TRAP 1. Its header carries the measurement.
* `splice_lock21.py` — takes **only** the named packages' entries from npm's own output (authoritative `version` / `resolved` / `integrity` / inner pins) and splices them into the pristine lock; every other byte stays pristine. Fixes TRAP 2. It refuses if the two locks hold different keys for those packages.

Result on the two PRs built with them: **added 0 / removed 0 / version-changed N** in every lock touched, and `libc` / `os` / `cpu` / `devOptional` counts identical before and after in all seven files.

## PROPOSAL — needs Kam, not this ticket's author

**A push-gate leg: a lockfile change must not move a platform discriminator.** Per changed `package-lock.json`, compare the before/after count of `os`, `cpu`, `libc` and `devOptional` markers; refuse the push on any delta that the change does not declare. **This is a gate change, so it is Kam's call** — recorded here as a proposal, not a decision, and deliberately not built. Evidence that it works: the check read `libc` **10 → 0** on the bad `services/mcp-server` lock and **10 → 10** after the splice. It is a guard that failed when it should have.

## What was searched before filing

The whole KS board, **1,279 issues including archived**, literal substring match on title + description for: `workspace member` (3 hits, none related), `package-lock` (36), `libc` (1 — KS-366, Done/archived, a currency review), `musl` (**0**), `os/cpu` (**0**), `optional binar` (4), `platform binar` (5), `rollup-` (1 — KS-1154), `esbuild` (13), `lightningcss` (**0**), `arborist` (**0**), `devOptional` (2), `lock-regen` (6), `package-lock-only` (9). Controls: `gate` matched **930** issues (the reader fires); a symbol that cannot exist matched **0** (it does not invent). **The only candidate was KS-1154**, related above.

## Also recorded from the same session

* A **full re-resolution of the root lock does not fix** either advisory pin it was tried for: `node_modules/ip-address` stays 9.0.5 and `@prisma/dev/node_modules/@hono/node-server` stays 1.19.11, with and without `overrides`. So a regen is not a fix and is destructive — see the 103-entry row above.
* `npm install --package-lock-only` is **inert for a version bump** on npm 11.5.1: it prints `up to date` and moves nothing. `npm update <pkg>` is what moves it. A command that reports success while doing nothing.
* Resolving a workspace root **from bare manifests with no** `node_modules` crashes npm: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')` at `#loadPeerSet` (`@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:1314`) — peer-dependency resolution, reproducible. With `node_modules` present it completes. Not a repo defect; a constraint on how any future measurement must be run.

## Done when

- [ ] `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` carries both traps and names the two scripts as the way to edit a lockfile
- [ ] the two scripts live somewhere durable in the repo rather than in one seat's record folder
- [ ] the push-gate leg is decided by Kam — built, or recorded as declined with the reason

title: Blockchain/Dev/.dockerignore excludes `tests`, which does not match `__tests__` - test sources ship into runtime images and one shared test change rebuilt 23 of 29
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/.dockerignore:13` is the single line `tests`. **That pattern does not match** `__tests__`, so every `__tests__` directory sits inside the build context. Two consequences: **test sources ship inside runtime images**, and **a change to a shared test file invalidates the cache for services that have no runtime change of their own.**

## Measured - the build cost

**2026-09-23 kintsugi deploy (Seat B 23rd).** Two files under `packages/shared/src/__tests__/` were the **only changed input for 23 of the 29 rebuilt images** - roughly **1 h 50 min of a 2 h 10 min build**, for images whose runtime code did not change. Excluding `__tests__` would cut a comparable rebuild to about **6** images.

**At develop** `6ab9d5021` **(Seat B 24th, 2026-09-25):** **471 tracked files** live under `__tests__/` paths beneath `Blockchain/Dev`, and none are excluded by the `tests` line.

## A path correction worth keeping

**There is no repo-root** `.dockerignore`**.** The only two tracked at `6ab9d5021` are `Blockchain/Dev/.dockerignore` and `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/.dockerignore`. Because `docker-compose.yml` builds every service with `context: .` = `Blockchain/Dev`, the first **is** the effective one. Earlier notes calling it "the root .dockerignore" mean the build-context root, not the repo root.

## Ask

Add a pattern that matches `__tests__` (and confirm nothing in the build needs those files). **Verify by rebuilding after a shared-test-only change and showing that the set of images which rebuild shrinks** - the measurement above is the before.

## Searched before filing

`searchIssues`, `includeArchived: true`, pages literal-matched: **".dockerignore"** (8 hits - all PS infra or unrelated: PS-193, PS-400, PS-180, PS-346, PS-182, KS-485, KS-36, KS-601) and **"tests** runtime images rebuild" (40 hits, none this finding). Nearest in spirit is **KS-918** (vite is a production dependency of `services/auth`; esbuild and fsevents ship into the runtime image) - same family of symptom, different mechanism. **Filed new.**

---

*Carried from Seat B 23rd's kintsugi deploy (2026-09-23), where it was ruled a FINDING. Filed by Seat B 24th, 2026-09-25, on Wednesday's ruling.*

title: ks781 LEG D pins api-gateway index.ts by LINE NUMBER - moved six times; pin by TEXT instead
description:
## BLUF

LEG D of the ks781 body-parser-order suite pins three `api-gateway/src/index.ts` sites **by line number**. Any edit above those sites moves the pins and reds the suite for a reason that has nothing to do with what it guards. **It has moved six times.**

## The most recent move, and why it is expensive

#1210 (KS-1239) removed 18 lines from `index.ts`, shifting all three pins by a uniform -18: 845 -> 827, 858 -> 840, 891 -> 873. The red surfaced in `packages/shared` while the **api-gateway** lane was green - a cross-package failure the author's own lane run could not see. The tier-1 gate NO GO'd the PR on it (Major, `LEGD-LINEPIN`).

Fixing it took re-keying the three `toEqual` line numbers, the CONTROL's `toContain`, and two adjacent comments that named the old numbers as live - all of which is work that a text pin would not have needed.

## Ask

Pin by **text** (the line's content, or a stable anchor) rather than by ordinal position, so an unrelated edit above the sites cannot red the suite.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts`, LEG D.

## Named, not related

**KS-1126** - "KS-953 instance 4: ks781 LEG D's hand-pinned api-gateway index.ts lines :854/:867/:900 drift" - is **Done and ARCHIVED**. It closed *one instance* of the drift, not the class. Archived issues refuse relations, so it is named here rather than linked.

## Searched before filing

`searchIssues`, `includeArchived: true`, every page literal-matched: **"LEG D pins by line number"** (40 hits), **"ks781 LEG D"** (40 hits). Nearest are KS-1126 (archived, an instance) and KS-1142 (Backlog - the entrypoint corpus pinned by two hand-maintained literals, a different class). **No open home; filed new.**

---

*Carried from Seat B 22nd (2026-09-23) as LEGD-BYTEXT. Filed by Seat B 24th, 2026-09-25, on Wednesday's ruling.*

title: OpenAPI: path parameter `index` on GET /api/status/{id}/check/{index} is published `required: false` — the only optional path parameter in the spec; Schemathesis 4.27.5 reports it as a Schema Error
description:
## BLUF

`docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` publishes the **path** parameter `index` of `GET /api/status/{id}/check/{index}` (`operationId: getStatusByIdCheckByIndex`) with `required: false`. OpenAPI 3 requires `required: true` on every `in: path` parameter. It is the **only** such parameter in the spec (scan of every operation's and path-item's parameters, 2026-09-21). Schemathesis 4.27.5 ([KS-1285](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1285/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4272-4275-the-ks-1270-ndjson-hold-is)) now reports it as a run-level **Schema Error**; 4.27.2 did not, so the defect has been in the spec unnoticed.

## Measured ([KS-1285](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1285/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4272-4275-the-ks-1270-ndjson-hold-is) after-sweep, slot 1, seed 1285, run `full-ks-1285-2026-09-21T11-57-14Z-slot1`)

JUnit XML, `<error>` on the `GET /api/governance/participants/{id}` testcase (the scenario it surfaced on — the location it names is the status-list op):

```
Schema Error

Invalid `required` definition

Location:
    paths -> /api/status/{id}/check/{index} -> get -> parameters -> 1 -> required

Problematic definition:
    false

Error details:
    true was expected

Ensure that the definition complies with the OpenAPI specification
```

The 4.27.2 before-sweep on the same head and seed reported only the standing [KS-611](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-611/post-apitimestampsbatch-errors-on-every-sweep-filter-too-much-response) Network Error; the verdict's `errors` moved from `[Network Error ×1]` to `[Network Error ×1, Schema Error ×1]`. `Run validity` still reads OK (2 of 342 errored, below the 10 % limit, not clustered).

## In the spec (as published)

```yaml
  /api/status/{id}/check/{index}:
    get:
      parameters:
        - schema: { type: string }
          required: true
          name: id
          in: path
        - schema: { type: integer, minimum: 0 }
          required: false          # ← path parameters cannot be optional
          name: index
          in: path
```

## Source

`Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/vc-issuer.openapi.ts:1485-1497` — `sharedRegistry.registerPath({ … path: '/api/status/{id}/check/{index}', request: { params: z.object({ id: z.string(), index: z.coerce.number().int().nonnegative().openapi({ type: 'integer', minimum: 0 }) }) } … })`. The `id` sibling (`z.string()`) renders `required: true`; `index` (`z.coerce.number()…`) renders `required: false`. The [KS-423](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-423/blocking-pr-pre-merge-schemathesis-coverage-6-contract-drift-failures) comment on that line already records a rendering quirk of the `coerce` wrapper (it emitted `[integer, "null"]` before the `.openapi({ type: 'integer' })` pin), so the `coerce` path is the first suspect for the `required` flag too — **not verified**; whoever fixes it should confirm by regenerating (`npm run generate-openapi`) and diffing the yaml.

## Fix shape (prose only — Kamil's area)

Make `index` render `required: true` (e.g. pin `required` via the `.openapi({...})` metadata, or express the param without the `coerce` wrapper and coerce in the handler), regenerate the spec, and confirm the Schemathesis `full` run's `errors` drops back to the single [KS-611](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-611/post-apitimestampsbatch-errors-on-every-sweep-filter-too-much-response) entry. A spec-side regression check would be a `check:openapi` rule that every `in: path` parameter is `required: true` — the scan that found this one is a 12-line yaml walk.

## Related

[KS-1285](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1285/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4272-4275-the-ks-1270-ndjson-hold-is) (the bump whose after-sweep surfaced it) · [KS-1269](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1269/post-apistatusidrevoke-accepts-index-object-where-integer-is-declared) (same operation family, different defect: `POST /api/status/{id}/revoke` accepts `index: {}`) · [KS-423](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-423/blocking-pr-pre-merge-schemathesis-coverage-6-contract-drift-failures) (the earlier `coerce` rendering fix on this parameter) · [KS-61](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-61/openapi-compliance-documentation-gaps-across-the-spec-descriptions) (OpenAPI compliance gaps).

*Raised by agent on Peter's behalf, 2026-09-21, from the* [KS-1285](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1285/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4272-4275-the-ks-1270-ndjson-hold-is) *evidence.*

title: Akto image 2.22.2 → 2.35.6 (latest paired _local — pair verified 2026-09-28), and surface the run counts + an exact HTTP status histogram
description:
Currency bump of the Akto scan-stack images, following the [KS-503](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-503/akto-image-21311-2142-latest-paired-local) / [KS-569](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-569/akto-image-2142-2165-latest-paired-local) / [KS-710](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-710/akto-a-stale-test-id-catalog-fails-nothing-locally-testsetup-should) pattern, **plus** the report enrichment Peter scoped on 2026-09-21 (the tool-update rule: a bump harvests the new coverage, it does not just move the number).

**Retargeted 2026-09-21 → 2026-09-28: 2.35.1 → 2.35.6.** Filed from the v2.35.1 notification; upstream released through v2.35.6 (2026-09-25) while the branch was in progress.

## Where the pin is

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| Was | **2.22.2** ([KS-710](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-710/akto-a-stale-test-id-catalog-fails-nothing-locally-testsetup-should), PR #761, validated 2026-08-28) |
| Now | **2.35.6** |
| Branch | `feature/ks-1286-akto-image-2222-2351-latest-paired-_local-pair-verified-2026` @ `981398ed8`, pushed; based on `develop` @ `d9ce1403d`. (Linear now suggests a `…2356…` branch name off the retitled ticket — the pushed branch keeps its original name; renaming it would orphan the pushed ref for no gain.) |
| Slot | 2 (Peter, 2026-09-21) |

## 1. The pair, verified against the registry (MUST rule 9 — not from the release tag)

`npm run update-images` recommends **2.35.6**, and direct tag probes on 2026-09-28 confirm both images publish it:

| version | dashboard | testing | valid pair |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 2.35.6 | 200 | 200 | **yes — the target** |
| 2.35.5 | 200 | 404 | no |
| 2.35.4 | 200 | 200 | yes |
| 2.35.3 | 200 | 404 | no |
| 2.35.2 | 200 | 404 | no |

Three of the five intervening releases are **dashboard-only** — the same trap that held [KS-569](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-569/akto-image-2142-2165-latest-paired-local) at 2.16.5. Reading the version from the release tag rather than the registry would have picked a broken pair.

## 2. What the range contains (blobless clone; every release body in the range is empty, as since 2.16.0)

**507 commits** (382 across 2.22.2→2.35.1, 125 across 2.35.1→2.35.6), and:

* **0 files under** `apps/testing` in either half. The testing Dockerfile and its netty pin are unchanged.
* `swagger-parser` **2.1.20** and `mongodb-driver-sync` **4.2.1** at every tag → the mongo 6.0 hold stands, and the [KS-429](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-429/openapi-32-readiness-akto-cannot-parse-32-swagger-parser-2248-sequence) OpenAPI 3.2 gate is unchanged (upstream swagger-parser issue 2248 still open).
* The bundled `tests-library-master.zip` is the **identical git blob** (`c6fd9c0c…`) at 2.22.2, 2.35.1 and 2.35.6 → the catalog is predicted to regenerate byte-identical.
* Shared-`libs` changes that touch scan execution: opt-in mTLS in `ApiExecutor` (only fires when a request carries a TLS auth param; ours never do) and a `demerge` flag consumed by api-runtime's URL merging, not the testing engine.
* **The scan-log activity-id gap is still open**: 0 of the 37 files under `apps/testing/src/main/java` reference `activityId` at v2.35.6, and the logger stamps a log only when it is set. The Service Logs tab stays empty; its version string moves with the pin, the cause does not.
* `TestRunStatusHelper`, `TestRunStatusAction` and `TestResultsStatsAction` **are byte-identical 2.35.1 → 2.35.6**, so the regexes this branch copies verbatim and the 3,000 sample cap still hold.

## 3. What 2.35.6 offers the report — and what was taken

**Nothing new**: no new result field, no new testing/results/export REST action, no SARIF/JUnit/CSV, and Akto's PDF path needs its puppeteer service and renders Akto's own UI. What Akto *already* exposed and this report never read is what was taken:

* `testInitiatedCount`, `totalExternalApiTokens`, `metadata` — on the run summary since long before this bump. *Initiated* beside *Tests run* is a direct started-vs-persisted reading: the [KS-709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-709/akto-reports-a-pass-for-a-test-that-executed-nothing-clean-0-not) executed-nothing false pass shows as initiated 0.
* **An exact per-run 4xx/5xx + Cloudflare histogram.** Akto's own `api/fetchTestRunStatusSummaries` computes those counts over its **first 3,000** non-vulnerable results (`TestRunStatusHelper.SAMPLE_LIMIT`), so on a pre-merge run its figure is a sample, not the run. The harness now computes the same thing itself in Mongo — Akto's regexes verbatim, **no** `$limit` — and the cross-check panel reconciles the two: they must agree at or below the cap, and differ only by it above.

**Declined, with the reason recorded in the code** (`apiTypes.ts`): 2.35.6 added `producerDone`, `leaseExpiryTs`, `leaseToken` to `TestingRunResultSummary`. They are mini-testing's Kafka lease coordination — which pod owns an attempt, not what the scan found — and this deployment runs the `akto-api-testing` engine, so they are always absent here.

## 4. Console = results.json = HTML

Both new lines come from **one formatter each**, shared verbatim by the console block, the Execution panel and the cross-check panel, so the three surfaces agree by construction rather than by coincidence (the existing `bucketCounts` precedent). A side that was not captured is recorded as **absent**, never as a zero — Kamil, [KS-709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-709/akto-reports-a-pass-for-a-test-that-executed-nothing-clean-0-not) (2026-08-28), verbatim: *"a report must not describe an empty set in the language of a clean one."* A comparable histogram mismatch flips `reconciles` only, never the verdict — Kamil, [KS-700](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-700/akto-harness-prints-a-false-zero-when-its-mongo-capture-fails-no) (2026-08-27), verbatim: *"this is harness integrity, not a security claim, and conflating them would relabel a harness fault as a finding (the* [KS-308](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-308/akto-scans-report-100percent-skipped-tests-testing-container-cant) *lesson, in reverse)."* Both quotes are carried beside the code they justify, per MUST #15.

## 5. Evidence so far — OFFLINE ONLY

`npm run quality` **exits 0** in `systemTest/akto` on the branch tip (2026-09-28): `format:check`, `lint` (tsc + eslint + stylelint), `knip`, **74 test files / 1275 tests, 0 failures**, `npm audit` 0 vulnerabilities. **36** `it()` **blocks added** against develop (1 retitled), covering the two new modules, the two shared formatters, the four cross-check outcomes and the omit-never-zero rule on both artifact helpers.

### A defect the new checks caught before any live run

Akto's `REGEX_CLOUDFLARE` was copied verbatim from Java **including its leading** `(?is)` **inline flag group** — Java/PCRE syntax that is **not a valid JavaScript RegExp**. Every failure in the histogram module is best-effort and degrades to *"not captured"*, so the Cloudflare count would simply have been absent on every run with nothing saying why; and had it compiled without the `s`, it would have been worse — a measured-looking **false zero**, because a captured response body spans newlines and every `.*` in that pattern must cross them.

Fixed by keeping the pattern body verbatim and carrying `(?is)` as Mongo `$options: "is"`, with the one deliberate departure from verbatim documented where it is made. Two checks now treat this module's silent-degrade design as the hazard it is: the generated mongosh program must **parse as JavaScript**, and both patterns must **compile** with the flags the pipeline passes. The Cloudflare test carries its own discriminator — the same body matches with dotall and does not match without it — so the load-bearing flag cannot be dropped again silently. Commit `981398ed8`.

Two side observations, both measured on `develop` @ `d9ce1403d` rather than inferred:

* [KS-755](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-755/akto-unit-suite-has-a-standing-red-rundir-resolverunid-ignores-the)'s standing red is gone — `tests/unit/core/runDir.test.ts` passes 14/14.
* [KS-990](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-990/npm-run-quality-cannot-pass-in-systemtestperformance-or-systemtestakto)'s akto leg is gone — `knip` is clean; the two `endpointFalsePositives.ts` exports it named no longer exist. Its `systemTest/performance` leg was not checked here. Kamil's ticket, so flagged rather than touched.

## 5a. Found from [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) (2026-09-28): the Akto unit suite is not hermetic to the slot variables

**BLUF:** `npm run test:unit` passes only when **no slot variable is exported**. Run the way the slotted workflow runs everything else — with `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` (or its `STACK_SLOT` alias) in the environment — the slot-coherence tests read the operator's slot instead of the one each test sets up, and go red for reasons that have nothing to do with the code. The §5 "exits 0" above is true in a clean shell, which is why this stayed hidden.

**Measured** on the [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) worktree (`develop` + [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9), no Akto file changed; `systemTest/akto` last touched at `db8ad2dad`), `npm run test:unit` = `vitest run --config vitest.unit.config.ts`:

| environment | result |
| -- | -- |
| no slot variable | **1238 / 1238 passed** |
| `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=3` | **2 failed**, 1236 passed |
| `STACK_SLOT=3` | **5 failed**, 1233 passed |

Failing with `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` exported:

* `tests/unit/config/slotRequired.test.ts` › *assertSlotNamedForLocalTarget › slot 1's gateway, unnamed: refused, naming both forms of the slot command*
* `tests/unit/config/validateSlot.test.ts` › *validate() enforces slot coherence › REFUSES an ordinary unslotted local run, naming the slot command* — the refusal message becomes *"Stack slot mismatch: this run's pieces name 2 different slots … slot 3 requested slot (SECUURA_STACK_SLOT) = 3"* instead of the unslotted refusal the test asserts.

Additionally failing with `STACK_SLOT` exported (the alias leaks further):

* `validateSlot.test.ts` › *passes an ordinary unslotted local run in CI — the one exemption*
* `validateSlot.test.ts` › *passes an unslotted REMOTE run — the rule is local-only*
* `validateSlot.test.ts` › *validate() refuses an unusable SECUURA_STACK_SLOT … › a blank SECUURA_STACK_SLOT is "not requested", not "unusable"*

**Why it matters:** `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` asks for tests to be hermetic ("never assert against ambient environment … neutralise it inside the test"), and the four-gate rule runs every suite's `quality` before a PR. On a slotted host, the Akto gate is red before any change is made. The schemathesis suite had the same class and closed it on [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) (a conftest that clears the slot / run-naming variables for every unit test, plus a guard that derives the list from the code that reads them).

**Fix shape (suggestion):** clear `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT`, `STACK_SLOT` and the slot-derived URL variables in a vitest `setupFiles` hook or a `beforeEach` in the slot tests, with each test setting the slot it means; and pin it red → green by running the suite with both variables exported. Measure on this branch's tip too — it adds 37 tests the numbers above don't include.

## 6. ✅ Done — merged in PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1336](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1286-akto-2356-honest-coverage-paced-tiers-stall-stop-and-slot-safe-cba284970402) (2026-09-28, merge commit `b5746d426`)

Everything below was completed and merged, including §5a (hermetic unit suites: 1632/1632 in clean, `STACK_SLOT`, sourced-slot and `AKTO_RUN_ID` shells). Two things were not re-run on the final head before merge, and are recorded here rather than dropped: the Akto pre-merge / security tiers after the container-resolution change (`c52b108d4`), and a live sighting of the stall stop (proven in unit tests only). Open follow-ups live on their own tickets: [KS-1374](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1374/akto-scans-are-now-paced-to-fit-the-platforms-rate-limit-test-times) (rate-limit decision, Kamil), [KS-1363](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1363/akto-a-skipped-har-replay-is-only-a-warn-the-tier-runs-on-synthetic) (skipped HAR visible in the report), [KS-709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-709/akto-reports-a-pass-for-a-test-that-executed-nothing-clean-0-not) criteria 1 and 3.

Original plan, kept for the record:

The live work, on slot 2: clean-slate template reload and catalog diff (predicted byte-identical, 194 ids / 20 categories), `npm run scan:skip-baseline`, `npm run scan:result-fields` (baseline 16 DOC + 14 RES), the imported endpoint count, and the **pr / pre-merge / security** tiers with the four-way console-vs-artifact-vs-HTML-vs-Akto check per tier. **Plus §5a** (hermetic slot tests), then `npm run quality` re-run with a slot variable exported. Then `systemTest/CLAUDE.md`, both HTML docs (version + measured timings with host and date), the PR with its Test Evidence block, and Peter's nod before demo.

PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1336](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1286-akto-2356-honest-coverage-paced-tiers-stall-stop-and-slot-safe-cba284970402) merged 2026-09-28; the feature branch, worktree and slot-2 stacks have been torn down.

## Related

[KS-569](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-569/akto-image-2142-2165-latest-paired-local) (the 2.14.2 → 2.16.5 bump, and the dashboard-only trap) · [KS-710](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-710/akto-a-stale-test-id-catalog-fails-nothing-locally-testsetup-should) (the 2.22.2 bump) · [KS-503](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-503/akto-image-21311-2142-latest-paired-local) / [KS-496](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-496/akto-image-2128-21311-all-systemtest-test-tooling-deps-to-latest) (earlier bumps) · [KS-429](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-429/openapi-32-readiness-akto-cannot-parse-32-swagger-parser-2248-sequence) (OpenAPI 3.2 gate, unchanged) · [KS-713](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-713/mcp-server-has-its-own-openapi-definition-and-10-routes-but-zero-scan) (MCP suites stay off — Kam ruled mcp-server internal-only) · [KS-717](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-717/akto-test-id-catalog-and-the-loaded-template-library-drift-silently) (catalog ↔ loaded-library drift guard; its #802 rulings constrain any allowlist change) · [KS-709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-709/akto-reports-a-pass-for-a-test-that-executed-nothing-clean-0-not) / [KS-696](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-696/akto-pr-scan-is-non-deterministic-three-runs-on-near-identical-code) (false pass and non-determinism — re-measure, not fixed by a bump) · [KS-755](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-755/akto-unit-suite-has-a-standing-red-rundir-resolverunid-ignores-the) and [KS-990](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-990/npm-run-quality-cannot-pass-in-systemtestperformance-or-systemtestakto) (see §5) · [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) (where §5a was measured)
