title: Bump systemTest schemathesis pin 4.27.2 → 4.27.5 — the KS-1270 NDJSON hold is lifted (upstream fixed it in 4.27.4, verified at the v4.27.5 tag); 4.27.4 + 4.27.5 = 20 fixes, four touch our estate
description:
## BLUF

Upstream released **4.27.5** (tag `v4.27.5`, commit `f7793b1`, 2026-09-21). Our pin is `schemathesis==4.27.2` ([KS-1268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1268/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4271-4272-retargeted-from-4273-whose)), held there by [KS-1270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1270/schemathesis-4273-ndjson-writer-thread-deadlocks-on-a-lazy-import): 4.27.3 moved `import requests` onto the NDJSON writer thread, the thread dies on `_DeadlockError`, the NDJSON is a 1-line file and the CLI exits 0 — measured 0/40 complete runs on 4.27.3 vs 40/40 on 4.27.2, with `run.py pr` printing *"Run validity: OK"* and a green PASSED banner over the empty stream.

**Update 2026-09-21 — the hold is lifted (verified upstream, not believed).** Peter's recollection that the fix shipped in an earlier release checks out:

* **4.27.4 (2026-09-18)** release notes — *Fixed*: **"Truncated** `--report ndjson` **output containing only the** `Initialize` **event. #4807"** and **"Show an error when a report writer fails instead of truncating its output silently."** (the second closes the class, not just the instance). Also in 4.27.4: examples phase fills missing values from schema `default`; `example`/`examples` on array items; property examples under `allOf`/`oneOf`/`anyOf` at any depth; self-referencing optional properties dropped instead of losing the body; boolean-subschema crash in recursive schemas; `ignored_auth` cookie crash (#4804); `anyOf` branches when both `oneOf`+`anyOf`; stable `example`/`x-example` order; `x-example`/`x-examples` on OAS3 parameters; discriminator pins the branch `enum` rejects.
* `src/schemathesis/reporting/ndjson.py` **at the** `v4.27.5` **tag** — no `import requests` anywhere. `serialize()` does `prepared_request = getattr(sys.modules.get("requests"), "PreparedRequest", None)` under the comment *"Looked up rather than imported: importing here deadlocks on the writer thread, and importing at module level slows CLI startup."* The deadlock path measured on [KS-1270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1270/schemathesis-4273-ndjson-writer-thread-deadlocks-on-a-lazy-import) is gone at the file level.
* Upstream issue 4807: **closed 2026-09-18 22:08Z,** `state_reason: completed`**, maintainer: "Fixed via #4809", release-bot: "Released in Schemathesis 4.27.4"** (read via the GitHub API on 2026-09-21). PR 4809 adds a `WriterWorker` that re-raises the writer's exception on `join()` (`handlers/base.py`) and removes the lazy import from `reporting/ndjson.py`.

**Cross-check against PRs and tickets (2026-09-21):** 25 open PRs — none touches Schemathesis, 4.27.x, NDJSON or [KS-1268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1268/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4271-4272-retargeted-from-4273-whose)/1270/1271; no other Linear ticket covers 4.27.4 or 4.27.5; PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1049](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1271-systemtest-guards-after-ks-1268ks-1270-ndjson-completeness-45f8e96c7a33) ([KS-1271](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1271/systemtest-guards-after-ks-1268ks-1270-ndjson-completeness-gate-writer)) **merged 2026-09-18 →** `59412d057`, so `tests/functional/config/test_ndjson_completeness.py` and `scripts/runner/ndjson_completeness_gate.py` are on `develop` and the one-op check already runs inside `quality` against the installed pin. Adjacent: [KS-1218](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1218/schemathesis-constraintstxts-documented-install-line-skips-the-pip) (Kamil, Backlog) — `constraints.txt`'s documented install line skips the pip upgrade; the bump edits `constraints.txt`, so don't collide.

So this is now the bump ticket ([KS-1268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1268/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4271-4272-retargeted-from-4273-whose) **shape), 4.27.2 → 4.27.5.** **Done in commit** `b6959f291` (PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1138](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1285-bump-schemathesis-4272-4275-the-ks-1270-ndjson-writer-hold-is-50f6770035ec); the first cut `d2aad5d18` was amended once for a stale flag count in the cheat sheet — see *Done* and the evidence comment); step 2 of the gate was the acceptance test.

~~The pasted 4.27.5 notes list eight fixes and none of them is the NDJSON writer. This ticket is the w/c 2026-09-21 decision~~ [KS-1270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1270/schemathesis-4273-ndjson-writer-thread-deadlocks-on-a-lazy-import) ~~scheduled: read the 4.27.4 notes and upstream 4807 first, and only if the fix is in the target release run the bump ritual. Otherwise the hold stands and the ticket records why.~~

`systemTest/CLAUDE.md` (Golden rules, formerly "do NOT bump past 4.27.2 …", [KS-1270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1270/schemathesis-4273-ndjson-writer-thread-deadlocks-on-a-lazy-import)) is the rule of record; this ticket's branch rewrites that bullet to "hold LIFTED" (commit `b0fb38b61`).

## What 4.27.5 fixes, and whether it touches us

| \# | Upstream fix (verbatim) | Our exposure |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Crash on schemas where `properties` is not an object | Low — our spec is generated (`npm run generate-openapi`) and the 4.27.2 sweeps load it without a crash; nothing to gain |
| 2 | Drop parameter examples built from nested ones that violate the parameter's own schema | **Yes** — [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage) added inline examples to every operation; [KS-665](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-665/ks-256-review-follow-ups-5-example-fixable-400s-the-tsx-transpile-only) tracks 5 "example-fixable 400s". If any of those are nested examples the parameter schema rejects, 4.27.5 stops sending them → examples-phase counts change. Re-measure [KS-665](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-665/ks-256-review-follow-ups-5-example-fixable-400s-the-tsx-transpile-only)'s five before/after |
| 3 | Skip parameter schema `examples` values that violate that schema in the examples phase | **Yes** — same surface as fix 2; expect a drop in examples-phase failures that were really invalid examples, which would mask [KS-665](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-665/ks-256-review-follow-ups-5-example-fixable-400s-the-tsx-transpile-only)'s list rather than fix it. Delta tab must show the disappearance as "not generated", not "passed" |
| 4 | Coverage phase probing methods of operations disabled via `[[operations]]` | No — `schemathesis.toml` has 44 `[[operations]]` blocks but none uses `enabled = false` (the four `enabled = false` mentions are comments about the retired `checks.not_a_server_error.enabled` form, [KS-1170](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1170/schemathesis-4271-ignores-the-per-operation-not-a-server-error-disable)). Nothing was being wrongly probed |
| 5 | Crash in the examples phase for `allOf` members with wrongly typed `examples` or `required` | Low — no such crash on the 4.27.2 sweeps; would surface as an examples-phase error line if present |
| 6 | SSE: false positives for event payloads containing U+2028 or other control characters | **No** (corrected 2026-09-21) — the one SSE op, `GET /api/dashboard/stream`, declares its `200` with no `content`/schema, and every profile passes `--exclude-path /api/dashboard/stream` (recorded argv) — nothing for the SSE checks to validate |
| 7 | Validate SSE events against both `itemSchema` and a sibling `schema` | **No** — same reasons as 6 |
| 8 | Report a schema error instead of a generic check failure for boolean `allOf`/`anyOf` branches | Low — changes how a failure is *labelled* (schema error vs check failure); the HTML parser and baseline gate key on check names, so a relabel on any op would move a row from a check bucket to the errors bucket. Verify counts reconcile |

Net: fixes 2, 3 (and 4.27.4's default-filling change) can change our sweep numbers — measured in the evidence comment; the rest are crash/labelling fixes we have not hit. (4.27.4's own fixes are listed in the update above — its examples-phase changes land on the same [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage)/[KS-665](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-665/ks-256-review-follow-ups-5-example-fixable-400s-the-tsx-transpile-only) surface.)

## Bump gate (from [KS-1270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1270/schemathesis-4273-ndjson-writer-thread-deadlocks-on-a-lazy-import) / `systemTest/CLAUDE.md`)

1. ~~Read upstream 4807~~ — **done 2026-09-21** (update above): fixed in 4.27.4, confirmed at the `v4.27.5` tag.
2. **One-op line-count check** ([KS-1270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1270/schemathesis-4273-ndjson-writer-thread-deadlocks-on-a-lazy-import) §bisect, scratch venv, no project deps): `st run <spec> --url <stub> --include-path <one op> --max-examples 2 --phases fuzzing --checks not_a_server_error --report ndjson --workers 1` → `ScenarioFinished` count = console `Tested:`, `EngineFinished` present. Expected on a fixed release: 21 lines; on a broken one: 1.
3. Only then the normal bump ritual ([KS-1169](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1169/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4252-4271-seven-negativecoverage) / [KS-1268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1268/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4271-4272-retargeted-from-4273-whose) shape): `pyproject.toml` + `constraints.txt` + `test_dependency_floors.py` pin, `--help` diff, `--report` list, compat tests, `quality` gate, before/after `full` sweep on the named slot with fixed seed ([KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete): seed, not version, moved the stateful op count).

[KS-1271](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1271/systemtest-guards-after-ks-1268ks-1270-ndjson-completeness-gate-writer)'s `test_ndjson_completeness.py` (red on 4.27.3, green on 4.27.2) and `ndjson_completeness_gate.py` make step 2 automatic — [KS-1271: systemTest guards after KS-1268/KS-1270 — NDJSON completeness gate + writer-shape pin, seed pass-through, ignored_auth 429 = inconclusive, update-deps floors line](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1271-systemtest-guards-after-ks-1268ks-1270-ndjson-completeness-45f8e96c7a33) merged 2026-09-18, so `quality` on the bumped venv IS the step-2 check; the scratch-venv one-liner is the belt-and-braces version.

## Outcome

* **4807 fixed in 4.27.4, present in 4.27.5** → this ticket is the bump ticket in the [KS-1268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1268/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4271-4272-retargeted-from-4273-whose) shape; step 2 is the acceptance test; re-measure [KS-665](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-665/ks-256-review-follow-ups-5-example-fixable-400s-the-tsx-transpile-only)'s five 400s and `/api/dashboard/stream`.
* ~~4807 not fixed → hold stays at 4.27.2~~ — not the case. For the record, the measured fallback had been the one-line `import requests` in `config/hooks.py` (40/40 on 4.27.3, +35 ms per run start — [KS-1270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1270/schemathesis-4273-ndjson-writer-thread-deadlocks-on-a-lazy-import) step 3c/5).

## Done (2026-09-21) — see the evidence comment for every number

* Bump commit `b6959f291` on `feature/ks-1285-…` (pin 4.27.5, constraints, yaml header, header-parity test, CLAUDE.md, both HTML docs). Acceptance 3/3, `quality` 2,564 passed / 98.85 %, before/after `full` on slot 1 at seed 1285, fixed-seed stateful comparison, six-step audit. **PR** [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1138](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1285-bump-schemathesis-4272-4275-the-ks-1270-ndjson-writer-hold-is-50f6770035ec) **opened 2026-09-21** (pushed through the [KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight) pre-push preflight: 15/15 legs, 43/43 shell suites). Spec defect it surfaced → [KS-1287](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1287/openapi-path-parameter-index-on-get-apistatusidcheckindex-is-published).

## Done on this ticket earlier (2026-09-21)

* Fetched and read: the 4.27.4 release notes, upstream 4807 (body only — status not readable), `reporting/ndjson.py` at `v4.27.5`.
* Worktree `~/dev_Obeden/wt/ks-1285`, branch `feature/ks-1285-…` from `origin/develop` @ `9f0265eb0`: `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` hold bullet rewritten as "hold LIFTED — fixed in 4.27.4; the one-op check stays as every bump's acceptance test, automated by [KS-1271](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1271/systemtest-guards-after-ks-1268ks-1270-ndjson-completeness-gate-writer)". Committed locally as `b0fb38b61` (docs-only); the bump itself followed on the same branch.

## Not done

* `test_dependency_floors.py` deliberately unchanged — its `4.27.2` is fixture text in a fake pyproject, not the pin. title: cardano/transaction.ts: add_json_metadatum_with_schema throws on any metadata string over 64 bytes — KS-721's identityCommitment (≥69 bytes) has never been anchorable on a real chain
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/cardano/transaction.ts:107` attaches every anchor's metadata with `txBuilder.add_json_metadatum_with_schema(label, JSON.stringify(metadataPayload), CSL.MetadataJsonSchema.BasicConversions)`. With the lockfile-pinned `@emurgo/cardano-serialization-lib-nodejs` **15.0.3** (`Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json`), that call **throws for ANY string value over 64 bytes**: `Max metadata string too long: 65, max = 64`. This is Cardano's own metadata rule (text strings and byte strings in transaction metadata are capped at 64 bytes each), surfaced by CSL at tx build.

**Consequence for KS-721:** the `identityCommitment` accepted since 2026-08-31 (#763, `436f37bed`) has the form `<label>.v<N>:<64 lowercase hex>`, whose regex minimum is **69 bytes** (`a.v1:` + 64). Platform-S's real value (`identity-commitment-l2.v1:<64 hex>`) is **90 bytes**. So every non-mock anchor carrying a commitment would fail at `buildAnchorTransaction` before submission — **the field has never been anchorable on a real chain through this code.** Nothing has hit it yet because: (a) the mock branch (`cardano/index.ts:234-238`) hands `JSON.stringify(payload)` to the mock provider and never touches CSL, which is why KS-721 could only be proven in mock mode ("no chain write was possible", history.md); (b) S ships `CardanoAnchor:AnchorIdentity = false` (PS-870), so S has never sent the field; (c) K's own originate→anchoring hops forward only `documentId`/`contentHash`/`network`. Every real preview anchor confirmed to date is all-short (64-hex hash, doc ids, ISO timestamps, verbs), so the demo's 194 confirmed anchors are unaffected.

**Consequence for KS-1175:** `actorDid`/`orgDid` (≤512 bytes) inherit the same limit. The KS-1175 PR fixes this at the tx-build boundary (see below) and `Refs` this ticket; this ticket is filed separately because it is a separate fix (KS-721's latent defect), per the one-ticket-per-fix rule.

## Measurement (2026-09-20, Seat A 15th, at develop `dc061f2bb6dff9180a0724b1d1d5c50b9a0173fa`)

Instrument: `5_Project_History/2026-09-20_seatA-15th/boot/csl_probe.cjs` — pure wasm against the worktree's hoisted CSL 15.0.3; no chain, no port, no wallet. Both directions:

| input | `encode_json_str_to_metadatum(…, BasicConversions)` |
| -- | -- |
| 64-char string | OK (78 bytes) |
| 65-char string | THROWS `Max metadata string too long: 65, max = 64` |
| minimal KS-721 commitment `a.v1:<64 hex>` (69) | THROWS |
| S's `identity-commitment-l2.v1:<64 hex>` (90) | THROWS |
| 512-char `did:web:…` | THROWS |
| array of 2 × 45-char strings | OK (107 bytes) |
| an all-short realistic anchor payload (hash/documentType/occurredAt/timestamps) | OK (305 bytes) |

And through the exact call `transaction.ts:107` makes — a `TransactionBuilder` built from fabricated protocol params: 69-byte commitment THROWS, 64-byte string OK. Wednesday reproduced the same table independently at 22:00 AEST (her `csl_probe2.js`).

`transaction.ts:107` is the **single** attach point for BOTH labels (674 single, 675 batch); `index.ts:744` (`json_metadata.secuura` off Blockfrost) is the single chain reader. No other encoder/decoder exists under `services/anchoring/src` (grep, non-test).

## Fix (shipping in the KS-1175 PR, as its own named test block)

A pure helper `services/anchoring/src/cardano/cardanoMetadatum.ts`: `toCardanoMetadatum(payload)` replaces any string > 64 UTF-8 bytes with an ARRAY of ≤64-byte chunks split on character boundaries (byte count, never `.length`); `fromCardanoMetadatum(md)` joins an all-string array back. Applied ONLY at `transaction.ts:106` and at the chain read `index.ts:744` (before the hash compare). `metadata_payload` in the DB and `buildFlatAnchorMetadataPayload`'s output stay in the logical (unchunked) form. Controls: an all-short payload encodes to a `to_bytes()`-identical metadatum with and without the helper (proves a no-op for every anchor made to date); `from(to(x))` deep-equals `x`; a multibyte string splits with no chunk over 64 BYTES. Consequence to document: an independent chain reader (Cardanoscan / raw Blockfrost) sees a long value as an array — the standard Cardano convention for >64-byte metadata strings.

## Not in scope here

A CSL version bump (it changes the on-chain encoder for every anchor — its own ticket if ever). KS-721 itself stays archived (`Deployed to UAT`); this ticket `Refs KS-721`.

## Checklist

- [ ] helper + tests merged (KS-1175 PR)
- [ ] §5f live sweep on kintsugi: one real preview anchor carrying a ≥69-byte commitment confirms and reads back joined on `GET /api/anchors/verify/:hash` (chain source) — Kam's deploy/anchor step, not the PR's

title: platform.ts: a widened SUPER_ROLES would admit a tenant ADMIN role on six requireSuperAdmin / requireOrgProvisioner surfaces that no cell pins - register-connector MINTS A KEY
description:
## BLUF

**Nothing in the suite pins that a tenant ADMIN** role is refused on six `requireSuperAdmin` / `requireOrgProvisioner` surfaces in `routes/platform.ts`. This is a **COVERAGE gap, not a live defect** — no widened `SUPER_ROLES` ships today, and today's code refuses these calls correctly. It is filed so a future widening of `SUPER_ROLES` cannot pass the suite silently.

**The highest-consequence row is the first one:** `POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector`**. With** `SUPER_ROLES` **widened to admit** `'ADMIN'`**, a tenant ADMIN JWT gets** `201` **and a connector key is MINTED**, forwarding `/api/tenants`, `/api/keys` and `/api/audit`. No cell reds that.

The existing cells all send a **connector key**. The gate measured that widening `SUPER_ROLES` to admit `'ADMIN'`/`'admin'` reds only **1 of 674** — the single cell added by #1101 for `GET /api/platform/tenants`. Every other route below goes past its guard unpinned.

**KS-1282's own cell is unaffected.** #1101 pins `GET /api/platform/tenants` for a tenant ADMIN role and that stays true; this ticket is the rest of the same dimension.

## The six rows — one fix shape, one test pass proves all six

All six are the same defect class (a widened `SUPER_ROLES` admits a role-ADMIN JWT where nothing pins it) and the same fix (add the role-dimension cell to `src/__tests__/ks1215-the-connector-branch-never-carries-the-callers-bearer.test.ts`, inside the `KS-1215 real app, NODE_ENV=test` describe, each with its `RAN.add(...)` and its COMPLETENESS `expected` entry). Tamper for all six: `platform.ts:64`, whole-line ×1, `const SUPER_ROLES = ['super_admin', 'SUPER_ADMIN', 'platform_admin', 'SYSTEM_ADMIN'];` → `[… , 'ADMIN', 'admin'];`.

- [ ] `POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector` **(guard** `:489`**, via** `requireOrgProvisioner` **at** `:91`**, its** `SUPER_ROLES.includes` **at** `:97`**) — LEAD ITEM.** Unguarded outcome: **403 → 201, and a connector key is MINTED**; forwards `/api/tenants`, `/api/keys`, `/api/audit`. ks480's `ORG_ADMIN` cell does **not** fire, because `ORG_ADMIN` is not in the widened list.
- [ ] `POST /api/platform/tenants` **(guard** `:239`**).** Unguarded: 403 → **200**, forwards `/api/tenants` and `/api/admin/refresh-tenants`.
- [ ] **All four** `/api/platform/tenants/:id` **guards —** `:284` **GET,** `:301` **PATCH,** `:320` **PATCH** `/status`**,** `:339` **DELETE.** Unguarded: each 403 → **200** and forwards. One `it` can cover the four.
- [ ] `GET /api/platform/audit-log` **(guard** `:362`**).** Unguarded: 403 → **200**, forwards `/api/audit-log?limit=50&offset=0`.
- [ ] **The three tenant-key guards —** `:767` **POST,** `:782` **DELETE** `/:tenantId`**,** `:792` **GET** `/:tenantId/status`**.** Unguarded: POST 403 → **400 BAD_REQUEST** (past the guard), the other two 403 → **200**. **Assert the error code, not only the status** — the widened POST gives 400, never a 2xx.
- [ ] **The three template guards —** `:806` **GET** `document-types`**,** `:832` **GET** `workflows`**,** `:859` **POST** `clone-to-tenant`**.** Unguarded: the two GETs 403 → **500** (their `new pg.Pool({ connectionString: process.env.PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL })` then dials), the POST 403 → **400**. **Assert the code**, and **never run these cells without** `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` **pointed at a closed port** — this is the only row whose route opens a real pool.

## Where this came from

Batch gate `2026-09-20-batch1100-1101-tier1-r1` on #1100 + #1101 (both merged; develop `dc061f2bb`, tree `1ccb80e0d66a`). The gate's NOT-PINNED section carries the full per-row evidence, the measured unguarded status/code for each route, and a proposed cell body for each. Ruled by Wednesday on 2026-09-20 as ONE ticket with the six as a checklist, under Kam's creation rule (2026-09-07 13:23: one ticket when one test pass proves it; split only for separate workloads or separate fixes).

Raised by the Seat B 9th agent seat. Nothing here was deployed; test files change no runtime image.

title: vc-issuer boot warns 'Could not ensure vc_credentials_store table … permission denied for schema public' (runtime DDL vs least privilege; benign, migration 001 owns the table)
description:
## BLUF

Every vc-issuer boot logs one WARN: `Could not ensure vc_credentials_store table {"error":"permission denied for schema public"}`. It is pre-existing. Seat A 14th's scoped kintsugi deploy (develop `f9c28a8b8`, 2026-09-19) surfaced it: the warn was present before and after the vc-issuer swap. It is benign today, because migration 001 creates the table. The pattern is runtime DDL against a least-privilege role.

## Recommendation

Low priority, no rush. Remove the runtime `CREATE TABLE` from `credentialRepo.ensureTable()`, since the migration path already owns the table, or reduce it to an existence check. No action is needed on any running environment.

## Detail

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts:28-42`.
  * `ensureTable()` runs `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vc_credentials_store (…)` and logs the WARN when it fails.
  * It is called from 6 sites (:57, :79, :116, :149, :213, :254).
  * It has been in place since `e50dbde98` (2026-02-18).
* **Why it is benign:** the table is created on the migration path: `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:745` (since `ca7c2bf03`, 2026-03-22) and `docker/init/03-service-tables.sql:135`. The runtime role lacks CREATE on schema `public`, so only the DDL fails.
* **Read from source, not measured on the box:** on a failure `tableEnsured` stays `false`, so each later call re-runs the CREATE and logs again. On kintsugi there have been 0 credential operations since the new container started, so the once-per-boot count is all that was observed.
* **Measured on kintsugi (read-only log counts):**
  * before the swap: 1 WARN in 1832 lines (container start 2026-09-18T22:21:34Z);
  * after the swap: 1 WARN in 43 lines (start 2026-09-19T06:09:06Z).
* **History:** KS-92 and KS-110 (both Done and archived) hardened runtime DDL for the `secuura_app` cutover. KS-110's investigation comment lists vc-issuer as doing "only a `SELECT 1` health check, no DDL", but this `ensureTable` predates it. That is how the site was missed.
* **Board search before filing** (`searchIssues`, archived and comments included, literal match on title and description):
  * Terms: the literal warn text, `vc_credentials_store`, `permission denied for schema public`, and `ensureTable vc-issuer credentialRepo`. 244 issues returned.
  * The nearest non-match is **KS-1121** (credentialRepo substring lookup: same file, different defect).
  * The literal `permission denied for schema public` hits (KS-92, KS-110, KS-215, KS-419, KS-60, KS-72, KS-80) are other services or closed history. None tracks this site.
* Filed by seat A 14th on Wednesday's ruling (2026-09-19 06:16:57Z). Related to KS-1272, the analogous pre-existing api-gateway boot WARN.

title: POST /api/certifications/:id/verify forwards a revoked session's Bearer to originate: the gateway's session check never runs on this route
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/certifications/:id/verify` (api-gateway `routes/verification.ts:784`, mounted with no `authenticateToken`) forwards whatever `Authorization` the caller sent to originate's `GET /api/documents/:id` (`:788`). Measured in-process: a **REVOKED** session's JWT, alone or beside a valid connector key, reaches originate as that user's Bearer, because the gateway's session check never runs on this route. On `POST /api/documents/:id/verify` (`:488`, `authenticateToken(true)`) the same revoked JWT alone is refused 401 `SESSION_INVALIDATED`. What originate does with that token is **NOT measured**.

## Recommendation

Measure originate's `GET /api/documents/:id` with a revoked session's JWT. That sets the severity, which the gate graded Minor pending that measurement.

## Detail

* Surfaced by the #1070-#1076 gate (`2026-09-19-batch1070-1076-tier1-r1`, finding N76-2).
* Pre-existing, not introduced by that batch: api-gateway product bytes are identical at develop `51dbedd39` and at every head of the batch. `verification.ts` is unchanged at develop `f9c28a8b8`.
* How the gate measured it: in-process, the real gateway app with loopback doubles; not against a live stack or a real session store.
* Related: KS-834, the pending decision on whether this route stays public. KS-834's text says a caller who sends a token "is still scoped downstream"; this finding is that a *revoked* session's token passes the gateway here unchecked.
* Also related: the revocation property established on the authenticated mounts (KS-1207, KS-1215).
* Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, archived included):
  * literal title/description contains `certifications/:id/verify`: KS-834, KS-815 (archived, a control-byte guard);
  * `certifications/{id}/verify`: 0; `verification.ts:78`: 0;
  * `api/certifications/`: 38, none about Bearer forwarding;
  * `searchIssues("certifications verify")`, literal re-match: KS-834, KS-815.
  * None records the revoked-session forwarding.

title: Preflight's legs-ran ratio counts leg 1 as run on a no-install run, while the next line says leg 1 could not RUN
description:
**BLUF:** on a run with no workspace install and a real failure elsewhere, preflight prints `PREFLIGHT FAILED on leg(s) 11 - fix the above before pushing. (12/15 legs ran)` and, on the next line, `Leg 1 also could not RUN (no workspace install): run npm ci in Blockchain/Dev as well.` The ratio counts leg 1 as a leg that ran. By the script's own next line, it did not. Surfaced by the #1061-#1069 gate; pre-existing.

## Measured (batch gate, run B3, real `preflight.sh` in the gate's own clones, /bin/bash 3.2)

* #1062's head (`preflight.sh` blob `712f89536`), leg 11 made to fail, leg 1 with no install. Verdict: the two lines above, rc 1.
* The ratio says 12. Leg 1's body never reached `check:openapi`, so 11 legs genuinely ran.
* The exit code is right (1). The defect is the explanation, not the gate.

## Where (read at develop `51dbedd39`)

* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:228-237`: leg 1's no-install branch sets `fail=1` and `env_fail=1` and declares no skip.
* `:154` `_leg_concluded()` therefore records leg 1 in `RAN_LEGS` (`:136`) when the next `step()` starts.
* `:704-707`: the early failure verdict (KS-1260's ratio, merged in #1062) prints `$n_ran` from `RAN_LEGS`, then the leg-1 line. The same count feeds the closing lines at `:711`, `:729`, `:742` and `:751`.

## Fix shape (the gate's prose, not a patch)

* Either have the no-install branch declare the leg skipped (`_note_skip SKIPPED_ADVISORY 1`), or subtract `env_fail` from `n_ran`.
* Regression cell: the B3 shape (a real leg failure plus no install) must print `(11/15 legs ran)`.

## Board search before filing

* A literal scan of all 1268 KS issues (811 archived), titles and descriptions, for `_leg_concluded`, `RAN_LEGS`, `n_ran`, `could not RUN`, `no workspace install`, `legs ran`, `env_fail`, `deps-present` and `Leg 1 also could not`.
* Nearest: **KS-1209** (In Progress), the closing verdict's environment WORDING. Its description carries none of `RAN_LEGS`, `n_ran`, `ratio` or `_leg_concluded`. **KS-1046** (Done, archived) introduced the skip tally.
* Neither covers the ratio's accounting of leg 1.

## Provenance

Batch gate `2026-09-19-batch1061-1069-tier1-r1` (report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-19-batch1061-1069-tier1-r1/report.md`, §LEAD 2 B, run B3), finding **N62-3** (Minor, pre-existing, made visible by #1062). Filed by Seat B 3rd on Wednesday's GO (2026-09-19 02:41:53Z). Related: KS-1260 (the ratio), KS-1209 (the leg-1 environment verdict), KS-1046 (the tally; archived, so cited here rather than linked).

title: Two concurrent POST /documents/:id/revoke both succeed: 2 updates, 2 provenance rows, 2 anchor calls (read-then-update is not atomic)
description:
**BLUF:** `/revoke` reads the document (the already-revoked 400 is decided on that read) and then runs an unconditional `updateDocument(... status: 'revoked')`. Two concurrent revokes can both pass the read, which gives **200 + 200, 2 updates, 2 action_provenance rows and 2 anchor calls**. The behaviour is the same at develop and after #1060: pre-existing, not caused or fixed by it.

## Measured by the batch gate (in-process, the real documentsRouter)

* **E1, two CONCURRENT revokes:** a 60 ms delay after the getDocument snapshot, so both read "not revoked". Result: 200 + 200, 2 updates, 2 rows, 2 anchors, at develop = head = the all-eleven tree.
* **E2, double submit, sequential:** 200 then **400 already revoked**, 1 row total on both sides. So the guard works when the calls do not overlap.

## Fix shape

Make the transition atomic: a conditional update (`UPDATE … SET status='revoked' WHERE id = … AND status <> 'revoked' RETURNING …`), or a row lock. Answer 400 "already revoked" when no row changed, and record provenance and anchor only for the winner.

## Provenance

Batch gate `2026-09-19-batch1050-1060-tier1-r1` (report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-19-batch1050-1060-tier1-r1/report.md`), finding **N60-2** (Minor, pre-existing). Wednesday's GO 2026-09-18 23:14:38Z. Archived KS-39 covered a *sequential* double-revoke answering 403 (an RBAC regression); different subject, not a duplicate. Refs KS-1264.

title: Job 04: a TRIVY_EXIT_CODE (or trivy.yaml exit-code) in the environment makes an image WITH findings read as scan-failed and drops its vulns
description:
**BLUF:** after #1051 (KS-1136 item 1), job 04 keeps trivy's own exit code. So if the caller's environment carries `TRIVY_EXIT_CODE` (or a `trivy.yaml` sets `exit-code`), trivy exits non-zero *because it found vulnerabilities*. The job then records that image as `error: "scan-failed"`, with `counts {}` / `vulns []`, which **drops the findings**, and says "could not scan" about an image it did scan.

## Measured by the batch gate (stubbed trivy on a private PATH)

* `TRIVY_EXIT_CODE=1`, an image WITH findings (1 CRITICAL + 1 HIGH):
  * develop: an UNPARSEABLE artefact, rc 0, "CRITICAL= HIGH=";
  * #1051's head: scan-failed, the 2 findings DROPPED, rc 1, "could not scan".
* `TRIVY_EXIT_CODE=1`, an image with no findings: clean, rc 0, on both sides.
* It is loud (rc 1), not silent, and develop was worse. No repo file sets either knob (grep).

## Fix shape

Pass `--exit-code 0` to trivy explicitly in `Blockchain/Testing/jobs/04-container-trivy.sh`, so its rc means "the scan ran", never "it found something". Add a cell to `container_trivy_failed_scan_is_loud.test.sh` with the env var set.

## Provenance

Batch gate `2026-09-19-batch1050-1060-tier1-r1` (report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-19-batch1050-1060-tier1-r1/report.md`), finding **N51-1** (Minor). Wednesday's GO 2026-09-18 23:14:38Z named it a ticket. Archived KS-490 mentions `--exit-code 0` for Gitleaks in CI; different subject, not a duplicate. Refs KS-1136.

title: api-gateway boot: the platform-DB de-dup DELETE fails 22P02 on every boot where platform_document_registry.tenant_id is uuid — "Platform DB migrations INCOMPLETE — 1 FAILED"
description:
## BLUF

Every api-gateway boot on kintsugi logs `Migration FAILED on platform {"error":"invalid input syntax for type uuid: \"\""}`, then `Platform DB migrations INCOMPLETE — 1 FAILED {"applied":6,"failed":1}`.

**Measured cause:** `platform_document_registry.tenant_id` is `uuid` in `secuura_platform`. The KS-39 #4 de-dup statement in the gateway's platform list compares `COALESCE(a.tenant_id, '')`, and `''` cannot be cast to uuid.

**Harmless today:** the table has 0 rows, and `uq_pdr_hash_tenant` already exists. But a permanent "1 FAILED" on every boot hides the next real platform-migration failure, which is the very signal KS-950 made visible.

## Recommendation

* Make the de-dup type-agnostic: `a.tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM b.tenant_id` works for both TEXT and UUID and keeps NULL = NULL.
* Add a cell that runs the platform list against a uuid-typed table.
* Decide which declaration is canonical. The init schema says `UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id)`; the gateway's in-code CREATE says `TEXT`. The init script runs first on a fresh database, so the gateway's CREATE is a no-op everywhere that script ran.

## Detail (measured 2026-09-19 by seat A 12th; read-only)

* **Where:**
  * `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`, the `platformMigrations` list (\~L1060–1093). The statement is `DELETE FROM platform_document_registry a USING platform_document_registry b WHERE a.id > b.id AND a.content_hash = b.content_hash AND COALESCE(a.tenant_id, '') = COALESCE(b.tenant_id, '')`. The in-code CREATE declares `tenant_id TEXT` (L1066; also L450 in CORE_MIGRATIONS).
  * `Blockchain/Dev/docker/init-platform/01-platform-schema.sql:209-213` creates the table with `tenant_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id)`.
* **Box:** kintsugi, api-gateway at develop `59412d057`, recreated 2026-09-18 22:16:35Z. Log since the recreate:
  * file-based main and platform: 0 applied / 0 failed;
  * main: 39 / 0;
  * **platform: 6 applied / 1 failed**, with the 22P02 above.
* **Schema** (information_schema, SELECT only): `tenant_id` = `uuid`. Control: `content_hash` and `document_id` = `character varying`. 0 rows. `uq_pdr_hash_tenant` present.
* **Mechanism, reproduced with no table touched:** `SELECT COALESCE(NULL::uuid, '')` → `ERROR: invalid input syntax for type uuid: ""`.
* **Pre-existing, not from the 2026-09-19 kintsugi deploy:**
  * neither `startup-migrations.ts` nor any migration changed in `a105cd32b..59412d057`, and postgres was not restarted;
  * the pre-deploy gateway's log went with its container, so "every boot" is inferred from the unchanged code and schema.
* **Not checked:** demo (out of this seat's scope) and local stacks. Any stack whose platform database was initialised from `docker/init-platform` should show the same line.
* **Related:** KS-598 (the same table's `ON CONFLICT (content_hash, tenant_id)` upsert); KS-950 (why this logs at warn); KS-1062 (the failure counter).

title: POST /api/status/{id}/revoke accepts `index: {}` (object where integer is declared) with 200 — outside the KS-518/KS-662 ruling, which covers only `index` below `minimum`
description:
## Finding

`POST /api/status/0/revoke` with body `{"credentialId": "example-credentialId", "index": {}}` answered **HTTP 200** `{"statusListId":"0","credentialId":"example-credentialId","revoked":true,"revokedAt":"2026-09-18T11:28:19.243Z"}` — the revoke side effect ran with an `index` that is an **object**, where the published schema declares an integer.

Surfaced by `by_design_input_tolerance_guard` ([KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the)) in the [KS-1268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1268/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4271-4272-retargeted-from-4273-whose) after-sweep — `full-2026-09-18T11-19-19Z-slot1`, Schemathesis 4.27.2, coverage phase, head `52df64f84`, slot 1. The guard's own message: *"accepted a schema-violating request with HTTP 200, and the violation is NOT the one ruled by-design for this operation (*[KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) */* [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the)*)."* That is the guard doing exactly what it was built for: the [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the) ruling tolerates **only** `index` below the declared `minimum` on this operation; a wrong-typed `index` is a different violation and must still be rejected.

Two things make this worse than "permissive input":

* The handler **performed the revoke** and reported `revoked: true` for an index it cannot have resolved as an integer — compare [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the)'s note that `GET /api/status/{id}/check/{index}` silently coerces a float to a different index. Which entry (if any) was actually flipped is unknown from the response.
* It is a **write** on a revocation status list, i.e. a legally significant record.

## Why it appeared now

Schemathesis 4.27.2 generates a different coverage-phase case set for this op (32 → 58 cases; `POST /api/status/{id}/unrevoke` 50 → 68) — the `allOf`/`additionalProperties` and example-completion fixes in that release. The platform behaviour is not new; the question had not been asked in this shape before. [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data)'s original repro set only exercised `index: -1`.

## Reproduce

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"<ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD>"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"credentialId": "example-credentialId", "index": {}}' \
  http://localhost:6882/api/status/0/revoke
```

Expected **400/422**. Actual **200** with `revoked: true`.

Artefacts: `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/full-2026-09-18T11-19-19Z-slot1/` (NDJSON `ScenarioFinished` for `POST /api/status/{id}/revoke`, check `by_design_input_tolerance_guard`).

## Fix direction

Validate `index` as an integer at the handler boundary (the Zod schema the spec is generated from already declares it) and refuse with a mapped 4xx before any list mutation. Per [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the), do **not** widen the harness exception — the guard is the arbiter; if the ruling is to be widened, that is a deliberate decision on this ticket, not a config edit.

Same class as [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) (Done, by-design for `index < minimum` only). Found by the [KS-1268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1268/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4271-4272-retargeted-from-4273-whose) bump sweep, 2026-09-18.

title: Four originate unit test files make a real DNS lookup and TCP connect to anchoring:4005 (the default ANCHORING_SERVICE_URL)
description:
## BLUF

`ks1213`**,** `ks444`**,** `ks445` **and** `ks543` **in** `services/originate/src/__tests__/` **reach the network. They do a DNS lookup of** `anchoring` **and a TCP connect to** `:4005`**, because they leave** `ANCHORING_SERVICE_URL` **at its default.** The unit suite is not hermetic, and its result depends on the host's resolver.

## Recommendation

In each file, point `ANCHORING_SERVICE_URL` at a loopback port that is refused, or mock `fetch` for the anchoring call. **Don't use port 1:** it is on the Fetch-spec bad-port list, and undici refuses it before opening a socket (the gate's N43-6). `127.0.0.1:2` gives a real `ECONNREFUSED`.

## Detail

* Measured per file by the batch gate, each file run alone at develop AND at #1043's head (`evidence/perfile_net.out`). The ks1228 file contacts nothing non-loopback.

title: A partly-completed /share or /transfer-custody is now unattributed: the multi-write is not transactional (share rows or the custody event written, no action_provenance row)
description:
## BLUF

**When** `/share` **fails at recipient k > 1, or** `/transfer-custody`**'s owner flip throws after the custody event is written, part of the action has happened but no** `action_provenance` **row exists.** Before KS-1228 (#1043) the same case carried a row, because every refused request did. The root is the pre-existing non-transactional multi-write.

## Recommendation

Wrap the per-recipient `createShare` loop in one transaction, and do the same for the custody INSERT plus the owner flip. Alternatively, record the row when `created.length > 0` before returning the error. Regression cell: two recipients, the second refusing, and the share rows and provenance rows must agree.

## Detail

* **Measured by the batch gate** (the #1043 D table). Each cell reads status · share rows · provenance rows:

| case | develop | head (#1043) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| D1 recipient 2 of 2 → SHARE_TARGET_NOT_FOUND | 404 · 1 · 1 | 404 · 1 · **0** |
| D2 recipient 2 of 2 → SQLSTATE 23503 | 400 · 1 · 1 | 400 · 1 · **0** |
| D3 recipient 3 of 3 → SQLSTATE 22007 | 400 · 2 · 1 | 400 · 2 · **0** |
| D4 recipient 2 of 2 → plain Error | 500 · 1 · 1 | 500 · 1 · 0 |
| C7 transfer: the owner flip throws after the custody event | 500 · 1 | 500 · **0** (the custody event row EXISTS) |

* **Reachability (READ):** `shares` has no foreign key on `recipient_user_id` (`migrations/022_shares_polymorphic.sql:28-48`). Every per-recipient field is validated up front. So a refusal at k > 1 needs a race (the document deleted mid-loop) or a transient DB error. The transfer handler's own comment accepts its window (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts` near the custody INSERT).
* **Why it is a trade, not a regression:** #1043 stopped a row being written on every refused request, which was common. The cost is no row on a rare partial one. Develop already answered an error for a half-written share.
* The facts line is on KS-1228. Found by the batch gate `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-batch1042-1045-tier1-r1/report.md` (finding N43-2; the drafter's lead D, confirmed).
* Refs KS-1228.

title: Security: PUT /api/settings/notifications writes the same key namespace as platform-settings — a non-admin whose userId is "platform-settings" replaces the platform-wide settings
description:
## BLUF

**A caller whose** `userId` **is** `platform-settings` **can replace the platform-wide** `platform-settings` **record through the per-user notification-settings endpoint, bypassing** `requireAdmin` **and KS-1230's validation.** Measured with a test token. **Production refuses test tokens. Whether kintsugi or demo accept them is UNMEASURED.**

## Recommendation

Give per-user notification settings their own key space (for example `notif:user:<userId>`), or refuse reserved ids at that writer. Regression cell: a role-`user` principal whose `sub` is `platform-settings` PUTs `/api/settings/notifications`, and `platform-settings` is untouched.

## Detail

* **Two writers, one namespace.** Both write through `setNotificationSettings(key, data)` (`services/api-gateway/src/services/redis.ts:680`), which stores `notif:<key>`:
  * `PUT /api/admin/settings` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts:1123`, `requireAdmin`) writes `setNotificationSettings('platform-settings', merged)` (`:1141`);
  * `PUT /api/settings/notifications` (`:1478`, `authenticateToken(true)`, no role gate) writes `setNotificationSettings(userId, body)` (`:1489`).
* **Measured by the #1045 batch gate** (`evidence/probe1045d.out`). The setup: the real `authenticateToken` and `parseTestToken`, with `configureAuth({enableTestTokens:true})`.
  * A role-`user` test token with `sub: "platform-settings"` PUT `/api/settings/notifications`. It got **200, and** `platform-settings` **was replaced** (with a malformed allow-list, or with an object container).
  * The same principal gets **403** at the admin door.
  * Control: `sub: "someone-else"` writes its own key, and platform-settings is untouched.
  * Control: `NODE_ENV=production` gives **401** (test tokens refused, `auth.ts:118-126`).
  * develop = head (pre-existing).
* **What it breaks:** the connector allow-list that KS-1204 and KS-1230 enforce can be replaced by anyone who can hold that `userId`. It can fail open, or lock every connector out. The rest of the platform settings are overwritten with it.
* **Severity (the gate):** Major where test tokens are enabled (dev/test with `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS=true`; the compose default is false). Minor otherwise.
  * In production the attack needs a real JWT whose `userId` is `platform-settings`. That is READ only; nothing was measured.
  * Whether kintsugi or demo run with test tokens enabled is **UNMEASURED**. KS-623 records that the auth service's test-token guard fails OPEN on an unset `NODE_ENV`.
* Line references are at develop `52df64f84`.
* Found by the batch gate `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-batch1042-1045-tier1-r1/report.md` (finding N45-2), on the #1045 / KS-1230 sibling-writer census.
* Refs KS-1230. Related: KS-1231 (the `integrations` container fails open), KS-1256 (the allow-list fails open on a Redis close), KS-623 (the test-token env guard).

title: api-gateway vitest suite is not isolation-safe: --no-isolate reds 10 of 30 runs non-deterministically at develop
description:
**From the #1040 / KS-1125 batch gate, finding N40-1: Minor, pre-existing (measured AT DEVELOP).**

## What's wrong

The api-gateway suite passes only because vitest isolates each file. With `--no-isolate`, it reds **10 of 30 runs, non-deterministically**, at develop, before any of the batch's PRs. Files leak module state, `process.env` changes and globals into each other. KS-1125's new file adds to the pattern (N40-2: unrestored `process.env` deletes and a global it never removes), though isolation contains it.

## Why it matters

A suite that needs isolation to pass hides order-dependent bugs, and switching to a faster pool or a shared worker would turn them into flaky reds.

## What to do

Run the suite with `--no-isolate` repeatedly and bisect the leaking files. Restore env and globals in each file's `afterAll`, and add a CI-equivalent local check that runs the suite un-isolated.

---

title: Connector allow-list still fails OPEN when Redis closes or errors at runtime, on a read error (catch {}), or on LRU eviction of platform-settings
description:
**From the #1038 / KS-1233 batch gate, finding N38-1: Major, pre-existing. Not #1038's regression.**

## What's wrong

KS-1233 (#1038, merged `e51686bed`) stops `platform-settings` expiring on a TTL. But a **missing** key is still read as "no restriction". The allow-list therefore still **fails open** on every other way the key can go missing or unreadable:

* a runtime Redis close or error (the gate's row R6, measured over a stateful fake);
* a read error swallowed by a bare `catch {}`;
* LRU eviction of the key.

In each case every restricted connector becomes unrestricted.

## Why it matters

It is the same fail-open class KS-1233 fixed for the TTL trigger. A connector allow-list should fail **closed** when the configuration cannot be read.

## What to do

Make the reader fail closed. A missing or unreadable `platform-settings` should refuse restricted connector operations (or fall back to a persisted source), not grant everything. Add cells for the close, error and eviction paths. Check the other readers in the gate's reader census (section C) for the same class.

---

title: Spec-example guard E7: the 40-char floor means a 38-39-char secret-shaped value is never a finding (sk_<uuid>, pk_<uuid>, 39-char random tokens)
description:
**From the #922 tier-2 gate, round 2 (F11, Minor, pre-existing), 2026-09-18.** #922 neither causes nor widens it.

## What's wrong

E7 returns before it reads `BENIGN_SHAPES` for any value under 40 chars (`HIGH_ENTROPY_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9+/=_-]{40,}$/`, `contract.mjs`; `rules-example.mjs:87-88`). So a 38-39-char value is never an E7 finding at all, deny list or not. That covers `sk_<uuid>`, `pk_<uuid>`, any 1-2-letter prefix plus a uuid, and a 39-char random secret-shaped value; the gate probed no finding at round 1 or at head. **No other rule (E1-E9) covers a short random token in a field that is not id-named or password-named.**

## Why it matters

Real-world key formats shorter than 40 chars would pass the only name-blind secret rule the published-spec guard has.

## What to do

Decide the floor from the key formats the platform and its integrators actually use (measure them), or add a second, shorter rule for secret-shaped prefixes. Pin the boundary with cells either side.

---

Filed from the gate report `2026-09-18-ks679-922-30c773ee8-tier2-r2` (F11).

title: Spec-example guard E7: the secret-name deny list in PREFIXED_UUID_RE is a denylist - tok_/sess_/sid_/pass_/refresh_/access_/csrf_/nonce_/invite_/reset_/totp_/hmac_/oauth_/creds_ + v4 are still admitted
description:
**From the #922 tier-2 gate, round 2 (F9, Polish, TICKET), 2026-09-18.** #922 merged as `570ea002d`.

## What's wrong

`PREFIXED_UUID_RE` (`scripts/spec-examples/check/contract.mjs`) refuses secret-NAMED prefixes with a **deny list**. The gate probed that `tok_`, `sess_`, `sid_`, `pass_`, `refresh_`, `access_`, `csrf_`, `nonce_`, `invite_`, `reset_`, `totp_`, `hmac_`, `oauth_` and `creds_`, each followed by a lower-case v4 uuid (43-44 chars, so E7 reaches them), are still admitted. They were admitted at round 1 too.

**Not a blocker today**, measured by the gate:

* the pre-existing bare-uuid shape already exempts the same uuid unprefixed;
* the minter census has **0** uuid-minted prefixed credentials;
* the spec holds exactly 1 prefixed value, the anchor id.

## What to do

The robust fix is an **ALLOW list of the minted prefixes** (the census's 13 benign ones: `anchor` `audit` `batch` `ce` `conn` `did` `event` `evt` `int` `req` `site` `sync` `ts`) in place of the deny list. Then a new record prefix is a reviewed addition, and a new credential name needs no foresight. Pin each allowed prefix with a guard-driven cell and red-proof the list. The same family as KS-1252.

---

Filed from the gate report `2026-09-18-ks679-922-30c773ee8-tier2-r2` (F9).

title: Spec-example guard E7: the ULID-ish benign shape exempts any prefix, secret-named ones included (session_/password_/accesstoken_ + 20-32 upper alnum)
description:
**Found 2026-09-18 while fixing KS-679 round 2 (the #922 gate's F1).** Pre-existing on develop `207716440`. #922 doesn't touch this line.

## What's wrong

The `BENIGN_SHAPES` entry `/^(?:[a-z]+_)?[0-9A-Z]{20,32}$/` ("prefixed ULID-ish fixture id", `scripts/spec-examples/check/contract.mjs:222` on develop) has an **unbounded, name-blind prefix**. E7 is the guard's only name-blind secret rule, so nothing else sees what this entry admits. Measured through `BENIGN_SHAPES` + `HIGH_ENTROPY_RE` from the contract:

| value | length | E7 |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `session_` + 32 upper-case alphanumerics | 40 | silent |
| `password_` + 32 | 41 | silent |
| `accesstoken_` + 32 | 44 | silent |
| 60-letter prefix + `_` + 20 | 81 | silent |
| control: `sk_live_` + 32 (two segments) | 40 | fires |
| control: `session_` + 32 lower-case | 40 | fires |

This is the same class as KS-679's F1, which Wednesday ruled fix-before-merge on #922.

**What depends on it today:** nothing, for E7. The published spec holds exactly 2 values this entry matches (`op_01HC9ZQ2WXYZ123ABCDEFG` and `exp_01HC9ZQ2ABCDEFGHIJKLMN`). Both are under E7's 40-char floor, so E7 never reads the list for them (measured over the spec's 4,730 tokens of 20+ chars; control: the anchor fixture token is found). Tightening the entry reddens nothing that exists.

## What to do

Give it KS-679 round 2's treatment:

* bound the prefix;
* deny secret-named prefixes (reuse `PREFIXED_UUID_RE`'s word list);
* pin each boundary with a guard-driven cell;
* red-proof each loosening.

Or remove the entry, if no fixture needs it after `anc_01HC…` left in KS-679.

title: Spec-example guard: eslint runs `rules: {}` on scripts/**/*.mjs and the ks256 test is type-checked by nothing, so 'rc 0' on the guard checks nothing
description:
**Found by the #922 tier-2 gate (F6) on 2026-09-18, and seen again in the KS-679 round-2 evidence.** Pre-existing: #922 doesn't change it.

## What's wrong

1. **eslint checks nothing on the spec-example guard.** The Dev-root flat config gives `scripts/**/*.mjs` `"rules": {}` (`npx eslint --print-config scripts/spec-examples/check/contract.mjs`). So "eslint rc 0" on `contract.mjs` is a check that cannot fail. The gate planted a `no-unused-vars` + `no-var` control through `--stdin --stdin-filename`: it fires on the three `.ts` files and **not** on `contract.mjs`.
2. **The ks256 test is type-checked by nothing.** `packages/shared/tsconfig.json` excludes `src/__tests__`. `tsc --listFilesOnly` lists `ks256-spec-example-contract.test.ts` 0 times (control: `fixtures.ts` 1), and vitest doesn't type-check.
3. Context: the guard runs only in local pre-push preflight leg 1 (`check:openapi` then `check:spec-examples`). GitHub Actions is retired for this repo, so nothing else runs it.

## Why it matters

KS-679 round 2 (`30c773ee8`) put a new `PREFIXED_UUID_RE` and 44 cells into exactly these two files. Their evidence is the vitest run and a 17-row tamper table. A reader who sees "eslint 0/0, tsc rc 0" in a Test Evidence block would take both as real checks, and neither is.

## What to do

* Give `scripts/**/*.mjs` a real rule set (at least `eslint:recommended`) and fix what it flags.
* Type-check `src/__tests__` with a test tsconfig. Note that `extends` inherits `exclude`, so that config needs `exclude: []`.
* Add a planted-violation control for each, so each check can be seen to fail.

---

title: O-2: RUNBOOK §2.2 documents SMOKE_BASE_URL, but scripts/smoke-test.sh ignores it
description:
The runbook (§2.2) tells an operator to point the smoke test at an environment with `SMOKE_BASE_URL`. `scripts/smoke-test.sh` **doesn't read it**, so it runs against its default target whatever the variable says.

The risk is a smoke run that looks like it checked kintsugi or demo when it actually checked something else. Found by the #1037 gate.

## What to do

Make the script honour `SMOKE_BASE_URL` (and print the target it's using), or correct the runbook.

---

title: N-2: a 2xx whose body is not exactly top-level 'degraded' — including 200 {status:'unhealthy'} — still reads up
description:
#1037 reads a 2xx body as degraded only when it is **exactly** top-level `"degraded"`. Any other 2xx body **still reads up**, including **200** `{status:'unhealthy'}`.

Pre-existing: develop already read it as up, and #1037 neither introduced it nor fixed it. It's a real correctness gap, though. A service reporting itself unhealthy on a 200 is shown as healthy.

## What to do

Decide the vocabulary the aggregates accept (`ok`/`up`/`healthy`, `degraded`, `unhealthy`/`down`), and treat an unrecognised or unhealthy body on a 2xx as at least degraded rather than up.

---

Filed from the #1037 / KS-1101 tier-1 gate report `2026-09-18-ks1101-1037-f87506f47-tier1-r1`, at merge of `207716440e2a6282b90ed2a118614d9cf98bee1e`.

title: N-1: /system/status troubleshooting marks a degraded required service critical and tells operators to restart it
description:
After #1037, a **degraded** required service reaches the `/system/status` troubleshooting output, which then **classifies it as critical and emits restart commands**.

**That's bad operator advice during an incident.** Degraded usually means the service is up and serving with a sick dependency, and restarting it can turn a partial outage into a full one. Anyone reading that panel under pressure gets told to do the wrong thing.

Surfaced by the #1037 gate as NEW, SHIPS-WITH.

## What to do

Give `degraded` its own troubleshooting branch: investigate the dependency, don't restart the service. Reserve critical and restart for `down`.

---

title: KS-1101 follow-up: the out-of-repo consumers of the gateway health endpoints are unmeasured
description:
#1037 changed what the gateway health aggregates **say**. A degraded service now reads `degraded` in `/health/deep`, `/system/status`, `/api/system/status`, the `/status/simple` body and `/api/system/health/dashboard`, where before it read `up`. HTTP statuses and readiness are unchanged.

**Any consumer outside this repository** (monitoring, alerting, uptime checks, dashboards, anything parsing those bodies) may now see a value it has never seen before. **None of them was measured.**

## What to do

Inventory who reads these endpoints outside the repo, and check each one handles `degraded`.

---

title: F-2: /health/services still reads response.ok only — a degraded service reads healthy there
description:
`/health/services` is the one aggregate #1037 didn't change. It still decides health from `response.ok` alone, so a 200 `{status:'degraded'}` reads **healthy**.

## Why it's low

It's **opt-in: 404 by default**, and the gate found the flag that enables it **set nowhere**. When opted in, it reads healthy. Graded SHIPS-WITH.

## What to do

Either route it through the same body-aware reading `services/health.ts` now uses, or remove the endpoint if nothing is meant to opt in.

title: A duplicated x-api-key header defeats key authentication via header joining
description:
Sending **two** `x-api-key` **headers** — in either order — **defeats key authentication**.

## Mechanism

Node joins the repeated header's values into one string; the joined string fails key validation; the request then **falls through to the anonymous / JWT principal**, which on an optional mount answers **200**.

## Measured

Identical at the #1034 head and at develop `34cdcfb26`, so it is **pre-existing** and not #1034's. The gate listed it as a ticket candidate without assigning a severity; filed here as High because it is an authentication-bypass shape.

This is **KS-736 / KS-1207 territory** — whoever picks it up should read those first, since the fall-through-to-anonymous pattern is the same one they cover.

## What to do

Reject a repeated `x-api-key` outright rather than validating the joined value, and make the failure a refusal rather than a fall-through.

---

title: T-3: /api/batch/* is a dead route family — 401 to every caller, 0 upstream hits
description:
`/api/batch/*` answers **401 to every caller**, with **0 upstream hits**, and **nothing sets** `req.user` anywhere on that path. It is a dead route family rather than a Bearer leak — the gate checked specifically that it is not an auth bypass.

Graded **Minor**. Pre-existing, identical at develop.

## What to do

Decide whether the family is meant to exist. If not, remove it and its spec entries; if so, wire its authentication. Either way a route that can only ever 401 is a misleading surface. Possibly one cause with T-4 (`POST /api/v1/documents`).

---

Filed from the #1034 / KS-1215 tier-1 gate report `2026-09-18-ks1215-1034-e4624218b-tier1-r1`, at merge of `a105cd32b1ed9c6927ae6e797f8259224d8480c6`. Pre-existing unless stated; **not** introduced by #1034.

title: T-1: authenticateToken is an async express-4 middleware with no catch — a throw after the await can kill the process
description:
`authenticateToken` in the api-gateway is an **async express-4 middleware with no catch**. Express 4 does not await a middleware's returned promise, so any future throw after the `await` becomes an **unhandled rejection**.

## Why it matters, and why it is not urgent

**Not request-reachable today** — the gate could not reach it, and it is identical at develop. Graded **Major *if* reached**.

The consequence depends on a setting most deployments do not set:

* `UNHANDLED_REJECTION_MODE` **unset =** `exit`**, the default** → the process **exits 0**, and later requests get `ECONNREFUSED`;
* under `survive` → only that one request hangs.

`survive` **is set in only two places:** `docker-compose.yml:441` and `deployment/azure/services.bicep:617`. `deploy/docker-swarm/docker-stack.yml` **and any bare** `node dist/index.js` **run in** `exit` **mode** — so the harshest behaviour is what an unconfigured deployment gets.

## What to do

Wrap the await, or adopt an async-middleware wrapper that forwards rejections to `next`. Worth doing for the whole gateway, not just this one middleware.

---

Filed from the #1034 / KS-1215 tier-1 gate report `2026-09-18-ks1215-1034-e4624218b-tier1-r1`, at merge of `a105cd32b1ed9c6927ae6e797f8259224d8480c6`. Pre-existing unless stated; **not** introduced by #1034.

title: T-2: the connector-token / key-validate fetch has no timeout — a slow upstream hangs the request
description:
**The sharpest of the four candidates the gate surfaced, and the only one that is request-reachable today.**

The api-gateway's connector-token exchange / key-validate `fetch` carries **no timeout**. A slow or non-answering upstream turns into a gateway request with no bound on how long it hangs, while the process carries on serving everything else.

## Measured on BOTH trees (head and develop) — so it is pre-existing

* an exchange that **never answers** → the request hangs;
* an exchange whose body arrives **2.5 s late** → the request hangs for that long.

Graded **Major**. Request-reachable, unlike T-1.

## What to do

Give the fetch an explicit timeout (AbortSignal / `AbortController`) and decide the refusal shape — a 503 on timeout is consistent with how the connector branch already answers a refused exchange.

---

title: ks1204 cells: three tampers stay green - the array-like allow-list, the refusal message class, and the connector info reader are unpinned (#1035 gate N-B, test-only)
description:
## BLUF

**Three tampers stay GREEN on the ks1204 file — the #1035 tier-1 gate measured each at 0 reds.** They are the KS-1229 shape one PR over: behaviour the merged PR establishes with nothing guarding it, so a later refactor can silently undo it and the suite will not notice.

Filed from the gate's **N-B — Minor — NEW — test gaps in the ks1204 file (MEASURED by tamper)**, report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-ks1204-1035-4b1fb0621-tier1-r1/report.md`. #1035 is MERGED (develop `34cdcfb2663b9e4c31025044e6f842ad2c5a10a3`), so the gate's "SHIPS-WITH optional" target has lapsed and this becomes the TICKET it names as the alternative.

Test file: `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1204-a-non-array-allow-list-fails-closed-and-documenttype-wins.test.ts`
Product file: `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts`

## The three rows, as the gate measured them

| row | aimed at | reds | what the tamper does, and what nothing catches |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **Q-ARRAYLIKE-OPEN** | predicate | **0** | An object with a numeric `.length` counts as a list. The array-like connector then gets `dt:DOCUMENT` → **500** `INTERNAL_ERROR`, `dt:SSD_DOCUMENT` → **500**, untyped → **201 FORWARDED**. Develop's 500 and its untyped admission both return. **No cell pins the array-like.** |
| **X-MSG-MEMBER** | message class | **0** | A non-array connector is told `Connector is not permitted to register document type "SSD_DOCUMENT"` for the very type its own list names, and `"undefined"` for an untyped body. **The misconfiguration becomes indistinguishable from a type refusal**, and no cell asserts the exact message. |
| **X-INFO-ALWAYS-EMPTY** | info reader | **0** | The array connector `["SSD_DOCUMENT"]` is told `[]` — "all permitted" — while `dt:DOCUMENT` is 403. **No cell sees what a connector is told.** Belongs with N-2 / KS-1232. |

Every figure above is the gate's own instrument, quoted, not re-measured here.

## Fix shape — test-only, no product line changes

The gate states the regression tests in terms:

> assert the exact message on one non-array cell; add `{"0":"SSD_DOCUMENT","length":1}` × {DOCUMENT, untyped} → 403.

1. **Q-ARRAYLIKE-OPEN** — add the array-like carrier `{"0":"SSD_DOCUMENT","length":1}` in two cells, `dt:DOCUMENT` and untyped, each expecting **403**. Red under the tamper (500 / 500 / 201), green at the tip.
2. **X-MSG-MEMBER** — one cell asserting the EXACT refusal message on a non-array connector, so a message that names the caller's own type cannot pass.
3. **X-INFO-ALWAYS-EMPTY** — one cell reading `GET /api/connector/info` for an array connector and asserting it is NOT `[]`.

**One ticket, not three:** one test pass over one file proves all three (the 2026-09-07 creation rule — split only for separate workloads or separate fixes).

## Done means

Each cell RED under its named tamper and GREEN at the untouched tip, with the whole api-gateway suite showing no new red and `tsc --noEmit` rc 0.

## Provenance

Every claim here is READ from the #1035 round-1 report (tamper table rows and the N-B section) at develop `34cdcfb26`. Nothing was re-measured in filing this. Filed by Wednesday 2026-09-18 under Kam's local-model-only week; the intent is that Ornith takes it as a test-only pin, the way KS-1229's rows were taken.

title: Approving a stale PENDING verification request after the subject's level rose answers 200 and stores the lower level
description:
## BLUF

**Approving a stale PENDING BASIC→ENHANCED verification request after the subject's level has already risen to HIGH answers 200 APPROVED and stores** `enhanced`**: a downgrade.**

* Submit refuses a target at or below the current level, but review re-checks nothing.
* Minor. Pre-existing: the same on develop, #1032 round 1 and #1032 round 2.
* PROBED on a stub. A real Postgres would do the same, since the level UPDATE has no level guard (read).
* Found by the #1032 round-2 QA gate (N-2).

## Recommendation

Not built here.

* At review, re-check the level ordering against the subject's current level, and refuse (400) or auto-close the request. Alternatively, make the level UPDATE conditional on the stored level being below the target.
* **Regression cell:** a subject at HIGH with a PENDING ENHANCED request → approve does not lower the level.

## Detail

* **Submit's check** (read at develop `34cdcfb26`): `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:1252-1254` compares `LEVEL_ORDER` indexes for the current and target levels.
* **Review:** the approve writes the target level through `updateUser` (`repositories/userRepo.ts:796`) with no comparison.
* **The gate's row Q-SIBLING-LEVEL-ABOVE-TARGET-UPD-OK** (a PENDING BASIC→ENHANCED request, the subject now HIGH, a healthy database): head, round 1 and develop all answer 200 APPROVED and store `enhanced`.
* **Unmeasured:** how the level rose between submit and review (an admin PATCH, another approve), and whether that ordering is reachable concurrently.
* **Related:** KS-1194.
* **Searched before filing** (Linear literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, at most 6 pages of 50 fuzzy results per term):
  * `downgrade`: 56, none about verification levels (Platform S pricing tiers and dependency or database version pins).
  * `stale PENDING`: 2 (KS-584, KS-590: verify by hash).
  * `LEVEL_ORDER`: 3 (KS-1176, KS-1190, PS-519: the gateway's level checks, not review).
  * `verification_level`: 9, none about review.
  * `already at or above`: 0.
* **Evidence:** #1032 round-2 gate report §6 and N-2: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-ks1194-1032-430672697-tier1-r2/report.md`.
* Refs KS-1194.

title: Under multi-tenancy, auth's tenant-pool statements carry no tenant GUC: with fail-closed RLS every approve's level UPDATE matches 0 rows
description:
## BLUF

**With** `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` **on, auth's** `db.ts` **sends every statement that carries a tenant argument through** `tenantManager.getPool(tenantId).query()`**: a raw pool query with no tenant GUC.** Under fail-closed RLS, a tenant-scoped UPDATE then matches 0 rows.

* On the verification approve, develop answers a false **200 APPROVED while the level stays basic**. #1032's head instead refuses every approve (503, PENDING).
* **Major while that configuration runs; latent today.** The auth container in `services.bicep` does not set `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` (read).
* **Evidence class:** MEASURED on the real `db.ts` and `TenantPoolManager` with `pg` faked and RLS MODELLED. Whether the runtime database role enforces RLS on that pool is unverified (no Postgres was run).
* Found by the #1032 round-2 QA gate (E-1, an escalation candidate).

## Recommendation

The owner's fix. Not built here.

* Route the tenant-pool branch through the GUC path (`queryWithTenantGuc`, with the GUC in the same transaction), or drop the tenant-pool branch while per-tenant databases are off.
* **Resolve the overlap first.** KS-174 (In Progress) step 1 plans this remedy: "Tenant-pool-manager (or a query wrapper) sets `set_config('app.current_tenant_id', tenantId, true)` per transaction". It never names `tenantManager`, `getPool` or auth's `db.ts`. KS-458 (Done) bundled the GUC for the default pool only. If KS-174 is the live home, merge this ticket into it; this one carries the measured location and consequence.
* **Census every** `query(…, tenantId)` **caller** before fixing. The gate's single-line grep found one, which is not a count.
* **Regression cell:** with multi-tenancy on and fail-closed RLS, an approve whose UPDATE carries the tenant either raises the level or is refused. Never a 200 over an unchanged level.

## Detail

* **Read at develop** `34cdcfb26`**,** `services/auth/src/db.ts:47-70`**:**
  * `query(text, params, tenantId)`: `if (tenantId && tenantManager)` returns `tenantManager.getPool(tenantId).query(text, params)` (`:53-60`). No GUC. The `try` does not `await`, so a rejected query is not caught by its fallback.
  * Only without a tenant manager does it use `runWithTenantId(tenantId, () => queryWithTenantGuc(getPool(), …))` (the KS-458 path).
* **When the branch is taken** (the gate's read): `initTenantManager` needs `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED === 'true'` and `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL`. `TenantPoolManager.getPool` returns the default pool unless `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB === 'true'` and the tenant resolves to another database.
* **The gate's pool table** (approve, RLS modelled on):
  * manager on, no per-tenant DB: the UPDATE runs on the default pool with no GUC and matches 0 rows. Develop answers 200 APPROVED with the level basic (a false success). Head answers 503 PENDING basic, even with no fault.
  * a distinct tenant DB: the level UPDATE lands in the tenant database while the request row stays in the default database (a pre-existing split).
* **Callers read so far:** `getUserById(id, tenantId)` (`repositories/userRepo.ts:407`) and `updateUser`'s UPDATE (`:796`). The census is not done.
* **Config** (READ; unverifiable without `az`, not run):
  * the auth container in `services.bicep` has no `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` (the only bicep hit, `:798`, is originate's);
  * `env.dev.json` / `env.demo.json` set it `true` in a shared block (whether [deploy.sh](<http://deploy.sh>) consumes it was not re-read);
  * `docker-compose.yml` auth uses `${MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED:-false}`;
  * `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` is set nowhere in deployment or compose.
* **Related:** KS-1194 (where it was measured), KS-174, KS-458, KS-1055 (per-tenant databases never receive the file migrations).
* **Searched before filing** (Linear literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, at most 6 pages of 50 fuzzy results per term):
  * `tenantManager.getPool`: 0 of 3 scanned.
  * `getPool`: 1, KS-213 (originate's per-tenant pool fan-out through pgbouncer; a different defect).
  * `applyTenantGuc`: 0, but the search returned no results, so that zero is the search's reach, not the board.
  * `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED`: 12, and `tenant GUC`: 19. The closest are KS-174 (above), KS-458, KS-468 (GUC not seeded on gateway proxy routes) and KS-1055. None names the tenant-pool branch in auth's `db.ts`.
* **Evidence:** #1032 round-2 gate report §7 and E-1: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-ks1194-1032-430672697-tier1-r2/report.md`.
* Refs KS-1194.

title: POST /api/v1/documents with application/json never answers, and /api/documents answers 307 to it in production
description:
## BLUF

**On the real gateway app, a connector's** `POST /api/v1/documents` **sent as** `application/json` **never answers. Under** `NODE_ENV=production`**,** `POST /api/documents` **answers 307 to that same route, so a production JSON create hangs either way.**

* Measured by the #1035 tier-1 QA gate (record R-1) on develop, on #1035's head and on the merged tree, in both the test and the production boot, with every connector shape it tried.
* Pre-existing. The mechanism the gate names: `express.json` consumes the request stream, and the hand-parsing route then waits for an `'end'` that never comes.
* Not graded by the gate; left to the owner. An escalation candidate: whether any deployed edge rewrites the path first is unknown.

## Recommendation

Not built here.

1. Confirm the mechanism in `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` (the `/api/v1` mount and body parsers) and `routes/verification.ts` (the `POST /documents` handler's body read).
2. Fix it so a JSON create on `/api/v1/documents` either reaches the handler with its parsed body, or is refused with an answer. It must never hang.
3. **Regression cell:** on the real app in the production boot, `POST /api/v1/documents` with `application/json` answers within a bound (with a connector key: 201 forwarded, or the documented refusal).

## Detail

* **The gate's measurements (client timeout 3 s):**

| Request | test boot | production boot |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `/api/documents`, `application/json` | 201, forwarded | **307** |
| `/api/v1/documents`, `application/json`, array allow-list | **no answer**, 0 forwarded | **no answer**, 0 forwarded |
| `/api/v1/documents`, `application/json`, non-array allow-list | **no answer** | **no answer** |
| `/api/v1/documents`, an `application/*+json` instrument type | 201 | 201 |

* **Why it hid:** every production-boot create the gate graded went through that `+json` instrument, which passes the content-type check and is not consumed by `express.json`. So "the refusal in production" was measured only through the instrument, and no real JSON client reaches it in-repo.
* **The same class** as the hang the #1034 gate drafter recorded (the stream is consumed before a hand-parsing route reads it).
* **Not tested:** any edge or ingress in front of the gateway; human (non-connector) callers on this route.
* **Searched before filing:** Linear literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, at most 6 pages of 50 fuzzy results per term (2026-09-17 \~16:00Z):

title: In Redis mode platform-settings expires 24 h after the last admin write, which erases every connector allow-list
description:
## BLUF

**In Redis mode the gateway stores platform-settings with a 24 h TTL, and nothing refreshes it.** So, by reading the code: 24 h after the last admin settings write, every connector allow-list disappears and every restricted connector becomes unrestricted.

* **Major, pending measurement.** This is READ ONLY: no Redis was run.
* The same fail-open class as the container fail-open ticket filed alongside it.
* Found by the #1035 tier-1 QA gate (finding N-A).

## Recommendation

An escalation candidate (the gate's grading). Not built here.

1. **Measure first**, read-only, in a non-production gateway running in Redis mode: store an allow-list, `EXPIRE` the key (or wait out the TTL), then create as the restricted connector. The code reading predicts 201.
2. **If confirmed**, the owner decides the fix. Either platform-settings must not expire (no TTL, or a refresh), or a missing platform-settings must not read as "no restriction" for a connector that had one. It may be sequenced with the container fail-open read-side fix.

## Detail

* **Read at develop** `34cdcfb26`**:**
  * `services/api-gateway/src/services/redis.ts:27`: `privacy: 86400` (24 hours);
  * `redis.ts:680-687`: `setNotificationSettings` writes `notif:<key>` with `setex(…, TTL.privacy, …)` when Redis is available;
  * after expiry, `getNotificationSettings('platform-settings')` returns null, and `routes/verification.ts:1214-1216` turns that into `integrations []`, which means no restriction;
  * the only `setNotificationSettings('platform-settings', …)` call is `routes/admin.ts:1127` (`PUT /api/admin/settings`), so nothing re-writes the key.
* **Why local runs never show it:** the in-memory fallback (no Redis) is a Map with no TTL.
* **It also affects KS-1204's migration-residual reading.** A key past its TTL reads as absent, which means "no restriction stored anywhere", not "no malformed list". So a reading must quote the key's TTL beside the shapes.
* **Not measured:** Redis mode was not run (KS-535).
* **Searched before filing:** Linear literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, at most 6 pages of 50 fuzzy results per term (2026-09-17 \~16:00Z):
  * `TTL.privacy`: 0 of 114 scanned.
  * `setNotificationSettings`: 0, but the fuzzy search returned no results, so that zero is the search's reach, not the board.
  * `platform-settings`: 3 (KS-1230, KS-1176, KS-37); none covers expiry.
* **Evidence:** #1035 gate report, finding N-A: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-ks1204-1035-4b1fb0621-tier1-r1/report.md`.
* Refs KS-1204.
