description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/connector/info` **reports** `allowedDocumentTypes: []` **for a stored** `""`**,** `0` **or** `false`**, while every** `POST /api/documents` **from that connector is refused with 403 since PR #1035.**

* `[]` is documented as "all types permitted", so the connector is told the opposite of what the create path enforces.
* The other non-array shapes are echoed raw, against the published contract (`array of string`).
* Minor: misinformation, not a widening. The reader is pre-existing; #1035 made it inconsistent. Found by the #1035 tier-1 QA gate (finding N-2, D2).

## Recommendation

Not built here.

* The info reader should answer what the create path enforces. For a present, non-array allow-list, it should report that the list is not usable, never `[]` and never the raw value. The reader is `services/api-gateway/src/services/health.ts:58`, `allowedDocumentTypes: connectorConfig.allowedDocumentTypes || []`.
* The MCP server relays this value to agents: `services/mcp-server/src/tools/info.ts:144` and `services/mcp-server/src/http-server.ts:258` (read only). Check that they carry the corrected answer.
* **Regression cell:** for each non-array shape, the info answer and the create refusal agree.

## Detail

* **Repro** (measured at runtime by the gate, on #1035's head and the merged tree, both boots):
  1. Store `allowedDocumentTypes: ""` (or `0` or `false`) for connector `c1`.
  2. `GET /api/connector/info` → `allowedDocumentTypes: []`.
  3. Every `POST /api/documents` → 403 "Connector document-type allow-list is not a list".

title: A connector allow-list fails open when platform-settings integrations is not a clean array; one admin Settings save lifts every restriction
description:
## BLUF

**A connector restricted by a document-type allow-list becomes UNRESTRICTED whenever the stored platform-settings** `integrations` **container is not a clean array of object entries. One ordinary save on the admin portal's Settings page produces exactly such a container.**

* Major, pre-existing: the same at develop before PR #1035, at #1035's head and on the merged tree.
* It widens authorisation through the product's own UI, and it is silent: `GET /api/connector/info` then tells the connector `[]`.
* Found by the #1035 tier-1 QA gate (finding N-1, D1). Filed as its own ticket, not folded into KS-1230, per Wednesday's ruling.

## Recommendation

The owner's fix. Not built here. An escalation candidate (the gate's grading).

* **Read side, fail closed, in both readers:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1212-1219` (the create path) and `services/api-gateway/src/services/health.ts:45-52` (the info reader). For the calling connector, any of these should refuse instead of reading as no restriction:
  * a non-array `integrations`;
  * a non-object entry;
  * a duplicate id;
  * a non-object `config`.
* **Portal:** `frontend/admin/src/pages/Settings.tsx` must not regroup `integrations`, or any array, through `key.split('.')`. It flattens every category into `category.key` form values on load (`:37-42`) and splits them back on save (`:66`), which turns an array into `{"0": entry}`.
* **Regression cells:** each container shape below × {typed, untyped} → 403. A Settings-save round trip keeps `integrations` an array.

## Detail

* **Repro** (measured at runtime by the gate: the real route, both boots):
  1. As SYSTEM_ADMIN, `PUT /api/admin/settings` with `integrations: [{ id: "c1", config: { allowedDocumentTypes: ["SSD_DOCUMENT"] } }]` and a `general.platformName`.
  2. Connector `c1` sends `POST /api/documents` with `documentType: "DOCUMENT"` → 403.
  3. On the admin portal Settings page, change the platform name and save. The PUT body carries `integrations` as `{"0": {...}}`. The portal transform was PROBED by emulation and confirmed by reading `Settings.tsx`; no browser was driven.
  4. The same create → **201, forwarded to originate**.
* **Stored containers measured fail-open.** Each gives typed `DOCUMENT` → 201 forwarded, and info tells `[]`:
  * `{"0": entry}`;
  * `[null, entry]` (`.find` throws on `null.id`);
  * `[{id, config: {}}, entry]` (duplicate id, first wins);
  * `[{id, config: "SSD_DOCUMENT"}]`;
  * `"x"` (`.find` is not a function);
  * `null`.
  * Control: `[entry]` → 403.
* **Mechanism:** the container parse sits inside `try { … } catch {}`. A throw or a miss leaves `connectorConfig = {}`, which reads as no restriction. The same parse is in the info reader.
* **Related:**
  * KS-1204: PR #1035 made the leaf value fail closed, but the container above it still fails open;
  * KS-1230: write-side validation of the value, a different defect;
  * the 24 h platform-settings TTL expiry, the same fail-open class, filed separately.
* **Searched before filing:** Linear literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, at most 6 pages of 50 fuzzy results per term (2026-09-17 \~16:00Z):
  * `Settings.tsx`: 0 of 118 scanned.
  * `connectorConfig`: 0, but the fuzzy search returned only 1 result, so that zero is the search's reach, not the board.
  * `integrations`: 15, none about the container parse (the security-review umbrellas KS-485, KS-488 and KS-492, harness tickets and m365 redirect tickets).
  * `platform-settings`: 3. KS-1230 (write-side validation of the allow-list value), KS-1176 (comments) and KS-37 (admin SPA tests); none covers the container.
* **Evidence:** #1035 gate report, finding N-1: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-ks1204-1035-4b1fb0621-tier1-r1/report.md`. Line references re-read at develop `34cdcfb26`.
* Refs KS-1204.

title: PUT /api/admin/settings stores a connector's allowedDocumentTypes in any shape - validate it as an array of strings at write time
description:
## BLUF

`PUT /api/admin/settings` **stores a connector's** `allowedDocumentTypes` **in any shape.** It should validate the value as an array of strings at write time, so a malformed allow-list can never be stored.

* This is the write-side twin of PR #1035 (KS-1204). #1035 makes the READ side refuse every create when the stored allow-list is not an array (fail closed). The write still accepts a string, an object or an empty string, so an admin can lock a connector out of all creates with one malformed save, and learn it only from 403s.
* The frontend types it as `string[]` (`frontend/admin/src/services/api.ts:1075`), but the API does not enforce that.

## Recommendation

In `services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts` `PUT /api/admin/settings` (`:1123-1129` at develop `732c13459`), validate every `integrations[].config.allowedDocumentTypes` present in the body as an array of strings (absent stays allowed). Refuse a malformed body with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the path, before the merge and the write.

* **Regression cells:** a string, an object and an empty string → 400, and the stored settings are unchanged; an array of strings, an empty array and an absent key → 200.
* Consider the same check for the other integration config fields the gateway reads (for example `workflowPolicy`) only if a reader depends on their shape; not required here.
* Not built here.

## Detail

* **Today:** the handler reads the stored `platform-settings`, shallow-merges the request body over it (`{ ...existing, ...body }`), writes it, and answers 200 with the merged settings. It does no validation.
* **Why it matters after #1035:** the read side refuses a non-array allow-list with 403 for every create, including the type it names and untyped bodies. So a malformed value is no longer a silent widening, but it becomes a silent outage for that connector. It is caught only by the connector's failed creates.
* **Migration residual (stated on #1035):** whether any such stored config exists today is unmeasured.
* **Searched before filing** (Linear, literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included):
  * `allowedDocumentTypes`: 3. KS-1204 (the read side), KS-1203 (an untyped create stored as DOCUMENT) and KS-1198 (a connector JWT presented directly as Bearer); none covers validating the write.
  * `PUT /api/admin/settings`: 1 (KS-1204, which names the write as the only path).
  * `admin/settings`: 0. The fuzzy search did not return KS-1204 for this shorter term, so the zero is the search, not the board.
* Refs KS-1204 (stays In Progress).

title: ks1213 cells: ten tampers stay green - a refused issue can mint a holder stub or an anchor, and non-string / padded types are unpinned (test-only)
description:
## BLUF

**Test-only.** PR #1031 (KS-1213, merged as `732c13459`) makes the four derived-document writers refuse a caller type that differs from the stored type, and the runtime at head is correct. But the tier-1 gate found ten ways to break it that the 85 ks1213 cells do not catch. In each, the tamper stays green on the whole originate suite (64 / 741) while the consequence was measured.

* Two are load-bearing: a refused issue that still mints a holder user in auth, or still submits an anchoring job.
* **A local-model candidate:** the cells go in `services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1213-a-derived-writer-relabel-is-refused.test.ts`. No product change.

## Recommendation

Add one cell per row below; each must red under its tamper. Priority order: the two external side effects on issue first (X-ISSUE-AFTER-HOLDER, X-ISSUE-AFTER-ANCHOR), then X-ISSUE-LOOSE, then the rest. R-a is a one-line spec wording fix in the sign-wallet operation's 400 description (plus regenerating the yaml).

## Detail

Each row gives the tamper (the gate's name), the consequence measured on the tampered tree, and the cell that pins it:

* **X-ISSUE-AFTER-HOLDER** (the issue guard moved before `const id = uuidv4()`): a refused issue → 400 with `POST /api/users/stub` **called once**, which mints or resolves an INVITED user in auth. Cell: refused issue → users/stub 0.
* **X-ISSUE-AFTER-ANCHOR** (the guard moved before `const certification`): a refused issue → 400 with `/api/anchors` **1** (an anchoring job). Cell: refused issue → anchors 0.
* **X-ISSUE-LOOSE** (`typeof x === 'string' &&` in place of `!== undefined`): a non-string `data.documentType` (7, an array, an object, true) → **201, served the non-string**, with saveCertification 1 and anchors 1. Cell: a non-string type on issue → 400.
* **X-SIGNCERT-AFTER-UPSTREAM** (the guard moved after the issuer-certs sign call): a refused `/sign-cert` → 400 with **the sign upstream called once**. Cell: refused sign-cert → sign upstream 0.
* **X-VERSION-TRIM** (`x.trim() !== source.type`): `'DOCUMENT '` / `' DOCUMENT'` → **201, served with the whitespace**. Cell: padded type on `/version` → 400.
* **X-SIGNWALLET-SERVED** (compare with `source.data?.documentType ?? source.type`): a legacy source + DEGREE → **201 served DEGREE**. Cell: sign-wallet compares with the STORED type.
* **Q-SIGNCERT-UNTYPED-SOURCE-SKIP** (skip the guard for an untyped source): untyped source + DEGREE → **201, served DEGREE**, sign upstream 1. In-memory only: Postgres reads `type` as `document_type || 'document'`. Cell: untyped in-memory source + differing type → 400.
* **Q-VERSION-TRUTHY** (`if (metadata.documentType && …)`): null / '' / false → 201, stored = served DOCUMENT (benign: no relabel). Cell: a presence-not-truthiness refusal, or a comment that the benign shape is accepted.
* **Q-SIGNWALLET-AFTER-VERIFY** (the guard moved after `verifyMessageSignature`): a refused sign-wallet runs the signature check first (CPU only; an invalid signature would answer INVALID_WALLET_SIGNATURE before BAD_REQUEST). Cell: refused sign-wallet → verify not called.
* **R-a** (Polish): the sign-wallet OpenAPI 400 description names only `VALIDATION_ERROR` / `INVALID_WALLET_SIGNATURE`, not `BAD_REQUEST`.
* **Not in this ticket:** the provenance ordering on `/version` and issue (filed separately, same session); KS-1203 (untyped connector create); the legacy-inheritance residual L03 (KS-1213 itself).
* **Source:** the tier-1 gate report on #1031 at `be8596a29` (GO WITH FINDINGS, verdict 2026-09-17 13:11Z), §4 tampers and §9. Wednesday ruled these SHIP WITH a ticket, not as cells in #1031.
* **Searched before filing** (Linear, literal, archived included): `ks1213-a-derived-writer`: 0 (the same search matched other terms, so the instrument can match). No ticket covers these cells.
* Refs KS-1213 (stays In Progress).

## BLUF

**A refused request still writes an action_provenance row for an action that never happened.** In `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, `POST /api/documents/:id/version` calls `handleOnBehalfOf` (`:1951` at develop `732c13459`) near the top of the handler. For a connector sending `onBehalfOf`, that calls `recordActionProvenance` (an `INSERT INTO action_provenance` for the SOURCE document id, action `version:watermark`) BEFORE the refusals that follow. The refusals are the KS-1213 type guard (400), the content-hash 400 and the 404.

* It is pre-existing: measured on develop AND on PR #1031's head.
* #1031 (KS-1213, merged as `732c13459`) adds one more refusal after it and does not widen the class.
* On `POST /api/certifications/issue` the ordering is correct today, but nothing pins it. Moving the guard after the provenance write reds no cell.
* **Severity Minor** (the tier-1 gate on #1031, finding D1, with Q-ISSUE-AFTER-OBO). The same class is already recorded in `BACKLOG.md` for `/share` and `/transfer-custody` (with no ticket); fix the four together.

## Recommendation

Move every `handleOnBehalfOf` / `recordActionProvenance` call below each refusal in its handler, so a provenance row is written only for an action that happened. Apply this to `/version`, `/share` (`:2136`) and `/transfer-custody` (`:1595`) in `documents.ts`, and keep issue's current order. (`/revoke` already had this done by KS-566.)

* **Regression cells:**
  * a connector's refused `/version` with `onBehalfOf` (a differing type, a bad hash, an unknown id) → `recordActionProvenance` NOT called;
  * the same on a refused issue (the gate's Q-ISSUE-AFTER-OBO tamper must red it);
  * the same for `/share` and `/transfer-custody` on a 404 / 403.
* Not built here.

## Detail

* **Measured by the #1031 gate** (in-process, `recordActionProvenance` mocked and counted; `resolveOnBehalfOf` stubbed to null, so a resolved-user attribution was not exercised):
  * V-OBO (a docs connector, `/version`, `onBehalfOf` + a differing type): 400 BAD_REQUEST, derived rows 0, **provenance 1** at head.
  * V-OBO-404 and V-OBO-HASH: provenance 1 on develop and head.
  * Q-ISSUE-AFTER-OBO (the issue guard moved below the holder stub and the provenance call): a refused issue → 400 with provenance 1, and 0 cells red on the originate suite (64 / 741).
* **What the row holds:** read at `services/provenance.ts:215-218`, an INSERT for the source document id. The existing `BACKLOG.md` entry adds that `action_provenance.document_id` is deliberately not a foreign key (`migrations/041_action_provenance.sql:33-36`), so nothing downstream rejects a row for an id that does not exist, and the row carries encrypted email and display name plus an email hash.
* **Existing record of the same class:** `BACKLOG.md` "`/share` and `/transfer-custody` write an action_provenance row BEFORE the 404/403" (discovered 2026-09-01 during the #742 review). It was deferred because KS-566 moved only `/revoke`.
* **Searched before filing** (Linear, literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included):
  * `handleOnBehalfOf`: 2, KS-566 (moved `/revoke` only, archived) and PS-616 (a Platform S interim), neither on this ordering.
  * `recordActionProvenance`: 0.
  * `action_provenance`: 16, none on writing before a refusal.
  * `version:watermark`: 1, KS-661 (a verb rename).
  * No ticket covers it.
* Refs KS-1213 (where it was found; KS-1213 stays In Progress).

title: systemTest performance `unitSuiteSlotIndependence.test.ts`: the 15 s budget at :127 is tight under load, and the :99 summary regex returns NULL when the child summary includes "skipped"
description:
**BLUF:** two defects in one consumer, `systemTest/performance/tests/unit/utils/unitSuiteSlotIndependence.test.ts`, which spawns child vitest runs and parses their summary. Both are pre-existing and unchanged between vitest 4.1.10 and 4.1.11. Severity Polish.

1. **:127 budget (F4).** The test's 15000 ms timeout is \~13.3–13.4 s of real work at load1 \~19 on BOTH vitest versions, so it times out under load. Seen twice on 2026-09-17: at 16139 ms during the #1030 author's run, and at 17.11 s in the gate's A/B. A duration, not an assertion.
2. **:99 regex (F5).** `/Tests\s+(?:(\d+) failed \| )?(\d+) passed \((\d+)\)/` returns NULL on a summary that includes skipped tests, e.g. `Tests  1 failed | 1 skipped | 243 passed (245)`. The consumer would then throw "could not read the child vitest summary" instead of reporting the counts.

Refs KS-1211. Found by the tier-2 QA gate on #1030, findings F4 and F5 (one ticket, same file). The report is `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1211-1030-e43af4934-tier2-r1/report.md`.

## The gate's findings, quoted

> | F4 | Consumer `unitSuiteSlotIndependence.test.ts:127` timed out at 15000 ms once at head (17.11 s, load1 20.6) under my own concurrent root installs; under the same load both sides took \~13.3–13.4 s; quiet A/B equal | measured, 10 runs | Polish (RECORD; duration, not assertion; READY saw the same at 17cbb1091) | TICKET-class (the 15 s budget vs a child-vitest matrix is \~13 s at load1 \~19 on BOTH versions) | Comparable (base vs head at equal load) |
>
> | F5 | Consumer `:99` regex returns NULL on a child summary that includes `skipped` (e.g. `Tests  1 failed \| 1 skipped \| 243 passed (245)`) → the consumer would throw "could not read the child vitest summary" | measured (probe, controls) | Polish (curio; pre-existing, format unchanged 4.1.10→4.1.11) | TICKET-class | Product |
>
> `:99` regex probe (`suites/consumer_regex_probe.out`), read from the file at head: vitest 4.1.11 passing output → failed 0 / passed 3 / total 3; 4.1.11 failing output → 1/2/3; packages/shared 4.1.11 → 0/851/851; 4.1.10 → 0/3/3. Controls: `Tests  245 passed` (no parens) → NULL; `… (245)` → match; `2 failed | 243 passed (245)` → match; `1 failed | 1 skipped | 243 passed (245)` → NULL (F5).

A/B timings from the gate (base 4.1.10 | head 4.1.11): concurrent round 1 13.42 s | 13.29 s; concurrent round 2 **timed out 17.11 s** | 6.33 s; quiet 5.98 s | 5.64 s and 5.62 s | 5.72 s.

## First item

This is a systemTest harness file, so the change goes through the systemTest rules (all four quality gates). Decide the budget: size it to the child matrix, or run the matrix without the per-test timeout. Also widen the regex to accept an optional `N skipped |` segment, with the gate's probe lines as the regression cells.

title: Root-of-service `overrides.postcss: "8.5.23"` (KS-531) now overrules vite 8.3.0's `postcss ^8.5.28` in 18 service locks — is the exact pin stale?
description:
**BLUF:** in 18 service lockfiles, vite 8.3.0 (dev) now declares `postcss ^8.5.28`. Each of those services' `package.json` carries `overrides.postcss: "8.5.23"` (added by KS-531 on 2026-08-12, commit 3418e9b92), which holds postcss at 8.5.23. npm itself reports `postcss@8.5.23 overridden` with rc 0. It is dev-only, with 0 runtime reach. **First item: decide whether the exact KS-531 pin is now stale** and should float, or be removed now that the advisories it cleared are fixed upstream.

Refs KS-1211. Found by the tier-2 QA gate on #1030 (vitest 4.1.11, merged as `bb848b828`), finding F1. Severity Polish (RECORD). The report is `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1211-1030-e43af4934-tier2-r1/report.md`.

## The gate's finding, quoted

> | F1 | In 18 service locks the regenerated vite 8.3.0 (dev) declares `postcss ^8.5.28`, but a pre-existing root `overrides.postcss: "8.5.23"` (KS-531, 3418e9b92, 2026-08-12) holds postcss at 8.5.23; at base vite 8.1.3's `^8.5.16` was satisfied | measured (parse + `npm ls` + cleanroom) | **Polish** (RECORD; dev-only, 0 runtime reach) | seat evidence (READY "every declarer's range satisfied") + TICKET-class for Wednesday (is the exact KS-531 pin now stale?) | Product (npm itself prints `postcss@8.5.23 overridden`, rc 0); Comparable (the 4 locks with no override — mcp-server, vc-issuer, both systemTest — moved postcss to 8.5.28) |

Gate self-audit note: its first edge check reported 18 false BADs because it ignored `overrides`. It was fixed to honour them, with a planted override control, and is confirmed by `npm ls`.

The READY said "every declarer's range satisfied". The seat's verifier checked the declarers of each **moved** entry. It did not check a moved entry's **own** dependency ranges against unmoved resolutions. That is how vite 8.3.0 → postcss 8.5.23 was missed. The verifier is being extended.

title: A client x-wallet-address is forwarded past the gateway strip, and referrals.ts:55 falls back to it when the principal has no walletAddress
description:
## BLUF

**A client-sent** `x-wallet-address` **reaches the upstreams, and the referral service trusts it.** The header is outside the gateway's edge strip pattern (`services/api-gateway/src/utils/trustHeaders.ts`), so it is forwarded on every proxied route. `services/referral/src/routes/referrals.ts:55` then uses it as the wallet address when the authenticated principal has none, directly under a comment saying direct header reads are spoofable. Pre-existing. Found by the tier-1 gate on PR #1028 (KS-744) as finding N-3. **Reachability and severity are UNMEASURED**, and so is the priority set here: the referral mount was not probed.

## Recommendation

Owners measure it, then decide:

1. probe `POST /api/referrals/generate` through the real gateway with a token that carries no `walletAddress` plus a client `x-wallet-address`, and read what the wallet address on a referral code drives;
2. if reachable, drop the header fallback (read the wallet from the authenticated principal only) and/or add `x-wallet-address` to the edge strip, with a cell proving a client value never reaches the handler.

## Detail

* **Measured at runtime by the gate** at the gateway on 3 mount kinds: a client `x-wallet-address` is forwarded on every forwarded http-proxy cell, on develop `19f1e5475`, the PR head and the merged tree (624 cells at develop, 714 at head; the 90 extra are exactly the cells KS-744's fix now forwards).
* **Read at develop** `0a2b1603f`**:**
  * `referrals.ts:51-55`: the comment reads "Pen-test F-04: read from authenticated req.user … NOT from raw headers. Direct header reads are spoofable.", and the next line is `const walletAddress = (authUser?.walletAddress as string) || (req.headers['x-wallet-address'] as string);`.
  * `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1286` hand-forwards a client `x-wallet-address` onward.
* **Not measured:** the referral mount itself; whether any real token lacks `walletAddress`; what a referral code's wallet address controls.
* **Searched before filing** (Linear, literal, archived included): `x-wallet-address` (0); `referrals.ts` (1: KS-202, input trimming, Done). No ticket covers this.
* **Related:** KS-744 (the gate that found it).

title: POST /api/documents/upload never reaches the gateway's blocked-extension / MIME screen (proxy.ts:551-620): 415 with a multipart body, 405 without
description:
## BLUF

**The gateway's upload screen never runs.** `POST /api/documents/upload` has a hand-forward branch in the gateway (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:551-620`) that refuses blocked file extensions (`BLOCKED_EXTENSIONS`, `:134`) and blocked MIME types before forwarding to originate. On the real app no request reaches it: a multipart request with a body is answered `415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` by `middleware/contentType.ts`, and an empty multipart request `405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`. Pre-existing. Found by the tier-1 gate on PR #1028 (KS-744) as finding N-2. **Severity is unmeasured**, and so is the priority set here: whether uploads reach originate by another path was not measured.

## Recommendation

The owners decide what the route should be:

* if gateway-side upload screening is meant to exist, make the route reachable (the JSON-only content-type rule would need a narrow, exact-path exception for multipart, like the KS-791 one for `application/octet-stream`), with a cell proving a blocked extension is refused through the real app;
* if uploads are meant to go some other way, remove or document the dead branch.
  First measure whether and how uploads reach originate today.

## Detail

* **Measured at runtime by the gate** on the real gateway app: 297 + 297 cells per tree (every token, every leg), 0 upstream hits, identical on develop `19f1e5475`, the PR head `e39521cfb` and the merged tree. Multipart with a body → 415 `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`. Empty multipart → 405 `"Method POST not allowed for /api/documents/{id}."` (the spec method gate).
* **Read at develop** `0a2b1603f`**:** the route is `router.post('/api/documents/upload', authenticateToken(true), …)` at `proxy.ts:551`; the extension check is at `:564`, the MIME check follows it, and the forward to originate's `/api/documents/upload` at `:592`.
* **Why the 415:** `contentType.ts` enforces `application/json` on `/api/*` writes (KS-439, a content-type-confusion defence). Its KS-791 comment records that `multipart` returned 415 on every path, and it relaxes only two exact verify paths for `application/octet-stream`.
* **Searched before filing** (Linear, literal, archived included): `documents/upload` (2: PS-449 and PS-424, Platform S add-in work, archived); `BLOCKED_EXTENSIONS` (0); `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` (3: KS-663 In Review, KS-439 Done, KS-781 Deployed). None covers the unreachable screen. KS-439 is archived, so no relation is added.
* **Related:** KS-744 (the gate that found it).

title: OAuth /authorize answers 500 server_error for an array-valued scope (repeated query param or JSON array) - should be 400 invalid_request
description:
## BLUF

**Minor, pre-existing:** `/api/oauth/authorize` answers **500** `server_error` when `scope` arrives as an ARRAY: a repeated query parameter (`?scope=a&scope=b`) on GET or POST, or a JSON array in the POST body. The request is malformed, so it should be refused 400 `invalid_request`. Measured by the tier-1 round-2 gate on PR #1026 (finding F-10) on all 53 apps, with develop equal to the PR head; not introduced by that PR.

## Recommendation

Refuse a non-string `scope` (and, by the same shape, any other non-string authorize parameter) with 400 `invalid_request` before the resolver runs, rather than casting the query. Add a cell per carrier (repeated query param on GET, the same on POST, JSON array body on POST) asserting 400, plus a control that a single string scope still resolves. Not built; `Refs KS-839` as its source.

## Detail

* **Cause, as the gate read it and re-read at develop** `20ab16f9a`**:**
  * `routes/oauth.ts:473-478`: GET `/authorize` destructures `scope` from `req.query as Record<string, string>`. The cast is compile-time only, so express/qs still hands over an array for a repeated parameter.
  * The resolver passes that `scope` to `parseScopeString` (`services/oauth.ts:357-360`), which calls `scope.split(/[\s,]+/)`. An array has no `split`, so the resulting TypeError reaches the handler's catch and answers 500 `server_error`.
  * POST `/authorize` (`routes/oauth.ts:619`) reads the same parameters from the query or body. The gate measured the POST query and JSON-array body carriers giving the same 500. Not re-measured here.
* **Why it matters:** a malformed client request is reported as a server fault. That is noise for monitoring and fuzzing (the `not_a_server_error` class), and it is the wrong contract for an integrator.
* **Not the same as KS-283** (Done): that was a 500 on malformed Unicode in authorize query parameters, a different input and cause.
* **Searched before filing** (Linear, literal matches, archived included): `server_error` (47 hits, the Schemathesis `not_a_server_error` family; the only authorize one is KS-283, above); `array-valued` (2: KS-256, KS-677, unrelated); `as Record<string, string>` (0); `invalid_scope` (3: KS-839, KS-840 on authorize error delivery, KS-822); `parseScopeString` (0).
* **Source:** gate report `2026-09-17-ks839-1026-df97c0def-tier1-r2` (F-10), relayed in Wednesday's GO for #1026 (2026-09-17 10:51Z).

title: Schemathesis: constraints.txt's documented install line skips the pip upgrade setup does, so quality:static reds on the venv's own pip
description:
**BLUF:** `systemTest/schemathesis/constraints.txt` documents the venv install as `venv/bin/python3 -m pip install -c constraints.txt -e '.[dev]'`. That line never upgrades pip. The harness's own setup does upgrade it first (`scripts/runner/dependencies.py:50-55`). So a venv built by the documented line keeps the host Python's bundled pip, and `run.py quality:static` goes red on pip-audit, flagging the venv's own pip rather than any harness dependency. No fix is in PR-3b; this is filed so it isn't lost.

Refs KS-1211. Found while running the systemTest rule-2 gates for PR-3b (vitest), which changes no Schemathesis file.

## Measured (2026-09-17, throwaway copy of `systemTest/schemathesis` at develop `19f1e5475`, 0 files differing from develop; host Python 3.14.5)

| run | venv built by | pip in venv | `quality:static` | pip-audit |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `pip3 install -c constraints.txt -e '.[dev]'` (the documented line) | 26.1.1 | **rc 1** | red: `pip 26.1.1` PYSEC-2026-196 (fix 26.1.2), PYSEC-2026-3721 (fix 26.2); 0 findings on the pinned harness dependencies |
| 2 | the same venv after `pip3 install --upgrade pip` (what `dependencies.py:50-55` does) | 26.2.1 | **rc 0** | passed |

In both runs Ruff format, Ruff lint and MyPy (src, scripts, config) passed. `quality:static` skips both pytest suites by design.

## The two paths, at source (read, not re-run)

* `constraints.txt` "HOW TO USE", Install: `venv/bin/python3 -m pip install -c constraints.txt -e '.[dev]'`. No pip upgrade.
* `scripts/runner/dependencies.py`, which `run.py setup` uses:
  * Step 2 (`:50-55`) is `pip install --upgrade pip`, run with `check=False`, so a failure there is silent.
  * Steps 3-4 (`:61`, `:73`) install with `--upgrade` and pass **no** `-c constraints.txt`. Whether setup therefore resolves outside the constraints was not measured here; KS-1002 notes `test_venv_pin_parity` catching a fresh setup that resolved 26 packages below them.

## Fix shape (prose only, for the owner)

Either add the pip upgrade to the documented install line, or pin pip in `constraints.txt` and have both paths install with `-c`. Either way, one path should build the venv the gate measures.

A regression check could build a venv from the documented line in CI-equivalent conditions and assert `quality:static` rc 0.

## Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, archived issues included, literal match on title, description and comments)

* `constraints.txt`: 4 issues (KS-1169, KS-1016, KS-1002, KS-687) and comments on KS-1169, KS-611, KS-662, KS-684. None is about the install line or pip.
* `dependencies.py`: KS-672 (canceled, slot targeting) and a comment on KS-666.
* `pip-audit`: 7 issues and comments on 10. Each mentions pip-audit as a passing gate; none is about the venv's own pip.
* `upgrade pip`: 0 issues, 0 comments.
* 1207 issues and 3441 comments were scanned.

title: ks1050 C1 pins only the helper message prefix plus a 3-phrase denylist - a not-applied claim in other words passes
description:
## BLUF

**Test-only, Minor:** the ks1050 test's C1 cell pins only the START of the refusal message plus a three-phrase denylist. So a profile-update refusal that goes on to claim the change was not applied, in words the denylist does not list, still passes. The product is correct today. This is a pin that is weaker than the property it protects. Found by the tier-2 round-2 gate on PR #1018 (merged as `e02515f8f`) as finding F-1, ruled SHIPS-WITH optional, and routed to its own test-only fix.

## Recommendation

Tighten C1 in `services/auth/src/__tests__/ks1050-profile-update-zero-rows-is-not-success.test.ts` to assert that `error.message` EQUALS the full helper string, read from `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` at develop `e02515f8f` (`updateUserOrThrow`, line 973: `` `${operation} could not be confirmed. Please retry — if you already succeeded, you may not need to.` `` with operation `Profile update`).

* **Regression proof:** the gate's denylist tamper must red. It appends " The write did NOT take effect." to the helper's message; today C1 stays green under it.
* Test-only; no product change. Not built here: routed to the local model.

## Detail

* **Today (develop** `e02515f8f`**):**
  * C1 asserts `res.body.error.message` matches `/^Profile update could not be confirmed\. Please retry/` (a prefix);
  * and `res.text` does not match `/not applied|matched no row|did not persist/i` (three phrases).
* **The gap:** anything appended after the prefix that avoids those three phrases passes. "The write did NOT take effect." is one such sentence, and it is exactly the claim the helper's docblock forbids: `updateUser` answers null for two causes, so a caller cannot say the change did not land.
* **Why it matters:** the message is the contract the round-2 change adopted (PR #1018 replaced a 500 "matched no row" shape with the helper's 503). A drift back toward a not-applied claim should red the cell rather than rely on the denylist naming the words.
* **Searched before filing** (Linear, literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included): `ks1050` (1: KS-1050, this PR's own comments); `could not be confirmed` (2: KS-1050, KS-1052, the helper's origin, Done); `Q-D1-DENYLIST` (0). No ticket covers tightening this cell.
* **Refs:** KS-1050 (the ticket this test belongs to; it stays In Progress).

title: Bundled js-yaml copies ship in service runtime images and are invisible to audit-gate/audit-locks
description:
**BLUF:** two service runtime trees carry their own bundled copies of js-yaml code. Both audit gates (`audit-gate`, `audit-locks`) look for packages by name, so neither copy can ever be reported. The originate copy accepts the GHSA-2883 input shape, the same way vulnerable js-yaml 3.15.1 does. Whether any request path reaches either copy is **NOT traced**. **Severity: UNMEASURED.** It is not "High" until the first item below is measured.

Refs KS-1211. Found by the tier-2 QA gate on #1027 (finding F1, recorded as pre-existing and not moved by #1027). The report is `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1211-1027-d7fc6cc55-tier2-r1/report.md`, "F1 detail".

## First item: a measurement, not a fix

1. **Runtime load trace in a built originate image.** Does anything load `confbox/dist/_chunks/libs/js-yaml.mjs` at start-up or on a request, and does `/shared`'s `@effect/platform` `httpApiSwagger` bundle load at all?
2. **Input reach.** Does any code path parse attacker-controlled YAML through either copy?

Only after both are measured: set a severity, and decide the fix shape (below).

## The gate's F1 paragraph, quoted

> * **Instrument, count-from-the-cause:** besides the package census (`*/node_modules/<name>/package.json`), every runtime tree was grepped for js-yaml's exception class `YAMLException` in `*.js/*.cjs/*.mjs`. Positive control (full installs): 8/9/8/8 files, including `node_modules/js-yaml/lib/*`. Runtime trees: governance 0, referral 0, vc-issuer 0, **originate 1** (`confbox/dist/_chunks/libs/js-yaml.mjs`), **/shared 2** (`@effect/platform/dist/{esm,cjs}/internal/httpApiSwagger.js`, a swagger-ui bundle with its own `YAMLException$1`). The package-name census reads NONE in the same trees. That is the blind spot: the drafter's D1 "none" is true of packages and false of code.
> * **Where they ship:** originate runner `:79 npm ci --omit=dev` keeps confbox (lock `node_modules/confbox` 0.2.4, `node_modules/c12` 3.3.4, `node_modules/@prisma/config` 7.8.0, none dev-flagged). Every service image `COPY --from=shared-builder /shared /shared` (governance :74, originate :88, referral :89, vc-issuer :81), and shared-builder is a full `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, never pruned.
> * **Not moved by #1027:** develop vs head lock entries are identical for confbox, c12, @prisma/config and @effect/platform, and the `packages/shared` diff is empty (evidence/parse.out, and the census step in evidence/runtime.out).
> * **Vulnerable shape present?** Neither bundle contains `maxTotalMergeKeys` (count 0; js-yaml 3.15.2's loader.js has 7). The confbox chunk carries a "4.1.1" string once (version identity by string only, not proven). Bounded probe (evidence/loader_probe.out), shape derived from the 3.15.1→3.15.2 loader.js diff (evidence/dev_jsyaml.out):
>
> | input | js-yaml 3.15.1 | js-yaml 3.15.2 | confbox 0.2.4 bundled |
> | -- | -- | -- | -- |
> | CONTROL in-bounds, 5 empty merges (45 B) | accepted `{x:1}` | accepted `{x:1}` | accepted `{x:1}` |
> | 1 key × 150 empty merges (625 B) | accepted | **THREW abnormal merge sequence size** | accepted |
> | 200 keys × 100 empty merges (82 KB) | accepted 4.6 ms | **THREW exceeded maxTotalMergeKeys (10000)** | accepted 5.3 ms |
> | 4000 keys × 100 (1.65 MB) | accepted 31.6 ms | **THREW** 1.3 ms | accepted 37.8 ms |
>
> Cost was linear and bounded within these sizes. No super-linear amplification was demonstrated.
>
> * **Reachability (assumed, not traced):** 0 tracked files under `Blockchain/Dev/services` or `packages` import confbox, c12 or @prisma/config, 0 import `@effect/platform`, and 0 mention `HttpApiSwagger` (control: `from 'express'` in 250 files). No `prisma.config*` is tracked. Plausibly unreachable from request handling. A runtime load trace in a running image was NOT done (no image, by bounds).
> * **Fix-shape (for the owner, prose only):** decide whether bundled-copy advisories are in the audit gates' contract. If yes, add a code-signature leg (e.g. a `YAMLException`/version-banner census over each image's runtime tree), with a positive control on a full install. If no, state the exclusion in the gate's OK line. Regression test the owner could add: a fixture runtime tree carrying a bundled copy must be reported, or explicitly named as out of scope.

## In short

* **originate runtime:** `confbox@0.2.4/dist/_chunks/libs/js-yaml.mjs`, on a prod chain (`c12` ← `@prisma/config`). Probed: it accepts the GHSA-2883 shape as js-yaml 3.15.1 does.
* `/shared` **in every service image:** the `@effect/platform@0.71.7` `httpApiSwagger` bundle carries its own js-yaml copy. **Not probed.**
* **0 tracked source importers** of confbox, c12, @prisma/config or @effect/platform.
* **Runtime reachability: NOT traced.**

## Board search before filing (2026-09-17, team Secuura-PK, archived issues included, literal match on title, description and comments)

* `confbox`: 0 issues, 0 comments.
* `@effect/platform`: 0 issues, 0 comments.
* `YAMLException`: 4 issues (KS-1117, KS-1109, KS-1108, KS-1099) and 1 comment thread (KS-1099). All four are about k6 and Akto config-loader error handling, not bundled copies.
* `GHSA-2883`: KS-1211 only, plus comments on KS-1024 and KS-1211 (the audit-baseline row).
* Control: `js-yaml` hits 13 issues, so the search can match. 1205 issues and 3440 comments were scanned.

title: mcp-server POST /hash hashes any server-local file named by a caller-supplied filePath, with no auth - measure deployed exposure first
description:
## BLUF

**mcp-server's REST mirror** `POST /hash` **returns the SHA-256 of any server-local file named by a caller-supplied** `filePath`**, with no authentication.** On error it echoes `err.message`, which tells the caller whether a path exists. **Severity is UNMEASURED:** it depends on whether the deployed port is reachable by untrusted callers. Pre-existing, found by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #1022 (finding O1).

## Recommendation

1. **Measure the deployed exposure first.** On the VM demo (and any other deployed target), establish whether `mcp-server:4023` is reachable from outside the compose network or by any untrusted caller. **Set this ticket's priority from that measurement** (the gate: Major if reachable).
2. Then fix, for example by dropping the `filePath` branch from the HTTP mirror (it has no remote use: a remote caller has no business naming server paths), and returning a generic error message.

## Detail

**MEASURED (the QA gate, 2026-09-17, report** `2026-09-17-ks1211-1022-ff49d0242-tier1-r1`**):** `POST /hash` with `{"filePath": "<scratch file>"}` over HTTP returned **200** with the file's SHA-256.

**READ (this seat, develop** `ee40d3099`**):**

* `services/mcp-server/src/http-server.ts:41-64`:
  * `const { filePath, content } = req.body;` and, if `filePath` is set, `hashFile(filePath)`, which is `readFile(filePath)` at `src/hashing.ts:5-6`;
  * the catch at `:60-62` returns `{ error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: err.message } }`.
* `:29` `express.json` and `:33` `rejectNulBytes()` are the only middleware; no auth is mounted.
* A second `doc.filePath` → `hashFile` read is at `:93-94`.
* **The image runs this server:** `services/mcp-server/Dockerfile:73` is `CMD ["node", "dist/http-server.js"]`, with `EXPOSE 4023`.
* `docker-compose.yml` sets `MCP_HTTP_PORT=4023`. The host port mapping was removed (pen-test F-04; it was `"6023:4023"`), so by repo config the port is reachable **from inside the compose network**.
* **The gateway forwards only one mcp route:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1237-1241` proxies `POST /api/mcp/generate-package` to `${MCP_SERVER_URL}/generate-package`, and no `/hash` route through the gateway was found.
* `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx{,-demo,-production}.conf`: 0 references to `mcp` or `4023` (control: 15 or 16 `proxy_pass` lines each).
* So by repo config the endpoint is internal-only. **The deployed hosts are NOT measured.** Any container on the same network, or a mis-published port, reaches it.

**Pre-existing:** the mcp-server source is identical at develop and at PR #1022's head (the gate's reading). Not introduced by the hono bump.

**Searched before filing** (Linear, team KS, title or description, archived included):

* `/hash` 12 hits;
* `filePath` 2;
* `http-server.ts` 2;
* `POST /hash` 0;
* `hashFile` 0;
* `mcp-server` 27.

The only mcp-related hits naming `/hash` are KS-713 (mcp-server scan coverage) and KS-104 (whether to expose mcp-server via the gateway), both Done and archived. Neither owns this finding; they are referenced here in text only.

title: Derived-document writers still relabel the served type: POST /api/documents/:id/version with metadata.documentType is stored as one type and served as another (plus the create guard's regression cells)
description:
## BLUF

**Major, pre-existing:** `POST /api/documents/:id/version` **still lets a caller relabel the type a document is served as.** A `metadata.documentType` is spread into the new version's `data`. The version is stored as the source's type but served as `data.documentType || type`, so it is served as whatever the caller named. The tier-1 gate on PR #1024 measured this through the real gateway: a connector key restricted to `['DOCUMENT']` got **201** and was then **served** `PROPERTY_DEED`, a type its allow-list refuses. By reading the code, `sign-cert`, `sign-wallet` and `certifications/issue` with `parentDocumentId` follow the same shape. PR #1024 closed this for create only.

## Recommendation

Decide the fix shape, then build it as ONE test pass in `services/originate`. The gate proposed two shapes, and neither is ratified:

1. **Write side:** each derived-document writer refuses a `metadata.documentType` (or a spread `data.documentType`) that differs from the source's type.
2. **Read side:** the two served readers (GET `/:id` and the list) serve the stored `type`. The gate's tamper for this shape closes every writer at once, but it turns the #1024 create cells red (10 of 656), so the create test would need re-shaping.

Fold into the same pass the regression cells the gate named for the create guard (N-B below). Not built yet; Wednesday queues it.

## Detail

**N-A, measured on** `/version` (tier-1 gate on #1024, develop = head = merged, so pre-existing and not widened by #1024):

* **Originate in-process**, for a connector, an `ISSUER_ADMIN` and a `SYSTEM_ADMIN`:
  * `metadata.documentType PROPERTY_DEED` on a DOCUMENT → 201; the derived version is stored `DOCUMENT` with data `PROPERTY_DEED`, and is **served** `PROPERTY_DEED` on GET and in the list.
  * `metadata.documentType DEGREE` on a `CERTIFICATE` without `data.documentType` → 201, **served** `DEGREE`.
  * Top-level `documentType` or `type` on `/version` is ignored (stored = served).
  * Control without metadata: stored = served. A plain `user` → 403.
* **Through the real api-gateway in front of a live originate:**
  * `/api/documents/*` sits behind authentication plus a `documents:read` OR `documents:write` scope check plus the proxy. **No document-type allow-list and no enforcement apply to** `/version`**.**
  * An `sk_` key restricted to `['DOCUMENT']` → 201, then served `PROPERTY_DEED` on GET and list. The same happens for an unrestricted key and an `ISSUER_ADMIN`.
  * Control without metadata → stored = served.
* **Blast radius (gate's reading):**
  * any `documents:write` principal can relabel its own document's served type to any string;
  * the verify path holds verifiers to the served type's level, so the level can be raised or lowered by relabelling;
  * a restricted connector escapes its allow-list for the served label.
  * The verify path end to end was NOT measured: the gate's instrument answered 404 for both the target and the control.
* **Same shape, read only:**
  * `POST /:id/sign-cert` (spreads `source.data`, then `metadata`);
  * `POST /:id/sign-wallet` (spreads `metadata`);
  * originate `POST /api/certifications/issue` with `parentDocumentId` (spreads the caller's `data`, `certifications:write`).
  * Not measured: they need an issuer-certs upstream or a valid CIP-8 signature.
* **Not writers of a caller type (read):** the `updateDocument` callers, which touch anchor / status / signatures / blockchain and round-trip `data`; the raw `UPDATE documents` statements; the demo seed.

**N-B, Minor, the create guard's unpinned properties** (same file, same test pass). The gate's tampers left 0 failing cells out of 656 for each:

* case-folding the comparison would reopen served ≠ stored for 6 carriers;
* trimming would reopen arrays and cause 500s;
* comparing with `documentType` only would refuse 6 legitimate shapes.

Cells to add:

* a case variant;
* an array carrier;
* legacy `{type X, data.documentType X}` → 201;
* untyped with `data.documentType DOCUMENT` → 201.

**Related, not in scope:** KS-1203 (#1014 gate N-4, still open): an untyped body from a restricted connector is admitted and stored as `DOCUMENT`. The #1024 gate re-measured it, and a `['DEGREE']` connector is served `DOCUMENT`. The measurement is added on KS-1203; this ticket does not widen into it.

**Searched first** (Linear, literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included):

* `metadata.documentType`: 18 hits, none about a served type (lineage-verb and vocabulary tickets: KS-279, KS-388, KS-663, KS-415, KS-534, KS-1172, KS-661, KS-480);
* `/version`: 18 hits, none about this (version anchoring, lineage, spec drift);
* `untyped body`: 2 (KS-1203, KS-1176);
* `N-4`: 9 (KS-1203 is the #1014 N-4).
* No existing ticket covers the served type of a derived-document writer.

**Source:** gate report `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1202-1024-d1a328088-tier1-r1/report.md`, §4 (writer census and `/version` rows), §11 (N-A, N-B).

description:
## BLUF

This ticket owns the **7 temporary audit-baseline rows** that KS-1024 recorded. KS-1024 is Done and archived (2026-09-13), so it can no longer take comments or relations.

The rows lapse at **2026-09-24T00:00Z (Thursday 24 September, 10:00 AEST)**. From that instant the pre-push preflight (leg 6 audit-gate, leg 7 audit-locks) refuses every push touching `Blockchain/Dev`.

**All 7 are fixable in range by pin bumps** (measured 2026-09-17, develop `f8c7aaa39`). The fix is a bump, not a new date. Each row comes out of `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json` only in the PR whose merge makes its advisory absent from every scanned lock.

## Recommendation

Bump the pins (package.json / package-lock.json only), one PR per lock footprint, through the normal QA gate. Never re-date a row.

## Detail

| GHSA-w5vr-8v7q-w6rv | baseline-browser-mapping | medium | 2.11.0 | 2.10.x → 2.11.24 (minor, inside browserslist's caret) | frontend/admin, issuer, outlook-addin, verifier; services/governance, originate, referral; root |

**Runtime reach:**

  * `services/mcp-server`: prod, via `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, a runtime dependency;
  * `services/originate`: `devOptional`, the class the mysql2 row measured into that runtime image.
* The other four families are dev-only in every scanned lock.

**Not scanned by the gate:** `mobile/secuura-app` is excluded until 2026-10-19 (KS-769, ruled dormant). Its lock carries js-yaml 3.14.2 and 4.1.1 (non-dev, inside the HIGH advisory's ranges) and baseline-browser-mapping 2.9.14. It is recorded here, not bumped.

### Before-state (measured 2026-09-17 06:40Z, prepared by the previous seat, unchanged)

* **Control:** the real baseline gave rc 0 `OK` on both.

title: OAuth app registration accepts any scope list, and any authenticated user can register an app or change its scopes
description:
## BLUF

**Any authenticated user, whatever their role, can register an OAuth app, or change an app's scopes, with any scope list at all**, including the wildcard `*`, the privileged `subjects:erase`, and strings that are not scopes (`made:up`). Measured in-process on 2026-09-17 at develop `f8c7aaa39`:

* A plain `user` token gets **201** on `POST /api/oauth/apps` with `scopes ['*', 'subjects:erase', 'made:up']`, and those exact scopes reach `createApp`.
* The same token gets **200** on `PATCH /api/oauth/apps/:id` for an app id it was never given, and the new scopes reach `updateApp`.
* The gateway requires a token on these routes but checks no role before forwarding them to auth.

## Recommendation

Decide the shape before building. Three independent questions for the owner:

1. **Which scopes may an app be registered with?** A closed vocabulary (the canonical scope list rather than any string) would refuse `made:up` and `*` at the schema. Whether a caller may register a scope it does not itself hold, such as `subjects:erase`, is a separate rule.
2. **Who may manage OAuth apps?** Today it is anyone with a valid session.
3. **Does** `PATCH /apps/:id` **check that the caller owns the app?** The handler does not. Whether `updateApp` scopes the write by organisation or tenant was not read or measured.

## Detail

**Code at develop** `f8c7aaa39` (read):

* `services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:1148`: `oauthRouter.post('/apps', authenticate(), seedTenantGuc, …)`.
* `routes/oauth.ts:1245`: `oauthRouter.patch('/apps/:id', authenticate(), seedTenantGuc, …)`.
* Neither carries a role check. `requireRole` exists in `middleware/authenticate.ts:176` and is not used on these routes.
* `CreateOAuthAppSchema` (`:1132`, `scopes: z.array(pgSafeStringSchema).optional()`) and `UpdateOAuthAppSchema` (`:1237`, the same field) accept any NUL-free string.
* `authenticate()` (`middleware/authenticate.ts:121`) verifies an access token and a live session, and nothing else.
* The PATCH handler calls `updateApp(req.params.id, updates)` with no ownership comparison in the handler.
* The gateway mounts `/api/oauth` as a plain proxy to auth (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:369`).

**Measured, auth side** (vitest, in-process). The REAL `oauthRouter` and the REAL `authenticate()` ran, plus `errorHandler`. Mocked: token verification (returns a `role: 'user'` payload), the session store (valid), `createApp` / `updateApp` (recording), the database, events and the logger.

* `CreateOAuthAppSchema.safeParse({…, scopes: ['*', 'subjects:erase', 'made:up']})` is true; `UpdateOAuthAppSchema` is true.
* `POST /api/oauth/apps` with no token: **401** `UNAUTHORIZED` "No token provided", `createApp` called 0 times (control).
* `POST /api/oauth/apps` as `role: 'user'`: **201**, response `allowedScopes ["*","subjects:erase","made:up"]`, `createApp` called once with exactly those scopes.
* `PATCH /api/oauth/apps/b0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000009` as `role: 'user'` with `scopes ['*', 'subjects:erase']`: **200**, `updateApp` called with `allowedScopes ["*","subjects:erase"]`. `updateApp` was mocked, so whether the real one would find or refuse another organisation's app is **not measured**.

**Measured, gateway side** (vitest, in-process, the REAL api-gateway app, `NODE_ENV=test`, auth and originate pointed at a recording server):

* `POST /api/oauth/apps` with no `Authorization`: **401** "Authentication required", **0** requests forwarded.
* `PATCH /api/oauth/apps/:id` with no `Authorization`: **401**, 0 forwarded.
* `POST /api/oauth/apps` with an RS256 access JWT for `role: 'user'`: **forwarded** (1 request `POST /api/oauth/apps` reached auth).
* Control: `GET /api/documents` with no `Authorization` is 401 with 0 forwarded.
* Caveat: in this harness the gateway's database is mocked (every query returns no rows), so this does not show how a revoked session is handled. It shows that no role gate refuses a valid `user` token.

**What a registered scope reaches (from Wednesday's defaults report, route-level, not re-run here):** with `allowedScopes ['subjects:erase']`, the authorize flow granted a code with scope `subjects:erase` (302). The code carries the grant into the token. Whether such a token then passes the erasure door as that user was **not measured** here. The KS-839 fix makes `*` grant nothing but does not affect a named privileged scope.

**Not measured:**

* live exposure (whether any registered app carries `*` or a privileged scope);
* whether the real `updateApp` is organisation-scoped;
* CSRF and the non-test gateway middleware order;
* the edge.

**Searched first** (Linear, literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included):

* `CreateOAuthAppSchema`: 3 hits (KS-821 and KS-824 on appType; KS-804 on authorize rules);
* `UpdateOAuthAppSchema`: 0;
* `/api/oauth/apps`: 19, none about who may register or which scopes;
* `POST /apps`: 2 (KS-821, KS-822);
* `register an OAuth app`: 0;
* `allowedScopes`: 5 (KS-839, KS-855, KS-804, KS-431, KS-822);
* `subjects:erase`: 7, none about registration.

**Source:** Wednesday's defaults report `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/2_Project_Files/local-model/night/briefs/DEFAULTS_2026-09-17_KS805-855-839.REPORT.md` (P8: the schema acceptance and the 302 grant), re-measured above with the role and gateway questions added.

title: Preflight's closing verdict says a run failed on the environment even when other legs failed for real
description:
## BLUF

When preflight leg 1 cannot run (no workspace install), the closing verdict tells the operator the failure is **"an environment condition, not a finding about your change"**, even when other legs failed for real. It was measured on 2026-09-17: at develop `d7e95cd9f`, legs 5 and 7 refused because the KS-769 fuse had lapsed, yet the last lines of the run led with the environment excuse. Only a trailing "Any OTHER failures above are real and still need fixing." hedged it. The defect predates the fuse PR: `preflight.sh` blob `28d3636c1` is identical before and after it.

## Recommendation

Print the environment verdict only when leg 1's missing install is the ONLY cause of the failure. Otherwise, name the legs that really failed first. Add a regression test: a stubbed run with leg 1 reporting DEPS MISSING plus a forced leg-7 exit 3 must end with a tail that names leg 7.

## Detail

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` at develop `f8c7aaa39`.
  * Line 96 sets `env_fail=0` and line 230 sets `env_fail=1` when leg 1 cannot run.
  * Lines 688-702 hold the closing branch. When `fail` is non-zero and `env_fail` is non-zero, it prints `PREFLIGHT FAILED — but leg 1 could not RUN: this working tree has no workspace install. That is an environment condition, not a finding about your change` and exits 1, whatever else failed.
  * This branch came in with KS-991 (Done, archived; cited here because Linear refuses a relation to an archived issue).
* **Measured** by the tier-2 QA gate on PR #1020 (2026-09-17), running the whole `preflight.sh` in fresh worktrees with no workspace install:
  * At base `d7e95cd9f`: leg 5 `FAIL — the audit-contract suites are red`, leg 7 `FAIL — the lock-advisory gate REFUSED to report a verdict`, and a tail headed by the environment verdict.
  * At head `71bd80a35`: legs 5 and 7 OK, and the same tail. The tail cannot tell the two runs apart, although one of them has real failures.
  * The gate's drafter reproduced it in an independent run.
* **Why it matters:** the verdict is read at the end of the output, and a reader skimming it is told the change is fine and the fix is `npm ci`. That is the reading the KS-991 wording was meant to prevent, pointed in the other direction.
* **Exit code is correct:** the run still exits 1, so nothing is let through. The defect is the explanation, not the gate.
* **Polish, same owner area (carried here, not a separate ticket):** `validateOutOfScope` in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/audit/lock-discovery.mjs` (lines 255, 257 and 277 at `f8c7aaa39`) reports a PRESENT but malformed `expires` as `missing expires (not an ISO YYYY-MM-DD date: "soon")`. The word "missing" describes a value that is there. The gate measured it with `expires: 'soon'`. It is pre-existing.
* **Searched first** (Linear, literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included):
  * `environment condition, not a finding`: 0 hits.
  * `leg 1 could not RUN`: 0 hits.
  * `env_fail`: 1 (KS-926, unrelated guard census).
  * `PREFLIGHT FAILED`: 6, none about this verdict.
  * `preflight.sh`: 39. The nearest are KS-813 (PREFLIGHT PASSED unconditional) and KS-1046 (pass verdict has no skip tally), both about the PASS verdict, not this one.
  * `KS-991`: 1.
  * `missing expires`: 0.
* **Not fixed here.** Filed from the #1020 gate as finding F2 (Minor), with R5 as the Polish line.

title: A verified token without a role or userId claim still 500s every proxied route (x-user-role / x-user-id set unguarded) — KS-744 residue
description:
## BLUF

A verified JWT that lacks the `role` or `userId` claim still makes every proxied route answer **500**, with the internal message `Invalid value "undefined" for header "x-user-role"` (or `"x-user-id"`). The upstream is never reached. The mechanism is KS-744's: the verified-JWT branch of `authenticateToken` copies the claim onto a forwarded header unguarded (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:388` `x-user-id`, `:390` `x-user-role`, the same line numbers at develop `d7e95cd9f` and at KS-744's local fix `6252f06ac`), and the proxy's outbound `setHeader` throws. KS-744 fixes only `email` and `verificationLevel`. Latent today: no signer mints a token without `userId` or `role` (READ in KS-744's brief).

## Recommendation

A shape decision first, not a copy of KS-744's guard. A token with no principal id or no role arguably should be refused **401** at the gateway rather than forwarded without `x-user-id` / `x-user-role`, because those headers are what the upstreams authorise on. Proposal: in the verified-JWT branch, answer 401 `UNAUTHORIZED` when `decoded.userId` or `decoded.role` is missing, before any header is set; cells for each claim on the KS-744 harness. Not built. Low: latent, but it leaks an internal error string (the KS-703 / KS-727 shape).

## Detail

* **Source:** the residue line of Wednesday's KS-744 brief (P3, measured by the brief writer at `d7e95cd9f`) and seat A's KS-744 build, 2026-09-17.
* **Re-measured by seat A** at the KS-744 head `6252f06ac7c913619888cb20e07cc5a0c846043d` (local, not pushed), 02:25Z, in-process. The harness is the KS-744 test's own: the real `authenticateToken(true)` and a real `http-proxy-middleware` proxy on a bare express app, in front of a recording upstream on loopback, with RS256 tokens carrying every claim except the one named:
  * no `role` → **500**, 0 upstream hits, `{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"Invalid value \"undefined\" for header \"x-user-role\""}`;
  * no `userId` → **500**, 0 hits, the same for `x-user-id`;
  * control, no `email` (fixed by KS-744) → 200, 1 hit;
  * control, every claim → 200, 1 hit.
* **The 500 body** in that harness comes from its own error handler; the gateway's real error shape is quoted on KS-744.
* **Evidence:** `5_Project_History/2026-09-17_seatA-4th/tickets/ks744-residue/` (`rows.json`, `probe.out`, the probe file, run once and moved out of the worktree).
* **Not measured:** the real app's error handler for this case; running upstream services.

### Search before filing

`searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), literal case-insensitive matches only: `x-user-role` 109 fuzzy / 4 literal (KS-1032, KS-741, KS-1041, KS-1091: trust-header reads and stripping, not a missing claim) · `x-user-id` 103 / 8 (KS-1087, KS-1032, KS-1084, KS-1041, KS-1083, KS-719, KS-736, KS-708: none about a missing claim) · `ERR_HTTP_INVALID_HEADER_VALUE` 101 / 2 (KS-744, the parent; KS-742 by mention) · `Invalid value` 113 / 5 (KS-744; KS-465, KS-703, KS-386, KS-283 unrelated) · `decoded.role` 111 / 1 (KS-486, archived review). None covers it. Related: KS-744.

title: Security: an unknown sk_ key on an optional-auth mount skips the gateway's Bearer check, so a revoked-session JWT keeps working on credentials, referrals, governance, nft and billing
description:
## BLUF

On the gateway's optional-auth mounts, **any** `x-api-key` **header that starts with** `sk_` **switches off the Bearer check**. `authenticateToken(false)` tries the API-key path first; when the key fails validation it calls `next()` with no principal and **never looks at the** `Authorization` **header**, so the session-revocation check (KS-257) never runs. **Measured:** a revoked-session JWT alone is refused 401 `SESSION_INVALIDATED`, but the same JWT plus `x-api-key: sk_anything` is forwarded, and the shared package's real `authenticate()` (what the upstreams mount) accepts it 200 with the revoked session's principal. That holds on `/api/credentials` (list, read, **revoke**), `/api/referrals` (read, **apply**), `/api/governance` and `/api/nft`, and by READ on `/api/billing`. Only the gateway and originate check revocation, so for vc-issuer, referral, governance, nft-certificate and billing **logout, the session cap and a suspension do not stop a token whose holder adds a junk key header**, until the token expires (`JWT_EXPIRES_IN` default 1h). Pre-existing; not from #1017.

## Recommendation

Fix in `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts`: when an `x-api-key` is presented and fails validation, **answer 401 regardless of** `required` (or fall through to the Bearer path instead of `next()`), and have the spec auth gate (`index.ts:1073-1074`) stop counting the header's presence as a credential. Add a cell per optional mount: revoked-session JWT + unknown `sk_` key → 401, 0 upstream hits. **High:** a measured revocation bypass on five services, bounded by the token lifetime and needing a token that was issued to someone. Not built; no deploy decision needed until a fix exists.

## Detail

**Source:** tier-1 QA gate round 1 on PR #1017, Record R-4 ("on optional-auth routes `/api/credentials*` and `/api/referrals/:sub`, no credential → 401 but an unknown `sk_` key → 200 forwarded"; report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1195-1017-cbe29597d-tier1-r1/report.md`), carried STILL OPEN by round 2. The gate also noted `admin.ts:1455` / `:1483` as optional-auth sites its list missed. The revoked-session route below is this ticket's own measurement, not the gate's.

### The mechanism (READ at develop `d7e95cd9f153e9036ed77935a73c93504fa6e3dc`)

* `index.ts:1073-1074`: the spec auth gate admits a `bearerAuth` operation when `x-api-key` is a string starting `sk_`. Presence only; nothing is validated there.
* `middleware/auth.ts` `authenticateToken`: the API-key block runs first. On `!meta` it answers 401 only `if (required)`; otherwise `next()` and return. The Bearer block, which verifies the JWT and calls `isSessionActive` (`auth.ts:376`), is never reached.
* Optional mounts in `routes/proxy.ts`: `/api/certifications` (`:573`, followed by `requireScope`), `/api/credentials` (`:859`), `/api/referrals` (`:942`), `/api/governance` (`:1031`), `/api/nft` (`:1048`), `/api/billing` (`:1097`). Every spec operation under the last five is `bearerAuth` except three verify ops (`POST /api/credentials/verify`, `POST /api/nft/verify/transaction`, `POST /api/nft/verify/asset`).
* **Who checks revocation (READ, every** `isSessionActive(` **caller outside tests):** `api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:376` and `originate/src/middleware/auth.ts:105` only. vc-issuer (`index.ts`), referral (`index.ts:81`), governance (`index.ts:132`), nft-certificate (`app.ts`) and billing (`index.ts:148`, mounted on `/billing`) use shared `authenticate()`, which verifies the RS256 signature and nothing else.

### The measurement (in-process, 2026-09-17 01:41Z)

* **Substrate:** the real assembled gateway app (`index.ts` default export) at `a067d4e3e`, whose `auth.ts`, `index.ts`, `proxy.ts`, `admin.ts`, `config/services.ts` and shared `middleware/index.ts` blobs equal develop `d7e95cd9f` (checked by blob id). Every `*_SERVICE_URL` pointed at one recording stub. The session store stubbed: session `r4-revoked` → revoked, `r4-active` → live. Tokens: throwaway RS256 JWTs from the test setup key. Each forwarded request was then replayed, with the headers the gateway actually forwarded, against shared `authenticate()` mounted on `/api` of a bare express app.
* **Rows** (84 = 12 paths × 7 credentials; gateway status / upstream hits / replayed upstream status):

| credential | credentials GET, GET :id, POST :id/revoke · referrals GET :code, POST apply · governance GET · nft GET |
| -- | -- |
| none | 401, 0 hits |
| unknown `sk_` key | **200 forwarded, 1 hit**; no Authorization forwarded; upstream **401** |
| known key (control) | 200, 1 hit, connector principal; upstream 200 |
| live-session JWT (control) | 200, 1 hit, session check ran; upstream 200 |
| revoked-session JWT (control) | **401** `SESSION_INVALIDATED`, 0 hits, session check ran |
| **revoked-session JWT + unknown** `sk_` **key** | **200 forwarded, 1 hit, 0 session checks, the revoked JWT forwarded as sent; upstream 200 with the revoked session's principal** |
| bad-signature JWT + unknown `sk_` key | 200 forwarded, 1 hit; upstream 401 (the signature is still checked upstream) |

* **Controls that separate the mounts:** `/api/documents` (required) answers 401 to the unknown key and to revoked JWT + unknown key, 0 hits. `/api/certifications` answers 401 to both (its `requireScope` refuses a request with no principal). So the bypass is exactly the five optional mounts with no gate after `authenticateToken(false)`.
* **Billing:** the gateway rows match the table (revoked JWT + unknown key → 200, 1 hit, 0 session checks). The upstream replay does not apply (billing mounts `authenticate()` on `/billing`, not `/api`), so billing's upstream acceptance is READ, not measured.
* `/api/settings/notifications` **and** `/api/privacy/settings` (gateway-local, `admin.ts:1455` / `:1483`): 200 with no credential and 200 with any junk credential, so the key adds nothing there. One oddity: a revoked JWT alone is 401 while no credential at all is 200.
* **Not measured:** the running vc-issuer / referral / governance / nft-certificate / billing services (their real routes, DB and error handlers), the edge (nginx / Caddy) and demo. A live repro is owed before calling it exploited anywhere.
* **Evidence:** `5_Project_History/2026-09-17_seatA-4th/tickets/r4/`: `rows.json`, `rows-table.txt`, `probe-run.out`, and the probe itself (`zz-r4-probe.test.ts`, run once, then moved out of the worktree).

### Search before filing

`searchIssues` (includeArchived, includeComments), literal case-insensitive matches only: `SESSION_INVALIDATED` 109 fuzzy / 8 literal · `isSessionActive` 7 / 7 · `authenticateToken(false)` 80 / 8 · `optional auth` 94 / 1 (KS-719, archived: unauthenticated PUT on the two admin settings routes) · `session revocation` 106 / 11 · `unknown sk_` 104 / 0. Nearest: **KS-736** (In Review): the mount-auth check scores `authenticateToken(false)` as authenticated on these same six mounts. It is about the guard, and mentions neither `x-api-key` nor revocation. **KS-570** (archived) and **KS-257** (archived) are the same revocation-bypass class on other mounts. **KS-588** (Backlog) is revoked-session regression coverage for `/api/status`. None covers the API-key path pre-empting the Bearer check. Related: KS-1195, KS-736, KS-588 (KS-570 and KS-257 are archived, so they are named here, not related).

title: originate admin API-key mint writes no connector_id and an unclamped rate_limit: a key minted with rateLimit -1 answers 429 forever
description:
## BLUF

Originate's admin API-key mint (`adminConfigRouter.post('/api-keys')`, `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`) writes a key into `svc_api_keys` with **no** `connector_id` and a `rate_limit` **taken from the request body without the security service's clamps**: `${d.rateLimit || 1000}` at `adminConfig.ts:946`, window fixed at 3600. Now that the per-key limiter fires (KS-1195, merged as `d7e95cd9f`), the stored value is enforced: a key minted with `rateLimit: -1` answers **429 on every request**, forever. The security service's own create path clamps the same fields (`services/security/src/index.ts:569-570`: int 1..10000, window int 60..86400).

## Recommendation

Validate the admin mint's `rateLimit` with the security service's bounds (int 1..10000; reject anything else with 400), and decide whether this mint should take a `connectorId` at all or stay a connector-less path. Low priority: the input needs an admin, and after KS-1195's per-key bucket a connector-less key no longer shares an allowance with other tenants. Not built.

## Detail

**Source:** tier-1 QA gate round 1 on PR #1017, Record R-1 (report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1195-1017-cbe29597d-tier1-r1/report.md`, "Records" and item 7); carried STILL OPEN by round 2 (`…/2026-09-17-ks1195-1017r2-a067d4e3e-tier1-r2/report.md`: originate untouched). Lines re-read at develop `d7e95cd9f153e9036ed77935a73c93504fa6e3dc`.

**What the mint writes (READ,** `adminConfig.ts:918-952`**):** `id key_<uuid>`, `organization_id` (body or caller or null), `tenant_id` (the request's tenant, else a fixed default), `name`, `key_hash`, `key_prefix`, `scopes` (body `permissions` or `['read']`), `rate_limit = d.rateLimit || 1000`, `rate_limit_window = 3600`, `usage_count 0`, `is_active TRUE`, `expires_at`. No `connector_id` column in the INSERT, although `svc_api_keys.connector_id` exists (`migrations/018_svc_api_keys_reconcile.sql:79`).

**What the gateway limiter does with an allowance (MEASURED by the gate on the real app, round 1** `a4` **stage):**

* absent / null / 0 → limit 100 (the default).
* 1000 / 3600 → 1000. Schema min 1 → `[200, 429, …]`. Schema max 10000 / 86400 → 10000.
* **-1 → 429 on every request**, `Retry-After: 60`.
* 1.5 → one request allowed, header `X-RateLimit-Limit: 1.5`. The string `'2'` → 2.
* The string `'abc'` → never limited, header `X-RateLimit-Limit: abc`, Remaining `NaN`. `true` → one allowed, header `true`.

**Reach:** `d.rateLimit || 1000` turns 0 into 1000 but passes a negative number straight to the INTEGER column, so -1 is storable (READ). A non-integer or a string would be rejected or rounded by the column: NOT measured, and the gate's Not-Tested list names it. Only the round-1 `-1` row is shown reachable through this mint by READ; the string rows show what the limiter would do with such a value, not that this mint can store one.

**The missing** `connector_id`**:** every key this mint issues has no connectorId, so its gateway principal is `connector:api-key`. Before #1017's round 2 that made all such keys share one limiter bucket across tenants (F-1, now closed by bucketing per key). Whether any other connectorId-keyed gate treats these keys differently is not measured here; the count of real keys without a `connector_id` is also unmeasured (gate round 2, Not Tested item 3).

**Search before filing** (`searchIssues`, includeArchived, includeComments, literal case-insensitive matches only): `rateLimit || 1000` 64 fuzzy / 0 literal · `adminConfig` 33 / 33 (none about the key mint's `rate_limit` or `connector_id`; nearest KS-337, the revoke 500, archived) · `rate_limit` 92 / 27 (none about this mint) · `connector_id` 101 / 14 (KS-869 connectorId never persisted, KS-908, KS-889: all about the security service's own create path; none names originate or `adminConfig`, checked by text) · `api-keys` 86 / 11 (KS-33, KS-337, both archived). None covers this. Related: KS-1195, KS-869.
