title: Document row keeps the originating persona's email (createdOnBehalfOf.email) after platform-s has erased them
description:
## Found by

[PS-875](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-875/11-end-to-end-journey-and-docs-one-persona-acts-through-every-verb-the)'s `@k-live` chain half (platform-s PR #856, 2026-09-16), whose privacy assertion first read K's **document** row for an S-originated document and found:

```json
"createdOnBehalfOf": { "email": "firstone@lhsg.com", … }
```

This is the `onBehalfOf` platform-s sends on originate ([PS-746](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-746/ks-566-has-shipped-on-platform-k-develop-revert-the-ps-616-interim) / [KS-1016](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1016/test-anchor-read-honesty-hardcodes-docker-exec-secuura-postgres-fails) territory), stored on K's document record. The spec now reads the **anchor** record, which carries no email — so this is **not** a [PS-869](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-869/5-decision-the-on-chain-identity-record-did-level-source-and-verified) breach (nothing personal is on chain).

## Why it matters

Platform-s implements the right to erasure ([PS-382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-382/security-reachable-right-to-erasure-dsar-for-identitykyc-data), [PS-690](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-690/adopt-org-owned-documents-ownership-model-for-single-vs-multi-user)): after `PersonGdprErasureService` runs, S holds no email for the person, and every S surface renders the actor from the immutable identity snapshot (DID, level, source) only. K's document row is a second, off-chain place the persona's email persists, outside S's erasure and outside K's anchoring rule. Anyone with the K account's read scope on the document sees it.

## Suggested work

1. Decide whether `createdOnBehalfOf.email` is needed on the document row at all, or whether the S-side `actorDid` / the K account id suffices (S already sends the [PS-869](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-869/5-decision-the-on-chain-identity-record-did-level-source-and-verified) `identity` block once [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) lands).
2. If it stays: give K an erasure hook S can call (or a scheduled sweep S can trigger) that blanks `createdOnBehalfOf.email` for a given email/DID, and have S's `PersonGdprErasureService` call it (a PS follow-up).
3. Either way, note it in K's data-retention statement.

## Acceptance

* An S-erased persona's email no longer resolves anywhere on K's document read API.
* platform-s's `identity_status_chain.spec.ts` can extend its no-`@` assertion from the anchor record to the document row.

title: v1 verify family refused for cookie-bearing callers in production (versioning redirect runs after CSRF) while v2 passes
description:
## BLUF

In `NODE_ENV=production`, a cookie-bearing browser caller that sends no `X-XSRF-TOKEN` gets through on the v2 verify family but is refused on v1. The v1 call is redirected 307 to `/api/v1/verification/verify` by `versioning.ts`, which is production-only and mounted AFTER CSRF. The re-POST then meets `403 CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING`, because `/api/v1/` is not in `excludedPaths`. Pre-existing on the v1 side. PR #1001 (part of KS-1165) exempted v2, which turned "both refused" into "different" in production.

## Recommendation

Owner decision on the intended behaviour, then one of these:

* exempt the v1 verify family under its `/api/v1/verification/verify` spelling too;
* run the versioning redirect before CSRF;
* publish the difference in the spec if it is intended.

Pin the choice with a production-import cell (`NODE_ENV=production`).

## Detail

Found by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #1001 (KS-1165) at `3925d4c072b940eb91de462b7b92eabfe8889c75`, 2026-09-16. Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-16-ks1165-1001-3925d4c07-tier1-r1/report.md`, section 7, F-2. The measurement, verbatim:

**F-2 — In NODE_ENV=production the v1 and v2 verify families diverge for cookie-bearing, header-less callers**

* Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME on a TRUE production import, replicated twice, plus the base-csrf run.
* Severity: **Minor**.
* Target: **TICKET** (pre-existing v1 routing/exemption interplay), noted against **KS-1165 DoD box 1**.
* SHIPS-WITH.
* Oracle: **P**roduct consistency (`csrf.ts:90-97` says the v1 verify family is exempt, but in production the redirected path is not). Also the PR title's claim "as v1's are", and box 1's "or the difference is published in the spec" (it is not).
* At head in production, cookie + allowed Origin + no X-XSRF-TOKEN:
  * `POST /api/v2/verification/verify` → **200** upstream (PT-1).
  * `POST /api/verification/verify` → **307 Location** `/api/v1/verification/verify` (PT-5; `versioning.ts:45-58` is production-only and mounted at `index.ts:530`, AFTER CSRF).
  * The re-POST the browser makes → **403** `CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING` (PT-6; `/api/v1/` is not in `excludedPaths`, as in M17).
* Controls:
  * PT-7: the same v1 alias with no cookie → 200.
  * PH-6 (hybrid): a valid double-submit token → 200.
  * Development PH-1: v1 → 200 with no redirect.
* At base in production, **both** families refuse this caller (v2 403: PT-1 red at base-csrf; v1 307→403 unchanged). So #1001 turns "same (both refused)" into "different" in production. Outside production they are the same at head (M1 = M3 = 200).
* Likelihood (READ ONLY; no browser):
  * The verifier portal calls `${VITE_API_URL || '/api'}/verification/verify` via `safeFetch`, which sends `credentials:'include'`, echoes `X-XSRF-TOKEN` when `document.cookie` holds it, and retries once on 403.
  * A same-site portal therefore probably passes on v1.
  * The refused shape is a cookie-holding caller that does not echo the header (cross-site cookie jar, or plain `fetch` with credentials), which is the caller class KS-1165 exists for, but on v1.
* Fix-shape (prose): exempt the v1 verify family under its `/api/v1/` spelling too, or run the versioning redirect before CSRF. The owner decides and publishes the difference if it is intended.

Not measured (report section 10): v1 `verify-file` in production (the 307 → alias path for octet-stream). F-2 is stated for `/verify` only.

Relation: KS-1165 DoD box 1 ("the v1 / v2 verify families behave the same for cookie-bearing callers, or the difference is published in the spec") is PARTIAL because of this. KS-1165's remaining close depends on this ticket existing plus its F-1 follow-up PR.

Dedupe before filing (seat A, 2026-09-16): literal matches over Linear `searchIssues` (archived and comments included), title + description + comments:

* `versioning.ts`: 0 of 117 results;
* `CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING`: 11 of 90 (KS-1165, KS-119, KS-188, KS-35, KS-428, KS-430, KS-46, KS-781, KS-798, KS-799, KS-841), none about the production versioning redirect running after CSRF;
* `/api/v1/verification`: 0 of 95;
* "versioning redirect": 0 of 113.
  Filed new.

title: api-gateway: connector-key principals (verificationLevel 'api_key') fail meetsVerificationLevel against 'none' — every Platform-S originate 403s once the doc-type catalogue is seeded
description:
**BLUF:** `meetsVerificationLevel('api_key', 'none')` **returns false because** `'api_key'` **is not in** `VERIFICATION_LEVEL_ORDER` **(**`indexOf` **→ -1, and** `-1 >= 0` **is false). So once the document-type catalogue is seeded, every** `POST /api/documents` **from a Platform-S connector key is refused with** `INSUFFICIENT_VERIFICATION_LEVEL` **— even though** [KS-388](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388/k-freeze-documenttype-as-a-strict-enum-originate-flat-anchor-metadata) **seeded** `SSD_DOCUMENT` **as "deliberately friction-free" with** `creatorVerificationLevel: 'none'`**. Fix is a few lines in** `services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts`**; this is the K-side root cause of** [PS-519](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-519/originate-403s-under-connector-keys-k-wants-a-verification-level-api).

## Symptom

Platform-S app log, on every upload under a connector key (135–142 occurrences per full S suite run):

```
CardanoAnchor: originate POST status=403 body={"success":false,"error":{
  "code":"INSUFFICIENT_VERIFICATION_LEVEL",
  "message":"This document type requires NONE verification. Your current level is API_KEY."}}
```

S then falls back to flat `/api/anchors`, which succeeds — so the anchor badge goes green but **no K document exists**: no content-hash resolution for `/api/verification/verify`, no lineage root, no lifecycle events. S's `@k-live` suite fails 11/14 on this alone.

Reproduced 2026-09-16 on Peter's Mac, slot 4 pair: platform-k `0b25f823f` (develop, fresh worktree, fresh volumes) ↔ platform-s `2fa69634` and again `d36ff71e` (develop). Two full S suite runs, 12 failures each, 11 of them this.

## Builds under test

| Platform | Branch | Commit (full SHA) | Slot |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| platform-k | `develop` | `0b25f823f6660ac52b665f14055799ff0c3b616d` | 4 — gateway `:7182`, `secuura_slot4`, fresh worktree + fresh volumes |
| platform-s (run 1) | `develop` | `2fa696340967313fef214bfe1232f17a69cec410` | 4 — `https://localhost:5422`, `ssd-slot4` |
| platform-s (run 2) | `develop` | `d36ff71e5d347089c5cff08a0892bd8cb0e45385` | 4 — same slot, `--rebuild --reset`; `/Health/Data` `build.Commit` matched |

## Cause

`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts`

* `:39` `VERIFICATION_LEVEL_ORDER = ['none','basic','social','standard','enhanced','high','government']`
* `:53-57` `meetsVerificationLevel(userLevel, requiredLevel)` = `ORDER.indexOf(user) >= ORDER.indexOf(required)`
* `middleware/auth.ts:276` sets `verificationLevel: 'api_key'` on every connector-key principal.

`'api_key'` is not in the order → `indexOf` = `-1` → `-1 >= 0` is false → a connector key fails even `none`. Any other unknown level string fails the same way.

The check is only reached when `resolveDocumentType` finds the type. On an unseeded K it returns null and `:110-127` (the [KS-388](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388/k-freeze-documenttype-as-a-strict-enum-originate-flat-anchor-metadata) fallback) passes through — which is why the failure appears and disappears between rebuilds, and why [PS-519](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-519/originate-403s-under-connector-keys-k-wants-a-verification-level-api) saw the suite "green 2h earlier against the previous K". `routes/admin.ts:283-303` seeds `SSD_DOCUMENT` with `creatorVerificationLevel: 'none'` and says why: *"deliberately friction-free … gating either would break those paths."* The ordering bug defeats that intent. Confirmed on the live K: `GET /api/document-types` lists `SSD_DOCUMENT`, `creatorVerificationLevel: none`.

## Fix (either; the first is narrower)

1. In `meetsVerificationLevel`, an unknown `userLevel` satisfies `requiredLevel === 'none'` only — treat `indexOf === -1` as index 0 when the requirement is `none`, and still refuse any higher requirement, so a connector key cannot originate a `STANDARD`-gated type by accident.
2. Or place `'api_key'` explicitly in the order — but where a machine credential ranks against human KYC levels is a product decision, not a bug fix.

Either way the message should stop rendering `NONE` as harder to meet than `API_KEY`.

## Verification

* Unit: `meetsVerificationLevel('api_key','none') === true`; `meetsVerificationLevel('api_key','standard') === false`; an arbitrary unknown string behaves the same as `'api_key'`.
* Live: S upload under a connector key against a **seeded** K → originate `201`; S `@k-live` `chain_match.spec.ts` green; `POST /api/verification/verify` resolves the document by content hash.

## Related

* [PS-519](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-519/originate-403s-under-connector-keys-k-wants-a-verification-level-api) — the S side (surface K's `error.code` instead of the "revoked or wrongly scoped" guess); its open question "deliberate tightening or seed drift?" is answered here: neither.
* [KS-388](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388/k-freeze-documenttype-as-a-strict-enum-originate-flat-anchor-metadata) — the catalogue seed that arms the check.

title: Anchor / originate / lifecycle-event schemas: accept and anchor platform-s's non-PII actor + organisation identity fields (actorDid, actorLevel, actorSource, actorVerified, orgDid, orgTrust, orgVerified) beside identityCommitment
description:
## What platform-s needs

Follow-on to [KS-721](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-721/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-opaque-identitycommitment) (which accepted `metadata.identityCommitment`). Platform-S now needs the Cardano record to **show** who acted and at what identity level, for the actor and their organisation — readable, not only committed. The S-side ruling on what is allowed in clear is [PS-869](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-869/5-decision-the-on-chain-identity-record-did-level-source-and-verified) (decision) under epic [PS-864](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-864/epic-id-status-stored-and-shown-throughout-the-system-actor-and); the field list there is the contract:

| Field | Type | Pattern / values |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `actorDid` | string ≤ 512 | `^did:(key|web):[A-Za-z0-9._:%-]+$` |
| `actorLevel` | integer | `1`, `2`, `3` — NIST 800-63A IAL alignment |
| `actorSource` | string | `platform` | `stripe` | `entra-verified-id` |
| `actorVerified` | boolean |  |
| `orgDid` | string ≤ 512 | as `actorDid` |
| `orgTrust` | string | `unverified` | `domain` | `document` | `kyc` | `government` |
| `orgVerified` | boolean |  |
| `identityCommitment` | string ≤ 128 | already accepted ([KS-721](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-721/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-opaque-identitycommitment)); the `vN` will move to `v2` |

All optional; all non-PII (DIDs are pseudonymous, levels and sources are enumerations, no dates, no names, no emails). Consistent with [KS-240](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-240/strict-by-default-on-chain-minimisation-strip-issuername-any-human) — no free text, nothing recoverable to a natural person.

## Suggested work

1. Accept the block as `metadata.identity` (or flat under `metadata` — say which) on **every** endpoint S anchors through: `POST /api/anchors`, `POST /api/documents` (originate), `POST /{id}/version`, `POST /{id}/anchor`, `POST /{id}/share`, `POST /{id}/transfer-custody`, `POST /api/certifications/issue`, `POST /{id}/lifecycle-events`. Today `anchorSchema.ts` strips unknown keys, so S will not send until K is live (the [PS-612](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-612/rename-the-certify-verb-to-declare-across-s) ordering).
2. Carry it into the on-chain record beside `documentType` / `occurredAt` / `identityCommitment`.
3. Return it in provenance / verify / anchor-status responses so S can render "on chain: Level 2, entra-verified-id" beside its local snapshot and flag any mismatch.
4. **State which existing request fields reach Cardano metadata**: `holderEmail`, `recipients[].email`, `newHolderEmail`, `onBehalfOf.email` / `displayName`. S sends these today; the requirement is that no PII is stored on the blockchain. If any of them is written to chain metadata, file the defect and link it here.
5. OpenAPI spec + Schemathesis / Akto examples updated in the same PR ([KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage) pattern), and both K-side testing HTML docs.

## Ordering

**K deploys first**, then PS-870 adds the fields on the S request. Pair-test from S against K on paired slots (S slot N ↔ K slot N) and quote the counts.

title: api-gateway collapses every API-key failure into 401 'Invalid API key' — forward the security validate reason as a distinct code, and answer 503 when the security service is unavailable
description:
## BLUF

**A Platform S connector cannot tell a dead key from an unavailable security service.** The api-gateway collapses every API-key failure — revoked, expired, unknown, security-service 5xx, security-service unreachable, non-JSON reply — into one response: `401 {code:'UNAUTHORIZED', message:'Invalid API key'}`. The security service's own `reason` is computed and then discarded.

Platform S is building a `KeyInvalid` state (PS-740) so a rotated-away key is *seen* rather than reported as an anchor backlog. Because of this collapse it has to be built as a persistence heuristic (two refusals ≥ 60 s apart) rather than a definitive classification, and it can never be made exact without a change here.

## Measured on `develop` @ `48e65c43` (2026-09-15)

**Security computes the reason** — `services/security/src/index.ts`, `POST /api/keys/validate`, all HTTP 200:

| line | condition | response |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `:1314-1316` | hash miss in `memApiKeys` and DB fallback empty **or thrown** | `{ valid:false, reason:'Key not found' }` |
| `:1318-1320` | `!apiKey.isActive` | `{ valid:false, reason:'Key revoked' }` |
| `:1322-1324` | `expiresAt < now` | `{ valid:false, reason:'Key expired' }` |

**The gateway throws it away** — `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts`:

| line | what happens |
| -- | -- |
| `:219` | security non-2xx → `null`, negative-cached 30 s |
| `:225` | `if (!data?.valid) → null` — `reason` **is never read** |
| `:240` | fetch throws (unreachable, DNS, reset, hang — `:214` has no timeout/AbortSignal) → `null` |
| `:265` | every `null` → `401 { code:'UNAUTHORIZED', message:'Invalid API key' }` |

So `'Key revoked'`, `'Key expired'`, `'Key not found'`, a security 500, and a security outage are **byte-identical to the caller**. A second transport-shaped 401 exists too: when the connector-bearer exchange fails (`:179-203`) the request goes downstream with no Bearer and answers `401 'No token provided'`.

Also: `:1309-1311` swallows a DB error in the validate fallback and reports `'Key not found'` — a cache-miss during a DB outage reads as an unknown key.

## Ask

1. **Forward the reason as a distinct error code** at `auth.ts:265`: `API_KEY_REVOKED`, `API_KEY_EXPIRED`, `API_KEY_NOT_FOUND` (the `ErrorResponse` schema's `code` enum would gain three values). Status can stay 401.
2. **Answer 503** `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`**, not 401, when the security service is unreachable or errors** (`:219`, `:240`) — that is the platform's own fault, not the caller's credential, and it must not be negative-cached as if it were.
3. Give the validate fetch at `:214` a timeout.
4. (Docs) `docs/S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md` §5 still says a rotate leaves the *"old key untouched"* and tells the admin to revoke by hand — stale since KS-577 (#880) retires prior keys as part of the mint. The OpenAPI 401 prose (32× "Missing or invalid Bearer token") documents no API-key body at all; the three strings above appear nowhere in the spec.

## Why it matters to the S↔K re-key cluster

KS-577 is merged with instant revoke by default, and KS-889's 39-key re-mint and KS-576's bulk re-key are waiting on S being able to survive a rotation. S's side of that (PS-740) lands as a heuristic because of this ticket; with (1) and (2) it becomes exact and the heuristic is deleted. Until then, a security-service outage on K will look to S like every connector key dying at once — and S's design deliberately keeps presenting the key so that false positive costs nothing, but it is still a lie on the dashboard.

Filed from PS-740's planning pass. Cited in prose, no `Refs` trailer.

title: Flow verbs: add `note`, `certified` and `verified` to the lifecycle vocabulary (platform-s Flow project)
description:
Raised from the platform-s **Flow** project ([PS-833](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-833/flow-01-design-note-and-the-decisions-the-framework-depends-on), decision 3, confirmed by Stuart 2026-09-15). S needs three new lifecycle verbs that K does not accept today. **K ships first**, exactly as [KS-661](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-661/rename-the-certify-lifecycle-verb-to-declare) → [PS-612](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-612/rename-the-certify-verb-to-declare-across-s) did: an out-of-vocabulary verb is rejected with 400 and the whole anchor fails ([PS-499](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-499/s-can-emit-three-verbs-platform-k-rejects-protect-unprotect-restore)), so S will not emit any of these until K's vocabulary and OpenAPI list them. [PS-836](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-836/flow-04-the-note-operation-a-users-note-on-a-document-recorded-on-the) and [PS-837](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-837/flow-05-flow-completion-chain-events-certified-verified-with-non-pii) on the S side are blocked on this ticket.

## The three verbs

Classified on the vocabulary's three axes (mutates bytes / on-chain / composable), in `docs/VOCABULARY.md` terms.

| Verb | Meaning | Mutates? | On-chain? | Composable? | S route to K |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `note` | A user attached a note to a document (text-only; a visible mark is a separate `watermark` row). The note **text stays on S** — nothing identifying or free-text crosses to K. | no (`contentHash` = current tip) | yes | yes | `POST /api/documents/{id}/lifecycle-events` (needs adding to `LIFECYCLE_EVENT_ACTIONS` as well as `LIFECYCLE_VERBS`) |
| `certified` | The **Certify flow completed** on this document: every required declaration was made and the organisation's signature applied. Written once per flow instance, after the constituent `declare` and `sign` events. | no | yes | yes (one per completed flow) | `/lifecycle-events` (or flat anchor) |
| `verified` | The **Verify flow completed**: the verifying organisation's required verifier(s) confirmed the declarers, the certifier and the document integrity. Written once per flow instance. **This is not the S-local** `verify` **read** ([PS-627](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-627/shared-with-me-cannot-show-that-a-recipient-verified-a-document)), which stays local-only and is never sent to K. | no | yes | yes | `/lifecycle-events` (or flat anchor) |

## What the completion events carry

Only the standard anchor body plus **actor identity as DID / verifiable-credential references** ([PS-833](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-833/flow-01-design-note-and-the-decisions-the-framework-depends-on) decision 4). No names, emails or positions — those stay in S's encrypted local payload, consistent with the certification `data` blob rule and [PS-627](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-627/shared-with-me-cannot-show-that-a-recipient-verified-a-document). Please say if K wants a specific field name for a list of credential references on a lifecycle event, or whether it should ride the existing allow-listed payload keys.

## Question for K: cross-organisation anchoring for `verified`

The Verify flow is run by a **different organisation** from the one that registered and certified the document (the recipient verifies what the certifier sent). S would therefore anchor a `verified` event **against the certifier's K document id, with the verifying organisation as the issuer org**. Is that acceptable to K's ownership model ([PS-319](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-319/sk-consistent-organisationuser-ownership-dr-credential-reconciliation) / [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) work), or does K expect the verifier org to anchor against a K document it owns (e.g. a copy registered by the verifier)? The answer determines how S builds [PS-845](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-845/flow-22-multiple-verifiers-the-verification-record-and-the-verified).

## Where the vocabulary lives

* K: `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts` — `LIFECYCLE_VERBS` (`:18`), `LIFECYCLE_EVENT_ACTIONS`, and the generated OpenAPI (`anchoring.openapi.ts`).
* S mirrors: `ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.cs` `PlatformKAnchorVerbs`, `tests/ssd.UnitTests/AnchorDocumentTypeTests.cs` (holds K's list verbatim — the drift test), `systemTest/utils/k_verb_matrix.ts`.

## Sequencing

1. This ticket lands and deploys on K (Kintsugi for dev-ps, demo-pk for uat-ps).
2. S switches on emission in [PS-836](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-836/flow-04-the-note-operation-a-users-note-on-a-document-recorded-on-the) / [PS-837](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-837/flow-05-flow-completion-chain-events-certified-verified-with-non-pii) and updates its drift tests to the new list.
3. Until then S's design note (`docs/flow-design.md`, [PS-833](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-833/flow-01-design-note-and-the-decisions-the-framework-depends-on)) lists the verbs as *planned*.

Related: [PS-833](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-833/flow-01-design-note-and-the-decisions-the-framework-depends-on) (design note and decisions), [PS-836](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-836/flow-04-the-note-operation-a-users-note-on-a-document-recorded-on-the) (`note` on S), [PS-837](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-837/flow-05-flow-completion-chain-events-certified-verified-with-non-pii) (`certified` / `verified` on S), [PS-845](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-845/flow-22-multiple-verifiers-the-verification-record-and-the-verified) (the cross-org question's consumer).

title: Add `note` and `verified` to the lifecycle vocabulary (LIFECYCLE_VERBS + LIFECYCLE_EVENT_ACTIONS) — S needs both for the Note feature and the Flow project
description:
Requested by Stuart 2026-09-15. **Vocabulary addition only** — two new verbs, no endpoint or storage change. Same shape as [KS-556](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-556/add-protectunprotectrestore-to-the-ks-134-lifecycle-verb-vocabulary) (`protect` / `unprotect` / `restore`, commit `d005344b6`), which is the template: six files, spec regenerated, gateway rebuilt.

Platform S is building two things that emit verbs K does not accept today:

| Verb | What it records | S ticket |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `note` | A user attached a short plain-text note (≤ 256 chars) to a document. Non-mutating: bytes unchanged, `ContentHash` = chain tip. The **text stays on S**; the lifecycle payload carries only `noteSha256` and `noteLength` (a content commitment, never the text — K's `payload` column is outside erasure). | [PS-857](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-857/note-add-a-plain-text-note-256-chars-to-any-document-recorded-on-the) (Feature/Bug Resolution) and [PS-836](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-836/flow-04-the-note-operation-a-users-note-on-a-document-recorded-on-the) (Flow 0.4) |
| `verified` | The completion event of the Verify **flow**: every required verifier has completed. Org-level, anchored, distinct from [PS-627](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-627/shared-with-me-cannot-show-that-a-recipient-verified-a-document)'s local-only `verify` (a recipient's read, never sent to K). Carries verifier identities as DID / credential references only. | [PS-837](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-837/flow-05-flow-completion-chain-events-certified-verified-with-non-pii) (Flow 0.5), [PS-845](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-845/flow-22-multiple-verifiers-the-verification-record-and-the-verified) |

[PS-833](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-833/flow-01-design-note-and-the-decisions-the-framework-depends-on) (Flow 0.1, decision 3) also names `certified` as the Certify flow's completion verb. It is **not** in this request — Stuart asked for `note` and `verified` — but if it is cheaper to take all three in one change, say so on this ticket and it can be widened before you start.

## Shape

1. `services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts` — add `note` and `verified` to `LIFECYCLE_VERBS` (the flat-anchor `metadata.documentType` enum). `TRANSITIONAL_LIFECYCLE_VERBS` untouched.
2. `services/originate/src/lifecycleActions.ts` — add both to `LIFECYCLE_EVENT_ACTIONS` so `POST /api/documents/{id}/lifecycle-events` accepts them (S routes every non-mutating verb there when `UsePerVerbEndpoints` is on; flat `/api/anchors` when it is off — both paths need the word).
3. Pinning tests: `services/anchoring/src/__tests__/anchorSchema.test.ts` (sorted literal list) and `services/originate/src/__tests__/lifecycleEventRepo.test.ts`.
4. `docs/VOCABULARY.md` §2 and §3, `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` regenerated — S's [PS-614](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-614/check-ss-verb-vocabulary-against-platform-ks-openapi-enum-at-gate-time) gate reads the committed yaml, so the spec must carry the new enum members, and the demo/Kintsugi gateway image must be rebuilt (it bakes the yaml).

Nothing else: no new endpoint, no migration (`document_lifecycle_events.action` is `VARCHAR(50)` precisely so a vocabulary addition is a code change), no change to `payload` handling — `note` sends only scalar non-identifying keys.

## Ordering — K first, then S (the [PS-499](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-499/s-can-emit-three-verbs-platform-k-rejects-protect-unprotect-restore) rule)

An out-of-vocabulary verb 400s the **whole** anchor and S's refresher re-sends forever. So S ships `note` **now** on the [PS-499](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-499/s-can-emit-three-verbs-platform-k-rejects-protect-unprotect-restore) safe path (label omitted → the event anchors unlabelled; the per-verb router falls back to the flat anchor), and adopts the label + `/lifecycle-events` route only after this ticket is **deployed** to the environment S targets (dev-ps → Kintsugi, UAT → demo-pk). Please ping the S adoption sub-task ([PS-857](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-857/note-add-a-plain-text-note-256-chars-to-any-document-recorded-on-the)'s "Note 5", which this ticket blocks) on deploy, not on merge — exactly as [KS-661](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-661/rename-the-certify-lifecycle-verb-to-declare) → [PS-612](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-612/rename-the-certify-verb-to-declare-across-s) ran.

## Verification

* A `note` lifecycle event and a `note` flat anchor are accepted, anchored and readable; same for `verified`.
* An unknown verb is still rejected (widening must not weaken the guard).
* The regenerated spec lists both in `FlatAnchorRequest.metadata.documentType` and `LifecycleEventRequest.action`; S's `k_openapi_vocabulary` gate flips from 23 → 25 verbs and the adoption sub-task turns S's `inKVocabulary` flags for both.

## Evidence

* `services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts:18-63` — current 22-verb `LIFECYCLE_VERBS`; neither word present.
* `services/originate/src/lifecycleActions.ts:38-56` — current 13-verb `LIFECYCLE_EVENT_ACTIONS`.
* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:2372-2381` — the strict `includes(action)` → 400 with the accepted list.
* `note` already appears as a free-text response field name in `anchoring.openapi.ts:112` and `verified` as the verify-response boolean — unrelated to the verb enum, but worth knowing when reading diffs.

title: Guard 3's re-poll reads a MIXED window as ABSENT — one early "not found" then an unreachable chain still schedules a retry that can re-mint a written-ahead transaction (#805 tier-1 r3 residue)
description:
## BLUF

After #805 (KS-726) merged as `48e65c435` on 2026-09-15, `reconfirmKnownSubmission` treats a bounded re-poll as `'unknown'` **only when NO attempt reached the chain** (`polled === 0`). A window in which at least one attempt answered "not found" (a Blockfrost 404) and every remaining attempt THREW (5xx / 402 quota / DNS) still reads `'absent'`, guard 3 calls it a definitive rejection, and the ordinary retry mints a second fee-paying transaction for a document whose first — the hash just written ahead — may be on its way to a block. This is the same class as the F1 the merge closed (an unreachable chain read as absent), one neighbour over: the fix weights **whether** the chain ever answered, not **when**.

Measured by the tier-1 delta gate (round 3) at `a4d182bf9` and on the merged tree — report `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-15-ks726-805-a4d182bf9-tier1-r3/report.md` §5 (cells R3a/b/c, R3b-2nd): with the answer early / middle / late in a 3-attempt window, `polled 1 / errored 2` each time → `'absent'` → `scheduleRetry` 1; R3b's second call minted TX_B (`minted [TX_B]`, `signedHashes [TX_A, TX_B]`, row `confirmed`/TX_B). Grade: **TICKET, ships-with** — the gate's, endorsed by the coordinator; filed by the merge seat as the ADDENDUM required.

## Why the early 404 is a likely FALSE negative in exactly the case that matters

The retry is wrong only when TX_A is in fact accepted while the node says "inputs spent" for it — a same-hash duplicate submit, the two-process race the module's NOT HANDLED list already names. In that premise TX_A entered the mempool seconds before the 400; Blockfrost's `/txs/{hash}` answers 404 until the tx is in a block **and** indexed; the production poll's first attempt lands \~10–12 s after the 400, the second \~15–17 s later, the third \~22 s later. So an early "not found" says little, and a rule that accepts any single answer as definitive is weakest at the start of the window — where a fresh transaction is most likely to be unindexed.

## Blast radius (round 2's units, the gate's reading)

Severity **HIGH** — a duplicate fee-paying transaction (\~181,825 lovelace) and an unrecorded on-chain anchor for the document (TX_B is a valid anchor; TX_A is the orphan; no data loss, no false "anchored" claim). Likelihood **LOW** — {a same-hash duplicate submit} ∧ {TX_A unindexed at every answered attempt} ∧ {the provider unreachable from the first unanswered attempt through attempt 30, \~27 min}. Blast radius one document per occurrence. The gate did not accept "rarer than F1": by its arithmetic the residue's outage-start window is of the same order as the closed case's; both hang on a long provider outage (or a 402 quota exhaustion, a sustained state that naturally arrives mid-poll) beginning within tens of seconds of a duplicate submit.

## Where it lives (at `48e65c435`)

* `services/anchoring/src/cardano/confirmation.ts` — `waitForConfirmation` reports `polled` / `errored` counts only; nothing says WHEN the last answer came.
* `services/anchoring/src/anchorSubmission.ts` — `reconfirmKnownSubmission`: the `confirmation.polled === 0` → `'unknown'` arm (after the `confirmed` return, before the `'absent'` return); guard 3's `refusedAndAbsent` reads `'absent'` as definitive.
* The shipped cells that pin today's rule: `__tests__/ks726-gate-f1-unreachable-chain.test.ts` — "a mixed window (throw, not found, throw) reads ABSENT … → retry" is a deliberate pin of the commissioned "any attempt" semantics and must be REWRITTEN, not deleted, by whoever changes the rule.

## Fix-shape (prose — the gate's, for the owner to weigh; not a committed artefact)

Have `waitForConfirmation` also report `lastAnsweredAttempt` (or the elapsed ms at the last answered attempt), and have `reconfirmKnownSubmission` treat `'absent'` as definitive **only when the last answer is late enough for a mempool transaction to be in an indexed block** — e.g. `polled >= 2`, or an answer ≥ 60 s after the 400 — else `'unknown'` (rest in `submitting` for the reconciler). Regression cells: (404, throw ×29) → `'unknown'`, `scheduleRetry` 0, the row rests; CONTROL (404 ×k spanning ≥ 60 s, then throws) → `'absent'` → retry; the existing all-404 and all-throw cells unchanged. **The cost to weigh:** a genuinely absent transaction whose late attempts threw would now rest \~24 h for the reconciler instead of retrying in \~15 s — the (c) ruling's own concern — so this is a design decision for the ticket owner, not a bug fix, which is why the builder did not make it under KS-726.

## Two smaller records the gate carries, stated here so they are not lost

* (8j) the `confirmed`-before-`polled === 0` ordering in `reconfirmKnownSubmission` is unpinned by any shipped cell; the cell to add if wanted: an injected `{ confirmed: true, polled: 0 }` → row `confirmed`, no `'unknown'` log.
* (8k) `getTransaction` returns `null` when no Blockfrost client is configured (`cardano/provider.ts`), which the `polled` counter reads as "the chain answered"; pre-existing, unreachable through the production submitter without a real 64-hex hash on the row.

## Symbol search before filing (the `issues` filter over title + description + comments, `includeArchived:true`, 1,160 issues; controls 1/0 as expected)

`reconfirmKnownSubmission` → 1 (KS-726 itself, the merge seat's own comments) · `lastAnsweredAttempt` → 0 · `mixed window` → 0 · `reads 'absent'` → 0 · `unreachable chain` → 1 (KS-671, the /health chain-path mechanism — different) · `polled` → 8 (KS-726's comments, wrap comments on the review parent, and KS-683's consumer re-poll — a different mechanism; the rest archived and unrelated). No open ticket owns this.

## Related

KS-726 (the parent finding; merged as `48e65c435`, PR #805) · the gate report above (§5, §7).

title: userRepo.ts: ILIKE search on encrypted PII columns can never match — :1017 and :1061 compare ciphertext to a pattern
description:
## BLUF

`services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` runs a text search over columns that hold ciphertext. `listUsersInner` (`:1017`) and `countUsersInner` (`:1061`) both push `(email ILIKE $n OR first_name ILIKE $n OR last_name ILIKE $n OR display_name ILIKE $n)` with the pattern `%<search>%`. Every one of those four columns is written through `encryptPiiCol` (`:832-840` — the `encryptedCols` map: `first_name`, `last_name`, `display_name`, `phone_number`, `email`, `mfa_secret`; `:671`, `:703-705`, `:712`, `:847`, `:856`), with AAD bound to the user id, so the stored value is a per-row ciphertext and an `ILIKE` over it answers a different question from the one asked: a search for a known user's name or address returns nothing, without an error, and looks like "no such user". It is the runtime form of the trap KS-968's schema comment now warns about at the column (`docker/init/01-schema.sql`, the `users.email` comment landed by PR #905): comparing ciphertext to a literal or a pattern never errors and never matches.

The file's own docblock at `:562-568` records the rule for equality — `getUserByEmail` moved to an HMAC lookup against `email_lookup_hash` "rather than LIKE/LOWER on the encrypted blob — the encrypted column is non-deterministic so direct equality doesn't work" — and the two search sites were left on the old shape. Measured and recorded by s232 on KS-968 (comment `1079a310`, 2026-09-14) while landing #905; filed by the merge seat s228 on Wednesday's ADDENDUM 2026-09-14 11:00:17Z. Board searched first — every KS issue incl. archived, titles + descriptions + comments: `ILIKE` 1 hit (KS-968's own comments), `userRepo.ts:1017` 1 (the same), `userRepo.ts:1061` 0, `searchUsers` 0, `listUsers` 2 (KS-968; KS-703 archived, a NUL-byte 500 — unrelated). No existing home.

## Where it hurts

* Any admin or tenant user-list with a `search` term (`listUsersInner` / `countUsersInner` are the search arm of the users listing; both take `search`, `role`, `tenantId`). The count and the page disagree with reality in the same direction, so the UI shows an empty, internally consistent result.
* Rows still holding legacy plaintext (the migration-window fallback the docblock describes) WOULD match — so the search "works" on exactly the rows that should not exist any more, and silently stops working as rows are backfilled. A test seeded with plaintext passes; production does not.

## Fix-shape (for the owner)

Pick one, and say which in the PR:

1. **Searchable-hash columns per searched field** — the `email_lookup_hash` pattern (`lookupHash(normalised)`) extended to `first_name` / `last_name` / `display_name`, with an exact-or-prefix match on the hash instead of a substring `ILIKE` (a substring search over a keyed hash is not possible; the product decision is whether prefix/exact search is enough).
2. **Resolve the search through the existing hash for email only** and drop the name columns from the predicate, documenting that the listing searches by exact email.
3. **Drop the search arm** and remove `search` from both signatures and their callers.

Whichever lands, the docblock at `:562-568` should name the search sites as covered.

## Regression cell

Seed one user through `createUser` (so the columns are ciphertext, not plaintext), then call `listUsersInner` with `search` = that user's display name (and separately the email) and assert the user is returned and `countUsersInner` reads 1; a control search for a name no user has reads 0. On develop today the first two assertions red (0 rows) — the cell is red-first by construction.

## Definition of done

- [ ] A search for a known, encrypted-at-rest user's name or email returns that user through both `listUsersInner` and `countUsersInner`, or the search arm is removed with its callers.
- [ ] The regression cell above green; the docblock at `:562-568` names the search sites.
- [ ] KS-968's schema comment stays true (the column is never compared to a literal or a pattern).

title: api-gateway CSRF excludedPaths carries no /api/v2/verification entry — the v2 verify paths are not excluded as v1's are
description:
## BLUF

`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/csrf.ts:82-98` `excludedPaths` lists `/api/verification/verify` (a `startsWith` match — its own comment says it covers `/verify`, `/verify-file`, `/verify-batch`) and has **0** `/api/v2/verification` entries. Outside `NODE_ENV=test` the mount order is `csrfMiddleware.protect` (`index.ts:389`) BEFORE `enforceJsonContentType` (`index.ts:397`), so a COOKIE-bearing browser caller of `POST /api/v2/verification/verify-file` (or the v2 `/verify` sibling) meets `403 CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING` before the content-type perimeter at `contentType.ts:135` — while the published operation says `security: []` (anonymous). Non-browser callers pass: no cookie (`csrf.ts:340`), or an `Authorization: Bearer` / `x-api-key` header (`csrf.ts:337`).

Pre-existing and unchanged by PR #813 (KS-791): `csrf.ts` is blob `1f16e2f89` at that PR's base M38 `0e78c7270` and at its head `7b6fb960d`. Recorded by the tier-1 QA gate on #813 as **Record 8a** (report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-14-ks791-813-7b6fb960d-tier1-r1/report.md` §8; READ ONLY — not measured live, the gate's harness mounts only `enforceJsonContentType` and the product skips CSRF under `NODE_ENV=test`). Filed by the merge seat s228 on Wednesday's ADDENDUM 2026-09-14 09:17:07Z. Board searched first — every KS issue incl. archived, titles + descriptions + comments: `excludedPaths` 3 hits (KS-428 archived, the inverted guard; KS-799 archived, the consent form; KS-801 live, the case-sensitivity class), `csrf.ts` 8 hits, `/api/v2/verification` 9 hits, `CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING` 10 hits — none about the v2 verify paths missing from the exclusion list.

## Severity and reach

Minor–Major depending on whether a browser page is meant to upload to v2 (usability of a public operation for one caller class); blast radius one operation family (`/api/v2/verification/verify`, `/verify-file`, and any v2 verify sibling). The v1 family is excluded and works for the same caller class — the asymmetry is the defect.

## Recommendation

Decide the intent first, then one of:

* add the v2 verify prefix to `excludedPaths` beside v1's (`/api/v2/verification/verify`, `startsWith`, same comment), or
* if v2 is meant to require the CSRF token for cookie callers, say so in the published spec (`security` on the v2 verify operations) so the contract and the gateway agree.

Either way one gateway cell: a cookie-only `POST /api/v2/verification/verify-file` with `application/octet-stream` through the real mount order (CSRF then content-type) — expecting 200-path (excluded) or 403 (documented), never the silent asymmetry; and a sibling cell proving the v1 path's behaviour is unchanged.

## Definition of done

- [ ] The v1 / v2 verify families behave the same for cookie-bearing callers, or the difference is published in the spec.
- [ ] One gateway cell pins the chosen behaviour through the real mount order; the existing `contentType.test.ts` cells stay green.
- [ ] KS-801's case-sensitivity class (`excludedPaths` is one of its four predicates) is cited, not re-filed.

title: gate/report.ts writeGateReport overwrites the input summary when --summary does not end in -summary.json
description:
## BLUF

`systemTest/performance/gate/report.ts:325` derives the gate-report path with `const reportPath = summaryPath.replace(/-summary\.json$/, '-gate-report.json');`. When the `--summary` path does not end in `-summary.json` the replace is a no-op, `reportPath === summaryPath`, and `:346` `fs.writeFileSync(reportPath, …)` **overwrites the raw k6 summary with the gate report** — silently, with the log line claiming success. The runner's own naming (`runner/cli.ts:209`, `run_dir.ts:300`) always ends `-summary.json`, so the default pipeline is safe; the exposure is the documented `--summary` override on either CLI (`runner/cli.ts:22`, `gate/cli.ts:15`) — the by-hand re-gate path — and the loss is of the run's only raw record.

Found by the tier-2 QA gate on PR #988 (KS-704) as **F-5, Major, develop-own**: `writeGateReport` is byte-identical at that PR's base M38 `0e78c7270` and head `8cb99a002`, so it is NOT #988's regression and was not a NO GO; it exists at M38 and on every later develop. Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-14-988-ks704-tier2-r1/report.md` §5 F-5 (evidence `cli_conv.out`, `p8`…). Filed by the merge seat s228 on Wednesday's ADDENDUM 2026-09-14 09:10:43Z. Board searched first by the symbol `writeGateReport` (0 hits), the path `gate/report.ts` (4 hits: KS-704 itself, KS-1066, KS-929, KS-971 — none about this overwrite), `summaryPath.replace` (0) and `-gate-report.json` (2 archived report mentions) — every KS issue incl. archived, titles + descriptions + comments.

## Repro (the gate's, verbatim in substance; measured at runtime, replicated ×3)

From a known state (`systemTest/performance` after `npm ci`):

1. `cp tests/unit/fixtures/smoke-summary.json <dir>/summary.json` (k6's own `--summary-export` default basename).
2. `npx tsx gate/cli.ts --scenario smoke --summary <dir>/summary.json`
3. Read `<dir>/summary.json`.

**Expected** (oracle: Purpose + Product — the function's docstring and the log line say it *writes the gate report beside the summary*; `runner/cli.ts:22` documents `--summary` as a free path): a new `…-gate-report.json`; the input untouched.

**Observed:** stdout `[ci-gate] Gate report written: <dir>/summary.json`; the file's keys become `scenario,slot,slotTag,gatewayPort,runLabel,timestamp,passed,results` — the `metrics` map is gone; sha256 `a8f5ed22…` → `86143afe…`. Reproduced on the breached copy, the healthy copy and a third fresh copy.

**Control:** the same file named `smoke-summary.json` → `smoke-gate-report.json` is written beside it and the input is intact.

## Reach

* The documented `--summary` override on either CLI (`runner/cli.ts:22`, `gate/cli.ts:15`) — the path a human uses when re-gating an old run by hand. The default runner pipeline never produces a non-conforming name.
* **Sibling of the same class (read only, not reproduced):** `runner/k6_docker.ts:241` `summaryMount.replace(/-summary\.json$/, '-k6.log')` — with the same non-conforming name the k6 log path collapses onto the summary mount.

## Fix-shape (for the owner)

* Derive `reportPath` from the directory + scenario: `path.join(path.dirname(summaryPath), scenario + '-gate-report.json')`, and/or throw when `reportPath === summaryPath`.
* Apply the same shape to the `k6_docker.ts:241` sibling.

## Regression cell

A unit cell that calls `writeGateReport(results, '<tmp>/summary.json', 'smoke')` and asserts (a) the input file's sha256 is unchanged and (b) a sibling `smoke-gate-report.json` exists beside it. A second cell for the `-summary.json` control keeps the existing behaviour pinned.

## Definition of done

- [ ] `writeGateReport` never writes to its input path; a non-conforming `--summary` name yields a sibling `<scenario>-gate-report.json` (or a thrown, named error).
- [ ] The `k6_docker.ts:241` sibling handled the same way or recorded as accepted with the reason.
- [ ] The two regression cells above green; the existing `tests/unit/gate/` cells and goldens unchanged.

## Follow-up (ruled by Wednesday 2026-09-14 10:11Z, from the #988 gate F-3)

* The `reportFailedGateBreakdown` cell (`systemTest/performance/tests/unit/gate/reportFailedGateBreakdown.test.ts:103-108`) builds its expectations with `String(n)` while the product prints `toLocaleString()` — they coincide only below 1,000; build the expectation with `toLocaleString()` or add one cell with a synthetic `{ http_server_error: { passes: 1234, fails: 0, value: 1 } }` expecting `passes=1,234` under a pinned locale.

title: start-secuura.sh never waits for five default-profile, healthchecked services — demo-service, mcp-server, pgbouncer, tenant-provisioning, tokenisation — "All 27 containers are healthy" can print while they are still booting
description:
## BLUF

`Start_Up/start-secuura.sh`'s health wait, `--status` report and timeout diagnostic all iterate `EXPECTED_SUFFIXES` — 27 names (the [KS-312](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-312/cut-midnight-zk-selective-disclosure-remove-service-privacy-ui) cut of the original list). The compose files declare **33** default-profile, long-running containers. Six are not on the list. One is `stack-marker` ([KS-666](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-666/prevent-destructive-rebuilds-of-the-shared-vm-stack-from-destroying) label carrier, correctly excluded). The other **five are real services with healthchecks and** `restart: unless-stopped` that the script has never waited for:

| service | healthcheck | in the wait list |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `demo-service` | yes | no |
| `mcp-server` | yes | no |
| `pgbouncer` | yes | **no** — and every service's `DATABASE_URL` goes through it |
| `tenant-provisioning` | yes | no |
| `tokenisation` | yes | no |

So `✓ All 27 containers are healthy` and `Containers: 27/27 running` can print while any of these is still starting or already `unhealthy`; the post-start checks that depend on them (anything through pgbouncer, tenant provisioning, tokenisation) then race the boot. Not new — measured the same on `develop` before [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s); [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) only made the list slot-correct and added the test that exposed the gap.

## How it was found

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/start_secuura_expected_services.test.sh` ([KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s), PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#959](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1096-derive-start-secuurashs-probe-names-and-dbredis-ports-from-the-7856c22cafff)) derives the set the script should wait for from the compose files — every `container_name: ${STACK_PREFIX:-secuura}-<svc>` (40) − `profiles:`-gated (5: cardano-mock, cardano-devnet, guardian, queue, ollama) − `restart: "no"` one-shots (2: migrations, demo-overlay) = 33 — and asserts equality with `EXPECTED_SUFFIXES`. To make that green without deciding platform-k base-code behaviour on Peter's ticket, the five above (plus `stack-marker`) sit in the test's `KNOWN_UNWAITED` list, each annotated "as above — script-behaviour call for Kamil". **This ticket is that call.**

## Decision needed (Kamil — platform-k base code)

Either:

1. **Wait for them.** Add the five suffixes to `EXPECTED_SUFFIXES` (`Start_Up/start-secuura.sh`, the `EXPECTED_SUFFIXES=(` block; the count comment says 27 → 32) and delete their five lines from `KNOWN_UNWAITED` in the test. The wait treats `health=none` as healthy, so a service without a healthcheck costs nothing; these five have one, so the wait becomes real. Or —
2. **Deliberately not wait**, per service, with the reason written next to it in `KNOWN_UNWAITED` (e.g. "demo-service is only reachable via a deleted gateway location, [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487/review-b-input-validation-injection-upload-xssssrf-and-crypto) B-6") — the test then keeps the exception honest, failing if the service is ever removed.

Red→green either way: the test is green now only because of the exceptions; removing a line from `KNOWN_UNWAITED` makes it red until the script waits for that service.

## Where

* `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` — `EXPECTED_SUFFIXES=(` block (27 entries).
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/start_secuura_expected_services.test.sh` — `KNOWN_UNWAITED` (6 entries).
* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` — the five services' `healthcheck:` blocks.

Live context: on the [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) slot-2/slot-4 runs the summary reads `33 running, 30–31 healthy` while the wait reported 27/27 — the gap is these services plus the two one-shots.

title: Three retired GitHub workflows bake slot-2/3/4 port literals (6982/7182/6732…) into CI env — a stack slot applied to a non-local build, typed per slot
description:
## BLUF

The CLAUDE.md Key Rules added under [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) (2026-09-14) make two things MUST: **a stack slot applies to a build on the developer's local host only**, and **every slot value is calculated from slot 1** (`base + 100*(N-1)`) in `stack_env.sh` / `slot-target.sh`, never typed per slot. Three GitHub workflow files break both — they hardcode slot-2/3/4 ports into CI job env and `with:` inputs:

| file | lines hitting | example |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml` | 37 | `GATEWAY_PORT: "6982"` … |
| `.github/workflows/nightly-platform-suites.yml` | 34 | header `offsets — schemathesis 6882 · playwright 6982 · perf 7082 · akto 7182`; `POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT: "6532"` |
| `.github/workflows/pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` | 14 | `GATEWAY_PORT: "7182"`, `POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT: "6732"`, `REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT: "6679"`, `TARGET_BASE: http://localhost:7182` |

Measured by `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/slot_is_local_host_only.test.sh` ([KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#959](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1096-derive-start-secuurashs-probe-names-and-dbredis-ports-from-the-7856c22cafff)): 85 hits across the three files; 0 in `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/`, the compose files, `docker/`, or any Dockerfile. All three workflows are **retired** — GitHub Actions is off for this repo (Kam, 2026-08-27); `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` is `workflow_dispatch`-only and `nightly-platform-suites.yml` has its `schedule:` commented out — so nothing runs today. They are exempted in that test's `KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS` against this ticket; **the exemption comes out when this closes.**

## Fix direction

Either:

1. **Derive, don't type.** One step per job sources `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh` with `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=N` and exports `GATEWAY_PORT`/`POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT`/`REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT` into `$GITHUB_ENV`; every literal goes. If CI genuinely needs parallel stacks, the slot is a job-level *input*, and the ports are still derived. Or —
2. **Delete the three dormant workflows.** Actions is retired and every retired job maps to a local runner in `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` §Manual CI-gate equivalents; dead YAML that contradicts a MUST rule is a liability. Needs Kam's nod.

Red→green: remove the three paths from `KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS` in `slot_is_local_host_only.test.sh`; the test is red before the fix and green after.

Found while adding that test under [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s).

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** point 4 — record the delete-or-derive decision here before [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default) closes, and whichever way it goes, the three paths leave `KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS` and the point-1 guard covers `.github/workflows/`.

title: redis healthcheck passes REDIS_PASSWORD as a `-a` argv — readable via `docker inspect` / `docker events` / `ps` by anyone on the host
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:228` defines the redis container's healthcheck as

```
test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "-a", "${REDIS_PASSWORD:-secuura_redis_dev}", "ping"]
```

Compose renders `${REDIS_PASSWORD}` into the container's **config** at create time, so the plaintext password is exposed on every surface that shows the healthcheck command: `docker inspect <redis>` (`.Config.Healthcheck.Test`), `docker events` (each `exec_create: redis-cli -a <password> ping`, every healthcheck interval), and `ps` inside the container while the probe runs. Any account that can talk to the Docker socket reads it without touching `.env`.

Work-stream **B** (crypto & secrets — [KS-487](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487>), Done 2026-09-14, so filed as a sibling rather than appended). Pre-existing; not introduced or changed by [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s).

## Measured — 2026-09-14, slot 4, Peter's Mac

Recording `docker events` for the [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) slot-4 deploy window (07:03–07:16 UTC, 431 events) captured the bootstrap-generated slot-4 `REDIS_PASSWORD` in clear, once per healthcheck tick, as the `exec_create` action string on `secuura-s4-redis`. The recording was deleted; no value is quoted here or in the PR/ticket. The same value is visible at any time via `docker inspect secuura-s4-redis --format '{{.Config.Healthcheck.Test}}'`.

## Why it matters

* Since [KS-731](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-731/local-slots-share-one-postgresredis-credential-pair-any-slot-can-read) the password is per-clone and generated, so a leak is no longer "the shared literal everyone knows" — it is the actual credential for that stack's Redis (sessions, rate-limit state, cache).
* Anyone reproducing a run with `docker events` / `docker inspect` in a log, a PR, or a support bundle ships the password with it. The `secuura-test-discipline` "never read a secrets file" rule is bypassed by a command that reads no file.
* The VM demo stack (`/home/secuura/secuura/Dev`) uses the same compose file, so the demo Redis password is exposed the same way to anyone with socket access there.

## Fix direction

Keep the password out of argv. Options, in order of preference:

1. `test: ["CMD-SHELL", "redis-cli ping"]` with `REDISCLI_AUTH` supplied via the service's `environment:` — `redis-cli` reads the password from `REDISCLI_AUTH` and it never appears in the command. (Environment is still readable via `docker inspect .Config.Env`, so pair with 2 if that surface matters.)
2. Mount the password as a file/secret and `test: ["CMD-SHELL", "REDISCLI_AUTH=$(cat /run/secrets/redis_password) redis-cli ping"]`.
3. Auth-less liveness: `redis-cli ping` unauthenticated answers `NOAUTH` when the server is up — the same signal `start-secuura.sh` already treats as "responding" ([KS-260](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-260/start-secuurash-verification-false-negatives-redis-noauth-counted-as)). Cheapest, and sufficient if the healthcheck only needs liveness.

Check whether `pgbouncer`/`postgres` healthchecks (`pg_isready -h localhost -p 6432`, no password — fine) or any other service put a credential on a command line: grep `docker-compose.yml` + `docker-compose.local.yml` for `-a `, `--password`, `PGPASSWORD=`, `:${…PASSWORD` inside `test:` / `command:` / `entrypoint:`.

**Red→green:** a static check (`check-stack-safety.sh` shape, or `check_slot_credentials.test.sh`) that greps rendered `docker compose config` for any `*PASSWORD*` value inside `healthcheck.test`, `command` or `entrypoint` — red on develop, green after; plus `docker inspect … .Config.Healthcheck.Test` on a running stack showing no credential.

## Where

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:228`
* Surfaces: `docker inspect` (Healthcheck.Test), `docker events` (exec_create), in-container `ps`.

Found during the [KS-1096](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1096/start-secuurashs-health-wait-status-and-dbredis-checks-probe-slot-1s) slot-4 verification ([Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#959](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1096-derive-start-secuurashs-probe-names-and-dbredis-ports-from-the-7856c22cafff)).

title: L3b gate record F-931-G1: the ks1061 shared-mock completeness guard is a text scanner — single-quoted jest.mock( only, non-recursive readdirSync, blind to jest.doMock and double quotes (F-931-G2 tsc-excludes-tests already homed at KS-1000 / KS-1090)
description:
## BLUF

The one Record from the L3b tier-2 gate on PR #931 (KS-1061, head `795307023` — GO WITH FINDINGS, no Blocker, no Major) with **no existing home**: **F-931-G1 (Minor, SHIPS-WITH — a class weakness of the new guard, not a regression).** Filed as ONE ticket on Wednesday's ADDENDUM 05:29:55Z. #931 landed as M37 `54e9b835d`. The gate's second finding, **F-931-G2**, already has a home and is NOT re-filed here (below).

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-14-ks1061-931-795307023-tier2-r1/report.md` (140 lines, 15:24 AEST; §4 extension probes T6a/T6b/T6c/T7, §5, §8).

**Search before filing (every KS issue incl. archived, 1,148 issues, title + description + comments, literal;** `5_Project_History/2026-09-14_s225/item10/symbol_search.log`**):** `makeSharedMock` → KS-1103 (archived) and KS-485 comments only; `sharedModuleMock` / `jest.doMock` / `ROOT_MOCK` → 0 outside KS-1061; `readdirSync` → KS-1082 / KS-899 / KS-917 (other walkers, not this guard). **No home for G1.** `tsconfig excludes` / `src/__tests__` → **KS-1000 (Backlog, live: "services/auth tsconfig EXCLUDES src/tests** — every 'tsc: 0 errors' …" — the class ticket the 2026-09-14 dedupe consolidated KS-848 / KS-892 / KS-933 / KS-1122 into) and KS-1090 (Backlog, live: "api-gateway + originate: tsc never type-checks #951's three wiring tests") — G2's homes. Controls: a known title hits 1, a nonsense term 0.

## F-931-G1 — the guard's blind spots (MEASURED by the gate, verbatim)

`services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1061-shared-mock-completeness.test.ts` (blob `05fdfa88d` at M37) is a text scanner whose `ROOT_MOCK` / `VIA_HELPER` regexes match only a **single-quoted** `jest.mock(` and whose `testFiles()` is **non-recursive**, while jest's `testMatch` (`**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts`) is recursive and no lint rule pins quote style (no prettier config, no `quotes` rule in `eslint.config.mjs`). Proven at HEAD by the gate's quarantined probes: a double-quoted factory (T6b), a `jest.doMock` factory (T6c), or a factory in `__tests__/sub/` (T7) each ships a partial `secuura/shared` mock (scope sigil omitted) with the guard green, while the ordinary shape (T6a) is caught. Oracle: Purpose — the ticket's stated goal is "forgetting an export is no longer possible", and the helper file's own doc says "every `jest.mock('secuura/shared', …) (the scoped package name, sigil omitted here — 0 at-signs rule)`". Likelihood in operation: low (all 12 factories use the single-quoted top-level shape; the repo's convention is single quotes) — hence Minor.

**Fix-shape (the gate's, for the owner):** `ROOT_MOCK = /jest\.(mock|doMock)\(\s*['"]secuura\/shared['"]\s*,/g` and the same class in `VIA_HELPER`; walk the directory recursively (`fs.readdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` on Node ≥ 20, filtering `.test.ts`). **Regression cells:** the T6b / T6c / T7 fixtures from the gate's `evidence/quarantine_zz-gate931-*.test.ts` as files the guard must name (red-first: each one green under the current guard; red under the widened one until it is named).

## F-931-G2 — indexed, not filed here (Record, no action per the gate)

`tsc --noEmit -p services/originate` is cited on PR #931 as evidence for a tests-only PR, but `originate/tsconfig.json` excludes `src/__tests__` and `src/**/*.test.ts` — `--listFilesOnly` shows 0 test files in that program, so the command type-checks none of the 14 files. The gap is covered in practice by ts-jest's per-file diagnostics (the gate demonstrated `TS2304` with `Tests: 0 total` on a broken file) and by the gate's inclusive pass (a temp tsconfig with `include: ["src/**/*"]`, 62 test files, rc 0; a planted `TS2322` fires). Worth one line in the READY template: "tsc excludes tests; ts-jest is the type gate for `__tests__`". **Home: KS-1000 (the class) / KS-1090 (originate + api-gateway instance)** — related from this ticket so the index reads both ways.

## Definition of done

One test pass (Kam's 2026-09-07 rule): the widened `ROOT_MOCK` / `VIA_HELPER` regex class + the recursive walk, with the three probe fixtures as named cells (red-first each), the existing 3 cells still green, whole originate green. G2 closes with KS-1000 / KS-1090.

**Related:** KS-1061 (#931, M37 — the guard's own ticket), KS-487 (the L3b review stream parent, #720), KS-1000 (G2's home). **Named, no relation (archived):** KS-1103 (the ks1103 fold), KS-764 (the ks764 fold), KS-862 (the stale-mock red that motivated the guard, Duplicate).

Filed by the merge seat s225 on 2026-09-14 after #931's squash (M37), before KS-1061's archive, so KS-1061's closing comment can name it.

title: L3a gate records (#912 r2 / #937): the placeholder-hash anchoredAt carry keys on string truthiness not authoritativeTxHash(), the network carry has one pin, stale line references in the ks1059 / ks1058 test headers
description:

The three Records with NO existing home from the L3a tier-1 round-2 gate (PR #912 r2, KS-1004, head `609c44c55` — GO WITH FINDINGS, zero findings against the diff; PR #937, KS-1059, head `6fd3a8bec` — GO), filed as ONE ticket on Wednesday's ADDENDUM 05:10:18Z so each is searchable by symbol/path and none is rediscovered as new. **None is a finding against either PR.** #912 r2 landed as M35 `be83eacd7`, #937 as M36 `7d1fccfcc`.

title: Add an OAuth marker to sessions minted by the OAuth grants (so a future deploy-step denylist can be selective) — the current forward-only window is accepted (Kam 14:53)
description:
## BLUF

**Kam ruled 2026-09-14 14:53 AEST (via Wednesday, ADDENDUM 04:53:30Z): (B) marker-only — add the OAuth session marker now; the current forward-only launder window is ACCEPTED, no deploy-time cutoff.** This supersedes his 14:45 ruling `denylist-at-deploy` (ADDENDUM 04:46:19Z), which this ticket was first filed under (title then: "Deploy step: denylist every OAuth refresh jti minted before #983/#984 (the forward-only launder window)", High) — rescoped after the merge seat measured that the pre-fix jtis are not enumerable (below). Priority Medium: no longer a deploy blocker. **The build is the next auth lane's; the deploy stays Kam's.**

**The accepted window, stated:** a refresh token minted at the OAuth grant BEFORE #983 (M31 `b9f541e6b`) / #984 (M32 `2c3315f37`) landed carries neither `client_id` nor `authMethod`, so #986's guard (`routes/auth.ts:677`, M33 `9864379e5`) cannot recognise it and it still launders at `POST /api/auth/refresh` until it expires. **Expiry mechanism:** the refresh JWT's own `exp` — `JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN`, default `'7d'` (`services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:44`, `env.example:107`) — so the window closes by itself at most 7 days after the deploy that carries M31–M33 (the last pre-fix mint is at that deploy). Population unmeasured (the AUTH4 gate, report §3.7). Accepted by Kam 14:53.

## What was measured (develop M34 `b42e260c9`, END tree `cf700ee32`, read verbs only, 2026-09-14 04:4x Z)

1. **The denylist exists and is jti-keyed:** `services/auth/src/services/refreshDenylist.ts:21` `refresh_denylist:${jti}` in Redis; `denylistRefreshJti(jti, ttlSeconds)` `:28` (`setex`; fail-loud `Refresh denylist requires Redis` `:34`); `isRefreshJtiDenylisted(jti)` `:46`. Readers `routes/auth.ts:693` and `routes/oauth.ts:1047`; writers `routes/auth.ts:718` (rotation) and `:762` (logout); 0 writers in `routes/oauth.ts` (= R-2 on KS-1150).
2. **A refresh token's jti is minted in memory and never persisted:** `jwt.ts:231` `jti: crypto.randomUUID()`; no `oauth_*` token table in `migrations/`; `refresh_tokens` (`001_initial-schema.sql`) is not written by the OAuth grants.
3. **No marker distinguishes an OAuth-minted session:** both OAuth grants call `createSession(user, req.ip, req.get('user-agent'), undefined, 'browser')` — the code grant at `routes/oauth.ts:965`, the refresh grant at `:1074`; the interactive logins pass `data.clientType ?? 'browser'` (`routes/auth.ts:284`, `:441`, `:590`) or `'browser'` (`:1247`, `wallet.ts:362`); `ClientType = 'browser' | 'native' | 'api'` (`services/session.ts:107`). The Redis `Session` (`sess:<id>`, `user_sessions:<userId>`) carries `clientType`, ip, user-agent, device, expiry, activity — nothing that says "minted by the OAuth grant", and no jti.
4. **Therefore a selective deploy-step denylist ("every pre-fix OAuth refresh jti, interactive untouched") had no enumerable target set** — the fact that turned 14:45 into 14:53.

## The work (one test pass proves it — Kam's 2026-09-07 rule)

* **Mark every session the OAuth grants create.** The builder's design; the two shapes the code already offers: (i) a new `ClientType` value (`'oauth'`) passed as `createSession`'s fifth argument at `routes/oauth.ts:965` and `:1074` — note the KS-43 cohort-aware eviction in `createSession` buckets by `clientType` (`session.ts:178–230`), so a new value needs its own eviction policy decided, not inherited by accident; or (ii) a dedicated field on `Session` (e.g. `mintedBy: 'oauth'` + the `client_id`), leaving `clientType` and the eviction cohorts untouched. Either way the marker is written at mint and readable on `getSession` / `getUserSessions` (`session.ts:256`, `:329`).
* **Make it queryable at deploy time:** a read that lists a user's OAuth-minted sessions (and, if a future cutoff is ever wanted, all of them — `user_sessions:<userId>` is per-user; a global enumeration needs a set of OAuth session ids or a SCAN, decided by the builder and stated).
* **Do NOT add a cutoff** — the window is accepted (14:53). The marker exists so that a FUTURE deploy-step denylist can be selective; it does nothing for tokens already in the wild, which is why the window is accepted rather than closed.
* **Test pass:** red-first at the parent (an OAuth-grant session carries no marker / `clientType 'browser'`) → green at head (the code grant's and the refresh grant's sessions carry the marker, read back through `getSession`); an interactive login's session carries no marker (control); the KS-43 eviction cohorts behave as decided for the new value (a cell per policy); `auth.integration` OAuth cells unchanged; the ks1151 / ks1150 / ks823 / ks835 suites unchanged.

## Search before filing (every KS issue incl. archived, 1,146 issues, title + description + comments, literal; `5_Project_History/2026-09-14_s225/item6/symbol_search.log`)

`denylistRefreshJti` → KS-1151 / KS-823 / KS-486 (archived), KS-485, KS-329 (PQ hybrid — other subject), **KS-756 (Backlog, live: "Wire up the opaque refresh token that** `createSession` **already mints" — a symbol neighbour, not this work; named, not related)**; `isRefreshJtiDenylisted` → KS-486 only; `JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN` → KS-1151 comments; `forward-only` → KS-1151 + KS-550 (unrelated); `denylist-at-deploy` → 0. No existing work item; KS-1156 §C carries the window as a record — this ticket is the work and links to it.

**Related:** KS-1150 (R-2: the OAuth refresh grant rotates/denylists nothing — the same denylist, the other route; open), KS-1156 (the AUTH4 records; §C the window). **Named, no relation (archived):** KS-1151 (#986, M33), KS-823 (#983, M31), KS-835 (#984, M32).

## Definition of done

The marker is on develop with the red-first / green / control cells above; `getSession` returns it; the KS-43 eviction policy for the new value is decided and tested; no cutoff added; the accepted window's end date (the M31–M33 deploy + `JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN`) written on this ticket by whoever deploys. KS-1156 §C and KS-1150 R-2 are not closed by this ticket.

Filed 2026-09-14 by the merge seat s225 on Wednesday's ADDENDUM 04:46:19Z (Kam 14:45); rescoped the same seat on ADDENDUM 04:53:30Z (Kam 14:53).

**Not this ticket:** R-2 / R-3 (the OAuth refresh grant rotates/denylists nothing; OPEN on KS-1150 — its own DoD) · H-wildcard (KS-839) · KS-1152 (L5 records) · KS-1153 (L7 records) · KS-1150's own #982 records.

## The records, each with its symbol/path

### A. From #984 r1/r2 (KS-835) — READ, open, UNEDITED at `06aafd51c` (report §2 c–d)

1. **H-limiter.** `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/rateLimitEnforce.ts:61` `MACHINE_AUTH_METHODS = new Set(['api_key','oauth_app'])` — nothing mints `'oauth_app'`; an OAuth-minted token now carries `authMethod: 'oauth'` (KS-835), so the machine-client limiter's label set and the mint's label do not meet. 3. **H-mounts "eight" is seven.** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts`: `requireScope(` ×6 (`:375 :394 :568 :575 :764 :770`) + `requireScopeOrRole(` ×1 (`:731`) = SEVEN scope-gated mounts. "eight" remains in the PR #984 body (2 hits), two KS-835 comments and the gateway test `ks835-oauth-token-scope-gate.test.ts:59` comment. Polish.
4. **H-wildcard** (`validateScopes`, `services/auth/src/services/oauth.ts:352` `if (allowed.includes('*')) return requested;`) — **home: KS-839**; listed here only so the AUTH4 index is complete.

### B. From #986 (KS-1151) — MEASURED, test-quality Polish against the PR's OWN tests, not the guard (report §3.5)

* **R-C1 (T5):** the shipped suite records `world.sessionLookups` (`:64`, `:82`) but no cell asserts it (30 `expect(` lines, 0 on `sessionLookups`) — the "before `getSession`" claim is pinned by the comment and the PR text, not by the suite. Described regression cell: C3 of `evidence/__qa1151_launder.test.ts` (assert `getSession` = 0 on the refusal). Tamper T5 (guard moved below `getSession`): the builder's 5 cells STAY GREEN; the gate's C3/C6/C7 go red.
* **R-C2 (T6/T7):** every OAuth fixture in the shipped file carries `client_id` (cells 1/2 both claims, cell 3 `client_id` only), so the `authMethod === 'oauth'` arm has NO earning cell — it can be dropped (T6) or case-broken (T7) and the suite stays green. Described regression cell: C7 (re-sign minus `client_id`, keep the label → 401).
* **R-C3 (Polish, message text):** the guard's 401 body is `InvalidCredentialsError`'s default `"Invalid email or password"` (C1/C2/C6/C7), while a garbage/access token reads `"Invalid token"` (C8). The route's other two `InvalidCredentialsError` sites (`:663` absent token, `:687` no session) say the same words, so it is the route's own idiom and `logger.warn` carries the reason for operators — but an integrator whose OAuth SDK hits this route by mistake is told about an email and a password. Not a defect in #986; a wording the owner may want to unify.
* File: `services/auth/src/__tests__/ks1151-auth-refresh-refuses-oauth-token.test.ts`; guard: `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` after `verifyRefreshToken`, before `getSession` (`client_id !== undefined || authMethod === 'oauth'` → 401).

### C. THE FORWARD-ONLY WINDOW — escalation candidate, deployment-side, Kam via Wednesday (report §3.7; NOT a grade on #986)

A refresh token minted at the OAuth grant BEFORE #983/#984 land carries NEITHER `client_id` NOR `authMethod` and therefore passes the guard and still launders at `/api/auth/refresh` until it expires (`JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN` default `'7d'`, `services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:44`). The deployed population is UNMEASURED (both round-1 reports, both PR bodies and this pass agree — no environment was probed). The instrument that closes the window is deployment-side (denylist the pre-deploy OAuth refresh jtis, or force re-authorisation at deploy). Also by design: a refused OAuth token is NOT denylisted by the sibling (C3 proves it stays alive at its own grant) — its replay protection is the OAuth grant's own `isRefreshJtiDenylisted` read (`oauth.ts:923`), which rotates/denylists nothing on success → R-2, open on KS-1150.

* R-C1 · MEASURED (T5) · Polish/test-quality · #986 · described regression cell C3 (assert `getSession` 0 on the refusal) — SHIPS-WITH as a follow-up test, not a blocker.
