title: packages/shared tree-walking guards exceed vitest's 5 s default under fleet load — 5 cells at load 32, 9 at load 25–49, 5,243 ms alone at load 27; assertions hold (green solo / with testTimeout raised / at load 11) — a load class that costs a re-run on every merge
description:
## BLUF

`packages/shared`'s repo-tree-walking guard cells exceed vitest's 5 s default `testTimeout` when the box carries the fleet's load (several seats' suites + QA gates at once). The assertions hold every time — the same cells pass solo, or with `--testTimeout` raised, or on the same tree minutes later at a lower load. So a red `Test timed out in 5000ms` in these files on a loaded box is a **load class**, not a product finding — but a merge seat cannot tell that from the run alone without a solo re-run or a raised-timeout re-run, which costs minutes on every merge. Filed so the class has a name and a home (KS-1053 names it only as context for the `services/auth` ks949 cell, a different suite).

## The measurements (all 2026-09-14, all on trees where the guard files are blob-identical to develop)

* **s224 (quoted as s224's, from its STACK READY mail 02:54:51Z):** `packages/shared` 43 files / 835 — **830 passed / 5 failed at load 32**, every failure `Test timed out in 5000ms` in the tree-walking guards (`crypto-agility.guard.test.ts`, `entrypoint-corpus.test.ts:180` the CENSUS cell, `ks727-errorhandler-class-guard.test.ts:905`, `ks764-key-revoke-call-site-guard.test.ts:263`, `ks860-test-listeners-bind-loopback.test.ts:463`); **1 at load 34**; the same cells green solo (**5,243 ms alone at load 27** — over the 5 s budget even solo, under that load).
* **s220 (the merge seat, PRED(985)** `3239e7207`**,** `item11/suite985/`**):** run at load 25–49 — **835: 822 passed / 9 failed / 4 skipped**, all nine timeouts: `crypto-agility.guard.test.ts` (5 s), `ks256-spec-example-contract.test.ts` (5 s, the positive-control cell), `ks727-errorhandler-class-guard.test.ts` ×4 (5 s: the CONTROL enumeration, the 🔴 corpus-is-the-shared-derivation cell, its CONTROL, the ROOTS-pinned cell), `ks764-key-revoke-call-site-guard.test.ts` (5 s, CALL_SITES), `ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts` ×2 (a 10 s **hook** timeout in KS-832's ACCEPTANCE BAR + LEG C 5 s), `threadToken.test.ts` (**30 s**, `parameteriseMintPolicy` different-seeds — a crypto cell, not a walk). Solo re-runs at load 47–49: four files green; `ks727` and `ks781` still one timeout each. With `--testTimeout 120000 --hookTimeout 120000` at load ~20: `ks727` **94/94**, `ks781` **231/231**. The full suite again with the raised timeouts at load 11: **43 / 835 / 0**.
* **s203 (KS-1053's context line, 2026-09-13):** three `Test timed out in 5000ms` in the same guards at load ~20.
* Not the same subject as KS-1053 (the `services/auth` ks949 cell, 5.7–6.0 s on a 5 s budget under load, mechanism unestablished) — related as the neighbouring load-class record.

## What this costs today

Every merge-seat run of `packages/shared` on a loaded box is a coin-flip red that has to be re-run solo or with the timeout raised before it can be read (the s220 protocol did both). The tree walks themselves are the guards' point (they read the whole `services/` + `packages/` tree by design); their budget is the default 5 s.

## Fix shapes (the owner's call)

1. A per-file `testTimeout` (and `hookTimeout`) for the tree-walking guards — 30–60 s — set in the test files or a `vitest.config` `test.testTimeout` override scoped to `__tests__/*guard*.test.ts`, so a slow walk under load is a slow walk, not a red. Keep the default for everything else.
2. Share one tree walk per run (a cached corpus) instead of one per cell — `entrypoint-corpus`, `ks727`, `ks781`, `ks860`, `ks879` each walk the tree; the walk is the cost.
3. `threadToken.test.ts`'s 30 s cell is a different shape (CPU-bound crypto); its own budget line.

## Done when

- [ ] the tree-walking guard cells carry an explicit timeout budget that a loaded box meets (measured: a full `packages/shared` run at load ≥ 30 reads 0 timeouts), or the walk is shared and the cells fit the default
- [ ] the merge-seat protocol no longer needs a solo re-run to read a `packages/shared` result on a loaded box

*(npm scope sigils are omitted throughout —* `rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu` *means the scoped package; the symbols stay searchable.)*

`Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` records exactly ONE rollup platform binary — `node_modules/rollup/rollup-darwin-arm64` (the lock was generated on macOS arm64); `rollup-linux-x64-gnu` appears only inside an `optionalDependencies` list (lock line 19376), never as an installed entry. So `npm ci` on `ubuntu-latest` installs no Linux rollup binary, and the two vite-6 frontends — `frontend/demo-overlay` and `frontend/outlook-addin` (rollup 4.60.4) — die at `vite build` with `Error: Cannot find module … rollup-linux-x64-gnu`. Upstream: npm/cli#4828 (npm's optional-platform-dependency flaw). Measured live by the L9 gate on PR #887's advisory job (`pr` run 34786655660 / job 103803259738, step 6): the four vite-8 frontends (rolldown) and all 26 service/package builds green; these two red. **Consequence:** `pr-platform-suites.yml`'s `Workspace unit suites (advisory, non-blocking)` job stays red at step 6 on EVERY PR until the lockfile carries `rollup-linux-x64-gnu` — advisory, blocks nothing, but the job cannot say anything useful until then. A macOS pass is not runner evidence for this job.

The gate's TICKET line, verbatim: *"the rollup-linux-x64-gnu lockfile matter — Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json -> node_modules/rollup/rollup-* (only rollup-darwin-arm64 installed; rollup-linux-x64-gnu only in an optionalDependencies list at :19376); frontend/demo-overlay, frontend/outlook-addin; pr-platform-suites.yml workspace-suites step 6; npm/cli#4828 — a KS or KS-1148 (c)."*

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-14-L9-940-941-942-887-ks1075-1077-1078-961-tier2-r1/report.md` (§2 the live job; §4b(iv) the mechanism — `git grep -o -E '"node_modules/rollup/rollup-[a-z0-9-]+"' 3aee3deed -- Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` → `rollup-darwin-arm64` only; findings register R-4). First recorded by s215 as an adjacent finding in KS-1148's comment (2026-09-13T22:32Z): "a DIFFERENT class from (a)/(b), so not added to the checklist".

**Why its own ticket, not KS-1148 (c):** KS-1148's class is *the runner never installs or builds* — its fix is an install/build step per job. This job DOES install and build; the defect is the lock's CONTENT, and `npm ci` on Linux cannot install a binary the lock does not carry. One fix, one file, a different owner's action — the 2026-09-07 one-ticket-per-fix rule. Related: KS-1148 (the runner-gap class this was first noted under), KS-961 (#887, the advisory job that surfaces it).

**Ancestors (archived — named, not related):** KS-653 (Done — root-workspace `npm run build` broken for 5 of 6 vite frontends: the same npm/cli#4828 class on rolldown's `darwin-arm64` binding; fixed by regenerating the root lock's optional native bindings) and KS-376 (Done — the esbuild platform-binary subtree inconsistent in the same lock, same class). The lock has lost a platform binary set three times now; the regen-on-one-host shape is what keeps re-creating it.

## Fix shape (the builder's call)

* Make the root lock carry ALL rollup platform binaries (as it once did for esbuild's 25/26 variants): a lock regeneration that records every `rollup/rollup-*` optional binary (npm ≥ 10 records all platforms when run with `--package-lock-only` from a clean state; or add `rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu` as an explicit optionalDependency at the root so the lock pins it), then verify on a Linux `npm ci` (the advisory job itself is the instrument: step 6 green for `demo-overlay` and `outlook-addin`).
* Regression guard: a lockfile cell that asserts the `rollup/rollup-*` entry set covers `darwin-arm64` AND `linux-x64-gnu` (the two hosts that build this repo), so a future macOS regen cannot drop the Linux binary silently.

## Done when

- [ ] `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` carries `node_modules/rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu` (and keeps `rollup-darwin-arm64`)
- [ ] `pr-platform-suites.yml` `Workspace unit suites` step 6 builds `frontend/demo-overlay` and `frontend/outlook-addin` green on a Linux runner (read from the live job at the fixing PR's head)
- [ ] a guard cell pins the platform-binary set, red-first on the current lock

title: OAuth /token grant hardening (measured by the #982 gate, pre-existing): the authorization_code grant has no status pin (:809), the refresh grant does not rotate/denylist the presented token (:836/:860), a 503-class lookup error is mapped to 500 (:889-891)
description:
## BLUF

Three pre-existing gaps on ONE logical path — `services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts`, `POST /api/oauth/token` — measured by the #982 (KS-790) tier-1 gate on 2026-09-14 and NOT graded against #982 (none changes its GO). One test pass, one fix on one file, three items:

* **R-1 — the** `authorization_code` **grant has NO status pin.** `routes/oauth.ts:809` `if (!user) {` — a SUSPENDED user's code mints 200 + a token pair (measured at the gated head in both stub legs). The refresh grant refuses the same user at `:868` `if (!user || user.status !== 'ACTIVE') {`; `/api/auth/refresh` pins ACTIVE at `auth.ts:687`; the authorize gates pin it too. Severity as a standalone defect: **Major** (a credential minted for a disabled account; the window is a 5-minute code minted before a suspension that post-dates the authorize gate's own status check).
* **R-2 — the** `refresh_token` **grant does not rotate / denylist the presented token.** `:836` `// Verify and rotate refresh token. verifyRefreshToken THROWS` (the comment says rotate; nothing rotates) and `:860` `if (decoded.jti && (await isRefreshJtiDenylisted(decoded.jti))) {` — the grant verifies, checks the denylist, mints. The same refresh token was accepted twice (200 / 200), 0 jtis denylisted by the product. The oracle is `/api/auth/refresh`: `auth.ts:695` `await rotateSessionRefreshToken(session.id, tokens.refreshToken);` and `:698` `await denylistRefreshJti(payload.jti, remaining);`. RFC 6749 §10.4 (rotation for public clients). **KS-823 (#983) rewrites this branch — the #983 gate re-measures R-2 at the new head.**
* **R-3 — a 503-class lookup error is mapped to 500.** `:889-891` `} catch (error: any) { logger.error('OAuth token error', { error: error.message }); res.status(500).json({ … code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: 'server_error' }) }` intercepts before `errorHandler.ts:77-80` (`export class ServiceUnavailableError extends AppError { … super(message, 503, 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE')`) can give the class its 503. Measured at both SHAs: ECONNREFUSED in the lookup → 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR server_error`, the code already burned. A retryable outage reads as a bug.

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-14-ks790-982-e62eab87a-tier1-r1/report.md` §8 (lines 195–203), §3a/§3b. Line refs are at `e62eab87a` (`oauth.ts` 1,260 lines there; develop-before-M19 `:800` for R-1's site).

**Neighbours, from the board census by symbol (title + description + comments, archived included):**

* KS-756 (nearest — the SESSION refresh handle; its item 4 names `routes/oauth.ts` `:254-271` as the OAuth refresh path that "moves in the same change or it becomes the bypass") — related, not the home.
* KS-999 (getUserById's decrypt path escapes the KS-253 classifier → 500 where 503 is mandated) — R-3's direct neighbour: with KS-999 fixed, this route's own catch still maps the class to 500. KS-1018 and KS-1132 are the same 503-class on other subjects.
* KS-486 (archived, Review A) — its 2026-08-13 row "G2 | Refresh rotation + jti denylist | VERIFIED | … replay refused at `routes/auth.ts:583` and `routes/oauth.ts:271`" read the CHECK at `oauth.ts:271` (now `:860`) as replay-refused. The measurement above says otherwise for the OAuth grant: the check exists, nothing on the OAuth path denylists a jti (only `auth.ts:698` does, on the session path). Named here as the ancestor; no relation (archived).
* KS-790 (#982 — the pre-auth lookup swap that made R-1 reachable at all: at develop the RLS-scoped lookup returned null for every code under migration 039, masking the missing pin).

## Proposed fix shapes (the gate's PROPOSALS, the builder's call)

1. R-1: `if (!user || user.status !== 'ACTIVE')` at `:809` with the same 400 `invalid_grant`; regression: the ks790 harness's cell 5 mirrored onto the code grant (a SUSPENDED-user code → 400).
2. R-2: on a successful refresh grant, denylist the presented jti for its remaining lifetime (the `auth.ts:696-699` shape) and, if a session backs it, rotate the session record; regression: a replayed refresh token → 400 + its jti denylisted. Re-measure after #983 lands (it rewrites the branch).
3. R-3: let `ServiceUnavailableError` (and any `AppError`) fall through to `errorHandler`, or map the class to 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` inside the route's catch; regression: a `ServiceUnavailableError` from either lookup → 503, not 500.

## Done when

- [ ] a SUSPENDED user's authorization code is refused with 400 `invalid_grant` at the code grant (R-1), with a red-first cell
- [ ] a replayed OAuth refresh token is refused with 400 and its jti reads as denylisted (R-2), with a red-first cell — measured on the post-#983 branch
- [ ] a `ServiceUnavailableError` from either user lookup on `/token` answers 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (R-3), with a red-first cell
- [ ] the ks790 / ks820-821 / ks823 harnesses stay green; `services/auth` full suite green; PR with a Test Evidence block

## Provenance

* Measured by the #982 gate (tier 1, round 1) on its own by-SHA copies of `e62eab87a` and develop M18 `8861e6216`, 2026-09-14 07:49–08:15 AEST; verdict GO 22:15:10Z; the three records stated at the same prominence as the findings and ruled to ONE ticket by Wednesday (22:40Z).

description:
## BLUF

Two CI jobs run test code whose runtime prerequisites the job never installs or builds. Both reds are **environment gaps on the runner**, not defects in the code under test — each suite is green locally on a tree that has a root `node_modules` and a built `packages/shared`. Recorded here as ONE ticket because one fix pass (an install/build step per job) proves both, and because both were surfaced by the same lane on the same day. **Fixing either is a** `.github/workflows/` **edit — Kam-class; nothing here is changed by the seat that filed this.** Filed on Wednesday's ADDENDUM of 2026-09-13T21:58Z; board searched first (`packages/shared is not built` 0 hits · `npm run build -w packages/shared` 0 · `Cannot find package 'semver'` 1 — the closed ticket that gave `scripts/audit/` its own `package.json`, Done + archived · `CI-runner environment` 0 · nonsense-token control 0).

## Checklist

- [ ] **(a)** `Security Scanning` **→ job** `Dependency Audit` **→ step** `Audit-contract suites`**:** `scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs` **cannot start.**
  * Evidence: PR #940's run 34426409872 / job 102712486541 / step 7 — the first run where this step printed anything (PR #940 dropped `bash -e` from that step). `ℹ tests 59 · pass 52 · fail 7`; the seven reds are every `audit-locks:` case in `scripts/audit/gate-exit-codes.test.mjs` (`:91`, `:104`, `:113`, `:180`, `:192`, `:201`, `:208`), each "got 1" where 3 / 2 / 0 was expected. The `:192` case's assertion captured the child's output verbatim: `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'semver' imported from /home/runner/work/Distributed_Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs` (Node.js v24.20.0).
  * Mechanism: the job deliberately runs **no install** — the comment above its `npm audit` step says advisories resolve straight from the lockfile so no `npm ci` is needed. That is true for `npm audit` and false for the next step's test suite: `audit-locks.mjs:50` imports `semver`, which is declared only in `scripts/audit/package.json` (a standalone member, intentionally outside the workspaces list; its own description names exactly this failure on any tree without a root install). Locally the hoisted root `node_modules` supplies it → 59/59.
  * Not the same defect as the closed root-declaration ticket: that one added the declaration; this one is the CI job never installing it.

title: ks860 loopback guard boundary (R-5, #980 delta gate): a listen call carried as a string fixture in a `"`-literal with an escaped host `\"127.0.0.1\"` is reported as host-less — the mask copies the backslash, `:440` wants a bare quote
description:
## BLUF

A class boundary of the ks860 loopback guard (`Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks860-test-listeners-bind-loopback.test.ts`, widened to `packages/` by #976 / KS-876), measured by the tier-2 delta gate on PR #980 (KS-924 + KS-901) at `103c235b4` and recorded as R-5 — not a finding against #980, which ships `app.listen(0, '127.0.0.1')` (single-quoted host, the guard's own `:517` accepted spelling) and reads GREEN: `packages/shared` 813/813 on the merged tree, ks860 23/23. Nothing on develop trips it today; it is the guard's, and #976's gate owns the guard's design. One file, one test pass; the fix shape below is the gate's PROPOSAL, not ratified.

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks924-901-980-103c235b4-tier2-r2/report.md` — §3 the Tg-B row, §4 the tamper table, §6 Records R-5. Line numbers at M17 `a4ef481c8` (the guard's blob `e0dfadb9c`, unchanged since M15).

## The boundary (MEASURED by the gate, Tg-B)

* A test file that carries a listen call as a string fixture inside a `"`-delimited literal can only spell a double-quoted host as `\"127.0.0.1\"`. Written to disk that body is `app.listen(0, "127.0.0.1");` — exactly the guard's own `:516` accepted spelling (`expect(offendingListenSites('const s = app.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve);')).toEqual([])`). Yet with #980's `:235` rewritten that way the guard's 🔴 cell reads RED naming `:235` (two-file run 51/52), the offender printed with its backslashes.
* Cause: `maskCommentsWithState` preserves string contents by design (docblock `:104-109` — a `//` inside `'http://x'` is data) and copies the backslash into the masked text; the site regex `:433` `/\.listen\(\s*0\s*(,|\))/g` matches, then the host check `:440` `/^\s*(['"])127\.0\.0\.1\1/` requires a bare `'` or `"` as the first non-space character after the comma — a `\` is neither, so the site is reported host-less.
* Blast radius: any test file carrying a listen call as a STRING FIXTURE in a `"`-literal with a double-quoted host. None exists on develop today (the merged tree is green); the natural escape is the single-quoted host, which #980 uses. Sibling boundary noted by the same gate (Tg-D): `listen(3000)` with no host passes `\s*0\s*` — the regex's declared narrowness (port 0 only), recorded, not a defect claim.

## Fix shape (the gate's PROPOSAL)

Let the host check accept an escaped quote: e.g. `/^\s*\\?(['"])127\.0\.0\.1\\?\1/` at `:440`, and add a control cell beside `:516-517` feeding a `"`-literal fixture whose host is `\"127.0.0.1\"` (as a string, i.e. the file's own text carries the backslash-quote), expecting `[]`. Regression instrument: Tg-B on the widened guard → the 🔴 cell GREEN; the T-860 tamper (host removed) must still RED.

## Dedupe (searched before filing)

By symbol over the KS board, title + description, includeArchived (s211 ITEM 0 for L): `offendingListenSites` 5 (KS-895, KS-894, KS-891, KS-874, KS-873 — all archived; the mask-desync / announcement-row classes, none the escaped-host boundary) · `SELF_EXCLUDED` 0 · `maskCommentsWithState` 1 (KS-891, archived — the re-synchronising desync) · `mask preserves` 0 · `ks860` 7 (KS-876/875/879/891/893/894/895, all archived; none this boundary) · `listen(` 11 (KS-860 the parent — 55 listeners binding all interfaces; KS-845 the nine bare sites; the rest other subjects). No home; filed new. KS-873 / KS-874 / KS-891 are the guard's mask-class neighbours (archived; named, not related).

## Items (one test pass)

1. **CN-1 — ID3's capture half has no size assertion.** ID3 (`:304-318`) pins the guard on two things only the guard changes: the command tag and `updated_at`. Its `updated_at` capture runs twice — `UPD_B` at `:308` and `UPD_A` at `:310` — and the cell compares the two lists. The gate's own R5 control shows the miss is real: on a fresh slug-ONLY drift the id-arm-only statement reads `UPDATE 0` (the drift stays), where the shipped two-arm statement reads `UPDATE 1` (repaired). **Proposal (the gate's):** an AG cell that plants slug-only drift on a second id (`c1…0001` → `slug-only-drift`), asserts `UPDATE 1` and the slug restored — reds under Tg3, green at head.

title: ks781 LEG F guard walk: a MENTION of a guard-bound local reads as a mount (`:2318`) — `void controlByteGuard; next();` leaves 19 admin routes `{ 19, true }`; and guard-BEFORE-parser reads `guarded: true` (no order predicate)
description:
## BLUF

PR #981 (KS-828 + KS-900, merged 2026-09-13) gave LEG F sight of the control-byte guard LEAVING a wrapped router (`{ routes, guarded }` per router module) and closed KS-828's T3 (`admin.ts:560` `controlByteGuard(req, res, next);` → `next();` now reds LEG F). The tier-2 gate measured two ways the new predicate still blesses an unguarded parser — both MEASURED AT RUNTIME, both the ticket's own class (KS-828's T3 is one token away from GF-1). GF-1 was DISCLOSED by the builder (PR body: "the same looseness the parser reach already has … stated rather than widened here") — a disclosed limit is still the limit, and this one errs in the UNSAFE direction (the parser-side mention at `:2293` over-reports, R-1). Fix shapes are the GATE'S PROPOSALS, not ratified. One file, one test pass.

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks828-900-981-04807ea0e-tier2-r1/report.md` — §6 GF-1, GF-2, Records R-1; §4 Tg1, Tg-ORDER. Line numbers at `04807ea0e` = develop after the squash.

## Items (one test pass)

1. **GF-1 (Minor) — a guard MENTION counts as a guard mount.** `routerParserAnalysis` `:2318` `if (ts.isIdentifier(m) && (guardSyms.has(m.text) || guardedWrappers.has(m.text))) { hit = true; return; }`. Repro at `04807ea0e`: `admin.ts:560` `controlByteGuard(req, res, next);` → `void controlByteGuard; next();` (anchor count 1) → `npx vitest run src/__tests__/ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts` in `packages/shared` → `Tests 231 passed (231)`; LEG F reads admin.ts `{ 19, true }` with the guard never invoked on 19 parsing routes. Fixture forms: W2's `g(req, res, next)` → `void g; next()` stays GREEN; a scratch cell with `const _ = g; next();` → `{ 2, true }`. Oracle: the file's own docblocks `:2307-2308` / `:2485-2488` ("a guard MENTIONED is not a guard MOUNTED") and the LEG F message `:2463-2464` ("`false` means the parser runs and nothing after it inspects the body"). **Proposal:** hit only on a CALL node — `ts.isCallExpression(m) && ts.isIdentifier(m.expression) && (guardSyms.has(m.expression.text) || guardedWrappers.has(m.expression.text))` (or a `guardCallName(m, b)` helper). Regression cells: the `void g; next();` fixture must read `{ 2, false }`; the admin.ts `void controlByteGuard; next();` form must red LEG F.
2. **GF-2 (Minor, borderline Record — Wednesday rates) — guard BEFORE parser reads** `guarded: true`**.** Fixture P7 (exactly `wrapperModule`'s shape with the body `g(req, res, () => raw(req, res, next));`) → `{"routes":2,"guarded":true}` — the guard inspects an unparsed `req.body`, the KS-800 class in the file's own name ("body-parser ORDER"). Not a regression against the parent (which saw no guard at all), but the LEG F message defines `true` as "something after the parser inspects the body", and this shape is `true` with nothing after the parser. **Proposal:** start the guard walk from the parser call's callback argument (`raw(req, res, cb)` → walk `cb`), not from the whole wrapper body. Regression: P7's fixture reads `false`; W2/W3 still `true`.
3. **R-1, for context (no change asked):** `:2293` `ts.isIdentifier(m) && syms.has(m.text)` — a MENTION of a parser-bound local admits a wrapper (P8 `void raw; next()` → `{ 2, false }`): pre-existing (KS-816), over-reports, SAFE direction. Whether item 1's fix should also tighten `:2293` is the builder's call; the asymmetry (safe on the parser side, unsafe on the guard side) is why the guard side is the item.

## Dedupe (searched before filing)

By symbol over 1,131 KS issues + 908 comments (includeArchived): `controlByteGuard` → KS-828 only (its own disclosure); `guardSyms` 0; `guardedWrappers` 0; `routerParserAnalysis` 0; `ks781-p3-3` → 12 hits, none on the guard-walk predicate (KS-802 the parser regex; KS-905 the IIFE clause; KS-953 line pins; KS-831 archived, the KS-800 guard-side ticket where LEG F was born — named, not related). No home; filed new.

title: Bare arithmetic-command `((X++))` under `set -e` — exits 1 at 0 and bash ≥ 4.1 errexit kills the script: 10 errexit-live sites remain in `sync-secrets.sh` (×8) and `validate-lint.sh` (×2) after #977's docker-build.sh fix
description:
## BLUF

The class fixed in `docker-build.sh` by PR #977 round 2 (KS-877) and in `validate-env.sh` by KS-680 is still present at **10 errexit-live sites in two host scripts**. An arithmetic command exits 1 when its expression evaluates to 0, and a post-increment yields the OLD value — so `((COUNT++))` at COUNT=0 "fails", and bash ≥ 4.1 `set -e` exits the script on it (bash COMPAT item 45), silently. bash 3.2 (macOS) does not apply errexit to arithmetic commands, so these scripts pass on the Mac and die on Linux / CI / containers at their first count.

## Census (develop `3fc158c39`, 2026-09-13)

Instrument: the CELL 4 regex from `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/docker_build_empty_table.test.sh` — `^[[:space:]]*\(\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*(\+\+|--)\)\)[[:space:]]*$` — over tracked `*.sh` (`git grep -nE`, `[[:space:]]` not `\s`: BSD grep). Positive control: 2 hits on `docker-build.sh` at `a70585823`, 0 at `aede93117`.

| file | sites | errexit | context |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/sync-secrets.sh` | **8** — `:186 :192 :198 :204 :216 :221 :227 :232` (`SKIPPED`, `GENERATED`, `UPDATED`) | `set -euo pipefail` at `:20` | each inside an `if … then` BODY (not a condition) — errexit-live; the first `((SKIPPED++))` / `((GENERATED++))` / `((UPDATED++))` at 0 exits the script on bash ≥ 4.1 |
| `systemTest/schemathesis/validate-lint.sh` | **2** — `:33 :38` (`PASS_COUNT`, `FAIL_COUNT`) | `set -e` at `:6` | to be confirmed at the site (a tested context suppresses errexit) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/validate-env.sh` | 3 — `:62 :81 :99` | `set -e` at `:9` | **NOT defects** — inside `if check_required_var …` bodies, where errexit is suppressed for the whole function (KS-680 measured both ways); listed so the census is complete |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/docker-build.sh` | 0 at `aede93117` (2 at `a70585823`) | `set -euo pipefail` | fixed in #977 round 2 |

## Fix shape (measured on 3.2.57; the shape Peter named on the archived bash-3.2 portability ticket, and KS-680's at `validate-env.sh:179-219`)

`COUNT=$((COUNT + 1))` — an assignment's exit status is 0 at every value and the effect is identical. Not `((++X))` (a pre-decrement evaluates to 0 at the last step and fails there); not `((X++)) || true` (masks the status instead of removing the failing construct).

## Durable home

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-script-portability.sh` has 7 rules and none for this construct (a "rule 8" was proposed on the portability ticket and reverted on KS-666). The census regex above is the candidate rule; the suite's CELL 4 shows the shape with its positive control.

## Searched before filing

`RUNNING++`, `((RUNNING`, `arithmetic command`, `post-increment`, `errexit`, `set -e`, `bash 4.1`, `sync-secrets`, `validate-lint` — 0 literal title hits among open issues; the archived homes (KS-680 and the docker-build portability ticket's defect (c)) surface only with `includeArchived: true`. Not fixed this round — filed on Wednesday's ruling (s208, 2026-09-13).

title: Audit jobs: a per-image trivy failure reads as a CLEAN image in 04 (`|| echo '{}'` + unguarded norm), and jobs 01/02/03/05/06/07/08 keep the unparseable-artefact hole 09 guards for 04 only
description:
## BLUF

PR #974 (KS-878 + KS-867, merged 2026-09-13) closed ONE silence: a truncated `04-container-trivy.json` is now loud in 09 (`04-trivy/unreadable-artefact`, high, rc 1). The tier-2 gate measured that the same silence family is still open in two places, both pre-existing, both in `Blockchain/Testing/jobs/` — the per-image failure path INSIDE 04 (R-2) and the artefact reads for every OTHER job in 09 (R-3). One workload, one test pass: a scan or a job that fails must never read as a clean result. KS-676 (Done, archived 2026-09-06) is the ancestor that made these two scripts runnable on macOS; KS-1127 is the runner-level neighbour (the harness's own skip tally).

Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks878-867-974-8da602309-tier2-r1/report.md` — §3 (the 04 table's last rows), §11 (a) and (b), R-1 / R-2 / R-3. Line numbers below are at `8da602309` = develop after the squash (M12).

## Items (one test pass)

1. **R-2 — the per-image trivy-failure path in** `04-container-trivy.sh:86-93` **and** `:96-112` **reads a failed scan as a CLEAN image.** `:93` is `"$img" 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"` — a `trivy image` that exits non-zero with no output becomes `{}`; the `norm` jq at `:96-112` then emits `counts: {}` / `vulns: []` for that image, and 09 counts it as scanned and clean. MEASURED at both base and head (recording stubs on the private PATH):
   * no-output failure → the image's entry is `{image, counts:{}, vulns:[]}`, rc 0, "across N image(s)" — a CLEAN read;
   * partial-output failure on N ≥ 2 images → an 89-byte unparseable artefact with `CRITICAL= HIGH= across 2 image(s)`, rc 0 (at head KS-878's guard in 09 now catches THIS shape as a side effect);
   * partial-output failure on the ONLY image → `{"images":[]}` — valid JSON, rc 0, 0 findings, "across 1 image(s)", **silent at BOTH SHAs** (09's `jq -e` accepts it).
     Fix shape (the gate's, the owner's call): fail the image entry loudly when `raw` came from the `|| echo '{}'` arm or `norm` is empty — e.g. write `{"image": $img, "error": "scan-failed"}` and let 09 emit a high per image with `.error`; never print `across N` for a scan whose `norm` was empty. Regression cells: a stub `trivy` that exits 1 with and without partial output, one- and two-image corpora, asserting a non-empty `.error` per failed image and rc 1.
2. **R-3 — the other artefact reads in** `09-aggregate-report.sh` **have the hole KS-878 closed for 04 only.** `:69` (01), `:77` (02), `:91` (03), `:164` (05), `:173` (06), `:181` (07) are each `jq -r … 2>/dev/null` inside `< <(…)`: a truncated artefact yields zero findings, rc 0, 0 bytes of output. `:186` (08) is `failed=$(jq '.tests.failed // 0' "$RUN_DIR/08-aiken-tests.json")` — no `2>/dev/null`, so it is stderr-loud but rc-silent. MEASURED (08): an 11-byte `{"tests":{` + LF artefact → 0 findings, rc 0, 65 bytes of `jq: parse error: Unfinished JSON term at EOF …` on stderr, at both base and head; control `{"tests":{"passed":10,"failed":2}}` → `tests-failed:2` critical, rc 1. Fix shape: one `jq -e . "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 || emit "<job>" high "<job>/unreadable-artefact"` in front of every artefact block (`:133-134` is the shape 04 now has), or a helper every block calls. Regression cells: one truncated artefact per job → one `<job>/unreadable-artefact` high and rc 1.
3. **Context, not an item — R-1:** 09's new-only rc gate (`:10-12` documents it) makes every loud finding ONE-SHOT: the second run of the same defect reads `findings 1 / new 0 / rc 0` (measured). So "must never read as a clean scan" is true for one run and false thereafter — by the aggregator's documented design, not a defect of #974; the builder should know it when writing the cells above (assert on the FIRST run, or clear the baseline in the fixture).

## Dedupe (searched before filing)

By symbol over 1,125 KS issues + 914 comments (includeArchived): `jq -e` and `unreadable-artefact` → KS-878 only; `|| echo '{}'` → 0; `scan-failed` → 0; `unparseable` → 11 hits, every one another subject (date/query parsing, launcher and preflight parsers, `SERVICES_TABLE`); `04-container-trivy` → KS-676 (archived), KS-680 (archived), KS-868 (archived), KS-867, KS-878; `09-aggregate-report` → KS-676, KS-868, KS-878. title: run-shell-suites.sh fails 6 of 25 suites under a long TMPDIR — tsx's IPC socket path exceeds macOS's ~104-byte sun_path limit (listen EINVAL); preflight leg 14 reds for the wrong reason
description:
## BLUF

With a **123-character** `TMPDIR` (a seat's scratchpad path), `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-shell-suites.sh` reads **19 passed, 6 failed (of 25)**; with a **28-character** `TMPDIR` symlinked into the same scratch, the same tree reads **25 passed, 0 failed**. The six — `manifest_path`, `manifest_quarantine`, `manifest_readers_agree`, `pre_suite`, `provision_base_url`, `quarantine_call_sites` — fail because `tsx` binds its IPC socket at `$TMPDIR/tsx-501/<pid>.pipe` and macOS refuses a `sun_path` over ~104 bytes (`listen EINVAL`), not because of anything they test. A seat or a runner with a deep `TMPDIR` sees spurious reds on preflight leg 14 (the shell-suite leg). Pre-existing; found by the #971 tier-2 gate while running the consumer; nothing in #971 touches it.

Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks922-941-971-c229aa256-tier2-r1/report.md` — §7 (the consumer), FINDINGS O1 (Open, pre-existing environment edge, MEASURED); `evidence/consumer-clean.out` (19/6) vs `evidence/consumer-clean2.out` (25/0).

## What is established and what is not

* **MEASURED:** the 19/6 vs 25/0 pair on one tree, changing only `TMPDIR`'s length; the six failing suites named; the error string `listen EINVAL` on the `.pipe` path.
* **READ ONLY:** the ~104-byte `sun_path` limit is the platform's (`sys/un.h`), and `tsx` derives the socket path from `TMPDIR`.
* **Not established:** whether any of the six suites spawns `tsx` directly or through a helper they share (`pre_suite`'s name suggests a shared preamble); whether the launcher's `TMPDIR` for seats is long enough to trip it (the gate's was a QA scratchpad); the exact byte threshold on this macOS.

## Fix shape (prose; the builder's call)

* In `run-shell-suites.sh` (or the shared preamble the six use), export a SHORT `TMPDIR` for the suite run — e.g. `mktemp -d /tmp/rss.XXXXXX` — and restore it after; or detect `${#TMPDIR} > 80` and print one line naming the cause before the suites run.
* A cell in `run_shell_suites.test.sh` (the KS-1127 harness home): a deliberately long `TMPDIR` must produce the named-cause line and NOT six anonymous reds.

title: verify-hash precedence: v1 hash-LAST, v2 hash-FIRST — document the split on both routes' descriptions (Kam 2026-09-13)
description:
## BLUF

**Ruled by Kam 2026-09-13 16:55 AEST on the decision panel:** `accept-split`**.** His option text, verbatim: *"Accept the split in writing: v1 hash-LAST (legacy bodies unchanged), v2 hash-FIRST; document it on both routes' descriptions"*. The two public verify routes read the same conflicting body to different hashes, by design after this ruling — so the work is documentation on both routes' OpenAPI descriptions, plus a cell on each route asserting its own order, not a code change to either chain.

## The finding this rules (the #965 tier-2 gate's F-1, Minor, MEASURED AT RUNTIME)

Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks1103-965-d63b27ab3-tier2-r1/report.md`, FINDINGS F-1; rows P1/W1 in `evidence/shapes-table.md`.

* `{contentHash:A, hash:B}` → **v1** `POST /api/verification/verify` looks up **A** (`providedHash || contentHash || documentHash || hash`, originate `routes/verification.ts:742` at `d63b27ab3`); **v2** `POST /api/v2/verification/verify` looks up **B** (`hash || providedHash || contentHash || documentHash`, `verificationV2.ts:446`).
* The divergence pre-dates #965 (at its base v1 ignored `hash` entirely); #965's T2 tamper pins v1's order by test, so the routes disagree by design rather than by omission. No caller sends two different hashes (the gate's §3 class (c) was empty), so the blast radius today is nil; the inconsistency is a contract fact a future connector author can trip on.
* The gate did not judge which order is right; Kam has: keep both, write it down.

## Checklist (one test pass)

- [ ] v1 route description in the served spec (`services/originate/src/openapi/*.openapi.ts` → regenerated `secuura-api.yaml`; the spec is bind-mounted, not baked): state the alias order `providedHash → contentHash → documentHash → hash` and that `hash` is read LAST so legacy bodies keep their answer.
- [ ] v2 route description likewise: `hash → providedHash → contentHash → documentHash`, `hash` read FIRST.
- [ ] One cell per route asserting the winner for `{contentHash:A, hash:B}` (v1 → A, v2 → B) — the gate's P1/W1 rows as tests, so a future "one shared chooser" cannot silently flip either route.
- [ ] Note the split in the spec's `VerifyRequest` description if it names the aliases (it currently describes a pre-KS-252 order — the gate's O-6, pre-existing prose; fix in the same pass if the sentence is touched).

## Neighbours

* **KS-1118** (Low, related): the `documentHash`-over-`hash` precedence within v1 is unpinned (F-2) + the overclaiming why-comment (F-3) — the same alias chain, one position over; a builder taking both in one pass loses nothing.
* KS-1103 (archived, #965 merged 2026-09-13) — where `hash` was first read at all on v1.

## Dedupe, before filing (s205, 2026-09-13)

Literal census over 1,120 KS issues (692 archived) and 911 comments — `hash-FIRST` 0 · `hash-LAST` 0 · `documentHash` → KS-1103 (archived), KS-1114, KS-1118, KS-1119, KS-256, KS-474, KS-480, KS-499, KS-501, KS-514 (KS-1118 is the neighbour; none carries the v1/v2 split as a ruled item). No home; filed new.

* Kam's ruling `accept-split`, 2026-09-13 16:55 AEST, decision panel; relayed in Wednesday's ADDENDUM to s205 (16:57 AEST) with the option text verbatim. Filed by s205 as the ticket that carries it.

title: getPlatformAdmin swallows an infrastructure failure to null — platform-admin login reads "platform DB down" as "not an admin" and answers InvalidCredentialsError (the class KS-963 removed)
description:
## BLUF

`services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` `getPlatformAdmin` (`:1714-1741` at develop after #970) catches every error from the platform-database lookup, logs `Platform admin lookup failed (platform DB may not be configured)` and **returns** `null` (`:1739-1741`). Its caller, `routes/auth.ts:345` `const platformAdmin = await userRepo.getPlatformAdmin(data.email);`, reads `null` as "not a platform admin" and falls through to the regular-user gate, which answers `InvalidCredentialsError` — the KS-253 shape ("a DB failure reported as no such user") on the highest-privilege door. This is exactly the class KS-963 / PR #970 removed from the five `getUserByIdPreAuth` callers, on a branch **outside KS-963's include** (Kam's scope named `getUserById` → widened to `getUserByIdPreAuth`). Named by the tier-1 gate as F-6 under "hunt the class"; needs its own ruling before a build.

Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks963-970-ae274f7cb-tier1-r1/report.md` — §9 HUNT THE CLASS (F-6 and the 15-catch census), WHAT WAS NOT TESTED item 3 (the branch was not exercised: `getPlatformAdmin` answered `null` because `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` was unset in the harness — which is itself the swallow at work).

## What is and is not established

* **READ ONLY (source at** `ae274f7cb`**):** the catch, its message, the `return null`, the caller at `auth.ts:345`, the fall-through to the regular-user gate (`auth.ts:344-482` is the platform-admin branch).
* **Catch census at head, brace-matched (the gate's):** 15 `catch` blocks in `userRepo.ts` — `return null` at `decryptPlatformAdminMfaSecret :206`, `getOrganizationTenant :541` (documented "treating as not found"), `getPlatformAdmin :1739` (this ticket); `return undefined` at `decryptPiiCol :109`, `decryptMfaSecret :186`; `return ''` at `decryptEmail :158`; void swallows at `seedDemoUsersInner :1658`, `reencryptMfaSecretIfLegacy :1708`, `reencryptPlatformAdminMfaSecretIfLegacy :1776`; rethrows at `getUserById :394`, `getUserByIdWithPasswordHash :430`, `getUserByIdPreAuth :496`, `getUserByEmail :578`, `getUserBySocialId :611`, `emailExists :638`.
* **NOT MEASURED:** the platform-admin branch was not driven at the gate (persona untouched); whether a platform-DB outage today produces a 401 on a genuine platform admin is inferred from the source, not observed. The "platform DB may not be configured" comment suggests the swallow is deliberate for single-DB deployments — the ruling has to say whether "not configured" and "configured but down" are the same case.

## Decision needed, then the build

1. **Ruling:** treat a platform-DB failure on the admin login path like KS-963 treats the five pre-auth callers (rethrow → 503, no token consumed, no write) — OR keep the swallow for the not-configured case and distinguish it from a connection/query failure (e.g. swallow only when `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` is unset; rethrow otherwise).
2. **Build (after the ruling):** the change at `:1739-1741` per the ruling + a cell in `ks963-preauth-rethrow.test.ts` (or a sibling) driving `POST /api/auth/login` for a platform-admin email with the platform lookup rejecting → 503, and the not-configured case → unchanged behaviour if the ruling keeps it.

## Neighbours (archived, named for context)

* KS-737 (archived; platform-admin login skipped MFA when `mfaCode` was omitted — the same `auth.ts` admin branch, a different defect).
* KS-171 (archived; `platform_admins.mfa_secret` plaintext — the same `getPlatformAdmin` read, a different defect).
* KS-999 (open, High): `getUserById`'s decrypt path escapes the KS-253 classifier — the same class one function over; related to KS-963 already.

## Dedupe, before filing (s205, 2026-09-13)

Literal census over 1,120 KS issues (692 archived) and 911 comments — `getPlatformAdmin` → KS-171 (archived), KS-737 (archived), KS-963 (the gate's own READY comment) · `Platform admin lookup failed` 0 · `auth.ts:345` 0 · `InvalidCredentialsError` → KS-486, KS-622 (archived), KS-732, KS-737, KS-963 · `getUserByIdPreAuth` → KS-1013, KS-1052, KS-790, KS-796, KS-943, KS-963, KS-999. Every open hit's description read: none names the `getPlatformAdmin` swallow. Filed new.

## Provenance

Tier-1 gate on PR #970 at `ae274f7cb`, 2026-09-13: §9 F-6 (named, not raised against #970; outside KS-963's include). Wednesday's ADDENDUM to s205, 2026-09-13 16:57 AEST: ONE Low ticket, related KS-963, dedupe by symbol first. Filed by s205 at the per-PR order's step 1, before KS-963's archive.

title: ks963 structural cells count raw text — a comment naming consumeResetToken reds the cell, a deleted consume stays green, a non-await write stays green, the wallet slice is positional
description:
## BLUF

PR #970 (KS-963, merged 2026-09-13) shipped three structural cells in `services/auth/src/__tests__/ks963-preauth-rethrow.test.ts` that check `auth.ts` / `wallet.ts` for the shape KS-963 requires (the consume inside the `!user` branch; nothing consumed before the lookup; no write before the wallet lookup). The tier-1 gate measured that all three read RAW TEXT and so can be fooled in both directions — a false red on a comment, a false green on a deleted consume, a false green on a non-`await` write — while the product itself is correct on every one of the five pre-auth callers driven over real HTTP. One file, one test pass, one helper away from closing.

Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks963-970-ae274f7cb-tier1-r1/report.md` — FINDINGS F-A, F-B, F-C, P2; §5 (tampers Tg3/Tg4/Tg5, R12/R13); §6 (the legitimate-shape table). Line numbers are head `ae274f7cb` = develop after the squash.

## Items (one test pass)

1. **F-A — a false RED.** `:219` `expect(count(src.slice(expiryGuard, lookup), consumeFn)).toBe(1)` is a raw split; `braceBlock` skips comments and quotes only while counting braces and returns the raw slice, and this clause does not use it at all. MEASURED: Tg3 (`// NOTE: consumeResetToken …`) and Tg4 (`logger.debug('… consumeResetToken')`) in the gap before the lookup both red the reset cell with `expected 2 to be 1`. The cell exists to detect a hoisted consume, not a mention.
2. **F-B — a false GREEN.** `:206` `expect(guardBody).toContain(consumeFn)` over the raw brace-matched block. MEASURED (R13): replacing `await userRepo.consumeResetToken(tokenHash);` inside `if (!user) {` with `// consumeResetToken deliberately not called here any more` leaves 13/13 GREEN while the cell's title ("the reset-token consume is INSIDE the !user branch") is false of the file. Property 2 does not catch it (the count before the lookup is still 1).
3. **F-C — a false GREEN.** `:256` `/await\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$.]*)\s*\(/g` — `void query('INSERT …')` (or a `.then` chain) before the wallet lookup is outside the allow-set's universe, so `['query']` still holds and the cell is green with partial state possible. MEASURED (Tg5).
4. **P2 — positional slice.** The wallet cell's body slice is `fn.indexOf('\n}\n')`; a trailing comment on the closing brace widens the slice to lines 183–277 without changing the verdict (R12). It would start mis-measuring only if a write were added between the function's true end and the next `\n}\n`.

## Fix shape (the gate's, not authored)

* Strip comments and string literals from a slice before counting — factor the skipper `braceBlock` already has into a `stripCommentsAndStrings(src)` helper — or count call-shaped matches (`/\bconsumeResetToken\s*\(/`).
* Allow-set every call to a write-capable name before the lookup regardless of `await` (`/\b(query|userRepo\.\w+)\s*\(/g`), or additionally assert `count(before, 'query(') === 1`.
* Brace-match the wallet function body with the file's own `braceBlock`, as the `auth.ts` cells do.
* **Regression cells that must RED after the fix, GREEN before:** Tg3 and Tg4 (a comment / a string in the gap stays green while T2 — the hoisted consume — stays red), R13 (the deleted consume reds), Tg5 (the non-`await` write reds). The report's tamper set is the oracle: `evidence/` under the report dir.

## Deliberately not here

* `getPlatformAdmin`'s swallow (F-6) — its own Low, filed alongside (same file, different class: product, not test efficacy).
* The RLS round-trip of the pre-change tenant-less UPDATE (NOT TESTED at the gate; on KS-963's closing comment); P3 (`/refresh` message, pre-existing) — a line on KS-963, no ticket.

## Dedupe, before filing (s205, 2026-09-13)

Literal census over 1,120 KS issues (692 archived) and 911 comments — `ks963-preauth-rethrow` → KS-963 (comment) · `stripCommentsAndStrings` 0 · `braceBlock` 0 · `consumeResetToken` 0 · `consumeEmailToken` → KS-963 (comment) · `structural cell` → KS-900 (a different guard, `packages/shared` parser factories), KS-963. No home; filed new. Controls fired (`persistedStatus == null` → KS-1073; `raw pg BIGINT` → KS-1129; nonsense → 0).

## Provenance

Tier-1 gate on PR #970 at `ae274f7cb`, 2026-09-13 (report path above): F-A, F-B, F-C (Minor, test efficacy), P2 (Polish). Wednesday's ADDENDUM to s205, 2026-09-13 16:57 AEST: ONE Low ticket, related KS-963, one file, one test pass. Filed by s205 (the merge seat for #970) at the per-PR order's step 1, before KS-963's archive.

title: anchoring's raw pg BIGINT reaches persisted and live readers unshaped
description:
## BLUF

`block_number` leaves anchoring's `buildResponse` (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts:604`) as a **string**, the KS-584 heal path in originate persists it into the document blob unshaped, and the gateway's live chain-scan reads have no shape rule at all. Three sites, one logical path: the raw `pg` value of a `BIGINT` column is passed through where every other reader of that column converts it. Found by the tier-2 gate on PR #969 (KS-1069) as F1 (the persisted half) and O1 (the live half); PR #969 merged with E7 STRICT by ruling, so this ticket carries the root fix — not the PR.

Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks1069-969-fb23ca6aa-tier2-r1/report.md` — §4 (the F1 chain), FINDINGS F1, Open O1, WHAT WAS NOT TESTED item 1.

## The chain (READ ONLY from source at develop `0f69129b3`; line numbers as printed there)

1. **anchoring** `src/index.ts:604` — `blockNumber: onChain?.blockNumber || row?.block_number || null,` on the DB leg of `GET /api/anchors/verify/:hash` (`:633-647`). `onChain` is the stored `metadata_payload`, which never carries `blockNumber` (`anchorSchema.ts buildFlatAnchorMetadataPayload`, 0 hits), so the value is `row.block_number` **raw**. The column is `BIGINT` (`:181`; migrations `001:717`, `003:29`). `pg` 8.20.0 returns int8 as a string by default, and **no** `setTypeParser` **/ int8 parser exists anywhere in** `Blockchain/Dev` (non-test, non-lock: 0). The same file converts that column with `Number()` at `:1314` (`blockNumber`), `:1315` (`slot`), `:1320` (`fee`) — the control that says the authors know.
2. **originate** `src/routes/verification.ts:338` — `confirmStalePendingAnchor` (`:293-348`) composes the healed blob with `blockHeight: chain.blockNumber ?? blob.blockHeight ?? 0`, where `chain` is anchoring's reply above; `persistHealedAnchor` **(**`:359-369`**) persists it** via `updateDocument(…, { blockchain: healed })` (`:366`) when the heal moved the status to `confirmed`. Called from `POST /api/verification/verify` (`:1082-1083`) and `/verify-file` (`:657-658`). This is the KS-584 heal path (PR #666, merged 2026-08-12) — the writer the E7 ruling's census ("every originate writer stores a number") did not see.
3. **api-gateway** `src/routes/verification.ts` — the persisted tier-1 read at `:623` (head numbering; `typeof persistedBlockHeight === 'number'`, PR #969) now refuses that string, so a healed document answers `verified:false` / `off-chain-only` where develop-before-#969 said on-chain — **only while the gateway's own live scan does not answer** (`:569-585`: anchoring unreachable, the 2.5 s timeout at `:570`, token refused, or `doc.contentHash` missing); when it does, `Number()` at `:582` coerces and `liveAnchored` wins. Tier 2 is unaffected (`rowToAnchor`).
4. **The live half (O1, MEASURED + READ ONLY):** the live chain-scan path (`:579-582`, `:645`) has no shape rule — `j.verified` truthiness (a string `'false'` counts), `liveTxHash` truthiness (`1`, a placeholder), `Number(blockNum)` coercion, no sign/integer rule (`-1`, `4242.5` on-chain), `simulated` ignored. Every L row on-chain at both SHAs. Safe today only because anchoring's `buildResponse :595-598` nulls placeholders and emits the literal `verified: true` — a response-shape accident, and its `:604` raw BIGINT pass is the same root as item 1. Blast radius = anything that can answer the gateway's `/api/anchors/verify/:hash` call.

**Evidence classes, as the report states them:** READ ONLY (the chain above) + PROBED (`pg-types` `getTypeParser(20)("4242")` → `"4242"`, `typeof string`, from the checkout's `node_modules`) + MEASURED (the shape: matrix cell `G:'4242':t1` on-chain at develop, off-chain-only at head). **Not run against a database.** F1's producible path is read from source, not reproduced end-to-end.

## Checklist (one test pass; RULED 2026-09-13)

- [ ] anchoring `src/index.ts:604`: `Number(row.block_number)` as `:1314` already does (null-safe: a null row stays null).
- [ ] originate `src/routes/verification.ts:338`: `Number(chain.blockNumber)` (or coerce once where `chain` is parsed), so the heal persists a number.
- [ ] Regression cell (prose, originate): a `submitted` blob with a real 64-hex hash healed via a stubbed anchoring reply `{verified:true, txHash, blockNumber:'4242'}` persists `typeof blockHeight === 'number'`. Red at develop (`'4242'` persisted), green after.
- [ ] The live chain-scan shape rule at api-gateway `src/routes/verification.ts:579-582, :645` (O1's class): `verified === true`, the KS-522 placeholder rule on `liveTxHash`, `Number.isInteger(h) && h > 0` on the height, `simulated` read — the same three guards PR #969 gave the persisted read, applied to the live read; cells for each.
- [ ] **The JSONB round-trip, measured in BOTH directions (KS-1069 item 1 — NOT TESTED by #969 or its gate; moved here so it survives KS-1069's archive).** Source implies type preservation: originate writes `JSON.stringify({…, blockchain})::jsonb` (`documentRepo.ts:523-532`, `:545-546`) and reads back Prisma's parsed JSONB (`:162`) — a JS number should come back a number, a string a string (which is what makes the persisted string above a string). **If that expectation were false the other way (every number read back as a string), E7's guard would refuse every persisted height and every tier-1 confirmed document — the four seeded demo documents included — would answer off-chain-only: a demo-visible blast radius.** Nothing proves it either way yet; measure against a real Postgres, both directions, before or alongside the fixes above.

## Deliberately not here

* The gateway's persisted guard itself (E7 STRICT) — shipped in #969, ruled. Coercing at the gateway was option (b); the ruling kept (a): fix the root.
* The `persistedStatus == null` carve-out — KS-1073 / KS-1068 territory.
* The presentation question (a placeholder echoed in `blockchain.txHash` with `source:'persisted'`) — recorded on the #969 verdict, not raised.

## Ancestry and neighbours (named, not related — see Dedupe)

* **KS-584** (P1, "Verify by hash selects the wrong registration: certified documents report as unanchored, and tenant fields leak") is the ancestor: its fix, PR #666 (merged 2026-08-12, verified live on demo 2026-08-14, S-side confirmation 2026-08-19), introduced the heal path at item 2. **KS-584 is archived (2026-08-19T02:00Z, Deployed to UAT)**, so Linear refuses a relation to it; it is named here instead.
* **KS-590** (Peter's, Backlog, parked on KS-584 — the systemTest side of the same class); **KS-607** (GET /api/anchors/{id} vs verify status divergence — the same `buildResponse` territory, status not height); **KS-1004** (the anchor-failed guard keys off the hash; traces `block_number` writers for a different reason). A reader arriving from any of the three finds this ticket the home of the height-shape defect.

## Dedupe, before filing (s205, 2026-09-13)

Literal census over 1,118 KS issues (691 archived) and 912 comments, by SYMBOL and path — `persistHealedAnchor` 0 · `setTypeParser` 0 · `BIGINT` 0 · `liveAnchored` 0 · `confirmStalePendingAnchor` → KS-590 (comment) · `buildResponse` → KS-1119, KS-521, KS-584, KS-590 · `block_number` → KS-1004, KS-607, KS-1070, KS-1057 · `/api/anchors/verify` → KS-489, KS-590, KS-683 · `JSONB` → KS-1069, KS-1115, KS-472, KS-537, KS-593, KS-787. Every hit's description read: none names the raw BIGINT pass or the heal path's string height. Controls fired (`persistedStatus == null` → KS-1073; `crossTenantLookup` → KS-1119 + KS-584; a nonsense token → 0).

## Provenance

* Tier-2 gate on PR #969 at `fb23ca6aa`, 2026-09-13 (report path above): F1 (Minor, against the ruling's premise), O1 (Open, the class outside the ticket), NOT TESTED item 1.
* Wednesday's rulings on the verdict, 2026-09-13 16:24 AEST: E7 STRICT stands; the root fix travels here; the JSONB half of KS-1069 item 1 moves here; ONE Medium ticket, related KS-1069 (KS-584 named, not related — it is archived; ruled 16:51 AEST).
* Filed by s205 (the merge seat for #969) at the per-PR order's step 1, before KS-1069's archive.

title: The platform tenant seed's catch logs `Platform tenant seed skipped` at debug — the KS-962 class on the platform-DB path: a seed that cannot seed reports into a level the demo does not read
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`, inside `runStartupMigrations()`'s platform stage (`if (platformDbUrl)` → the `pSeedPool` block that inserts Secuura Co. + five client tenants + `tenant_config`): the seed's own catch is

```ts
} catch (seedErr: any) {
  log('debug', 'Platform tenant seed skipped', { error: seedErr?.message?.substring(0, 80) });
}
```

The main-DB user statement had the identical shape (`log('debug', 'User seed skipped', …)`) and it hid a statement that threw on every boot for as long as encryption had been live — KS-962's own words: *a defect that reports itself into a channel nobody is watching is indistinguishable from no defect.* The KS-950/KS-962 round raised the main-DB arm to warn and left this one alone by ruling (the platform seed does not move in that round).

## What is owed

* Raise the arm to `warn` with a message that names it a failure (`Platform tenant seed FAILED (platform DB)`), error text to 200 chars, in the same shape as the main-DB arm.
* A cell that proves it: boot the real `runStartupMigrations()` with `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` pointing at a database whose `tenants` table cannot take the insert, and assert the `[WARN]` line. The ks949 suite's boot driver (a mkdtemp `tsx` script importing `runStartupMigrations()` against a socket-only PostgreSQL) is the pattern; the platform path was **not** exercised in that round (`PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` unset — stated in its PR's NOT run).

## Not this ticket

Whether the platform seed's `ON CONFLICT (slug) DO NOTHING` INSERT and the `tenant_config` upsert are themselves correct on the deployed platform schema — nobody has measured that on a real platform database in this round; KS-1055 covers the tenant-migration path.

description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-shell-suites.sh` scores a suite by its exit code only: `if bash "$REPO_ROOT/$rel"; then pass=$((pass + 1))`. A suite that cannot run its cells and exits 0 with a SKIP line is counted as **passed**, and the runner's verdict `shell suites: N passed, M failed (of K)` — the line preflight leg 14 prints and PR Test Evidence blocks quote — is the same whether that suite ran all its cells or none.

## Where it bites today

`scripts/__tests__/ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh` (KS-962 / KS-950 round, PR on `feature/ks-950-the-boot-seed-dies-permanently-at-boot-2-migration-030-drops`) needs a PostgreSQL keg. Ruled 2026-09-13: on a box without one it prints `SKIP — no PostgreSQL binaries (initdb pg_ctl postgres psql) found; searched: …; 0/26 cells run` and exits 0, so a push from such a box is not refused. The runner then reports it as one of the `passed` — the suite's own SKIP line is the only honest signal, and it sits above the verdict, not in it.

This is the class STANDING_LINES names as *a verdict composed separately from the work*: ask what the runner would print if half the work never ran — the same thing.

## What is owed (the durable fix; not in the ks949 round's files)

* The runner recognises a skip: a suite that prints a line matching `^\s*SKIP —` (or exits with an agreed code, e.g. 3) and exits 0 is tallied as **skipped**, not passed.
* The verdict carries the ratio: `shell suites: N passed, M failed, S skipped (of K)` — and leg 14 quotes that line.
* `run_shell_suites.test.sh` gains a cell: a fixture suite that prints SKIP and exits 0 is counted under `skipped`, and a control fixture that prints nothing and exits 0 stays `passed`.
* Whether a skip should fail a push is a policy decision to record beside the tally (today: no — ruled for the ks949 suite).

## Not this ticket

KS-1046 is the same class one level up (the preflight's `PREFLIGHT PASSED.` has no skip tally over its 14 legs). KS-910 is leg 12 running zero cells by design. Neither covers the per-suite tally inside leg 14.

## Provenance

Measured 2026-09-13 by s201 while adding the ks949 suite: `run-shell-suites.sh` at develop `0f69129b3` (the `bash "$REPO_ROOT/$rel"` branch); the SKIP behaviour ruled by Wednesday's ANSWER to s201's plan confirmation (05:40:37Z). Board searched by `run-shell-suites`, `skip tally`, `exit-0 SKIP` before filing: KS-1089, KS-1088, KS-1086, KS-1046, KS-948, KS-926, KS-910, KS-903 — none is this.

title: originate: a non-prod certification whose anchoring submission FAILED persists `confidence:'pending-onchain'` beside `anchoringStatus:'failed'` and is reported "pending-onchain" by the gateway indefinitely; and the thread-token mint REPLACES the document's blockchain blob (a fifth statusless producer, racing the anchor accept write) (QA-967/968 F4 + O1)
description:
## BLUF

Two READ ONLY findings in originate's `blockchain`-blob writers, recorded by the tier-2 gate on the #967 → #968 stack (KS-1071 / KS-1070) as Option B's blast radius — the gateway now honours a statusless blob's `confidence:'pending-onchain'` literal by ruling, and these are the producers of that literal. Neither is the PRs' change; both are pre-existing and identical at base. **F4:** `routes/certifications.ts:406-469` (and `:1131-1191`) sets `anchoringStatus='failed'` by default and `'submitted'` only if anchoring accepted (`:429`); in production a failure 503s (`:435`), but in non-prod it **persists** `{anchorId, txHash:null, blockHeight:null, anchoredAt:null, confidence:'pending-onchain', anchoringStatus:'failed'}`, and `:510` copies `certification.blockchain` verbatim onto the NEW document created at certify. The gateway reads neither `anchoringStatus` nor `anchorId`, no poller exists in `certifications.ts` (0 `updateDocument` / `pollAnchorUntilConfirmed` references), and `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` needs `bc.anchorId` (`anchorStateSync.ts:298`), which is `undefined` on the failed leg — so that document answers **pending-onchain at base,** `51e74ea7a` **and** `1b7c03a22` (the row was driven) for as long as it exists. **O1:** `routes/documents.ts:764-774` (the thread-token mint callback) writes `blockchain: { ...(create-time blob = nothing), threadToken }` via `updateDocument`, which **replaces** the blob (`documentRepo.ts:510-514`: `{...doc, ...updates, updatedAt}` — `updates.blockchain` replaces `doc.blockchain` wholesale). The auto-anchor accept write (`:880`) is also fire-and-forget; whichever resolves later wins. If the mint lands after the anchor accept, the document's `txHash` / `status` / `anchorId` are lost until the poller rewrites — and the confirmed-path rewrite (`anchorStateSync.ts:206-216`) does not carry `threadToken` back; only the failed path (`:160`) does. Gateway effect of the `{threadToken}`-only blob: off-chain-only at every SHA (driven, harmless); the race itself is originate's.

## Recommendation

One logical path — originate's statusless `pending-onchain` producers and the blob-replacing writers — so one ticket; split only if the two fixes land separately:

1. **F4:** on the failed leg, do not persist `confidence:'pending-onchain'` (write no `confidence`, or a `status` the gateway's closed mapping reads as off-chain-only), and/or make the gateway's Option-B arm read `anchoringStatus`; add a certifications cell asserting a failed submission never presents pending-onchain through the gateway. Prove the row first with the gate's Sweep B shape.
2. **O1:** merge rather than replace in the mint callback (spread the CURRENT persisted blob, not the create-time local), and carry `threadToken` through the confirmed-path rewrite as the failed path already does; a cell that lands the mint after the accept write and asserts `txHash` / `status` / `anchorId` survive. Prove the race first (it was READ, not reproduced).

## Detail

* **Where (READ ONLY at** `721b333a6`**):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:406-469`, `:429`, `:435`, `:510`, `:1131-1191`; `routes/documents.ts:764-774` (`:766` the only spread of a prior blob into a write — and `document` there is the create-time local from `:650`, which has no `blockchain` key), `:864-876` / `:880` (the accept write), `:895-903` (the failure write), `:1341-1351` / `:1367-1372` (the retry route's blobs); `repositories/documentRepo.ts:510-514`; `services/anchorStateSync.ts:146`, `:160`, `:206-216`, `:212`, `:247`, `:298`, `:320`, `:348`.
* **Writer census (the gate's,** `git grep -n "pending-onchain" 721b333a6 -- …/originate/src`**, non-test):** five literals — `documents.ts:1371`, `certifications.ts:467`, `:1189` (persisted), `anchors.ts:347`, `:441` (202 bodies, not writes). The status-writers never write `confidence`, and every one REPLACES the blob. Conclusion carried: no writer at develop can leave a blob carrying BOTH `status` and a stale `confidence` — which is why F2's guard is unpinned rather than wrong.
* **Serve boundary:** `GET /api/documents/:id` serves `{anchored, ...composeHonestBlockchainBlob(document.blockchain)}` (`documents.ts:1061-1072`; `anchorHonesty.ts:92-106`), which returns the blob unchanged unless `simulated === true` or the hash has a fabricated prefix — so `status` and `confidence` reach the gateway exactly as persisted.
* **Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks1071-1070-967-968-1b7c03a22-tier2-r1/report.md`, §2 "Option B proved, and its blast radius" (R1), FINDINGS F4, "Open — for Wednesday" O1. NOT TESTED: no running originate; the writer census and the race are from source.
* **Related:** KS-1071 (PR #967, Option B ruled there); KS-1073 (the gateway's tier-2 statusless-blob cell — the consumer side of the same literal); KS-1074 (the poller/reconcile writers erase `threadToken` on the CONFIRM/heal path — O1 is its mirror: the mint erases the anchor fields); KS-1058 (the `markDocumentAnchorFailed` erasure already fixed).
* **Dedupe, before filing (s200, 2026-09-13):** literal census over 1,106 KS issues (685 archived) and 899 comments — `pending-onchain` → KS-1057, KS-1068, KS-1071, KS-607, KS-834 + archived (none about the failed-leg persistence); `certifications.ts` → 15 issues, none this; `anchoringStatus` → 0; `thread token` / `threadToken` → KS-1074 (the mirror), KS-1058 (archived), KS-1004, KS-1068 — none describes the mint replacing the blob. Controls: `persistedStatus == null` → KS-1073; a nonsense token → 0.

description:
## BLUF

Coverage and claim-accuracy findings from the tier-2 gate on the #967 → #968 stack (KS-1071, KS-1070; merged 2026-09-13). The shipped code is right on every one of 119 status × tier × shape cells driven over real HTTP at three SHAs; what is missing is the pin. **F3 (Blocker-class blast radius if it regresses):** `persistedStatus = … ?? null` at `routes/verification.ts:597` (stack head numbering) — changing `??` to `||` flips six cells (`""`, `0`, `false` status with a real hash and height, both tiers) from off-chain-only to **on-chain /** `verified:true`, and 0 of 331 tests red. `""` is a value `anchor_store.status TEXT` can hold (no CHECK constraint — KS-1115); `0`/`false` are what a loose JSON writer yields. **F1:** the tier-2 comment `:334-342` says a second mapping copy "would be unreachable … this one always has [a status]" — true only by anchoring's `index.ts:1544` + `NOT NULL` guarantee, not the blob's; restoring the old ternary reds 0 of 331 while moving four tier-2 rows (`ABSENT`/`null`/statusless-with-confidence/`ABSENT+hash+sim`) from off-chain-only to pending-onchain. **F2:** "the fallback is for STATUSLESS blobs only" (`:680` `persistedStatus == null &&`) — dropping the conjunct reds 0 of 331 while five tier-1 both-keys rows move up to pending-onchain. **P1–P3:** `:644` "(line 265)" points at a line #967 moved to `:312`; the BACKLOG #G6 JSDoc (`:201-216`) is orphaned by the KS-1071 insert; the PR body's census line numbers (`:581`/`:663`/`:479`) match no committed SHA, and "ONE mapping" over-reads for the on-chain claim (the mapping's `'on-chain'` arm is consumed by no route path — `persistedAnchored` alone decides it).

## Recommendation

One test pass in `src/__tests__/ks1071-verify-confidence-one-mapping.test.ts` (or a sibling), F3 first:

1. **F3 — one cell, both tiers:** tier-1 `{txHash:<64-hex>, blockHeight:4242, status:''}` and the tier-2 twin → `verified:false`, `verificationConfidence:'off-chain-only'`. Red-proof: `??`→`||` at `:597` must red it.
2. **F1 — one tier-2 cell:** `{transactionHash:null, blockNumber:null}` with no `status` key → `'off-chain-only'`, `verified:false` (this is also KS-1073's cell — land it once); reword `:334-342` to "anchoring emits `status` unconditionally (`index.ts:1544`) over `TEXT NOT NULL`, so a tier-2 record without `status` is not producible today; if one arrives, the Option-B arm cannot read a confidence this blob no longer carries and it answers off-chain-only (closed)".
3. **F2 — one tier-1 cell:** `{txHash:null, blockHeight:0, status:'anchor_failed', confidence:'pending-onchain'}` → `'off-chain-only'` (the positive side, `{status:'pending', confidence:'pending-onchain'}` → `'pending-onchain'`, is C-pending already).
4. **P1–P3:** cite `:312` or drop the number at `:644`; move the G6 JSDoc to sit above `function makeFetchDocFromAnchorStore` (`:263`); the PR-body numbers are history — nothing to change in code; whether the title should say the on-chain decision stays `persistedAnchored`'s is the coordinator's call.

## Detail

* **Where (stack head** `1b7c03a22` **numbering):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` — `:597` (`??`), `:656` (the carve-out), `:680` (`persistedStatus == null &&`), `:334-342` (the tier-2 comment), `:644`/`:628`/`:646` (pointers; the latter two pre-date #967, from `dd9463b37`), `:201-216` (the G6 JSDoc), `:263` (`makeFetchDocFromAnchorStore`); tests `ks1071-verify-confidence-one-mapping.test.ts` (header `:33-36`, `:49-50`).
* **F3 (MEASURED AT RUNTIME):** tamper Tc (`??`→`||`) → 0 of 331 red; under it `A:"":t1`, `A:"":t2`, `A:0:t1`, `A:0:t2`, `A:false:t1`, `A:false:t2` all flip off-chain-only → on-chain / `verified:true` (hash + height present). As shipped all six answer off-chain-only at every SHA (Sweep A). Attribution: the `??` is base code and KS-1057 did not pin it either — pre-existing gap; #967 is the PR that now presents the closed default as pinned (C4/C5/C6), so it is the natural home.
* **F1 (MEASURED):** tamper Tx (old ternary restored) → 0 of 331 red, moves `B:ABSENT:t2`, `B:null:t2`, `B:OB-statusless-confidence:t2`, `C:ABSENT+hash+sim:true:t2` from off-chain-only to pending-onchain; base answered pending-onchain from that copy, head answers off-chain-only, and no cell in either PR pins the move (the builder recorded it under KS-1073 in PR #967 comment 5650200989).
* **F2 (MEASURED):** tamper Tb (drop `persistedStatus == null &&`) → 0 of 331 red; five tier-1 both-keys cells move up to pending-onchain. The shape is unproducible today (the gate's writer census over every originate `blockchain` writer at `721b333a6`), so nothing is wrong at head — but the guard that keeps a future writer's stale `confidence` from out-voting a terminal `status` can be deleted with the suite green.
* **Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks1071-1070-967-968-1b7c03a22-tier2-r1/report.md`, FINDINGS F1, F2, F3, P1, P2, P3; §1 the 119-cell matrix; §5 red-proof.
* **Related:** KS-1071 (PR #967) and KS-1070 (PR #968) — one file, one test pass, so one ticket carrying both ids; KS-1057 (the status-aware confidence this builds on); KS-1073 (the tier-2 statusless cell, = item 2 above); KS-1115 (the CHECK constraint that would make `""` unstorable); KS-1069 (PR #969, the input-shape validation, stacked on #968).
* **Dedupe, before filing (s200, 2026-09-13):** literal census over 1,106 KS issues (685 archived) and 899 comments — `confidenceForAnchorStatus` → KS-1071 (a comment) only; `api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` → 13 issues incl. KS-1057, KS-1069, KS-1070, KS-1072, KS-1073, KS-1083, KS-1084 — none pins the `""`/`0`/`false` status or the two claims. Controls: `persistedStatus == null` → KS-1073; a nonsense token → 0.

title: Security (multi-tenant only): POST /api/verification/verify can answer verified:true for a WRONG hash — crossTenantLookup's by-documentId fallback feeds buildResponse with hashMatch hard-coded true (QA-965 O-1)
description:
## BLUF

READ ONLY finding from the tier-2 gate on PR #965 (KS-1103), not driven: when `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` and the local hash SELECT misses, strategy 1 calls `crossTenantLookup(documentId || '', computedHash)` (`routes/verification.ts:910` at `d63b27ab3`). Inside, the registry is searched by `document_id` FIRST (`:417-421`), then the tenant DB by hash, **then it falls back to** `WHERE d.external_id = $1` **by documentId (**`:457-466`**)** — and the returned row goes to `buildResponse(docRow, true, …)` (`:1087`) with `hashMatch` hard-coded **true**. So `{documentId:X, <alias>:WRONG}` with a registry hit for X answers `verified:true, hashValid:true` for a hash that does not match. Pre-existing for `contentHash` / `providedHash` / `documentHash`; #965 adds `hash` as a fourth key into the same path (no caller sends it). **Dormant in the live single-tenant configuration** (`db.ts:22, 347-359`: `tenantManager` is built only with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` and `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL`); severity there would be Major (a confident false "verified"). Adjacent, not the same defect: KS-590 (Peter, parked on KS-584) covers the by-hash path resolving to an arbitrary registration and names `crossTenantLookup` as unscoped; this ticket is the by-documentId fallback plus the hard-coded `hashMatch`.

## Recommendation

1. **Prove it first, live:** one probe with multi-tenancy enabled — register X in tenant A, send `{documentId:X, contentHash:<wrong 64-hex>}` from a caller whose local SELECT misses, and record the answer. Expected today: `verified:true`. The gate could not drive it (`getTenantManager()` was null in every row).
2. **Fix-shape (for the owner):** never pass `hashMatch=true` from the by-id fallback — compute it by comparing the row's `content_hash` with the sent hash (as the local path does), or refuse the by-id fallback when a hash was supplied and does not match. Add one cell per alias (`hash`, `contentHash`, `providedHash`, `documentHash`) asserting `verified:false` / `hashValid:false` for a wrong hash with a registry hit.
3. Sequence with KS-584 / KS-590 (the resolution-model decision) so the assertion pins a chosen behaviour.

## Detail

* **Where (READ ONLY at** `d63b27ab3`**):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts` — `:910` the `crossTenantLookup(documentId || '', computedHash)` call from strategy 1; `:417-421` registry search by `document_id`; `:457-466` the `WHERE d.external_id = $1` fallback; `:1087` `buildResponse(docRow, true, …)`; `db.ts:22, 347-359` the multi-tenancy gate.
* **Callers that send the pairing today:** mcp-server (`{documentId, contentHash}`), e2e-v2 (`{documentId, providedHash}`), USER_TESTING v2.3's "Wrong hash → verified=false" cell — the last is the exact shape that would read TRUE under multi-tenancy.
* **Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks1103-965-d63b27ab3-tier2-r1/report.md`, "Observations, out of #965's scope", O-1; NOT TESTED names the path as not driven.
* **Related:** KS-1103 (PR #965, where `hash` joined the chain); KS-590 (the by-hash / cross-tenant field-disclosure half, parked on KS-584); KS-584 (the resolution-model decision).
* **Dedupe, before filing (s200, 2026-09-13):** literal census over 1,106 KS issues (685 archived) and 899 comments — `crossTenantLookup` → KS-584 (archived), KS-590 only; `hashMatch` → KS-563 only (isCertified vs verified, a different flag). Neither describes the by-id fallback answering a wrong hash TRUE. Controls: `LIKE` → KS-1020; a nonsense token → 0.

title: POST /api/verification/verify: the `documentHash`-over-`hash` precedence is unpinned, and the why-comment + test header overclaim "every body that worked before keeps its answer" (QA-965 F-2 + F-3)
description:
## BLUF

Two test-side gaps left by PR #965 (KS-1103, merged 2026-09-13), from its tier-2 gate; neither is a product defect and neither held the merge. (1) The alias chain `providedHash || contentHash || documentHash || hash` is pinned by test only against `contentHash` and `providedHash`: moving `hash` to THIRD leaves all 575 originate cells green, so the "read LAST" claim is not fully pinned. (2) The why-comment at `routes/verification.ts:739-740` and the test header at `ks1103-verify-hash-field.test.ts:15-17` say "every body that worked before keeps its answer" — two body shapes that worked at base now answer from a different strategy (no caller in the repo sends either; the new behaviour is v2's and arguably better), so the sentence, not the code, is wrong.

## Recommendation

One test pass, one file each:

1. **F-2 — add one cell** in the precedence block of `ks1103-verify-hash-field.test.ts`: `{documentHash:A, hash:B}` with no rows → 200, exactly 1 lookup, the lookup saw A (documentHash) and never B. The gate's T5 tamper (`hash` moved to third) is the red-proof: today it reds nothing.
2. **F-3 — narrow the two sentences** to: "every body carrying a pre-existing alias keeps its lookup value; documentId-only, documentData-only and alias bodies are unchanged; a body pairing `hash` with `documentId` or `documentData` now takes the hash strategy, as v2 already does — no caller in the repo sends that pairing."

## Detail

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts` — the chain at `:742` at `d63b27ab3` (`providedHash || contentHash || documentHash || hash`), the why-comment `:739-740`; `src/__tests__/ks1103-verify-hash-field.test.ts` header `:15-17` and its P block (P1 `{contentHash:A, hash:B}`, P2 `{providedHash:A, hash:B}`).
* **F-2, measured by the gate (MEASURED):** row P3 `{documentHash:A, hash:B}` → head saw A, never B (correct today); tamper T5 (`hash` moved to third) → 575/575 green, and the gate's probe on the tampered code moves exactly that row. Evidence: `evidence/jest-tamper-T5.summary.txt`, `evidence/probe-head-T5.json` in the report directory.
* **F-3, measured (MEASURED):** `{documentId:X, hash:B}` — base: strategy 2 (by id, 2 lookups saw X); head: strategy 1 (by hash, 1 lookup saw B), rows DH1/DH2/DH3. `{documentData:{…}, hash:B}` — base: hashes the data; head: uses the sent `hash` (DD1). The repo-wide caller census (73 files) finds no caller sending either pairing; DH3 shows a matching `hash` now proves integrity where base answered `verified:false` with a false "no hash was provided" warning.
* **Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks1103-965-d63b27ab3-tier2-r1/report.md`, FINDINGS F-2 and F-3; §2b rows P3, DH1–DH3, DD1.
* **Not in this ticket:** F-1 (v1 reads `hash` LAST, v2 reads it FIRST — the same conflicting body looks up two different hashes on the two public routes) is a product-consistency ruling, on the CTO's panel, not ticketed by the merge round.
* **Related:** KS-1103 (PR #965), KS-1114 (the `title`-only contract), KS-735 (verify-result display).
* **Dedupe, before filing (s200, 2026-09-13):** literal census over 1,106 KS issues (685 archived; titles + descriptions) and 899 comments on non-archived issues — `documentHash` → KS-1103, KS-1114, KS-256, KS-480 and four archived; `originate/src/routes/verification.ts` → 11 issues, none about the alias precedence pin or the comment's claim. Controls: `LIKE` → KS-1020; a nonsense token → 0.
