title: k6 YAML loader: a BOM immediately followed by a comment is a marked syntax error in js-yaml 5.2.3, so a comments-only config prints "at line 1, column 2" — strip a leading U+FEFF in readYaml() (QA-963-2)
description:
## BLUF

js-yaml 5.2.3 rejects a file whose first bytes are a byte-order mark followed directly by `#` as a marked syntax error ("end of the stream or a document separator is expected" at raw mark 0:1). `readYaml()` in `systemTest/performance/utils/yaml.ts` prints that mark faithfully, so a comments-only `secrets.yml` or `scenarios.yml` written by a BOM-emitting editor answers `Could not parse YAML in <file> at line 1, column 2 (the file's content is not shown).` — a verdict true of what the parser did and false of the file, which holds no document. Pre-existing and identical at base (`34be9c18a`); outside PR #963's promise; content-free on every path. Measured by the tier-2 gate on #963 (QA-963-2).

## Recommendation

One line in `readYaml()`: strip a leading U+FEFF from `source` before `loadYaml(source)`. That makes `<BOM># comment` read `: it contains no YAML document` (the KS-1109 wording) and, as a side effect, makes the K4 row print the editor's column rather than the BOM-shifted one. The alternative is to leave js-yaml's behaviour and document it in the loader's why-comment. Either way, add the two regression cells below.

## Detail

* **Where:** `systemTest/performance/utils/yaml.ts` (`readYaml()`, the `loadYaml(source)` call; the mark is printed at the lines the gate cites as `:68-70` at `90d7d0c75`). The parser behaviour is js-yaml 5.2.3 `dist/js-yaml.mjs` (READ ONLY by the gate: the BOM is not skipped before a `#` at position 1; `BOM + space + #` and `BOM + LF + #` parse; `BOM` alone and `BOM + LF` raise the "input is empty" constant).
* **Measured (gate evidence** `evidence/instruments/bom.mjs`**,** `evidence/probe963/`**,** `evidence/drives/`**):** `<BOM># c\n` → `YAMLException` at raw mark 0:1; probe rows E08 (BOM + comments holding a sentinel) and E21 (BOM + comment + `---`) print `at line 1, column 2` at head and base, 0 content in every rendering and in the uncaught print; drive D09 (`runner/cli.ts`, `secrets.yml` = BOM + a comment holding a sentinel) prints `[run] ERROR: … at line 1, column 2 (…)`, rc 1, 0 sentinels, at head and base alike. Rows E06 (BOM alone) and E07 (BOM + LF) already print `: it contains no YAML document`.
* **Blast radius:** `config/secrets.example.yml` begins with `#` (22 of 58 lines are comments), so `cp` + an editor that writes a BOM (Windows Notepad, some IDE encodings) lands a first-run operator on "line 1, column 2" of a file whose line 1 looks like a comment. The bootstrap hint is not involved.
* **Regression cells to add with the fix:** `'﻿# only a comment\n'` reads `: it contains no YAML document`; `'﻿admin:\n  a: 1\n'` still parses to `{admin:{a:1}}`.
* **Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-13-ks1109-963-90d7d0c75-tier2-r1/report.md`, FINDINGS QA-963-2 (severity Polish there; filed Low here as a one-line fix with a first-run operator in its blast radius).
* **Related:** KS-1109 (PR #963, the loader's wrapped-parse-failure round this was found in); KS-1110 (the two unit tests that bypass `readYaml()`), KS-1099 (the sanitiser this loader carries).
* **Dedupe, before filing (s200, 2026-09-13):** a literal census over 1,106 KS issues (685 archived, titles + descriptions) and 899 comments on non-archived issues — `readYaml` → KS-1099 (archived), KS-1109, KS-1110; `utils/yaml.ts` → the same plus KS-429 (archived); `BOM` → KS-975 only (a rateLimitScope input-shape table; unrelated). None describes the BOM-plus-comment mark. Controls: `LIKE` → KS-1020; a nonsense token → 0.

title: KS-1020 item 2: which subject OWNS a presentation (and a credential) — the ownership model for GET /api/presentations/:id and GET /credentials/:id, and the policy for the existing holder_id NULL rows
description:
## BLUF

**This is a decision for Kam, not a build.** KS-1020 recommendation item 2 — *"Add the ownership/tenant check the path never had"* — needs an ownership model before any code: which subject OWNS a presentation (and a credential), and what happens to the rows that have no owner today. Item 1 (exact-or-404) is PR #966 and closes KS-1020 on its merge; this ticket is where items 2 and 3 live.

## What was measured (develop `721b333a6`, `services/vc-issuer/src`)

* `holder_id` is written from `(presentation as any).holder || null` at `routes/presentations.ts:102` — non-null only when `POST /` was given `holderDID`; KS-1020 records every stored row as `holder_id NULL`.
* `GET /api/presentations/:id` sits behind `jwtAuthenticate` at `index.ts:86-92`, whose `publicOps` names only `POST /credentials/verify`, `POST /presentations/verify` and `GET /identity-credentials/types`; the spec agrees (`security: [{ bearerAuth: [] }]`, `vc-issuer.openapi.ts:1262`). So the caller is an authenticated bearer — **a SUBJECT exists** (`req.user`'s userId / organizationId) — but `routes/presentations.ts` never reads `req.user` (0 occurrences), and **no stored OWNER exists**: `holder_id` is a DID string when present and NULL otherwise, and the route writes no tenant/organisation column.
  * Correction of record: the s198 brief said *"*`GET /:id` *is mounted PUBLIC per the KS-442 note at* `:52-54`*"*. That note is about `/presentations/verify`. Wednesday has accepted the correction as her brief's error.
* The sibling `repositories/credentialRepo.getById` (`:75-108`, reached from `GET /credentials/:id` at `routes/credentials.ts:268`) has the same no-owner property; whatever is decided here applies to credentials too.
* Adjacent on Platform S, not touched: PS-690 (In Progress, Stuart) — *Adopt org-owned documents: ownership model for single- vs multi-user orgs, user/org deletion semantics, and the S→K erasure bridge*. The K-side answer here should not contradict whatever S adopts there.
* Adjacent ruling, not acted on: `secuura-org-trust-boundary-within-tenant` → **bind** (shipped in #954, on kintsugi). An ownership/tenant check on these paths is a trust-boundary question of the same family and should be decided against that ruling, not beside it.

## The decision needed

1. **What owns a presentation / a credential?** The minting caller's organisation, the holder DID mapped to a user, the tenant of the bearer — or something else.
2. **Policy for the existing** `holder_id NULL` **rows:** deny-all, allow-any-authenticated, or owner-less-means-issuer-org (with or without a backfill).
3. Then **item 3 of KS-1020**: re-test the cross-holder question against rows that actually carry an owner, so the inferred half of KS-1020 becomes measured either way.

## What is NOT established

* Cross-holder disclosure remains inferred from the mechanism, not measured (KS-1020's own bound).
* Whether any of this is reachable in a deployed environment — not probed; taken separately, per KS-1020.

## Provenance

Measured by s198 (seat D) on 2026-09-13 while shipping KS-1020 item 1 (PR #966 @ `1f0d08841`); filed on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-09-13 02:27:19Z ("its OWN ticket … Kam's decision, carded after #966's gate").

title: anchor_store.status has no CHECK constraint — an out-of-union status can be stored silently (producer side of KS-1071 F10)
description:
**BLUF:** `anchor_store.status` is `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'` with **no CHECK constraint**, so a status outside anchoring's union (`'pending' | 'submitted' | 'confirmed' | 'failed'`, `anchoring/src/index.ts:112`) can be written silently. KS-1071 closed the *consumer* side (the gateway's one status→confidence mapping now falls **closed** on any out-of-union value); this ticket is the *producer* side — a schema guard so the value cannot be stored in the first place.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:714` and `003_consolidate-anchors.sql:26` — the column, verified 0 CHECKs in the block against a control of 5 elsewhere in 001 (KS-1071's measurement).

**Fix shape:** a new migration adding `CHECK (status IN ('pending','submitted','confirmed','failed'))` on `anchor_store.status` — after a read-only census of the live rows on every environment (a row already holding another value would fail the migration; that row is a finding, not a reason to skip the constraint). Consider a shared TS status union exported from anchoring alongside it, so the code and the schema cannot drift apart silently.

**Why deferred from KS-1071:** a migration is out of that PR's scope by ruling (Wednesday, 2026-09-13 plan confirmation s199: "CHECK constraint → one Low ticket, not this round"). Migrations on this repo are baked into the `migrations` image — see the project CLAUDE.md note on rebuilding it, and KS-1031/#914's "migration 048 first" line before any deploy.

**Not covered here:** originate's own `document.blockchain.status` vocabulary (`anchor_failed`, `submitted`, `confirmed`) is a JSONB field, not this column; it lands on the gateway mapping's closed default and needs no schema change.

Source: KS-1071 F10 (QA tier-1 gate round 2 on #935); filed by s199 after a literal census of 1,104 issues for `anchor_store` + `CHECK` found no home (the only hit was KS-1071 itself). Related: KS-1071.

title: POST /api/verification/verify refuses a title-only body with 400, while the published VerifyRequest says 'Provide ONE OR MORE of documentId, hash, title, contentHash'
description:
## BLUF

* **A title-only verify body is refused.** The served spec's `VerifyRequest` says *"Provide ONE OR MORE of documentId, hash, title, contentHash. The verifier tries chain-first, then originate-id lookup, then hash/title strategies."* A body carrying only `title` gets 400.
* **Cause:** the handler validates `title` as a string and never reads it — there is no title lookup strategy in `/verify`.
* Pre-existing; found by s193's KS-1103 probe (row E3) on develop `34be9c18a`, re-measured by s197 on `b1cb8466f`. **Not fixed this round.**

## Recommendation

* Decide the contract first: either implement a title strategy in `/verify` (the spec promises one), or remove `title` from `VerifyRequest` and the two descriptions so the spec stops promising it. Then make the 400 description list what is actually required.
* This is a product call (what a title-only verify should return — a title is not unique and proves no integrity), not a one-line fix.

## Detail

* **Spec, in** `services/originate/src/originate.openapi.ts` **at** `d63b27ab3` **(PR #965's head; unchanged from** `b1cb8466f`**):**
  * `:551-552` — the `VerifyRequest` description quoted above;
  * `:1915-1916` — the operation description: *"provide documentId, hash, title, or contentHash. Strategy: chain-first → originate-id lookup → hash/title fallback."*;
  * `:1944` — the 400 description: *"Missing verification input (no documentId / hash / documentData)"* — it does not list `title` either, so the spec contradicts itself on this field.
* **Handler,** `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts` **at** `d63b27ab3`**:**
  * `:705` — `body('title').optional().isString()` is in the validator chain (KS-222);
  * `:735` — the destructure reads `documentId, providedHash, documentData, contentHash, documentHash, hash` — not `title`;
  * `:744-750` — a body with none of documentId / a hash alias / documentData answers 400. The handler has 0 reads of `req.body.title` (the four `title` occurrences in `:695-760` are a comment, the validator, a comment and the 400 message).
* **Measured:** `{title:'x'}` → 400, 0 lookups, on ks584-verify-row-selection's harness at develop `b1cb8466f` (s197 ITEM 0 probe, row E3; `5_Project_History/quarantine/2026-09-13-s197/probes/`). The KS-1103 test pins this row at 400 on both sides of that fix (cell E3, status only) precisely because this ticket owns the title question.
* **History:** KS-222 (archived) put `title` into the validator chain with every other `VerifyRequest` field; nothing has ever read it. KS-1103 (PR #965) fixed the sibling case for `hash`, which HAD a lookup path; `title` has none.
* **Who is affected:** any integrator who follows the published description. The mobile app and the portals send hashes or ids, not a bare title (verify call sites: `mobile/secuura-app/src/services/api.ts:157-158`; `frontend/verifier/src/components/VerifyPage.tsx:127`).

### Dedupe

* **Census 1 (s193, 2026-09-12 05:4xZ):** literal, case-insensitive, over 1,100 KS issues (683 archived; title and description) and 2,954 comments (includeArchived). Positive control `hashToVerify` → KS-1103 (issue), KS-222 (comment). 0 hits for 'one or more of documentId', 'title strategies', 'title-only', 'title only', 'by id, hash, or title'. Weak hits, none covering it: 'hash/title' in a KS-474 comment (transfer snapshots); `VerifyRequest` on KS-627 (wallet verify contract) and KS-735.
* **Census 2 (s197, 2026-09-13 ~09:39 AEST), the delta since 2026-09-12T05:40Z:** searched `VerifyRequest`, `hashToVerify`, `originate.openapi.ts`, `routes/verification.ts`, the literal 'ONE OR MORE of documentId' and 'title-only' over 1 new KS issue (KS-1111) and 8 new KS comments — 0 hits each. Server-side all-time search for the two phrases: 0. Positive control (server-side `hashToVerify`) → KS-1103.
* **KS-735, opened whole:** it is about what the verify RESPONSE renders (registered title/issuer never displayed by the portal; the presented `fileName` discarded) — a different defect on the same contract. It never claims a title-only REQUEST should work. Not this ticket's home.
* **Result:** no existing home.

## Related

* KS-1103 — the `hash` sibling (PR #965).
* KS-222 (archived) — the validator chain.
* KS-735 — the verify-result display ticket on the same `VerifyRequest` contract.

title: e2e gdpr-compliance.prelaunch.spec.ts 15.2.5 PATCHes a DSR with status 'processed', a value DSR_STATUSES does not contain — the cell 400s at every SHA and cannot pass (QA-962 O-2)
description:
## BLUF

The e2e cell `15.2.5 Process DSR — admin marks DSR as processed via API` (`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/gdpr-compliance.prelaunch.spec.ts:425-488`) creates a DSR, then PATCHes `${dsrPath}/${dsrId}` with `status: 'processed'` (line 464), and on a 4xx retries with PUT carrying the same body (line 475). The route's body schema is `status: z.enum(DSR_STATUSES)` with `DSR_STATUSES = ['pending', 'processing', 'completed', 'denied', 'extended']` (`services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts:80, :89`). `'processed'` is not in the enum, so the PATCH answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR before any id or lookup logic runs, at base and at head alike (the tier-2 gate on PR #962 measured it; it is pre-existing and not #962's). The PUT fallback has no route. A test that cannot pass is a defect in the suite: it reports the product as failing to process a DSR when the product refused a status the test invented.

## Recommendation

One change in the spec file, proven by one run of the cell against a local stack:

1. send a value the enum accepts — `'processing'` for the mark-in-progress step, or `'completed'` for the terminal step (`TERMINAL_DSR_STATUSES` in `gdprService.ts:1077`) — and assert the 200 `{success:true, message:'DSR updated'}` the route returns for a real id;
2. drop the PUT fallback (no PUT route exists; the fallback only doubles the failure);
3. optionally add one negative cell asserting that `'processed'` answers 400, so the vocabulary is pinned from the e2e side too.

Keep `failOnStatusCode: false` and the NOT-IMPLEMENTED guards as they are.

## Detail

* **Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-12-ks1029-962-ac6f4fa91-tier2-r1-relaunch-20260913b/report.md`, Observations O-2 and §3 (callers that PATCH `/dsr/:dsrId`). Recorded in the verdict comments on PR #962 and KS-1029 as "not filed by this round"; filed now on Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER s196, 2026-09-12T23:44:51Z).
* **Related:** KS-1112 (the PATCH 200-vs-404 split on the same route), KS-1029 (the malformed-id guard, PR #962, Done + archived).
* **Dedupe, before filing:** a literal census over 1,101 KS issues (684 archived) and their comments on non-archived issues — `'processed'` 0 hits, `gdpr-compliance.prelaunch` 0 hits. Controls: `UUID_PATTERN` → KS-1029 (1); a nonsense token → 0.

title: PATCH /api/gdpr/dsr/{dsrId} answers "DSR not found" with 200 for a canonical absent id and 404 for a non-canonical one, while GET answers 404 for both — align or document (QA-962 F-2)
description:
## BLUF

After PR #962 (KS-1029), `PATCH /api/gdpr/dsr/:dsrId` answers "DSR not found" with two different statuses depending on the spelling of the id:

* a canonical (8-4-4-4-12) id that names no row → `200 {success:false, message:'DSR not found'}` — unchanged from base, deliberately preserved by #962;
* a non-canonical id (malformed, hyphenless, braced, uppercase hyphenless, hyphen-after-any-four) → `404 NOT_FOUND 'DSR not found'`, no DB call.

`GET /dsr/:dsrId` answers 404 for both (`getDSR` swallows the 22P02 and returns null). Neither PATCH answer is spec-invalid: the spec's own 200 description reads "DSR updated (success=false if id not found)" and 404 is declared. This is an internal-consistency gap, not a defect in #962. Measured at runtime by the tier-2 gate on #962 (rows A1 vs M1).

## Recommendation

One decision, then one small change: either

1. align PATCH's canonical-absent answer with GET's 404 (change `routes/gdpr.ts`'s `res.json({ success: updated, ... })` branch to 404 when `updated` is false, update the spec's 200 description, and add one cell), or
2. document the split in the spec's 200 and 404 descriptions and in the route's comment, and add one cell pinning each answer.

Whichever is chosen, keep KS-754's behaviour (a DB error stays a loud 500) and the body checks before the guard.

## Detail

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts` — the PATCH `/dsr/:dsrId` handler's `res.json({ success: updated, message: updated ? 'DSR updated' : 'DSR not found' })` (the 200 path) and the `UUID_PATTERN` guard #962 added (the 404 path); `originate.openapi.ts` PATCH `/api/gdpr/dsr/{dsrId}` responses 200 and 404.
* **Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-12-ks1029-962-ac6f4fa91-tier2-r1-relaunch-20260913b/report.md`, FINDINGS F-2 and §2 (rows A1, M1; the GET sibling in §4).
* **Related:** KS-1029 (PR #962, the guard), KS-754 (the 200 `{success:false}` path on a real id, fixed by #914).
* **Dedupe, before filing:** a literal census over 1,101 KS issues (684 archived) and their comments — `routes/gdpr.ts` (9 issues), `success:false` / `success: false` (8 / 10), `DSR not found` (KS-1029, KS-754 only), `/dsr/:dsrId` and `/dsr/{dsrId}`. The only issues naming both the route and `success:false` are KS-1029 (its base/head table) and KS-730 (err.message leaks). None describes the 200-vs-404 split. Controls: `UUID_PATTERN` → KS-1029 (1); a nonsense token → 0.

title: k6 echo mask reads one argument of lookbehind — a flag value that looks like an env flag prints the next env assignment in clear (QA-961-1..3; two regressions from #961)
description:
## BLUF

PR #961 (KS-1098) masks every single env spelling docker and k6 accept: 51 of 51 rows, 27 of which printed in clear at base. Its tier-2 QA gate (GO WITH FINDINGS at `644965d9095a962e783bd3d16fef588301c1ede6`) found three latent gaps in `systemTest/performance/runner/k6_docker.ts`, all in one function and fixable in one pass.

* **All three need an argv that no caller builds today:** `cli.ts:221` hard-codes `extraFlags: []`, and `buildEnvFlags()` (`env_flags.ts:143`) emits only `-e NAME=VALUE` pairs.
* **Two of QA-961-1's seven leaking argvs (L02 and L03) were masked at base and print in clear at head.** They are latent regressions introduced by #961.
* **The JSDoc claim at** `k6_docker.ts:141` ("read the way docker and k6 read flags") does not hold for these argvs.

## Recommendation

One fix in `runner/k6_docker.ts` plus its test rows, proven by one pass of the unit suite with the new rows red first:

1. **QA-961-1.** When the lookbehind branch matches, also apply the `--env=` and attached-short-flag masks to the current argument if `maskEnvAssignment` leaves it unchanged. That is the gate's fix-shape (a), recorded here as the gate's proposal, not a ruling. The alternative is (b): narrow the JSDoc. Either way, add the gate's three rows.
2. **QA-961-2.** Add rows for `-Pe NAME=VALUE` and `-diteNAME=VALUE`. Add one row asserting that `-l SECRET_NAME=VALUE` prints in clear, or drop that JSDoc line.
3. **QA-961-3.** Add to the JSDoc's does-NOT-cover list: a token docker or k6 rejects is printed verbatim by the tool itself.

## Detail

**Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-12-ks1098-961-644965d90-tier2-r1/report.md` (FINDINGS, COVERAGE MAP, NOT TESTED).

### QA-961-1 · Minor (latent)

* **Where:**
  * `runner/k6_docker.ts:171-172` — the lookbehind branch returns `maskEnvAssignment(arg)` and never tries the one-argument forms;
  * `:97` — `ENV_SHORT_FLAG_TWO_ARG`;
  * the JSDoc claim at `:141`.
* **Mechanism:**
  * The previous argument (`-e`, `-one`, `-qe`) is really the VALUE of `--label`, `-a` or `-u` to the real parser.
  * But it matches `ENV_SHORT_FLAG_TWO_ARG`, so the current argument goes to `maskEnvAssignment()` whole.
  * The "name" it reads is then `--env`, `-qe`, `-e` or `-eKEY`, which no clause of `SECRET_ENV_NAME` matches, so the value prints.
* **Measured** against docker CLI 28.4.0 (a loopback create-recorder) and `k6 archive` v1.6.1:

| row | argv tokens | accepted by | echo at head | echo at base |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| L01 | `--label -e --env=NAME=VALUE` | docker | clear | clear |
| L02 | `--label -one --env=NAME=VALUE` | docker | clear | masked (regressed) |
| L03 | `--label -qe -eKEY=VALUE` | docker | clear | masked (regressed) |
| L04 | `-e -e -eKEY=VALUE` | docker | clear | clear |
| L05 | `--label -one -qe=NAME=VALUE` | docker | clear | clear |
| L07 | `-a -e --env=NAME=VALUE` | k6 | clear | clear |
| L08 | `-u -qe -e=NAME=VALUE` | docker | clear | clear |

* **Control:** L06 (`--label -one -e NAME=VALUE`) is masked on both sides.
* **The gate's fix-shapes:**
  * (a) mask every interpretation of the argument, not only the first;
  * (b) narrow the JSDoc;
  * (c) structural — pass bare `-e NAME` and give `spawnSync` an `env` carrying the values (the #958 gate's O-1).
* **The gate's regression rows:** `['--label', '-one', '--env=NAME=VALUE']`, `['--label', '-qe', '-eKEY=VALUE']` and `['-u', '-qe', '-e=NAME=VALUE']`. Each asserts that the echo lacks the value and the argv keeps it.

### QA-961-2 · Polish

Three shapes the code covers have no pinning row. Each of the gate's tampers Q1–Q3 left 1027/1027 green while the echo measurably changed:

* **Q1** narrowed the two-argument cluster, so `-Pe`, `-dite` and `-qqe` printed in clear.
* **Q2** narrowed the attached cluster, so `-Pe…` and `-qPe=…` printed in clear.
* **Q3** made every short flag's value masked, which masks a secret-named `-l` label. That contradicts "Does NOT cover: non-env arguments".

### QA-961-3 · Polish (latent)

* **The leak:** when docker or k6 REJECTS a token, its own error output prints the token verbatim to the inherited terminal (`stdio: 'inherit'`). That bypasses both the mask and the run-log tee.
* **Measured:** 12 docker rows and 7 k6 rows. In 11 of them, the runner's echo had masked the value.
* **Control:** on every row where a tool ACCEPTED a secret-named env assignment, its output carried the value 0 times.
* **The structural fix** is QA-961-1 (c).

### Not covered by the gate

* a live k6 or docker run, or dockerd itself;
* the k6 2.1.0 image's flag set;
* node ≥24.11.0, and Linux;
* process-table exposure of the argv values.

### Dedupe, before filing

Searched this board by symbol and path:

* `maskEnvAssignment`, `extraFlags` and `k6DockerRedaction`: KS-1098 only.
* `lookbehind`, `QA-961` and `ENV_SHORT_FLAG`: 0 hits.
* `k6_docker.ts`: KS-1098, plus five slot-isolation tickets (KS-1066, KS-971, KS-687, KS-1056 and KS-706), none of them about the mask.

**Related:** KS-1098 (PR #961) and KS-1094.

title: Two k6 unit tests parse config/scenarios.yml with js-yaml directly, bypassing readYaml(), so a malformed scenarios.yml prints its lines into the test output (QA-960-2)
description:
## BLUF

* **Two unit tests in** `systemTest/performance` **parse** `config/scenarios.yml` **with js-yaml directly, bypassing** `readYaml()`**, the KS-1099 sanitiser.** On a malformed `scenarios.yml`, their failure output carries the lines around the error.
* **The gate rated it Polish, because only a tracked, credential-free file is involved.** No secrets path reaches these tests.
* **It is pre-existing.** Both tests are identical at develop `4554b25e21dfd01113bf40e8f6d34573345a5f37`, before #960.
* **Found by** the tier-2 QA gate on PR #960 (KS-1099).

## Recommendation

* **Import** `readYaml` **from** `utils/yaml.ts` **in both tests.** It returns the same data: the gate measured the canonical sha of `scenarios.yml` through `readYaml` as equal to a direct js-yaml parse, at both SHAs.
* **Add a source-text guard** that js-yaml is imported only by `utils/yaml.ts`, with that import as its positive control.
* **Why a separate ticket from QA-960-1/3/4:** the files and the fix are both separate. The fix-shapes are the gate's proposals, not rulings.

## Detail

**Source:** the tier-2 gate report `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-12-ks1099-960-0e70ed1c7-tier2-r1/report.md`, verdict GO WITH FINDINGS at `0e70ed1c77e1f832a4ab165152e024926be509a0`. Line numbers are at that SHA and identical at develop `4554b25e2`.

### QA-960-2 · Polish · two unit tests bypass `readYaml()`

* **Where:**
  * `tests/unit/config/sheddingCeiling.test.ts:29` imports `* as yaml from 'js-yaml'`, and `:46` calls `yaml.load(readFileSync(join(perfRoot, 'config', 'scenarios.yml'), 'utf8'))`.
  * `tests/unit/package_scripts.test.ts:21` imports `{ load as loadYaml } from 'js-yaml'`, and `:44` calls `loadYaml(raw)`.
* **Census (PROBED):**
  * At the head, js-yaml is imported at exactly 3 sites under `systemTest/performance`: these two and `utils/yaml.ts:12`.
  * All 6 product YAML loads go through `readYaml()`:
    * `runner/cli.ts:130`, `:131` and `:132`, via `loadConfig`;
    * `runner/cli.ts:180`, via `loadSecrets`;
    * `runner/setup.ts:80`, via `loadConfig`;

title: POST /api/auth/register accepts a client-supplied organizationId with no existence or membership check — impact not traced
description:
## BLUF

* `POST /api/auth/register` **lets an anonymous caller choose the organisation its new account belongs to.**
  * `registerSchema` accepts `organizationId` as any UUID (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:139`).
  * The handler stores it on the new user unchanged (`auth.ts:233`, `organizationId: data.organizationId`).
  * Nothing checks that the organisation exists, or that the caller has any relationship to it.
* **Impact NOT traced.** What an account carrying another organisation's id can reach has not been established. That covers the token's `organizationId`, organisation-scoped reads and the KS-597 issuer binding. Nothing was exercised on any environment.
* **Found by s189** while measuring the public account-creation path for KS-1100, on develop `4554b25e2`, which is the code kintsugi runs.

## Recommendation

* **Trace every consumer of a user's** `organizationId` **before choosing a fix.** Then either drop `organizationId` from the public register schema, or bind it to a verified invitation or membership.
* **Do not exercise it on a running environment** without explicit authorisation. Registering under another organisation's id is testing an exploit.
* **Priority High:** it sits on the organisation trust boundary Kam ruled `bind` (card `secuura-org-trust-boundary-within-tenant`, shipped in #954).

## Detail

### Code (develop `4554b25e2`)

* `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:133-142` defines `registerSchema` with `organizationId: z.string().uuid().optional()` and `.strip()`.
* `auth.ts:156` is `authRoutes.post('/register', ...)`. It is unauthenticated, and the gateway exempts it from CSRF (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/csrf.ts:85`).
* `auth.ts:221-243` builds the new `User`:
  * the role is fixed server-side as `OWNER`, and a client-sent `role` is refused (KS-82);
  * but `organizationId: data.organizationId` comes straight from the request body.
* `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:611-672`: `createUser` writes that value to `users.organization_id`.
* **Contrast:** `POST /api/users/admin/create` requires an ORG_ADMIN or SYSTEM_ADMIN caller and pins the tenant (KS-467). The public route has no equivalent check on the organisation.

### Not established

* Which reads, grants or attributions key off `users.organization_id`, or the token's `organizationId`, for an OWNER.
* Whether any downstream check already neutralises it. One candidate is originate's KS-597 binding (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:454-469`).

### Dedupe

* **Method:** a literal, case-insensitive search over KS issue titles, descriptions and all comments, archived included. Run 2026-09-12 by s189.
* **Results:**
  * `registerSchema`: 3 issues and 4 comments, across KS-283, KS-202, KS-94, KS-266, KS-255 and KS-82. All are Done and archived, and none mentions `organizationId`.
  * `organizationId: data.organizationId`: 0.
  * `register accepts organizationId`: 0.
  * `self-assign organization`: 0.
* **Controls (the instrument can hit):** `getUserByIdWithPasswordHash` found KS-732 and KS-1005; `UUID_V4_RE` found KS-663.

### Related

* KS-1100: where this was found.
* KS-597: issuer organisation attribution (option B, #954).

title: Verifier shows 'Verification Failed' / 'INVALID' for an id that is not in the registry, with no next step
description:
## BLUF

* **Enter an id that is not registered, and the verifier shows "Verification Failed" and "INVALID" with no next step.** The API behind it said `"Document not found in the registry"`.

  * `POST /api/verification/verify` → 200 with `"Document not found in the registry"`; 0 console errors.
* **Oracle:** user desires. The message is not precise about what went wrong or what to do.
* **Related:** KS-735, on the same verifier result page, which shows nothing about what was registered on a success.

title: Unauthenticated /system/status, /api/system/status and /api/system/health/dashboard publish internal service URLs, ports, versions and which third-party keys are unset
description:
## BLUF

* **Three gateway routes answer 200 with no credential and publish a map of the platform's internals:** `GET /system/status`, `GET /api/system/status` and `GET /api/system/health/dashboard`.
* **What the bodies carry:**
  * internal service URLs and ports (`http://auth:4003`, `http://anchoring:4005`, …);
  * service versions;
  * gateway uptime, Node version and environment (`development`);
  * which third-party keys are unset (Blockfrost, Stripe and WalletConnect reported "missing").
* **Measured on kintsugi, an internet-reachable host.** Pre-existing, found by the kintsugi deploy gate on `4554b25e2` (finding F-3, Minor).

## Recommendation

* **The fix:** gate these routes behind admin auth, or serve a public variant with hosts, ports, versions and key state stripped.
* **Keep** `/status/` **working.** The public `/status/` page reads `/system/status`, so the fix has to keep that page working. The page's other defects are on KS-864.

## Detail

* **Probed by the gate** 2026-09-11 22:55:20–22:55:22Z, with no credential; all three returned 200. Bodies are in `evidence/wire/h2_*.body`.
* **Oracle:** statutes and standards, following the audit's own F-04 reasoning about attack-surface maps. The spec side of F-04 is on KS-491.
* **Related, not graded by the gate:** Swagger UI and the raw spec are public on kintsugi (`ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS` on).
  * The gateway comment allows that on a dev portal, but the host is internet-reachable.
  * KS-658 covers the same guard on the demo VM.

### Evidence

title: Gateway health aggregates read anchoring's HTTP status only, so its degraded body (#728) never reaches /health/deep, /system/status or the health dashboard
description:
## BLUF

* **Anchoring now reports** `degraded` **honestly, but no public health surface can show it.**
  * Since #728 (KS-671), anchoring's `/health` answers HTTP 200 with `status: 'degraded'` and `degradedReasons` when the chain is unreachable. Keeping the 200 is deliberate.
  * All three public gateway health aggregates classify a service by HTTP status alone, so they show anchoring as `up` while it cannot reach the chain.
* **This is the** `/health/ready` **middle path the KS-671 review offered to split out** (KS-671 comments `eba1c64d` and `0c76ac61`, 2026-09-08). It was never filed.
* **Pre-existing, found by the kintsugi deploy gate on** `4554b25e2` (finding F-2, Minor). The aggregate code is older than #728; #728 is what made it matter.

## Recommendation

* **The fix:** make each aggregate read anchoring's body `status` and map `degraded` to a state other than `up`, with the regression cell below.
* Until then, `/health/deep` and `/status/` cannot show anchoring's chain health.

## Detail

### Mechanism, read at `4554b25e2`

* **Anchoring keeps the 200 on purpose.** `services/anchoring/src/index.ts`, around lines 336–347, keeps HTTP 200 on degraded, with the comment "Wiring an alert to `status: 'degraded'` is the monitoring change, tracked on KS-671".
* **The aggregates key on** `response.ok`**:**
  * `services/api-gateway/src/services/health.ts:132` → `/health/deep` and `/health/ready` (the same handler, `health.ts:166-167`);
  * `services/api-gateway/src/routes/system-status.ts:333` → `/system/status` and `/api/system/status`;
  * `services/api-gateway/src/routes/health-dashboard.ts:59` → `/api/system/health/dashboard`.
* **No public route reaches anchoring's own** `/health`**.** The gateway mounts anchoring at `/api/anchors` and `/api/anchoring` only (`proxy.ts:765-781`).
* **The fields never surface.** `degradedReasons` and `reachability` appear in none of the four public aggregate bodies (the gate's `evidence/wire/`).

### Why a ticket of its own

* **It was left out of #728.** #728 is merged and running on kintsugi. The aggregate half was named on KS-671 as an offered split and left out of that push.
* **Its only record would go stale.** KS-671 moves on when #728 reaches demo, and the code comment above would then point at a closed ticket.
* **Kam's 2026-09-07 13:23 rule:** a separate fix gets its own ticket.

### Regression test (the gate's)

* A stub anchoring that returns 200 with `{status: 'degraded'}` must not appear as `up` in `/health/deep`.

### Not tested

* Whether anchoring is degraded on kintsugi right now: its own `/health` has no public route.

### Evidence

* **Report:** `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-12-kintsugi-deploy-4554b25e2-tier1-r1/report.md`
  * section `### F-2 — Every public health aggregate derives a service's state from response.ok`;
  * `## CLOSING`, item 2.

### Dedupe

* **Method:** a literal, case-insensitive census over all 1,089 KS issues (682 archived; title and description) and 2,946 comments (includeArchived), run 2026-09-12 by s188. Per-ticket comment counts equal direct API reads on 9 of 9 tickets.
* **Searched:**
  * `degradedReasons`: 1 (KS-671's comment table)
  * `/health/ready`: 7 (6 archived; the live one is KS-671's own open question)
  * `health-dashboard.ts`: 0
  * `monitoring change`: 0
* **Result:** no existing home. The offered split lives only in KS-671's comments.

title: Kintsugi deploy 4554b25e2: four live changes have no QA gate record — #872 (KS-732), #896 (compose ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD), #728 (KS-671), #808 (KS-663)
description:
## BLUF

* **Four changes now running on kintsugi have no QA gate record:**
  * #872 (auth, KS-732);
  * #896 (compose, `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` passed into auth);
  * #728 (anchoring, KS-671);
  * #808 (originate's published contract, KS-663).

  Kintsugi runs develop `4554b25e2`, deployed 2026-09-11 22:16–22:21Z.
* **This is a coverage gap, not a verdict on the code.** #872, #728 and #808 each carry a human approval at the merged head, under the merge rule of the time. #896 has no review.
* **Found by the kintsugi deploy gate on** `4554b25e2` (tier 1, GO WITH FINDINGS, finding G-1).
  * Not a pre-existing defect: these changes shipped in that deploy.
  * The gate listed five; #936 is reconciled out below because its gate record exists.

## Recommendation

* **Commission gates for the four, in the gate's risk order:** #872 (MFA disable, proof of possession) and #896 (the admin seed password config) first, then #728 and #808.
* **The runtime half of each needs a QA credential on kintsugi. Creating one is Kam's call.** No account or credential was created for this ticket.

## Detail

### The four gaps

| PR | Ticket | Service | Runtime change | Human review at the merged head | QA gate record |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| #872 | KS-732 | auth | yes: `mfa.ts`, `userRepo.ts`, spec | APPROVED by PeterObeden at `1fb2cc6b2` (2026-09-08 11:48Z), after CHANGES_REQUESTED at `235bb1ba3` | none |
| #896 | KS-682 | compose | config: `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD=${ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD:-}` into auth | none: authored and merged by PeterObeden (2026-09-11 07:38Z), 0 reviews | none |
| #728 | KS-671 | anchoring | yes: `chainHealthStatus.ts`, `index.ts` | APPROVED by PeterObeden at `720a6968b` (2026-09-08 12:30Z) | none |
| #808 | KS-663 | originate contract | published contract only: `originate.openapi.ts` and the regenerated `secuura-api.yaml` | APPROVED by PeterObeden at `3d8b40a07` (2026-09-08 14:18Z) | none |

#872, #728 and #808 merged 2026-09-10 21:43–21:46Z, when an approval at head was the merge signal. Since Kam's 2026-09-11 16:56 rule, TESTED includes a QA gate verdict at the head.

### What the gate could not reach from outside

* **#872:** proof of possession on MFA disable needs a logged-in user. The no-token 401 the gate saw was equally true before #872, so it cannot see the fix.
* **#896:** whether `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` reaches the auth container, and the seeded SYSTEM_ADMIN's state. Both live in the container and the database.
* **#728:** anchoring's own `/health` (`degradedReasons`, `chain.reachability`) has no public route.

title: k6 runner echo mask: -e=NAME=VALUE and -qe NAME=VALUE still print the value, contrary to its JSDoc; the name set and BASE_URL userinfo are open; PASSWD is unpinned (QA-958-1..3)
description:
## BLUF

* PR #958 (KS-1094) masks secret values in the k6 runner's echoed docker command. Its tier-2 QA gate returned GO WITH FINDINGS at `ffb285752` and found three gaps in that mask. None sits on a path the shipping CLI takes today.
* **QA-958-1 (Minor, latent):** two spellings docker accepts, `-e=NAME=VALUE` and the clustered `-qe NAME=VALUE`, print the value in clear. The fix's own JSDoc says "Every spelling docker accepts is covered".
* **QA-958-2 (Polish):** credential-shaped names outside the masked word set, and a BASE_URL carrying userinfo, print in clear. No name the runner emits today falls in that gap.
* **QA-958-3 (Polish):** `PASSWD` is in the masked set, but no test cell pins it.
* Medium because a merged comment overclaims a security property, not because anything leaks today.

## Recommendation

* The name set is Peter's to confirm. The QA-958-2 list below is input to that decision. The gate recommends redacting URL userinfo in BASE_URL whichever way the name set goes.
* Then one fix round on `k6_docker.ts` and its redaction test: resolve QA-958-1 (narrow the JSDoc, or handle both spellings) and add the `PASSWD` row (QA-958-3).
* The fix-shapes below are the QA gate's proposals, not decisions. Re-read the code before editing.

## Detail

* **Source:** the tier-2 gate report `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-12-ks1094-958-ffb285752-tier2-r1/report.md` (findings QA-958-1..3, observation O-1).
* **Lines** under `systemTest/performance/` are cited at the gated head `ffb28575223dbd611a91242e3cd711aaeb3085b7` for the two #958 files, and at develop `8515d1db7fb52e783610812480f7a720fc193d6e` for the rest. All were re-read on 2026-09-12 and are unchanged in the merged tree `ceaa132f`.
* **No credential value appears here.** Every value the gate used was a sentinel it wrote into a fixture.
* **One ticket for three findings:** one fix round on one file and its test, proven by one run of the performance unit suite. QA-958-4 is a separate fix in other files and has its own ticket.

### QA-958-1 · Minor · latent: two docker spellings print the value

* **Where** (`runner/k6_docker.ts`):
  * :99, the JSDoc claim "Every spelling docker accepts is covered";
  * :83, `if (separator <= 0)` returns the assignment unchanged, inside `maskEnvAssignment` (:80);
  * :115, the two-argument branch matches only an exact `-e` or `--env`;
  * :122, the glued `-e` branch.
* **Measured by the gate** (a probe with `spawnSync` replaced, at the head and at the merged tree):
  * `-e=NAME=VALUE` and `-qe NAME=VALUE` both read CLEAR, the sentinel printed once, on the docker side and on the k6 side;
  * the four handled spellings read MASKED;
  * at the merge-base every valued shape leaks (48 of 48), which shows the probe can see a leak;
  * the argv is intact in every row.
* **Mechanism (read only):**
  * `-e=NAME=VALUE`: the glued branch passes `=NAME=VALUE` to `maskEnvAssignment`, where `indexOf('=')` is 0, so the guard returns it unchanged.
  * `-qe NAME=VALUE`: the previous argument is `-qe`, not `-e`, so the assignment is never inspected.
* **Does docker accept them?** Read only, not run: docker and k6 both parse flags with spf13/pflag, which reads `-e=VALUE` as the value `VALUE` and `-qe VALUE` as `-q -e VALUE`.
* **Why latent:** `buildEnvFlags()` emits only the two-argument `-e` form (`runner/env_flags.ts:143`), and `runner/cli.ts:221` hard-codes `extraFlags: []`. The shipping CLI produces neither spelling.
* **Fix-shape, the gate's proposal — one of:**
  * (a) narrow the JSDoc to the four spellings actually handled;
  * (b) handle both: strip one leading `=` after `-e`, and treat a short-flag cluster ending in `e` as the two-argument form;
  * (c) mask by value: `runK6` (:168) knows which secret-named assignments it was given, so it can replace those exact values anywhere in the rendered line. The cost is over-masking when a value is a short common substring.
* **Regression test:** two `it.each` rows (`-e=NAME=VALUE`, `-qe NAME=VALUE`), each asserting the echo lacks the value and the argv keeps it.

### QA-958-2 · Polish: names outside the set, and BASE_URL userinfo (input to the name-set decision)

* **Where:** `runner/k6_docker.ts:70`, `SECRET_ENV_NAME = /PASSWORD|PASSWD|SECRET|TOKEN|MNEMONIC|(?:^|_)KEY$/i`.
* **Printed in clear by the gate's probe**, at the head and at the merged tree:
  * `DB_PASS`;
  * `APIKEY` (no underscore);
  * `PRIVATE_KEY_PEM` (KEY is not the last segment);
  * `AUTH_BEARER`;
  * `SESSION_COOKIE`;
  * `AWS_CREDENTIALS`;
  * a name ending `_PWD`;
  * `OTP_SEED`;
  * `PERF_BASE_URL` holding a URL with userinfo.
* **Over-masking, the accepted cost:** `SORT_KEY`, a non-secret `_KEY`, reads MASKED.
* **Not a live leak.**
  * The runner emits 26 env names, the same list at head, merge-base, merged tree and develop.
  * 3 carry credentials (`ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `ISSUER_PASSWORD`, `VERIFIER_PASSWORD`), and all 3 are masked.
  * The other 23 are non-secret and print in clear.
  * `GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is read from the host environment for the annotation push and is never passed to docker.
* **BASE_URL is the one conditional carrier.** If `config/environments.yml` `baseUrl` or `PERF_BASE_URL` held userinfo, the password would print:
  * in the echo (measured);
  * in the banner, `runner/cli.ts:260` (read only);
  * in `run-metadata.json` as `baseUrl`, `runner/run_metadata.ts:34` (read only);
  * in the HTML report's Target row, `runner/report_header.ts:122` (read only).
  * The tracked `environments.yml` has 4 `baseUrl` lines, 0 with userinfo.
* **Fix-shape if the set is widened, the gate's proposal:**
  * `PASS` only as a whole segment (a bare substring matches `BYPASS` and `PASSPORT`);
  * `PWD`, `CREDENTIAL`, `COOKIE`, `BEARER` and `SEED` as segments, and a `KEY` segment anywhere rather than only last;
  * for URLs, redact userinfo: parse with `new URL()` and set the password to `***`.
* **Regression test:** one row per word added, plus a userinfo row.

### QA-958-3 · Polish: PASSWD is unpinned

* The gate replaced `PASSWD` in the regex with a nonsense word. tsc rc 0; the unit suite ran 48 files / 537 tests with 0 failed.
* Every other clause of the mask reddened exactly the cells the gate predicted before the run.
* The behaviour is right (a `WALLET_PASSWD` row reads MASKED). It is only unpinned.
* **Regression test:** add a `PASSWD`-named row to the `it.each` at `tests/unit/runner/k6DockerRedaction.test.ts:178`.

### Recorded, not reconciled: O-1

* The persona passwords still travel in docker's argv as `-e NAME=VALUE`, by design: the mask covers the echo only. While the docker CLI runs, the values sit in the host process table.
* A structural alternative: pass a bare `-e NAME` and give `spawnSync` an `env` carrying the values. Docker forwards host values, which takes them out of the argv and the echo together.
* Not introduced by #958. Not measured.

title: Merge-rule docs after #957: the v4 footer and two gate statements gloss TESTED weakly, 'the reviewer' has no referent, one sentence lets a person sign off (QA-957-1..5, W-2)
description:
## BLUF

* **PR #957 (KS-1095) passed its tier-2 QA gate as GO WITH FINDINGS at** `9a8afaaa835c9dc8f571dac2167becb31c565e18`**.** What it changed is correct. The gate raised six findings, all Polish. Five sit in text the PR did not touch, and none changes a merge condition.
* **This ticket carries QA-957-1..5 and W-2, as ruled by Wednesday.** QA-957-6 is a no-op.
  * **QA-957-1:** `DEV-PROCESS.md` :262 (the v4 footer) glosses TESTED more weakly than the rule.
  * **QA-957-2:** `CLAUDE.md` :274 and `CONTRIBUTING.md` :603-:604, "The gate is approval + a Test Evidence block filled from local runs", still differ from the other gate statements.
  * **QA-957-3:** `CONTRIBUTING.md` keeps "the reviewer" with no referent at :466, :550 and :600-:601.
  * **QA-957-4:** `DEV-PROCESS.md` :65 is the one sentence whose letter lets a person sign off.
  * **QA-957-5:** `CONTRIBUTING.md` :456-:458 still calls a superseded proposal "not yet team-agreed".
  * **W-2:** the QA-2 "NOT APPLIED" annotation in `CLAUDE.md` :237-:239 names neither the pending ruling nor "do not turn it on".
* **One ticket, because one tier-2 docs pass proves all of it** (Kam, 2026-09-07 13:23).
* Docs only. Nothing here blocks a merge.

## Recommendation

* **One docs PR against** `develop`, carrying the rulings below and nothing else. Every site goes in the PR body: edited, or not edited with the reason.
* **The fix-shapes below are the gate's PROPOSALS.** Re-read each site before editing. Line numbers are the gate's, at `9a8afaaa8`.
* **Prove it with** one tier-2 docs gate at the PR's head, then Wednesday's GO.
* **Not in that PR:**
  * `.github/workflows/` files (Kam's to merge);
  * the red-pen lines at `CONTRIBUTING.md` :531-:532 and `DEV-PROCESS.md` :26, which are attributed to Kam's 2026-08-27 ruling.

## Rulings (Wednesday, 2026-09-11: brief s184 at 12:39:22Z and its answer at 13:04:26Z)

**QA-957-1 [Polish], owed: the v4 footer's TESTED gloss.**

* `DEV-PROCESS.md` :262 today: "a PR merges once it is TESTED — a QA gate verdict at its current head, a Test Evidence block and our own suites — and Wednesday's GO is the approval."
  * It has no "(GO or GO WITH FINDINGS)" qualifier, so a NO GO verdict at head satisfies the gloss in letter.
  * It defines the approval without the head SHA.
  * KS-1095's QA-3 ruling listed :262 and gave no exemption for footers.
* **Fix:** gloss by reference, AFTER the colon. `CONTRIBUTING.md` :455 copies the footer only up to "(16:56)", and that text must stay a byte prefix of the footer.
* The gate's proposal: "… once it is TESTED (as defined in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, step 6 of *Adopted merge flow*) and Wednesday's GO, naming the head SHA, is the approval".

**QA-957-2 [Polish], owed: two gate statements still differ.**

* `CLAUDE.md` :274: "The gate is approval + a Test Evidence block filled from LOCAL runs"
* `CONTRIBUTING.md` :603-:604: "there are no CI checks to pass. The gate is approval + a Test Evidence block filled from local runs"
* KS-1095's QA-3 ruling named exactly this pair. The gate statements that already follow the ruling are `CONTRIBUTING.md` :502-:504, `DEV-PROCESS.md` :73 and `CLAUDE.md` :405-:406.
* **Intent:** state the gate as a TESTED PR + Wednesday's GO naming the head SHA, with the Test Evidence from local runs.
* The gate's proposal: "The gate is a TESTED PR (see *Merge flow* / step 6) + Wednesday's GO naming the head SHA, with the Test Evidence block filled from LOCAL runs".
* The project-root copy of `CLAUDE.md` (untracked) carries the :274 sentence too. Mirror the fix there after the PR merges.

**QA-957-3 [Polish], in scope: "the reviewer" has no referent in CONTRIBUTING.**

* :466: "6. The author merges once the PR is TESTED — not the reviewer."
* :600-:601: "once the PR is TESTED and has Wednesday's GO — not the reviewer (Kam, 2026-09-11; see Adopted merge flow above)"
* :550: "A box ticked on a not-applicable rationale reads to the reviewer as a run."
* After KS-1095's QA-1, no line in `CONTRIBUTING.md` says who "the reviewer" is. `DEV-PROCESS.md` keeps a referent: the stream table's `Reviewer` column (:217).
* **Leave alone:** `CONTRIBUTING.md` :531-:532 and `DEV-PROCESS.md` :26, "the reviewer red-pens the results (Kam, 2026-08-27)".
* The gate's proposal: drop "— not the reviewer" at :466 and :601, or define the term once; and :550 → "reads to the QA gate as a run".

**QA-957-4 [Polish], in scope: the one sentence that lets a person sign off.**

* `DEV-PROCESS.md` :65 today: "Separate the ticket from the review. The author tests, but a second pair of eyes signs it off — never the same person on both."
* **The ruled sentence, whole:** "The author tests, but a second seat signs it off — the QA gate verdict at head plus Wednesday's GO — never the seat that built it."
* This replaces the brief's phrase-only wording, which would have left "never the same person on both" in place (Wednesday, 13:04:26Z).

**QA-957-5 [Polish], in scope: a superseded proposal still reads as pending.**

* `CONTRIBUTING.md` :456-:458: "One item in that document differs and is flagged there as a proposal, not yet team-agreed — approval may come from any of the three who is not the author."
* `DEV-PROCESS.md` :238 marks that section "Superseded 2026-09-11 (KS-1092)". The CONTRIBUTING pointer gains the same status.
* The gate's proposal: append "— superseded 2026-09-11 (KS-1092): the approval is Wednesday's GO on a TESTED PR".

**W-2, owed (the ruled wording was Wednesday's): the QA-2 annotation.**

* `CLAUDE.md` :237-:239 today: "[NOT APPLIED (2026-09-11, KS-1095): Kam has ruled on the required-approvals setting and that ruling is not yet applied; turning required reviews on while fleet PRs carry 0 GitHub reviews would block every fleet merge.]"
* A seat asked to "apply pending rulings" could read that as a to-do.
* **Fix:** the annotation says what the pending ruling is, AND "do not turn it on while fleet PRs carry 0 GitHub reviews".
* The pending ruling, as relayed in Wednesday's brief s184 (not a Kam-signed artefact): card `secuura-required-approvals-zero-after-the-untick`, ruled `raise-to-1`. Kam applies it himself, and it is not yet applied.

**QA-957-6 [Polish]: no-op.** It concerns PR #957's body (a "3 / 2 / 6" count that matches neither file order, and two "now" quotes joined by an ellipsis), which is historical once #957 merges.

## Recorded, NOT reconciled

* `DEV-PROCESS.md` **:21, row 04:** "and, when GitHub Actions is available, checks are green". This sits against :71 ("decided state, not an outage: there is nothing to wait for and no leg that re-arms by itself") and :247 ("this requirement must never be enabled now").
  * Pre-existing.
  * Which one is authoritative is not established.
* **Where CONTRIBUTING's step 4 sits in the flow (the gate's OPEN-2).**
  * Step 4 (:464) is now a periodic activity inside the per-PR numbered sequence.
  * No numbered step says the QA gate runs: step 5 (:465) presupposes it, and step 6 defines TESTED with it.
  * **This is ruled text, copied byte-for-byte from** `CLAUDE.md`**. Do not edit it without a ruling.**

## Detail

* **Source:** QA tier-2 gate, round 1, on PR #957 @ `9a8afaaa835c9dc8f571dac2167becb31c565e18`. Verdict: GO WITH FINDINGS. Report: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1095-957-9a8afaaa8-tier2-r1/report.md`.
* **Re-read at** `9a8afaaa8` **before filing.** Every quoted line above carries the quoted text at the cited lines. The check ignores markdown emphasis and blockquote markers.
* **Related:** KS-1095, the source PR's ticket.
* **Related context, not an item here:** KS-1037. The gate's W-1 found that none of the three docs carries the no-force rule; that rule lives in `.githooks/pre-push`, which is KS-1037's subject.
* **Searched before filing.** Team KS; a literal `containsIgnoreCase` on title + description (archived included), and on comment bodies:
  * **File names:** `DEV-PROCESS.md` (15 issues) and `CONTRIBUTING.md` (11). Classified by title, none carries these findings.
  * **The gate's phrases:**
    * `QA-957`, `reads to the reviewer`, `weaker than the rule`, `a second seat signs`, `do not turn it on`: 0 each;
    * `The gate is approval`, `v4 footer`, `no referent`, `required-approvals`: KS-1095 only;
    * `second pair of eyes`, `not the reviewer`, `not yet team-agreed`, `NOT APPLIED`: hits on unrelated tickets, or on the archived process ticket where that proposal originated.
  * **Controls:** a nonsense token → 0; "Merge-rule docs still disagree" → KS-1095.
  * **Re-checked just before filing:** 0 KS issues created since 12:40Z (control: the same query from 10:40Z returns the four issues created in that window).
* **Not in scope:**
  * workflow files, rulesets and branch-protection settings;
  * the project-root `CLAUDE.md` mirror of KS-1095's QA-3 and QA-5 wording, which is done separately after #957 merges.

title: check-stack-safety.sh 6f reports a FALSE red once a real Playwright run exists — git check-ignore refuses a path beyond the latest-slot<N> symlink
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-stack-safety.sh` §6f (the [KS-682](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-682/playwright-slot-isolation-port-the-proven-platform-s-mechanism-no-run) per-slot Playwright artefact probe) goes **red on a clean tree the moment a real Playwright run has been made on a slot** — and stays green only while no run has ever happened. Observed 2026-09-11 on the [KS-687](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-687/akto-slot-targeting-dump-result-fieldssh-resolves-the-un-prefixed) / PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#933](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-687-slot-isolation-akto-refuses-a-cross-slot-run-k6-schemathesis-227100b6440d) verification, slot 4, this Mac.

## Measured

```
$ bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-stack-safety.sh
::error::latest-slot4/index.html is NOT gitignored on slot 4 (KS-682).
```

The probe (`check-stack-safety.sh:307`, in the loop at `:291-315`) asks:

```
git check-ignore -q systemTest/playwright/results/latest-slot4/index.html
```

After a run, `results/latest-slot4` is a **symlink** (→ `playwright-report-2026-09-11T10-45-11-710Z-slot4`). git refuses to evaluate a path *through* a symlink:

```
$ git check-ignore -v systemTest/playwright/results/latest-slot4/index.html
fatal: pathspec '…/results/latest-slot4/index.html' is beyond a symbolic link
```

The non-zero exit is read as "not ignored" and the gate fails. Everything **is** ignored — `systemTest/playwright/.gitignore:17` `results/` covers the whole tree, and `git check-ignore -v systemTest/playwright/results/latest-slot4` answers with that rule. Same gate, same tree, with `results/` empty: **95 invariants hold**.

## Why it matters

The gate is red exactly when it has just been used for what it exists for — and the message names a real-looking defect ("NOT gitignored on slot 4 ([KS-682](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-682/playwright-slot-isolation-port-the-proven-platform-s-mechanism-no-run))"), so the next person either hand-edits `.gitignore` for nothing or learns to ignore the gate. It also means preflight/push from a worktree where Playwright has run will fail 6f for anyone.

## Fix shape (not chosen)

Probe the symlink itself, or the directory it resolves to (`readlink`), or a sibling non-symlink shape (`playwright-report-<ts>-slot<N>/index.html`) — never a path *through* the symlink. Add the case "a `latest-slot<N>` symlink exists" to the gate's own suite so the false red cannot return.

## Provenance

Found running the offline gates for PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#933](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-687-slot-isolation-akto-refuses-a-cross-slot-run-k6-schemathesis-227100b6440d) ([KS-687](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-687/akto-slot-targeting-dump-result-fieldssh-resolves-the-un-prefixed)) on 2026-09-11 after `npm run test:e2e` on slot 4 (12/12 passed) created `results/latest-slot4`. Not caused by [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#933](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-687-slot-isolation-akto-refuses-a-cross-slot-run-k6-schemathesis-227100b6440d) — its change to this file is §6f2 (Akto), a different block. [KS-682](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-682/playwright-slot-isolation-port-the-proven-platform-s-mechanism-no-run) (which added the probe) is Done, so this is filed new rather than appended ([KS-595](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-595/three-undeclared-verb-catalogue-skips-cite-closed-tickets-ks-406-ks) rule). [KS-1034](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1034/check-stack-safetysh-resolves-the-wrong-repo-root-inside-a-git-hook) is a different `check-stack-safety.sh` defect (repo-root resolution inside a hook), linked for the file, not the cause.

PR under verification: [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#933](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-687-slot-isolation-akto-refuses-a-cross-slot-run-k6-schemathesis-227100b6440d)

title: KS-1041 residual: the cross-tenant JWT probe on originate's direct path — reasoned, never run, not commissioned
description:
## BLUF

* **Recorded from KS-1041, so it stays on a live ticket when KS-1041 is archived.** It was outside KS-1041's Step 1 and Step 2, and it is **not commissioned and not ruled**.
* **The open question:** can a caller already inside the compose network, holding a **valid** JWT, go straight to originate and have an `x-tenant-id` for **another** tenant honoured?
  * KS-1041 **measured** only the credential-free connector-header case.
  * This wider case was **reasoned, never tested**.
* **What has changed since:**
  * #938 (Step 1, `0f8fb33c3`) closed nginx `/originate/`.
  * #951 (Step 2) adds originate middleware that strips unvouched trust headers — but only once `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is provisioned. That is unset everywhere (PROVISIONING SAFETY: UNSAFE, KS-1083), so originate's direct path behaves as before.

## Recommendation

No action until Kam rules. Running the probe needs a fresh commission — KS-1041 `116ed2d6`: *"If it should be run, that goes back to Kam."*

## Detail

* **KS-1041's measured/reasoned split, verbatim** (`116ed2d6`):
  * MEASURED:
    * direct to `originate:4000`, no headers → 401;
    * direct, with forged `x-user-role: connector` + `x-tenant-id` → 200;
    * the same request through `api-gateway:8080` → 401;
    * not externally reachable, but reachable by any of the 34 peers on `dev_secuura-network`.
  * REASONED: *"the same door is open wider, including a cross-tenant read — needs a valid JWT and a probe nobody has run."*
* **Why it was not run:**
  * `ba0f7402`: *"That the same door is open wider (a peer with a valid JWT setting* `x-tenant-id` *for another tenant) is reasoned, not tested — it needs a probe I have not run and will not run without a fresh commission."*
  * `47e0b331`: *"Not done and deliberately so: the cross-tenant JWT probe. It is the next measurement and belongs to a seat with room to act on the answer."*
* **Where it sits:** `originate/src/index.ts:230` reads `x-tenant-id` before auth (`ba0f7402`). Once the secret is provisioned, #951's middleware strips unvouched trust headers ahead of it; KS-1083 holds that precondition.
* **Neighbours, not duplicates:**
  * KS-619 — the gateway's conditional `x-tenant-id` overwrite (the gateway path, not originate's direct path);
  * KS-1032 — trust-header reads outside auth middleware (a code census);
  * KS-1084 — the gateway's Authorization-only calls to originate.
* **Why its own ticket, not a comment on KS-1032:** this is a live measurement, and KS-1032 is a code census and guard. Separate workloads get separate tickets under Kam's 2026-09-07 13:23 rule.
* **Board searched before filing** (literal, live tickets only):
  * `JWT probe` 0 · `valid JWT` 0 · `gateway-only ingress` 0 · `flat network` 0 · `tenant confusion` 0;
  * `originate:4000` → KS-1041 only;
  * `another tenant` → 6, none about originate's direct path;
  * `cross-tenant` → 62 literal hits, none about this probe.

title: api-gateway + originate: tsc never type-checks #951's three wiring tests, and the mint-scope test pins 2 of 17 non-originate keys
description:
## BLUF

* **The type-check claim does not cover the tests (R2-2).** #951's Test Evidence says "`tsc --noEmit` rc 0 on both services", but that run never reads its 3 new test files.
  * Both services' tsconfigs exclude `src/__tests__`.
  * A type error planted in each test file returns rc 0; the same plant in `routes/proxy.ts` returns rc 2.
* **The mint-scope test pins 2 of 17 (R2-3).** `ks1041-vouch-mint-scope.test.ts` asserts "no vouch" only at analytics and auth. An allowlist widening that spares those two keys stays green.
* **Test-quality findings, not runtime defects.** They come from the round-2 tier-1 gate on #951 at `02a22f4bb`, and one test pass proves both.

## Recommendation

One change, one test pass:

1. **A type-check that includes the tests** (e.g. a `tsconfig.test.json`), run in the local gate, with a planted-error cell that must exit non-zero.
2. **A structural mint-scope guard:** derive every `proxy('<key>')` mount from the factory and assert, per mount, that only originate receives `x-gateway-vouch`, with a reach control on each. The gate's `evidence/harness/mounts.qa.ts` does this in 172 cells, in under 2 s.
3. **R2-4, record only:** quote tamper shapes that compile. `void stripTrustHeaders;` alone fails the gateway's tsc (TS6133, `req` unused); `void stripTrustHeaders; void req;` compiles and gives the identical red.

## Detail

* **R2-2, measured:**
  * Planted `const qa951r2Planted: number = 'qa951r2-not-a-number';` into each file.
    * 3 test files: rc 0.
    * Controls — `routes/proxy.ts` and `utils/gatewayProvenance.ts`: rc 2 (TS2322).
  * `--listFiles`: the gateway checks 33 `src` files and originate 51, with 0 under `__tests__` in each.
  * `api-gateway/tsconfig.json` excludes `src/__tests__`; `originate/tsconfig.json` excludes `src/__tests__` and `src/**/*.test.ts`. Both exclusions pre-date #951.
* **R2-3:**
  * V2 asserts absence at analytics and auth only.
  * The proxy has 18 service keys: 17 non-originate, on 16 hosts.
  * Example of a change that stays green: `VOUCH_RECIPIENTS.has(k) || k.startsWith('vc')`.
* **R2-4:**
  * C3a (`void stripTrustHeaders;`) — tsc rc 2, TS6133.
  * C3b (`… void req;`) — tsc rc 0.
  * Both redden the edge-strip C3 cell.
* **Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1041-951-02a22f4bb-tier1-r2/report.md`, §R2-2, §R2-3, §R2-4.
* **Board searched before filing:**
  * literal match over the 7 KS issues and 12 comments created since 2026-09-10T22:40Z, for `R2-2`, `R2-3`, `R2-4`, `mint-scope`, `tsconfig.test`, `TS6133`, `void stripTrustHeaders`, `VOUCH_RECIPIENTS` and `noEmit`;
  * 0 hits, except `R2-2` on KS-1089 — that is #953's gate ID, read in context.
  * all-time `searchIssues`, matched literally and counting live tickets only: `type-check` 6, `__tests__` 12, `tsconfig` 7, `typecheck` 4, `mint-scope` 0.
  * The same tsconfig class is already filed per package elsewhere — KS-848 (services/kyc), KS-1000 (services/auth), KS-933 (packages/shared), KS-993 (systemTest/fixtures). None covers api-gateway or originate, and none covers the mint-scope pin.
* **Related:** KS-1041, PR #951, KS-1083.

title: run-shell-suites.sh polish from #953's tier-2 gate: make `--list` survive a tree with no suites on bash 3.2 (QA-8, `:72`) and give the git-list refusal a headline per cause (QA-7)
description:
## BLUF

Two Polish findings from the tier-2 QA gate on PR #953 (KS-1086), both in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-shell-suites.sh`. Neither blocks #953, and no gate reaches either.

- [ ] **QA-8 — pre-existing on develop.** `run-shell-suites.sh --list` on a tree with zero reached suites dies on bash 3.2 with `line 72: reached[@]: unbound variable`, rc 1. It is present on develop `2d864ae92` and unchanged by #953.
- [ ] **QA-7 — in #953's delta.** The run-mode refusal prints the headline `FAIL — could not ask git which variables are repository-local` for every cause, including when git DID print a list. Only the parenthetical names the cause. These lines reach develop only when #953 merges.

## Recommendation

**Filing only; no action today.** Whoever next edits `run-shell-suites.sh` after #953 is on develop should:

* fix both items;
* prove both with one run of `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/run_shell_suites.test.sh`, using the regression cells below.

If the file is touched before #953 merges, QA-8 can land alone and its item closes on its own.

**Why one ticket, under Kam's ticket rule (2026-09-07 13:23).** The rule: when a single test proves several items, file one ticket with several items; file separate tickets only for separate workloads or separate fixes.

* Both items are changes to the same file.
* One pass of the same test file proves both.
* Both follow the same route.
* QA-7's lines exist on develop only once #953 merges. That is an ordering constraint, recorded above, not a separate workload.

## Detail

### QA-8 — `--list` with no suites (pre-existing)

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-shell-suites.sh:71-74` on develop `2d864ae92`, identical at #953 head `8987b8a0e`:

  ```
  if [ "$MODE" = "list" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "${reached[@]}"
    exit 0
  fi
  ```
* **Mechanism:** the runner runs under `set -u`. On bash 3.2, which macOS ships, `"${reached[@]}"` on an EMPTY array raises `unbound variable`. The same file already documents this class at `:87-91` (QA R2-2) and converts `:92` to `${reached[@]+"${reached[@]}"}`. `:72` was never converted.
* **Measured by the gate (probe v2 §F):** a committed repo with the runner and no `*.test.sh` under ROOTS, then `/bin/bash scripts/run-shell-suites.sh --list`. Result: rc 1 and `line 72: reached[@]: unbound variable`, on the head and on develop. Control: with one suite, `--list` prints it, rc 0.
* **Mechanism re-measured for this ticket** on `/bin/bash` 3.2.57, using minimal shapes rather than the script:

  | shape (all under `set -u`, empty `reached=()`) | result |
  | -- | -- |
  | rintf '%s\n' "${reached[@]}"`— the`:72` shape | eached[@]: unbound variable`; the next command never runs |
  | rintf '%s\n' ${reached[@]+"${reached[@]}"}`— the`:92` shape | 0, but **writes one newline (1 byte)** |
  | ${#reached[@]} -eq 0 ] || printf '%s\n' "${reached[@]}"` — guarded | 0, **0 bytes** |
  | ntrol: the `:92` shape with one element | ints it |
  * **Why the** `:92` **shape writes a byte:** `printf` with no arguments still prints its format once.
  * **Why that never mattered at** `:92`**:** there the output goes into `$(…)`, which strips the newline.
  * **Why it matters at** `:72`**:** the output goes to stdout, so the reader sees a blank line.
* **Fix shape:** either the guarded form, or the `+alternate` form if one blank line is acceptable. Choose by the regression cell.
* **Regression cell:** `--list` on a repo with no suites must give:
  * rc 0;
  * 0 `unbound variable` lines;
  * **empty output, measured in bytes.** A `$(…)` capture reads empty for both forms (measured length 0), so it cannot tell them apart.
* **Exposure, from the gate's read census:**
  * no gate calls `--list`: preflight uses `--check-unreached` and run mode, and `test:shell` and the two retired workflows use run mode;
  * `DEV-PROCESS.md:129` and `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1195` tell a person to run `--list` for inspection.

  A person running it on an empty tree is the only exposure.

### QA-7 — refusal headline (in #953's delta)

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-shell-suites.sh:196-206` at #953 head `8987b8a0e`.
  * `:202` prints the same headline for every cause.
  * `:197-201` choose the cause text, and `:203` prints it inside the parenthetical: `printed nothing`, or `printed a list with N usable name(s), GIT_DIR absent`.
* **Not on develop:** `could not ask git` occurs 0 times in develop `2d864ae92`'s runner. Control: it occurs once at the head.
* **Why it is imprecise:** the file's own comment at `:176-183` separates "git printed nothing, so it could not be asked" from "git printed text from which no usable name parses". The headline fits the first and misstates the second.
* **Measured by the gate (probe v2 §A/§E, bite T13):**
  * A fake git printing nothing, the real list with CRLF endings, or the real list minus `GIT_DIR` all print the same headline; only line 2 differs.
  * With git absent from PATH, the output is identical to the empty-list case, and nothing says git is missing.
  * T13 swaps the empty-case reason text for the CRLF one and reddens no cell, because the empty-list cell matches only the headline (test `:315` at `8987b8a0e`).
* **Behaviour is correct:** every cause refuses before any suite runs. This is wording only.
* **Fix shape (the gate's):** a headline per cause, e.g. "git's list of repository-local variables is unusable" or "git is not on PATH".
* **Regression cell:** the empty-list cell (test `:310-317`) also matches `printed nothing`, so a T13-style swap reddens it.

### Board search before filing

`searchIssues` with comments and archived issues included, every page read:

| term | hits |
| -- | -- |
| `reached[@]` | 127 |
| `run-shell-suites.sh` | 88 |
| `unbound variable` | 124 |
| `could not ask git` | 127 |
| unique across all four | 394 |

* **Positive control:** the path search returns KS-1086 and KS-1088.
* **Literal match:** Linear's search tokenises the term (`reached[@]` returns 127, the same count as bare `reached`). So every hit's description and comments were matched as literals for `reached[@]`, `reached[@]: unbound variable`, `could not ask git`, `run-shell-suites.sh --list` and `line 72`.
  * **Result: 0 tickets carry any of them.**
  * Matcher controls: a planted string matched all five, and a near-miss string matched none. On an earlier pass, the same fetch path counted `run-shell-suites.sh` 4 times in KS-1086.
* **Related, not duplicates:**
  * KS-1088: QA-6, suite isolation in the same runner.
  * KS-910: leg 12 runs `--check-unreached`.

**Source:** the tier-2 report on the Platform K machine, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1086-953-8987b8a0e-tier2-r2/report.md`, with QA-7 at line 248 and QA-8 at line 269.

title: run-shell-suites.sh restores git discovery but does not isolate suites: a suite that runs git from its cwd writes the repository it runs in (KS-1086 QA-6)
description:
## BLUF

* **The boundary.** KS-1086's fix (PR #953) clears the hook's repository-local git variables before the shell suites run. A suite's `git` calls then fall back to normal discovery. That restores discovery; it does not isolate.
* **The consequence.** A suite that runs `git` from its working directory, without first moving into a temp repo of its own, still writes to whichever repository it started in. Under a push, that is the pushing repository.
* **Today, no current suite does this.** All 18 ran under the fixed runner from a linked worktree, and the shared config, refs and HEADs came out identical. This is a boundary for a future suite, not a live defect.

## Recommendation

Low priority. Decide whether the runner should enforce isolation, or whether the fixture convention is enough.

The gate named two fix shapes:

* run each suite with its cwd in a fresh temp dir;
* or have the runner snapshot its own repo's config, refs and HEADs around the loop, and fail loudly on any change.

The second overlaps KS-948's proposed runner-level check that a suite run left nothing behind, so one change could close both. This is filing only; nothing is scheduled.

## Detail

**Source.** Tier-1 QA gate on PR #953 @ `de1ab62c0`, finding QA-6 (Observation), arm M3. MEASURED in scratch repositories.

* The suite was `git config qa.cwdplant 1` with no `cd`, run under the head runner from a linked worktree.
* It saw `GIT_DIR=unset`, with a cwd of `<worktree>/Blockchain/Dev`.
* The shared config gained `[qa] cwdplant = 1`.

**Current suites.** Gate arm F2 ran all 18 real suites under the head runner from a linked worktree. Shared config, refs, main HEAD and worktree HEADs were IDENTICAL.

**Scope, reasoned from the mechanism and NOT run:** the same would happen from a normal clone, and from a manual `npm run test:shell`.

**Where.** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-shell-suites.sh`, in the suite loop (`bash "$REPO_ROOT/$rel"`). Each suite starts in the runner's own cwd.

**Board searched before filing.** The issue columns search title and description, archived included; the comment column searches comment bodies.

| term | issues | comments on |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `run-shell-suites` | KS-1086, KS-1046, KS-948, KS-926, KS-910, KS-903 | KS-1027, KS-1086, KS-909, KS-926, KS-936, KS-945, KS-948 |
| `run_shell_suites` | KS-1086, KS-971 | KS-1086, KS-731 |
| `git_local_env` | 0 | 0 |
| `local-env-vars` | 0 | 0 |
| `suite isolation` | 0 | 0 |
| `temp dir` | PS-529 | KS-1027, KS-682 |
| control: `leg 14` | KS-1086 | KS-1086, KS-485, KS-731, KS-772, KS-926 |

None of them covers a suite writing the repository it runs in through a cwd-relative `git` call. Two are adjacent but do not cover it:

* **KS-948:** a backtick in a case name executes as a command. Its fix shape includes a runner-level left-nothing-behind check.
* **KS-903:** a survey of repo-root derivations, including the env-dependent ones.

**Report.** `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1086-953-de1ab62c0-tier1/report.md`

title: workflow-approve deletes the pending document and answers 200 "Document has been created" without reading originate's response — a refused forward (401, measured) loses the document
description:
## BLUF

* **Approving the last step of a workflow can silently lose the document.** `POST /api/workflow-instances/:id/approve` forwards the pending document to originate, deletes it from Redis without reading originate's response, and answers **200** `approved`**, "All workflow steps approved. Document has been created."**
* **Measured** by the QA agent's round-2 tier-1 gate on #951 (`02a22f4bb`, 2026-09-11):
  * the recorded forward (`x-user-id` only, no bearer) replayed into the real originate app gets **401**, with the gateway vouch secret unset and set alike;
  * with originate answering 401, the real gateway handler still returns **200** `approved` and **deletes the pending document**.
* **Pre-existing, not #951.** The same code is on develop `2d864ae92`.
* **NOT established: whether any environment has workflow-gated document types.** Reachability for real users is unknown. The gate assessed severity as Major; priority is left for the humans.

## Recommendation

1. Report approval and delete the pending document **only after originate returns 2xx**. On any other status, or a network error, keep the pending document and return an error to the caller.
2. Forward a credential originate accepts. Today the forward carries `x-user-id` alone, and originate answers 401.
3. Regression test: an originate stub returning 401 must not yield 200 `approved`, and the pending document must survive. Add the same cell for a network error.
4. If `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` is ever provisioned, this forward is also on KS-1083's vouch precondition list.

## Detail

**Code on develop** `2d864ae92`**,** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` (at `02a22f4bb`: route `:700`, `x-user-id` `:783`, `http.request` `:785`):

* `:781` `router.post('/api/workflow-instances/:id/approve', authenticateToken(true), …)`
* `:860-864` forward headers: `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, and `x-user-id` from `pendingDoc.createdBy`. No `Authorization`, no `x-tenant-id`.
* `:866` `http.request` to originate `/api/documents`. The response callback only logs "Workflow approved — document forwarded to originate" on `end` (`:871`), whatever the status.
* `:880` `proxyReq.end()`, then `:881` `await redisService.deletePendingDocument(documentId)`, before any response has been read.
* `:889` the 200 body: `status: 'approved'`, `message: 'All workflow steps approved. Document has been created.'`

**Consequence by case:**

| originate outcome | pending document | caller is told | evidence |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 401 | deleted | 200 approved, "created" | MEASURED (gate P2, F2b) |
| other 4xx / 5xx | deleted | 200 approved, "created" | READ |
| network error | deleted; "Failed to forward" logged | 200 approved, "created" | READ, not driven |

**Correction carried here:** KS-1084's body says this forward sends `x-user-id` / `x-tenant-id`. It sends `x-user-id` only (`:864`). A dated correction comment is on KS-1084.

**Board searched before filing** (team KS, archived included; titles, descriptions and comments):

* `/api/workflow-instances/:id/approve` → 0 issues, 0 comments
* `/api/workflows/:workflowId/approve` → 0, 0
* `workflow-approve` → KS-1083 and KS-1084, which name only this forward's vouch/tenant shape, not the lost document
* `workflow approve`, `workflowApprove`, `pending document`, `pendingDocument`, `approved and deletes` → 0 each
* `verification.ts:8` → KS-1083 and KS-501 (Done, an unrelated crash)
* controls: `verification.ts` → 33 issues; a nonsense term → 0

**NOT tested:** a live stack; any environment's workflow configuration; the sibling route `POST /api/workflows/:workflowId/approve` (`:943`), which was not examined.

**Source:** `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1041-951-02a22f4bb-tier1-r2/report.md`, section "Open", O-1. Filed by Platform K seat s177 on Wednesday's brief; the QA agent cannot post.
