title: Launcher preflight: four findings — a concurrent seat clobbers the warnings file, KS-907 miscounts sessions, F-02 names a missing key, rule 7 still says extranet
description:
## BLUF

Four defects in `Launch_Claude.command`. **This ticket files them; it does not fix them.** None blocks a session today. Each one either loses a boot warning, misreports seat state, or tells a seat to do something wrong.

1. **The warnings file is one file per project, so a second seat's launch overwrites the first seat's warnings.** Measured by s172 on 2026-09-11: s173's launch at 07:11:31 overwrote s172's at 07:11:14, 17 s apart, and s172's own warnings were lost.
2. **The KS-907 seat registry counted a session running in** `Testing Agent MAIN` **as "a live session on this project".** Measured by s173 on 2026-09-11. The mechanism is not verified.
3. **The F-02 remedy tells the operator to** `ssh-add ~/.ssh/secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw` **— a file that does not exist on this machine.** git works regardless, through the repo-local `core.sshCommand` → `3_Access_Keys/github_deploy_rw`.
4. **Launch-prompt rule 7 still prescribes "an extranet to-do per person plus a Linear comment".** That contradicts Kam's 2026-09-05 ruling that everything goes through the tickets. The project `CLAUDE.md` step 3 was corrected on 2026-09-11; the launcher was not.

A fifth finding already has a home: the SessionStart hook still tells every seat to `POST /api/seen`. That is **KS-925**, and the evidence is added there.

## Recommendation

Fix all four in the **master launcher template** as well as this copy. Per the launcher notes, `Launch_Claude.command` is a per-project copy of a master template, so fixing one copy fixes no other project. One pass proves all four:

* launch two seats about 10 s apart and check both warnings survive;
* run with a non-Blockchain Claude session alive and check it is not counted;
* read the F-02 text against `ls`;
* grep the assembled boot prompt for `extranet to-do` and expect 0.

## Detail

**1 — clobbered warnings file.**

* `Launch_Claude.command:90` writes `PREFLIGHT_LOG="$PROJECT_DIR/4_Credentials/.launch_preflight_last.txt"`, one path per project. The boot prompt then tells the seat to relay that file verbatim (`:392`).
* s172 (PID 64454, launched 07:11:14 AEST) read a file stamped `# launch 2026-09-10T21:11:31Z`, which is s173's launch.
* In that file, the KS-907 line listed s172's own PID as an "other" seat.
* Control from s176 today: the stamp `2026-09-10T22:36:54Z` equals `ps -o lstart= -p $PPID`. The file is not always clobbered — only when two launches race.
* Workaround in use: compare the stamp with your own start before relaying the warnings.

**2 — KS-907 miscount.**

* s173 attributed one of the two "other live sessions" in its KS-907 line to the fleet QA agent, by its cwd (`Testing Agent MAIN`).
* The registry lives at `Launch_Claude.command:244-379`. It reads `ps -eo pid=,command=` at `:328`.
* Not re-measured here, and which predicate matched is not verified.

**3 — F-02 names a missing key.**

* `Launch_Claude.command:107`, `:133` and `:138` all say `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw`.
* On this machine (s176, 2026-09-11 ~23:3xZ), `ls ~/.ssh/secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw` → `No such file or directory`.
* `3_Access_Keys/github_deploy_rw` is present, and `git fetch` returned rc 0 through `core.sshCommand` while the F-02 warning was showing.

**4 — rule 7.**

* `Launch_Claude.command:476` says: *"notify Stuart AND Peter — an extranet to-do per person plus a Linear comment @-mentioning them"*.
* Kam, 2026-09-05 13:55, verbatim: *"The team is not using the extranet much. I mentioned this yesterday. If anything needs to be escalated, please tell me and I'll send a WhatsApp message. Otherwise, everything has to be done through the tickets."*
* The project-root `CLAUDE.md` step 3 was rewritten to "on the tickets only" by s176 on 2026-09-11, as ruled by Wednesday. The pre-edit copy is in `5_Project_History/quarantine/2026-09-11-s176/`.

**Searched before filing:**

* `launch_preflight_last` — 14 KS hits. KS-907 and KS-911 name the file only as test hygiene ("every run overwrites it"); none covers the clobber.
* `secuura_blockchain_deploy_rw` — no launcher ticket.
* `extranet-session-check` and `api/seen` — found **KS-925**, which is finding 5, so it is not duplicated here.
* `Launch_Claude.command` — KS-907, KS-925, KS-655, KS-911, KS-912, KS-681, KS-78; none covers these four.
* Control: `KS-907` → 1 hit.

Filed by s176. Findings 1 and 2 are other seats' measurements, credited above. Findings 3 and 4 were re-measured at source by s176.

title: READ ONLY / unverified: the gateway's own Authorization-only calls to originate send no x-tenant-id — single-tenant originate may scope them to DEFAULT_TENANT_ID
description:
## BLUF

**READ ONLY, not driven by anyone.** api-gateway calls originate directly — outside `createProxyRoutes` — at several sites and sends only `Authorization`. With no `x-tenant-id`, originate's KS-458 block (`services/originate/src/index.ts:248-256`) sets `req.tenantId` to `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` in single-tenant mode, so those calls **may** read or write in the default tenant rather than the caller's. Independent of PR #951 (unchanged by it). Raised by the #951 tier-1 gate (round 1, Open item b) and not measured.

## Recommendation

Measure before any fix: drive one site per shape (a read, a write) as a caller in a non-default tenant on a two-tenant local stack and compare which tenant's rows come back. **Unknown that could dissolve this:** whether originate's `authenticate()` sets the tenant from the forwarded JWT on these routes. If confirmed, route gateway→originate calls through one helper that forwards the verified tenant — the same helper #951's F5 residual needs for the vouch.

## Detail

Sites at `develop` `2d864ae92` (grep for the originate URL in `services/api-gateway/src`, headers read at each):

* `routes/proxy.ts:554-556` — `GET /api/signatories`, headers `{ Authorization }`
* `routes/proxy.ts:578-579` — `GET /api/third-party-verifiers`, headers `{ Authorization }`
* `routes/verification.ts:129-138` and `:167-176` — `GET /api/documents/:id`, headers `{ Authorization }` when present
* `routes/batch.ts:146`, `:194` — batch certify / verify via `ORIGINATE_SERVICE_URL`, `authorization` forwarded; `x-tenant-id` 0 mentions in the file
* `routes/platform.ts:249-251` — `POST /api/admin/refresh-tenants`, `Content-Type` + `Authorization`

Not in this ticket (different shape, tracked on PR #951's body as READ ONLY): `routes/verification.ts` `POST /api/documents` and the workflow-approve forward DO send `x-user-id` / `x-tenant-id`, but without the vouch, so #951 would strip them once its secret is provisioned.

**Board searched before filing:** exact `getReqTenantId` → 4 (KS-174, KS-22, KS-26, KS-48 — none about gateway direct calls), `tenantGucContext` → 6 (none), `KS-458` → 1 (itself); control `KS-468` → 1. Fuzzy `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`, `x-tenant-id`, `signatories`, `third-party-verifiers`, `Authorization-only` → nearest KS-468 (Done — audited the 44 gateway proxy MOUNTS, not these direct calls) and KS-619 (Backlog — `middleware/auth.ts` conditional tenant overwrite).

Related: KS-1041 · KS-468 · KS-619 · PR [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951>) · gate report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1041-951-dd0a0c934-tier1/report.md` (Open b).

title: GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET: nothing provisions it and no deploy order or rotation is written — #951's control ships inert, and a gateway/originate mismatch drops gateway identity
description:
## BLUF

PR #951 (KS-1041 Step 2) adds a secret that lets originate tell a gateway-routed request from a direct one. **No tracked deploy, bootstrap or CI path supplies** `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET`, so every environment boots with the control **DISABLED** (fail-open by design, with a WARN). And **when the gateway and originate disagree about the secret** — originate deployed first, a gateway rollback, a rotation, or a gateway container not recreated after `.env` changes — originate drops every gateway-set identity. This is one logical path: provisioning, deploy order, rotation. It is also where the **provisioning-safety question** lives — whether switching the control on breaks the gateway's own non-proxy writes to originate (Detail, first section).

## Recommendation

Needs decisions before code. Decide:

1. where each environment's value comes from — Key Vault → `deploy.sh` `--parameters gatewayVouchSecret=…`, and a `fill_if_blank "GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET" "openssl rand -hex 32"` line in `bootstrap-env.sh` for local;
2. the gateway-first deploy order and a rotation procedure (a dual-accept window or a transition flag), written into the runbook **before any box receives the secret**;
3. whether production should REQUIRE it (`enforceProductionConfig` in originate).
4. **Before provisioning on ANY box, answer the provisioning-safety question below.** The #951 round-2 tier-1 gate (commissioned 2026-09-10 22:52Z against `02a22f4bb`) is measuring it as a separate PROVISIONING SAFETY verdict.

## Detail

**Provisioning-safety question — READ ONLY, not driven (added by s174, 2026-09-11).** The gateway's own `POST /api/documents` handler (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:879`; the verification router is not mock-gated — `index.ts:876-891`) forwards to originate through its own `http.request` (`:1044`, headers built at `:1024-1042`) carrying `x-user-id`, `x-tenant-id` and `x-tenant-slug` and **no vouch** — the file has zero `vouch` mentions at `02a22f4bb`. With `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` set, originate's provenance middleware strips those headers. The handler's own KS-39 #4 comment (`:1036-1040`) states what a missing `x-tenant-id` does: the POST writes to the fallback tenant and the new document looks invisible / 404s on the next read. The workflow-approve forward (route `:700`, `http.request` at `:785`, `x-user-id` at `:783`) has the same shape. **Unknown:** whether originate's `authenticate()` recovers the tenant from the forwarded JWT — if it does, the consequence shrinks. If the question holds, the fix is the one #951's F5 residual already names: send every gateway→originate call through one helper that adds the vouch.

**F4 — nothing supplies it.** Re-measured at `dd0a0c934` from git objects: **0 mentions** of the secret in `deployment/azure/deploy.sh`, `services.parameters.json`, `env.demo.json`, `env.dev.json`, `sync-secrets.sh`, `setup-keyvault.sh`, `deploy-all.sh`, `scripts/bootstrap-env.sh`, and 0 files under `.github` (control: `services.bicep` → 10). `bootstrap-env.sh:198,200,208` generate `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `PII_LOOKUP_HMAC_KEY` and `DEMO_SERVICE_KEY`, not this. originate's `enforceProductionConfig` requires `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `ANCHORING_SERVICE_URL` only. The #951 tier-1 gate counted 35 `--parameters` at `deploy.sh:721-757`, none of them this. Azure deploys therefore take the bicep default `''` and wire neither app.

**F3 — mismatch.** Measured in-process by the #951 tier-1 gate (round 1, cells S2.1 and S4.1): a merge-base gateway, or a head gateway with the secret unset, in front of an originate that has it → gateway-set `x-tenant-id` / `x-user-id` are stripped. Consequences read from source: the metering connector shim (`originate/src/routes/metering.ts:42`) stops matching and `authenticate()` answers 401; with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` in production `extractTenantContext` answers 400 "Missing tenant context" (`packages/shared/src/db/tenant-context.ts:67-74`); single-tenant falls to `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` (`originate/src/index.ts:248-256`). **No forgeability window in any order** (gate cells S2.2–S2.4) — order affects availability and tenant scoping, not the hole.

**Board searched before filing** (exact to decide, fuzzy to discover): `gatewayVouchSecret` → 0; `vouch` → 12, none about provisioning (KS-1041, KS-1080 akto-autoheal, KS-1081 env-template drift, the rest Platform S identity/verify work); `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET`, `deploy order`, `bootstrap-env.sh` → fuzzy noise, nothing about this secret; control `KS-1041` → 1.

Related: KS-1041 · KS-1081 (whichever env template wins must carry this variable) · PR [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951>) · round-1 gate report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1041-951-dd0a0c934-tier1/report.md` (F3, F4).

title: The Playwright env guard added in #896 reads config/ only — the variable breaking the CI run is read from fixtures/ and appears in no template
description:
## BLUF

PR #896 (KS-682) adds `systemTest/playwright/tests-unit/env-example.test.ts`. It pins `systemTest/playwright/.env.example` to every variable that `config/` **reads**. **The variable now failing the Playwright run in CI,** `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD`**, is read outside that scope**, so the guard stays green over exactly the gap that breaks the run.

**This is measured on #896's head** `a7b588a05f1a40b29b429e7dafa4a84d9a6283d0`**, which is unmerged. The guard does not exist on** `develop`**.** s171 found it by reading during its Phase 1 review of #896 (2026-09-10), not by running a test, so it was not filed then. Filing, not fixing: `systemTest/` is Peter's authority.

## Measured

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| Guard scope (#896 head) | `env-example.test.ts:23-24`: `PACKAGE_ROOT` = `systemTest/playwright`, `CONFIG_DIR = path.join(PACKAGE_ROOT, 'config')`. `:40` reads only `readdirSync(CONFIG_DIR)` |
| Where the variable is read (#896 head) | `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts:155`, `password: process.env.BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD ?? ''`. This is outside `systemTest/playwright/` entirely (`:110` on `develop` `2d864ae92`) |
| How the Playwright run reaches it | `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts:40` spawns `fixtures/pre-suite.ts`, which provisions the actors |
| In the `.env.example` the guard pins | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0** · control `API_BASE_URL` **1** |
| Readers inside the guard's scope | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0 files** under `playwright/config/` · control `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **1 file** |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docs/ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md` on `develop` `2d864ae92` | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0** · control `DATABASE_URL` **2** |
| `.github/workflows/` on `develop` `2d864ae92` | `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` **0 files** · control `API_BASE_URL` **4 files** |

## Why it matters

The guard's claim is true as written: it covers what `config/` reads. But a green guard reads as "the Playwright environment is documented", and the variable that decides whether the run can authenticate at all is read by the shared `fixtures/` the run spawns.

It also compounds with KS-969. Without `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` the pre-suite reports DEGRADED and exits 0, the actor manifest is not published, and `auth.setup` logs in with `''`. In CI that login returns HTTP 400, and 11 of the 12 tests never run. See KS-969 comment `e1358ef7`.

## Not decided here

Two questions for Peter:

* Should the guard also scan the `fixtures/` the suite spawns?
* Does `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` belong in any `.env.example` at all? It is a privileged bootstrap credential, and KS-969's open question comes first: what supplies it now that the published default is retired?

## Searched before filing

* Exact: `CONFIG_DIR` (10 hits, none about this guard), `env-example.test.ts`, `PACKAGE_ROOT`, `getTestAdminPassword` (KS-969 only).
* Fuzzy: "env-example guard", "readEnv config .env.example guard", "env drift guard fixtures directory".
* Opened, none carries this finding:
  * KS-967: a different pair of guards, the credential scanners.
  * KS-1081: two templates disagreeing with each other.
  * KS-973: pre-suite step items.
  * KS-682's 19 comments: `env-example` appears only in a bite table.
* Control: `KS-682` returns 1 hit.

Links: KS-969 · KS-966 · KS-682 · [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/896](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/896>)

title: CONFIG DRIFT: two tracked env templates disagree by ~39 vars — bootstrap-env.sh reads .env.example, CLAUDE.md documents env.example
description:
**BLUF —** `Blockchain/Dev/` **carries TWO tracked env templates that disagree by ~39 variables, and the two consumers read different ones:** `scripts/bootstrap-env.sh` **reads** `.env.example` **while the project** `CLAUDE.md` **documents** `env.example`**. A developer who follows the docs and a developer who runs the script get different environments.**

## Measured

| file | lines | vars (`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*=`) | tracked |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/env.example` | 444 | **103** | yes |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` | 302 | **64** | yes |

They are **separate files**, not a symlink or hardlink — different inodes (13295153 / 13295132).

**Consumers disagree:**

* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/bootstrap-env.sh:26` — `ENV_EXAMPLE="$DEV_DIR/.env.example"`, and it errors with *".env.example not found"* / succeeds with *"Created .env from .env.example"*.
* The project `CLAUDE.md` documents `cp Blockchain/Dev/env.example Blockchain/Dev/.env`.

**Divergence is substantial, not cosmetic.** Variables present in one and absent from the other include `ADMIN_USER_EMAIL`, `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS`, `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED`, `ENCRYPTION_SALT`, `ENTRA_CLIENT_ID`/`ENTRA_CLIENT_SECRET`, `BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS`, `API_BASE_URL` — against `API_GATEWAY_PORT`, `AUTH0_*`, `AZURE_AD_*`, `BILLING_SERVICE_URL`, `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS` in the other direction. **Several are security-relevant gates** (`ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS`, `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED`, `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS`), so which template a developer copies determines which gates they even know exist.

## Class — this is the KS-1077 shape

**Two competing sources of truth for the same configuration, where each consumer picks one and nobody reconciles them.** That is exactly [KS-1077](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1077)'s two npm-audit allow-lists, where Kam ruled `one-list-triage-two` (2026-09-10 11:29) — make the local triage record the single source. **Worth resolving as ONE decision with KS-1077 rather than twice**, because the same ruling shape almost certainly applies: name one file the source, and reconcile the other into it.

## How it surfaced

Found 2026-09-10 (seat s170) doing the KS-1041 Step 2 config-drift pass required by the PR verification protocol Kam adopted the same day (§3b: *"a var read in code but absent from the template is a finding"*). Adding `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` meant choosing a template — and there were two.

## Explicitly NOT done

**No winner picked.** The var was added to **both** templates in [PR #951](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951>) so neither consumer is left short, but reconciling the files is a decision about which is authoritative and what the ~39-var delta means — not a drive-by edit. **Scoped and evidenced only.**

Related: KS-1041, KS-1077.

title: SECURITY (local test stack): akto-autoheal runs as root with /var/run/docker.sock RW — env-scoping is only as strong as who holds the socket
description:
**BLUF —** `akto-autoheal` **runs as uid=0 root with** `/var/run/docker.sock` **mounted read-write, which grants host-equivalent read of EVERY container's environment through the daemon API and therefore defeats environment-variable scoping as a security control — but it is confined to the local Akto test harness: it sits on network** `akto_default` **rather than the platform's** `dev_secuura-network`**, and it is defined only in** `systemTest/akto/docker-compose.yml`**, so it does not exist on demo or kintsugi.**

The bound is in that sentence deliberately. A reader who stops after the first clause should not walk away believing this is live on a VM, and a reader who stops after the second should not walk away believing it is nothing.

## What was measured

| probe | result |
| -- | -- |
| containers with a bind mount of `/var/run/docker.sock` | **1 —** `akto-autoheal` (`willfarrell/autoheal:1.2.0`), mount **RW=true** |
| its user | `uid=0(root) gid=0(root)`, `Config.User` empty |
| tooling present inside it | `curl` **PRESENT**, `wget` **PRESENT** (no `docker` CLI, which is not a mitigation — the daemon API is HTTP over that socket) |
| its networks | `akto_default` — **not** `dev_secuura-network` |
| defining compose file | `systemTest/akto/docker-compose.yml` only |
| occurrences of `autoheal` in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` (the file the VMs run) | **0** |

**Controls, so the zeros discriminate:**

* The bind-mount scan enumerates and prints **all six** distinct bind sources across the 38 running containers (`docker/init`, `docker/init-platform`, `docker/seed`, one `secuura-api.yaml`, one `nginx-demo.conf`, `/var/run/docker.sock`) — so it can see bind mounts, and the absence of a repo-root or `.env` mount is a real null.
* The `0` for `autoheal` in the VM compose file is measured against a positive control in the same file: `originate` returns **1**. So the grep matches when the string is there.

## Why this matters beyond the container itself

**It is the general case of the specific control being shipped in KS-1041 Step 2.** That work scopes a gateway-vouch secret to exactly two of 34 containers by declaring it per-service, and verifies the scoping by probing container environments. **Any container with root + RW** `docker.sock` **can read those same environments through the daemon regardless of how narrowly they were declared** — so env-scoping is a control whose strength is bounded by who holds the socket, and nothing today records that dependency.

That is why this is filed separately rather than inside the KS-1041 PR: a finding about the estate's secret-handling as a class, buried in another ticket's PR description, is discoverable only by someone reading that PR, and it outlives the change that surfaced it.

## Explicitly NOT proposed

No fix, no privilege change, no compose edit. Changing a test stack's privileges was outside the commission this was found under and outside the current deploy grant. **Scoped and evidenced only — the remedy is a decision for whoever picks this up.**

## Provenance

Found 2026-09-10 (seat s170) while measuring the blast radius of the KS-1041 Step 2 vouch secret, at Wednesday's instruction to establish who can read it before building a control that depends on it. All readings taken read-only against the running local stack; nothing was changed.

Related: KS-1041 (the specific control this generalises).

title: kintsugi lost demo-service to the KS-641 fail-closed gate — the flag is unset on BOTH boxes and enabling it is a one-line decision with no owner
description:
**BLUF — kintsugi served** `demo-service` **for 20 hours and now refuses to start it. That is KS-641's fail-closed gate working correctly, not a bug. The point of this ticket is that the box lost a running service and the decision to restore it has no owner.**

Found during the s169 whole-estate rebuild of kintsugi (KS-601, under Kam's 2026-09-10 15:24 AEST ruling).

## What changed

|  | before the rebuild | after |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `secuura-demo-service` on kintsugi | `Up 20 hours (healthy)` (measured 05:35Z) | `restarting`**, exit 1, 18 restarts** |
| image | `62fb55bf4fa1` (2026-08-19) | `c4823b0d2fc1` (2026-09-10) |

Log, every restart:

```
FATAL: DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED must be exactly "true" to run demo-service.
This is a deliberate opt-in, not a default — refusing to start.
```

**The swap itself succeeded** — the container is on the new image. The service declines to start.

## Why — and why it is not a regression in the code

**KS-641** ("inbound auth + fail-closed non-prod gate on demo-service") introduced the gate. `DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED` is **unset on both kintsugi and demo**. The old image kintsugi was running had no such check, which is why it served for 20 hours — *it ran because the gate did not exist yet, which is the defect KS-641 fixed, not a capability that was lost.*

On **demo** this is the status quo, already recorded in the s168 handover as *"a deliberate opt-in guard working as designed"*. **On kintsugi it is new**, because kintsugi was three weeks behind and had never received KS-641.

## The decision, and why it is deliberately not taken here

`DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED` **stays OFF** — ruled 2026-09-10, on three grounds: it matches demo (and Kam ruled the same day that *"everything that we do this week is replicated and fixed on both servers"*, making parity an instruction); OFF is the gate's own intent as a fail-closed opt-in; and OFF is the branch that requires no signature, since enabling a fail-closed non-prod auth gate is a config change with a security shape.

**So this ticket is not a request to flip the flag.** It exists because a service that was serving is now not, on both boxes, and *"enabling it is a one-line change nobody has decided to make"* is precisely the kind of state that gets rediscovered by accident weeks later.

## What is needed

1. **A decision with a stated reason** on whether `demo-service` should run on either box at all — or a decision that it should not, recorded so the next rebuild does not re-raise this.
2. If it should run: set `DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED=true` in that box's `.env` (gitignored, so this is a per-box config action, not a code change) and recreate the container.

## Note on classification, recorded because it cost a correction

This was initially reported as *"the known demo-service down"*. **That classification was borrowed from the s168 record of DEMO and applied to KINTSUGI, a different box, where nothing had established it.** The mechanism was evidenced; the *expectation* was not. Flagged here so the distinction survives: on demo this is status quo, on kintsugi it is a state change.

⚠ The rebuild did not hide it — the swap ran with an exception keyed to the **failure signature** (`DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED must be exactly`), not the service name, so the same service failing for any other reason still halts the run. Every hit is recorded in `.rebuild/blocked.txt` on the box.

title: No Playwright e2e test has run on any PR since 2026-09-07 — the suite dies at a static lint gate before any browser opens, and the job name hides it
description:
**BLUF — no Playwright test has executed on any PR since 2026-09-07. The** `Playwright suite` **job goes red at a static lint gate that runs BEFORE any browser opens, so the red names the wrong subject and the coverage hole has been invisible for three days.**

This is a **test-coverage** ticket, not a CI-config ticket. It was found while measuring CI gate failures (KS-1075) but must not be closed as gate tuning: the gate is a symptom, the missing e2e coverage is the defect.

## What happens

`Playwright suite` (job in `.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml`) fails at **step 6, "Quality gate — static (tsc/ESLint/Prettier/knip/audit)"**. That step runs `npm run format:check && npm run lint && …` ahead of the suite. It exits 1, so **the job stops before a single browser test runs.**

```
  27:1  error  Missing JSDoc @param "label" declaration  jsdoc/require-param
  27:1  error  Missing JSDoc @throws declaration         jsdoc/require-throws
  27:1  error  Missing JSDoc @example declaration        jsdoc/require-example
  48:1  error  Missing JSDoc comment                     jsdoc/require-jsdoc
✖ 4 problems (4 errors, 0 warnings)
```

All four in `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts`. Prettier passes cleanly — it is the ESLint jsdoc rules alone. ESLint's own output says **3 of the 4 are** `--fix`**-able**.

## Why it hid — the part worth keeping

**The job's name names the wrong subject.** "Playwright suite :: failure" reads as *browser tests ran and failed*. Nobody re-reads a suite they believe is already running. The same shape as a wrapper printing a banner it did not earn: the red was true, and what it implied was false.

## Proven pre-existing, with controls

* Measured identically on **two unrelated PRs** — #938 (one nginx `location` block, zero service code) and #939 (TypeScript type declarations in one service): same rules, same line numbers, same count.
* `global-setup.ts` is touched by **neither** — 0 hits in each diff, against controls of 4 and 3 files actually touched.
* Last changed `42e778203`, **2026-09-07**, *"KS-969 round 2: a role collapse is not a success…"* — three days before either PR.

## What needs doing

1. Fix the four jsdoc errors in `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts` (3 are `--fix`-able).
2. **Then confirm the suite actually runs and report what it finds** — three days of unrun e2e may be hiding real failures. A green job after the lint fix is not the same as a suite that was green all along, and it must not be reported as one.
3. Consider whether a static lint gate belongs *ahead* of the suite in the same job at all: as configured, any lint error in the harness silently converts "e2e coverage" into "no e2e coverage" while still reporting a normal-looking red.

## Related

Found during KS-1075 (CI gate measurement, commissioned by Kam as `measure-then-decide`). KS-1075 covers the two *other* gate causes — a `bash -e` swallowed diagnostic and an empty npm-audit allow-list — and should not absorb this one.

title: The poller/reconcile blob writers also erase threadToken — on the CONFIRM/heal path, not just the failure path #936 fixes
description:
## BLUF

**The threadToken erasure KS-1058 fixed in** `markDocumentAnchorFailed` **is NOT the only writer that drops it. Every blob-rebuild writer in** `anchorStateSync.ts` **rebuilds** `blockchain: {...}` **as a literal with NO** `threadToken` **— including the CONFIRM and heal-to-confirmed paths.** So a document that mints a thread token at create and then anchors successfully has its `threadToken` cache erased on the success path, not just the failure path. Read from source, NOT runtime-measured.

## Mechanism (source, on develop `d4cf7e3cf`)

`updateDocument` replaces the `blockchain` column wholesale (`repositories/documentRepo.ts:480`, shallow top-level spread — established by KS-1058). Any writer that provides a fresh `blockchain` object therefore drops every field it does not re-list. The `anchorStateSync.ts` writers rebuild the blob from scratch with no `...existing` spread:

* `markDocumentAnchorFailed` **(:140)** — failure writer. **Fixed by #936 (KS-1058).**
* **poller confirm-writer (~:191)** — `blockchain: { txHash, blockHeight, anchoredAt, network, status, anchorId }` — no threadToken.
* **poller simulated-declaration writer (~:226)** — no threadToken.
* **reconcile heal-to-confirmed (~:299)** — `status: 'confirmed'` — no threadToken.
* **reconcile heal-to-simulated (~:327)** — no threadToken.

The confirm-writers are arguably the more serious of the set: they run on the **success** path, so a document that anchors normally loses the token cache that dashboards read (`state_thread_registry` is the canonical truth, but the whole point of the blob field per KS-1058 is to avoid that lookup).

## Why the type does not catch this

KS-1068 declared `threadToken?` as OPTIONAL (it is legitimately absent on many blobs), so a writer that omits it still compiles. The type makes the drop **visible to a reader**, not compile-fatal. Catching it needs either a spread-preserve pattern (as #936 applied to the failure writer) or a test per writer.

## Scope (behaviour — deliberately NOT KS-1068, which was type-only)

Decide, per writer, whether it should carry `threadToken` (and `simulatedTxRef`) forward — then either spread the prior blob or re-fetch the token from `state_thread_registry`. Same shape as KS-1058; extend that fix to the confirm/heal writers. **Verify at runtime first** — this ticket is a source read; a boot repro (mint → anchor → confirm, then read `document.blockchain.threadToken`) should confirm the erasure before the fix.

## Provenance

Surfaced by the KS-1068 writer re-check (scope item 3), 2026-09-10, read from source on develop `d4cf7e3cf`. Not runtime-measured. Sibling of KS-1058 (one instance fixed) and KS-1068 (the type hole).

title: Tier-2 verify has no statusless-blob cell — the carve-out is unguarded on the tier a third party reaches
description:
**BLUF:** the code half of the gate's **F5**, deliberately kept off PR #935 because round 2 of 2 was spent and a new cell would have moved the gated SHA.

**What #935 shipped instead:** the comment and title corrections only (commit `dd9463b37`), which need no re-gate. This is the work that was carved out of it.

**The gap:** the legacy carve-out `persistedStatus == null` is pinned by exactly **one** cell — the tier-1 `REGRESSION: a legacy statusless blob` — measured by s165: deleting `|| persistedStatus == null` gives **1 failed / 8 passed / 9 total**, and that is the only red. There is **no tier-2 equivalent**.

**Why it is worth a cell even though tier 2 cannot currently reach it:** after KS-1057, tier 2 always carries a status (`formatAnchorResponse` emits `status: anchor.status` unconditionally, `anchoring/src/index.ts:1503`, over a `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'` column). That unreachability is a **property of two services agreeing**, not a guard — exactly the "safe by accident" shape #935 exists to retire. A cell makes it stop compiling-as-true if anchoring ever stops emitting the key.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1057-verify-confidence-is-status-aware.test.ts`.

Source: QA tier-1 gate round 2 on #935, finding F5 (code half; the retitle+comment half shipped in `dd9463b37`). Related: KS-1057, KS-1069.

title: The latest-anchor selector documents a `confirmedAt` tiebreak it does not implement — and since KS-1057 that selector decides the verdict
description:
**BLUF:** `verification.ts:240` says *"Latest = highest blockNumber, fall back to most-recent confirmedAt."* **There is no secondary key.** The sort is `(b.blockNumber || 0) - (a.blockNumber || 0)` and `confirmedAt` is never consulted.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:240-242`, read at PR #935 head `dd9463b37`.

**Failure scenario:** two anchors on one document with equal `blockNumber` (including the common `0`/null case, which `|| 0` collapses). Ties break only on `Array.prototype.sort` stability over whatever order anchoring returned — `ORDER BY created_at DESC`. That is an **undocumented cross-service coupling**: anchoring can change its ORDER BY and silently change the gateway's verdict. The gate drove two equal-`blockNumber` anchors and **flipped the verdict**.

**Why it matters now and did not before:** until KS-1057 the selected anchor's `status` was dropped on the way into the blob, so which anchor won was cosmetic. **It is now the verdict** — `status: latest.status` is carried at line 265. A cosmetic selector became a decisive one in the same commit that fixed F1.

**Fix shape:** implement the documented tiebreak (or correct the comment to say there is none), and pin it with a cell driving two equal-`blockNumber` anchors.

Source: QA tier-1 gate round 2 on #935, finding F9 (POLISH). Confirmed at source by s165 before filing. Related: KS-1057.

title: A gate that examined NOTHING exits 0 — check-package-format reports "0 packages checked, 4 skipped" as a pass, and the hook's systemTest-only path skips in silence (third instrument in the family)
description:
## BLUF

**For a** `systemTest/`**-only push, NO gate examined the change — and "gate passed" is byte-indistinguishable from "gate did not apply" in the push output.** Measured on a real push (#927, commit `1041d2d32`), not constructed.

## What was measured

The push completed in **4 seconds** with a **2-line** log; the sibling push minutes earlier produced **100 lines** and `PREFLIGHT PASSED`. The difference is entirely legitimate and is **not** the finding:

* the hook files in both worktrees are **byte-identical** (`cc940299b2ae…`);
* the #927 commit touches `systemTest/` only — **zero** `Blockchain/Dev/` files — so the hook's documented `[ -z "$changed" ] && exit 0` (`.githooks/pre-push:216`) correctly ran no platform preflight.

**The finding is what happened instead.** The KS-989 formatting gate — deliberately placed *before* that early return precisely so systemTest-only pushes are not ungated — ran and exited **0** having checked **nothing**:

```
$ bash systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh --all
[format-gate] SKIP (advisory) — systemTest/akto deps not installed (npm ci in systemTest/akto).
[format-gate] SKIP (advisory) — systemTest/api-explorer deps not installed (...)
[format-gate] SKIP (advisory) — systemTest/performance deps not installed (...)
[format-gate] SKIP (advisory) — systemTest/playwright deps not installed (...)
[format-gate] 0 package(s) checked, 4 skipped, 0 failed
exit 0
```

All four gated packages skip for missing deps on this machine, and a bare `.sh` under `systemTest/__tests__/` belongs to no gated package in any case. **So the only gate that could have applied examined zero files and reported success**, and the hook's systemTest-only path prints nothing at all — no "systemTest-only change, platform preflight not applicable".

## Why this is a separate ticket and not another instance

🔑 **The family is now THREE INSTRUMENTS, and that is the point of filing it.**

| instrument | how a non-run reads as a pass | ticket |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `preflight.sh` leg count | `PREFLIGHT PASSED.` printed identically whether 13 legs ran or 10 | KS-1046 |
| the service unit suites | a blocking gate automated nowhere, so `develop` stays red | KS-1051 |
| **the pre-push hook +** `check-package-format.sh` | **exit 0 over** `0 packages checked, 4 skipped`**, and a silent skip path** | **this one** |

Three separate mechanisms with three separate fixes. **Three is where this stops being a run of bugs and becomes a design question about what "gate passed" is permitted to mean in this repo** — specifically whether a gate that examined nothing may exit 0 at all, or must report its corpus the way KS-773 made `lockfile-cleanroom.sh` report its own.

## ✅ Status 2026-09-30 — fix shape 1 DONE (PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1353](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1063-a-format-gate-that-examined-nothing-refuses-instead-of-passing-9372ddff6cb0), merged `d8b6c2a7a`); fix shape 2 moved to [KS-1049](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1049/a-prs-test-evidence-must-state-whether-the-preflight-ran-the-hook)

* **Fix shape 1 — ✅ DONE.** `check-package-format.sh` now refuses a run that examined nothing: when every selected package is skipped it prints `NOTHING CHECKED … This is NOT a formatting failure`, names the `npm ci` fix and exits 1 (Peter's ruling 2026-09-29). A run that checked at least one package still passes on its own verdict. `package_format_gate.test.sh` 29 passed / 4 failed on the old script → 33 / 0 after.
* **Fix shape 2 — NOT done here, by design.** The hook's silent systemTest-only skip is additive-output work on `.githooks/pre-push`, which is [KS-1049](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1049/a-prs-test-evidence-must-state-whether-the-preflight-ran-the-hook)'s scope (Kamil's). Noted there on 2026-09-29.
* **Fix shape 3** (the policy across [KS-1046](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1046/preflight-passed-is-printed-identically-whether-13-legs-ran-or-10-the) / [KS-1051](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1051/develop-is-red-on-the-servicesoriginate-jest-suite-and-nothing-catches) / this ticket) is unchanged.

## Fix shapes (not implemented — the design question comes first)

1. `check-package-format.sh` should distinguish **"checked 4, all clean"** from **"checked 0, skipped 4"**. The latter is not a pass; at minimum it should say so on stdout, and the project should decide whether an all-skipped run may exit 0.
2. The hook's systemTest-only path should **announce** that the platform preflight does not apply, rather than exiting silently — the hook's own comments already argue this position elsewhere (*"announce it and RUN, rather than skip in silence"*, `.githooks/pre-push:126`).
3. Neither is urgent on its own; together with KS-1046 and KS-1051 they are a policy, and that is what wants deciding.

## Scope — honest

The change that exposed this was **comment-only** (`git diff -U0` non-comment changed lines: **0**) and independently verified with `bash -n`, so nothing shipped unverified. The exposure is the general one, not this commit's.

⚠ **How this was found is worth recording:** I first read the 2-line log as a silent-skip defect. That was **wrong** — the mechanism above fully explains it. Investigating my own wrong hypothesis is what put me in front of the format gate's green-over-four-skips. The false alarm found the real finding.

Provenance: measured by s163 on 2026-09-10 during the F-927-1 ride-along push. Filed on Wednesday's ruling; not folded into KS-1046 because that ticket is In Review on #925, nor into KS-989 which is closed.

title: Per-tenant databases never receive the file migrations — CORE_MIGRATIONS FORCEs RLS with ZERO policies, so a per-tenant DB is dark on 5 core tables from boot 1 (permanent)
description:
## BLUF

**Per-tenant databases receive** `CORE_MIGRATIONS` **and NEVER the file migrations — not on any boot.** Measured, not read. The consequence is not "039 is missing": `CORE_MIGRATIONS` **enables and FORCEs** row-level security on five core tables while **every policy for them lives only in** `migrations/*.sql`, so a per-tenant DB lands with **FORCE RLS and ZERO policies**. A non-superuser runtime role then reads **zero rows** from `documents`, `certifications`, `audit_logs`, `custody_events` and `shares` — unconditionally, with no GUC able to fix it — and the boot log reports `{migrated: N, skipped: 0}`.

**Latent today, live the moment** `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB=true` — i.e. the moment KS-160 Path A (per-tenant-DB isolation) ships. This is a landmine directly under that roadmap item.

## The defect, in source

`services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`

* **:932** `applyFileMigrations(pg, dbUrl, 'main', fileMigrations)`
* **:939** `applyFileMigrations(pg, platformDbUrl, 'platform', fileMigrations)`
* **:1108** `migrateDatabase(pg, tenantConnStr, tenantDbName, CORE_MIGRATIONS)` ← the tenant loop, **no** `applyFileMigrations` **call anywhere in it**

`applyFileMigrations`' own signature makes it structural, not an oversight in one call: `dbName: 'main' | 'platform'`. A tenant database is not a value that type admits, and the routing inside it (`if (dbName === 'main' && m.isPlatform) continue`) has no third branch.

**The trap is the split:** `CREATE POLICY` appears **0 times** in the whole of `startup-migrations.ts` (control: the same grep finds **19** in `migrations/*.sql`), while CORE_MIGRATIONS runs `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` + `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` at :439-440 (`custody_events`), :485-486 (`shares`), :551-552 (`documents`) and a `format()` loop at :633-634. **Enforcement ships in the array; permission ships in the files. Tenant DBs get only the array.**

The second path that can seed a tenant DB does not close the gap either: `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:62` `createTenantDatabase()` applies `INIT_SCRIPTS_DIR` (`docker/init`, bind-mounted at `docker-compose.yml:2038`) — **12 .sql files, 0** `CREATE POLICY`**, 0** `tenant_scope_bypass` (control: `migrations/` has 17 files with `CREATE POLICY`, 3 with `tenant_scope_bypass`).

## Measurement

Disposable `postgres:15-alpine`, SSL enabled with a locally-signed CA so the product's hard-coded `?sslmode=require` tenant connection could genuinely succeed. Product's own `runStartupMigrations()` driven from source; `startup-migrations.ts` blob verified **identical on** `origin/develop` **and HEAD** (`6a1b53bafa1ad707e663814f95ed92a668e96280`), `migrations/` identical too. Platform DB + main DB + one genuinely separate tenant DB (`tenant_alpha`). Four boots.

| read on `tenant_alpha` after 3 boots | value |
| -- | -- |
| public tables (**connection proof**) | **27** — `documents`, `users`, `anchor_store` all present |
| `_secuura_migrations` table exists | **0 — the file stage never ran, once** |
| `pg_policy` rows | **0** |
| tables with RLS **enabled** | **5** — all also `FORCE` |

**Same reader on the main DB (positive control):** `_secuura_migrations` **48 rows**, `039_rls_fail_closed.sql` **recorded**, `pg_policy` **28**, RLS tables **25**.

### The consequence, measured as an action (not asserted)

`secuuraadmin` is a superuser and bypasses RLS, so the owner read proves nothing. Re-measured as `s163_app` — `LOGIN NOBYPASSRLS`, non-superuser, the KS-109 runtime-role shape:

```
tenant_alpha  documents / certifications / audit_logs   ->  0 , 0 , 0
tenant_alpha  documents WITH both GUCs the product sets ->  0    (no policy exists to satisfy)
tenant_alpha  organizations (non-RLS table, 1 row)      ->  1    <- NON-ZERO CONTROL: login + grants work
superuser, row_security=off, tenant_alpha documents     ->  1    <- the row DOES exist
secuura       documents, NO GUC set                     ->  0
secuura       documents WITH app.tenant_scope_bypass    ->  1    <- DISCRIMINATION CONTROL
secuura       documents WITH app.current_tenant_id      ->  1
```

The zeros on `tenant_alpha` are real zeros, not an unreachable database: the same role, in the same database, reads 1 from a non-RLS table.

## Scope — honest in both directions

**REFUTED for the configuration running today.** `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` defaults false (`services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:245`), so every `tenant_config` row points at the shared app DB — which *does* get the file migrations via the `'main'` path. Confirmed in my own run: the 6 seeded tenants all carried `db_name = secuura`. **5 occurrences of the flag repo-wide, all code/comment, ZERO config sites** (control: `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` appears in `docker-compose.yml`).

⚠ **NOT measured against demo or UAT** — both are held. The above is source + a local reproduction.

**CONFIRMED for per-tenant DBs.** Set the flag — or provision any tenant whose `db_name` differs from the app DB — and that tenant is dark on its five core tables from its first boot, permanently, with a success line in the log.

## Fix shape (not implemented here)

Give `applyFileMigrations` a tenant arm and call it from the loop before `migrateDatabase`, with the file corpus filtered the way `'main'` filters it. The `'main' | 'platform'` union is the thing to widen — an omission should stop compiling rather than be remembered. Any fix must also address the **ordering** KS-1054 documents (039 needs tables CORE creates), or a tenant DB simply reproduces the boot-1 window instead of the permanent one.

## Provenance

QA gate finding **F-928-3**, read-from-source and explicitly UNMEASURED, carried inside KS-1054. Measured here by s163 on 2026-09-09, local disposable containers only, removed at close. Demo, UAT and every shared database untouched.

---

## TLS: the tenant connection is VERIFY-FULL, and that is what makes F-928-4's counter load-bearing

**The product hard-codes** `?sslmode=require` **on the tenant connection string** (`startup-migrations.ts:1105`), and `pg-connection-string` **2.12.0 treats** `require` **as** `verify-full` — it says so itself at runtime: *"The SSL modes 'prefer', 'require', and 'verify-ca' are treated as aliases for 'verify-full'."* So the tenant loop does not merely want TLS; it requires a **CA-verifiable certificate chain and a matching hostname**.

**Proved both ways before any of the measurement above was trusted**, against the same container and the same connection-string shape:

```
no trusted CA   ->  "unable to verify the first certificate"
trusted CA      ->  connected, current_database() = tenant_alpha
```

That is why this ticket's zeros mean something: had I not stood the CA up, the tenant DB would have been unreachable and I would have measured my own container instead of the product.

**The consequence on a real deployment:** on any deployment whose tenant database does not present a CA-verifiable certificate, **the tenant loop connects to nothing at all** — and because of the counter defect below, the boot still logs `{migrated: N, skipped: 0}`.

### F-928-4 — the counter cannot report a failure under any condition (measured)

Registered a tenant pointing at `tenant_does_not_exist` — **proved absent** in `pg_database`, **proved present** in the loop's own `SELECT` — and booted:

```
[INFO] Tenant DB migrations complete {"migrated":8,"skipped":0,"total":8}
```

**Mechanism, to the line:** `migrateDatabase` (`startup-migrations.ts:800`) swallows every per-statement error in its own inner `try/catch` and returns `applied`, so it **never throws**, so the tenant loop's `catch` arm at `:1112` is **dead code**. And `new pg.Pool()` does not connect eagerly, so even total connection failure surfaces inside `pool.query` and is swallowed with the rest. `migrated++` therefore counts a tenant whose database does not exist.

### These three legs are ONE path, which is why they are on one ticket

**Tenant provisioning is broken and nothing reports it:**

1. a per-tenant DB arrives **deny-all** on five core tables (the body of this ticket),
2. it **cannot be connected to at all** without a CA-verifiable cert,
3. and the boot **reports success under every one of those failures**.

Filed together deliberately — as three separate tickets each one looks survivable on its own.

title: Fresh databases are FAIL-OPEN until the second boot — 039_rls_fail_closed does not apply on boot 1 (file stage runs before the CORE stage it depends on)
description:
## BLUF

**On a freshly provisioned database,** `users.tenant_isolation` **is FAIL-OPEN after the first boot — an unset tenant GUC sees ALL rows.** `039_rls_fail_closed.sql` does not apply on boot 1 because the file stage runs **before** the CORE stage that creates a table it depends on. Seven file migrations fail on boot 1; all seven succeed on boot 2.

⚠ **PRODUCTION IS NOT IMPLICATED by this mechanism.** A long-lived database already has the dependency tables, so `039` applies on the first boot after deploy. **The exposure is freshly provisioned databases: new environments, CI and local stacks, DR restores, and newly provisioned tenant DBs.**

## Provenance — this is the QA gate's measurement, not mine

Measured by the cross-project QA agent on 2026-09-09 against PR #928, on a real `postgres:15-alpine` driven by **the product's own** `runStartupMigrations()` via `tsx`, `MIGRATIONS_DIR` pointed at the repo `migrations/`, a fresh database per side. Report: `2026-09-09-s161-batch-six-prs/report.md` §2, with boot transcripts in its `evidence/` directory.

**I have NOT re-run it.** Filed because §2 of that report says it bears on the deploy hold and asks for it loudly. The numbers below are relayed; the mechanism is the gate's, and the pre-deploy check is the gate's own recommendation.

## The measurement

```
after boot 1:  USING ( current_setting('app.current_tenant_id',true) IS NULL
                       OR current_setting(...) = ''
                       OR tenant_id::text = current_setting(...) )      <-- unset GUC sees ALL rows

after boot 2:  USING ( current_setting(...) IS NOT NULL AND <> ''
                       AND tenant_id::text = current_setting(...) )
                     OR current_setting('app.tenant_scope_bypass',true) = 'platform_admin'
               + policy users_auth_lookup
```

`039` fails on boot 1 with `type "oauth_apps" does not exist` — the file stage runs before the CORE_MIGRATIONS stage that creates that table.

**Seven file migrations fail on boot 1 and all seven succeed on boot 2:** `006, 008, 026, 027, 028, 039, 047`. `048_ks754_widen_processed_by_to_text.sql` **applied cleanly on boot 1.**

## Why it matters beyond the fresh DB

**Both #928 and #929 assume** `039` **is in force.** #929's whole justification is that fail-closed RLS with an unresolved tenant GUC produces a 0-row UPDATE. On a database where `039` has not applied, that condition does not arise from that cause — **and cross-tenant rows are visible.**

The same assumption runs through **KS-1052** (the credential-lifecycle guards) and the KS-963 work.

## 🔴 Pre-deploy check — put this on any deploy that touches these services

On the **target** database, confirm **both**:

1. `048` is present in `_secuura_migrations`.
2. `pg_policy` for `users.tenant_isolation` shows the `IS NOT NULL AND <> ''` form — **not** the `IS NULL OR = ''` form.

⚠ `run-migrations.sh` **exits 0 when migrations fail**, so compose's own gate does not catch this. The check has to be made against the database, not inferred from a runner's exit code.

## Related, un-driven, and probably the more serious half

**QA F-928-3 (read from source, NOT measured):** the tenant loop calls `migrateDatabase(pg, tenantConnStr, tenantDbName, CORE_MIGRATIONS)` only — **it never calls** `applyFileMigrations`. If `039` exists only as a file, **tenant databases never receive the fail-closed flip at all**, on any boot. The gate never configured `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` and provisioned no tenant DB, so this is a code-path reading and not a measurement. **It should be measured before it is believed, and if true it is worse than the boot-1 window** — a permanent state rather than a transient one.

## Fix shapes (not a ruling)

1. **Order the stages by dependency** — run the CORE stage before the file stage, or make `039` tolerate the absent table and re-assert later.
2. **Make boot-1 failure visible where it counts:** related to **F-928-2** (migration failure is still log-only; `runStartupMigrations()` is `Promise<void>`, so no call site can branch on `failed`). That is a design decision with deploy consequences and is **Kam's**, tracked separately.
3. **Provisioning-time assertion** — a new environment is not "ready" until the `pg_policy` shape check above passes.

## Related

* **KS-1052** — the credential-lifecycle guards that assume `039` is in force.
* PR **#928** (KS-950) — surfaced this; its `INCOMPLETE — 7 FAILED` log line is the first thing in the system that says so out loud.
* PR **#929** (KS-943).

*Filed by s162, 2026-09-09, on Wednesday's brief item 4. Numbers relayed from the QA gate and labelled as such.*

title: FLAKE (3rd occurrence, first with a name): ks949 seed-site enumeration fails ~1 in 7 full auth runs and passes alone — timeout hypothesis refuted
description:
## BLUF

`ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts` **fails intermittently in the FULL** `services/auth` **suite and passes on every re-run.** This is the **third** occurrence of a self-healing auth failure. It is the first one with a **name**, which is the only reason it is a ticket rather than a memory.

**Cell:** `the real person is gone from every EXECUTABLE seed site › the enumeration actually finds seed sites, including the one the gate planted in`

## The measurement, 2026-09-09

| run | scope | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | full `services/auth` suite | **FAILED** — `Error: STACK_TRACE_ERROR` at `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts:314` |
| 2, 3 | full suite, identical tree | 642/642 green |
| 4, 5 | full suite, after an unrelated mock fix | 641/642 then 641/642 (a *different*, deterministic failure, since fixed) |
| 6, 7 | full suite | **642/642 green** |
| — | that file ALONE | **30/30 green, 2.73 s** |
| control | full suite on clean develop `d4cf7e3cf`, separate worktree | **635/635 green** |

## Hypothesis TESTED and NOT SUPPORTED — do not re-propose without new evidence

**Timeout under full-suite parallelism.** The failing cell walks the whole `Blockchain/Dev` tree reading every `.ts/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.sql/.sh` file, which is the slowest thing in the suite, and `STACK_TRACE_ERROR` is a shape vitest produces for a task-level abort. **Refuted by the same instrument:** it passes under *identical* parallelism on runs 2, 3, 6 and 7. A timeout that fires once in seven identical runs is not explained by the walk being slow.

**Mechanism therefore UNESTABLISHED.**

## 🔑 How this was caught — the part worth keeping

`HANDOVER-s161.md` **§3 records two earlier occurrences (**`api-gateway` **1/293,** `auth` **2/633) whose test names were NEVER captured.** Without a name there is nothing to pick up, which is precisely why s161 declined to file them and why that was the right call at the time.

That handover shipped an instrument for the next occurrence:

```bash
npx vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/vitest-run-$(date +%s).json
```

…with the standing instruction: **capture the name FIRST, before re-running, because a re-run destroys the evidence** — and both earlier events were lost to exactly that.

**It was used on the third occurrence and it produced the name. The instrument paid inside one day of being written.** That is the difference between *"we keep seeing flakes"* and *"we caught the third one because the second one left us a tool."* This ticket exists to make that fact survive the handover it came from.

## Why this is now closeable when the first two were not

It carries a **named subject**, a **reproduction attempt with its result** (7 full runs + 1 isolated + 1 clean-develop control), and a **refuted hypothesis** so the next person does not spend the hour re-proposing it. Mechanism-unestablished is a fine state for a ticket; *unidentified* was not.

## Where to start

1. Re-run the full suite in a loop capturing JSON per run until it reproduces (it took 1 in 7 here) — **do NOT pipe through** `tail`**/**`head`, which is how the first two names were lost.
2. When it reproduces, read `failureMessages` from the JSON rather than the terminal: `STACK_TRACE_ERROR` is what the JSON reporter emitted, and the human reporter may carry more.
3. `ks949…test.ts:314` is the tree-walk control cell — `expect(sites.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3)`. Worth logging `sites` on failure, since an enumeration that transiently returns fewer sites is a different defect from a timeout, and both would present this way.

## Related

* **KS-1052** — found during that work; carries the same record.
* `5_Project_History/HANDOVER-s161.md` §3 — the two earlier occurrences and the instrument.

*Filed by s162, 2026-09-09, on Wednesday's ruling.*

title: develop is RED on the services/originate jest suite and NOTHING catches it — the suite is a blocking gate nowhere automated
description:
## BLUF

`develop` **is RED on the** `services/originate` **jest suite right now, and no instrument in this repository objects.** Measured tonight: 2 of 4 cells in `ks444-webhooks-create-description-guard.test.ts` fail on develop's own blob. **The suite is a blocking gate NOWHERE automated**, so the mainline can be red indefinitely and nothing says so.

Filed on Wednesday's ruling as a **new** ticket rather than folded into KS-961, because KS-961 is In Review and adding scope to an in-review ticket either reopens reviewed work or buries the new scope under a review that never covered it.

## The measurement

```
npx jest src/__tests__/ks444-webhooks-create-description-guard.test.ts   (in services/originate)
  2 passed   the two NEGATIVE cells (400s an object, 400s a null)
  2 FAILED   both POSITIVES - expected 201, received 500
  EXIT=1
```

Run on blobs verified byte-identical to develop: the test file is `229a3ccde` at both `origin/develop` and `b6884888d`; `routes/webhooks.ts` is `c88eb97db` at both. **PR #926 is the fix and it is open and unmerged**, blocked on an approval.

**Scope of the redness, which the QA gate did not measure:** the full service run is **48 suites / 509 tests, 1 suite / 2 tests failed** — the ks444 positives are the *only* failures in the whole service. ⚠ That run covers **48 of develop's 49** originate suites: it was executed on a tree missing `ks754-processed-by-widened.test.ts`, which is **unswept and named rather than rounded away**.

## Why nothing catches it — four instruments, each checked with a control

| instrument | originate/jest | control on the same file |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` (13 legs, 428 lines) | **0 hits** | `step` -> 18 hits |
| `.githooks/pre-push` (244 lines) | **0 hits** | `preflight` -> 18 hits |
| 17 GitHub workflows | only `ci.yml` + `deploy-demo.yml` invoke workspace tests, **both** `workflow_dispatch`**-only** | 17 mention `test` |
| the 7 `pull_request`-triggered workflows | **none runs any service unit suite** | read their `run:` steps individually |

**This conclusion does not depend on the Actions billing state.** Even with Actions fully funded, no PR-triggered workflow invokes this suite. Actions being retired (Kam, 2026-08-27) is a second, independent reason.

## The actual gap

**The only instrument that would ever catch a red mainline is a human filling in a Test Evidence line — and it only fires if a PR happens to touch that service.** `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` requires `**Unit suites (touched services):** run/result | not run + why`. A suite that is red on develop and untouched by the current PR is invisible to that, by construction.

## The precedent that makes this concrete

`DEV-PROCESS.md` **has already made this exact argument once, for a different subject, and acted on it.** Cross-cutting guards get their own Test Evidence line specifically because, under "run `npm test` in the touched service", they *"execute only when someone touches* `shared`*, which is the change least likely to add a fifteenth service error handler"* — and it concludes **"A guard on no path that runs is not a guard."**

**The same argument applies to a red mainline suite, and nothing currently makes it.**

## Fix shapes (not a ruling - the cheapest is probably the third)

1. A preflight leg that runs the touched service's unit suite, so a red mainline blocks the next push that goes near it.
2. A periodic mainline run whose only job is to answer "is develop green" - no PR coupling.
3. A **baseline-diff** rule in the Test Evidence block: the author records develop's own result for the suites they ran, so "2 failed" is visibly pre-existing rather than silently attributed to the change. This is the same shape KS-660 already applies to Schemathesis ("the failing SET ... + its diff vs the develop baseline set, never a bare count").

## Related

* **KS-961** - the aggregate workspace suite never runs on a PR. Adjacent, In Review, deliberately not extended.
* **KS-1046** - `PREFLIGHT PASSED` printed identically whether 13 legs ran or 10. Same family: a claim whose check did not run.
* **KS-927 / PR #926** - the fix for the red itself.

## Ask

**Kam or Wednesday to pick a fix shape** (or rule that the red simply waits for #926 and no instrument changes). Nothing here is urgent in the sense of a live outage - it is urgent in the sense that the next person to read a green board about `originate` will be reading a false one.

*Filed by s162 (Platform K), 2026-09-09, on Wednesday's ruling. Measurement is mine and reproducible from the commands above.*

title: users.ts:933 answers success: true over a 0-row profile update — KS-943 changes the symptom from stale values to undefined ones
description:
## The defect

`services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:933` updates a profile and answers success **regardless of whether the update took effect**:

```ts
const updated = await userRepo.updateUser(user.id, updates);
logger.info('User profile updated', { userId: user.id });
res.json({ success: true, data: { id: updated?.id, email: updated?.email, … } });
```

The `?.` tolerates a null return, and `success: true` is unconditional. So a 0-row UPDATE — which under fail-closed RLS (`039_rls_fail_closed.sql`) is exactly what an unresolved tenant GUC produces — is reported to the caller as a successful profile update.

## Relationship to KS-943 — this is its named consequence, filed deliberately

[KS-943](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-943) made `updateUser` return `null` when its UPDATE matches 0 rows (previously it returned `getUserById(id)`, i.e. the row's **stale** values). That fixes the repo's honesty and the two wallet call sites.

**Its effect here is a change of symptom, not a fix:**

|  | before KS-943 | after KS-943 |
| -- | -- | -- |
| response | `success: true` + the row's **stale** values | `success: true` + **undefined** fields |

**Both are wrong. The second is at least detectable** — which is why KS-943 is still an improvement — but a client reading `success: true` with an empty `data` object has been told the write happened when it did not.

⚠ **Filed rather than folded into KS-943's PR on purpose.** A consequence with a ticket is tracked; a consequence quietly fixed inside an unrelated change is invisible to review. KS-943's scope is the repo function and the two wallet handlers; this is a third call site with its own response contract.

## Fix shape (not a decision)

Check the return and answer honestly — a 5xx like the wallet paths now do, or a 404/409 if a missing row is a legitimate client-visible outcome here. **The response contract question is real:** unlike the wallet routes, this one returns a data payload, so "what should the client see" needs a call rather than a copy of the wallet shape.

## The wider question this raises, NOT swept

`updateUser` has **24 non-test callers** and most `await` and discard it. This ticket covers the one that reads the return and answers with it. **Whether any of the other ~21 discarding callers answer success over a write that did not land has NOT been swept** — it is the obvious next question and it is deliberately not claimed here.

## What is NOT established

* **No observed incident.** Filed on the mechanism, exactly as KS-943 was — not on a caught failure in a real environment.
* Whether a 0-row update is reachable on this route in practice depends on the RLS/GUC path for the caller, which was not traced.

Filed by s161, 2026-09-09, as the named consequence of KS-943.

title: A PR's Test Evidence must state whether the preflight RAN — the hook skips systemTest/docs/vault-only pushes and emits nothing at all
description:
## The ask

**A PR's Test Evidence block must state whether the preflight gate RAN.** One line:

```
preflight: 13/13 legs ran
preflight: NOT RUN (systemTest-only push — skipped by design)
```

⚠ **Scope, explicitly: this is about the RECORD, not the FLOW.** Do **not** change `.githooks/pre-push`'s skip behaviour. Skipping cheap pushes (vault-only / docs-only / systemTest-only) is a deliberate workflow property that keeps the hook out of the way, and changing it would land on Peter and Stuart without either being asked. **Additive only.**

## The defect

`.githooks/pre-push` *"skips instantly for vault-only / docs-only / systemTest-only pushes"*. When it skips it emits **zero** `[pre-push]` lines — no SKIP notice, nothing.

So for those PRs the natural reading — *"it was pushed, therefore the preflight passed"* — is **wrong**, and nothing in the PR says so. **The only thing that made PR #927 honest was the author volunteering it. A property that holds because the author remembered is not a property.**

The exposure is a client human's assumption: **Peter reads PRs personally**, and the assumption is wrong for every systemTest-only, docs-only and vault-only PR.

## Evidence — CORRECTED 2026-09-09, see below for what was withdrawn

**1. The hook executed directly, the way git invokes it** (ref line on stdin), in the ks1027 worktree:

```
printf 'refs/heads/… <local> refs/heads/… <remote>' | bash .githooks/pre-push origin <url>
  → ZERO output, exit 0
```

**2. The decisive predicate, recomputable by anyone** — files changed against the merge-base with `origin/develop`, matched against the hook's `^Blockchain/Dev/` test:

```
ks1027 (#927)  2 files, both systemTest/__tests__/*.sh        matches: 0  → hook SKIPS, silently
ks927  (#926)  services/originate/.../*.test.ts               matches: 1  → hook RUNS
ks950  (#928)  services/api-gateway/startup-migrations.ts     matches: 1  → hook RUNS
```

The two neighbouring cases are the control: the same instrument distinguishes a skip from a run, so the ks1027 zero is a real skip and not a blind test.

## 🔴 WITHDRAWN — the original evidence line, and why it is worth leaving visible

This ticket first cited: *"Measured on PR #927:* `grep -c -i preflight` *over the full push output = 0."*

**That zero was mine, not the hook's.** The push had been run as `git push … 2>&1 | tail -5`, which **discarded the hook's output before it was grepped.** The absence measured was one the filer had created. The finding was right; the provenance was not, and it has been replaced above rather than quietly patched.

🔑 **This ticket's own thesis, demonstrated on its own filer.** The claim here is that *an absent gate-signal is indistinguishable from a present one that nobody notices*. **The filer could not tell "the hook skipped" from "I truncated the output" by reading the record — hours after writing it.** If the argument above is ever doubted, that is the strongest thing in the ticket.

## Suggested fix (shape, not detail)

Additive, in the PR template / evidence convention rather than in the hook:

* The evidence block carries a **preflight line, always** — the ratio when it ran, or `NOT RUN` plus the reason when the hook skipped.
* Optionally the hook could print one line when it skips (`[pre-push] skipped — systemTest-only push; the preflight gate did not run`) so the operator has something to paste. **Additive output, not a change to what the hook gates.**

## What is NOT established

* **No measurement that anyone has actually been misled.** Filed on the exposure, not on an observed incident — say it that way if it is quoted.
* Whether **docs-only** and **vault-only** pushes behave identically. **Not measured** — only the systemTest-only case was executed. The hook's own comment groups all three, which is a reason to expect it, not evidence of it.

Filed by s161 on Wednesday's ruling, 2026-09-09. Related to KS-1046 and PR #927.

title: CLAUDE.md's "rebuild local after any merge to develop" needs its written exception — a merge with zero buildable surface is a measured no-op
description:
## The ask

**Give** `CLAUDE.md`**'s "rebuild local after any merge to** `develop`**" rule its own written exception**, so the next seat does not have to re-derive it — or, worse, skip it without measuring.

Current wording (project `CLAUDE.md`, "Local + new-Azure sync workflow" §1):

> *"After any merge to* `develop`*, rebuild local so it stays current."*

## Why

On 2026-09-09 (s161) #904 was merged to `develop`. Measured before spending ~30 min of image builds:

```
2 files:  systemTest/__tests__/pre_suite.test.sh            +26/-1
          systemTest/__tests__/quarantine_call_sites.test.sh +27/-1
files with a buildable/deployable surface: 0
```

No service, frontend, package, migration, Dockerfile or compose file. **An image rebuild could not have changed anything** — so the local `develop` ref was synced and the images left alone, and the report said so plainly rather than claiming "local rebuilt".

That was the right call, but it is the **second** time in one session a written rule needed a measured departure. **A rule with a legitimate exception that every seat rediscovers is a rule someone will eventually skip without measuring** — and the departure is invisible unless the operator volunteers it.

## Suggested wording

> *"After any merge to* `develop` *that touches a **buildable surface** (*`services/`*,* `frontend/`*,* `packages/`*,* `migrations/`*, a Dockerfile or a compose file), rebuild local so it stays current. A merge touching only test scripts, docs or CI config is a **measured no-op** — say so, name the file count, and sync the ref instead of rebuilding."*

The load-bearing half is **"say so"**: the exception is only safe while the operator states which branch they took and on what measurement.

## Scope note

⚠ **There are TWO copies of this file** — the project-root `CLAUDE.md` and the repo copy at `2_Project_Files/CLAUDE.md`. Both need the edit or they drift, which is its own recurring trap here.

## What is NOT established

Whether the rule has ever actually been skipped *without* a measurement. **Not swept** — this is filed on the near-miss shape, not on an observed incident.

Filed by s161 on Wednesday's instruction, 2026-09-09.

title: pre-push:230 names the stack-dependent legs as (3, 4, 7); measured they are 3, 4, 8 — a comment asserting a corpus that moved
description:
## The defect

`.githooks/pre-push:230` names the preflight's stack-dependent legs as **"(3, 4, 7)"**. Measured 2026-09-09 from a real run with `GATEWAY_URL` pointed at a closed port, they are **3, 4, 8**:

```
PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 10/13 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.
  legs 3 4 8 — local stack not up; you can clear this by starting it.
```

Leg 7 is *standalone-lock advisories* (not stack-dependent); leg 8 is *served-spec consistency* (which is). A leg was inserted and the comment did not move.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a quiet edit

This is **KS-1046's own failure mode wearing a comment** — a claim about what runs, written independently of what runs, and unable to fail. The comment is load-bearing: it is the rationale for sourcing `slot-target.sh` before the preflight so those legs probe the right slot, and it warns about the worse failure of probing slot 1 while testing another. **A reader chasing "leg 7" for that reasoning is sent to the wrong leg.**

KS-1046 (#925) makes it **self-correcting** — the verdict now *prints* the skipped legs rather than a comment asserting them. Filing rather than fixing quietly so the record holds that the comment was wrong for some period, and that the remedy was to stop asserting it in prose at all.

## Suggested fix

Either correct `(3, 4, 7)` to `(3, 4, 8)`, or — better, and in the spirit of #925 — drop the enumeration and point at the verdict line, which cannot drift.

## What is NOT established

When the comment became wrong, or which change inserted the leg. **Not traced** — I measured the current state, not its history.

title: KINTSUGI-DEV-SERVER-PLAN.md still says the VM "has NOT been created" — Stage B ran ~3 weeks ago and the credit-expiry warning has lapsed
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/deployment/KINTSUGI-DEV-SERVER-PLAN.md` **still says the VM has not been created. It was created about three weeks ago, and it has since run, failed, and been recovered from a 53-hour outage.** Record correction — no action on the VM.

## The stale claims, with line numbers

**1.** `:3` **— the status line**

> *"**Status:** Stage A complete (this document). **Stage B — creating the VM — has NOT been run and needs Kam's explicit go on spend.**"*

Stage B **has** been run. Measured read-only 2026-09-09 on tenant `efc17e5f…` / sub `a0ee7d32…`:

```
Name                   Rg               Size              Power       Ip               Loc
secuura02-kintsugi-vm  SECUURA-DEMO-RG  Standard_D2ps_v6  VM running  20.198.226.148   southeastasia
```

Note the size is `Standard_D2ps_v6` — **the exact option this document recommends** at `:40-42` (the non-burstable one, for $2.77/month more). So the decision the document treats as pending was not only taken, it was taken *as written here*.

**2.** `:50` **— the credit-expiry line**

> *"Project records show the **Founders Hub credit expires 6 September 2026** — about three weeks out. … **This should be confirmed against the current subscription before the spend decision**."*

That date is **in the past** (today is 2026-09-09) and the document's own instruction to confirm it was never carried out. I carried it out: `az account show` returns `state: Enabled`. So the line is **stale, not live** — it describes a deadline that has passed without the outcome it warned about.

**3.** `:151` **— the decision table, row B**

> *"⏸ **HOLDS for Kam's explicit go on recurring spend.**"*

Reads as a live hold on a thing that already happened.

## Why it matters rather than being tidy-up

This is the **KS-601 plan document** — the artefact a reader goes to for the state of the Kintsugi server. It currently tells that reader the box does not exist. Anyone reasoning about the 2026-09-07 outage from this document would conclude they were looking at the wrong machine. A plan that outlives its own execution and still reads as pending is worse than no plan, because it is *confidently* wrong.

⚠ This is the same failure family the fleet keeps paying for: **a deferral outliving its tracker**, and **a document whose position in the text is part of the claim** — the status line at `:3` is the sentence people act on.

## Suggested fix (record only, no infra action)

* Update `:3` to Stage B complete, naming the VM, its size and its creation.
* Replace `:50`'s credit line with the measured subscription state, or delete it and point at wherever credit is actually tracked.
* Mark row B done in the `:151` table and note the outage + recovery so the document is not silent about the box's one significant event.
* Link the outage handover: `5_Project_History/HANDOVER-kintsugi-outage-CLOSED.md`.

## What is NOT established

* The **exact** creation date of the VM. I confirmed it exists and is running; I did not pin the timestamp (the disk-list query needed a resource group and I did not re-run it). *"About three weeks"* comes from KS-601's own history, not from my own measurement — treat it as approximate.
* Whether the `:112` open question (does Kintsugi need its own Blockfrost project key?) was ever answered. **Not swept** — flagging it as still-open-looking rather than asserting it is open.

## Provenance

`az vm list -d` and `az account show`, read-only, tenant verified `efc17e5f-7637-4118-b92c-c5236d591cad` / sub `a0ee7d32-2e4a-47a0-9a49-9c001817a545` before the call. Document read at `2_Project_Files/Blockchain/Dev/deployment/KINTSUGI-DEV-SERVER-PLAN.md` (152 lines, last touched by `44ad82027`).
