title: 95 archived tickets sit in NON-TERMINAL states — measure whether a cascade put them there
description:
## BLUF

**97 archived tickets on the KS+PS boards are in non-terminal states.** Two were archived today (mine, restored the same session). **The other 95 predate this session and nobody has established how they got there.**

```
Backlog     83
Todo         6
In Progress  4
In Review    3
Blocked      1
```

**This is a hypothesis with evidence, NOT an asserted cause.** [KS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-995) established that `issueArchive` cascades onto sub-issues — including non-terminal ones — and that the parent-side check reads clean afterwards. **That mechanism would produce exactly this population, silently.** It may also be that some were archived deliberately.

## The measurement that would settle it

For each of the 95: **is its parent archived, and does the parent's** `archivedAt` **match the child's to the millisecond?**

That is the same discriminator that disproved a wrong third-party attribution during today's pass, applied backwards:

* **match → decisive for cascade.** One batch, one cause.
* **mismatch → closes nothing.** It was archived separately, which is consistent with a deliberate act.

One-directional, and that limit should be carried into whatever the measurement concludes — a mismatch is not evidence of intent.

## 🔴 Do NOT unarchive anything on the strength of this ticket

**83 tickets reappearing in Backlog changes what the team sees.** A restoration is as much a board change as an archive, and it is Kam's call on a measurement — not a tidy-up. **Measure first, report, then ask.**

## Items

- [ ] **1. Run the parent/timestamp measurement** across all 95 and report the split.
- [ ] **2. For any confirmed cascade victim, establish whether the work is still live** — an In Progress ticket archived by accident is different from a Backlog item nobody was going to do.
- [ ] **3. Only then** put a restoration proposal to Kam, with counts by state.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

Every count taken with a default query has been wrong on this board today — *twice*. `Tested Not Deployed` read 24 when it was 29, and a Duplicate census read 4 when it was 5 because the query capped at 250. **If 95 live-state tickets are invisible, every "what is open" number anyone has quoted is short by some part of 95.**

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, alongside KS-995.

title: Archiving a ticket silently archives its sub-issues, including NON-TERMINAL ones — and the parent-side check cannot detect it
description:
## BLUF

`issueArchive` **cascades to sub-issues.** Archiving 23 terminal tickets on 2026-09-08 also archived **KS-918 (Backlog)** and **KS-920 (In Progress)** — children of **KS-490**. Neither was in any target list. **In Progress is live work.**

**And the obvious verification cannot catch it:** once archived, the parent's `children` connection returns **nothing**. Asking the parent what it took with it reads clean.

Both were restored the same session. This ticket is about the mechanism, which is still live.

## Measured

```
child -> parent    KS-918.parent = KS-490      ✅ reveals the link
                   KS-920.parent = KS-490      ✅
parent -> children KS-490.children = 0         ❌ shows NOTHING
```

**The timestamps are what identified it as a cascade rather than a concurrent actor:**

```
KS-490  (mine, targeted)      archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z
KS-921  (mine, targeted)      archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z
KS-918  (NOT targeted)        archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z   <- identical ms
KS-920  (NOT targeted)        archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z   <- identical ms
```

Identical to the millisecond = one batch = one cause. **My own first diagnosis blamed a concurrent actor and was wrong; the timestamp disproved it.**

**Full accounting for the pass:** 33 intended + 2 collateral = 35 archived, measured 35. Only KS-490 had children, so the blast radius was bounded at exactly two.

## Why it went unnoticed until arithmetic caught it

The only reason anyone knows is the **census delta: −25 against an expected −23**. That is the shape most easily rationalised as a stale count. Every other signal looked clean:

* the archive calls all returned `success: true` — and they had, for the 23 asked;
* the parent-side `children` query returned **0**;
* no error, no warning, nothing in any response mentioning the children.

## The rule this produces

**Before archiving, query** `child → parent` **for the target's children and record the count. After, take a full paged census.**

```
expected delta = |targets| + |children found|
```

**If the delta is not exactly that, stop.** Asking the parent side for `children` is *the check that cannot fail* here — it reads zero both when there are none and when they have just been archived.

## Items

- [ ] **1. Make the children pre-check part of any archive procedure**, with the delta equation above as its pass condition.
- [ ] **2. Decide whether a cascade onto a NON-TERMINAL child should be refused outright.** Kam's standing ruling is that non-terminal work stays visible on the board; a cascade violates that silently.
- [ ] **3. Measure the historical population — see the sibling ticket** on the 95 pre-existing archived non-terminal tickets. This mechanism would produce exactly that.

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, from the archive pass that hit it.

title: `npm run quality` cannot pass in systemTest/performance or systemTest/akto — two pre-existing reds unrelated to formatting
description:
## BLUF

**Neither package's** `quality` **script can exit 0 today**, on `develop` or on any branch, for reasons that have nothing to do with the formatting reds fixed in #901. Filed separately from [KS-989](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-989) so they are visible rather than folded in as noise.

**This is load-bearing for KS-989:** any gate wired into the push path must start at `format:check`, never at `quality` — a gate that can never pass gets bypassed, and a bypassed gate is how five formatting instances accumulated unseen.

## Measured 2026-09-08, on `develop` and on the fix branch

### 1. `systemTest/performance` — `lint` fails

```
runner/actor_manifest.ts(140,18): error TS2540: Cannot assign to 'secrets' because it is a read-only property.
```

**Pre-existing, and proven so:** the identical error appears on `develop` at `:140` and on #901's branch at `:133`. **The 7-line offset is exactly #901's reformat collapsing an 8-line** `join(...)` **call into 1** — so the offset is positive identity evidence that it is the same defect, not a new one.

`lint` is `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.node.json --noEmit && eslint . --ext .ts`, and it is the second leg of `quality`, so `quality` stops there.

### 2. `systemTest/akto` — `knip` fails

```
Unused exports (1)       PUBLIC_BY_DESIGN_TEMPLATE_IDS  src/core/endpointFalsePositives.ts:70:14
Unused exported types (1) PublicByDesignTemplateId type  src/core/endpointFalsePositives.ts:73:13
```

`npm run quality` exits 1 on `develop` for this reason.

## Items

- [ ] **1.** `performance`**: resolve the TS2540.** Either the assignment at `runner/actor_manifest.ts:140` is wrong, or the type's `readonly` is. Deciding which is the work; it is a real type error, not a lint preference.
- [ ] **2.** `akto`**: resolve the two unused exports** — remove them, or mark them intentionally public in the knip config if something outside the type graph consumes them.

## Why they went unnoticed

Same reason as KS-989: nothing runs these gates. The pre-push hook scopes to `^Blockchain/Dev/`, `preflight.sh` is invoked by that hook, and Actions is retired. Both reds were found only by running `quality` by hand while fixing something else.

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, at Wednesday's direction.

title: A deploy that rsyncs the OpenAPI spec and does not restart api-gateway ships a silently stale published contract — rsync breaks the bind mount by inode
description:
## BLUF

**The demo redeploy runbook can ship a stale published API contract with every check passing.** `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` is a **file-level** bind mount into `api-gateway` (`docker-compose.yml:542`, `:ro`). `rsync` **writes a temp file and renames it, so the updated file gets a NEW INODE** — and a Docker file bind mount resolves to the inode at container-create time. The container goes on serving the **old** file indefinitely.

It is not stale cache. The container is looking at a **different file on the same path**.

## Measured during the 2026-09-08 deploy (632f16dfe → 400517aaf)

After the rsync, before any restart:

|  | md5 | bytes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| host `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` | `7e43a8d89afb…` | 1332983 (new) |
| inside `api-gateway` `/app/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` | `c014b2fce71c…` | 1329831 (**old**, dated Sep 7 03:45) |
| served `GET /api/docs/openapi.yaml` | — | 1329831 = the container's copy |

After `docker compose restart api-gateway`: container md5 `7e43a8d89afb…`, identical to the host; served bytes 1332983; the new text `BOUND TO THE` went **0 → 1** and `DIFFERS FROM the ACTING` **0 → 2**, with `organizationUuid` **1 → 2** as a control and an impossible string at 0.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a note

**The failure mode is exactly KS-978's**, which this same deploy shipped the fix for: *the published contract says something the route does not do*. KS-978 was a wrong sentence in the source. This is the **delivery mechanism** producing the same outcome from a correct source — and it is quieter, because every signal an operator would check looks right:

* `rsync` exits 0 and reports the file transferred ✅
* the file on the VM disk **is** correct ✅
* rebuilding the image does nothing (the spec is mounted, not baked) — so "I rebuilt it" feels like the fix and is not ✅
* the container is healthy, the endpoint returns 200 ✅

Nothing surfaces the divergence except comparing the md5 **inside** the container against the host.

## Items

- [ ] **1. Add the gateway restart to the runbook as a required step**, not an optional one — `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md` §Redeploy runbook. Wording should carry the mechanism (inode), because "restart to pick up the spec" reads as cargo-cult and gets dropped.
- [ ] **2. Correct the existing guidance.** The current understanding recorded in project notes is "a rebuild does not publish it, a restart does" — true but incomplete, and it does not say the container will serve the old file *forever* until something re-resolves the mount.
- [ ] **3. Add a post-deploy assertion** that fails loudly: compare `md5sum` of the host spec against `docker exec api-gateway md5sum` of the mounted path, and refuse to call a deploy complete when they differ. This is the check that would have caught it with no human judgement involved.
- [ ] **4. Audit for other file-level bind mounts with the same exposure** — `nginx-demo.conf` is the known sibling. Directory mounts are not affected; only single-file mounts are.

## Not a live defect right now

The 2026-09-08 deploy restarted `api-gateway` and the served spec is verified correct. This ticket is about the **next** deploy, by whoever does not know.

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, from the deploy itself.

title: The published admin credential survives in USER_TESTING docs while nothing on the demo seeds it any more — and the switch that would restore seeding now suspends that account
description:
## BLUF

`USER_TESTING/CREDENTIALS-AND-PORTALS.md` advertises `admin@secuura.com` **/** `admin123` at **:68** and **:177**. KS-964/KS-966 retired that published fallback in the seeder, and separately the demo's seeder does not run at all. So the doc is a published credential for an account nobody can currently prove is loginable — and the obvious remedy (turn seeding back on) **suspends** the account unless a second variable is set in the same change.

Two items, one code path (the seed-credential surface). Filed together per the aggregate rule.

## What was measured, 2026-09-08 (s149)

**On the demo VM's** `auth` **container, read-only, authorised narrowly by Wednesday (set/unset only, value never read):**

* `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` = **UNSET**
* `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` = **PRESENT-EMPTY**
* `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED` = **UNSET**
* Instrument validated first: `NODE_ENV`, `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `JWT_PUBLIC_KEY` all read **SET** (4 of 4 boot-critical controls), a nonsense variable read UNSET, and `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` reading PRESENT-EMPTY proves the probe separates present-empty from absent.
* ⚠ **Round 1 of this read was discarded, not reported.** Its positive control was `DEMO_USER_PASSWORD`, which also read UNSET — but that variable has a *published fallback* (`seedPw(var,'demo123')`), so its absence is invisible and it cannot prove the probe can see a present value. The control was mine and it was wrong.

**Direct evidence from the running system** (`auth` container log, started 2026-09-07T05:46:39Z, 7676 lines readable):

* `"Demo user seeding skipped — set ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true to enable"` — **present ×1**
* `"Demo user seeding skipped in non-dev env"` — **0**
* `"Demo user seeding enabled in non-dev environment"` — **0**
* Controls: 3762 unrelated startup matches (log is greppable), an impossible string returns 0.

**So** `seedDemoUsersInner` **returns at its FIRST gate on the demo and never reaches any account row.** The gate block is byte-identical between `632f16dfe` (deployed) and `400517aaf` (trunk) — sha256 `e77a5c30…` both sides, with a control block that DOES differ across the same range, so the comparison can see a change.

## Items

- [ ] **1. The doc advertises a credential the platform no longer seeds.** `USER_TESTING/CREDENTIALS-AND-PORTALS.md:68` and `:177` publish `admin@secuura.com` / `admin123`. Decide and apply: correct the doc, or restore the account deliberately. **Whether that login works on the demo today is NOT established** — the row may persist from an earlier seeding era with its old hash. Answering it needs a DB read that was outside this seat's authorisation.
- [ ] **2. Turning seeding back on now suspends the platform admin.** The moment anyone sets `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` on the demo to restore seeding, `requiredSeedPw('ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD')` returns null (`userRepo.ts:1039,1075`), and the null branch writes `status='suspended'` plus an unusable hash — **actively suspending a pre-existing row, not merely skipping it**. `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` must be set in the *same* change. This is a trap for whoever next tries to re-seed, and nothing warns them at the point of the switch.
- [ ] **3. Consider making the trap loud rather than documented** — the seeder could refuse to start (or log at `error`) when `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` is combined with a `requiredSeedPw` account whose variable is unset, instead of silently suspending it.

## Why this is filed and not fixed

Wednesday's ANSWER, 2026-09-08: *"Do not edit USER_TESTING/CREDENTIALS-AND-PORTALS.md yet… the fix depends on which way Q1 goes. File it as a ticket now so it cannot be lost."* Setting a credential on a running system is Kam's signature class and collides with his own `rotate-properly` ruling on the admin credential (2026-09-07).

**Q1 came back in a way that DE-ESCALATES the deploy:** the `632f16dfe..400517aaf` deploy does **not** suspend `admin@secuura.com`, because the seeder never runs. Item 2 is the residual risk that outlives the deploy.

## Not blocking the deploy

The 19-commit deploy is unaffected by this ticket. Recorded here so the finding cannot be lost when the deploy card closes.

title: Eight dashboards show a slot picker that filters nothing — latent today, wrong the day /metrics lands
description:
## What

All 12 dashboards under `observability/grafana/dashboards/` carry a `slot` template variable, so every one presents a slot picker. Only **four** actually use `$slot` in a query.

Measured 2026-09-07 by counting panel targets containing `$slot`:

| Dashboard | Panels filtering by slot |
| -- | -- |
| `k6_engineering` | 32 |
| `k6_executive` | 12 |
| `test_quality_trends` | 8 |
| `platform_engineering` | 4 |
| `platform_auth` | **0** |
| `platform_cardano` | **0** |
| `platform_document_lifecycle` | **0** |
| `platform_queue` | **0** |
| `platform_slo` | **0** |
| `platform_traffic_services` | **0** |
| `security_posture` | **0** |
| `test_openapi_coverage` | **0** |

On those eight, moving the picker changes nothing.

## Why it is not urgent, and why it is not nothing

It is **not currently misleading**, because those eight query application `/metrics` endpoints that no service implements ([KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never)) — the panels are empty whatever the picker says. Nothing wrong is being displayed.

It becomes wrong the moment [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never) lands. Those panels will then merge all four slots into one number, with a picker sitting above them implying they are scoped. That is precisely the defect [KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) existed to remove — a plausible-looking dashboard that quietly answers about the wrong system — reintroduced through the panels nobody had to touch.

## Evidence that the other four are correct

Same sweep, evaluating every slot-aware panel for `slot1` vs `slot2` against live Prometheus during a four-slot run: **56 slot-aware panels, zero returned identical data**. Where the filter exists it discriminates properly. This ticket is only about the panels where it is absent.

## Scope

Add the `slot` filter to those panels' PromQL when their metrics start existing, or drop the picker from dashboards that will never be slot-scoped. Do it **with** [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never), since the correct filter cannot be written or tested against metrics that do not yet exist.

A validator check in the shape of `observability/scripts/checks/container-join-slot.mjs` — fail the build when a dashboard declares a `slot` variable that no panel consumes — would stop it recurring, and would have caught this.

## Depends on

[KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never) (no service exposes `/metrics`).

Found while verifying [KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) on a live four-slot stack.

title: No service exposes /metrics — the secuura-services scrape job has never collected a single series on any slot
description:
## What

`observability/prometheus/prometheus.yml` defines a `secuura-services` scrape job over seven service targets. Every one of them is **down with HTTP 404**, and has been since the job was written — the endpoints do not exist.

Measured 2026-09-07 on a freshly rebuilt four-slot stack:

* `secuura-services` targets: **7 down, 404 Not Found** (every other job is `up`, except `kafka`, which is phase2-only and correct).
* `prom-client` is a dependency of **no** service.
* No `/metrics` route is registered anywhere under `services/*/src`, using `/health` as a positive control.

## Why it matters

This is not an observability-stack defect — the stack is healthy and correctly configured. It is that the thing it is pointed at does not exist. The consequence is that **every application-level panel across eight dashboards renders empty**:

`platform_auth`, `platform_cardano`, `platform_document_lifecycle`, `platform_queue`, `platform_slo`, `platform_traffic_services`, `security_posture`, `test_openapi_coverage`.

So the platform currently has **no application telemetry at all** — no request rates, error rates, latency, queue depth or SLO burn from the services themselves. What Grafana does show comes from cAdvisor, the DB/Redis/nginx exporters, and the test harnesses pushing their own results.

## Not to be confused with

[KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) corrected this job's **target ports** (they were 3000-3006 against services that listen on the 4000-range and 8080) and added `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/prometheus_targets.test.sh` to stop them drifting again. That work made the job name the right addresses. It did not, and could not, make the endpoints exist.

## Scope

Instrumenting the services. Roughly: add `prom-client` to the service template, register a `/metrics` route alongside the existing `/health`, and export the handful of series the existing dashboards already query.

## Blocks

* Per-slot application metrics. The scrape job uses static container names, so only slot 1 is discovered. Making slots 2-4 discoverable needs either a Docker socket mounted into Prometheus (root-equivalent) or a generated targets file plus a per-slot `docker network connect` — not worth its cost while the job collects nothing on any slot. Revisit **after** this, not before.
* The slot picker on those eight dashboards, which currently filters nothing because their panels have no slot-aware data to filter.

Found while verifying [KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) on a live four-slot stack.

title: systemTest: no suite drives a path-spelling (`//`) variant — the KS-858 class is guarded only by gateway unit tests, and 7 rate-limited auth routes were never driven
description:
## BLUF

**No systemTest suite anywhere drives a** `//` **path-spelling variant.** The [KS-858](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-858/security-class-a-scope-gate-mounted-as-an-exact-route-above-a-catch) class — a gate mounted as an exact route above a catch-all prefix, walked around by re-spelling the path — is currently guarded **only by gateway unit tests**. Nothing exercises it black-box, through the live gateway, the way an attacker would reach it.

Raised from Kamil's report (2026-09-07 00:50) of the **auth rate-limiter** instance: an extra slash on `/api/auth//login` skipped the limiter completely, was live on demo, and made the probed route *"about 300x more permissive"*. **He drove one route; his own note says the other seven look the same in code but were not driven there.** Driving them is systemTest work, so it lands here under Review G rather than on the class ticket.

## What is already covered — verified, not assumed

Read from `develop` on 2026-09-07:

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| Fix present | `normaliseRepeatedSlashes()` imported at `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:28`, mounted at `:234` **as the first layer** |
| Unit coverage | `src/__tests__/ks858-edge-path-normalisation.test.ts` (22K) and `ks843-erasure-path-bypass.test.ts` |
| Class ticket | [KS-858](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-858/security-class-a-scope-gate-mounted-as-an-exact-route-above-a-catch) (In Review, PR #884) — covers the **scope-gate** instances (`/api/anchors/batch`, `/api/documents/:id/sig-json`) |

**So the fix is in and unit-guarded. This ticket is not about the fix.** It is about the absence of any end-to-end guard: if the normaliser is ever removed, re-ordered below another predicate, or bypassed by a future mount, **no systemTest suite would notice**.

## What is NOT covered

**Nothing drives the spelling.** A sweep for `//api`, `api//`, double-slash or path-normalisation probes across `systemTest/**` returns **three hits, all false positives** — they match on `https://api.example.test/api`, the protocol slashes, in Playwright unit tests about base-URL resolution.

Worth stating plainly: **Schemathesis cannot find this class.** It fuzzes *values* against a published spec; the spec declares one spelling per path, so an alternate spelling of the same route is not in its input space. It did not find this one and will not find the next.

## The instance family this ticket adds

Seven auth routes carry an exact-path rate-limit mount in `index.ts` — the same *exact route above a catch-all* shape [KS-858](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-858/security-class-a-scope-gate-mounted-as-an-exact-route-above-a-catch) describes:

```
app.use('/api/auth/login',           rateLimit({...}))
app.use('/api/auth/register',        rateLimit({...}))
app.use('/api/auth/forgot-password', rateLimit({...}))
app.use('/api/auth/refresh',         rateLimit({...}))
app.use('/api/auth/password-reset',  rateLimit({...}))
app.use('/api/auth/verify-email',    rateLimit({...}))
app.use('/api/auth/mfa',             rateLimit({...}))
```

⚠ **Discrepancy, stated rather than smoothed** (the habit [KS-858](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-858/security-class-a-scope-gate-mounted-as-an-exact-route-above-a-catch) itself models): Kamil's message says **eight** protected auth routes, six unauthenticated. My count of exact-path `app.use('/api/auth/…', rateLimit)` mounts is **seven**. Whoever picks this up should re-derive the population rather than trust either number — the predicate here is narrow and may miss a mount expressed differently.

## Acceptance

**The assertion shape matters, and** [KS-858](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-858/security-class-a-scope-gate-mounted-as-an-exact-route-above-a-catch) **already learned this the hard way:** *"assert on the upstream, not on the status code, because in the failing case the status is 200."* The rate-limiter analogue is the same trap in a different costume — a bypassed limiter does not return an error, it returns **ordinary success, forever**.

1. For **every** rate-limited auth route, drive N+1 requests at the `//` spelling and assert a **429 appears**, exactly as it does for the single-slash spelling. Asserting "not 200" measures nothing: the bypassed case is a long run of perfectly normal responses.
2. Red-proof first — with `normaliseRepeatedSlashes()` removed or mounted below the limiters, every one of these must fail. A guard that cannot go red against the unfixed shape is not a guard.
3. Cover the shapes [KS-858](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-858/security-class-a-scope-gate-mounted-as-an-exact-route-above-a-catch) measured, not just one: `//route`, `///route`, `/route//suffix` — its table shows the obvious remedy closes only three of six.
4. Extend the same driver to [KS-858](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-858/security-class-a-scope-gate-mounted-as-an-exact-route-above-a-catch)'s scope-gate instances (`POST /api/anchors//batch`, `GET /api/documents//:id/sig-json`) so one suite covers the class rather than one family.
5. Positive control: the legitimate single-slash spelling still behaves — limiter engages at the same threshold, scope-holders still reach the upstream.

## Harness

Playwright, not Schemathesis: this needs hand-built request paths that the published spec does not contain, and Playwright already drives the gateway directly with per-slot isolation ([KS-682](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-682/playwright-slot-isolation-port-the-proven-platform-s-mechanism-no-run)). A rate-limit test also needs its own slot — it deliberately trips the limiter, and the [KS-682](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-682/playwright-slot-isolation-port-the-proven-platform-s-mechanism-no-run) sweep showed a limiter storm on one slot is felt by anything else logging in against that stack.

## Status

**Not started. Blocked on a Docker slot** — all four are held by another session as of 2026-09-07. The test can be written and unit-tested offline; it cannot be red-proofed without a stack.

title: pre_suite.test.sh silently quarantines a developer's live manifest and reports 24 passed, 0 failed
description:
## BLUF

`pre_suite.test.sh` **now silently quarantines a developer's live manifest and still reports**
`24 passed, 0 failed`**.** Round 4 made `pre-suite.ts` quarantine on the catch path; that suite drives
`pre-suite.ts` for real and does **not** protect `generated/`.

**The gate's sentence is why this blocked the merge rather than becoming residue:** it
*"REINTRODUCES KS-969's OWN FAILURE CLASS FROM INSIDE KS-969's OWN TEST SUITE."* **A fix that**
**reintroduces the class it removes is not residue to ticket; it is the ticket, unfinished.**

## ⚠ SCOPE — measured, and neither the gate nor the coordinator stated it

**This is NOT live on** `develop`**.** `systemTest/__tests__/pre_suite.test.sh` and the two quarantine
suites exist **only on** `feature/ks-969-…` **(#892)**, which is **frozen and unmerged**. Measured with
`git ls-tree` on both refs: `develop`'s `systemTest/__tests__/` holds exactly
`run_in_slot.test.sh` and `slot_target.test.sh`; the #892 branch holds those plus
`pre_suite.test.sh`, `manifest_quarantine.test.sh` and `quarantine_call_sites.test.sh`.

**So the exposure is anyone working on the #892 branch, not anyone on the trunk.** That does not
lower the severity inside the PR — it is why these are **round 5's scope if Kam grants it** — but a
reader should not go looking for this on `develop`.

## The fix already exists in the same commit — one file across

`quarantine_call_sites.test.sh:42-55`, added in the **same** round-4 commit, snapshots `generated/`
and restores it in a `trap … EXIT`, with the comment *"the real generated/ is this repo's, not*
*ours."* `pre_suite.test.sh` **needs exactly that.** The pattern was written, the reasoning was
written down beside it, and it was not carried one file across.

## Why "24 passed, 0 failed" is the dangerous part

The suite's assertions are about the pre-suite step's OUTCOME classification, not about the
filesystem. So moving the developer's manifest aside changes nothing it checks, and it reports a
clean run. **The consumers then have no manifest until someone re-provisions** — and the three
suites that read it fall back to seeded accounts, which is precisely the silent fallback KS-969
exists to remove.

## Verified read-only, and the honest half matters more than the clean result

On the worktree that carried round 4, `generated/actors.json` is **byte-identical to its**
**pre-session state** (seed `presuite-test-72460`, `provisionedAt 2026-09-07T07:57:14.721Z`) with
**zero** `actors.superseded-*` left behind. It survived for two reasons and **only one was**
**deliberate**:

1. the stash/restore in the sibling suite held — by design;
2. `pre_suite.test.sh` **was never run**, a refusal recorded in the round-4 commit for an unrelated
   reason (it writes to the `:6882` stack).

**(2) is a protection nobody designed.** A protection you did not know you had is not a protection,
and converting it into a designed one is this ticket.

KS-973 **item 3** is the near neighbour: same file, and also about its side effects (a fresh
`presuite-test-$$` seed each run, five real accounts, and overwriting the manifest). I read it before
filing, and I commented on it earlier tonight escalating item 3 for exactly this reason.

**It is still a different fix.** Item 3's shape is *a stable seed and an explicit opt-in gate* — stop
the suite touching a live target at all. **This ticket's shape is stash/restore** — protect the
manifest even when the suite legitimately runs. **You want both, and neither substitutes.**

Two further reasons to keep it separate: **KS-973 is Medium and currently HELD**, and burying a
MAJOR silent-mutation finding as an item inside a held Medium ticket is how it goes quiet — which is
this finding's own failure mode. **They cross-reference; they do not merge.**

title: The round-4 quarantine call throws out of a "Never throws" function, and the strict arm quarantines in silence
description:
## BLUF

**Two defects in the round-4 call site added to** `pre-suite.ts`**, both mine.** F-1 makes a function
whose docstring says *"Never throws"* throw; F-3 leaves the strict arm quarantining in silence with
no cell pinning it. One edit region — the catch block — so one ticket, two items.

## ⚠ SCOPE — measured, and neither the gate nor the coordinator stated it

**This is NOT live on** `develop`**.** `systemTest/__tests__/pre_suite.test.sh` and the two quarantine
suites exist **only on** `feature/ks-969-…` **(#892)**, which is **frozen and unmerged**. Measured with
`git ls-tree` on both refs: `develop`'s `systemTest/__tests__/` holds exactly
`run_in_slot.test.sh` and `slot_target.test.sh`; the #892 branch holds those plus
`pre_suite.test.sh`, `manifest_quarantine.test.sh` and `quarantine_call_sites.test.sh`.

**So the exposure is anyone working on the #892 branch, not anyone on the trunk.** That does not
lower the severity inside the PR — it is why these are **round 5's scope if Kam grants it** — but a
reader should not go looking for this on `develop`.

## ITEM 1 (MAJOR, gate F-1) — the quarantine call is inside the catch, so nothing catches IT

**Location:** `systemTest/fixtures/pre-suite.ts:157`, and `systemTest/fixtures/manifest.ts:107-114`.

`runPreSuite`'s docstring at `:90-91` states the contract: *"Never throws: classifying the failure IS*
*this function's job."* Round 4 added `quarantineManifest(...)` **inside the catch block**. If that
call throws, there is no enclosing handler left and `runPreSuite` **propagates** — so the function
stops classifying failures and becomes one.

It is reachable, not theoretical, because `quarantineManifest` is a **TOCTOU**: it does
`fs.existsSync(manifestPath)` and then `fs.renameSync(...)`. Between the two, another process can
move or remove the file, and `renameSync` throws `ENOENT`.

**Measured by the gate: two concurrent runs in one checkout crash 9 of 12, against a parent-commit**
**control at 0 of 12** — so it is introduced by round 4, not pre-existing. `run-in-slot.sh` documents
that slots run in parallel, so concurrency here is the designed case, not an edge one.

**Major rather than Blocker because it is LOUD** — the gate's words, *"it makes the instrument stop*
*rather than lie"*. No false green and no wrong assertion.

**Fix-shape:** make the quarantine unable to escape — wrap the call, and make `quarantineManifest`
itself tolerate the race (catch `ENOENT` from `renameSync` and return `null`, since a file that
vanished underneath us is already not in the consumers' way). **Regression cell:** two concurrent
`runPreSuite` calls in one checkout, asserting neither throws.

## ITEM 2 (MINOR, gate F-3) — the strict arm quarantines and does not say so

When `SYSTEMTEST_REQUIRE_PROVISIONED` is set, the catch still quarantines — correctly — but the
strict banner reports only that the run is FATAL. **It does not mention that a manifest was moved**
**aside.** Round 4's whole banner change was to stop predicting and start reporting; the strict arm was
not brought along.

**No cell pins it**, which is why it survived a round whose entire point was pinning call sites.

**Fix-shape:** say what was done to the manifest in the strict arm too, and add the cell.

## Grouped, and the reasoning so it can be overturned

The coordinator proposed F-1 + F-3 together and **it holds**: both are the behaviour of the same new
call site in the same catch block, and whoever fixes one is already in that code. F-1 additionally
touches `manifest.ts` for the TOCTOU, which is the only reason it is not a single-file change.

**F-2 is filed SEPARATELY** — different file, different fix (the test suite's own hygiene).

## SEARCHED BEFORE FILING

SYMBOL `runPreSuite`, `quarantineManifest`, `existsSync`, `renameSync`, `SYSTEMTEST_REQUIRE_PROVISIONED` ·
PATH `systemTest/fixtures/pre-suite.ts`, `systemTest/fixtures/manifest.ts` · STRING `Never throws`.
Open hits: **KS-969** (parent) and **KS-973** (its round-1 residue). Neither carries these — KS-973's
items are the pre-suite step's *reporting* and the test suite's *side effects*, not this call site's
exception behaviour. Control: a `KS-970` search is non-zero, so the search discriminates.

## PROVENANCE

QA tier-2 gate on **#892 round 4** @ `1e31c80b9`, verdict 2026-09-07T11:34:44Z, findings **F-1**
**(MAJOR)** and **F-3 (MINOR)**. Both introduced by my round-4 commit. **Branch scoping re-measured**
**with** `git ls-tree` **before filing.**

title: The KS-597 integration suite claims two RLS-permissive paths and exercises one — platform_bypass never reaches its own mechanism
description:
## BLUF

**The KS-597 integration suite's header claims it isolates TWO RLS-permissive paths. It exercises ONE.** The `platform_bypass` cell never reaches the mechanism it is named for.

**The property under test still holds** — the gate measured it separately on the real path — so this is a **coverage-claim** defect, not a behaviour one. The suite is not wrong about the product; it is wrong about itself.

## The mechanism, verified on merged develop (`2ff0eb850`)

The header (`ks597-issuer-organization-id.integration.test.ts:25-28`) states:

> *"both cells here isolate the two paths where RLS does NOT exclude the row: P1* `app.tenant_scope_bypass = 'platform_admin'` *(the documented admin path), P2 a BYPASSRLS role (the documented rollback connection)."*

But `writerOn()` (`:138-147`) opens **the same connection for both**, and its own comment says why:

```
// 'bypassrls' needs no GUC: TEST_DATABASE_URL's role is the BYPASSRLS one.
```

**The role already bypasses RLS in both branches.** The `platform_bypass` branch merely sets a GUC on top of a connection that was never subject to the policy — so the GUC is **inert**, and P1 (a non-bypassing role relying on the admin GUC) is never exercised at all.

**Corroborating evidence produced by accident:** during KS-597's round-2 tamper (deleting the tenancy predicate from both `organizations` subqueries), the `platform_bypass` and `bypassrls` cells reddened **identically**. Two genuinely distinct mechanisms would not have to.

## Why it matters

P1 is the path a **platform admin** actually uses. It is the arm where the tenancy predicate is doing the work alone against a role that RLS *would* otherwise constrain — which is precisely the property the suite exists to prove. Today that arm has no coverage while the header says it does, and a reader auditing this file would reasonably stop looking.

## Fix-shape — a decision, not just an edit

Either:

1. **Make P1 real** — connect as a role that does **not** carry BYPASSRLS (e.g. `secuura_app`), set `app.tenant_scope_bypass = 'platform_admin'`, and assert the same property. This needs a second connection string in the harness, and the disposable-Postgres provisioning already creates `secuura_app` (`rolsuper=false, rolbypassrls=false`), so the role exists; or
2. **Correct the claim** — state that the suite covers the BYPASSRLS path only, and record P1 as uncovered.

**(1) is the better outcome and (2) is honest.** What is not acceptable is the current state, where the file asserts coverage it does not have.

## Filed separately from F-A — and why

The coordinator proposed grouping this with F-A conditional on their being one edit. **They are not:** F-A is a two-line comment sweep with no decision; this carries the choice above and possibly a new connection role. **Different fixes, different workloads.** Collapse them if you disagree.

Only **KS-597** returns an open hit. Related but not duplicate: the RLS/tenancy tickets on this board concern product behaviour, not this suite's self-description. title: Rate-limit refusals name the wrong field: 400 says "Key required" when the key was fine, and 403 says "Caller has no tenant" when the caller has one
description:
## BLUF

**Every new refusal path returns a message that names the wrong thing.** A 400 says the key is missing when the key was fine; a 403 says the caller has no tenant when the caller has a perfectly good one. Charter §4d: a 4xx must not be scored as a healthy rejection without knowing *why* it was returned — and these messages actively mislead about the why.

Recoverable rather than silent: `details` carries the truth on the 400.

## ITEM 1 — `/reset` answers 400 "Key required" for failures that have nothing to do with the key

`index.ts:1358` — the top-level message is a constant:

```
{"key":"login","tenantId":"   "}      -> 400 "Key required"  details:[{path:["tenantId"],message:"must not be blank"}]
{"key":"login","tenantId":"\ud800"}   -> 400 "Key required"  details:[{path:["tenantId"],message:"must not contain an unpaired surrogate"}]
{"key":"login","tenantId":257 c.p.}   -> 400 "Key required"  details:[{path:["tenantId"],message:"must not exceed 256 characters"}]
```

The key was supplied and was fine in all three. **KS-970 item 6 has just PUBLISHED "Refused with** `400` **if present but blank"** — so the contract now promises a refusal whose top-level message names a different field.

**Fix-shape:** derive the message from the first failing path, or make it generic ("Invalid request body").

## ITEM 2 — the 403 "Caller has no tenant" now fires when the caller HAS a tenant

`index.ts:1267` (`/check`) and `index.ts:1377` (`/reset`). After KS-970 item 2 this fires when the caller has a good tenant and the *user* claim or the *body* is unusable:

```
claims {tenantId:'…a', userId:123}  -> 403 "Caller has no tenant"   <- false: the caller has tenant …a
```

**Fix-shape:** split it, so "no claim to scope by" and "present but unusable" say different things.

## ⚠ AN IMPLEMENTATION HAZARD I MEASURED, WHICH THE FINDING DOES NOT MENTION

`"Caller has no tenant"` appears at **FOUR** sites, not two: `index.ts:665`, `:716`, `:1267`, `:1377`. **A fix that greps for the string will touch all four and two of them are correct.**

Verified at `0281b0faa`:

* `:665` **and** `:716` **are NOT instances.** Both guard `if (!isPlatformRole(...) && !callerTenantId)` — they test the tenant claim *directly*, so the message is literally true there.
* `:1267` **and** `:1377` **ARE the instances.** Both sit behind `if (scope === null)`, and `scope` is null for **three** different reasons — no tenant claim, a MALFORMED tenant, or a MALFORMED user/`sub`. The message asserts only the first.

So the finding named the right two sites. **The other two share the string and not the defect**, and that distinction is the thing to carry into the fix.

## REGRESSION TEST

**Assert the message TEXT, not just the status.** Every cell here passes today on status alone, which is why the defect shipped: a 400 is a 400 and a 403 is a 403 whatever they say. Include a cell for `:665` or `:716` asserting the message stays "Caller has no tenant" there, so a fix does not over-reach into the two correct sites.

## RELATED, NOT MERGED IN

Item 2's root cause is the same tri-state as **KS-975**. Kept separate because the fix lives in the error-construction path rather than in the tri-state itself — but whoever takes one should read the other.

## SEARCHED BEFORE FILING

STRING `Caller has no tenant`, `Key required` · SYMBOL `resetRateLimitSchema`, `checkRateLimitSchema`, `explicitScope`, `principalScope` · PATH `services/security/src/index.ts`. Linear's search is fuzzy on multi-word phrases and returned ~20 loosely-related hits for each string; **none on inspection concerns these routes' message construction.** The precise symbol searches return only **KS-970** (parent) and **KS-645** (a closed Duplicate about `/reset`'s role check, a different property). Control: a `KS-970` search is non-zero, so the search discriminates.

## PROVENANCE

QA tier-1 gate on **#894 over #893**, verdict 2026-09-07T09:45:45Z, quoted verbatim by the coordinator. **All four call sites re-verified against** `0281b0faa` **before filing** — which is how the two non-instances were found.

title: rateLimitScope tri-state: a MALFORMED `sub` silently became a 403 on the ungated /check, and `null` still slips through explicitScope's second line
description:
## BLUF

**Two arms of the ABSENT-vs-MALFORMED tri-state in** `rateLimitScope.ts` **that nothing pins.** Item 1 is a **behaviour change that already shipped on a live, ungated route** and is currently reversible without a single test going red. Item 2 is a hole in a backstop, not reachable at the wire today.

**Correcting the framing I was handed:** the grouping described both as *"unpinned arms rather than live defects"*. That is right for item 2 and **understates item 1** — item 1 changed a live response from **200 to 403** on `/api/rate-limit/check`, which has **no role gate**. Unpinned, yes; but not merely theoretical.

## ITEM 1 (MINOR by severity, but a live behaviour change — gate F-2) — a MALFORMED `sub` became a refusal, undisclosed and unpinned

**Location:** `rateLimitScope.ts:118` — `const user_ = rawUser === ABSENT ? claim(user?.sub) : rawUser;`

Gate measurement, same input at both SHAs:

| claims | #893 `ab1053141` | #894 `e02d0fecc` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `{tenantId:'…a', sub:123}` | `t:…\|u:` (tenant bucket, **200**) | `null` **-> 403** |
| `{tenantId:'…a', sub:'  '}` | `t:…\|u:` (**200**) | `null` **-> 403** |

`sub` inherits the refusal because `claim(user?.sub)` can itself return `MALFORMED`, and `:121` refuses on `MALFORMED`.

**Verified in code at** `0281b0faa`**:** the comment at `:114-116` does address `sub` — but only to say a MALFORMED `userId` must not route around via `sub`. It never states that a MALFORMED `sub` is itself a refusal. So the gate's reading is right: the documented tri-state covers `userId`, and the new cells cover `sub` only as a good string.

**It is unpinned, proved by the gate:** restoring #893's behaviour (map a MALFORMED `sub` back to `ABSENT`) leaves **all 179 cells green**. A future change can silently revert it. **A check that cannot fail wearing a feature's clothes.**

**Fix-shape:** decide it deliberately, say so in the comment, and pin it — one cell each way (`sub: 123` refuses; `sub: 'u1'` scopes), so the arm has a failure mode.

## ITEM 2 (MINOR, gate F-4) — `explicitScope`'s second line still has item 1's exact hole for `null`

**Location:** `rateLimitScope.ts:86` — `if (value === undefined || value === null) return ABSENT;`

The design is stated at `:228-231`: *"The schema refuses these first; this is the second line, for any caller that bypasses it."* Across 14 shapes the second line refuses 12 (`'   '`, `'\t\n'`, `''`, NBSP, BOM, U+3000, `123`, `{}`, `[]`, `false`, `NaN`, `0`) and **treats JSON** `null` **as ABSENT**, which falls through to `principalScope(caller)` — reproducing item 1's exact shape: a **present** field silently retargeting the caller's own bucket.

**Honestly bounded, and this is the half not to lose: NOT reachable at the wire today.** `z.string()....optional()` rejects `null` — the gate drove it: `{"key":"login","tenantId":null}` -> `400 invalid_type, expected string, received null`, caller's bucket untouched. Independently confirmed here before filing: `scopeField()` is a non-nullable `z.string()`, and the only product caller of `explicitScope` (`index.ts:1373`) passes already-validated `parsedBody.data`.

So this is **a hole in the backstop, not a live defect**. It matters only because the backstop exists precisely for the case where the schema is bypassed — and `null` is exactly what a client library serialising an unset field would send.

**Fix-shape:** `explicitScope` should treat `null` in a **body** as MALFORMED while `principalScope` keeps treating a `null` **claim** as ABSENT — different questions about different inputs. **Regression test:** extend the second-line cell with `explicitScope({tenantId: null}, caller)` -> `null`, plus a CONTROL that `explicitScope({}, caller)` still returns the caller's own scope.

## SEARCHED BEFORE FILING

SYMBOL `rateLimitScope`, `explicitScope`, `principalScope`, `claim(`, `MALFORMED`, `ABSENT`, `scopeField` · PATH `services/security/src/rateLimitScope.ts`. Only **KS-970** (this work's parent) returns an open hit; `scopeField` returns 0. Control: a `KS-970` search is non-zero, so the search discriminates.

## PROVENANCE

QA tier-1 gate on **#894 over #893**, verdict 2026-09-07T09:45:45Z, quoted verbatim by the coordinator. **Every code claim re-verified against** `0281b0faa` **before filing.**

title: Published bound vs runtime bound on rate-limit scope: /check enforces code UNITS against a published code-POINT maxLength, and scopeField bounds the untrimmed string
description:
## BLUF

**Two places where the PUBLISHED bound does not match the bound the runtime enforces.** F-1 is MAJOR and leads: `/api/rate-limit/check` publishes `maxLength: 256` and enforces **UTF-16 code units**, on the route with **no role gate** — so the published contract is wrong for every unauthenticated integrator on the one endpoint anybody can reach.

**Correcting the grouping rationale I was handed:** these are the same **CLASS**, not the same fix. They sit in different schemas in different files and the edits differ — F-1 changes the counting UNIT, F-5 changes WHAT is counted. They are one ticket because they are one logical path (published contract vs runtime bound), not because one change closes both.

## ITEM 1 (MAJOR, gate F-1) — `/check` publishes code points and enforces code units

Measured at `0281b0faa`:

```
RATE_LIMIT_KEY_MAX = 256                                rateLimitScope.ts:48
/reset  key: boundedByCodePoints(z.string().min(1))     requestSchemas.ts:81
        -> [...value].length <= 256   = CODE POINTS
/check  key: z.string().min(1).max(RATE_LIMIT_KEY_MAX)  index.ts:513
        -> zod .max() on a string     = UTF-16 CODE UNITS
```

The published contract states the bound **counts code points** in as many words (`security.openapi.ts:560`, and again at `:570` and `:581`).

So a key of **256 astral characters is 256 code points and 512 code units**: inside the published limit, refused by `/check`.

**Not introduced by #894.** `/check` was always `.max()`; KS-970 item 4 aligned `/reset` and thereby revealed the asymmetry. It was deliberately NOT folded into #894, because that would have moved a gated head and turned a clean GO into a re-gate.

**Fix-shape:** `boundedByCodePoints` on `/check`'s `key`, matching `/reset`.

## ITEM 2 (POLISH, gate F-5) — the published bound measures a string the runtime does not use

`scopeField()` validates the **raw** string; `claim()` scopes by the **trimmed** one. Verified in code at `0281b0faa`: `rateLimitScope.ts:88` trims, while `requestSchemas.ts:68-70` applies `[...value].length <= RATE_LIMIT_KEY_MAX` to the raw value (only the blank-check at `:67` trims).

Gate measurement:

```
tenantId = " " + "a"x256   raw 257 c.p. / trimmed 256 c.p.  ->  400 "must not exceed 256 characters"
tenantId =       "a"x256                                     ->  accepted
...and both would target the SAME bucket (explicitScope equal -> true)
```

So a caller is refused for exceeding a bound on a value that, after the runtime's own normalisation, is inside it.

**The house standard already prescribes the idiom that avoids this** — `2_Project_Files/CLAUDE.md:173-181` (KS-202): `.trim()` **before** `.min()`/`.max()`. It also notes `z.string().trim().min(1)` already rejects `'   '`, i.e. the platform's existing idiom would have closed KS-970 item 1 without a bespoke refine and kept the bound on the value actually used.

**Also:** item 6's published descriptions state the blank and surrogate refusals but never say values are trimmed, so `" acme "` is published as a distinct valid value that silently targets `acme`.

**Fix-shape:** `z.string().trim()` at the head of `scopeField()`, and one clause in the published description saying leading/trailing whitespace is stripped.

## SEARCHED BEFORE FILING

SYMBOL `checkRateLimitSchema`, `scopeField`, `boundedByCodePoints`, `RATE_LIMIT_KEY_MAX`, `rateLimitScope`, `explicitScope`, `principalScope` · STRING `maxLength`, `code points` · PATH `services/security/src/index.ts`, `requestSchemas.ts`, `rateLimitScope.ts`.

`scopeField` and `boundedByCodePoints` return **0** hits. `rateLimitScope`/`explicitScope`/`principalScope`/`maxLength` return **KS-970 only** (this work's parent). `checkRateLimitSchema` **returns KS-645 — checked, and it is NOT this**: KS-645 is a closed **Duplicate** about `/api/rate-limit/reset`'s role check, a different property of a different route. Control: a `KS-970` search returns a non-zero hit, so the search discriminates.

## PROVENANCE

QA tier-1 gate on **#894 over #893**, verdict 2026-09-07T09:45:45Z. Findings quoted verbatim by the coordinator; **every code claim above re-verified against** `0281b0faa` **before filing**, not taken on relay.

`playwright/config/actorManifest.ts`, `performance/runner/actor_manifest.ts` and
`schemathesis/tests/actor_manifest.py` all exist and are imported by live code. **akto has no**
**manifest consumer at all** — no `actorManifest`, no `generated/actors`. Its Secuura credentials come
from `config/secrets.yml` (`.env.example:40`).

So every akto run performs a real **account-creating** provisioning pass whose output akto never
reads, then prints `PROVISIONED — 5 generated actor(s)`. Under this PR's own vocabulary
(`pre-suite.ts:17`, *"the manifest is written; suites read generated actors"*) **that banner is false**
**for akto** — on the suite whose whole job is BOLA/BFLA role enforcement, a reader is told the wrong
identity was under test.

May be deliberate staging for KS-969 item 4. **Decide: either give akto a manifest consumer, or do**
**not hook it and say why.** A green banner asserting something untrue today is the worse of the two.

## ITEM 2 (MAJOR, was F5) — the schemathesis DEGRADED banner never reaches the run record

`_run_pre_suite` uses `subprocess.run` with inherited fds while `Logger` writes the archived log
itself. Measured with `--enable-logger-file`: **pre-suite lines in the archived log = 0.**
On the fatal path the log at least records `Pre-suite provisioning step failed`; on the **DEGRADED**
path `pre_rc == 0`, so nothing is logged and **the archived artefact contains no record that the scan**
**ran on seeded accounts** — the entire point of the banner. The silent fallback, relocated into the
artefact layer.
**Fix-shape:** capture the child's output and re-emit through `Logger`, or log the outcome
unconditionally rather than only on non-zero.

## ITEM 3 (MINOR, was F6) — `pre_suite.test.sh` mutates a shared stack and clobbers the real manifest

Run against any stack answering on `localhost:6882`, the suite **creates five real accounts** with
`FIXTURE_SEED="presuite-test-$$"` — **a fresh seed every run**, so they accumulate and are never
cleaned up — and **overwrites** `systemTest/fixtures/generated/actors.json`, leaving every consumer
pointed at throwaway identities until someone re-provisions.
**This is confirmed by consequence:** the author exhausted the local register limiter (100/hour)
during development, which is exactly this defect compounding. Round 2 partly mitigates it (a role
collapse no longer publishes the manifest), **but the account creation is unchanged.**
**Fix-shape:** a stable seed, and gate the live arm behind an explicit opt-in rather than "a stack
answered".

## ITEM 4 (MINOR, was F7) — the `ALLOW_REMOTE_PROVISION` control is inert and its comment is wrong

`pre_suite.test.sh` comments a cell *"the SAME remote target with the documented override must NOT*
*refuse"* — but it targets `http://127.0.0.1:1`, a **local** host, so it passes through the
`LOCAL_HOSTS` branch and the override is never exercised. Proved by tamper: making the override
branch permanently unreachable still left the suite fully green. **The documented escape hatch is**
**untested in both directions.** The cell still does the job of proving the step does not refuse
everything — so this is a weakened control plus a misleading comment, not an absent one.

## ITEM 5 (MINOR, was F8) — the DEGRADED stream routing is documented and pinned by nothing

`pre-suite.ts` routes DEGRADED to stderr with a comment explaining why. Collapsing both branches to
`console.log` left the suite green, because the harness merges the streams with `2>&1`. **A**
**documented invariant with no test is a comment.**

## ITEM 6 (MINOR, was F9) — unredacted server-error passthrough, PREMISE UNVERIFIED

`provision.ts:282` interpolates the server's `error.message` verbatim into the Error, and
`pre-suite.ts` interpolates that into the DEGRADED banner. Against a stub that echoes the request
body, **the generated password appeared in the banner in cleartext.**
**The gate proved the pipe is unredacted; it did NOT prove the real endpoint echoes payloads** — it
never reached a real stack. **Recorded with the premise unverified rather than smoothed over.** Value
at risk is low (generated `.invalid` local accounts); fix-shape is trivial — redact `password` keys
before interpolation.

## PROVENANCE

QA tier-2 gate on **#892 @** `f54b2dce1`, reported 2026-09-07. F1/F2/F3 closed in round 2 at
`42e778203`. Wednesday ruled **no round 3**, so these ship as their own work.

title: start-secuura.sh banner prints admin@secuura.com / admin123, which has returned 401 since PR #888
description:
## BLUF

`Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` ends every successful start with a **Credentials** block that still prints `Admin: admin@secuura.com / admin123`. Since PR #888 ([KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a) items 1+2) retired the published SYSTEM_ADMIN default, that login **returns 401** — measured on a fresh slot-2 stack on 2026-09-07. The banner now hands every operator a credential that does not work, on the one screen they are guaranteed to read.

Found during the [KS-682](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-682/playwright-slot-isolation-port-the-proven-platform-s-mechanism-no-run) four-slot isolation sweep, not by reading the script.

## Measured

```
POST /api/auth/login  {"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}
  -> 401 {"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"Invalid email or password"}
```

`demo@secuura.io / demo123` on the same banner line still authenticates (200), so the issuer half is correct and only the admin half is stale.

## Why it is its own ticket rather than a [KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a) sub-item

[KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a)'s ruled order item 3 — *"4 startup/scripts + 3 harnesses — env var, no fallback"* — covers scripts that **read** the fallback. This is the script **printing** it: a documentary line, not an executable read, so it is not caught by that sweep's definition of "site" and would survive item 3 landing. Related to [KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a) so it is sequenced beside it; raised separately so it is not lost inside a routing change.

## Suggested fix

Either drop the admin line from the banner, or print the mechanism instead of a value — e.g. *"Admin: provisioned per run, see* `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts`*"* — since [KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a)'s answer was that no shared admin credential should exist to print.

## Context

* The banner also prints `Project: <compose default>` for slot 1 while the container labels read the worktree-derived project name (`ks-682` in this sweep). Minor; noted while here, not the subject of this ticket.
* Raised from the [KS-682](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-682/playwright-slot-isolation-port-the-proven-platform-s-mechanism-no-run) sweep; platform-k base code, so filed to Kamil per the review-authority rule.

title: systemTest actor/credential path: provisioning is never invoked, so the generated-actor path never resolves — and exactly one site (the SYSTEM_ADMIN persona) can never use it
description:
**KS-966 item 4 was stood down on measurement.** It was scoped as *"route the 12 systemTest sites through the existing generated-actor path"*. **That path never runs**, and for one site it could not work even if it did. This is the one logical path — the systemTest actor/credential story — with its items inside it, per Kam's 2026-09-07 13:23 rule.

## Searched before filing (958 issues, including archived)

| searched | hits |
| -- | -- |
| SYMBOL `getGeneratedActor` | KS-966 only (this ticket's parent) |
| SYMBOL `ADMIN_ACTOR_KEY` | KS-966 only |
| SYMBOL `provision-actors` | KS-966 only |
| PATH `systemTest/fixtures/generated` | **none** |
| SYMBOL `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | KS-967 only (as a guarded key name, different subject) |
| STRING `actor manifest` / `actors.json` | **none** |

**No existing ticket covers this.** Four sessions worked this repo today, so the check was worth making.

---

## ITEM 1 — Wire actor provisioning into a pre-suite step

`getGeneratedActor()` reads `systemTest/fixtures/generated/actors.json` (`playwright/config/actorManifest.ts:45`) and returns `undefined` when absent. Measured on `origin/develop`:

* **0** files tracked under `systemTest/fixtures/generated`; the manifest is **absent** on a fresh tree.
* Written **only** by `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts`.
* **Nothing automated invokes it**: no npm script · no `.github` workflow · no shell runner · **not** `playwright/global-setup.ts` (imports only `getApiBaseUrl`) · **not** `auth/auth.setup.ts` (imports `getTestAdminEmail`/`getTestAdminPassword` and logs in with them). Its only references are its own docstring showing manual invocation.
* **CONTROL:** the same `git grep` over the same paths finds `"test:unit"` in `playwright/package.json`. The instrument fires, so the zeros are real zeros.

**So the fallbacks are the live path, not redundancy.** This item is a pre-suite hook (a Playwright setup-project dependency, or the slot runner) **with its own test** — not a tail-end edit.

## ITEM 2 — The SYSTEM_ADMIN split. **M = 1**, and here it is

Of the 12 occurrences, **8 are documentary** (comments, docstrings, `@example` blocks) and belong to KS-965, not here. **Four are executable credential sources**, and three of them are satisfied by `orgAdmin`:

| site | drives | verdict |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `schemathesis/tests/conftest.py:83` | `resolve_credentials("orgAdmin", …)` | **already keyed to** `orgAdmin`, with env override + fallback |
| `schemathesis/scripts/setup_api_key.py:53` | `POST /api/admin/api-keys`, gated `requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN','ORG_ADMIN')` | **ORG_ADMIN is admitted** by the route |
| `schemathesis/tests/test_authentication.py:26` | `POST /auth/login` only (success / invalid / missing-field) | **login requires no role at all** |
| `schemathesis/config/fixtures.py:82` | `Persona(key="super_admin", role="SYSTEM_ADMIN", …)` — *"Cross-tenant reads via X-Tenant-Override"* | **🔴 genuinely requires SYSTEM_ADMIN** |

**So exactly ONE site cannot be served by the generated-actor path** — and it cannot be served by design, not by omission. The manifest module says so in its own words:

> *"*`orgAdmin` *stands in for* `admin`*: SYSTEM_ADMIN is deliberately not grantable through the API, so it can never be generated."*

**That single site is the whole decision.** Either its cross-tenant persona keeps a seeded SYSTEM_ADMIN credential supplied by environment, or the suite loses cross-tenant coverage. **Nothing else in the 12 needs a ruling.**

## ITEM 3 — `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is documented, but documented WRONG

The concern raised was that it might be undocumented. **It is named** — `playwright/README.md:27` and `:152`, `playwright/docs/setup_guide.md:89` and `:238`. **The defect is sharper than absence:**

* `playwright/.env.example:27` has it **commented out**, so `cp .env.example .env` supplies nothing.
* `playwright/docs/setup_guide.md:89` documents its **default as the retired literal** — a value that no longer works, because #888 removed the seeder's published default *and* the `getTestAdminPassword()` fallback.

**So a runner who follows the documentation sets a password that cannot authenticate**, and with GitHub Actions retired (20 of 20 runs `startup_failure`, measured 2026-09-07) nothing fails loudly to tell them. **This is an operational precondition #888 introduced without updating its documentation.** The security change was right; this is its unpaid half.

Both of those lines also carry the retired literal and are in KS-965's documentary census — **fix them here, since here is where their wrongness is load-bearing.**

## ITEM 4 — Only then, the 12 sites

Blocked on items 1–3. Doing it first inverts the F3 error corrected on KS-968 today: removing the harmless thing and leaving the one that detonates.

---

*Filed by s146 from the KS-966 item-4 measurement. Items 3 and 4 of KS-966 are closed by comment against this ticket. The 12/8/4/1 counts are mine and were re-derived after I found my first pass had omitted* `.py` *from its extension list — which had hidden six of the eight executable files.*

title: MAJOR: when both platform-admin rows exist the id-row rewrite throws 23505, the seed loop swallows it, and the KS-966 F3 email arm never runs — with a green cell standing over the hole
description:
**MAJOR. When both rows exist, the platform-admin remediation throws 23505, the loop swallows it, and the email-keyed arm — the whole KS-966 F3 fix — NEVER RUNS. A green cell stands over the hole.**

**"Both rows present" is not an exotic state. It is the state Kam's own row is in**: `…0020` holding one address, and a distinct row holding `admin@secuura.com`.

Found by the #888 round-2 tier-1 gate. **Pre-existing — reproduced identically against round 1's** `userRepo.ts`**, so it is not introduced by round 2 and is equally open on** `develop` **today** (merged at `9e9a88709`).

### The mechanism — and my published one was WRONG

I argued in #888 and on KS-966 that the collision came from **rewriting the address onto the row found BY that address**. That is wrong, and it matters: **writing the same address back onto the row that already holds it cannot collide with itself.**

The collision is on the **other** side:

1. `if (byId)` (`userRepo.ts:1363`) rewrites the `…0020` row's `email_lookup_hash` to the hash of `admin@secuura.com`.
2. If a **distinct** row already holds that hash, that write violates `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq` → **23505**.
3. The seed loop's `catch` (`userRepo.ts:~1506`) turns it into `logger.error('Failed to seed demo user', …)` and `continue`s — **no rethrow**.
4. `if (emailRowIsDistinct)` sits at `:1388`, *after* the throwing statement. **It never executes.**

**So I located the hazard on the wrong row, then declined a rewrite that was harmless and left standing the rewrite that actually detonates.** The gate accepted my *conclusion* (the email row should get credential-neutralisation only) and rejected my *reasoning* — and the wrong reasoning is why the hole is still open.

**The arm itself is correct and merely unreachable:** the gate neutered only the id-row guard and the email arm fired perfectly — suspended, sentinel hash, verify FALSE.

**Verified independently on** `origin/develop` **before filing:** `byId` at `:1363` precedes `emailRowIsDistinct` at `:1388`; the id-row UPDATE writes `email_lookup_hash = $3`; the loop catch logs and continues without rethrowing. And `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq` **exists and is UNIQUE on the deployed demo database** (measured read-only 2026-09-07, with controls: `users` 33 columns, `uuid_generate_v4` present).

---

## ITEM 1 — the misleading green cell. Fix this first.

`services/auth/src/__tests__/ks952…`/`ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts`:

```
it('remediates BOTH when both exist, and the id row still gets the full identity rewrite')
```

**It passes, and it is asserting that a live hole is closed, on a credential surface.** It passes because the vitest `db` double answers `{rows: []}` to every UPDATE and **cannot enforce a unique index** — so the 23505 never happens in the test and the swallow never happens either.

The tester's words: *"the one thing here I would fix before the deploy rather than after."* It could not go into #888 because what merges must be what was gated, so it is the first item here.

**A mocked** `query` **cannot express this defect at all.** The regression test must drive the same both-exist scenario against a **real Postgres carrying** `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq`. That is the important half of this ticket — more than the fix.

## ITEM 2 — the fix, three shapes offered by the gate

* **Order the two remediations email-row-first**, so the credential neutralisation lands before the statement that can throw; **or**
* make the id-row rewrite **conditional on** `!emailRowIsDistinct`; **or**
* **wrap both in one transaction**, so the credential neutralisation is not lost to the identity rewrite's failure.

Whichever is chosen, **the swallowing catch is part of the defect**: a remediation whose failure is indistinguishable from success at `logger.error` level is the same class as KS-962, where the seed failure logs at `debug` and is invisible.

## ITEM 3 — do NOT probe the demo

**Likelihood on the demo is UNKNOWN.** The gate had no authorisation to contact the box and did not. **That probe is Kam's to authorise and he has not.** Do not go and look.

---

**Related:** KS-966 (#888, where the F3 arm shipped — my incorrect mechanism is corrected in a comment there) · KS-949 (the identity half) · KS-962 (the sibling swallow, at `debug`) · KS-963 (the PII cutoff).

*Filed by s146 after the #888 merge, from the round-2 gate verdict. The mechanism above is the gate's; the develop-side verification and the deployed-index measurement are mine.*

title: Neither credential guard can see a value in a .env.example — one scans the wrong roots and extensions, the other excludes the file and self-tests the exclusion
description:
**Two credential guards run on every push and NEITHER could see the one that mattered.** KS-966 F1 was a live exposure — `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` shipped a value for `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, and `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:381` plus `services/api-gateway/src/docs/developer-portal.html:382` both instruct `cp .env.example .env`, so the documented setup path seeded the platform SYSTEM_ADMIN **ACTIVE and loginable** on a credential published in this repository. It sat there through a full round-1 gate.

**This is the guards' blind AXIS, not a bug in either implementation, and it was not introduced by #888.** Both behave exactly as written. That is the problem.

### Measured, from the scripts themselves

**1.** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-default-passwords.sh:28-32` — cannot reach the file on two independent axes:

```
grep -rEn --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.js' \
     --exclude-dir=__tests__ --exclude-dir=tests --exclude-dir=scripts \
     ... services/ packages/
```

* **Extension:** `.ts` / `.tsx` / `.js` only. A `.env.example` is not scannable by construction.
* **Root:** `services/` and `packages/` only. `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` is above both.

Either one alone is sufficient to miss it. Widening one and not the other changes nothing.

**2.** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/no-tracked-credentials.sh:37-38` — excludes it *deliberately*:

```
EXCLUDE_RE='\.(example|sample|template)$'
```

with the comment at `:34-36` explaining that 25 `.env.example` files are tracked on purpose and are the documented way to describe required config. **And its own self-test at** `:51-53` **asserts the exclusion holds**, naming `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` as a probe that MUST be excluded:

```
for probe in "Blockchain/Dev/.env.example" "svc/config.example"; do
  echo "$probe" | grep -Eq "$EXCLUDE_RE" || { echo "SELF-TEST FAIL: did not exclude $probe"; ok=1; }
done
```

So the guard is not merely blind here — **it is tested to be blind here.** Any fix has to change that self-test too, consciously, or it will be reverted by the next person who reads it as a regression.

### Why the exclusion is right and still leaves a hole

The exclusion exists for a good reason: an example file must be allowed to *name* `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, or it cannot document the variable at all. **The distinction the guards do not draw is between naming a key and assigning it a value.** `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD=` is documentation. `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD=<something>` is a credential. A file-level exclusion cannot tell those apart; a line-level rule can.

### Shape when picked up

A check over tracked `*.env.example` files that fails on **a non-empty assignment to a credential-shaped key**, rather than on the file's existence. Keys named, not pattern-guessed — the pattern-guessing is what produces the false positives the current exclusion was written to avoid.

### Interim cover — real but partial, and it must not be mistaken for this ticket being done

#888 round 2 adds a cell (`services/auth/src/__tests__/ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts`, the `KS-966 F1` block) that walks the tree for `*.env.example` and fails on a non-empty `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` / `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD`. It is red-proved (restoring a value gives 2 red of 23 executing).

**It covers two key names in one service's test suite.** It is not a push-time gate, it does not run when only non-auth code changes, and it says nothing about any other credential-shaped key. The gap this ticket names is the guards' coverage axis, and that is still open.

title: Retire the published SYSTEM_ADMIN credential (Kam: rotate-properly) — a deletion, not a rotation: no new shared secret is needed
description:
**Kam ruled** `rotate-properly` **(2026-09-07 11:43:32).** This is the ticket for that work; it was executed before it was filed, which is the cause of a naming error recorded at the bottom.

## What the measurement changed about the job

The card described a 183-occurrence credential spread across 128 files. Measured:

|  | count | files |
| -- | -- | -- |
| total | 183 | 128 |
| **executable** (something reads it) | **93** | 72 |
| **documentary** (a human reads it) | **87** | 55 |

And the executable 93 splits again — **8** env-var-with-a-published-fallback, **12** comment lines inside executable files, **73** hardcoded. Of those 73, **43 are in spec files nothing runs** (KS-964).

**So the real surface was ~32 sites, not 183.**

## The answer that collapsed it into a deletion

**No new shared credential is needed.** `systemTest/playwright/config/environment.ts` already reads `getGeneratedActor(ADMIN_ACTOR_KEY)?.password`, and `provision-actors.ts` provisions actors per run. The published default is the fallback that made that machinery moot. So: nothing to mint, nothing to distribute, and no second rotation waiting in a year.

## Ruled order (Wednesday, 2026-09-07)

1. ✅ **The 8 fallbacks** — delete the default, keep the var, fail closed. **DONE, PR #888.**
2. ✅ **The 5 CI literals** — replaced with a secrets reference. **DONE, PR #888.**
3. ⬜ **4 startup/scripts + 3 harnesses** — env var, no fallback. Same shape as (1). **NOT STARTED.**
4. ⬜ **12 systemTest sites** — route through the generated-actor path. **NOT STARTED.** Ordered last because it is a *routing* change rather than a deletion and carries the only real regression risk in the set. **Prove the actor path resolves BEFORE removing the fallback**, not after.
5. → dead specs: **KS-964**.  6. → documentary sites: **KS-965**.

## ⚠ Behaviour change already shipped in PR #888

With `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` unset, the platform SYSTEM_ADMIN is **not seeded** — unusable hash, suspended status, as the `…060` identity already is. Any environment relying on the default can no longer authenticate as that account. Deliberate.

## 🔴 A naming error to be aware of when reading the history

**PR #888, its branch** `feature/ks-964-retire-published-admin-default`**, and its commit messages all say "KS-964" and mean THIS ticket.** The identifier was guessed from the sequence before the ticket was filed, and the number went to the dead-specs ticket instead. The code and evidence are unaffected; only the label is wrong. Recorded here rather than rewritten, because rewriting pushed history is worse than a documented mislabel.

**Measured 2026-09-07.**

title: 87 documentary sites still publish the retired admin credential — wrong rather than dangerous, clean up after KS-964's code items
description:
**BLUF** — after KS-964 retires the published SYSTEM_ADMIN default, **87 documentary occurrences across 55 files still name it**. They are wrong rather than dangerous, and this is the cleanup pass for them.

## Why this is separate, and lower priority

**Once the credential no longer works, a document naming it is misleading, not exploitable.** The security value was in KS-964 item 1 (the seeder stops accepting a default) and item 2 (the CI literals). This pass is about not leaving 55 files telling a reader to log in with something that will fail.

Blocking the rotation on it would have delayed the part that mattered.

## Scope

**87 occurrences / 55 files**, classified as documentary by extension (`.md`, `.mdc`, `.txt`) — the remainder of the 183 total measured for KS-964, after 93 executable and 3 unclassified.

Known clusters include `CLI-AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS.md` (a login recipe reproduced 4 times), `USER_TESTING/Secuura-Platform-Credentials.md`, `USER_TESTING/M365-Integration-Test-Guide.md`, `docs/BROWSER-TESTING-GUIDE.md`, and the `.cursor/` rules files.

## What "fixed" looks like

Not a find-and-replace to a new value — **there is no new shared value**, which is the point of KS-964. Each site should name the **environment variable** instead, the same way KS-949 F2 handled the three files that published a password beside the platform-admin identity: say the credential is not published and name what supplies it.

## Do after, not before

This should land **after** KS-964's code items, so the docs describe the world as it then is rather than a world in transit.

**Measured 2026-09-07 during the KS-964 rotation measurement.**
