title: m365 /api/teams/notify: a serial per-row loop with no LIMIT and no aggregate bound, inside the request handler — N rows x the guard's 10s default
description:
## No aggregate bound over an unbounded row set, in a request handler

`POST /api/teams/notify` loops over every active webhook row **serially**, inside the request handler, with **no** `LIMIT` **on the query** and **no aggregate deadline** over the loop.

The gate confirmed the call site passes **no** `timeoutMs`, so each row rides `safeOutboundRequest`'s 10 s default. Worst case is `rows x 10s` with the HTTP request held open throughout.

KS-914 improved the per-row behaviour — before it, `fetch` was called with no signal at all — but the aggregate was never bounded and still is not.

### Fix shape

A `LIMIT` with paging, or an aggregate deadline over the loop, or move the dispatch off the request path entirely (which is the shape the webhooks dispatcher already uses). **Concurrency is not the fix on its own** — it changes the constant, not the bound.

Red-proof with N rows against a destination that never answers, asserting the handler returns within an aggregate bound rather than N x per-row.

*From the #868 round-1 gate (F4). Filed by s141, 2026-09-06.*

title: KS-921 residues: five Dockerfile shapes the re-link guard cannot read, an nginx final stage it can NEVER pass, and one A_FAIL branch no test can red
description:
## KS-921 gate residues F-3, F-6, F-7 — five legitimate Dockerfile shapes the guard cannot read, one it can never pass, and one branch no test can red

From the #870 gate. Deliberately **not** fixed in that PR: F-1/F-2/F-4/F-5 were, because they are false cleans and false blocks that bite today; these three are shapes with **no live exposure** and one design question that deserves a decision rather than a patch.

**Live exposure today is zero, measured:** all seven frontend Dockerfiles use nginx/alpine final stages, **none** consumes `shared-builder`, and no frontend source imports `@secuura/shared` (0 files). So nothing in the tree hits these paths now — which is exactly why they should be recorded rather than left to be discovered by whoever first writes one.

### F-6 comes first, because it is the one with no answer

**For an nginx final stage the guard offers no route forward.** A static-serving final stage legitimately has no `node_modules` at all, so clause A's `final stage writes node_modules nowhere` fires and there is no way to make the file green except by adding a pointless `node_modules` write purely to satisfy the check.

**A guard with no green path for a legitimate shape is a design question, not a bug.** The options are roughly: exempt a final stage that writes no `node_modules` and consumes no builder tree; require an explicit opt-out marker; or narrow the class further so such files never enter it. **This is the first item on this ticket and it should be decided before anything below it is coded**, because the answer changes what the other shapes need.

### F-3 — five legitimate shapes the parser cannot read

1. **BuildKit heredoc** — `RUN <<EOF … EOF`. The parser joins on trailing `\` and treats each logical line independently, so a re-link inside a heredoc body is invisible.
2. **An nginx final stage with no** `node_modules` — see F-6.
3. **The non-final-stage write.** Clause A is stated over the FINAL stage. A Dockerfile whose runtime stage is not the last `FROM` in the file (a valid multi-target build) is judged against the wrong stage.
4. `npm i` **shorthand.** The install detector matches `npm ci|install`; `npm i` alone is not matched, so a stage installing that way reads as writing no `node_modules`.
5. **The JSON** `COPY` **form** — `COPY ["--from=builder", "/app/node_modules", "./node_modules"]`. Valid Dockerfile, unreadable to a whitespace-token parser.

Plus the two parser edges the gate noted.

### F-7 — and this one is the same family as three tickets already on this board

**The** `A_FAIL` **branch for "final stage writes node_modules nowhere" is pinned by NO test.**

Measured 2026-09-06, by neutering it (`note("A_FAIL", …)` → `note("A_OK", …)`) and re-running:

```
suite with the branch neutered ............ 26 passed, 0 failed
"final stage has NO" ...................... pinned by 4 cells
"runs BEFORE the last instruction" ........ pinned by 1 cell
"runs after a non-root" ................... pinned by 1 cell
"writes node_modules nowhere" ............. pinned by 0 cells
```

The tamper was restored and the file verified byte-identical by sha256.

**A branch no cell can red is a check that cannot fail** — and it is the fourth mechanism of that family on this board tonight, alongside [KS-926](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-926) (a check nothing runs), [KS-927](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-927) (a check running with the half that would notice already dead) and [KS-928](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-928) (a check whose wiring is unasserted). Here the guard runs, the suite runs, the wiring is asserted — **and one branch of it still cannot be shown to work.**

Note the ordering trap for whoever fixes it: this branch is also *unreachable in practice for the current class*, since every one of the 25 files writes `node_modules` in its final stage. Pinning it needs a fixture, and the fixture is the nginx shape from F-6 — **so F-6's decision and F-7's cell are the same piece of work.**

### Fix shape

Decide F-6 first. Then a cell per F-3 shape, each red-proofed by the shape it describes, and the F-7 cell falling out of F-6's chosen semantics. **No shape should be "supported" without a cell that reds without it** — the guard already shipped one branch without that and this ticket is the receipt.

*Filed by s141 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from the #870 gate at Wednesday's direction to ticket rather than widen that PR. The F-7 measurement above is mine; the shapes are the gate's.*

title: The demo-seed gate's predicate is tested but its CALL SITE is not — delete adminConfig.ts:1824 and every test still passes (same class as KS-914 A-2)
description:
## The demo-seed gate's PREDICATE is tested; the fact that the route CONSULTS it is not

Delete `adminConfig.ts:1824` and every existing test still passes.

### Measured 2026-09-06 (s141), from the #867 gate's B-3

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| the route consults the gate | `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:1824` — `if (!isDemoSeedEnabled()) {` |
| the only test file | `src/__tests__/ks487-b3-demo-seed-gate.test.ts` |
| what it imports | `isDemoSeedEnabled, DEMO_SEED_FLAGS` from `../utils/demoSeedGate` — **and nothing else** |
| does it import `routes/adminConfig`? | **No.** Its own header says so, and gives the reason: importing it loads `config.ts`, which throws unless `DATABASE_URL`/`JWT_SECRET` are set |
| executable references to `seed-demo-users` in any originate test | **0** — the single grep hit is a line of prose in that header |
| **control** | the same grep for a covered route (`api/webhooks`) returns **13** |

So the truth table of `isDemoSeedEnabled` is well covered — the default-deny cases especially, which is the valuable half — but **nothing observes that** `POST /api/admin/seed-demo-users` **calls it.** Remove the call and the suite is 100% green.

### Why this is the same class as KS-914 A-2, and why that matters

The #868 gate found exactly this shape one ticket over: six cells tested `pinnedLookup` while nothing tested that `safeOutboundRequest` used it, and stripping the wiring left 778 passed / 0 failed. **A tested helper plus an unasserted call site is a guard that can be removed silently.** It is worth treating as a recurring pattern in this codebase rather than as two coincidences.

What that gate is protecting here is not small: without it, any authenticated `ORG_ADMIN` of any tenant could reset 14 named accounts — across every tenant, under `runWithPlatformScope` — to the bcrypt of `admin123` published in the same file, then sign in as one. Four of those fourteen are themselves `ORG_ADMIN` (counted 2026-09-06 at both `develop` and PR #867, with a control).

### Fix shape

An assertion that the ROUTE refuses when the gate is closed. The blocker the existing header names is real — importing `adminConfig.ts` pulls `config.ts`, which throws without env — so the options are (a) mount the router with `DATABASE_URL`/`JWT_SECRET` stubbed, the pattern `ks444-*`/`ks445-*` already use in this service, or (b) a static assertion that the call site exists, which is weaker and should be a fallback, not the plan.

**Red-proof it by deleting the** `if (!isDemoSeedEnabled())` **line and confirming the new cell reds.** A cell added without that has only been observed agreeing with correct code.

### The naming confusion the gate also flagged

Two different gates are called "the demo-seed gate" in prose: **auth's** (`services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`, pen-test F-05, which allows an `isDevLike` bypass) and **originate's** (`utils/demoSeedGate.ts`, deliberately stricter — both flags, no bypass). The comment block at `adminConfig.ts:1770-1800` discusses both within a few lines. Worth one clarifying sentence naming which is which, so a reader does not carry auth's bypass across to originate's route.

*Filed by s141 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from the #867 gate's finding B-3, at Wednesday's direction to file it rather than widen that PR. The measurement above is mine; the finding is the gate's.*

title: Launcher boot step tells every agent session to POST /api/seen as EXTRANET_ME=kam, which clears Kam's own unread flags — and the extranet is input-only
description:
## What is wrong

`Launch_Claude.command:522` (boot step 7) instructs every session:

> "…GET the summary for this operator (EXTRANET_ME), and fold my open tasks + replies-to-me + new documents into the confirmation below; **mark seen afterwards**."

which routes to the `extranet` skill's step 3:

> `POST $EXTRANET_URL/api/seen {"person":"$EXTRANET_ME"}` so "new" resets next session.

And in this project's `4_Credentials/.env`:

```
EXTRANET_ME=kam
```

So the "operator" an agent marks caught-up as **is Kam himself**. An agent that follows the boot step clears **Kam's** unread flags on his own portal — the tasks, replies and documents he has not yet read. The next time he opens the extranet, the things an agent read on his behalf are no longer marked new to him.

It is the human's signal, and an automated session destroys it as a side effect of booting.

## Why it is a defect and not a preference

Two independent reasons, either of which is sufficient:

1. `EXTRANET_ME` **is doing two jobs.** It identifies *whose* summary to fetch — correct, an agent working for Kam should see Kam's queue — and it also identifies *who has now seen it* — wrong, because the agent saw it and Kam did not. One variable, two meanings, and the second one is only ever wrong when an agent uses it.
2. **The extranet is input-only for agents** (standing rule for this project). `POST /api/seen` is a write. The boot step asks for a write the operating rules forbid, so the instruction cannot be followed as stated regardless of who `EXTRANET_ME` names.

## Reproduced

Not by running it — running it *is* the defect, and it is not reversible from the API. Established from the artefacts instead:

* `4_Credentials/.env:4` → `EXTRANET_ME=kam` (agent key on line 3 not reproduced here)
* `Launch_Claude.command:522` → the "mark seen afterwards" instruction
* `Notes (MASTER)/skills/Current/extranet.md:27` → the `POST /api/seen {"person":"$EXTRANET_ME"}` step
* `…/extranet.md:111` → `POST /api/seen | {person}` in the endpoint table

The three artefacts compose into the behaviour without needing to execute it. **This session declined the step and said so rather than skipping it silently** — that is the current mitigation, and it relies on every future session making the same judgement, which is not a control.

## Fix shape

Any of these closes it; the first is the smallest:

1. **Drop "mark seen afterwards" from the launcher's step 7** and the corresponding step from the skill, for agent sessions. The summary is read-only; nothing needs the flag reset, and "new since last session" is more useful to an agent unreset anyway.
2. **Separate the two meanings** — `EXTRANET_ME` for whose queue to read, a distinct `EXTRANET_SEEN_AS` for whose flags to clear, unset by default so the write never happens unless someone deliberately sets it.
3. **Make** `/api/seen` **refuse an agent key** for a person other than the key's own identity, server-side, so no launcher wording can cause it. This one belongs to the extranet app rather than the launcher.

## Scope

The launcher is a per-project copy of a master template, so fixing this copy does not fix the others — the same boot step exists in every project's launcher, and any project whose `EXTRANET_ME` names a human has the same defect. Whoever picks this up should decide at the template level, not here.

Filed at Wednesday's direction (2026-09-06) after this session declined the boot step. Not applied mid-queue: the launcher is not this seat's to edit.

title: `/shared` ships the TypeScript compiler and a 267 MB dev tree into all 24 runtime images — KS-490 closed the service tree only
description:
## KS-490 closed the SERVICE tree and left the SHARED tree open — `/shared` ships the TypeScript compiler into all 24 runtime images

KS-490's two PRs (#849, #851) removed the build toolchain from the runtime *stages* and pruned each service's *own* `node_modules`. **Neither touches** `/shared`, and every runtime stage copies it wholesale.

### Measured on the live demo box, in RUNNING containers

| Reading | `secuura-security` | `secuura-governance` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `/shared/node_modules/typescript` | **present, 22.9 MB** | **present, 22.9 MB** |
| `bin/tsc` | **present** | **present** |
| `/shared` total | **267.2 MB** | **267.2 MB** |
| top-level entries under `/shared/node_modules` | **243** | **243** |

*(The #851 gate's tester reported 342 packages; I counted **243 top-level entries** with* `ls | wc -l`*, which counts a scoped* `@org` *directory once regardless of what it contains. Both numbers are probably right about different things — stating my instrument rather than reconciling them by assertion.)*

### It is footprint and attack surface, NOT loadability — measured, with a control

```
require.resolve('typescript', {paths:['/app']})  ->  MODULE_NOT_FOUND
require.resolve('express',    {paths:['/app']})  ->  resolves
```

The control is what makes the first line meaningful: the resolver works, and `typescript` genuinely is not reachable from the app's module paths. So no runtime code can load it — but a compiler binary and 267 MB of dev tree are present in every running container, which is exactly what KS-490 exists to remove.

### Cause

`shared-builder` runs `npm ci` **without** `--omit=dev` and is never pruned, and all 24 runtime stages `COPY --from=shared-builder /shared /shared`.

### Fix shape — and the hazard it carries

Prune `shared-builder` after its build: one place, all 24 services.

⚠ **This is exactly the hazard #851 just fixed.** `@secuura/shared` is a hand-made undeclared symlink; pruning removed it, and three runtime stages that did not re-create it shipped images that crashed on start with `Cannot find module '@secuura/shared'`. **A** `/shared` **prune therefore needs a real start probe per service, not reasoning** — the same shape of evidence #851 ended up needing. See [KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490) and #851's fix commit.

*Filed by s140 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from #851's gate findings (F1).*

title: Demo platform-admin account has mfa_enabled = false — deliberate demo posture, or a gap that outlived KS-737?
description:
## The demo platform-admin account has MFA disabled — decision needed, not a fix

**Measured, not inferred.** Found while running the KS-913 pre-check on the demo box (read-only).

| property | value |
| -- | -- |
| id | `a0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000060` |
| role | `system_admin` |
| status | `active`, `email_verified = true` |
| `mfa_enabled` | `false` |
| credential | `$argon2…`, unique among the 30 users |
| last login | **2026-07-14 10:36:41Z — the account is genuinely used** |

This is the demo environment's real platform-admin account, reachable at the public demo URL.

### Why this is a question and not a defect report

[KS-737](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-737) — *platform-admin login skips MFA entirely when* `mfaCode` *is omitted* — is **archived**. I have **not** established whether this row is the same case, a deliberate demo posture (an admin nobody wants to carry a TOTP device for on a throwaway environment), or a gap that outlived its ticket. Establishing that would mean testing an authentication path against a real person's account, which I am not doing to close an observation.

**So this ticket carries the measurement only.** No fix is proposed and nothing changes until it is ruled on.

### The decision

Is MFA-off on the demo `system_admin` intended? If **yes**, close this and the row is documented for the next reviewer who trips over it. If **no**, it becomes a remediation ticket and should say whether it is demo-only or reaches the same code path as KS-737.

title: vite is a production dependency of services/auth — esbuild and fsevents ship into the runtime image, imported by nothing
description:
## `vite` sits in auth's production `dependencies`, dragging esbuild and fsevents into the runtime image

Found by the #849 (KS-490) tier-2 gate as F-2, and measured before filing.

### The measurement

| Reading | Value |
| -- | -- |
| `services/auth/package.json` → `dependencies.vite` | `7.3.6` |
| `services/auth/package.json` → `devDependencies.vite` | **absent** |
| runtime sources under `services/auth/src` importing `vite` (excluding `__tests__`) | **0** |
| CONTROL: runtime sources importing `express` | **15** |

The control is what makes the zero mean something — the same grep shape finds 15 files for a package auth genuinely uses at runtime, so 0 for `vite` is a real absence and not a grep that cannot match.

### Why it matters

Because `vite` is a production dependency it survives `npm prune --omit=dev` and `npm ci --omit=dev`, and it pulls `esbuild 0.28.1` and `fsevents 2.3.3` with it. Both carry install scripts, which is why auth's production set shows three `hasInstallScript` entries where the estate has only one package that actually requires compilation.

**This is not a security finding on its own** — the runtime `npm ci --ignore-scripts` means none of those install scripts ever runs, and that is why #849 passed. It is image weight and attack surface: a build toolchain shipped into a running container that no runtime code imports.

### The fix

Move `vite` to `devDependencies` in `services/auth/package.json`, regenerate the lock, and re-measure the runtime `node_modules` file count (the tester counted **5,591 files** in auth's runtime tree). Expect esbuild, rollup and fsevents to leave with it.

**Verify before assuming:** confirm nothing in auth's build path (not just `src/`) needs `vite` at runtime — a config file or a script entry could. The import walk above covers `src/` only.

*Filed by s140 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from #849's gate findings.*

title: A clean stack has no supported way to obtain its first privileged account
description:
## The gap

On a freshly built stack there is no supported path to a first privileged account:

* `POST /api/admin/seed-demo-users` is now default-deny (B-3 hardening) and needs **both** `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` and `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED=true`.
* Registration cannot mint a privileged role — KS-82 deliberately refuses a client-supplied role.

Both of those are **correct** and neither is questioned here. The gap is that nothing owns the bootstrap step, because historically the seed accounts were simply always present, so no one had to.

## Status of the original claim — corrected

An earlier KS-487 comment (2026-09-01 11:36Z) asserted a hard **deadlock**: that a clean stack could never call `seed-demo-users` at all. **That was retracted 21 minutes later by its own author** (11:57Z) — `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:47` fires `userRepo.seedDemoUsers()`, so there is no deadlock. This ticket carries the *remaining* gap only: not "impossible", but "undocumented and unowned".

## What would close it

One of: a documented first-run procedure naming the two env vars and their intended lifetime; or a one-shot bootstrap command that creates a single named admin without the demo-persona list; or an explicit decision that operators set the env vars, written where an operator will find it (`DEV-PROCESS.md` or the deployment runbook).

## Provenance

Recorded on [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487) as prose (2026-09-01, with its correction) rather than a ticket, because the Linear workspace was at its free issue cap. The cap was lifted 2026-09-06, so it is filed now. **This is the finding whose existence-only-in-prose was the reason the table was built.**

*Filed by s140 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from the KS-487 stream-B table.*

title: KS-907 suite residues: CASE 2 never asserts the pruning it is named for, a cell count printed as a launcher-run count, and a grep -qc diagnostic
description:
## BLUF

**Three residues in** `Launch_Claude.seats.test.sh` **from the KS-907 by-hash gate (F3, F4, F6 — all Polish). The worst is F4: CASE 2, the cell the suite calls "the one that matters most", never asserts the thing it is named for. All three reproduced here before filing.**

Ships with the launcher follow-up by the same by-hash mechanism — the suite sits at the project root, outside git, like the launcher.

## F4 — CASE 2 asserts the consequence, not the act

CASE 2 exists to prove that a **dead** registry entry is *pruned*, because a guard that latched on a stale PID would pin every future launch of the project into read-only mode. It asserts `DRY_COUNT = 0` and that the step carries the pull text — both of which are the *downstream effect*. **It never checks that the dead pid left the file.**

So a launcher that read the entry, counted it as not-live, and left it in the registry forever would pass CASE 2 while the file grew without bound.

**Fix shape:** assert the dead pid is absent from `$SEAT_FILE` after the run, and — the control that makes it discriminate — that the *live* pid in CASE 1 is still **present**. Presence and absence in the same batch.

## F3 — the hygiene cell prints the cell count and calls them launcher runs

The label is built from `$((pass+fail))`:

> `2_Project_Files/.git/config is byte-identical after 12 launcher runs`

**12 is the number of cells that had run at that point. The true number of launcher invocations is 6** — measured: `run_launcher` is called exactly 6 times (control, live, dead, recycled, scan, scanoff).

The assertion itself is sound; only the number in the sentence is wrong, and it is wrong in the direction that overstates the evidence. The figure `12` was carried into KS-907's READY and its ticket comment; both are corrected to 6.

**Fix shape:** count the invocations in `run_launcher` and print that.

## F6 — `grep -qc` with `echo $?` as a diagnostic

`Launch_Claude.seats.test.sh:98`, inside the CONTROL's failure message:

```
pull-text=$(grep -qc "$PULLTEXT" "$WORK/control.step" 2>/dev/null; echo $?)
```

`-q` and `-c` contradict: `-q` wins, so nothing is counted and the `echo $?` prints an exit status labelled as if it were a count. It appears only in a `bad()` message, so it has never been rendered — which is exactly why it survived.

**Fix shape:** use the same `grep -q … && echo YES || echo NO` form the neighbouring field already uses.

## Declared limit, recorded not fixed (F5)

The process scan matches the project directory as a **substring** of the argv, so a sibling project directory named `Blockchain-<anything>` would be counted as a seat of this project. No such sibling exists (measured). The failure direction is safe — a false positive costs a read-only boot — and it is recorded on KS-907 as a limit rather than worked.

Residues of the KS-907 tier-2 by-hash gate (F3, F4, F6; Polish). Parent: KS-907.

title: KS-907 launcher residues: a sentinel comment describing a test that does not exist, and a 2>/dev/null placed after the append it silences
description:
## BLUF

**Two residues in** `Launch_Claude.command` **from the KS-907 by-hash gate (F1, F2 — both Minor). One is a comment describing a test that does not exist; the other is a** `2>/dev/null` **placed *after* the append it is meant to silence, so a failed open still prints. Both reproduced here before filing.**

⚠ **Ships by the BY-HASH mechanism, not as an in-place edit.** The hash that passed the gate (`9609c8453da8d7743a4b3ed2a94db6b09bef588c29f83e57b16255963a0929f1`) is the hash that runs. Any fix takes a new `.pre-` copy, the three hashes in the READY, and a narrow tier-2 gate on the diff — the same shape KS-907 used.

## F1 — a sentinel comment that describes a test that does not exist

`Launch_Claude.command:244`:

```
# ── KS-907 SEAT REGISTRY — BEGIN (do not edit the sentinels; the test extracts here) ──
```

The suite does **not** extract between the sentinels. It runs the real launcher via `SECUURA_LAUNCH_DRY_RUN=1` and parses the `DRY_RUN_*` markers — which is the better design, and it is what shipped. The sentinel wording is left over from a design that was replaced.

Measured: `Launch_Claude.seats.test.sh` contains **0** references to `KS-907 SEAT REGISTRY`, against a control of **2** occurrences of `SECUURA_LAUNCH_DRY_RUN=1` — so the suite really does not touch the sentinels, and the same grep can find what is there.

Consequence: nothing guards the sentinels, and the comment tells a future editor to preserve something for a reason that is not true. This is the same class as the KS-904 slip in the same session — a comment asserting a guard that is not in the code.

**Fix shape:** either delete the sentinels and the claim, or make them real by having the suite assert exactly one `BEGIN` and one `END`. Prefer the first: the dry-run markers already are the contract, and a second contract nothing checks is worse than none.

## F2 — `2>/dev/null` placed after the append it is meant to silence

`Launch_Claude.command:292` and `:295`:

```
printf '%s' "$SEAT_KEPT" > "$SEAT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
printf '%s|%s\n' "$$" "$SEAT_SELF_STARTED" >> "$SEAT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
```

Redirections apply left to right. The file is opened **before** `2>/dev/null` takes effect, so a failed open writes its error to the still-live stderr. The `|| true` swallows the status but not the noise, and a boot that cannot write its registry prints a bare shell error into the operator's pane.

Reproduced under `/bin/bash 3.2.57` — the shell the launcher runs under, not the zsh this repo's tooling defaults to:

|  | stderr |
| -- | -- |
| **A** `>> file 2>/dev/null` (the shipped shape) | `/bin/bash: line 2: /nonexistent-dir-xyz/f: No such file or directory` |
| **B** `2>/dev/null >> file` (redirect first) | *(none)* |
| **control** — a successful append, shape A | *(none)* |

The control matters: shape A is not simply always noisy, so the difference is the ordering and not the instrument.

*(An earlier A/B of mine did not discriminate because the Bash tool runs **zsh**, where both orderings reported the error.* `BASH_VERSION` *was empty — that is the tell.)*

**Fix shape:** move the redirection ahead of the target, at both sites.

## Regression

A launch whose registry directory is unwritable must produce no shell error on stderr — with a control launch that writes successfully, so the cell can fail.

Residues of the KS-907 tier-2 by-hash gate (F1, F2; Minor). Parent: KS-907.

title: Preflight leg 12 executes ZERO suite cells — it is a reachability check, so with Actions retired no shell suite runs on a gated push
description:
## BLUF

**Preflight leg 12 runs** `run-shell-suites.sh --check-unreached` **— a REACHABILITY check that executes ZERO suite cells. With GitHub Actions retired for this repo, that means NO shell test suite runs on a gated push at all, while the push prints** `PREFLIGHT PASSED`**. Measured: a full gated push emitted 0** suite `ok` lines; the same grep over one suite run directly emits **16**, so the zero is a real absence and not a grep that cannot match.

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:400` — `bash scripts/run-shell-suites.sh --check-unreached`.

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-shell-suites.sh:56-58` — `--check-unreached` sets `MODE="check"`; the **empty** argument sets `MODE="run"`. The preflight never uses the run mode, so the runner's executing path is unreachable from a push.

## Measured

|  | suite `ok` lines |
| -- | -- |
| a full gated push (12/12 legs, `PREFLIGHT PASSED`) | **0** |
| **control** — one suite run directly, same grep | **16** |

## A comment that is false as written

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base.test.sh:49-51` says:

> Leg 12 of the preflight now reaches this suite on every gated push, so anyone who signs their commits gets that red, pointing at the hook rather than at their own config.

"Reaches" is doing work it cannot do. Leg 12 proves the suite is not an orphan; it never runs it, so a signing misconfiguration produces no red on a push. The sentence should say **reachable**, and the promise about the red should go or move to wherever the suites actually run.

The same claim was published in #861's first draft and corrected there before it left this seat; this ticket is the code-side half.

## Fix shape (a decision, not yet a build)

Two options, and the choice is a real trade:

1. **A leg that runs the bare runner** — the suites execute on every gated push. Cost: minutes added to every push, on top of an already multi-minute preflight.
2. **Keep leg 12 as reachability**, run the suites wherever replaces Actions, and correct the comment to "reachable".

Option 2 leaves a real gap while nothing replaces Actions, which is the current state. Option 1 makes every push slower for every author. This wants a call before anyone builds it.

## Not introduced by #861

Pre-existing. Named by the #861 tier-2 gate (F-2, Minor, explicitly NOT that PR's) and reproduced independently here against `develop` before filing.

title: connectorId persists but is invisible through the API — POST and GET both return null while the row holds the value
description:
## `connectorId` persists correctly but is invisible through the API — a Platform S caller cannot read back the connector it just set

Found during probe 5(ii) on the demo box, 2026-09-06, against `security` rebuilt from `db1848abf` (KS-869's code live: `connector_id` 7 occurrences in `/app/dist`, 0 in the pre-rebuild image).

### What happens

`POST /api/security/keys` with `connectorId: "probe-connector-20260906T084007Z"`:

* **HTTP 201.** Response body carries `connectorId: null`.
* `GET /api/security/keys?organizationId=…` for the same key: `connectorId: null`.
* **The database has the value**: `SELECT connector_id FROM svc_api_keys WHERE name = 'wednesday-probe-20260906T084007Z'` → `probe-connector-20260906T084007Z`.

So KS-869's write half works — the totals moved **39 rows / 0 connectors → 40 / 1**, exactly one new row with exactly one connector. What does not work is the read-back: **neither the write response nor the list response exposes the field**, so the only way to confirm a connector was recorded is direct database access, which an integrator does not have.

### Why it matters

The S↔K ownership contract has Platform S minting connector-scoped keys through this endpoint. Under KS-843's cutover the connector is load-bearing. An integrator that sets `connectorId` and reads the response back sees `null` and cannot distinguish "not persisted" from "persisted but not returned" — the two have opposite remedies.

`rowToApiKey` (`services/security/src/index.ts:345`) does map `connectorId`, which suggests the write and list responses are served from the in-memory representation rather than a row read — that is a hypothesis, stated as one; the measurement above is not.

### Controls

* Impossible token in the same image → 0.
* Validate on the revoked probe key → `valid:false, reason:"Key revoked"`; on a key that never existed → `valid:false, reason:"Key not found"`. Different reasons, so the API's own instruments do discriminate — this is not a blanket read failure.

### Housekeeping

The probe key `wednesday-probe-20260906T084007Z` was revoked in-leg through the API (`DELETE`, HTTP 200) and the revocation confirmed two ways: `is_active = f` in the row, and `validate` → `"Key revoked"`. No probe key is live.

Related: KS-869 (the write), KS-889 (the empty backfill window), KS-887 (the write-half pin that cannot discriminate).

title: Audit the eleven cwd- and script-relative repo-root derivations under scripts/ and systemTest/ — one family, several blind in different ways
description: ## BLUF**The** `$(cd ../.. && pwd)` **/** `$(dirname "$0")/../..` **family appears eleven times across** `scripts/` **and** `systemTest/`**, in at least three variants with different failure modes.** KS-859 fixed one of them (`no-tracked-credentials.sh`); the rest are unaudited.## ScopeEnumerate every repo-root derivation under `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/` and `systemTest/`, classify each as script-relative, cwd-relative, or git-derived, and record for each whether it is:- **layout-dependent** (breaks where the repo root is not two levels up — the KS-859 defect), and/or- **cwd-dependent** (breaks when invoked from elsewhere — worse), and/or- **env-dependent** (breaks under an inherited git environment).Known starting points, measured at `34347a8fa`: `action-pins-labelled.sh:46` and `bare-path-scripts-executable.sh:57` are cwd-relative. `run-shell-suites.sh:45` **is NOT blind** — its KS-731 zero-suites guard fails loudly, and is the model for what a safe one looks like.## Why one ticket rather than elevenThis is a survey, not a defect: the deliverable is the classification plus a ticket per genuinely-blind site. Filing eleven speculative tickets before measuring would be the aggregation shape Kam withdrew.## Fix shapeThe audit first. Then, per blind site, the KS-859 idiom — ask git from a self-derived directory with the environment scrubbed — and a shared helper if the count justifies one.Charter named by the #858 gate as its round-2 work. Parent: KS-859, merged at `34347a8fafb5feca69d59dcee12b8aca9ce4a69d`.

title: no-tracked-credentials.sh cites two scripts as "structurally immune" exemplars — both use a WORSE cwd-relative root derivation
description: ## BLUF**The comment added by #858 points the next reader at two scripts as exemplars of the safe idiom. Both use a strictly worse one.**`no-tracked-credentials.sh:81-82` says:> `bare-path-scripts-executable.sh` and `action-pins-labelled.sh` already derive their root this way and are structurally immune; this is the same idiom.Measured at the merged tip `34347a8fa`:`action-pins-labelled.sh:46          REPO_ROOT="$(cd ../.. && pwd)"bare-path-scripts-executable.sh:57  REPO_ROOT="$(cd ../.. && pwd)"`That is **cwd-relative**, not script-relative. It depends on the caller's working directory, where the idiom the comment describes (`$(dirname "$0")/../..`) does not. They are not immune, and they are not the same idiom.## Why it mattersThe comment is load-bearing prose: it exists to tell the next person what shape to copy. Pointing at a worse form is how the family spreads.## Fix shapeCorrect the comment to describe the idiom without endorsing those two, and either fix their derivations or reference the audit ticket that covers them.Residue of the #858 tier-2 gate (F-QA-01, Minor). Parent: KS-859, merged at `34347a8fafb5feca69d59dcee12b8aca9ce4a69d`.

title: build_fixture swallows its own failure — `>/dev/null 2>&1` makes a fixture that did not build indistinguishable from one that did
description: ## BLUF**`build_fixture` redirects its entire body to `/dev/null 2>&1`, so a fixture that fails to build is silent.** Every case downstream then asserts against a repository that may not exist, and the failure surfaces (if at all) as a confusing assertion rather than as "the fixture did not build".Pre-existing — introduced with the suite in #855 (KS-854), not by #860.## Where`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base.test.sh` — the closing `) >/dev/null 2>&1` of `build_fixture`. The redirect is deliberate (the fixture build is noisy: `git init`, `commit`, `push`), but it swallows failure as well as noise.## Why it is worth a lineIt is the enabling condition for KS-896's class: a control that cannot tell "absent" from "verified" is only dangerous because the absence can happen quietly. Fixing the control without fixing the silence leaves the next fixture failure equally hard to read.## Fix shapeKeep the redirect, capture the status: `( … ) >"$WORK/build.log" 2>&1 || { echo "FIXTURE BUILD FAILED for $root — see $WORK/build.log" >&2; exit 2; }`. A suite that cannot build its fixture must abort, not proceed — the exit-2 convention this file already uses for a missing hook.## RegressionA `build_fixture` call against an unwritable path must abort with a named error rather than continuing into the cases.Residue of the #860 tier-2 gate (carried as pre-existing, filed separately per one-ticket-per-defect). Parent: KS-881, merged at `0be4deef94011a2d04273336b403c14254b58cad`.

title: KS-881's CONTROL is satisfied when the branch does not exist — `upstream=NONE` cannot tell an absent branch from a branch with no upstream
description: ## BLUF**The CONTROL cell added by KS-881 asserts** `upstream=NONE`**, and that is satisfied when the branch DOES NOT EXIST AT ALL.** A fixture whose `git checkout` failed produces the same reading as a correctly-built one, so the cell certifies a shape it has not observed.Introduced by #860 (KS-881), which added that assertion. Found by its own gate.## Where`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base.test.sh` — the CONTROL block:`bashgit checkout -q -b feature/x --no-track origin/developup="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref 'feature/x@{upstream}' 2>/dev/null)"[ -n "$up" ] || up=NONE`If the checkout fails, `feature/x` never exists, `rev-parse` fails, `up` is empty → `NONE`. The absence of a branch and the absence of an upstream are indistinguishable.## Reproduced against the merged code (`develop` @ `0be4deef9`)Tamper: the CONTROL's checkout cut from `origin/NOSUCHREF` instead of `origin/develop`.`ok   CONTROL — the fixture is a real fresh clone: local branches [main], develop local=NO remote=YES, upstream=NONE8 passed, 0 failed`The branch was never created and the cell reported the shape as verified.## Why it matters beyond this cellIt is the exact class this suite exists to police, in the suite itself: **an absent thing reading as a verified one**. KS-854 (the hook skipping and saying nothing), KS-676 (a scan reporting clean having examined nothing) and KS-891 are the same shape.## Fix shapeAssert the branch EXISTS before asking about its upstream — `git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/feature/x` must succeed — and only then that `@{upstream}` fails. Report both facts in the cell's message, as it already reports `local=` and `remote=`.## RegressionThe tamper above (the CONTROL cutting from a non-existent remote ref) must **red the CONTROL**. Today it passes 8/0.Residue of the #860 tier-2 gate (F-860-01, Minor). Parent: KS-881, merged at `0be4deef94011a2d04273336b403c14254b58cad`.

title: Runbook: a code-first deploy leg must use `docker compose up -d --no-deps <svc>` and start `migrations` explicitly, last — `up -d` pulls depends_on and applied three migrations early
description:
## BLUF

On 2026-09-06 a demo deploy ran its migrations **~5 minutes before the service they were ordered after**, because `docker compose up -d <svc>` starts that service's `depends_on` — and `migrations` is one of them. The order had been analysed, escalated and explicitly ruled; it was defeated by a compose edge nobody checked.

**Measured harm: none** (0 violating rows in both affected tables, against controls of 30 and 3). This ticket exists so the next leg does not rely on that luck.

## The timeline

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| 05:55:43Z | `docker compose up -d api-gateway` |
| **05:56:47Z** | **045, 046, 047 applied** (`_secuura_migrations`) — 046 and 047 **ADD CHECK constraints** |
| 06:01:41Z | `auth` finally rebuilt and healthy — until then the box served **Sept-3** code |

A ~5 minute window in which a tightened schema faced code written before the vocabulary existed. The migrations' own normalisation had nothing to do, so nothing broke.

## The runbook lines this should produce

1. **A code-first leg uses** `docker compose up -d --no-deps <svc>`**.** Without it, "code first, schema last" is not enforceable — the first `up` runs the schema.
2. **Start** `migrations` **explicitly, last, as its own step**, so its timing is a decision rather than a side effect.
3. **The migration runner's** `Summary: applied=N failed=0` **is a COUNT, not a version list.** It printed identically on all three `up` invocations that day and would have read the same had 045–047 never run. **The evidence is** `_secuura_migrations` **and** `pg_constraint`**, read directly.** This is the same class as the project's existing baked-migrations warning, from the other direction.

## Acceptance

`deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md` (and any deploy runbook) carries the three lines above with this timeline as the reason. **No runbook edit without this ticket** — that was the ruling.

title: KS-869's COALESCE backfill has an EMPTY window — the 39 pre-existing keys never backfill, so the KS-843 cutover flip still has no usable evidence
description:
## BLUF

**KS-869 does not fix the KS-843 cutover's evidence problem for keys that already exist.** The `COALESCE(EXCLUDED.connector_id, svc_api_keys.connector_id)` backfill I described as filling pre-fix rows "for free" **has no window in which to fire**. Found by the KS-869 tier-1 gate; **correcting my own claim** in that PR body.

## Why the window is empty

`connectorId` enters an `ApiKey` object in exactly two places:

* at **mint** (`services/security/src/index.ts:1004`), or
* from the **row** (`:345`, `rowToApiKey`)

`memApiKeys` is warmed **only from the database at boot** (`:376-381`). The deploy restarts the service, so every pre-fix row re-warms with `connectorId` **undefined**; every later save therefore passes NULL; and `COALESCE` correctly declines to overwrite with NULL. **"The next save backfills it for free" is true only for keys minted after this deploys.**

## The consequence, and it lands on KS-843

Kam's 2026-09-06 13:59 logged-grace ruling flips `SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED` **once the log shows Platform S on the new key**. After KS-869 merges and deploys, the `[KS-843]` grace log will **still record** `connectorId: null` **for every EXISTING Platform S key**. The flip's evidence is not restored by KS-869 alone.

## FIRST ITEM — the measurement that decides the fix

**Does anything on the row determine the connector?** Check `key_prefix`, `organization_id`, `name` (the mint sets `name` to `Platform S connector — <org|externalRef>`) against the 39 existing rows (measured 2026-09-06; this ticket originally said 43). If one of them does, a one-off backfill is possible. If none does, **the answer is a re-mint of Platform S's keys** — which is Stuart's window and therefore Kam's call, and it merges with the KS-577 rotation conversation rather than being a separate ask.

## Acceptance

Either the 43 rows carry a correct `connector_id` (backfilled from a source named in the measurement above), or a ruling is recorded that Platform S's keys will be re-minted, with the flip explicitly waiting on it. **KS-843's cutover comment must be updated either way** — today it says KS-869 is the prerequisite; if that is not sufficient, it should say so.

title: dbSaveApiKey SWALLOWS a failed INSERT — POST /api/keys answers 201 for a key that was never written; blast radius is ALL key persistence, not one column
description:
## BLUF

`dbSaveApiKey` catches every error from its INSERT and only logs it (`services/security/src/index.ts:236-238`). **A key that fails to persist still returns 201 with live key material.** Pre-existing; KS-869 grew its blast radius by taking the statement from 14 columns to 15.

## Mechanism

```ts
} catch (err: any) {
  logger.error('DB save API key failed', { error: err?.message });
}
```

The route continues and answers 201. The key exists in `memApiKeys` and validates — until the process restarts, at which point it silently does not exist.

**KS-869's contribution:** on a schema lacking `connector_id` the 15-column statement raises `42703` where the parent's 14-column one succeeded. Likelihood measured **LOW** by the gate — every deployment path lands the column (migration 018 is a single commit, and the demo now carries it) — but the failure mode is the swallow, not the column.

## Fix shape

Either a **boot assertion** that the named columns exist (fail fast, loudly, at start), or **narrow the catch** so `42703` (undefined column) and other structural errors are re-raised rather than logged. A mint that cannot persist must not answer 201.

## Acceptance

With the column absent, `POST /api/keys` does **not** return 201. A driven test: point the service at a schema without `connector_id` and assert the response is a 5xx, not a 201 — the shape that would have caught this.

title: KS-869 test defect (mine): the WRITE-half column-list pin can be satisfied by the COALESCE clause, so a statement missing connector_id from the column list passes all six cells
description:
## BLUF

**This is a defect in a test I wrote**, found by the KS-869 tier-1 gate. My WRITE-half cell claims to pin `connector_id` into the INSERT's **column list**. It does not — it can be satisfied by the `COALESCE` clause twelve characters further on.

## The hole

```js
expect(code).toMatch(/INSERT INTO svc_api_keys[\s\S]{0,400}?connector_id/)
```

The `{0,400}` window reaches past the column list into the `ON CONFLICT … COALESCE(EXCLUDED.connector_id, …)` clause. So the assertion is satisfied by a statement that **never names** `connector_id` **in the columns at all**.

**Measured by the gate (X2):** `connector_id` removed from the column list, `$14` placeholders against 15 params — **all six cells GREEN**, on a statement that would fail on every single save.

## Why it matters more than its severity

The whole of KS-869 is "a column nobody wrote". The test meant to stop that recurring can be green while exactly that recurs. It is the same shape as the defect it guards.

## Fix shape

Capture the **column list itself** — `INSERT INTO svc_api_keys \(([^)]*)\)` — and require `connector_id` inside **that capture**; add a separate assertion for the `,$15)` placeholder count. **Regression:** the X2 shape (column dropped, 14 placeholders) must go **RED**.

## Acceptance

The X2 tamper reds. The current fix still passes. Both stated as a predicted-then-measured red-proof, not a verdict.

title: pre-push resolves the bare name `develop`, so a TAG named develop beats the branch — and --quiet suppresses the ambiguity warning
description:
## BLUF

`git rev-parse --verify --quiet develop` **resolves a TAG named** `develop` **in preference to the branch, and** `--quiet` **suppresses the ambiguity warning that would otherwise say so. The hook would then compute its base against the tag.** Latent, not live: `git tag -l develop` is empty in this repo today.

## Where

`.githooks/pre-push:98–99` — the loop's first candidate is the bare name `develop`, verified with `git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$_ref"`.

## Measured (git 2.51.0, isolated fixture)

Three commits c1/c2/c3; a tag `develop` at c1, a branch `develop` at c2, `HEAD` at c3.

```
SCENARIO A — tag develop, NO branch develop
  git rev-parse --verify --quiet develop  -> b02eae510   (THE TAG)
  the loop breaks on it and uses it as the base: YES

SCENARIO B — BOTH a tag (c1) and a branch (c2)
  git rev-parse --verify --quiet develop  -> b02eae510   (THE TAG)
  git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/develop -> 621667116   (the branch)

ambiguity warning
  with --quiet : 0
  without      : 1            <- the control: the warning exists, --quiet is what hides it

consequence
  git merge-base develop HEAD            -> b02eae510
  git merge-base refs/heads/develop HEAD -> 621667116
```

Two different bases, so two different `changed` sets — and with the warning suppressed there is no signal which ref was used.

## Fix shape

Iterate fully-qualified refs — `refs/heads/develop`, `refs/remotes/origin/develop` — so the name cannot be captured by a tag. This also composes with the fix for the sibling ordering defect (KS-882), which changes which of those two is tried first.

## Regression

A fixture carrying a tag named `develop` at a different commit from the branch must still resolve the base to the branch.

Residue of the #855 tier-2 gate (F-4, Polish). Parent: KS-854, merged at `f72c9023f6e5ca5ca035c0734282d91775533a17`.

title: Quarantine or reconcile the dead converters copy — a second rowToApiKey that maps neither tenantId nor connectorId, with a passing test on it
description:
## BLUF

`services/security/src/converters.ts:122` holds a **second** `rowToApiKey`, imported only by its own test and by **nothing in production**. It has already diverged from the live one, and it is the shape that silently reintroduces a whole class of defect if anyone ever "consolidates" onto it.

Found during KS-869. **Deliberately not fixed there** — fixing one field in a dead copy would have been arbitrary.

## The divergence, measured

| field | `index.ts:309` (live) | `converters.ts:122` (dead) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `tenantId` | mapped — **the load-bearing tenancy field**, NOT NULL + RLS-enforced since migration 018 | **absent** |
| `connectorId` | mapped (KS-869) | **absent** |
| `organizationId` | `(r.organization_id as string \| null) ?? null` — nullable since KS-33 | `r.organization_id as string` — not nullable |

Imported by: `src/__tests__/row-converters.test.ts` only. Production (`index.ts:253`, `:379`, `:1162`) uses the `index.ts` copy. Verified with a grep whose control fires (`keyRevokePolicy` is imported at `index.ts:26`).

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

**KS-869 exists because a mapper did not map a column.** This file is a second mapper that does not map *two* columns, one of which is the tenancy field the RLS policies depend on. It is currently harmless because nothing calls it — and it carries a passing test, which is exactly what would make a future reader trust it. A refactor that points production at "the canonical converters module" reintroduces KS-869 **and** a tenancy bug in one move, with a green suite.

## Two dispositions — either closes this

* **Quarantine:** move it out of the compiled/imported tree (rename, or fold into the test that is its only consumer) so it cannot be reached by an import. Per the never-delete rule, quarantine by rename — not deletion.
* **Reconcile:** make `index.ts` import from `converters.ts` so there is exactly one mapper, with the live field set, and the existing test then pins the real thing.

Reconciling is the better end state; quarantining is the cheaper one. Either is fine, but **leaving two is not** — the current state is a trap with a passing test on it.

## Acceptance

Exactly one `rowToApiKey` is reachable from production code, and a test pins it. If the reconcile route is taken, the test must assert `tenantId` and `connectorId` — the two fields whose absence is the whole finding.

title: packages/shared project tsc is RED on develop — crypto.JsonWebKey is gone in @types/node 26.1.0; a live type error no gate owns
description:
## BLUF

`packages/shared`'s **project** `tsc` reports **1 error** on develop, and no gate owns it.

```
src/crypto/jwks.ts(129,51): TS2694 — namespace 'crypto' has no exported member 'JsonWebKey'
```

`crypto.JsonWebKey` was removed in `@types/node` **26.1.0**. Found by the KS-843 round-3 gate.

## Not caused by the KS-843 work — measured

`git diff 59248bf38 e1d9d9380 -- '*packages/shared*'` is **EMPTY**. The toolchain moved under the shared install some time after 12:38; the source did not change.

## Why nothing caught it

The push preflight's twelve legs do not include a `packages/shared` project type-check, and the vitest suite is green (**709/709**) because vitest does not type-check. So this is red in `tsc` and invisible everywhere the team actually looks.

## Fix shape

Either import `JsonWebKey` from where `@types/node` 26.x now exposes it, or declare the shape locally (it is a small, stable JWK interface). Check whether the dependency bump was intended before pinning around it — an unintended `@types/node` major arriving via a transitive install is itself worth knowing.

## Acceptance

`npx tsc -p packages/shared --noEmit` exits 0 **with a planted-error control proving the check is live**; `packages/shared` stays 709/709; and the reason it went unnoticed is closed — either the preflight gains a shared project type-check leg, or a ticket says explicitly why it should not.

title: The audit log records `req.path` AFTER the response, so a REFUSED erasure is logged with the path trimmed to `/` instead of /api/gdpr/erasures
description:
## BLUF

`middleware/audit.ts` **gates** on `req.path` at entry but **reads it again inside** `res.on('finish')` — by which time express has left it trimmed to the mount-relative remainder. A **refused** erasure is therefore audited with the wrong path.

Found by the KS-843 round-3 gate. **Its own ticket, not KS-858's** — KS-858 is the path-normalisation class; this is a lifetime-of-`req.path` bug.

## Measured

| request | `req.path` at entry | `req.path` at `res 'finish'` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/gdpr/erasures` refused 403 | `/api/gdpr/erasures` | `/` |
| `GET /api/gdpr/erasures/:ref` refused 403 | `/api/gdpr/erasures/abc` | `/abc` |
| admitted requests | correct | **correct** |

Admitted requests are unaffected because the door's `req.url = original` restore runs on `next()`. A **refused** request never reaches that restore — the responding handler stops the chain — so it is logged with whatever express left behind.

## Where

`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/audit.ts`

* `:206` — gates on `req.path` at **entry** (correct)
* `:224` — inside `res.on('finish')`, calls `deriveAction(req)`
* `:108` — `deriveAction` reads `req.path` (**now trimmed**)
* `:280` — writes `details.path = req.path` (**now trimmed**)

## History

The degradation **began at round 2** of KS-843, when the gate became `router.use('/api/gdpr', handler)` — a responding `use` handler leaves `req.path` as `/erasures`. Round 3's inner-Router shape trims it one level further, to `/`. So this is a consequence of the KS-843 work, disclosed rather than left for someone else to find.

## Fix shape (the tester's, prose — no code was written)

Capture the path **once at entry** — `const auditPath = req.originalUrl.split('?')[0]` — and use that inside the finish handler. One line, and it fixes **every** `router.use(prefix, …)` gate in the file, not just this one.

## ⚠ Latent or live is UNMEASURED

The tester **did not run** `createAuditMiddleware` and could not determine whether `isDbAvailable()` is ever true on the demo. So whether these wrong paths are actually being persisted anywhere, or the middleware is inert, **is not known**. Establish that first — it decides the priority.

## Acceptance

A refused erasure is audited with `/api/gdpr/erasures` (and the GET with its full path), driven; admitted requests unchanged; the fix is at the capture point so other `router.use` gates in the file benefit.

title: Every ADMITTED erasure authenticates twice — the door's chain and the catch-all both run authenticateToken, doubling a remote key validation on a partner path
description:
## BLUF

On the erasure path an **admitted** request authenticates **twice**; a refused one authenticates once. Measured fresh by the round-3 gate across 14 shapes × 2 modes: **refused = 1, admitted = 2**.

Carried out of KS-861 when #845 merged, per the ruling that F-11 is a follow-up and not a gate item. **Not a live defect — a cost defect on a partner-facing path.**

## Mechanism

`services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts`:

* `:677` — the erasure door's chain carries `authenticateToken(true)`
* `:696` — the catch-all `router.use('/api/gdpr', authenticateToken(true), proxy('originate', …))` carries it again

An admitted request passes through the door, `next()`s, and hits the catch-all's copy. A refused one is stopped by the responding handler, so the second never runs — the correct direction, and why this is a cost issue rather than a correctness one.

## Why it matters

In production `authenticateToken` validates an `sk_` key **over HTTP** to the security service — `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:257` → `validateApiKey:209` → `POST /api/keys/validate`. So every admitted erasure doubles a remote call on a partner-facing path. It surfaces as latency, not as an error, which is why nothing has flagged it.

## Fix shape (from the round-2 tester)

Either the door's chain omits `authenticateToken` and relies on the catch-all's, or `authenticateToken` short-circuits when `req.user` is already set. **The second touches shared auth middleware and therefore every route** — it wants its own measurement rather than being folded in as an obvious win.

## Note on the round-3 fix

The F-9 fix (an inner express `Router`) was checked against this and **does not** close it for free — that was the stated condition for folding it into round 3, and it was not met.

## Acceptance

An admitted erasure invokes `authenticateToken` **once**, driven by counting invocations of an injected factory (the harness in `ks843-erasure-path-bypass.test.ts` already injects one); a refused erasure still invokes it once; guardrail behaviour and the 403/200 outcomes across the 14 shapes are unchanged.

title: connectorId is never persisted — svc_api_keys.connector_id is written by nothing and read by nothing, so it dies on restart; blocks KS-577 and nulls KS-843's cutover evidence
description:
## BLUF

`svc_api_keys.connector_id` **exists as a column and NOTHING in the security service ever writes it or reads it.** A key's `connectorId` lives only in the in-process `memApiKeys` map, from the moment it is minted until the service restarts. After a restart it is gone — and the boot loader cannot bring it back, because the row mapper does not map the column.

Two consequences, one of which lands on a ticket shipped today.

## Measured (static, with a control that fires)

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| the column exists | `migrations/018_svc_api_keys_reconcile.sql:79` — `ALTER TABLE svc_api_keys ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS connector_id TEXT` |
| nothing writes it | `dbSaveApiKey` (`services/security/src/index.ts:197`) — `connector_id` is **not** in the INSERT column list |
| nothing reads it | `rowToApiKey` (`:309`) — **not** mapped |
| anywhere in the service | `grep -n "connector_id" services/security/src/*.ts` → **0 hits**, against a control on `key_prefix` → **2 hits**, so the grep discriminates |
| memory is rebuilt from those rows | `loadFromDb()` (`:334`) warms `memApiKeys` from `svc_api_keys` through `rowToApiKey` |

`connectorId` is in the `ApiKey` interface (`:132`), set in memory at mint (`:985`), and returned by validate (`:1182` — `connectorId: apiKey.connectorId || null`). All in-process only.

## Consequence 1 — it blocks KS-577 (revoke-on-rotate)

KS-577 requires finding a connector's **prior** keys in order to revoke them on rotate. The only identifier tying sibling keys together is `connectorId` (`platform-s:<externalRef>`, set at `platform.ts` mint time). **There is no durable copy of it**, so after any restart of the security service the association needed to find the prior key does not exist in the database at all. KS-577 cannot be built on `connectorId` until this is fixed.

## Consequence 2 — it degrades KS-843's cutover evidence

Traced end to end:

```
security  /api/keys/validate  ->  connectorId: apiKey.connectorId || null      (index.ts:1182)
gateway   auth.ts:230         ->  meta.connectorId = data.connectorId || ''
gateway   auth.ts:272         ->  userId = `connector:${meta.connectorId || 'api-key'}`
gateway   auth.ts:281         ->  req.user.connectorId = meta.connectorId
scopes.ts (KS-843 grace log)  ->  connectorId: user.connectorId ?? null
```

**After a restart, every Platform S connector key validates with** `connectorId: null`**.** So:

* the `[KS-843]` grace-log line — the operator's *only* evidence for flipping `SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED` — records `connectorId: null`, and cannot say **which** connector was admitted;
* `userId` collapses to `connector:api-key` for every connector, so audit attribution loses the same distinction.

KS-843's cutover is stated as "flip to scope-only once the log shows S on the new key". **That log cannot show which key it is, after a restart.**

## Honesty about the evidence

This is a **static** read of the write path and the read path, with a grep control that fires. **I did not drive a restart and observe a null**, because that means restarting a container on the local stack while gates are running. The static chain is unambiguous, but it is not a driven observation and is not offered as one. Driving it is a ~10-minute job if wanted.

## Fix shape

Write `connector_id` in `dbSaveApiKey`'s INSERT (and in the `ON CONFLICT` set, since it is immutable per key it can be omitted there), and map it in `rowToApiKey`. The column already exists, so **no migration is needed**. Existing rows backfill as NULL — which is what they effectively are today, so nothing regresses; a backfill from any surviving source is a separate question.

## Acceptance

A key minted with a `connectorId` still validates with that same `connectorId` **after the security service restarts**, driven not read; `rowToApiKey` maps the column; the `[KS-843]` grace log names the connector after a restart; `userId` is `connector:platform-s:<ref>`, not `connector:api-key`. Then KS-577 becomes buildable.

title: Merge protocol: the server-side `sha=` pin protects the PR head, not the base — a 9-second race merged onto an unapproved parent and invalidated the gate's predicted tree oid
description:
## BLUF

**The merge protocol we were running could not enforce its own central assertion.** "Sha-asserted against a tip re-read in the same minutes" was executed via `PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/merge -f sha=…` — and **that** `sha` **pins the pull request's HEAD. There is no base parameter on that endpoint.** So the base could move between the assertion and GitHub executing the merge, and the merge would silently succeed onto a parent nobody had approved.

Measured, not theorised. This ticket is the record for the next reader; the fix is already ruled and in force.

## What happened (PR #852, 2026-09-06)

| time | event |
| -- | -- |
| 04:27:09Z | asserted `develop` = `81bf7b078`, exactly as the GO named |
| 04:27:18Z | **#848 (the other seat) merged** → `606aa385b` |
| 04:27:20Z | #852 merged onto `606aa385b`, **not** `81bf7b078` |

A **nine-second** window, with the protocol followed exactly.

## What it cost

**Nothing in content.** #848 touched only `.githooks/pre-push`; #852 touched only four `deployment/azure` files; `git diff --name-only 81bf7b078 af078257` returns all five, so both landed and the sets are disjoint.

**Something in evidence.** The gate's predicted merge-tree oid `82acc2da…` was computed against `81bf7b078` and is **not** the tree that exists — the real tree is `39acb349…`. A reviewer checking the merge against the predicted oid finds a mismatch and is right to stop. That is the actual damage: a correct merge that cannot be checked against its own gate's prediction.

## The ruling now in force (both seats)

1. Merge from **your own checkout**: `git ls-remote origin develop` → `git fetch origin develop` → `git merge --no-ff --no-edit <pr-head-sha>` onto `origin/develop` as read → `git push origin HEAD:develop`.
2. **No** `--force`**, no** `--force-with-lease`**.** A plain push already refuses a non-fast-forward, so **a base that moved turns a silent wrong merge into a refused push** — which is exactly the property wanted. On refusal: re-read, re-merge onto the new tip, push again, and **the receipt names both attempts**.
3. **Every receipt carries the base line:** `first parent = <sha>` beside `asserted = <sha>`. Equal → "base held". Different → name what landed, whether the file sets are disjoint (measured with `diff --name-only`), and that the gate's predicted tree does not apply.
4. A gate's predicted merge-tree oid is carried as **"predicted against base** `<sha>`**"**. A differing first parent invalidates the **prediction**, not the merge — re-derive `merge-tree` against the real first parent and name the new oid.
5. The server-side `PUT … sha=` shape stays acceptable **only for a seat merging alone**, which with two parallel seats is never.
6. **Serialising the seats was explicitly not ruled** — parallel stays. The mechanism above is what makes a lost race safe.

## Why this is filed rather than just fixed

The mechanism is already in force from the next merge. What a ticket preserves is the *reason*: a future reader seeing `PUT … sha=` in old receipts, or wondering why we push a merge commit by ref instead of using the API, needs the nine-second timeline above — otherwise the API call looks simpler and someone reintroduces it.

## Acceptance

No further build. Closed when the merge shape above appears in `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` alongside the existing merge-flow section, with the timeline as its justification.

title: check-no-latest-tags.sh silently skips a missing input — it scans 5 of the 6 files it advertises and still prints OK
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-latest-tags.sh` **cannot fail on one of the six files it claims to check**, and says nothing about it. A check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from a check that passed.

Found by the KS-490 (3) tier-2 gate on PR #852 — the same gate this script was used as evidence in, which is what makes it worth fixing.

## Mechanism

`CHECK_FILES` lists `.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml`. The script `cd`s to `Blockchain/Dev`, where that path **does not exist** (the workflows live at the **repo root**). Line 42's `[ -f "$f" ] || continue` skips it **silently**, and the gate prints `OK`.

**Scanned: 5 of the 6 advertised.**

## Why it matters here specifically

This script is on the push preflight and was cited as passing evidence on #852 — where its pass *was* meaningful, because the file under test (`main.parameters.json`) is one of the five it really reads. But the sixth has been unchecked for as long as the list has been wrong, and nothing in its output says so.

## Acceptance

A listed input that is missing is an **error**, not a skip — or the path is corrected to the repo root and the file is actually scanned. Either way the script **reports how many of the advertised files it examined**, so an examined-nothing run cannot read as clean. Same shape as KS-676, where a `mapfile` under bash 3.2 made a CVE scan examine 0 of 34 images and report clean.

title: The OAuth `AVAILABLE_SCOPES` list is a second, divergent scope vocabulary — derive it from SCOPES or pin it
description:
## BLUF

`packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts` declares itself the *"single source of truth … so the vocabulary can't drift between services"*. **That is true of the enforcement FUNCTIONS and false of the VOCABULARY.** `services/auth/src/services/oauth.ts:57` holds `AVAILABLE_SCOPES`, a **second hardcoded scope list that already diverges** — and the divergence has a live consequence for KS-843.

## Measured (KS-843 half-1 gate, PR #841 @ `4111f409ef9f69afeda78249125281476aca19d7`)

* `AVAILABLE_SCOPES` carries **four names that are not in** `SCOPES` **at all**: `verify:read`, `webhooks:manage`, `admin:read`, `admin:write`.
* It does **not** carry `subjects:erase`.
* **Nothing anywhere validates a scope string against** `SCOPES` **at runtime.** `requireScope(...)` takes free strings, so a typo'd or invented scope is simply a scope that never matches — silently.
* `scopes.ts:31-32` additionally claims *"the admin portal's API-key issuance UI reads from this array"*. **No frontend file imports** `SCOPES`**.**

## The live consequence, which is why this is filed rather than noted

**An OAuth app can never be granted** `subjects:erase`, because OAuth grants filter against `app.allowedScopes` / `AVAILABLE_SCOPES`. KS-843's cutover concerns `sk_*` connector keys only, so nothing is broken today — **but that limitation was discovered by a gate rather than stated by the design, and it should be said out loud.** If an OAuth-app caller is ever expected to perform an erasure, this list is the thing that will refuse it, and the refusal will look like a scope bug rather than a vocabulary one.

## Fix shapes (not chosen)

* **Derive** `AVAILABLE_SCOPES` from `SCOPES` (with per-scope consent copy alongside), so a new scope appears in both by construction; or
* **pin** it with a cell asserting the relationship between the two lists, so a divergence is a deliberate edit rather than an accident.

Either way the two claims in `scopes.ts`'s header that are currently false — the drift guarantee and the admin-portal import — should be corrected or made true. A header that overstates what a module guarantees is how the next reader stops checking.

## Related

* **KS-843** — the ticket whose gate surfaced this; its `subjects:erase` is the scope OAuth apps cannot be granted.
* The vocabulary now has a literal pin cell (added in KS-843 half 2) so a member cannot silently disappear from `SCOPES`. **This ticket is the other half of that problem: a member that never arrives in the second list.**

## Provenance

KS-843 half-1 tier-2 gate, finding F-3, verdict 2026-09-06T01:20:23Z, PASS. Both files are untouched by that PR — pre-existing, surfaced because the PR relies on the single-source-of-truth claim. Report: `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s138-ks843-841-half1-4111f409e/report.md` §F-3, read directly.

title: KS-386 residues from the round-2 gate: G-1 column ordinal drift, G-2 the second-image orphan, G-3 the in-memory docstring is wrong at the wire, G-4 two write spellings the guard cannot see
description:
## BLUF

Four Minors from the KS-386 round-2 tier-1 re-gate, none blocking. All four shipped as-is under the two-round cap — the gate PASSED and #839 merged as `b6ae609e6`. **This description is taken from the gate report's own findings section**, `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s138-ks386-839-regate-3b5a09403/report.md` §3, with its evidence file names; every fix-shape below is the report's, and the report marks all four *advisory only — no change was made by the tester*.

---

## G-1 · MINOR · A fresh-init schema and a migrated schema still differ: `user_id` and `created_at` are in **opposite ordinal positions**

**Oracle:** product, internal consistency. The claim under test was the builder's own — "the two shipped schemas now match the migrated one."
**Evidence class: MEASURED.** `pg_attribute` projection of both schemas, `evidence/cols-qa_i.txt` vs `evidence/cols-qa_mig.txt`, diff in `evidence/schema-diff-freshinit-vs-migrated.txt`:

```
  fresh-init (i)          migrated (mig)
  4|user_id|text|f||      4|created_at|timestamp with time zone|f|now()|
  5|created_at|…|now()|   5|user_id|text|f||
```

Sorted by name the two are **identical** — names, types, nullability, defaults, comment, both indexes. The difference is ordinal position only.
**Cause (read, not speculated):** `init.sql` and `docker/init/04` declare `user_id` *between* `mime_type` and `created_at`; migration 035 `ADD COLUMN`s it, so on a migrated database it lands last. No DDL reconciles the two short of a table rewrite.
**Blast radius:** nothing in the service is positional — the only INSERT names its columns and every read is by name. It bites anything comparing schemas structurally (a `pg_dump` diff, a drift detector, a snapshot test) or any future `INSERT … VALUES` with no column list, **which would write a** `user_id` **into** `created_at` **on one of the two shapes.**
**Falsifying tamper:** reorder `user_id` and `created_at` in `init.sql` to match 035's result and the ordered diff goes empty.
**Fix-shape:** accept and document the ordinal difference in the comment block that already explains the coupling, or move the `user_id` declaration in both shipped files to sit after `created_at`.

## G-2 · MINOR · A partial write leaves an orphan attestation, and the 500 says "No document was accepted" **when one was**

**Oracle:** explainability — "the most serious defect class is claiming something true that isn't."
**Evidence class: MEASURED**, driven on the tester's own copy of schema (i) with a trigger failing the **second** image only (`RAISE EXCEPTION` on `mime_type = 'image/jpeg'`, the back image).
**Repro:** schema (i) → install a constraint/trigger rejecting only the second INSERT → boot kyc at `3b5a09403` → initiate (bearer) 201 → `/document` with front PNG + back JPEG → `/selfie`.
**Observed:**

* `/document` → **500** `KYC_ATTESTATION_WRITE_FAILED` **— "No document was accepted."**
* `svc_kyc_images` holds **the front row anyway** (`data` NULL, `user_id` set) — *the message is false about the state it describes*. `dbSaveImage` is called once per image and each `query()` is its own autocommit statement; there is no transaction around the pair.
* `/selfie` then answers **200** `success:true` and writes **a second row**.
* `svc_kyc_verifications` for that subject: `documents` **IS NULL**, `liveness_completed` **true**. The record claims a completed liveness check for a subject whose document step failed, and two attestation rows exist that nothing references.

**Privacy or correctness?** **Correctness and honesty, not privacy.** The orphan rows carry `user_id`, so the KS-291 erasure path (`DELETE … WHERE user_id = $1`) still reaches them; nothing becomes undeletable and no payload is held. What is exposed is a compliance record asserting more than happened, and a client sentence that contradicts the database.
**Not introduced by #839** — the pair was untransacted before it too, and the builder named it without widening. What **is** new is the sentence "No document was accepted", now a specific claim the state can contradict.
**Fix-shape:** wrap the front/back pair in the existing `transaction()` helper — the orphan disappears and the sentence becomes true. **Regression test the owner should add:** drive `/document` against a DB that rejects the *second* insert, assert `count(*) = 0`, and assert `/selfie` does not then succeed.

## G-3 · MINOR · `dbSaveImage`'s "ONE HONEST LIMIT" docstring is wrong about the path this gate is about

**Oracle:** product — the code contradicts its own comment. **MEASURED** (two boots, driven) **and READ** (`index.ts:290-293`, `db.ts:125-147`).
The docstring, added by this diff, says *"when* `isDbAvailable()` *is false this returns early and writes nothing, and the route still answers 200."* Driven both ways into that state, the route answers **404** `NOT_FOUND` **"Verification not found"**, not 200 — `dbGetVerification` returns `undefined` before `dbSaveImage` is ever called, because nothing keeps verifications in memory.
**Why it matters even though reality is better than described:** this docstring is the written scope of F-1(b)'s exemption. A future reader will believe there is a live 200-with-no-row hole here and either chase it or, worse, treat a genuine one as already known.
**Also worth the owner's eye, pre-existing, not #839:** in that state `POST /api/kyc/initiate` still returns **201 with a** `verificationId` that is never persisted anywhere and 404s on the very next call.
**Falsifying tamper:** the finding *is* the tamper — boot with no `DATABASE_URL` and drive; a 200 from `/document` would refute it. **Fix-shape:** restate the limit as "the route 404s because the verification itself was never persisted", or delete the paragraph.
**Owned:** that sentence is mine, written in round 2 while trying to be explicit about a limit.

## G-4 · MINOR (carried from pass-1's H-b hunts, now louder) · The retitled cell claims "exactly ONE write path IN THIS FILE" while two spellings *in that file* are invisible

**Oracle:** explainability — a guard's title is a claim, and this one over-reaches.
**Evidence class: MEASURED.** Both planted in `index.ts` as **real payload writes**:

* `INSERT INTO "svc_kyc_images" (id, data, mime_type) VALUES ($1,$2,$3)` → **0 failed / 26**
* `INSERT INTO public.svc_kyc_images (id, data, mime_type) VALUES ($1,$2,$3)` → **0 failed / 26**

Both reader functions return `[]` on both. An `UPDATE` split across lines **is** caught (1 failed / 25), so the blindness is specifically about how the table **name** is spelled, not about whitespace.
F-2 as filed — the corpus overclaim — **is** closed. This is the residue: the docstring's "OTHER LIMIT" paragraph names the behavioural limit and the string-literal limit but says nothing about name spellings, and the retitle to "IN THIS FILE" makes the in-file claim stronger than the regex supports.
**Likelihood in operation: low** — nobody in this codebase quotes or schema-qualifies that identifier today, verified by `git grep -a`.
**Fix-shape:** match `(INSERT\s+INTO|UPDATE)\s+(?:"?public"?\.)?"?svc_kyc_images"?`, or name the spellings in the docstring's limits paragraph as the corpus limit is now named.

---

## Scope

One ticket, four items, product. G-3 is docs-only and can land with any of the others. G-1 and G-4 are decisions as much as fixes; G-2 is the only one with real design weight.

## Provenance

KS-386 round-2 tier-1 re-gate, verdict 2026-09-06T00:43:59Z, PASS, scored 1.0. #839 merged `b6ae609e6847b399ef695c9cd69fe1ef671693df`. Text from the report's §3 findings, read at `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s138-ks386-839-regate-3b5a09403/report.md`.
