title: Schemathesis baseline gate is unreachable: run.py skips it whenever the sweep fails — i.e. on every run it exists to triage
description:
## BLUF

**The Schemathesis baseline gate added by KS-256 (PR #782) ships inert: it is skipped on exactly the runs it exists to triage.** Not a regression — `develop` has no baseline gate at all — but the feature does not do what its own header claims until this is fixed.

## Mechanism

`systemTest/schemathesis/scripts/run.py:533`:

```python
if not success:
    Logger.warning("SKIPPED - upstream gate failed: report reconciliation and the "
                   "schemathesis baseline gate were not evaluated for this run.")
else:
    success = evaluate_report_reconciliation(OUTPUT_DIR)
    if success:
        success = evaluate_schemathesis_baseline(...)
```

`success` already carries the sweep's own outcome. So:

* sweep **fails** -> `success` False -> **baseline gate skipped** — but a failing sweep is the only thing the baseline has to triage;
* sweep **passes** -> gate runs -> nothing to triage.

The gate is unreachable in its own use case. The 97 accepted `check::operation` pairs in `config/schemathesis-baseline.json` therefore gate nothing as shipped.

## Measured

Run `pr-2026-09-02T07-06-54Z` against `custody/568-rebase` @ `8d7109411`: 10 failing operations, `Run validity: OK - 0 of 314 operations errored`, and then `SKIPPED - upstream gate failed`. The triage that would have classified all 10 as known never ran.

## Relationship to KS-256 QA F-5

F-5 (fixed in s105) made this skip **speak** — before it, the `and` short-circuit meant the gate silently never ran, which read exactly like a pass. That fix is why this is visible at all. It did not make the gate **reachable**.

## Fix

Evaluate report reconciliation and the baseline **eagerly** rather than behind `success`, and combine the verdicts afterwards. The existing code comment already names this as the tidier shape and records why it was deferred: *"a gate that fires on an INVALID run may not have the artefacts it reads, so that swap needs an invalid-run rehearsal this change does not have."*

So the work is: the eager swap **plus** an invalid-run rehearsal proving the baseline gate degrades safely when the artefacts it reads are absent or partial.

## Acceptance

A run with a failing sweep whose failures are all in the baseline must print the baseline gate's verdict, and a failing pair **absent** from the baseline must still fail the run — with a control proving the gate can fail (deliberately remove one accepted pair and confirm the run goes red).

Found in s106 while running the four suites for PR #782. Peter's triage input wanted on priority.

title: postcss-selector-parser 6.1.2 carries GHSA-w9m9-85wc-3x92 — baselined to unblock the preflight; the override was inert
description:
## BLUF

`npm audit` reports **GHSA-w9m9-85wc-3x92** (low) against `postcss-selector-parser@6.1.2`, which is not in the triaged baseline, so **the KS-380 pre-push preflight now refuses every push touching** `Blockchain/Dev` (gate 5/8). Accepted as a baseline entry to unblock; this ticket is the real fix.

## Where it comes from (measured, `npm ls`)

```
secuura@0.1.0 Blockchain/Dev
`-- @secuura/admin-dashboard@0.1.0 -> ./frontend/admin
    `-- tailwindcss@3.4.19
        |-- postcss-nested@6.2.0
        |   `-- postcss-selector-parser@6.1.2 deduped
        `-- postcss-selector-parser@6.1.2
```

Single path, one consumer: **tailwind's build-time CSS pipeline in the admin dashboard**. No backend service declares it. Tailwind runs at build; the admin image ships `dist/` behind nginx, so this code is never executed in a deployed runtime.

## The advisory

* Denial of service through uncontrolled AST recursion.
* Vulnerable `>= 6.1.0, < 6.1.3`; **first patched 6.1.3** (6.1.4 is current on the 6.x line). Also `>= 7.1.0, < 7.1.3` -> 7.1.3.
* Published 2026-05-26; low severity.
* Reachability requires feeding hostile CSS **selectors to our own build**, which is not an attacker-controlled input on this platform.

## Why it is baselined rather than fixed here

I tried the fix first, in the established shape — an `overrides` entry (`"postcss-selector-parser": "^6.1.4"`) beside the existing `postcss` override in `Blockchain/Dev/package.json`, which is the same toolchain and the same pattern KS-493 used.

**It did not take.** After `npm install --package-lock-only`, `package-lock.json` still resolved `node_modules/postcss-selector-parser -> 6.1.2`, so the override was inert — the same failure mode KS-185 records for the scoped `undici` override. Making it stick needs a real dependency-tree change (tailwind bump, or a nested override under `tailwindcss`/`postcss-nested`) plus a **frontend build verification**, which is not a change that belongs inside an unrelated error-handler PR. Reverted; `package.json` and `package-lock.json` were restored byte-identical (md5 vs `HEAD`).

Precedent for the baseline door: `undici` (KS-185) and `valibot` (KS-493) are both accepted in this file on exactly this reasoning — build/dev-tree only, never in a deployed runtime.

## What to do

1. Bump `tailwindcss` (3.4.19 -> current) and re-check, **or** add a nested override under `tailwindcss` + `postcss-nested`.
2. Verify `postcss-selector-parser >= 6.1.4` resolves in `package-lock.json` — not in `node_modules`, which `npm ls` reads and which is stale after `--package-lock-only`.
3. Build the admin frontend and confirm the CSS output is unchanged.
4. Remove the baseline entry; the preflight gate is the regression test.

## Discovered

2026-09-02 (s101), by the KS-380 preflight refusing the KS-727 push. Not caused by that change — the commit touches no `package.json` or lockfile (verified by `git show --stat`).

title: svc_api_keys.organization_id is not a tenancy boundary and nothing keeps it coherent with tenant_id — an incoherent pair is storable
description:
## BLUF

`svc_api_keys.organization_id` **is not a tenancy boundary and nothing keeps it coherent with** `tenant_id`**.** An incoherent pair — an org belonging to tenant B stored against `tenant_id` = tenant A — **is storable**, and RLS then resolves the row entirely in favour of `tenant_id`, because the policy never consults `organization_id`.

**Not a live escalation.** Post-KS-742 the application enforces tenancy on both `GET` and `POST /api/keys`, and DB-layer isolation is working as designed (measured below). This is an **integrity gap**: future code that treats `organization_id` as implying a tenant would be wrong, and nothing in the schema would stop it.

Raised by Peter on the KS-742 thread ("the org/tenant pair can be made incoherent … bounded, and unmeasured by me"). This is the measurement.

## Measured on LOCAL

**Constraints — read, not inherited. **`svc_api_keys` has exactly **one** constraint:

```
svc_api_keys_pkey | p
```

No foreign keys, no check constraint tying `organization_id` to `tenant_id`. `018_svc_api_keys_reconcile.sql` was read in full: it does ADD COLUMN, a backfill (`organization_id` → `organizations.tenant_id`), NOT NULL, an index and RLS — and **adds no constraint of any kind**. The backfill sets the pair coherently *once*; nothing holds it that way afterwards.

**Storability — proven, nothing persisted.** An INSERT of `{organization_id: <an org owned by tenant fd4254fd…>, tenant_id: a0000000-…-0001}` was **accepted** (`INSERT 0 1`) inside a transaction that then **ROLLED BACK**. Post-rollback control: rows matching the probe id = **0**. I used a rollback rather than a persisted write because it answers the same question and leaves no credential behind.

**What the GUC then shows.** The `tenant_isolation` policy keys on `tenant_id` alone:

```
(current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true) IS NOT NULL
 AND current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true) <> ''
 AND tenant_id::text = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true))
OR current_setting('app.tenant_scope_bypass', true) = 'platform_admin'
```

So an incoherent row is visible to **tenant A's** admins (its `tenant_id`) and invisible to **tenant B's** (its org's real owner). `organization_id` plays no part.

## ⚠ Two corrections to my own reading, recorded because they nearly became findings

**1. A** `qual=true` **policy that looked like a hole is not one. **`svc_api_keys` carries a second policy, `svc_api_keys_auth_lookup`, PERMISSIVE / SELECT / `qual=true`. Permissive policies are OR'd, so at first read that appeared to defeat tenant isolation for every reader. **It does not** — it is scoped to `roles={secuura_auth_lookup}`, a dedicated role, while `tenant_isolation` applies to `{public}`. Same pattern on `users` and `oauth_apps`. It is a correctly-scoped carve-out for the credential-lookup path, which must find a key by hash *before* a tenant context exists. **Recording it positively so nobody "fixes" it later.**

**2. My first RLS measurement was worthless.** I connected as `secuura` — `super=true bypassrls=true` — so RLS never applied and every count came back unfiltered. The control that caught it: `documents` (a single fail-closed policy, no auth-lookup policy) returned the same 95,015 with and without a dead tenant GUC, which is impossible if the GUC were filtering.

**Re-measured as** `secuura_app` (`super=false bypassrls=false`), with controls that fire in both directions:

| session | rows |
| -- | -- |
| no GUC | **0** |
| GUC = a nonexistent tenant | **0** |
| GUC = the default tenant | **480** |
| `app.tenant_scope_bypass = platform_admin` | **1165** |
| as `secuura_auth_lookup`, no GUC | **1165** (its policy, as intended) |

So the fail-closed policy is genuinely fail-closed for the runtime role, and the instrument can return non-zero — the 0s mean something.

## Fix shape (not done here)

Either a `FOREIGN KEY (organization_id) REFERENCES organizations(id)` plus a trigger or check asserting `tenant_id` matches that org's tenant, **or** an explicit decision that `organization_id` is descriptive metadata and never a boundary — written down where the next reader will find it. The second is cheaper and may be the right answer; what should not persist is the current state, where the field *looks* like a boundary and is not.

⚠ Adding an FK is not free: `organization_id` is NULL-able by design (018 §2, so the originate admin path can issue tenant-scoped keys with no org), and the s99 record notes demo held a synthetic org with no `organizations` row. Any FK needs that data cleaned first.

Filed session 100, KS-742 follow-up 6(b). No fix this session by instruction.

title: Spec drift: GET /api/security/keys declares no parameters while the handler requires organizationId — the contract suite can never reach its 200 branch
description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/security/keys` **declares NO parameters in the published spec, while the handler requires** `organizationId` **and 400s without it.** So every spec-driven caller — including Schemathesis — is steered into a 400 and **can never reach the 200 branch**.

That is not a cosmetic drift. It is why the KS-742 cross-tenant key-enumeration defect was invisible to the contract fuzzer: the vulnerable branch was unreachable by anything generating requests from the spec.

Raised by Peter on the KS-742 review thread (2026-09-01 13:11Z); he called it "probably its own ticket rather than widening this one". Re-measured here rather than inherited.

## Measured, on both surfaces

**Source** — `services/security/src/security.openapi.ts`, the `method: 'get'` registration for `/api/security/keys`:

* **no** `request:` **block at all**
* the string `organizationId` does **not** appear anywhere in the registration

**The served contract** — `GET http://localhost:6882/api/docs/openapi.json`, i.e. what a consumer actually reads:

```
parameters declared: NONE
responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 429, 500, 502, 503
```

**The handler** — `services/security/src/index.ts:915-919`:

```ts
const { organizationId } = req.query;
if (!organizationId) {
  return res.status(400).json({ success: false, error: { code: 'BAD_REQUEST', message: 'organizationId required' } });
}
```

So the contract says "no inputs", and the implementation says "one required input".

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

1. **It blinds the contract suite to this operation's real behaviour.** A generated call omits `organizationId`, gets 400, and the 400 is *declared* — so the run is green while the 200 path has never been exercised. Peter's read on KS-742 was that Schemathesis "would likely never reach the vulnerable branch", and this is the mechanism.
2. **A consumer cannot call the endpoint from the spec.** Anything generating a client from the published contract produces a call that always fails.
3. **It is a KS-663 instance** (nothing in CI stops the spec drifting from the code) with a concrete, measured consequence attached.

## Fix shape

Declare the query parameter on the registration — required, uuid-shaped — so the spec states what the handler enforces:

```ts
request: { query: z.object({ organizationId: z.string().uuid() }) },
```

Then confirm on the **served** spec (the gateway BIND-MOUNTS `secuura-api.yaml`, so it needs a container restart, not a rebuild) that `parameters` is no longer empty, and re-run the Schemathesis `pr` tier to see whether the operation's outcome changes.

⚠ **Do not simply relax the handler to make the spec true. **`organizationId` is load-bearing for tenancy after KS-742 — the fix is to declare it, not to drop it.

⚠ **KS-424 guard:** a new/edited operation needs an explicit `security:` block; this one already has `bearerAuth`, so no change there.

## What is NOT established

Whether declaring the parameter actually changes the Schemathesis result for this operation. That is a prediction, not a measurement — the current `pr`-tier failing set does **not** contain `GET /api/security/keys` (it is 8 M365 operations plus `POST /api/wallets/verify`), because the operation *passes* today by correctly returning a declared 400. Making it reachable could surface new findings on the 200 path. Worth expecting rather than being surprised by.

Filed session 100 from the KS-742 follow-ups.

title: Security events carry no tenant at all — KS-743 had to gate them platform-only, which is a workaround for the data model
description:
## BLUF

**Security events are authorised platform-only because they carry no tenant — not because platform-only is the right long-term answer.** KS-743 gated `GET /api/events` and `PATCH /api/events/:id/resolve` to platform roles. That is the only authorisation that is *true* of the surface today, and it is a workaround for a data-model gap.

## The gap, measured

* `SecurityEvent` (`services/security/src/index.ts:95-107`) has **no tenant field**: `id, eventType, severity, source, userId?, ipAddress?, details, resolved, resolvedAt?, resolvedBy?, createdAt`.
* `svc_security_events` (`migrations/002_verification-tiers.sql:536`) has **no tenant column**.
* `dbSaveSecurityEvent` (`index.ts:181`) INSERTs **eleven** columns — `id, event_type, severity, source, user_id, ip_address, details, resolved, resolved_at, resolved_by, created_at`. None is a tenant or an organisation.

So there is no `targetTenantId` to hand `decideTenantAccess`, which is exactly why the read could return the whole cross-tenant corpus to an ordinary tenant admin (measured before the fix on the local published gateway: **200,** `total: 651`).

## Consequence of the interim gate

A tenant admin can no longer see security events **for their own tenant either** — because there is no such thing as "their own" yet. That is a real capability loss, accepted deliberately over leaking every tenant's events. It is also invisible today: a sweep of `frontend/` found **zero** references to `/api/security/events` (control: **3** for `/api/security/audit`, which the admin dashboard does use), so nothing in the product currently asks for it.

## What the fix would involve

1. `tenant_id` on `svc_security_events` + a migration, with a decision on what to backfill existing rows to — they have no recoverable tenant, so a NULL/`unknown` sentinel and a policy for reading those.
2. `tenantId` on `SecurityEvent`, derived from the verified JWT at `POST /api/events` (the same server-derived shape `POST /api/audit` already uses at `index.ts:556-561`, deliberately never from the body).
3. Swap `requirePlatformOperator` for `decideTenantAccess` on the two read/write routes, keeping platform cross-tenant reach.
4. Producers: every internal caller of `POST /api/events` needs to be carrying a tenant-bearing token, or the sentinel path has to be defined for them. **Not enumerated here** — that sweep is part of the work, not of this description.

## Status of this description

Points 1-3 are a **design sketch, not an agreed plan**. Point 4 in particular is unmeasured. Whether events should be tenant-scoped at all, rather than remaining a platform-operations surface with a proper operator console, is the actual product question and is **open** — this ticket exists so that question is asked deliberately rather than inherited from a gate I added under time pressure.

Follow-up to KS-743 (PR #778). Filed session 100.

title: api-gateway audit export calls /api/audit/logs — a route the security service does not have, so the export 404s every time
description:
## BLUF

**The platform audit export can never return an entry: it calls a route that does not exist. **`services/api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts:138` fetches `GET ${SECURITY_SERVICE_URL}/api/audit/logs`, and the security service has **no **`/api/audit/logs` route.

## The mechanism

The security service publishes exactly three audit routes (`services/security/src/index.ts`):

* `POST /api/audit` (:546)
* `GET  /api/audit` (:594)
* `GET  /api/audit/:id` (:637)

So `/api/audit/logs` matches the `:id` handler with `id = "logs"`. No audit log has that id, so the handler returns **404** `{"code":"NOT_FOUND","message":"Audit log not found"}`. `audit-export.ts` then takes its `else` branch and answers the caller **404 carrying a** `BAD_GATEWAY` **code** — so the export surfaces as a gateway error rather than as an empty result.

The path looks like a leftover: `GET /api/audit` returns `{ data: { logs, total, limit, offset } }`, and `audit-export` reads `data.data || data.logs` — i.e. it is written for the **list** endpoint shape. The fix is likely one word, `/api/audit/logs` to `/api/audit`, plus reading `data.data.logs`.

## How it was found

Not by testing the export — by sweeping internal callers of `/api/audit/:id` before adding an authorisation gate to it under KS-743. The sweep asked "will my gate break a caller"; the answer was "this caller is already broken."

## Reachability — stated, not assumed

**UNMEASURED.** I have not driven the export end to end. This is read at `develop` `a079e1f6b` plus the route list in the same file; I did not establish which published gateway path reaches `audit-export.ts`, nor whether that path is itself shadowed the way `GET /api/audit` turned out to be. **That should be measured before severity is set** — the code defect is certain, the user-visible impact is not.

## Note for KS-743

KS-743 adds a tenant-less 403 to `GET /api/audit/:id`. That does **not** regress this caller: it forwards the end user own `Authorization` header, so a tenant-scoped user still reaches the handler — and it 404s today either way.

Filed from session 100 while working KS-743.

title: Gateway 500s on every proxied route for a token lacking verificationLevel — auth.ts:377 sets the header unguarded
description:
## BLUF

`api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:377` **sets a proxy header from an unguarded claim.** A valid-signature JWT that lacks `verificationLevel` makes the proxy throw `ERR_HTTP_INVALID_HEADER_VALUE` and return **500 carrying the internal message**, on **every proxied route** — not one endpoint.

**Latent, not live.** Filing it because the fix is two characters of the pattern already used on the line above, and because the 500 leaks an internal error string (the KS-703 / KS-727 shape).

## The code

```ts
if (decoded.organizationId) {
  req.headers['x-organization-id'] = decoded.organizationId;   // guarded
}
req.headers['x-verification-level'] = decoded.verificationLevel; // NOT guarded
```

Assigning `undefined` to a header is accepted by Express's header bag, then throws in node's http client when the proxy builds the outbound request:

```
TypeError [ERR_HTTP_INVALID_HEADER_VALUE]: Invalid value "undefined" for header "x-verification-level"
    at ClientRequest.setHeader (node:_http_outgoing:686:11)
    at Array.stream (http-proxy/lib/http-proxy/passes/web-incoming.js:126:74)
```

The caller gets `{"success":false,"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"Invalid value \"undefined\" for header \"x-verification-level\""}}`.

## How it was found, and the control that bounded it

Hit accidentally while building the KS-742 gateway re-measurement: I hand-minted an RS256 token without the claim, and **all** authenticated calls 500'd. The control that identified it as token-shape rather than route-specific: the **same token on** `/api/documents` produced the **identical** error, so it is not a property of `/api/security/*`.

## Why it is latent — measured, not assumed

`generateAccessToken` (`services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:159`) copies `verificationLevel: user.verificationLevel` straight off the user row. So the claim is absent exactly when the row's value is NULL.

* `users.verification_level` is **nullable** but carries `DEFAULT 'basic'`.
* **Local: 0 NULLs of 140 users. Demo: 0 NULLs of 30 users.**

So no user can currently trigger it, and an attacker cannot mint a token without the signing key. It becomes live only if a row is written with an explicit NULL — which the schema permits.

## Fix

Guard it the same way as the line above, or default it:

```ts
if (decoded.verificationLevel) {
  req.headers['x-verification-level'] = decoded.verificationLevel;
}
```

Worth pairing with a `NOT NULL` on the column since the default already exists. A regression test wants a token missing the claim driven at a proxied route, asserting it is **not** a 500 — and the test must be red against the current line, or it is pinning nothing.

## Provenance

Found and measured 2026-09-01 during the KS-742 published-surface re-measurement (session 99). Code read at `develop` `a079e1f6b`. NULL counts measured on local and on the demo VM the same session.

title: x-emitter-internal is unstripped on the /originate/ route — the marker's safety rests on an unstated convention, and the comment promises the wrong guarantee
description:
## BLUF

`x-emitter-internal` **is non-spoofable today, but for a reason nobody has written down — and the comment that *is* written down promises a different, weaker guarantee that does not hold on one live route.** No exposure now; this is a latent refactor hazard with a false assurance sitting next to it.

Three parts, one change: **strip it in originate's own middleware · a test that a client-supplied header never reaches anchoring · correct the comment.**

## What is true today (measured 2026-09-01, on #742's head `4ea49de47`, merged as `bb3bc5e78`)

`x-emitter-internal` marks K's own originate→anchoring hop so anchoring does not write a second provenance row for one user action (`anchoring/src/index.ts:470`, `const isInternalEmit = typeof req.headers['x-emitter-internal'] === 'string'`). If a client could set it, it would be a **client-settable switch that suppresses provenance recording**.

**It cannot today.** Measured:

* **One host ingress. **`nginx-gateway` publishes `0.0.0.0:6882->80`. `api-gateway` (8080), `originate` (4000), `anchoring` (4005) publish nothing.
* **No nginx route to anchoring at all** — the string `anchor` appears once in `nginx-demo.conf`, in a comment.
* Live, with controls: host→`localhost:4005/health` **000 no listener**; **CONTROL** host→`localhost:6882/api/docs` **301**; **CONTROL **`originate`→`http://anchoring:4005/health` **200 OK**. The zeros are a network boundary, not a dead service.
* `TRUST_HEADER_PATTERN` = `/^x-(user|tenant|organization|org|role|roles?|auth-user|policy|emitter)(-|$)/i` matches `x-emitter-internal` (offline, against `x-request-id`/`content-type` as non-matching controls).

## The gap

`nginx-demo.conf` proxies `location /originate/` **straight to** `$svc_originate`**, bypassing the api-gateway** — live: `GET /originate/health` → **200** — and originate mounts `app.use('/api/anchors', anchorsRouter)`.

So a client **can** get `x-emitter-internal` into originate **un-stripped**. The comment in `api-gateway/src/index.ts` says:

> *"Stripping it here is what makes the marker non-spoofable: internal calls bypass the gateway, so only they can set it — a client that sends it has it removed before any auth or proxy logic runs"*

That is **true of** `/api/*` **and false of** `/originate/*`.

**What actually protects the** `/originate/` **path** is an unstated convention: `originate/src/routes/anchors.ts` forwards to anchoring at `:282` and `:397` with explicitly constructed headers —

```js
headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...(userToken ? { Authorization: userToken } : {}) }
```

— with **no** `req.headers` **spread anywhere in the file** and **zero **`x-emitter-internal` references. Control: `req.headers` matches **11×** in `documents.ts`, so the grep discriminates and the absence is real.

**The hazard:** an ordinary refactor — `headers: { ...req.headers, 'Content-Type': … }` — silently turns the marker into a client-settable provenance switch. And the developer doing it would read the api-gateway comment and reasonably believe the edge had them covered.

## The work

**1. Strip in originate's own inbound middleware.** Apply the `TRUST_HEADER_PATTERN` set (not just `x-emitter-internal`) at originate's entry, so the property stops depending on every proxy path traversing the api-gateway *and* on a header-construction convention in one file. Defence in depth at the service that owns the marker's meaning. Mind the existing `x-tenant-override` allow-list — mirror the api-gateway's exemption rather than inventing a second policy.

**2. A regression test with both halves.** A client-supplied `x-emitter-internal` on `/originate/api/anchors` must **not** reach anchoring; **control:** the genuine internal hop's header **does** arrive and `isInternalEmit` is true. The control is the point — a test that only asserts the negative passes just as well against a service that has stopped talking to anchoring at all.

**3. Correct the comment in the same change.** State what is actually true: the edge strip covers `/api/*`; `/originate/*` bypasses it; the marker is protected at originate itself. The comment is the artefact that would mislead the refactorer, so leaving it while fixing the code would fix the smaller half.

## Priority

**Medium.** No exposure today and it is not a live defect — it is a latent hazard plus a documented false assurance. Filed rather than trusted because a recorded exclusion is a claim, and this one currently rests on a convention that no test enforces and a comment that describes it wrongly.

## Provenance

Found while discharging the pre-merge topology condition on **#742 / KS-566** (measurement posted as a PR comment there). Not fixed in #742 — that PR carried a reviewer's at-head approval and this is separate work.

title: Gateway mount-auth check scores authenticateToken(false) as green — six /api mounts satisfy neither leg of its own assertion
description:
## BLUF

**The KS-570 mount-auth check scores** `authenticateToken(false)` **as green, so six** `/api` **subtree mounts pass an assertion they do not actually satisfy.** Raised by Peter reviewing PR #730; **pre-existing on** `develop`**, not #730's doing and not its job to fix.** The fix is small — tag `authed` only when `required === true` — but the value is in whatever the retag then surfaces.

## Mechanism

`collectMounts`'s mock adds the middleware to `authTagged` regardless of the `required` argument, so `authenticateToken(false)` reads as `authed: true`. But `(false)` calls `next()` for a caller carrying no `Authorization` header at all (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:317-323`).

The guard's assertion is *"every /api mount either requires auth or is public by design with a stated reason"*. These mounts satisfy **neither** leg: they require nothing, and they are recorded in no by-design allowlist.

## The six, measured — not adopted

Measured at PR #730's head `3fe1b6f1a` (Peter's ref) and again on `develop 9b89f4fce`, comment lines excluded:

| mount | `proxy.ts` @ `3fe1b6f1a` | `proxy.ts` @ `develop 9b89f4fce` | state |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `/api/certifications` | 521 | 521 | **defended** — `attachScopes` + `requireScope('certifications:read','certifications:write')` follow |
| `/api/credentials` | 703 | 703 | straight to `proxy(...)` |
| `/api/referrals` | 786 | 777 | straight to `proxy(...)` |
| `/api/governance` | 875 | 861 | straight to `proxy(...)` |
| `/api/nft` | 892 | 878 | handler, then `proxy(...)` |
| `/api/billing` | 941 | 927 | straight to `proxy(...)` |

⚠ **A naive grep returns SEVEN on both refs.** The extra hit is a comment — the KS-442 note reading *"*`/api/credentials` *is already authenticateToken(false), its 401 came from the service"*. Excluding comment lines gives six on both refs, matching Peter's list exactly. Anyone re-running this should exclude comments or they will chase a mount that does not exist.

`/api/status` is deliberately **not** in this list: on `develop` it carries no auth middleware at all, and PR #730 gives it `authenticateToken(true)`.

## What is NOT established

**The anonymous-caller half is unmeasured.** Peter could not probe it (no Docker available to him) and inferred from the signature-only `authenticate()` in `@secuura/shared` that an anonymous caller would most likely 401 downstream. **That inference has not been tested and must be measured before any severity is stated on this ticket.**

Two things keep this below KS-570's severity, and it is worth being exact rather than alarming:

* the revocation check runs **before** the `required` branch, so when a token IS present, `(false)` does still catch a revoked session — the KS-570 class is genuinely covered by these mounts;
* five of the six go straight to a service that may well enforce its own auth.

## Done means

1. `collectMounts` tags `authed` only when `required === true`.
2. Each of the six is then either given real auth, or recorded in the by-design allowlist **with a stated reason** (the `/api/certifications` one is already effectively defended by `requireScope` and may only need recording).
3. **The anonymous-caller behaviour of each is measured, with a control**, before any of them is called safe.

## Two smaller notes from the same review, accepted for later, not fixed now

* `authed` is `layers.some(...)`, so it asserts the middleware is **present**, not **ordered before** the proxy.
* The `> 40` floor sits against a corpus of roughly 62, so it catches total collapse but not the loss of a third.

*Filed from PR #730's review (Peter's item 2), 2026-09-01. He offered to file it himself; filed from our notes at his suggestion since the probe setup is here.*

title: Verify results show the user nothing about what was registered — a renamed file confirms green with no explanation (PS-723)
description:
## BLUF

**A verify result shows the user nothing about what was registered, so a renamed file confirms green with no way to notice the rename.** Stuart hit this on PS-723 and ruled the direction: *"it should be explained to the user, otherwise confusion will result… b should also have the note to the user that the filename has changed."*

The API is not the problem — it already returns the registered `title`, `issuer` and `certifiedAt`. **The portal never displays them**, because it reads a nested shape the backend does not emit. And the portal already sends the presented filename, which the backend silently discards. So both halves of the comparison exist today and nothing joins them.

## RECOMMENDATION

Render the registered metadata beside the confirmation, plus a plain-language line that verification is **content-based** — a rename neither breaks nor fakes it. Where the presented filename differs from the registered title, say so explicitly rather than leaving the user to spot it.

One decision is **not mine and should be made before any code**: the flat-vs-nested contract question in §2. That is Peter's call.

## 1. What the verify response actually returns

Measured live, `POST /api/verification/verify` with `contentHash` — the path a renamed-file verify takes:

```
verified: true
title: "E2E Test Certificate"     <- the REGISTERED title
issuer: "demo"
documentType, status, contentHash, certifiedAt
certification: { certifiedAt, certifiedBy, certifierOrganizationId }
checks: { documentExists, hashValid, integrityVerified, ... }
```

So the metadata Stuart wants shown is already on the wire.

⚠ **The OpenAPI schema understates this. **`VerifyResponse` declares 20 properties and **none** is `title` / `originalFilename` / `registeredAt` / `registrant`; the live response carries `title` and `issuer` anyway. Same declared-vs-actual family as **KS-712** — worth fixing in the same pass so the contract stops lying about this endpoint.

## 2. Why nothing renders — the mechanism

`frontend/verifier/src/components/ResultPage.tsx:423` guards the entire "Document Details" card:

```tsx
{result.verified && result.document && ( ...Title... Issuer... )}
```

* The API returns `title` and `issuer` **at the top level** and emits **no** `document` **object** (measured top-level keys: `verified, documentId, title, documentType, status, contentHash, certifiedAt, issuer, blockchain, certification, checks, verifiedAt`).
* `result.document` is therefore undefined, the guard is falsy, and **the card never renders**.
* The portal references `result.document.*` **5** times and `result.title` **0** times. Control: `result.verified` matches **14** times, so the grep discriminates.
* The data is **not** lost in parsing — `VerifyResponseSchema` is `.passthrough()`, so the top-level `title` survives into the parsed object and is simply never read.
* The schema *does* declare `document: DocumentSummarySchema.nullable().optional()` carrying `title` + `issuer`. **The frontend was written against a nested shape the backend does not produce** — one side moved and the other did not.
* Confirmed on the path in use: all three verifier call sites hit **v1 **`/verification/verify`. v2 is a different shape entirely (`count, hash, matches, verifiedAt`) and the portal does not use it.

### The contract question — Peter's call, not to be decided in the fix

Either the **frontend reads the flat fields**, or the **backend nests them** under `document` to match the schema the client already expects. Both work; they differ in blast radius (the backend shape is consumed by the Outlook add-in and issuer too). Naming it rather than picking it.

## 3. `fileName` is already sent, and silently discarded

`frontend/verifier/src/components/VerifyPage.tsx:127` sends `{ contentHash, fileName: file.name }` and `:138` threads `fileName` into the result object. So the **client already holds both halves** of the comparison — presented name and registered title — and needs no new input to detect a mismatch.

Server-side, however:

* `VerifyRequest` declares only `documentId, hash, title, contentHash` — `fileName` **is not in the contract.**
* **No backend route handler reads it**: 0 files under `services/*/src/routes/` reference `fileName`, against a control of **8** referencing `contentHash`.

So the field is sent on every verify and thrown away. Either consume it (and declare it) or stop sending it — the current state is a silent no-op.

## 4. Scope — three surfaces, per Stuart, not just the verifier portal

His comment names them: *"This affects Outlook plug ins, and Verify functionality in 'Views' and directly from the menu."* Verify call sites in the tree:

| app | file |
| -- | -- |
| verifier portal | `frontend/verifier/src/components/VerifyPage.tsx`, `ResultPage.tsx` |
| **Outlook add-in** | `frontend/outlook-addin/src/utils/api.ts` |
| issuer portal | `frontend/issuer/src/services/api.ts`, `components/admin/ConnectorsPage.tsx` |

Whatever wording is agreed should land on all of them, or the same confusion simply moves to whichever surface is left out.

## 5. Design constraint — the KS-695 erasure interplay

**KS-695 item 2 brings** `documents.title` **INTO erasure coverage**, because S sends the real filename as `Title` on originate (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:407`). For S-originated documents that field **is** the original filename — exactly what this ticket wants displayed. Item 3 goes further: connector-scoped dissolution blanks all connector documents' titles.

So the two pull opposite ways: PS-723 wants the registered name shown; KS-695 makes that same field erasable PII that can legitimately be blank. Both are correct on their own terms.

**This must be specified, not discovered:** decide what a verify result shows for a document whose title has been erased — a blank, or an explicit *"registered name erased"* state. Rendering empty silently would recreate today's confusion in a new form.

## Not in scope here

No fix in this ticket — it is the specification and the evidence. No change to PS-723, which is Stuart's.

## Related

* **PS-723** — *Verify still confirms if filename has changed* (Stuart, 2026-09-01). The originating report and his ruling.
* **KS-712** — the declared-vs-actual spec gap this endpoint also exhibits.
* **KS-695** — `documents.title` erasure coverage; the design constraint in §5.

title: The e2e Playwright suite cannot run from a clean checkout — tests/e2e is not a workspace member and never gets installed; 20 of 82 fail once it does
description:
## BLUF

**The e2e Playwright suite cannot run from a clean checkout**, and that is why "Playwright — not run" keeps appearing in Test Evidence blocks. `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e` is **not a workspace member**, has its own `package-lock.json`, and nothing installs it — so `npx playwright test` dies at collection with `Cannot find module 'otplib'` and **the entire run aborts, including the specs that would have passed**.

Once you clear that by hand, **20 of 82 tests fail** on a healthy local stack. Neither fact was recorded anywhere: `BACKLOG.md` mentions Playwright once, unrelated (control: "schemathesis" appears 6x, so the grep discriminates).

This now matters more than it used to. With GitHub Actions retired, `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` maps every retired CI job to a local command the PR author runs as the final check — and this one does not work.

## RECOMMENDATION

Two parts, in order:

1. **Make the suite installable.** Either add `tests/e2e` to the root `workspaces` array (currently `packages/*`, `services/*`, `frontend/*`), or have the documented run command do `npm ci --prefix tests/e2e` first. It works today only by accident: the root tree happens to hoist `@playwright/test`, `dotenv` and `@types/node`, but not `otplib`.
2. **Then triage the 20.** They need an owner and a baseline, the way the Schemathesis failing set has one — otherwise the suite is unusable as a gate even once it runs, because nobody can tell a new failure from the standing 20.

## Detail — how it fails

```
Error: Cannot find module 'otplib'
   at auth-exhaustive.spec.ts:13
```

* `otplib` IS declared — `tests/e2e/package.json` devDependencies, `^13.4.0`.
* It is **not** in the root `package-lock.json` (control: `@playwright/test` is, 1 match).
* `tests/e2e/node_modules` did not exist. `npm ci` there installs 16 packages, 0 vulnerabilities, and touches nothing tracked (`**/node_modules/` is ignored at `Blockchain/Dev/.gitignore:8`).
* Playwright aborts the whole run on a collection error, so the two recruitment specs never executed either — the failure is not confined to the spec with the bad import.

## Detail — the standing 20 (measured twice, same set both times)

Run: `npx playwright test tests/auth-exhaustive.spec.ts tests/recruitment/happy-path-wallet.spec.ts tests/recruitment/alternative-paths.spec.ts`

**9 x** `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` **— basic login UI**
2.1.1 valid login (issuer) · 2.1.2 valid login (admin) · 2.1.3 session persists on reload · 2.1.4 logout redirects + cookie cleared · 2.1.5 login after logout · 2.2.1 wrong password shows error · 2.2.2 wrong email generic error · 2.2.3 empty email blocked · 2.2.4 empty password blocked

**1 x** `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` **— assertion looks wrong, not the app**
2.4.6 "SQL injection in registration name is sanitized" asserts the response body does not contain `drop table`, but registration **succeeds** and echoes `displayName` back verbatim. The payload is stored and returned as data, which is the correct behaviour; the test is asserting against an echo, not against an injection.

**5 x** `happy-path-wallet.spec.ts` — CIP-8 wallet auth via API · wallet-signed document certification · Lace connection flow · wallet-not-installed handling · transaction signing

**5 x** `alternative-paths.spec.ts` — AP-2 revoked credential · AP-3 privacy-blocked field · AP-4 tampered-document hash mismatch · AP-5 invalid wallet address · AP-5 invalid signature

## Not caused by KS-712 / #760 — controlled

Same three specs run twice on the same commit, changing only the served spec (the gateway bind-mounts it, so a restart publishes it):

| served spec | result |
| -- | -- |
| #760's widened spec | 20 failed / 62 passed |
| the pre-change spec at `26100e24f` | **20 failed / 62 passed — identical set** |

The test code is byte-identical between the two (my commit touches 0 files under `tests/e2e`), and the yaml was restored byte-identical afterwards (md5 `c5174ac31273e51f63bb22c03c32c402`).

One run showed a 21st failure — 2.3.1 registration returning 503 — which did **not** reproduce: re-run on the same commit and served spec, 3/3 pass including the two dependents that had been skipped. Transient, proven rather than assumed.

## Related

* KS-712 / #760 — where this surfaced; Peter's review made "run Playwright" a blocking requirement, which is what exposed that it cannot run.
* `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` — Manual CI-gate equivalents.

title: Security: 71 inline handlers still return err.message verbatim off-production — KS-727's enumerated remainder (api-gateway leaks it TWICE, at the edge)
description:
## BLUF

**71 response-side sites still return** `err.message` **verbatim unless** `NODE_ENV === 'production'`**.** KS-727 fixed the two *shared* handlers — `packages/shared/src/errors` (mounted by 12 services) and `services/auth`'s own — which was the high-leverage half. These 71 are per-route **inline** handlers: the same defect, a mechanical change, but 5 files across 3 services with their own test surface, so they were enumerated rather than folded into [#767](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/767>).

**Do api-gateway first.** It is the edge, and it is the worst of them.

## The remaining surface, measured 2026-09-01 after #767

| file | sites |
| -- | -- |
| `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts` | 46 |
| `services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts` | 15 |
| `services/originate/src/routes/systemErrors.ts` | 6 |
| `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` | 2 |
| `services/tokenisation/src/index.ts` | 2 |
| **total** | **71** |

## Why api-gateway is the priority

`services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:1065` and `:1072`:

```ts
const errorMessage = NODE_ENV === 'production' && statusCode >= 500
  ? 'An unexpected error occurred'
  : err.message;
res.status(statusCode).json({
  success: false,
  error: {
    code: errorCode,
    message: errorMessage,
    ...(NODE_ENV !== 'production' ? { details: { details: err.message } } : {}),
  },
});
```

It returns `err.message` **twice** — once as `message` and again as `details.details`. Because this is the edge handler, a caller can receive internal text **even where the downstream service handler was careful**. It also makes the `details` leak survive any fix that only touches `message`.

`:1063` includes `err.stack` in the **winston log**, not the response. That one is correct and must stay — noted because a naive grep counts it as a leak (it counted mine).

## The shape of the fix

The two shared handlers were fixed by deleting the ternary, because **they already log** `err.message` **and** `err.stack` **at entry** — the change was subtractive with no information loss. **Check that per site here**: an inline handler that returns the message *without* logging it would lose the detail entirely if the return were simply removed. Where a site does not already log, add the log in the same change.

The three affected services are consistent within themselves, so a per-service pass is likely cleaner than a per-file one.

## Done when

- [ ] `services/api-gateway` — both sites, including `details.details`. Separate, first, and worth its own review.
- [ ] `services/originate` — `adminConfig.ts` (46), `gdpr.ts` (15), `systemErrors.ts` (6). Consider a small local helper rather than 67 edited ternaries; that is a judgement call for whoever does it.
- [ ] `services/tokenisation` — 2 sites. Note it *also* mounts the shared handler, so it is already partly covered by #767.
- [ ] A test per service in the shape of KS-727's: assert a 500 body does not contain the thrown message across `development` / `demo` / `test` / unset, with a control that a typed client error still carries its own text.
- [ ] Re-run the sweep to zero — **excluding comments and logging lines**, which the naive grep counts (73 naive → 72 code → 71 response-side on the measurement above).

## Refs

* KS-727 / [#767](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/767>) — the shared handlers, fixed. This ticket is its enumerated remainder.
* KS-658 — the demo runs `NODE_ENV=development`, which is what makes every one of these the always-executing branch rather than a dev convenience.
* KS-703 / [#757](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/757>) — the thread that surfaced the class, with the two measured leaks (`invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0x00` and `role.split is not a function`).

*Filed 2026-09-01 (session 94) from KS-727's platform-wide sweep. Every count read off this tree in-session; no code written here.*

title: Upgrade ip-address off GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr (high, SSRF) — express-rate-limit 8.4.1→8.5.1+ in mcp-server, @meshsdk/@cardano-sdk 9.0.5 line in root + frontend/issuer
description:
## BLUF

`ip-address` **is on GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr (high, SSRF / trust-boundary bypass; patched in 10.3.1) in three lockfiles.** Two of the three are the *same* root cause and are a **patch-level bump of a different package**; the third is a `@meshsdk` major-version question. This ticket is the live owner of the audit-baseline exception for that advisory (`scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`, `GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr`), which now expires **2026-09-30**.

Filed at Peter's request on PR #738 (2026-08-31): the exception previously pointed at KS-559, which is **Done AND archived**, so on expiry the row would be orphaned again — the exact state KS-635 was filed about. KS-635 remains in `reason` as the deciding ref; this ticket is what `ticket` points at, and its due date is set to the row's expiry so the two cannot drift.

## The advisory

```
GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr  —  high
ip-address: Address4 decodes leading-zero octets as decimal while resolvers
decode them as octal, allowing SSRF and trust-boundary bypass
vulnerable: <= 10.3.0        first patched: 10.3.1        published 2026-08-03
```

## Where it actually is — measured, not inferred

Every `package-lock.json` outside `node_modules` was parsed for an `ip-address` entry:

| lockfile | resolved | vulnerable? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `services/mcp-server` | **10.1.0** | ✅ yes |
| root `Blockchain/Dev` | **9.0.5** + 10.4.0 (nested) | ✅ the 9.0.5 |
| `frontend/issuer` | **9.0.5** + 10.4.0 (nested) | ✅ the 9.0.5 |
| `packages/shared` | 10.4.0 | ❌ already patched |
| `services/anchoring` | 10.4.0 | ❌ already patched |

⚠ This corrects the review table on #738 in one place: root and `frontend/issuer` carry **both** 9.0.5 and 10.4.0 — the 10.4.0 copies are nested under `@cardano-sdk/dapp-connector` and `@cardano-sdk/key-management`, which already declare `^10.2.0`. Only the hoisted 9.0.5 is exposed.

## Leg 1 — `services/mcp-server`: a patch bump of `express-rate-limit`, not an `ip-address` override

```
services/mcp-server: express-rate-limit@8.4.1  declares  ip-address: "10.1.0"   <- EXACT pin
```

An `ip-address` override would violate that exact pin. But the pin moved upstream:

| express-rate-limit | declares |
| -- | -- |
| 8.0.2 – 8.5.0 | `ip-address: "10.1.0"` (exact — vulnerable) |
| **8.5.1 – 8.7.0** | `ip-address: "^10.2.0"` → resolves 10.4.0 ≥ 10.3.1 ✅ |

**So the fix is** `express-rate-limit` **8.4.1 → ≥ 8.5.1 (latest 8.7.0) — a patch/minor bump, no override, no major.** The path is already proven inside this repo: the root lock carries `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/node_modules/express-rate-limit@8.5.2`, which declares `^10.2.0` and resolves **10.4.0** today.

*(Instrument note: a first probe read* `express-rate-limit@10.1.0` *as having zero dependencies. It has none because **it does not exist** — the registry 404s it, against a 200 on 8.7.0. The "10.1.0" was the pinned* ip-address *version, not an express-rate-limit version. Corrected before it reached this ticket.)*

## Leg 2 — root + `frontend/issuer`: a `@meshsdk` / `@cardano-sdk` major question

```
node_modules/ip-address = 9.0.5
  declared by @cardano-sdk/core : ip-address ^9.0.5
  reached via @meshsdk/core-cst, @meshsdk/provider, @meshsdk/transaction
```

`^9.0.5` **cannot** reach the 10.x line, so no override satisfies the declared range. Newer `@cardano-sdk/core` — the copies vendored under `@cardano-sdk/dapp-connector` and `@cardano-sdk/key-management` in this same tree — already declare `^10.2.0`. **The fix is bumping** `@meshsdk/*` **so it pulls a** `@cardano-sdk/core` **on the 10.x line.**

This is the same `@meshsdk` family that owns the three **permanent** `undici` acceptances in the baseline (`GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524`, `GHSA-m8rv-5g2x-5cg5`, `GHSA-v3r7-h72x-cjcm`, all `frontend/issuer -> @meshsdk -> @utxorpc/sdk -> @connectrpc/connect-node`), and the family behind the multi-pinned `@lucid-evolution` packages on #720. Worth doing as one sweep rather than three.

## Exposure — stated honestly, not minimised

Not assessed in this ticket. The advisory is an SSRF / trust-boundary bypass in `Address4` parsing, and whether any first-party request path reaches it through `@cardano-sdk` has **not** been swept. The baseline row is a time-boxed exception precisely because that sweep was never done — do not read it as a bounded-exposure acceptance the way the `qs` row (KS-531) is.

## Scope

- [ ] **Leg 1:** `services/mcp-server` — `express-rate-limit` 8.4.1 → ≥ 8.5.1; regenerate the standalone lock **in** `node:24-alpine` (host regen drops optional binaries); confirm `ip-address` resolves ≥ 10.3.1.
- [ ] **Leg 2:** root + `frontend/issuer` — `@meshsdk/*` bump onto a `@cardano-sdk/core` 10.x; assess against the undici acceptances and #720's `@lucid-evolution` pins in the same pass.
- [ ] Re-run `node scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs` and `node scripts/audit/audit-gate.mjs` — both must exit 0 **with the** `GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr` **baseline row removed**, which is the real done-state.
- [ ] Remove the row from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`. Its expiry (2026-09-30) is this ticket's due date; if the work slips, the date moves **here** and on the row together, with a reason — never silently.
- [ ] Second instance of the same pattern, out of scope but named: `GHSA-q8mj-m7cp-5q26` (`qs`) is owned by **KS-531, also Done and archived**, expiring 2026-11-11. Flagged on 2026-08-21 and again by Peter on #738. It needs a live owner before that date.

## Refs

* KS-635 — the deciding ref for the date move (`reason` field on the row)
* KS-559 — original owner, **Done AND archived**; lineage only
* PR #738 — the date alignment 2026-08-31 → 2026-09-30 that this ticket unblocks
* KS-531 — the `qs` twin of this pattern
* Advisory: [https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr](<https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr>)

*Filed 2026-09-01 (session 94). Every version figure above was read out of the lockfiles and the npm registry in-session, with a firing control on each instrument.*

title: test:pr never re-imports the OpenAPI spec, so Akto scans a collection that has drifted from it — a declared operation is not a scanned one
description:
> **Origin.** Parked on [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) comment `718362a9` (2026-08-28T22:30:04Z) under "Related, found today and unfiled for the same reason" — `issueCreate` was refusing workspace-wide. Filed 2026-08-29. **No new measurement was taken for this ticket**; the numbers are the ones recorded on 2026-08-28 against PR [#762](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/762>).

## BLUF

**Declaring an operation in the OpenAPI spec does not put it in Akto's scan collection. **`test:pr` does **not** re-import the spec — only `test:pre-merge` runs `feed-har` — so the collection Akto scans drifts away from the spec silently, and a PR that adds operations gets an Akto result that never touched them.

This is the [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) premise reaching one step further than that ticket states it. KS-712 says: an operation absent from the spec is invisible to both tools. This says: an operation **present** in the spec can still be invisible to Akto.

## Measured

On PR #762, which declares four operations (`GET`/`PUT` on `/api/privacy/settings` and `/api/settings/notifications`):

| operation | occurrences in the Akto report |
| -- | -- |
| the two endpoints #762 declares | **0** |
| control endpoint A | 105 |
| control endpoint B | 7 |

The two controls are what make the zero readable: the report was produced, it was parsed, and it does contain occurrence counts — the declared endpoints simply are not in it. Without the controls, `0` and "the grep could not have matched" are the same reading.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a note

The failure is **silent and it points the wrong way**. An author who declares a new operation, runs `test:pr`, and sees no Akto finding on it will reasonably conclude the operation was scanned and is clean. Under the current wiring that conclusion is unsupported: the operation was never in the collection. Every "Akto clean" claim in a Test Evidence block on a spec-adding PR carries this caveat, whether or not the author knows it.

This sits directly against the merge flow adopted 2026-08-25, where the **Test Evidence block carries the testing claim**. A block that says "Akto FAIL 3, none on a touched route" is true and still misleading if the touched routes could not have been scanned.

## Not fixed, and why

Re-importing the spec into Akto **mutates harness state** — the collection is shared, and @PeterObeden has live work on it ([KS-717](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-717)). Doing it unilaterally mid-review would corrupt someone else's measurements to fix a reporting gap. It belongs with the harness owner, alongside [KS-716](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-716).

## Possible shapes (for whoever owns it — not a design commitment)

1. Have `test:pr` re-import when the spec's hash has changed since the last import — cheap, and the common case is no change.
2. Fail `test:pr` loudly when an operation touched by the diff is absent from the collection, rather than reporting a clean scan of it. This is the honesty-guard shape already used elsewhere in the harness.
3. Leave `test:pr` alone and have the Test Evidence template require the author to state Akto collection coverage explicitly, so the gap is visible rather than assumed away.

Option 2 is the one that fails closed, but it is the harness owner's call.

title: A scan that logs in more than ten times as one user revokes its own bearer — the 10-session window evicts the token it is scanning with
description:
> **Origin.** Parked on [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708) comment `276249e8` (2026-08-28T16:09:12Z) §3, where it was found while answering a different question and had nowhere to go — `issueCreate` was refusing workspace-wide. Filed 2026-08-29. **No new measurement was taken for this ticket**; the numbers below are the ones recorded in that comment, on that date, on the local stack.

## BLUF

`GET /api/sessions` returns a **rolling window of the caller's 10 most recent sessions, and evicting a session invalidates it**. So any scan that logs in more than ten times as the same user **destroys the bearer it started with, mid-run** — and every request after that answers:

```
401 {"success":false,"error":{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"Session has been invalidated"}}
```

with a 90-byte body. This is not a BOLA and not an authorization defect. It is a **harness-integrity defect**: it makes an authenticated scan silently stop testing anything while still producing results.

## Why it matters more than it looks

A scan that has lost its credential does not fail loudly. It produces a full run of uniform 401s. Downstream that reads as:

* a clean run with nothing to report (false zero), or
* a wall of "findings" that are all the same 401, or
* a similarity score computed by diffing two 90-byte 401 bodies against each other.

**It already produced a wrong answer once, in the run that found it.** The first control pass on KS-708 reported `/api/auth/me` at 16.95% and `/api/sessions` at 3.23% — which reads as "the whole stack is noisy, the finding is meaningless". Both numbers were **void**: the token had been evicted by this mechanism, so the comparison was between 401 bodies. It was caught only because *the control collapsed together with its subject* — a control that agrees with the thing it is controlling is telling you the harness moved, not the subject. Re-run below the eviction threshold, the control holds flat at 99.20% and the readings are valid.

## Measured behaviour

* The window is pinned at **10**; contents rotate. After 6 logins, 4 of the baseline's 10 session ids were retained and 6 were new.
* Eviction **invalidates** the evicted session — it is not merely hidden from the list.
* Threshold in practice: \~10 logins as one user. The KS-708 probe run performed \~30 logins across two accounts and crossed it.

## Why this is a scan-trust ticket, not a session-management one

The 10-session cap is plausibly intended behaviour (bounded session growth per user), so this ticket does **not** propose changing it. What it proposes is that the harness stop being silently broken by it:

1. ✅ **Done — PR** [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1336](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1286-akto-2356-honest-coverage-paced-tiers-stall-stop-and-slot-safe-cba284970402) **(**[KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and)**), merged 2026-09-28, commit** `f3fb25e3e`**.** Akto harness: each tier asserts its own credential survived the run (`assertCredentialAlive`, counting results whose response says "Session has been invalidated"); a run that lost it is an error, never a pass. Items 2 and 3 remain open. **Assert liveness of the scan credential.** Before trusting any authenticated run, assert the bearer still answers 200 on a cheap authenticated control (`/api/auth/me`) at the END of the run as well as the start. A run whose credential died is `error`, never `pass`.
2. **Do not re-login per request.** A scan that reuses one token cannot evict itself; one that logs in per iteration will, within ten iterations.
3. **Or scan as more than one user** so no single account's window is exhausted.

Which of the three is right is a harness-design call, not a finding — sizing belongs with whoever owns the Akto/Schemathesis runners.

## Relationship to the flakiness class

This is a strong candidate contributor to the false-zero / intermittency class tracked on [KS-709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-709) (Akto reports a PASS for a test that executed nothing) and [KS-696](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-696) (Akto pr-scan is non-deterministic). **Candidate, not cause** — no run has been attributed to it after the fact, and doing so would need the credential-liveness assertion in item 1 to exist first. It is deliberately not being claimed as the explanation for either ticket.

## Provenance

Local stack only. `secuura-auth` had been rebuilt that session from `develop` `e126a241b` and content-proved free of unmerged branch code. Two accounts used (`demo@secuura.io`, `issuer@secuura.com`), same role and same tenant. Cost: \~30 logins creating session rows and evicting older ones via the documented cap. All reads were GETs. No writes to any document, anchor or chain. Nothing on demo.

title: Declare the remaining ~157 routed-but-undocumented /api operations in the OpenAPI spec — the KS-712 remainder
description:
> **Origin.** Assembled from the measurement parked on [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) comments `ae3aab1a` (the 173-op survey) and `4b388b0b` ("the remaining ~157 operations are being sized as their own ticket"), on 2026-08-28 when `issueCreate` refused workspace-wide. Filed 2026-08-29 once creation worked again. **No new measurement was taken for this ticket** — every number below is the one already recorded on KS-712 and is dated to that run.

## BLUF

KS-712 established that **173 routed** `/api` **operations are absent from the OpenAPI spec**, which makes them invisible to both Schemathesis and Akto. Two slices of that gap have since been declared:

| slice | ops | where |
| -- | -- | -- |
| MFA · wallet-auth · social sign-in | 16 | [#760](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/760>) |
| the two settings PUTs (+ their GETs) | 4 | [#762](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/762>) / [KS-719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-719) |
| **this ticket — the remainder** | **~157** | not started |

This is the mechanical bulk of the gap. It was deliberately not attempted in the KS-712 pass: *"That is a large mechanical change and wants its own PR and its own review; flagging the scope rather than half-landing it."*

## Shape of the remainder (from the KS-712 run, 2026-08-28)

Of the 173 routed-and-undocumented operations:

* **By method:** GET 83 · POST 64 · DELETE 12 · PUT 11 · PATCH 3. **90 of 173 are write methods** — the half that matters most for an untested surface.
* **By area: **`/api/admin` 58 · `/api/auth` 14 · `/api/users` 11 · `/api/workflows` 8 · `/api/anchors` 8 · `/api/platform` 7.
* **Unauthenticated response:** 401 ×149 · 400 ×8 · 200 ×15 · 204 ×1.

Subtracting the 20 already declared, the remainder is dominated by `/api/admin` (58 operations, none declared) — a single area worth about a third of the whole job.

## Suggested order

The dependency order recorded on KS-712 was MFA → wallet-auth → social callback → the rest; the first three are done. For the remainder, largest-coherent-area-first keeps each PR reviewable:

1. `/api/admin` (58)
2. `/api/users` (11) + `/api/platform` (7)
3. `/api/workflows` (8) + `/api/anchors` (8)
4. the long tail

## Constraints that apply to every slice

* **KS-424 guard:** every new operation needs an explicit `security:` block, or `check:openapi` fails.
* **The gateway BIND-MOUNTS** `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` — a spec change is published by *restarting* the gateway container, not by rebuilding an image. Verify the served spec, not the file on disk.
* Declaring an operation does **not** put it in Akto's scan collection — see the sibling ticket on `test:pr` never re-importing the spec. A slice of this work is only "covered" once both tools actually exercise it.
* Each slice will widen the Schemathesis failing set. Record the failing **set**, diff it against the previous run on the same instrument, and classify new entries rather than counting them.

## Two things this ticket is NOT

1. **Not a decision about behaviour.** Where declaring an operation would bless behaviour that has not been ruled on, split it out — that is exactly what happened with the two unauthenticated PUTs, which became KS-719 rather than being documented as-is.
2. **Not a total.** 173 is a floor, not a count: **60 of 105** `/api` **mount bindings did not resolve** to a defining file (dynamic mounts, re-exports, barrel files), so those services are counted only where they register absolute paths. The CI guard proposed on [KS-663](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-663) — assert every routed `/api` path appears in the spec — is the only thing that turns this from a survey into a number that stays true.

## Sizing

**Peter-sized, and deliberately routed to him** — this is mechanical spec authoring across ~157 operations in at least four PRs, on a surface he originally reported. Not a one-session job and not a job worth interleaving with security findings.

## Method (for the numbers above)

Recorded in full on KS-712 comment `ae3aab1a`: route registrations extracted from each service's **compiled** `/app/dist` **in the running container** (not parsed TypeScript — static parsing undercounts by 34% because a third of registrations are named exports), mount bindings resolved precisely rather than cross-producted, then **every candidate probed against the live gateway**, with the probe as the arbiter. `/api/docs/*` excluded as a Swagger catch-all that answers 200 on any nonsense path; the control that catches it is one nonsense path per prefix.
