title: The whole super-admin surface is silently unscanned — no system_admin block means the HAR replay fallback never fires (0 of 16 endpoints, incl. KS-694's GDPR routes)
description:
## BLUF

Every **super-admin-only** endpoint is invisible to Akto on a stock local checkout, and nothing says so. `config/secrets.yml` carries no `system_admin` block — `config/secrets.example.yml` documents one — so `resolveReplayTokens()` returns `adminToken: null`, the issuer→admin fallback never fires, and each endpoint `ISSUER_ADMIN` cannot get a 2xx from stays a spec-imported placeholder (`responseCode: -1`) that `api_selection_filters` excludes from **every** BOLA/BFLA/authz template.

The bias is the problem: the endpoints that are hardest to authenticate to are the privileged ones, so the harness systematically skips the surface where an authz defect matters most — and reports green.

## Measured — 2026-08-29, local slot-1 stack, Akto 2.22.2

```
collection 56068490 "OpenAPI Secuura API": 323 endpoints
  absolute (scannable)  : 307
  relative (unscannable):  16

endpoints scanned, BOLA run:
  relative : 0 / 16
  absolute : 46 / 80 sampled     <-- discriminating control
```

The 16 that never get scanned:

```
/api/admin/audit/export      /api/analytics/activity        /api/analytics/certifications
/api/analytics/governance    /api/analytics/overview        /api/analytics/revenue
/api/analytics/users         /api/analytics/verifications   /api/audit-log
/api/billing/customers/by-email  /api/gdpr/consent/check    /api/gdpr/deletion-log
/api/m365/callback           /api/oauth/authorize           /api/onedrive/files
/api/system-errors
```

The 7 `analytics` paths are excluded on purpose (`VOLATILE_PATH_RE`, KS-357). **The other 9 are not excluded by anything — they are simply unreachable by the replay persona.** They include `/api/gdpr/deletion-log`, `/api/gdpr/consent/check` and `/api/system-errors` — the exact routes **KS-694 (Urgent)** just put a role gate on, and `/api/oauth/authorize`.

Note the tell: an unscannable entry is stored as a bare path (`/api/audit-log` — the tenant-provisioning upstream path) while a scanned one is a full gateway URL (`http://localhost:6882/api/documents`). That difference is a cheap, reliable detector.

## Proof of causation

Adding the documented `system_admin` block to local `secrets.yml` (gitignored; seeded `admin@secuura.com`, per `secrets.example.yml`):

```
captured 2xx samples : 71 → 79
audit-log in api_info: /api/audit-log  →  http://localhost:6882/api/platform/audit-log
ADD_USER_ID on it    : 0 rows → 1 row
```

That change is what made **KS-708** reproducible at all. Before it, `ADD_USER_ID` reported *"188 tested, 0 vulnerable"* while never touching the endpoint under investigation.

## The documentation understates it

`secrets.example.yml:30-34` says `system_admin` is *"optional. Only needed to seed the locked-account test-role… Absent ⇒ that one role is skipped (best-effort), and* `AUTH_BYPASS_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_TOKEN_ROLE` *keeps skipping honestly."*

That is not the whole consequence. Absent, it also removes the entire super-admin surface from HAR replay, and therefore from every similarity-based authz template. Nobody reading that comment would expect it.

## Suggested shape

1. **Warn loudly when** `adminToken` **is null** — name the count of endpoints that will consequently have no 2xx sample. Silence is the actual defect; a skipped endpoint should never be indistinguishable from a clean one (the KS-700 / KS-709 principle, applied to coverage rather than results).
2. Correct the `secrets.example.yml` comment to state the coverage consequence.
3. Consider failing `test:setup` when the block is absent, or defaulting it to the seeded local admin.

## Done means

1. A run without a system-admin token says so, with the affected endpoint count.
2. `secrets.example.yml` states the real consequence.
3. The relative-vs-absolute URL split is asserted somewhere, so this cannot silently regress.

title: Akto reports a PASS for a test that executed NOTHING — 'clean 0 / not-applicable 969 ✓' is a second false-zero axis that richCaptureFailed does not catch
description:
## BLUF

**KS-700 closes one false-zero axis and this is the other one.** On @PeterObeden's 2026-08-28 review run, `analytics: code injection` returned **clean 0 · not-applicable 969** and reported **✓**. The capture *succeeded* — so `richCaptureFailed` is correctly false — and the scan still measured nothing that actually executed. A green tick on zero executed requests.

⚠ **Provenance: Peter's measurement from his** `test:security` **run, not independently reproduced here.** Filed so the class is tracked rather than living in a PR thread.

## ✅ Done so far — PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1336](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1286-akto-2356-honest-coverage-paced-tiers-stall-stop-and-slot-safe-cba284970402) ([KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and)), merged 2026-09-28

These sections are delivered; the ticket stays open for criteria 1 and 3 below.

* ✅ **A 429 result is no longer scored as a pass** — its own `rateLimited` bucket (it was 79% of a full scan's "passes"); COVERAGE DEGRADED when refusals outnumber what executed.
* ✅ **A zero-run report says NO COVERAGE** instead of "0 vulnerable" (the `-t` filter case in Kamil's comment).
* ✅ **Pacing** so the platform's limiter no longer decides coverage — 0 of 50,306 full-scan results refused (open decision on the platform side: [KS-1374](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1374/akto-scans-are-now-paced-to-fit-the-platforms-rate-limit-test-times)).

## Why KS-700's fix does not cover it

KS-700 distinguishes *"asked Mongo and got nothing"* (`richCaptureFailed`) from *"never asked"*. Both are about the **capture**. This is a third state the capture cannot see: **the capture worked, and what it faithfully reports is that nothing ran.** `clean 0` with `not-applicable 969` means every candidate was filtered out before a request was sent — so the ✓ attests to an empty set, not to a clean one.

Read the way a reader naturally reads it, *"analytics: code injection ✓"* means the endpoints were tested and were fine. It means neither.

`DEV-PROCESS.md` already says an Akto PASS should be read as *"nothing was reported"*, not *"nothing is there"* — this is the sharpest instance of why.

## Suggested shape

Treat **executed == 0 with a non-zero candidate count** as its own verdict, the way `richCaptureFailed` is — not PASS. Something like `NO COVERAGE — 969 candidates, 0 executed`, failing or warning per tier. The count is already computed: `executedResultCount(breakdown)` in `src/scan/runTiming.ts`, and `clean + vulnerable` is the executed figure.

Note the same shape appears in the aggregate: this session's `test:pr` runs report `not-applicable 3281` and `not-on-stack 360` against `clean ~803` — so roughly 80% of every run is filtered before a request is sent. That is not necessarily wrong, but nothing currently asserts a floor on it.

## Done means

1. A scan where a whole test category executes nothing does **not** report ✓.
2. ✅ **Done** — a control: a category that genuinely executes and is clean still passes (so the fix is not "fail everything"). Shown live on slot 2, 2026-09-28: `clean 140 · rate-limited 0` reported PASS three times in the same run.
3. Reproduced from a real run, not only a unit test — the [KS-700](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-700/akto-harness-prints-a-false-zero-when-its-mongo-capture-fails-no) review's own standard.

title: No table references `users`: 0 of the database's 29 foreign keys point at it, across 52 user-reference columns — KS-697 was this hole being exercised
description:
## BLUF

**No table in the platform database has a foreign key to** `users`**.** Not one — across **52** columns named `%user_id` / `%holder_id` / `%_by_id`. The schema *does* use foreign keys (**29** of them), which is what makes this a gap rather than a deliberate house style.

Every one of those 52 columns can therefore hold a uuid that references nobody, and nothing in the database will object.

## Measured — live local DB, `develop cc65abad5`

| measure | value |
| -- | -- |
| foreign keys in the database | **29** |
| of those, pointing at `users` | **0** |
| columns named like a user reference | **52** |
| FKs on `shares` (any) | **0** |
| FKs on `custody_events` | **1** — `document_id` only |

The `custody_events` row is the tell: that table *does* carry an FK, on `document_id`, and `to_holder_id` sits beside it without one.

## Why this is being filed now

[KS-697](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-697) was exactly this hole being exercised: `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` accepted an invented `newHolderId`, returned 201, and **minted an anchor** for a custody chain pointing at a user that has never existed. That route is fixed in application code ([PR #751](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/751>)) — but the fix is one handler, and the underlying condition covers 51 other columns.

Known second instance, unfixed: `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` format-checks `recipients[].userId` (KS-536) but **never checks it exists** — `shares.recipient_user_id` is cast to `::uuid` and inserted with no FK behind it. Lower blast radius than custody (no ownership flip, no anchor), but the same class.

## Not a "just add the FKs" ticket

Recording the reasons up front so whoever picks this up does not discover them the hard way:

1. `users` **is** `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` **fail-closed** (migration 039). FK validation runs as the referencing statement's role, so adding FKs to an RLS-forced table needs thought about which role validates the reference and whether the tenant GUC is set at that moment. This is the KS-458 surface.
2. **Multi-tenancy may put** `users` **in a different database** from the referencing table under the per-tenant-DB model — a cross-database FK is not expressible. That has to be established per table before anything is added.
3. **Existing rows may already violate** what a new FK would assert. KS-697 alone wrote several on local. Any `ALTER TABLE … ADD CONSTRAINT` needs a survey first, and `NOT VALID` + a later `VALIDATE` is probably the shape.
4. **A count guard will lie here. **`users` under FORCE RLS returns 0 rows to a non-superuser without the tenant GUC — an "are there orphans?" query can read clean on a table full of them. Set `app.tenant_scope_bypass` before counting.

## Suggested first step

Not a migration. An **inventory**: for each of the 52 columns, which are genuinely user references, which live in the same database as `users`, and how many current rows are already orphaned. That survey decides whether this is one migration, several, or an application-layer rule instead.

Found during KS-697, 2026-08-27. Filed separately so it does not die when that ticket closes.

title: Akto pr-scan is non-deterministic — three runs on near-identical code gave 1 HIGH / 1 HIGH (different endpoint) / 0 HIGH
description:
## BLUF

**Three Akto** `test:pr` **runs tonight, same harness, same command, gave three different answers — and none of the three carried a captured request or response.** A gate that answers differently on identical input cannot be read either way: its PASS is not evidence of absence, and its FAIL is not evidence of a defect until re-derived by hand.

## Measured — 2026-08-27, all three within ~20 minutes

| run | target | HIGH |
| -- | -- | -- |
| baseline (s76) | `develop ca5b643e0` | **1** — `BOLA / ADD_USER_ID` on a **GDPR** route |
| KS-694 fix branch | `develop` + the KS-694 role-gate fix (touches `gdpr.ts` + `systemErrors.ts` only) | **1** — `BOLA / ADD_USER_ID` on `GET /api/documents` |
| 17-PR integration stack | `develop cc65abad5` + 17 open PRs | **0** — `verdict: PASS`, 804 clean, 2 known-FP |

The middle run is the one that rules out "the code changed": that branch touches two route files and cannot have introduced or removed a finding on `/api/documents`.

## The `/api/documents` finding does not reproduce

Derived by hand rather than trusted:

* `?userId=` **injection changes nothing.** The identical document set comes back with no `userId`, with another user's, and with a third user's.
* **Cross-tenant isolation holds.** A default-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN` sees 18 documents, an oxford-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN` sees 70, **full-id overlap 0**. (An earlier probe of my own appeared to show a shared document — that was an 8-character id truncation in my script, not a leak. Recording the false alarm so nobody re-derives it.)

## Why this matters now

Since 2026-08-27 the four local suites are the **only** merge gate (Kam: *"billing will not be fixed"*). Akto is one of the four. **Two of tonight's three runs would have produced a different merge decision on the same code.** That is the same failure mode `KS-519` names for permanently-red checks, arriving from the other direction.

## Related, already known

`KS-694` came out of the first of these runs — the finding was real but its **label** (`BOLA / ADD_USER_ID`) was wrong, and re-deriving it produced a more precise and more serious defect. Same pattern: the scanner points at something; the label and the endpoint are both unreliable.

## Suggested next step

Establish whether the variance is in the scan (endpoint sampling / timing / auth state) or the reporting, by running `test:pr` N times against a frozen commit with the stack untouched between runs, and recording the HIGH set each time. **Not started** — filed so tonight's measurement is not lost.

title: S↔K (K-side): erasure by external_ref, documents.title coverage, and connector-scoped org erasure — PS-690 dependency
description:
Platform-S is adopting org-owned documents with non-destructive user deletion and org dissolution ([PS-690](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-690/adopt-org-owned-documents-ownership-model-for-single-vs-multi-user), accepted plan on that ticket). Its S→K erasure bridge ([PS-701](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-701/ps-690-phase-6-sk-erasure-bridge-lifts-the-gates), Phase 6 — the only K-dependent phase) needs three K-side changes. Everything else in [PS-690](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-690/adopt-org-owned-documents-ownership-model-for-single-vs-multi-user) proceeds without K; S records pending erasures durably and a sweep converges once these land.

## Context

S holds **no K** `users.id` — the per-user credential tier was removed in [PS-465](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-465/s-adopt-k-connector-keys-provisioning-key-per-organisation) phase 4 (`PlatformKAccount` dropped). The only per-user link S has is `Person.PersonGuid`, which K already receives as `onBehalfOf.externalRef` on every attributed write, and which K's own erasure deliberately **retains** while blanking email/displayName. The org-level identity is the connector `platform-s:<OrganisationGuid>` with the once-only operational `sk_` key.

## Asks

1. **Erasure addressable by** `external_ref`**.** K's GDPR erasure route is keyed on `users.id`, which S cannot supply. Accept `external_ref` as the subject key (resolving to the same `executeErasure` path), idempotent, with a status read so S's retry sweep can converge without double-executing.
2. `documents.title` **in erasure coverage.** S sends the real filename as `Title` on originate (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:407`); K's `executeErasure` anonymises `documents.metadata`, `certification_metadata` and `owner_did` but not `title`, so real filenames survive erasure. Include title blanking for the subject's documents. Worth doing regardless of [PS-690](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-690/adopt-org-owned-documents-ownership-model-for-single-vs-multi-user).
3. **Connector-scoped (organisation) erasure for dissolution.** For `connectorId platform-s:<OrganisationGuid>`: blank the org display name and all connector documents' titles, revoke the operational key (S supplies the `svc_api_keys` id it holds in `PlatformKKeyId`), retain anchored hashes and the graph (S anchors explicit `action=delete` events for every document before calling this — [KS-389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-389/k-confirm-deleterevoke-semantics-for-ssd-soft-delete-clarification-for) semantics, never `/revoke`). Idempotent + status endpoint; S drives it from a resumable state machine and will retry until Confirmed.

## Sequencing

Lands on top of the [PS-319](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-319/sk-consistent-organisationuser-ownership-dr-credential-reconciliation)/[KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) connector-key model ([KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) currently In Review). S's Phase 6 ([PS-701](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-701/ps-690-phase-6-sk-erasure-bridge-lifts-the-gates)) is the only consumer and is gated on this ticket — until then S refuses dissolution of K-registered orgs at preview, deliberately, so no dangling K-side state can be created.

title: M365 routes answer 503 when ENTRA_* is unconfigured — 9 permanent Schemathesis failures on every dev machine, and the local sweep is now the merge gate
description:
## BLUF

**Four M365 operations answer** `503 Service Unavailable` **when** `ENTRA_*` **is unconfigured, and a 503 is a server error — so every Schemathesis run on a normal dev machine records 9 failures that are configuration, not defects.** This is the KS-478 / KS-451 / KS-431 "raw 5xx instead of a clean refusal" family, and it now matters more than it did: since Kam retired GitHub Actions on 2026-08-27, the local Schemathesis run **is** the merge gate, so a permanent 9-failure floor makes that gate unreadable.

Found on the first run under the new final-check rule — develop `ca5b643e0`, full 32-service stack, auth re-seeded, run validity OK (0 of 307 operations errored).

## The failures

`9 failures, 3 warnings in 72.21s` — all `Server error`, all the same body:

```
[503] Service Unavailable
{"success":false,"error":{"code":"SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE",
 "message":"M365 integration not configured",
 "details":{"setup":"Add Microsoft 365 Business Basic license and configure ENTRA_* env vars"}}}
```

Operations:

| operation |
| -- |
| `POST /api/m365/connections/init` |
| `POST /api/m365/connections/complete` |
| `POST /api/m365/connections/{id}/refresh` |
| `POST /api/m365/documents/sync` |

Reproduce (from the report):

```bash
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"organizationId":"e3e70682-c209-1cac-a29f-6fbed82c07cd","tenantId":"84fe882e-d558-4800-892d-eb967ea4a232"}' \
  http://localhost:6882/api/m365/connections/init
```

## Why this is a defect and not just "configure your env"

**A missing integration credential is a known, permanent, expected state on every developer machine and in CI — it is not an unexpected server fault. **`503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` says "the server broke or is overloaded, retry later". Neither is true: the server is healthy and retrying will never help until someone buys an M365 licence.

The service already knows exactly what is wrong — it returns a precise, actionable `details.setup` string. It has all the information needed to answer honestly and chooses a 5xx anyway.

This is the same reasoning the team already accepted for KS-478 (`raw 5xx on POST /api/governance/delegate … instead of a clean business refusal`). The only difference is that this one is triggered by configuration rather than by input.

## Options

1. `501 Not Implemented` — the literal meaning: this server does not support this function. Declares in the spec, is not a server error, and Schemathesis will not flag it.
2. `400`**/**`422` **on the call** — treats "no connection configured" as a precondition failure like every other precondition in KS-478.
3. **Do not mount the routes at all when** `ENTRA_*` **is absent**, so they 404 like any unmounted feature. Cleanest, but changes the published surface conditionally, which the OpenAPI contract work (KS-663) would need to account for.

Whichever is chosen, **the response must be declared in the OpenAPI spec** or it will simply move from a `server_error` failure to a `status_code_conformance` failure.

## Interim, so the gate is usable today

Until this is fixed the four operations should be registered as by-design tolerated in `systemTest/schemathesis` (the KS-662 / KS-518 guard pattern) **scoped to these four operations by name and to the 503-when-unconfigured case only** — not a blanket 5xx tolerance. Without that, every author running the mandated final check sees 9 red and has to learn to ignore it, which is precisely how a gate stops working.

## Provenance

Schemathesis `pr` tier, develop `ca5b643e0`, 2026-08-27T08:50:44Z, seed 2899853179.
Report: `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/pr-2026-08-27T08-50-44Z/`.

title: Security: /api/status revoke/unrevoke has no tenant ownership check — an ISSUER_ADMIN in any tenant can revoke another tenant’s credential (KS-586’s deferred half, now untracked)
description:
## Summary

`POST /api/status/:id/revoke` and `/unrevoke` enforce an **admin-class role** but **no tenant ownership check**. An `ISSUER_ADMIN` in one tenant can revoke or un-revoke a credential in **another tenant's** status list. Reproduced live on `develop 576ebef85`.

This is the **second half of KS-586**, which fixed the role gap and explicitly deferred the tenant gap — but **KS-586 is now** `Done`**, so nothing tracks the remainder.** That is why this ticket exists.

## ⚠️ What is already FIXED — read this before working the ticket

**KS-586 is done and its fix is live. **`/api/status` is no longer "no authorization at all". Anyone picking this up from a summary of [KS-570](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-570) will be looking for a defect that is not there.

| probe (local, `develop 576ebef85`) | result |
| -- | -- |
| `holder@secuura.com` (**OWNER**, non-admin) → revoke | **403 **`Role OWNER is not authorized for this action` |

The role gate at `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/status.ts:42-53` (`STATUS_WRITE_ROLES`, applied as a router-level gate ahead of the route table) works. Commit `bda40c91c` on `develop`, present in the running container.

## The defect that IS live — reproduced, controls both ways

Two `ISSUER_ADMIN`s in **different tenants**:

* `demo@secuura.io` — tenant `default`
* `registrar@oxford-test.invalid` — tenant `oxford`

| # | actor | request | result |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | demo (owner) | `POST /api/status` create list | **201** |
| 2 | demo (owner) | `POST /api/status/:id/allocate` `cred-xtenant-probe` | **200**, index 0 |
| 3 | **oxford registrar (foreign tenant)** | `POST /api/status/:id/revoke` that credential | 🔴 **200** — `{"revoked":true,"reason":"cross-tenant probe"}` |
| 4 | demo (owner) | `GET /api/status/:id/revoked` | **200** — `{"revokedIndexes":[0],"totalRevoked":1}` — the write really landed |
| 5 | **control** — oxford registrar | revoke against a **non-existent** list id | **404 **`Status list not found` |
| 6 | **control** — holder (OWNER) | revoke the same list | **403** (role gate) |

**Controls 5 and 6 are what make row 3 mean something.** Row 5 proves the 200 was a genuine authorisation pass and not a blanket accept — the same foreign caller is refused when the target does not exist. Row 6 proves role is still evaluated, so the only thing missing is the tenant comparison.

## Root cause

`services/vc-issuer/src/routes/status.ts`. The router-level gate checks **role only**:

```ts
return requireRole(...STATUS_WRITE_ROLES)(req, res, next);
```

There is no comparison of the caller's tenant to the status list's owner — **because the status list has no owner to compare to.** Status lists live in a process-local `Map` with no tenant linkage. The code says so itself (`status.ts:35-38`):

> *"Tenant scoping is NOT enforced here yet: status lists live in a process-local Map with no tenant linkage, and the ownership model is the KS-539/KS-547/KS-586 joint authorization decision — tracked on KS-586."*

**"tracked on KS-586" is no longer true.** KS-586 is `Done` (2026-08-12) and KS-547 is `Done`; KS-539 is open but scoped to *governing rules for document operations by agents*, not status-list tenancy. The deferral outlived its tracker — which is the actual reason this went untracked for two weeks.

## Why this is not a duplicate

* **KS-586** — `Done`. The **role** half. Fixed.
* **KS-570** — the **authentication** half: the gateway mount at `proxy.ts:702` has no `authenticateToken`, so revoked-session JWTs still pass. Different layer, still open.
* **KS-588** — `Backlog`. **Test coverage** for `/api/status` authorization. Would catch this once it exists; is not the fix.
* **This ticket** — the **tenant/ownership** half. No ticket held it after KS-586 closed.

## Severity

**High.** Revocation state is an integrity operation on a document-authenticity platform — an attacker with any admin-class role in any tenant can un-revoke a credential their victim revoked, or revoke a live one. Same family as [KS-643](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-643) (cross-tenant API-key revoke) and [KS-642](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-642), and it sits on the same **KS-621 tenancy boundary** that is currently held for @kamil.kreiser's design ruling.

Not raised to Urgent: exploitation needs a valid admin-class credential in *some* tenant, so it is privilege-escalation-across-tenants, not anonymous.

## Suggested fix — NOT implemented, deliberately

The ownership model is a **KS-621 boundary decision** and is @kamil.kreiser's call, exactly as with KS-643. Filing only, per the same hold.

The prerequisite is structural: **a status list must carry an owning tenant before any check can be written.** The process-local `Map` has nowhere to put one, so this is not a middleware one-liner — it needs the list persisted with a tenant column, which is likely the same decision as KS-539's ownership model.

Note the interlock, learned from KS-578/KS-643: adding a tenant check **without** giving lists an owner would refuse every caller, since no list has a tenant to match.

## Reproduction

Local stack, `develop 576ebef85`, both accounts seeded. Full curl sequence is rows 1–6 above. Probe artefacts were written to the **local** stack only (`ks661-tenantprobe-*`); status lists are process-local and clear on a `vc-issuer` restart. **Nothing was written to demo.**

Handed over by @peter on KS-570 (2026-08-26 08:10Z): *"The one still open is the /api/status authorisation gap … I will let you file that one too, as you hold the evidence for it."* — filed with the measurement rather than the paraphrase, which is how the KS-586 half turned out to be already fixed.

title: Anchor-status standoff: a consumer repolls anchors K reports as terminally failed — K's labelling is already honest (KS-587), so the fix is terminal-state handling, not a new K signal
description:
## BLUF

**The standoff is real, but its stated mechanism is wrong — and measuring demo inverted the ownership.** The premise going in was *"K reports simulated anchors as* `confirmed`*; Platform S's honesty rule refuses a* `mock_tx_` *hash; S repolls forever."* Measured on demo tonight, **K does not report them as confirmed.** All 83 simulated anchors on demo are flagged `simulated = true`, `status = failed`, carrying the explicit error `KS-587: simulated placeholder — never on chain; marked …`. **Zero rows on demo are** `simulated = true` **and** `confirmed`**.** K already fixed this — that is what **KS-520 → KS-522 → KS-587** were.

So the accurate statement is: **a consumer is polling anchors that K reports as terminally** `failed`**, forever.** That is not a labelling defect on our side. It is a missing terminal-state rule on the consumer side.

## Recommendation

1. **Layer 1 — the actual fix, PS-side (Stuart's):** treat `status: failed` as **terminal** and stop polling. No new K signal is required; the one already published is sufficient and has been since KS-587 deployed.
2. **Layer 2 — K exposes** `simulated` **machine-readably: ALREADY DONE. This is a no-op, closed here, and no work should be raised for it.** Verified in the **shipped** demo image, not just the source tree.
3. **Layer 3 — env hygiene (Stuart's call):** whatever is polling demo from `52.74.18.212` should not be pointed at demo at all.
4. **Layer 4 — per-environment Blockfrost keys:** still open, still pending the credential question below.

## Detail — what was measured, on demo, read-only

**Demo is not simulating.** `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` is **absent** from the anchoring container's environment (0 matches against a 22-line env, so the read itself is proven). Boot logs: `Cardano integration active — real blockchain anchoring enabled`, `cardanoMode: "REAL (Blockfrost)"`, network `preview`.

`anchor_store` **composition — 285 rows total:**

| shape | `simulated` | `status` | n | first | last |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| real 64-hex | false | **confirmed** | **194** | 2026-07-08 | 2026-08-14 |
| `mock_tx_*` | **true** | **failed** | **83** | 2026-07-31 | 2026-08-01 |
| NULL | false | failed | 6 | 2026-07-11 | 2026-08-05 |
| real 64-hex | false | failed | 2 | 2026-08-04 | 2026-08-10 |

Crosstab, stated plainly because it is the whole argument: `simulated = true` appears **only** with `status = failed`. **There is no (**`simulated = true`**,** `confirmed`**) row on demo.** Controls: `simulated` is never NULL (0 of 285); totals reconcile 194 + 83 + 6 + 2 = 285.

**The loop's corpus is fully resident on demo — the cross-instance hypothesis is dead.** All **71** distinct anchor ids the loop requests are present in demo's `anchor_store`: **71 present / 0 absent**. Controls both fired: a fabricated id `anchor_0000…0000` matched **0**, a known-real id matched **1**. So these anchors were minted **on demo**; they were not minted on a simulated instance elsewhere and verified here.

**And every one of them is a failed anchor:**

|  | n |
| -- | -- |
| `simulated = true`, `failed`, mock hash | **68** |
| `simulated = false`, `failed`, NULL hash | **3** |
| **confirmed** | **0** |

That is the finding. The loop is polling **71 anchors that can never succeed**, 68 of which K has explicitly labelled as simulated placeholders that were never on chain.

**The** `simulated` **flag is machine-readable, and it ships.** In the **running** demo image (`/app/dist/index.js`, and `docker inspect` shows **no bind-mounts**, so the image *is* what serves):

* `...(simulated ? { simulated: true, simulatedTxRef: rawTxHash } : {})` — 3 emit sites
* `verified: !txView.simulated && anchor.status === 'confirmed'`
* a placeholder hash is moved to `simulatedTxRef` and `transactionHash` is set to **null**, so a mock hash is never presented as a transaction hash

Control: a nonsense token grepped for in the same file returned 0. Source agrees (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts` `honestTxView`, `anchoring.openapi.ts` `simulated: z.boolean().optional()` + `simulatedTxRef`).

**The Blockfrost split — both "zero Blockfrost calls" and "quota exhausted" are true at once.** They describe **different routes**:

| route | behaviour | last 60 min |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /api/anchors/{id}` | **pure DB read**, ~1 ms, no Blockfrost | **1,970 × 200** |
| `GET /api/anchors/verify/{hash}` | **live Blockfrost** | **608 × 200 · 460 × 500** |

**457** of those 500s carry Blockfrost's own string `"Usage is over limit."` (against 3,935 total anchoring log lines). So Stuart's agent's *"zero Blockfrost calls in two hours"* is **correct for status GETs** — that is exactly what they observed, and it is a real property of the code. Our *"quota exhausted"* is **correct for verify-by-hash**. Neither observation refutes the other; the earlier reconciliation hypothesis (creation-simulated / verify-live) was the right shape but the wrong axis — it is **status-read vs verify-by-hash**, not creation vs verification.

**Traffic, for scale.** Last 6 h at demo's edge: **23,515 requests from** `52.74.18.212`**, of 23,515 total — 100.0%** of demo's inbound. Split: `POST /api/verification/verify` 11,620 · `GET /api/anchors/{id}` 9,704 · `GET /api/documents/{id}` 2,190 — **all 200 at the gateway.** ~3,919/hr, consistent with the ~3,850/hr measured on KS-670 across 08-14 → 08-21.

## Attribution, corrected gently

Stuart's agent read the honesty rule as **S's**. The record says the honest-labelling rule was implemented **in K**: **KS-520** (Urgent, Done) — anchoring fabricated a `tx_sim_` hash and marked the document anchored under `SIMULATE_ANCHORING`; **KS-522** (High, Done) — a simulated anchor presented as genuinely verified, no honest-labelling signal; **KS-587** (High, Deployed to UAT) — *"84 demo anchors carry* `mock_tx_` *hashes but are flagged* `simulated=false` *+ confirmed"*. KS-587 is the direct ancestor of this ticket: it found **84** mis-flagged rows and remediated them. Tonight demo holds **83** rows carrying its remediation message. **The defect Stuart's agent describes is one K already found and fixed** — which is worth saying clearly, because it means no K change is needed and the polling behaviour is unaffected by anything we ship.

Credit where due: their diagnosis of the *mechanism* — a consumer refusing a mock hash and retrying forever — is correct and is what made this tractable. Only the direction of the labelling defect was off, and their own caveat (which K instance they queried was unstated) is what prompted the measurement that found it.

## What their numbers describe

Their **1,638 anchors, all simulated** is **not demo** — demo has **285** anchors, of which 83 are simulated. Since all 71 polled ids resolve on demo, the polling target is demo; the 1,638-row instance they inspected is a different K (most likely one of the local development stacks). **Not asserted, and it does not change the finding:** the fix is terminal-state handling regardless of which K holds the larger simulated corpus.

## Still open

* **The credential question, unanswered since 2026-08-20:** does the local K stack hold **demo's** Blockfrost key or its own? If demo's, per-environment key scoping becomes the durable fix, and Kintsugi (its own free-tier project per environment) is the working precedent.
* **The Blockfrost allowance *period* is still unverified** — nothing here should be sized on a 50k/day assumption.

## Provenance

* Demo measurements | read-only SSH to `secuura02-demo-vm`, 2026-08-21 10:26–10:40Z | container env, `docker logs`, `psql` SELECTs, and one `docker inspect`. **No writes, no config change, no key action, no restarts.** Two scratch files created under the VM's `/tmp` during extraction were removed in the same command.
* Loop corpus | demo nginx gateway logs, 6 h window | two of my own extraction patterns were wrong on the first pass (`doc_` vs `doc-`, and verify hashes ride in the POST body rather than the URL); both corrected before any figure here was written down.
* KS-520 / KS-522 / KS-587 / PS-522 | live Linear reads, 2026-08-21 | `PS-522` returns nothing; `KS-999` used as a not-found control.

title: Published Anchor.id is anc_… but anchoring only ever mints anchor_<uuid> — format-false, live on develop, and #568 promotes it to the canonical fixture
description:
## BLUF

**The published** `Anchor` **example carries an id in a format the anchoring service has never minted, and #568 is about to make that format the canonical fixture.** The service mints `` `anchor_${randomUUID()}` ``; the spec publishes `anc_…`.

This is the **fourth** instance of the class KS-665 keeps surfacing — a published value that is *plausible* but *false*, which the guard **certifies rather than catches** because the value sits in the fixture set (after 16 `address` fields, `userAgent`, and `channelName: Demo Issuer`).

It is **live on** `develop` **today** — not only on #568.

---

## Evidence

**What the service actually mints** — `services/anchoring/src/index.ts`:

```js
:417   const anchorId = `anchor_${require('crypto').randomUUID()}`;
:699   const anchorId = `anchor_${require('crypto').randomUUID()}_${i}`;   // batch
```

**What the live table holds** (local stack, `anchor_store`, 2026-08-21):

| Query | Rows |
| -- | -- |
| `select count(*) … where id like 'anc\_%'` — the **published** shape | **0** |
| `select count(*) … where id like 'anchor\_%'` — the **real** shape (control) | **61,507** |
| `select split_part(id,'_',1), count(*) … group by 1` | exactly one group: `anchor` → 61,507 |

The control proves the `LIKE` can match, so the zero discriminates. A real id: `anchor_e83ba0cc-47b0-4bd1-8117-52120de467ef` — `anchor_` + a UUID, exactly as line 417 says.

**Where** `anc_` **occurs at all.** Repo-wide on `develop`, **exactly 2 occurrences**, and they are the same example twice: `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml:893` and its source `services/anchoring/src/anchoring.openapi.ts:63`. Control: `anchor_` occurs **52** times in the same service. Nothing anywhere mints `anc_` — it exists only in the published example.

---

## What each branch publishes — and why #568 makes it worse

| Ref | Published `Anchor.id` | Backed by |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `origin/develop` | `anc_01HC9ZP3WXYZQ12345VWXY` | a raw literal, in no fixture set |
| `c114ceddd` (#568) | `anc_01HC9ZN4ANCHORFIXTURE1` | `FX.anchor.id` — the canonical fixture |

#568's change is *right in its own terms* and its comment says so honestly (`anchoring.openapi.ts:63`): there were two different anchor ids for one canonical anchor, and collapsing them onto `FX` is exactly what `FX` exists for. **The problem is which shape it collapsed onto.** After #568, a wrong format stops being a stray literal and becomes the fixture the whole spec draws from — and `FIXTURE_ID_VALUES` membership then makes E8 *vouch* for it.

`fixtures.ts` states the contract this breaks, in its own words:

> ⚠ NOTHING HERE IDENTIFIES A LIVE ACCOUNT — and that is the point. … Every value below is *format-true and account-false*: shaped exactly like the real thing, backed by nothing.

`anc_01HC9ZN4ANCHORFIXTURE1` is account-false ✅ and **format-false** ❌. It is not shaped like the real thing.

---

## Fix

Change `FX.anchor.id` (`packages/shared/src/openapi/examples/fixtures.ts:209`) to the shape the service mints — `anchor_` + a fixture UUID from the existing all-zero family, keeping it account-false:

```
anchor_00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000030
```

Then regenerate the spec so `secuura-api.yaml:893` follows.

⚠ **This interacts with rule E7 and must not be done blind.** `HIGH_ENTROPY_RE` is `/^[A-Za-z0-9+/=_-]{40,}$/`, and `anchor_` + a 36-char UUID is **43 characters** — it will trip E7 unless the prefixed-UUID shape is admitted to `BENIGN_SHAPES`. KS-665's design comment already proposes that widening and tested it (proposed set → exit 0; the seeded-account leak control → still exit 1). **Land the E7 widening first, or this fix turns the build red.**

---

## Sequencing

Implementation deferred to the post-#568 tranche, per the KS-665 plan — a branch off `c114ceddd` cannot reach `develop` until #568 merges, and this touches a file @PeterD is actively editing.

**One call from @PeterD:** the shape above assumes `anchor_<uuid>` is what you want published. If you would rather keep a ULID-ish opaque id in the spec, then the *service* is the thing that is inconsistent, and this becomes a different (larger) ticket about id format across the platform. Your call — but the spec and the service should not disagree.

---

**Verified by:** @kamil.kreiser, 2026-08-21 — mint sites read, live `anchor_store` census with a passing control, repo-wide occurrence sweep, both refs compared. Working tree untouched. Related: KS-665 (design), KS-256/#568.

title: #568 publishes 17 URLs on secuura.io — an unresolving, seemingly unowned domain (KS-669 class; no guard rule covers URLs)
description:
## BLUF

**#568 publishes 17 URLs on** `secuura.io` **— a domain that does not resolve and that we do not appear to own.** This is the same class as [[KS-669]] (`exports.secuura.com`, an unowned for-sale domain in the published spec), three weeks on, and it is back because **no guard rule covers URLs** — E1 splits on `@` and only sees email addresses.

Filed separately from KS-669 rather than as a comment on it, deliberately: KS-669 is In Progress with its own scope (17 of its 18 URLs are still open work) and its operative defect is that it is **unassigned**. Folding a second, differently-sourced class into it makes it bigger, not more actionable. Cross-linked both ways.

**Stated fairly in both directions: #568 is a net improvement here.** It *removes* all **3** `demo@secuura.io` addresses that `develop` publishes today — E1 doing exactly its job. The URL class is the part nothing checks.

---

## Evidence

**DNS, with a control set** (2026-08-21):

| Domain | rcode | NS | SOA |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `secuura.io` | **NXDOMAIN** | none | none |
| `secuura.ai` | NOERROR | `dns2.registrar-servers.com.` | present |
| `secuura.net` | NOERROR | `dns1.registrar-servers.com.` | present |
| `secuura.com` | NOERROR | `ns4.afternic.com.` | present |

The three controls resolve, so the resolver works and the NXDOMAIN discriminates.

⚠ **A limit on this evidence, stated rather than glossed:** `whois secuura.io` falls through to IANA and returns the `.io` **TLD** record, so its `status: ACTIVE` describes the TLD, not the domain. **I am reporting DNS only — NXDOMAIN with no NS and no SOA. I am not claiming a registration status.** Someone with registrar access should confirm ownership before this is closed either way.

**Occurrences in the published spec** (`Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`):

| Pattern | `c114ceddd` (#568) | `origin/develop` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `example.secuura.io` | **17** | **0** |
| `demo@secuura.io` | **0** | **3** |

Repo-wide on #568 the string appears **35** times across 7 files — the 17 published ones plus 18 in the generating sources (`auth`, `billing`, `m365-integration`, `originate`, `prism` `.openapi.ts`, and `synthesize.ts`). Fixing the source fixes both.

**The 17, by field** — these are not all cosmetic:

* `redirectUri` ×1 · `webhookUrl` ×1 · `successUrl` ×2 · `cancelUrl` ×2 · `siteUrl` ×1
* `serviceEndpoint` ×5 · `url` ×3 · bare array items ×2

`redirectUri`, `webhookUrl`, `successUrl`/`cancelUrl` and `serviceEndpoint` are all fields an integrator may copy into a working configuration. A published spec that points them at an unregistered domain is a domain anyone can register.

**Source** — `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/openapi-examples/synthesize.ts:203`:

```ts
case 'uri':
case 'url':
    return 'https://example.secuura.io/resource';
```

Every `format: uri` / `format: url` field gets this one literal.

---

## Fix direction

Use a domain reserved for the purpose. `example.com` **is reserved by RFC 2606 / RFC 6761** and can never be registered by anyone — which is the same guarantee the email side already relies on (E1 permits `example.com` addresses). `https://example.com/resource` is a one-line change at `synthesize.ts:203`, plus a regeneration.

**Then close the hole that let it back in:** add a URL rule to the guard — an example whose value parses as a URL must have a host in the reserved set (`example.com`/`.org`/`.net`, `localhost`), or be allowlisted with a reason. Without it this class returns a third time. That rule belongs with the guard-coverage work in the sibling ticket.

---

## Calls needed from @PeterD

1. **Do we own** `secuura.io`**?** If we do, this drops to "point it somewhere real or use `example.com` anyway". If we don't, it should not be in a published spec at all.
2. Is `example.com` acceptable as the synthesised URL host, or do you want a real owned host (e.g. under `secuura.ai`)?

---

**Verified by:** @kamil.kreiser, 2026-08-21 — DNS with control set, occurrence counts on both refs, source line read. Working tree untouched. Related: KS-669 (same class, `exports.secuura.com`), KS-256/#568, KS-665.

title: Published spec points integrators at 18 URLs on domains we do not own (one is for sale) — E1 only inspects emails, never URLs
description:
## BLUF

**The published OpenAPI spec points integrators at 18 URLs on two domains Secuura does not own — one of which is currently for sale.** The guard rule that fixtures.ts names as enforcing our domain policy (**E1**) only ever inspects **email addresses**; it does not look at URLs at all, so this has never been checkable.

The sharpest instance is one line:

```yaml
# components.schemas.AnalyticsExport.example
url: https://exports.secuura.com/exp_01HC9ZQ2ABCDEFGHIJKLMN/document...
```

`secuura.com` is **not ours**. The project `CLAUDE.md` records it as *"not owned (parked for sale on Afternic/GoDaddy; **do not link to it**)"* — and the customer-facing API documentation links to it, on the field a client reads to fetch a completed analytics export.

## Measured

Every URL appearing inside an `example:` block in `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, by host:

| host | count | status |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `api.example.com` | 6 | fine — RFC 2606 reserved |
| `example.secuura.io` | **17** | `secuura.io` is not a domain we control |
| `exports.secuura.com` | **1** | **not owned; parked for sale** |

`fixtures.ts` already states the policy and the reason, for emails:

> *"*`secuura.io` *is not a domain we are known to control (we hold [secuura.ai](<http://secuura.ai>) and [secuura.net](<http://secuura.net>)), so publishing it in customer-facing docs points integrators at third-party infrastructure. Enforced by guard rule E1."*

The policy is right. The enforcement claim is not.

The 17 `example.secuura.io` occurrences span **12 schemas**: `OAuthAppCreateRequest` (redirect URIs), `WebhookCreateRequest`, `WebhookUpdateRequest`, `M365TeamsWebhookConfigRequest`, `M365CompleteConnectionRequest`, `M365AddSiteRequest`, `BillingCheckoutBundleRequest`, `BillingCheckoutCustomRequest`, `BillingCheckoutSessionResponse`, `DidService`, `DidCreateRequest`, `DidUpdateRequest`.

Note what those fields are: OAuth **redirect URIs**, **webhook delivery targets**, and **billing checkout** URLs. If a domain we do not own is documented as the canonical shape for a redirect target, the failure mode is not cosmetic.

## Why the guard never caught it — the mechanism

`scripts/spec-examples/check/rules-global.mjs:67-77`:

```js
/** E1 — an address outside the single reserved example domain. */
function checkEmailDomain(text, docPath, allow, findings) {
  for (const match of text.match(EMAIL_RE) ?? []) {
    const domain = match.split('@')[1].toLowerCase();
    ...
```

It iterates `EMAIL_RE` matches and splits on `@`. A bare URL produces no match, so it is never examined. E1 is an *email*-domain rule wearing a *domain*-rule name — which is exactly why fixtures.ts's "Enforced by guard rule E1" reads as covering more than it does.

The gate is green today (`check:openapi` PASS, 394 example blocks, *"every published example resolves to the fixture set"*) **with all 18 of these published**, so a passing run is not evidence here.

## Recommendation

1. **Add a URL-host rule to the global rules** (an E-rule sibling of E1) accepting only RFC 2606 reserved hosts plus an explicit allow-list of domains we actually own (`secuura.ai`, `secuura.net`). Anything else fails the gate. This is the piece that makes the rest stay fixed.
2. **Add** `FX.webhookUrl` **/** `FX.redirectUri` **/** `FX.exportUrl` on `example.com`, and repoint all 18. Needs the matching accept-list entry in `scripts/spec-examples/check/contract.mjs` — the duplication trap recorded on KS-665.
3. **Fix** `exports.secuura.com` **first and separately** if 1–2 will not land quickly. It is one line, and it is the one pointing at a domain a third party can currently buy.

## Relationship to other tickets

* **KS-665** carries an open *"webhook example URL"* decision from the KS-256 §4 review — *"*`POST /api/webhooks` *publishes a URL the API refuses because the host cannot resolve, and fixing it collides with E1's reserved-domain rule."* This ticket supersedes the framing of that item: it is not one example needing a judgement call, it is **18 across 13 schemas with no guard coverage**, and there is no collision with E1 because E1 never sees URLs.
* **KS-256 / PR #568** is the branch these examples were generated on. **No change is requested there** — the branch is reviewed and waiting on sign-off, and this predates it in kind.

## Evidence

* `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` — measured by walking every `example:`/`examples:` block and extracting URLs by host.
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/spec-examples/check/rules-global.mjs:60-77` — `applyGlobalRules` and `checkEmailDomain`; no URL inspection anywhere in E1–E4.
* `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/openapi/examples/fixtures.ts` — `EXAMPLE_DOMAIN`, and the comment claiming E1 enforcement.
* Project `CLAUDE.md` — `secuura.com` not owned, "do not link to it".

Found while working KS-665 item 2.

title: Compose seeds published *123 credentials by default, and the 11 rotation vars never reach the auth container from .env — every compose deploy (local, demo VM, Kintsugi)
description:
## BLUF

**Any compose deploy of this platform comes up seeding the published** `*123` **credentials, and the documented way to rotate them silently does nothing unless you happen to put them in the one undocumented file.** Two halves of the same asymmetry in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`:

* the single variable that **enables** published default passwords is interpolated from `.env` and **defaults to** `true`;
* the eleven variables that **replace** those passwords are not interpolated at all, and reach the container only via `.env.local` — which no example file and no doc mentions.

So the natural path (`.env`, which is what `env.example` and the deploy docs use) gives you: seeding **on**, published credentials **live**, and your rotation **ignored** — while the seeder logs that it updated the accounts.

Blast radius is **every compose deploy**: local, the demo VM, and Kintsugi. `docker-compose.local.yml` `include:`s `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`, so the canonical local stack inherits it, and the demo VM + Kintsugi run that file directly.

## Recommendation

Two small changes, both in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`:

1. Flip the default: `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=${ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS:-false}`, and set it explicitly to `true` in the local-dev path that actually wants it. Opting in should be an act, not an omission.
2. Interpolate the eleven rotation variables in the `auth` service's `environment:` block the same way every other secret is (`- DEMO_USER_PASSWORD=${DEMO_USER_PASSWORD:-}` …), so `.env` — the file everyone edits — is a working channel. Then document them in `env.example`.

Neither is a code change to the auth service; the seeder's logic (`userRepo.ts:965-995`) is correct as written.

## A — the gate defaults to ON, and its stated premise is dead

`Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:626`

```yaml
- ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=${ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS:-true}
```

The pen-test **F-05** fix gated the demo seeder on this variable. The auth service states the premise the gate rests on, at `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:987-991`:

> *"The hardcoded fallbacks remain only because the seeder itself is now gated on* `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` *(above) — i.e. **a deploy that doesn't explicitly opt in never sees these strings**."*

That premise is false for every compose deploy, because the compose file opts in on your behalf.

The justification for the default is at `:623-625`:

> *"Defaults to true here ONLY because docker-compose.yml is the local-dev compose; production is on Container Apps where this env var is unset and the gate stays closed."*

**That reasoning died with the KS-414 VM pivot (2026-07-08).** The Container Apps estate was deleted on 2026-07-31. Since the pivot, `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` is not "the local-dev compose" — it is *the* deployment artefact for the demo VM and now for Kintsugi as well. The comment describes an architecture the project no longer has.

Measured on the running local stack:

```
$ docker exec secuura-auth sh -c 'echo $ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS'
true
```

## B — the eleven rotation variables never reach the container from `.env`

Derived from source rather than from any prior write-up — every `seedPw()` call site in `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`:

`ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_APEX_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_BUPA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_DELTA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_GREENFIELD_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_HOLDER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_ISSUER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_OXFORD_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_SECUURA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_USER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_VERIFIER_PASSWORD`

| check | result | control |
| -- | -- | -- |
| occurrences of each of the 11 in `docker-compose.yml` | **0 / 11** | `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` → **1** |
| present in the running `secuura-auth` container | **0 / 11** | gate present, value `true`; 95 env vars total |

Both zero-results carry a control that fires independently, so they are real absences and not a grep that could never match.

The code's own rotation instruction (`userRepo.ts:992-993`) is:

> *"For per-tenant rotation, set* `DEMO_<TENANT>_PASSWORD` *env vars in Azure Key Vault and **surface them to the auth container**."*

"Surface them to the auth container" is the whole problem — it names no channel, and only one of the two obvious ones works.

## The correction — this is NOT "rotation is impossible"

An earlier write-up of this (KS-601 comment `4ada1e3a`) concluded the documented rotation *cannot work*. **That over-claims, and the correction matters because it changes the fix.** The `auth` service does declare an env_file:

```yaml
env_file:
  - path: .env.local
    required: false
```

Tested rather than assumed: of the **66** variables declared in `.env.local`, **66** are present in the running container. `.env.local` is a fully working injection channel.

So the accurate finding is an **asymmetry of channel**, which is worse than a flat "it doesn't work" because it fails silently in exactly one direction:

| variable | channel | reaches container from `.env`? | effect |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` | `${…:-true}` interpolation | **yes**, and defaults **true** | published `*123` credentials get seeded |
| the 11 `*_PASSWORD` vars | `.env.local` env_file only | **no** | rotation silently ignored |

`.env` is the file `env.example` is copied to, the file the setup instructions name, and the file compose reads for `${…}` interpolation — but it is *not* an env_file for `auth`, so values placed there are invisible to the seeder. Neither `env.example` nor `.env.local.example` mentions any of the eleven, or the gate.

## Why it fails convincingly

Recorded on Kintsugi during the KS-601 Stage C build (2026-08-20) — **this half is that session's on-box measurement; I have not re-run it here**, because reproducing it locally means changing `demo@`'s password and breaking the preflight persona:

Setting the eleven in `.env` and recreating the auth container printed `Demo user updated to match seed config` account after account — on a code path that genuinely does execute an `UPDATE … password_hash`. **The old password still authenticated.** Only a negative control (attempting a login with the *old* credential and expecting it to fail) caught it. Fixed on that box with a compose override making all 11 visible, then verified both directions: old `demo123` → **401**, new credential → **200**.

That is the part worth carrying: the failure produces success-shaped log output, so anyone rotating credentials and checking the logs will believe they succeeded.

## Scope note

Not in scope here: whether the demo VM *should* keep its seeded public credentials. Those are deliberate, documented sample logins for public demos (project `CLAUDE.md`). This ticket is about a deploy coming up more permissive than its operator intended, and a rotation that reports success without doing anything.

## Evidence

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:570-666` — `auth` service; `:626` the gate; `:623-625` the dead premise; `env_file` at `:576-578`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:965-995` — the F-05 gate, the `seedPw()` helper and its rotation instruction.
* `docker-compose.local.yml:33-35` — `include:` of `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/env.example`, `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local.example` — neither names the eleven or the gate.
* KS-601 comment `4ada1e3a` — the Kintsugi on-box record (superseded on the "cannot work" point by the correction above).

## Suggested owner

Unassigned deliberately. Compose/deploy topology rather than service logic — @peter or @stuart to route; happy to take it myself if neither has context loaded.

title: KS-256 review follow-ups: 5 example-fixable 400s, the tsx transpile-only spec-gate trap (§10), and a new `userAgent: Demo Issuer` instance
description:
The three items left open from @kksecura's 2026-08-19 review of PR #568. Split out per his own §8 reasoning — the parameter-example work is the bigger half of the same problem, and bundling it would expand a PR he has already reviewed twice.

**Every figure below was re-verified against the branch head** `92feea4a9`**, not carried over from the review.**

---

## 1. §4 — the five example-fixable 400s are still published

His triage stands unchallenged: **5 strictly example-fixable**, or **8 counting parameter examples**. My original "at most 4" was low. All five are still live in `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`:

| # | Defect | Count at head |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `example-documentId` violates `SAFE_ID_PATTERN` | **17** |
| 2 | `example-code` exceeds the documented max of 8 | **3** |
| 3 | `example-challengeId` is not a uuid | **1** |
| 4 | `example-country` is not exactly 2 chars | **2** |
| 5 | `transfer-custody` pins two mutually exclusive fields | 1 |

Number 5 is the sharpest, because the spec contradicts itself **four lines apart** (`secuura-api.yaml:6318-6322`):

```yaml
description: Exactly ONE of `newHolderId` / `newHolderEmail` is required — neither is 400, both is 400.
example:
  newHolderId: example-newHolderId
  newHolderEmail: demo.issuer@example.com     # ← publishing exactly what the line above calls a 400
```

A reader copying that example gets a guaranteed 400, and the description already tells them why.

**Fix direction:** these land in the Zod sources (`services/*/src/*.openapi.ts`), then `npm run generate-openapi`. Numbers 1–4 need the placeholder to satisfy the constraint the schema already documents; number 5 needs the example to pin one field only.

## 2. The bigger half — parameter examples

Verified at head: **132 path parameters, 2 carrying an example.** That is the §7 gap on [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage)'s own body, and it is why this is a follow-up rather than a patch. Together with `operationId`/`links` ([KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) — 0 of 613 links covered) it is the next real coverage step, and it dwarfs the five above.

## 3. §10 — the trap that produced the build failure, recorded nowhere

`npm run generate-openapi` runs the `*.openapi.ts` files through `tsx`**, which is transpile-only**. A type error in the very file the generator reads therefore **cannot** fail the spec gate.

That is exactly how the `documentUuid` breakage shipped: `check:openapi` was **green** — drift clean, E1–E9 0 findings across 354 blocks — while `originate` would not compile, and the failure only surfaced in the Docker build (30/34 images, `originate` + `migrations` red, no containers started).

`check:openapi` **green is not evidence the images build.** Nothing in `scripts/`, `CLAUDE.md` or `package.json` says so today. Options, in increasing order of strength:

1. Document it where the gate is defined and in `CLAUDE.md`.
2. Add a `tsc --noEmit` pass over the `*.openapi.ts` sources to `check:openapi`, so the gate covers the files it consumes.

Option 2 would have caught the original defect at the gate rather than in a 50-minute image build. @kksecura offered the wording or is happy for us to take it — his call.

## 4. A new instance of the §3 class his sweep did not reach

`secuura-api.yaml:7265` publishes:

```yaml
userAgent: Demo Issuer
```

Same mechanism as the 16 `address` fields fixed in `704c8c0f2`: a legitimate `FIXTURE_PERSON_VALUES` member landing on a **non-person** field, so **E5 passes it** — the guard is working to spec and the spec is wrong for the field. Not a leak; a documentation defect, since no client sends `Demo Issuer` as a user agent.

**Verified the rest are correct** — the other 21 `Demo Issuer` hits are all on genuine name fields and should stay:

```
17  displayName     2  channelName     1  fullName     1  name
 1  userAgent   ← the defect
```

**Fix direction:** same as §3 — either give `userAgent` its own fixture, or stop masking-category-3 claiming it. Worth deciding once for the class rather than per field, since `address` and `userAgent` are now two instances of it.

---

## Why these are not on [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage)

[KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage)'s own acceptance already carries the 26×400 triage as an open box, and its two remaining boxes are gated on [KS-660](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-660/ci-every-needs-build-suite-job-dies-in-3s-with-zero-steps-develop-is) (CI executes zero steps). Items 1 and 4 here are small, item 2 is large, and item 3 is a gate change — none of them belongs in a PR that has been reviewed twice and is waiting on sign-off.

*— raised by agent on Peter's behalf, 2026-08-19. Figures verified at* `92feea4a9`*.*

title: deepmerge-ts GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx (high) — override to 8.0.1 in originate; hoisted root lock baselined to 2026-10-31 on reachability
description:
**Ask:** remove the `expires: 2026-10-31` entry for `GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx` from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json` once Prisma ships a `@prisma/config` that pulls `deepmerge-ts` 8.x — at which point the override below can go too.

Same class as [KS-585](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-585/js-yaml-3142-ships-in-runtime-images-ghsa-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj-and-dev) / [KS-599](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-599/bump-nanoid-ghsa-2v37-7h3g-55p8-high-dompurify-ghsa-55q2-fjhq-7xh7): a freshly-published advisory tripping the [KS-470](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-470/npm-audit-25-transitive-advisories-on-the-develop-lockfile) npm-audit preflight gate with no code change on our side. Work-stream **H** ([KS-493](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-493/review-h-dependency-currency-and-known-vuln-package-upgrades-all)) per CLAUDE.md.

> ## 🌿 The work is already written — branch `fix/deepmerge-ts-ghsa-ggr8`
>
> **Use this branch, not Linear's auto-suggested** `feature/ks-664-…`**.** It was cut before this
> ticket existed and already carries both commits, verified:
>
> | commit | what |
> | -- | -- |
> | `307bc11ef` | `overrides: deepmerge-ts ^8.0.1` in `services/originate/package.json` + regenerated standalone lock |
> | `c28b09a65` | the reasoned `audit-baseline.json` entry citing this ticket, `expires: 2026-10-31` |
>
> **⚠ It exists ONLY on the Ubuntu VM (**`~/dev/Distributed_Secuura`**) — never pushed, no second copy.**
> Push it before anything else, or the work is one `git branch -D` from gone. It branches from
> `origin/develop`, touches **3 files**, and contains **no backend source** — only dependency
> metadata and build tooling.
>
> With it applied the full preflight **PASSES, exit 0** (legs 5 and 6 both green) — the first clean
> preflight on that VM. Without it, every `Blockchain/Dev` push from the VM fails the audit gate.
>
> Author of record is PeterD (the VM's git identity); the work is assigned here per the
> work-stream H ownership rule.

## The advisory

**GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx \[high\]** — *"DeepmergeTS has stack exhaustion when merging recursive object graphs."* Merging an object containing a cycle or very deep nesting recurses until the call stack blows and the process crashes. Affects `<8.0.0`; we pinned **7.1.5**.

Note the advisory carries **no CVSS vector** (score reports 0) — "high" is the publisher's own label, not a scored assessment.

## Why an override, not a dependency bump

It is transitive and **upstream has not fixed it**:

```
services/originate
  └─ prisma@^7.8.0            ← devDependencies
       └─ @prisma/config
            └─ deepmerge-ts   ← pinned EXACTLY 7.1.5 by @prisma/config
```

Checked against the registry on 2026-08-19: `@prisma/config@latest` **(7.9.1) still pins** `deepmerge-ts@7.1.5`, and `prisma` already resolves to the latest 7.9.x via `^7.8.0`. So bumping Prisma changes nothing; an `overrides` entry is the only route until Prisma moves.

## Reachability today: none that ships

* `prisma` is the **CLI**, in `devDependencies`. The runtime deps are `@prisma/client` + `@prisma/adapter-pg`, neither of which pulls `deepmerge-ts`.
* `services/originate/Dockerfile:79` runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts --omit=dev`, so it is **not in the runtime image**. No deployed service carries this code. (The lock entry is even marked `"devOptional": true`.)
* The vulnerable path is `@prisma/config` deep-merging **Prisma's own config file** at CLI invocation — developer-authored input, not untrusted API input — and the impact is a crashed CLI, not a compromised service.

Build-time only, developer-input only, crash not compromise. Accepted on reachability, not absence — same standard as [KS-599](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-599/bump-nanoid-ghsa-2v37-7h3g-55p8-high-dompurify-ghsa-55q2-fjhq-7xh7).

## What has been done

**Fixed where it actually ships** — `services/originate` standalone lock (the one the Dockerfile's `npm ci` consumes) now resolves **8.0.1** via an `overrides` entry. Regenerated with the containerised procedure (`scripts/preflight/lockfile-cleanroom.sh:113`), because a plain `npm install --package-lock-only` in a member dir silently does nothing — npm walks up to the `Blockchain/Dev` workspace root and refuses to write a member lock.

Surgical: **655 packages before and after, exactly one version changed** (7.1.5 → 8.0.1), 13 insertions. Verified by real container install — `deepmerge-ts` 8.0.1 installed, and `@prisma/config` **loads successfully against it** despite still declaring 7.1.5. Preflight **leg 6 (**`audit:locks`**) goes green**.

## Why the root lock is baselined rather than fixed — measured, not assumed

Preflight **leg 5 (**`audit:gate`**)** resolves the **hoisted workspace tree**, whose root lock still pins 7.1.5. npm will not re-resolve it incrementally: it reports `up to date` and skips, even with the override present in the root `package.json`, and even run containerised.

A full root-lock rebuild *does* apply the override, but the delta was measured and **rejected**:

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| entries before → after | 1,970 → 2,830 |
| added / removed / version-changed | **956 / 96 / 11** |
| diff | **13,406 lines** |

It **downgraded** `@effect/schema` 0.68.27→0.66.16, `@lucid-evolution/core-types` 0.3.0→0.1.24, `@anastasia-labs/cardano-multiplatform-lib-*` 6.2.0-1→6.0.2-3 and `@prisma/get-platform` 7.8.0→7.2.0; **dropped** `@azure/keyvault-secrets`, `@noble/post-quantum` and `pglite`; and **added darwin-arm64 binaries** while resolving on Linux. Exactly the drift the clean-room guard exists to catch. Reverted; root `package.json` and `package-lock.json` are untouched.

So there is no safe code fix for the hoisted view, and the baseline entry covers only that view — what ships is genuinely fixed.

## Removal path

1. Watch for a `@prisma/config` release depending on `deepmerge-ts` ^8.
2. Bump `prisma`, drop the `overrides` entry in `services/originate/package.json`, regen the standalone lock in `node:24-alpine`.
3. Remove the `GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx` entry from `scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json`.

⚠ The `expires: 2026-10-31` is a forcing function: on expiry the gate fails again and **blocks every** `Blockchain/Dev` **push** — see [KS-635](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-635/audit-baseline-exception-expires-2026-08-31-and-will-block-every-push) for the same mechanism biting on 2026-08-31.

## How it surfaced

Only became visible on 2026-08-19, when the pre-push preflight was made runnable on Linux at all (PR #724 — `.githooks/pre-push` invoked a `#!/usr/bin/env bash` script with `sh`, and dash rejects `set -o pipefail`, so the gate had been aborting before leg 1 on the Ubuntu VM). Surfaced during [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage) validation but unrelated to that work.

*— raised by agent on Peter's behalf, 2026-08-19.*

title: The OpenAPI spec is now a consumed contract, but nothing in CI stops it drifting — plus two known spec/code divergences
description:
Raised by Platform S, 2026-08-19, from a full S↔K audit against K develop `74a330fc0`. **Nothing is broken today** — the spec is in sync. This is about keeping it that way now that something depends on it.

## What changed on our side

[PS-614](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-614>) (merged, S develop `2403313`) makes Platform S read `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` at gate time and fail its build when S's lifecycle-verb vocabulary disagrees with K's published enum, in either direction.

We built it because of [KS-556](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-556>): K added `protect`/`unprotect`/`restore` on 2026-08-03, S adopted them on 2026-08-18, and for 15 days those events anchored with **no** `documentType` **at all**. Nothing failed, because every guard S had compared one hand-maintained copy of K's list against another. Reading K's own spec is the fix.

**Your spec is a strong contract, and that is why we chose it.** Verified: it is *generated* (`scripts/generate-openapi.ts:28`) from the same `LIFECYCLE_VERBS` / `LIFECYCLE_EVENT_ACTIONS` constants the runtime validates against, and the enums match exactly — 22 and 13, diffed programmatically, empty symmetric difference. That is a better guarantee than a hand-written spec could give.

## The gap

`check:openapi` **is not wired into any CI workflow.** It exists as an npm script (`Blockchain/Dev/package.json:43`), but grepping all 17 files in `.github/workflows/` for `openapi` returns **zero** hits. (`quality:static` in `pr-platform-suites.yml:238` runs in `systemTest/playwright`, a different workspace.)

So the spec is correct today by diligence, not by enforcement — and it is now load-bearing for a consumer outside this repo. A PR that changes a verb without regenerating would leave S's gate green while S sends something K rejects, which is the [KS-388](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388>) 400-the-whole-anchor case.

**Ask:** run `check:openapi` in the PR workflow.

## Two divergences worth closing while you are there

**1.** `/api/v2/verification/verify-file` **is in code but absent from the spec.** Handler at `services/originate/src/routes/verificationV2.ts:497`; `verify-file` does not appear in `secuura-api.yaml` at all. The v1 equivalent is missing too. It is the only verify variant where the **server** computes the hash — i.e. the one a client cannot lie to — so it is the one most worth publishing. Invisible to a spec-reading consumer today.

**2.** `documentUuid` **is stricter in code than in the spec.** Code requires UUID **v4** specifically (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:350` `UUID_V4_RE`, 400s v1/v5/v7); the spec publishes `format: uuid` (`secuura-api.yaml:4556-4557`), which any RFC 4122 version satisfies. A client generating a v7 UUID passes spec validation and is rejected at runtime. We happen to send v4 ([PS-570](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-570>) enforces the version nibble before sending), so this has not bitten us — but it would bite a new integrator. Either publish the v4 constraint or relax the code.

## One observation, no action implied

`emitLifecycleAnchor` (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1120-1128`) posts only `{documentId, contentHash, network}` to `/api/anchors` — no `metadata.documentType`, no `metadata.timestamp`. So lifecycle events recorded through **K's own** endpoints anchor unlabelled, while the same verbs sent by S on the flat path carry the verb on-chain. Consistent with [KS-319](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-319>)'s scope, but it means the [KS-556](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-556/add-protectunprotectrestore-to-the-ks-134-lifecycle-verb-vocabulary) / [KS-534](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-534>) / [KS-415](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-415>) vocabulary only ever reaches the ledger via the flat path. Flagging in case that is not intended.

## Verification

* A PR that edits a verb constant without regenerating the spec **fails** CI.
* `verify-file` (v1 and v2) appears in the published spec.
* `documentUuid`'s published constraint matches what the code enforces.

*Everything above verified read-only against develop* `74a330fc0`*. Happy to review a draft against our gate before you merge — we are the consumer and can tell you quickly whether it reads correctly from our side.*
