title: GET /api/anchors/{id} and verify report different statuses for the same anchor — 91 UAT anchors read "failed" while verify says confirmed
description:
Raised from the S side 2026-08-12 (S ticket: [PS-577](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-577>)). @kamil.kreiser — one authenticated call settles this; details below.

## The observation

Platform S polls `GET /api/anchors/{id}` to learn when an anchor confirms. On UAT, **91 transactions are stuck reporting** `failed` — while `POST /api/verification/verify`, asked about the same document's content hash, reports the **same anchor id** as confirmed on chain.

Concretely, anchor `anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2`:

```
POST /api/verification/verify  {"providedHash":"6ffa6a0d4378007a480af701b6113cc0252544bcfde93cf11c2654c8bbe2367e"}

  verified   : true              status  : anchored
  anchorId   : anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2
  bc.status  : confirmed         txHash  : e64759a924ea314e…
  anchoredAt : 2026-08-09T06:18:39.090Z
  checks     : documentExists ✓ hashValid ✓ isCertified ✓ isAnchored ✓ integrityVerified ✓
```

S recorded its failure for that same anchor at **06:32:20** — **fourteen minutes after** `anchoredAt`. So this is not a race between a poll and a late confirmation.

A second sample behaves identically: document ref `doc-1785566174843-631e2310` (an originate/upload), `verified: true`, `confirmed`, txHash `38adf13132f6856a…`, while S has it marked failed.

## What has been ruled out on the S side

Both plausible S-side causes were eliminated before raising this:

* **Not a failed/unauthenticated read.** All six affected organisations are registered with connector keys, and each has rows that *did* confirm — org 6: 77 confirmed vs 58 failed, org 9: 39 vs 20, org 13: 8 vs 6. Reads plainly work for these tenants.
* **Not an S mapping bug.** For an `anchor_…` reference S takes the `status` field from `/api/anchors/{id}` **verbatim** — no interpretation layer is involved. S is reporting the exact word it is given.

Spread is across every verb (share 39, upload 16, share-attach-consent 13, certify 5, sign 5, watermark 4, and the share-edit verbs), so it is not verb-specific.

## The question

Does `GET /api/anchors/{id}` return a stale or different status than the anchor's true state?

Candidates worth checking:

1. The anchors read serves a row that `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` ([KS-535](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-535/a-failed-on-chain-anchor-still-reports-statusanchored-async-failure)) later healed, without the anchors view reflecting the heal.
2. There are two anchor records and the endpoints resolve different ones — the [KS-563](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-563/verify-api-iscertified-is-true-for-merely-anchored-documents-so)/584 "answer from the row that evidences its claims" family, except here it is the *anchors* endpoint that looks wrong.
3. `/api/anchors/{id}` is correct and verify is optimistic — in which case S's reading is right and the bug is elsewhere.

**The one call that settles it:**

```
GET /api/anchors/anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2
```

on demo-pk, authenticated. If it returns `status: failed` while verify reports that anchor confirmed with tx `e64759a924ea314e…`, the inconsistency is confirmed and the question becomes which is authoritative. I could not make this call myself — the endpoint requires auth — so the diagnosis above is inferred from S's behaviour plus the eliminations, not directly observed.

## Why it matters to S

1. Users see **"anchor failed" on documents that are anchored and confirmed on chain** — a false negative on a trust surface.
2. **S never collects the real transaction hash.** Those rows keep their `anchor_…` placeholder permanently, so the chain evidence K is holding is silently lost to S.
3. It makes S's anchoring-failure count unusable as an alert signal.

## What S has done meanwhile

S no longer takes a bare `failed` as final ([Secuura/platform-s#440](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-577-dont-take-anchor-failed-as-final-when-ks-own-verify-disagrees-4a8640ddf0ac), merged). When the anchors endpoint reports failed, S asks verify and prefers the evidenced answer **only** when verify names the same `anchorId`, reports it anchored, not simulated, and carries a real 64-hex transaction hash.

That is a mitigation, not a fix — it recovers the lost hashes and stops the false failures, but the two endpoints still disagree, and S is now quietly compensating for it. Worth resolving at source.

Related: [PS-577](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-577>), [KS-535](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-535/a-failed-on-chain-anchor-still-reports-statusanchored-async-failure), [KS-563](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-563/verify-api-iscertified-is-true-for-merely-anchored-documents-so).

title: BM-2: Verification is a configurable workflow via smart contracts — record the workflow path, not casual views
description:
## BLUF

**Verification is a CONFIGURABLE WORKFLOW, not a fixed function.** Clients configure verification workflows via smart contracts; Secuura does NOT prescribe compliance. The workflow PATH is verified against the smart contract and recorded; simple interactions like document VIEWING are NOT recorded on-chain (noise). A third-party verifier (e.g. recruiter verifying a university document) sees the inspectable steps (identity checks, domain matching). End-user sees a binary "verified"; audit/legal sees full rigor.

## Carried ruling (PS-556, Kam 2026-08-11)

A verification is a **public, repeatable READ** — it sits OUTSIDE canonical lineage (lineage = versions from certifications/modifications). If a verification act is recorded at all, **S records it for S's own reporting/lineage annotation — K does NOT become a source of record for verification acts.**

Source: 2026-08-11 technical weekly (Stuart, Phil, Kam).

title: BM-1: Certification model — certification = attestation + signing + optional watermarking; any modification → new version → mandatory re-certification
description:
## BLUF

**Certification is an UMBRELLA term** = attestation + signing + (optional) watermarking. Attestation = a user attesting a document is correct — on-chain, distinct from the file itself. Watermarking is a distinct, optional element. **ANY modification (including watermarking) creates a NEW document version, tracked via document lineage, and requires mandatory RE-CERTIFICATION.**

## Scope note

Likely an epic: data model + lineage enforcement + re-certification triggers + API/spec surface. This is the parent ticket — split into sub-tickets when the build starts.

Source: 2026-08-11 technical weekly (Stuart, Phil, Kam) — load-bearing project clarification.

title: Architecture P1: defuse the MULTI_TENANCY registry upsert — it silently collapses registrations per (hash, tenant) if the flag is ever enabled
description:
**Ask:** In the same phase that touches registration (plan-sheet requirement — not later, not beside), defuse `platform_document_registry`'s armed landmine: UNIQUE `uq_pdr_hash_tenant (content_hash, tenant_id)` + `ON CONFLICT (content_hash, tenant_id) DO UPDATE` in `registerInPlatformRegistry`. Either re-key the registry on the document UUID, or explicitly remove/disable the upsert.

**Why it matters:** the code path is dormant ONLY because `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED !== 'true'` on local and demo (0 registry rows in both DBs). If that flag is ever switched on with today's code, the upsert wakes and silently collapses registration pointers — newest write wins per (hash, tenant) — which directly violates ruling (b): duplicate bytes = two registrations, distinguished by UUID. A landmine that has been found and left armed is worse than one nobody found.

**Spec:** `1_Project_Definition/architecture/2026-08-07_K-side-plan-sheet.md` ("The MULTI_TENANCY landmine — inside P1, not beside it").

title: Three undeclared-verb catalogue skips cite CLOSED tickets (KS-406 / KS-421) — are the defects still live?
description:
## Summary

`tests/test_undeclared_method_safety.py::test_known_undeclared_verb_defect_is_tracked` skips three parametrised cases, each naming a ticket that is **Done and archived**:

| Case | Cited ticket | Ticket state | Skip reason |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `/tiers/calculate-discount-GET` | [KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of) | ⚠ Done 2026-07-08 | authed GET executes (200) on an undeclared verb |
| `/tiers/calculate-vote-power-GET` | [KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of) | ⚠ Done 2026-07-08 | authed GET executes (200) |
| `/billing/customers/by-email-PUT` | [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) | ⚠ Done 2026-07-10 | authed PUT crashes (500) |

The catalogue is doing its job — it records a known defect so the sweep does not re-report it — but it points at tickets closed a month ago. Either the defects are still live and need a current owner, or they were fixed and the entries should be removed so the tests execute.

**This is the same class the** [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-schemathesis-integration-mode-anchor-honesty-consistency-a) **report fix addresses**, one layer over: a stale ticket reference reads as "tracked" when nothing tracks it.

## Why you

The question is a platform one, not a harness one: **did** [KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of)**'s auth-first-401 posture decision and** [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods)**'s billing classifier actually resolve these three, or not?** Once that is known, the systemTest side is mechanical (remove the entries, or repoint them at a live ticket) and I'll do it.

[KS-406](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-406/design-call-undeclared-http-methods-return-401-auth-first-instead-of) was a *design decision* (adopt auth-first 401 for undeclared verbs) rather than a fix, so its two entries may be permanently correct behaviour that should be recorded as accepted rather than as a tracked defect. [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) was a real fix for `GET .../payment-methods`; whether it covered the `PUT .../by-email` sibling is worth checking.

## Reproduce

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

# undeclared GET — expect a safe rejection (401/403/404/405), not 200
curl -i -X GET  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:6882/api/tiers/calculate-discount
curl -i -X GET  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:6882/api/tiers/calculate-vote-power

# undeclared PUT — expect a safe rejection, not 500
curl -i -X PUT  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' \
  http://localhost:6882/api/billing/customers/by-email
```

The suite's own guard: `cd systemTest/schemathesis && venv/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/test_undeclared_method_safety.py -v -rsxX`

## Environment

**Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS** (kernel `7.0.0-28-generic`, **aarch64**) on Parallels, 8 vCPU / 31 GB, `10.211.55.4`. Node 24.19.0, PostgreSQL 15.18, Redis 8.10.0, Python 3.14.6, Schemathesis 4.24.3. Run `full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z`, seed `2794626967`.

## Outcome wanted

For each of the three: **live defect** (→ new ticket, repoint the entry) or **accepted/fixed** (→ remove the entry so the test executes and asserts the safe rejection). A skip is not a pass — while these sit in the catalogue the vectors are unverified.

Refs as KS-NNN text. Found by the [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-schemathesis-integration-mode-anchor-honesty-consistency-a) sweeps, 2026-08-07.

title: not_a_server_error recurs — 17 raw 5xx across 8 ops (KS-431 / KS-449 / KS-497 recurrence, full-2026-08-07 sweep)
description:
## Why a new ticket

The whole predecessor chain is **Done and archived**:

* [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) — Done 2026-07-10 · [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) — Done 2026-07-13 · [KS-449](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-449/write-path-residuals-from-ks-430-ks-431-remaining-raw-500s-request) — Done · [KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks) — Done 2026-07-29, archived

Each closed having fixed the raw-500 class down to its listed operations, and each time it has come back on different ones. Filed fresh per that precedent.

## Finding

**17** `not_a_server_error` **failures across 8 operations** — an unhandled value reaches a handler or the DB and throws, instead of being rejected with a mapped 4xx.

`GET /api/users/admin/list` · `POST /api/documents/{id}/lifecycle-events` · `POST /api/documents/{id}/revoke` · `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` · `POST /api/m365/outlook/exchange-token` · `POST /api/security/rate-limit/check` · `POST /api/users/admin/create` · `POST /api/webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret`

**Three of these are the** [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) **endpoints** — `/share`, `/lifecycle-events`, and the `documents/{id}` family. Kamil shipped the connector-actor fix on 2026-08-07 (`develop` `307483672`, PR #652) and verified all three return 201 on demo for a connector. These 5xx are on *fuzzed* input rather than the connector path, so they are likely a different trigger on the same handlers — but worth confirming they are not a regression from that change.

`GET /api/users/admin/list` and `POST /api/users/admin/create` are already documented on [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) **§2** with root causes traced (`parseInt(offset) || 0` lets `-1` through to Postgres; `data.email.toLowerCase()` with no type guard). [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) also notes **the negative-offset pattern is six sites across four services**, not the two the sweep reaches.

## Important — this count was inflated until today

`not_a_server_error` read **79 failures** on the previous sweep. It dropped to **17** once the governance active-proposal cap was cleared: the cap throws a bare `Error` that the route maps to `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, and every fuzzed proposal-create was counting as a server error. That mis-mapping is filed separately. **62 of the previous 79 were that one defect** — worth knowing before sizing this.

## Where this was run

**Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS** (kernel `7.0.0-28-generic`, **aarch64**) on Parallels, 8 vCPU / 31 GB, at `10.211.55.4`.

| Component | Version |  | Component | Version |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (aarch64) |  | Docker | 29.7.2 |
| Python (venv + host) | 3.14.6 |  | Node (services) | 24.19.0 (`node:24-alpine`) |
| Schemathesis | 4.24.3 |  | PostgreSQL | 15.18 (`postgres:15-alpine`) |
| pytest / Hypothesis | 9.1.1 / 6.165.2 |  | Redis | 8.10.0 (`redis:8-alpine`) |

Run of record: `full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z`, seed `2794626967`, 24.1 min.

## Reproduce

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

# KS-565 §2 — negative offset reaches Postgres
curl -i -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  'http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/list?offset=-1'

# KS-565 §2 — non-string email hits .toLowerCase()
curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":{},"password":"Str0ng-Passw0rd!","role":"OWNER"}' \
  http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/create
```

Full sweep: `cd systemTest/schemathesis && python3 scripts/run.py full` — 94 replayable crash files with `code_sample` curls under `output/reports/full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z/schemathesis-crashes/`.

## Fix direction

Per [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) / [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) / [KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks): classify the error at the route boundary — map known provider/validation failures to 4xx/503, keep genuine unknowns as 500 with structured logging, and guard path params and body fields before they reach the DB. Add unit tests pinning each classifier. **Fix all six negative-offset sites, not the two the sweep found** ([KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) §2 lists them).

## Note

The report had been attributing this class to [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) **with a bare ticket reference**, which reads as ownership. PR #656 now renders `KS-431 (closed — recurrence untracked)`; this ticket is the live owner.

Refs as KS-NNN text. Found by the [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-schemathesis-integration-mode-anchor-honesty-consistency-a) sweeps, 2026-08-07.

title: positive_data_acceptance recurs at scale — 734 failures across 64 ops (KS-255 / KS-515 recurrence, full-2026-08-07 sweep)
description:
## Summary

This register tracks the biggest single class in the sweeps: the API politely refusing (4xx) request bodies the published spec says are valid. The steady fix is to bring each operation's spec and validator into line, in whichever direction is right for it. A small new member was added on 2026-09-28: `POST /api/gdpr/consent`, where the database declines a value the spec allows. Details are below for whenever it's picked up. Thank you, Kamil.

+++ The register (2026-08-07) and the 2026-09-28 addendum

### Why a new ticket

The predecessors are Done and archived: [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done 2026-06-15) and [KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) (Done 2026-07-29, itself the [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked) recurrence). This is the same class recurring at a larger scale, filed fresh per the [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked)→[KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) / [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks)→[KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks) precedent.

### Finding

**734** `positive_data_acceptance` **failures across 64 operations**, about 75% of all check failures in `full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z` (seed `2794626967`, 22,744 cases, 317 operations; Ubuntu 24.04.4 aarch64 VM, Schemathesis 4.24.3, Postgres 15.18). Each failure card embeds a curl; the run also wrote 94 replayable crash files. Counts are a floor, not a total: generation samples rather than enumerates.

### Fix direction

Per [KS-423](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-423/blocking-pr-pre-merge-schemathesis-coverage-6-contract-drift-failures) / [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked): compare each route's validator with the spec, then tighten the spec to the runtime truth **or** loosen the runtime where the spec is right. Never narrow the generator. Cluster by service registration file.

### Addendum 2026-09-28 ([KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9)): `POST /api/gdpr/consent`

* **What:** a spec-valid body answered **400** `VALIDATION_ERROR` *"One or more field values cannot be stored (too long or not an allowed value)"*. It's a draw: 2 of the 6 [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) sweeps (sweeps 2 and 5, ×1 each).
* **The case:** `userId` (uuid), `purpose: "marketing"`, `source` = a 5-character string with a supplementary-plane character, `expiresInDays: 552`, plus 3 undeclared keys (allowed, since the schema doesn't set `additionalProperties: false`).
* **Where the 400 comes from:** `services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts:153` (`mapGdprWriteDbError`) maps Postgres **22001 / 23514 / 22007 / 22008 / 22021** to this 400. Its own comment says *"Value the spec permits but the schema can't store"*. So the refusal is deliberate; the gap is that the published contract doesn't declare the constraint.
* **Which constraint fired isn't recoverable:** the originate logs predate a slot rebuild. Candidates: `source`'s unusual character (22021 or a length limit), `expiresInDays` with no declared `maximum` (22008), or the extra keys if they reach a stored column. (An earlier note that said "extra keys → 400" was too specific.)
* **Direction:** a targeted probe per candidate names the Postgres code, then declare it in the spec (`maxLength`, `maximum`, a `pattern`, or `additionalProperties: false`).
* Listed in [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing) for baselining against this ticket.

+++

title: systemTest (Schemathesis): verify-by-hash must not resolve to an arbitrary registration — anchored-ancestor + cross-tenant field disclosure (KS-584 class)
description:
## Status: parked — not actionable yet

**Blocked on** [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) (Kamil, Urgent). That ticket has to decide *what correct resolution means* before a regression can assert it — Stuart offered three candidate shapes (prefer a row carrying chain data · return the anchored ancestor · report ambiguity) and they produce three different assertions. Writing tests now would pin a behaviour nobody has chosen.

Filed so the systemTest leg is visible from [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) rather than forgotten when [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) lands. **No work until the platform decision is made.**

## Why it belongs in Review G

[KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) has two consequences from one root cause, and G already owns regression coverage for both classes:

**1. Anchored-ancestor selection.** `POST /api/verification/verify` resolves a content hash with `ORDER BY d.certified_at DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1` and no preference for a row carrying chain data (`services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts`). The normal certify flow creates a *second* row with the same `content_hash` (the certification's `signed_document`), which wins the ordering and carries no `certification_metadata.blockchain`. So a document with three confirmed on-chain anchors verifies with `isAnchored: false`, `blockHeight: null` — reproduced live on UAT (`1.15412159T20251122.pdf`, `f4fd83a9…`, anchors at preview blocks 4547897 / 4547901 / 4547907).

This is the **anchor-honesty class** — the same shape as [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-anchor-honesty-consistency-a-mock-tx-tx-sim-hash-must-never) and the [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) D rows. A document's on-chain proof exists and the platform reports it doesn't.

**2. Cross-tenant field disclosure.** `buildResponse` returns the selected row's `title`, `issuer` / `organization_name`, `documentId`, `status`, `certifiedAt` and the lineage chain. The fallback `crossTenantLookup` is also unscoped, also `LIMIT 1`. Verifying a document you legitimately hold can return **another tenant's filename and organisation name** — and the anonymous verify path has no caller identity, so it cannot scope.

This is the **A / BUG-ISOLATION-001 class** that [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions) covered for documents and api-keys. [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions) is Done, so there is no open ticket carrying it, and the verify family went public under [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424) — the sweep reaches these operations today.

Note `platform_document_registry` is already `UNIQUE (content_hash, tenant_id)`. K models tenancy correctly here; verify just doesn't use it.

## Sketch — to be finalised once [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) decides

Placement: cross-tenant assertions with the `@pytest.mark.isolation` siblings; anchor-resolution assertions in the anchoring-integrity Integration mode.

| # | Property | Assertion | Depends on |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Certify does not un-anchor | Upload → anchor → certify → verify. `isAnchored` must stay true and the txHash must still resolve. Assert **after** certification propagates, not before — the UAT reproduction only appears once the second row exists | [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) decision |
| 2 | Multiple registrations resolve deterministically | Two rows sharing a `content_hash` → verify must not return an arbitrary one. Exact assertion depends on which of the three shapes is chosen | [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) decision |
| 3 | Ambiguity is not hidden | If the chosen shape is "report ambiguity", assert the match count / flag is present and a relying party can see it | Only if that shape wins |
| 4 | Anonymous verify discloses no tenant-owned fields | Register a document under tenant A; verify the same bytes anonymously → response carries no `title`, `organization_name`, `issuer` or lineage belonging to A | **Independent of the** [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) **decision** — this one could be written now if the disclosure half is ruled on separately |
| 5 | Cross-tenant fallback is scoped | A caller with a tenant does not silently receive another tenant's registration via `crossTenantLookup` | [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) decision |

Test 4 is the only row that does not wait on the resolution semantics — the disclosure question ("should an anonymous verify name an organisation at all?") is separable, and Stuart's framing is that it can honestly answer *registered / integrity intact / not revoked / anchored yes-no* without naming anyone.

## Out of scope

Everything platform-side — row selection, tenant scoping, and what an anonymous response may contain — is [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents)**, Kamil's**. This ticket only proves the outcome once chosen. Platform-S consumption ([PS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-546/verify-shows-a-permanent-for-certification-and-never-reports-anchoring) / [PS-547](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-547/share-link-verify-re-derives-the-document-by-hash-so-a-duplicate)) is Stuart's and not tracked here.

## References

[KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents) (platform defect, Kamil, Urgent — the blocker) · [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) (Review G parent) · [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor) (Review A) · [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions) (the closed isolation ticket this class belonged to) · [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-anchor-honesty-consistency-a-mock-tx-tx-sim-hash-must-never) (anchor honesty — sibling class) · [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424) (verify family made public) · [KS-478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-478/ks-466-11-state-machineprecondition-400s-resolve-via-ks-188-stateful) (red→green rule) · [PS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-546/verify-shows-a-permanent-for-certification-and-never-reports-anchoring) / [PS-547](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-547/share-link-verify-re-derives-the-document-by-hash-so-a-duplicate) (S-side consumers, merged).

Evidence is Stuart's UAT reproduction and Kamil's root-cause read on [KS-584](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-584/verify-by-hash-selects-the-wrong-registration-certified-documents). Not independently re-verified by me; nothing written.

title: systemTest (Schemathesis): /api/status authorization + revoked-session regression coverage (KS-570 class — vc-issuer status lists)
description:
## Why this exists as a new ticket

Created rather than commented onto an existing one because the systemTest ticket that would naturally carry it — [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions), cross-tenant / cross-owner isolation regressions — is **Done** (PR #590, merged 2026-07-23). Per the [KS-532](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-532/sk-dr-k-side-key-store-restore-path-joint-restore-point-coverage-demo) precedent, appending to a closed ticket means nobody sees it. Scope is **systemTest only**; the platform remediation is [KS-570](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-570/get-apistatus-apileaderboard-accept-revoked-session-jwts-bypass-the) and the (not-yet-filed) authorization gap, both K-side.

## Source — Kamil's severity assessment, [KS-570](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-570/get-apistatus-apileaderboard-accept-revoked-session-jwts-bypass-the), 2026-08-07

[KS-570](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-570/get-apistatus-apileaderboard-accept-revoked-session-jwts-bypass-the) was raised as a revoked-session JWT bypass on two mounts (`/api/status`, `/api/leaderboard/*`) that skip the gateway session check [KS-257](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-257/session-revocation-only-enforced-at-the-auth-service-revoked-session)/[KS-360](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-360/suspendingdeactivating-a-user-doesnt-revoke-active-sessions-access) enforce elsewhere. Kamil's assessment, verified on the local stack against `develop` `c8ce65dca`, found the bypass is the **smaller** half:

> `/api/status` has no authorization whatsoever. `grep -c 'tenantId|organizationId|req.user|requireRole|scopes'` over `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/status.ts` returns **0**. The service applies `jwtAuthenticate()` at `/api` (`services/vc-issuer/src/index.ts:79`), which is signature-only, and the routes add nothing.

His probes, role OWNER (not an admin), valid session:

| Probe | Result |
| -- | -- |
| `POST /api/status/default/revoke` (bogus credentialId) | **404** "Credential not found in status list" — reached business logic, so authz passed. A role gate would have given 403 |
| Same call, no token (control) | 401 — the route is not public; authentication is the only gate |
| `POST /api/status` — create a status list | **201 Created** (`ks570-probe-list`) — a non-admin successfully changed state |

Surface: 4 GET + 4 POST — `GET /:id`, `/:id/check/:index`, `/:id/revoked`, `/`; `POST /:id/allocate`, `/:id/revoke`, `/:id/unrevoke`, `POST /`. `unrevoke` is the sharp end: restoring a deliberately revoked credential to valid is an integrity operation on an authenticity platform, not an information leak.

**Fixing** [KS-570](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-570/get-apistatus-apileaderboard-accept-revoked-session-jwts-bypass-the) **as written does not close the hole.** Adding `authenticateToken(true)` to the two mounts stops revoked sessions; every authenticated user of any role and any tenant retains full access with a perfectly valid session.

## Bounds — stated, not reassurance

Kamil named these deliberately rather than rounding them up:

* `status.ts` makes **zero DB calls** (`grep -c` = 0). `statusListManagers` is a process-local in-memory `Map`, referenced in no other file.
* A `credential_status_lists` table exists (`migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:759`) and issued credentials embed `statusListUrl` + `statusListIndex` (`services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts:103-166`) — but this code never reads or writes that table.
* Consequently an attacker's revoke/unrevoke survives only until the next vc-issuer restart, and is not shared across replicas.
* **He has not verified whether any verification path consults these endpoints.** That single unknown is the difference between High and Urgent, and it is test 0 below.

## Test matrix

Per the standing rule, each test is demonstrated **red on broken code** before it goes green. Everything here is red today — that is the point, and these land as `xfail(strict=True)` with the [KS-570](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-570/get-apistatus-apileaderboard-accept-revoked-session-jwts-bypass-the) reference until the platform fix ships, never as bare skips.

Placement: `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_status_list_authz.py`, following `test_user_admin_isolation.py` / `test_cross_owner_isolation.py`. Anything needing restart or replica behaviour goes to `tests/integration/`.

| # | Property | Assertion | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 0 | **Does anything consume this?** | Issue a credential, read its `statusListUrl` / `statusListIndex`, then assert whether the public verify path resolves status through `/api/status/:id/check/:index`. | Not a security assertion — the **fact-finding test that settles severity**. Kamil named this as the open question; one test answers it. Do this first. |
| 1 | Non-admin cannot create a status list | `POST /api/status` as a plain OWNER → 403 | Red today: returns 201. Reproduces Kamil's probe exactly |
| 2 | Non-admin cannot revoke | `POST /api/status/:id/revoke` as OWNER → 403, **not** 404 | The 404-vs-403 distinction is the whole finding: 404 means authz passed and business logic was reached |
| 3 | Non-admin cannot **unrevoke** | `POST /api/status/:id/unrevoke` as OWNER → 403 | Integrity operation; assert separately from revoke so a partial fix cannot pass |
| 4 | Non-admin cannot allocate | `POST /api/status/:id/allocate` as OWNER → 403 |  |
| 5 | Cross-tenant status lists are not reachable | A list created under tenant A is not readable or mutable from tenant B | Currently unscoped by construction — no `tenantId` anywhere in the file |
| 6 | **Revoked session is refused** — `/api/status` | Authenticate, revoke/suspend the session ([KS-360](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-360/suspendingdeactivating-a-user-doesnt-revoke-active-sessions-access) path), then call each of the 8 routes → 401 | The original [KS-570](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-570/get-apistatus-apileaderboard-accept-revoked-session-jwts-bypass-the) finding. Parameterise over all 8 |
| 7 | **Revoked session is refused** — `/api/leaderboard/*` | Same, over the 3 GET routes | The low-severity half, below |
| 8 | Control — anonymous | Every route above, no token → 401 | Guards against a "fix" that makes the routes public |

## `/api/leaderboard/*` — the low half, folded in here

Three GET routes, no writes (`services/referral/src/routes/leaderboard.ts:39,100,177`). Payload is rank, `displayName`, `totalReferrals`, `qualifiedReferrals`, `totalRewardsEarned`, tier, badge (`formatLeaderboardEntry`). The only PII-ish field is `displayName`, which falls back to `User <first 8 chars of userId>`. No tenant scoping (`grep -c tenantId` = 0) — cross-tenant by construction, which reads as deliberate for a global referral board rather than a leak.

A terminated user reading this sees a leaderboard. That is the whole impact — so it gets tests 7 and 8 only, and **no** authorization assertions. Recording the reasoning so the absence isn't read later as an oversight.

Related: [KS-509](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-509/verify-akto-auth-bypass-locked-account-on-apileaderboard-anonymous-is) (Akto `AUTH_BYPASS_LOCKED_ACCOUNT` on `/api/leaderboard*` — whether the referral-service auth path enforces account-lock/role). Test 7 is the direct answer to that question; coordinate rather than duplicate.

## Out of scope

* The platform fix itself (mount-level `authenticateToken(true)`) — [KS-570](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-570/get-apistatus-apileaderboard-accept-revoked-session-jwts-bypass-the), Kamil.
* The authorization gap — Kamil has **not** filed it as a separate ticket pending Kam's ruling, deliberately, so that closing [KS-570](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-570/get-apistatus-apileaderboard-accept-revoked-session-jwts-bypass-the) does not read as closing both. When it is filed, link it here.
* Whether the in-memory status list should be persisted to `credential_status_lists` at all — a design question, not a regression.

## Acceptance

* Test 0 has run and its answer is written down, including a "nothing consults it" outcome.
* Tests 1–8 exist and execute; each is red against current `develop` and carries `xfail(strict=True)` with a [KS-570](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-570/get-apistatus-apileaderboard-accept-revoked-session-jwts-bypass-the) ref, so it flips loudly when the platform fix lands.
* No bare skips ([KS-478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-478/ks-466-11-state-machineprecondition-400s-resolve-via-ks-188-stateful) red→green rule).
* Unit-tested pure predicates + QA-doc sync per `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` MUSTs #2/#3/#8.

## References

title: DR rehearsal: lose a key → re-key → read-back survives on pre-loss anchors → the old key is dead
description:
## BLUF

@peter asked for this rehearsal on KS-532. **KS-532 is Done and was archived on 2026-08-04, so it rejects comments and nobody would see it** — @kamil.kreiser ruled 2026-08-07 that it gets a fresh ticket rather than a reopen. This is that ticket.

**It needs four steps, not three.** As @peter wrote it, the rehearsal **would pass today while leaving the compromised credential live** — which is the clearest possible illustration of Finding A ([KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577)).

## Detail

**The rehearsal**

1. Anchor a document; record the proof.
2. Re-key the org — `register-connector` with `rotate: true`.
3. Confirm read-back survives on the pre-loss anchor using the **new** key. *(@peter's assertion — expected to hold.)*
4. **Confirm the OLD key no longer works.** *(Added. This is the step that fails today.)*

**Why step 4 matters.** Rotation currently mints without revoking ([KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577)), so steps 1–3 would all pass on a credential that is still live and still valid with identical scopes. A rehearsal that stops at step 3 proves **read-back continuity only, not containment** — and would be reported as a successful DR rehearsal.

**Sequencing.** Steps 1–3 can be run before [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) lands, but the result must be recorded as *continuity only*, explicitly not containment. Step 4 is blocked on [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577).

**Also worth folding in** (@peter's sequencing asks on KS-480): [PS-473](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-473) first — a lost key is recoverable by rotation, a lost GUID mapping is not — and [PS-463](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-463), which is the only detection a botched re-key would have under async anchoring.

**Done when:** all four steps pass on demo and the run is recorded here with its evidence.

---

Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`*; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.*

title: [Decision] Approval shape for bulk re-key — two approvers for a batch, one for a single-org rotation
description:
## BLUF

@peter's proposal: a **batch** re-key needs two approvers; a **single-org** rotation needs one. The shape needs deciding, but it **cannot be implemented until** [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579) **lands** — the shared platform-admin account cannot make a two-approver rule real, because the same credential can satisfy both approvals.

Carried over from @peter's own candidate list on KS-480, unchanged.

## Detail

Open questions for the decision:

* Who counts as an approver, and is the *requester* allowed to be one of the two?
* Is approval synchronous (the call blocks) or a request/approve/execute flow with a record between the steps?
* What is the break-glass path when a genuine incident cannot wait for a second approver, and what does it cost in audit terms?
* Does the second approval cover the whole batch, or the specific list of refs (so the list cannot be edited after approval)?

**Blocked on:** [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579) (per-person platform-admin identities).

**Done when:** the shape is agreed and recorded here, with the break-glass path named explicitly rather than left implicit.

---

title: register-connector: volume alerting, rate limit, and correlation of refused re-key attempts
description:
## BLUF

`register-connector` is the highest-blast-radius admin operation on the platform and has **no volume alerting and no rate limit**. Bulk re-key ([KS-576](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-576)) makes it cheaper to trigger, which raises the cost of leaving it unmonitored.

Carried over from @peter's own candidate list on KS-480, unchanged.

## Detail

The route (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:476`) refuses connector-authorised rotates (`:499-509`) but nothing observes the pattern of use:

* no alert on an unusual **volume** of rotations in a window
* no rate limit on the route itself
* refused re-key attempts are not correlated — a series of 403s from a connector credential probing the rotate path looks like nothing

### Added 2026-09-14 — register #15 from [KS-533](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-533/sk-security-register-data-loss-unrecoverability-scenarios-code) (`externalRef` collision / wrong environment)

Carried here on closing [KS-533](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-533>) (register row #15, Low likelihood, ⚠️ manual merge to recover). Same route, same blast radius, so it belongs with the rate-limit/alerting work rather than on its own ticket.

**Scenario:** a reused or typo'd OrganisationGuid, or a staging S registering against prod K. Duplicate orgs split provenance; `rotate: true` aimed at the wrong org kills a prod key.

**State on** `develop` **today** (`platform.ts:495,537`): `externalRef` is trimmed and checked for presence and `≤128` chars only — no shape check, although §4 defines it as S's Org GUID. Nothing ties the provisioning credential to an environment, so a staging S holding a prod-shaped key is indistinguishable from prod S.

**Add to the done-when:**

* `externalRef` validated as a GUID (400 on anything else) — a typo cannot mint a second org.
* Environment-scoped provisioning credentials: a key minted for one environment is refused by another (env tag in the key record or prefix, checked at `register-connector`), so a staging S cannot register or rotate against prod K.

**Done when:** an anomalous rotation volume raises an alert, the route is rate-limited, and refused attempts are correlated well enough that a probing pattern is visible rather than scattered across logs.

---

title: Append-only recovery audit held outside the estate being recovered
description:
## BLUF

Today's audit for the credential-recovery path is **best-effort, fire-and-forget, and lives inside the estate being recovered** — so the one incident where it matters most is the one where it is least trustworthy.

Carried over from @peter's §4 candidate on KS-480, unchanged.

## Detail

* The rotate handler's audit write is `.catch(() => {})` — `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:698-709`. A failed audit write is silently dropped and the rotate still succeeds.
* `GET /api/audit` is memory-backed (`services/security/src/index.ts:597`), and under fail-closed RLS the boot warm loads nothing (see [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578)).
* The records live in the same Postgres instance as the data being recovered. A compromise or loss that triggers a bulk re-key is exactly the event that can take the evidence of the re-key with it.

**Scope:** an append-only record of recovery actions (who, which refs, when, outcome per ref) written outside the estate, where a failed write is a **loud** failure rather than a swallowed one.

**Done when:** a bulk re-key produces a durable, append-only record that survives loss of the primary estate, and a failed audit write cannot pass silently.

Sizing: 3–5 days.

---

title: Per-person platform-admin identities — the shared seeded admin cannot carry attribution or approval
description:
## BLUF

Platform-admin is a **shared** seeded account today, so no rule that depends on *which person* acted can be made real — including the two-approver shape for bulk re-key ([KS-582](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-582)) and any honest attribution on a recovery action.

Carried over from @peter's own candidate list on KS-480, unchanged.

## Detail

Every guardrail on the `register-connector` path is currently "platform-admin or refuse" (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:499-509`). That is a capability check, not an identity check. Consequences:

* An approval rule ("two approvers for a batch") cannot be enforced — the same shared credential can satisfy both sides.
* Recovery-action audit records the role, not the person.
* Off-boarding a person does not remove their platform-admin access, because the access is not theirs.

**Gates:** [KS-582](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-582) (approval shape) cannot be implemented until this lands.

**Done when:** platform-admin actions attribute to a named person, and the shared seeded account is no longer a route to platform-admin in any environment that matters.

---

title: rotate: true mints a new key but never revokes the old one — implement revoke-on-rotate and agree the cutover window
description:
## BLUF

@kamil.kreiser **ruled 2026-08-07: rotation SHOULD revoke the prior key.** He accepts that this makes an honest bulk re-key ~1.5 weeks rather than 2 days, on the reasoning that shipping the additive version would hand out N new credentials, leave N compromised ones live, and look like recovery.

**The cutover window is a contract question for** @stuart.jamieson**, not a unilateral K-side call** — revoking instantly means S's in-flight anchor writes 401 until it picks up the new credential.

@peter independently reached the same conclusion on KS-480 (2026-08-06): *"if someone left a company with a grudge and used the key maliciously, the company affected would not look kindly on our solution."*

## Detail

**The defect (Finding A, verified in code).** The rotate handler has **no revoke step**: on `rotate: true` it skips the early return at `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:638-645` and goes straight to the mint. `dbSaveApiKey` (`services/security/src/index.ts:196-223`) is a plain upsert on the *new* key's own id and never touches sibling rows sharing a `connectorId`. Validation keys purely off `key_hash` → `isActive` → `expiresAt` (`services/security/src/index.ts:940-1012`), so the prior key keeps validating indefinitely.

Guardrail 1's own comment concedes it — *"it invalidates nothing by itself"* (`platform.ts:501`) — so this is known at code level. What is absent is any sign the semantics were decided deliberately for the DR case that §4/§5 of KS-480 rests on.

**Consequence:** after re-keying a lost credential, the lost credential still works. Neither half of "lose a key, re-key" has a working admin path on demo today (the other half is [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578)).

**The open decision — cutover.** Options to put to @stuart.jamieson, with the consequence stated plainly rather than softened:

1. **Instant revoke.** S's in-flight anchor writes **401 until S picks up the new credential.** Cleanest containment, hardest on S.
2. **Overlap window** (old key valid for a bounded period). Softer on S; leaves a compromised credential live for exactly that window, which is the thing being fixed.
3. **S confirms adoption, then the old key dies.** Best of both, needs an S-side acknowledgement path and a fallback for when it never arrives.

**Done when:** the cutover shape is agreed with @stuart.jamieson and recorded here; `rotate: true` deactivates the prior key per that shape; a test pins that the old key no longer validates; and [KS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-583) step 4 passes.

Sizing: decision first, then 2–3 days.

---

Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`*; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.*

title: Bulk re-key: one admin-authorised rotate across a named set of externalRefs
description:
## BLUF

@peter asked for **one** admin-authorised action that re-keys a named set of Organisations by `externalRef`, instead of N separate `register-connector` calls during an incident. The loop itself is **1–2 days**.

**It must not ship before** [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) **(revoke-on-rotate).** Built on today's additive rotate, a bulk re-key would hand out N new credentials, leave N compromised ones live, and *look* like recovery.

## Detail

Today's single-org path is `POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector` with `rotate: true` — `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:476-729`:

* platform-admin only; guardrail 1 refuses a connector-authorised rotate with 403 (`:499-509`)
* resolves the org by `metadata->>'externalRef'` under platform scope (`:590-593`)
* mints a fresh `sk_` key via the security service (`:674-686` → `services/security/src/index.ts:800`)
* plaintext key returned exactly once (`:719-720`)

`runWithPlatformScope` (`packages/shared/src/db/tenant-guc.ts:102`) already handles the cross-tenant access, so multi-tenancy is **not** the hard part here.

**Scope**

* Extract `platform.ts:476-729` into a reusable per-org function; add a bulk route taking a list of `externalRef`s.
* Return a **per-ref result array** — partial success must be explicit. An incident operator has to know which refs failed and why.
* OpenAPI entry + `generate-openapi` regen + api-gateway rebuild (the gateway bakes the spec) + KS-380 preflight.

**Explicitly out of scope:** delivery of the key material for N keys. One response body carrying N live secrets is not the answer; that needs its own design and a security review (see the KS-480 sizing table).

**Cheaper alternative on the record** (raised because @peter asked not to have the manual path assumed away): a scripted loop over the existing admin endpoint gives one *operator action* today at near-zero build cost. It does not give one *authorisation*, which is the part actually being asked for.

**Done when:** an admin can re-key a named set of refs in one authorised call, each prior key is revoked per the [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) semantics, per-ref outcomes are explicit, and the [KS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-583) rehearsal passes all four steps.

---

title: systemTest (Schemathesis): pin the KS-546 unhandledRejection posture — config drift + the mirrored KS-529 guard
description:
Work-stream **G** child of [KS-492](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492>). Origin ticket: [**KS-546**](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546>) — *unhandledRejection posture: api-gateway survives (log+alert), everything else stays fail-fast* (Kam, 2026-07-31; Done 2026-08-03, PR #621, **archived 2026-08-04**). Root outage class: [KS-529](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-529>).

## Why a systemTest is required when unit tests already exist

The [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything) **decision logic** is well covered and this ticket does **not** duplicate it. `packages/shared/src/__tests__/gracefulShutdown.unhandledRejection.test.ts` has 8 cases (mode precedence option > env > default, unrecognised values fall back to `exit`, `survive` never calls shutdown, occurrence counter, non-Error stringify). That is a pure function with no I/O — a live test of it would be slower, flakier, and would add nothing.

What unit tests **structurally cannot reach** is that the posture is only ever as real as its configuration and its wiring, and both live outside the test boundary:

1. **The posture is one env var in two files.** `UNHANDLED_REJECTION_MODE=survive` exists only in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:325` and `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/services.bicep`. Drop either in a merge or an env refactor and every unit test stays green while the gateway silently reverts to the [KS-529](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-529/gateway-intermittent-502-bad-gateway-to-healthy-upstreams-under-sweep) posture — one malformed authenticated request = platform-wide outage. Nothing in the repo reads those files.
2. **The** [KS-529](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-529/gateway-intermittent-502-bad-gateway-to-healthy-upstreams-under-sweep) **guard test is a mirror, not the guard.** `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks529-non-object-body-guard.test.ts` re-implements the predicate in the test file (`// Mirrors the guard in routes/verification.ts`). Deleting the real guard from the route leaves the suite green. The one thing that actually proved the fix — 9 malformed bodies → 400 each, `RestartCount` unchanged — was a manual live run recorded on the ticket, and is automated nowhere.
3. **The mode is resolved at boot from the environment**, so only a running container can show which posture actually shipped.

Per the standing rule (*a fix is proven by a test red on broken code, green after*), the [KS-529](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-529/gateway-intermittent-502-bad-gateway-to-healthy-upstreams-under-sweep) regression has no test that would fail if the fix were reverted. That is the gap this ticket closes.

## Scope

* **Config assertion (cheap, offline):** the api-gateway service block in both `docker-compose.yml` and `services.bicep` declares `UNHANDLED_REJECTION_MODE=survive`, and **no other service does**. Fails on drift in either direction.
* **De-mirror the** [KS-529](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-529/gateway-intermittent-502-bad-gateway-to-healthy-upstreams-under-sweep) **guard test:** export the real predicate from `routes/verification.ts` and assert against it instead of a copy, so deleting the guard turns the test red.
* **Live regression (systemTest tier):** against the local stack on `:6882`, POST the exact DoS payloads (`null`, `[]`, `42`, `"str"`, `true`) to `/api/documents` authenticated → 400 each, and the api-gateway container's `RestartCount` is unchanged across the run. This is the manual proof from [KS-529](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-529/gateway-intermittent-502-bad-gateway-to-healthy-upstreams-under-sweep), automated.
* **Boot-posture assertion:** gateway boot log contains `unhandledRejection mode: survive`; a sampled non-gateway service does not.

## Findings surfaced while scoping (NOT in scope here — backend, Kamil)

Recorded so they are not lost; both are platform-side, so they belong to Review B / the [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything) follow-up, not to G:

* `setupGracefulShutdown` **has zero call sites.** `rg "setupGracefulShutdown"` outside `packages/shared` returns nothing. All the mode plumbing in `packages/shared/src/utils/gracefulShutdown.ts:99-179` — including the `Graceful shutdown handlers registered (unhandledRejection mode: X)` line [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything)'s Verify section says to check — never executes. The only live path is the gateway wiring the exported pieces directly at `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:1072`. [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything)'s *"all other services log* `exit`*"* is therefore unobservable as written.
* **originate is not fail-fast.** `services/originate/src/index.ts:64-69` registers its own `unhandledRejection` listener that logs, calls `trackError`, and returns — **no exit**. Registering a listener also suppresses Node 24's fatal default, so originate already *survives* rejections. The gateway's own comment cites "originate's own handler" as the example of the fleet staying fail-fast, which is backwards. Either originate is a second, undocumented `survive` service or it is a bug — but *"everything else stays fail-fast"* is not true as shipped.

Services with no listener do fail fast correctly (base images are `node:24-alpine`, fatal default).

## Acceptance

Each test is red against a deliberately reverted posture (env var removed / guard deleted) and green after; the live leg runs in the pre-merge tier. **systemTest changes only — local commits, no GitHub push/PR/issue interaction** ([KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) convention); backend remediation of the two findings above stays with Kamil.

title: systemTest (Schemathesis): KS-539 agent document-operation rules — onBehalfOf realignment (G-1) + R2/R4/R5/R6 regression coverage
description:
systemTest consequences of the [KS-539](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-539/k-define-governing-rules-for-document-operations-by-agents) agent document-operation rules doc and Kam's G-1 split ruling (2026-08-05, WED-65): **onBehalfOf pattern = share / revoke / transfer-custody · connector pattern = anchor / lifecycle**. Raised from Peter's sign-off comment on [https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-539](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-539>) — filed here so the test-side work doesn't get lost behind the doc closing. Implementation side is [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from); this ticket is the systemTest side only.

## 1. `schemathesis.toml` documents the superseded §6 list

`systemTest/schemathesis/schemathesis.toml:331-352` is the only `onBehalfOf` reference in systemTest source. Its comment block enumerates the honoured-surface set from the accepted 07-29 contract §6 — including **lifecycle-events** and **flat** `POST /api/anchors`, both now superseded to connector-only attribution — and cites Peter's 2026-07-29 sign-off as the authority.

Rewrite the block to the ruled split, and re-cite it to the 2026-08-05 ruling. **Sequencing: this lands with** [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from)**, not before** — otherwise the config and the code disagree in whichever direction lands first.

## 2. Revoke needs the connector-only expected-statuses exception

Today only `/share` (`:355-357`) and `/transfer-custody` (`:359-361`) carry the `positive_data_acceptance.expected-statuses` exception. Once [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) adds `onBehalfOf` extraction to **revoke**, a JWT persona sending the field gets the deliberate 400 ("connector-only") and the sweep goes red on correct behaviour. Add the matching `[[operations]]` entry for the revoke route in the **same PR as** [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from).

Lifecycle-events + flat `/api/anchors` move the other way — whether anything is needed depends on whether the field leaves the spec or is merely ignored. If the spec changes, **rebuild api-gateway on local + demo** (the image bundles `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`).

## 3. R2 / R4 / R5 / R6 have no end-to-end systemTest coverage

As `docs/security/AGENT-DOCUMENT-OPERATION-RULES.md` itself notes, the schemathesis sweep authenticates as **JWT personas**, so it only ever exercises the *refused* path. Untested end-to-end:

* **R2** — scopes as authority, deny-by-default
* **R4** — consent chains through the Organisation (cross-org 403)
* **R5** — provenance never on-chain (pinned only by the `ks480-provenance.test.ts` unit test)
* **R6** — server-side layered enforcement: connector key revocation and 10-minute JWT expiry

`http_client.py` already supports `x-api-key`, so this is **coverage work, not plumbing**: drive the accepted connector-key path and assert the refusals.

## Acceptance

* Config block (1) + revoke exception (2) land with [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from); sweep green against the aligned code.
* R2/R4/R5/R6 each get a regression that is **red on the broken behaviour, green after** — no skips, no report-only ([KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) standard).
* Live Docker sweep on :6882 before Done, not offline gates alone.

## Refs

* [KS-539](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-539/k-define-governing-rules-for-document-operations-by-agents) rules doc + G-1 ruling — [https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-539](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-539>) (PRs [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#632](https://linear.app/secuura/review/docsks-539-governing-rules-for-agent-document-operations-c61a242d41fc), [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#648](https://linear.app/secuura/review/docsks-539-g-1-split-ruling-onbehalfof-sharerevoketransfer-connector-b73850970a5e))
* [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) — implementation alignment (blocks items 1 + 2)
* [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) §6 contract · [KS-547](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-547/decision-certificationsissue-has-no-role-gate-any-authenticated-user) (certify, unchanged by the ruling) · [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks-480-option-a) (adjacent connector-identity coverage)

title: systemTest (Schemathesis): S↔K connector identity regression coverage (KS-480 Option A) — tier separation, rotation read-back, provenance exclusion
description:
## Why

[KS-480](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480>) landed the S↔K ownership contract (Option A — passwordless per-Organisation `sk_` connector identity, two credential tiers, `onBehalfOf` provenance). The security properties that sign-off rests on are currently asserted by **manual probes in ticket comments**, not by tests. This ticket adds the regression coverage so they stay true.

The properties at stake, and how each is verified today:

| Property | Verified today by |
| -- | -- |
| Provenance never reaches the chain | K-side unit test (`ks480-provenance-exclusion.test.ts`) — no systemTest regression; Peter owed this one at sign-off (§6-1) |
| Provisioning tier cannot touch documents / operational tier cannot provision | Kam's manual curl probes, local + demo |
| Read-back survives key rotation | **One manual probe by Stuart**, once |
| Revoked key fails closed | Not verified |
| Cross-org `onBehalfOf` → 403 | Manual probe on document-create only |
| Erasure pseudonymises rather than deletes | Manual DB inspection |

Scope is systemTest only. All Platform-K implementation work arising from [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) belongs on separate K-side tickets.

## ⚠ Blocking prerequisite — [KS-516](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-516>)

**No real seeded** `sk_*` **key exists in any test environment.** `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/conftest.py:78` falls back to the placeholder `sk_test_abc123xyz789…`, and `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_document_lifecycle.py:231-272` **skips** the API-key document-creation test for exactly this reason. Every test below needs real key material, so [KS-516](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-516/schemathesis-systemtest-seed-a-real-sk-api-key-documentswrite-so-the) is a hard dependency.

[KS-516](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-516/schemathesis-systemtest-seed-a-real-sk-api-key-documentswrite-so-the) as written seeds one key (`documents:write`). This ticket needs **two**, matching the two tiers:

1. a **provisioning** key scoped `organizations:register` only;
2. an **operational** key with the §8 set (`documents:read/write`, `documents:share`, `documents:transfer-custody`, `anchors:read/write`, `certifications:write`).

## Placement

* Authz-matrix tests → `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_connector_identity.py`, following the existing patterns in `test_cross_owner_isolation.py`, `test_tenant_isolation.py`, `test_user_admin_isolation.py`.
* Anything requiring rotation, revocation or DB state → `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/integration/`, alongside `test_anchoring_fail_closed.py` (live Docker stack on :6882).

## Test matrix

Per the standing rule, **each test must be demonstrated red on broken code before it goes green** — the "make it red" column is part of the deliverable, not a suggestion.

| # | Property | Assertion | Make it red first |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Provenance never reaches the chain (§6-1) | Create a document via the operational key with `onBehalfOf` populated; read the anchor row's `metadata_payload`; assert the **key set matches the whitelist exactly** and contains no email, displayName or externalRef. Key-set equality, not value absence — a value-only check silently passes when a new field is added. | Add a provenance field to the payload builder locally; test must fail. |
| 2 | Tier separation, both directions | Provisioning key → `GET`/`POST /api/documents` = 403, `POST /api/anchors` = 403. Operational key → `POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector` = 403. | Mint a key holding both scope sets; both assertions must fail. |
| 3 | Provisioning cannot self-escalate | Attempt to mint `organizations:register` from a provisioning key (403) and a wildcard `*` / `<resource>:*` (403). Drive against the **security service directly**, not only the gateway route — that is where the guard lives, and a key can be presented there directly. | Point the test at the route only; it passes while the direct path is open. |
| 4 | **Read-back survives rotation** | Anchor a document under an operational key → rotate that org's key (`rotate: true`) → read the pre-rotation document with the **new** key = 200. Read it with a **different org's** key = 404 (cloak intact). | This is the property the entire DR posture rests on and it currently has one manual observation behind it. |
| 5 | Revoked key fails closed | Revoke a key; assert read **and** write both fail with an auth error, and that the write does not return 2xx-with-no-effect. Assert no row was created. | The silent-no-op case is the one that matters — async anchoring hides write failures entirely. |
| 6 | Cross-org attribution → 403 on **all seven** endpoints | Parameterise over `POST /api/documents`, `/{id}/version`, `/{id}/share`, `/{id}/transfer-custody`, `/{id}/lifecycle-events`, `POST /api/certifications/issue`, flat `POST /api/anchors`. `onBehalfOf` naming a user in another Organisation → 403 on every one. | Drop the check on a single endpoint locally; the parameterised case must fail for that endpoint alone. |
| 7 | Erasure pseudonymises, not deletes | After erasure the provenance row echoes `{email: null, externalRef: <unchanged>, pseudonymised: true}` — assert `externalRef` is **still present**. | Change erasure to hard-delete locally; test must fail. One assertion pair catches both failure modes (leaving PII, and destroying the attribution record). |
| 8 | Connector token exchange doesn't leak | Assert the short-lived connector JWT never appears in a response body or error, and that a caller-supplied `Authorization` header cannot override the key-derived principal. | The exchange is invisible to S, so a leak or an override would otherwise be silent. |

## Conditional extension

If the **admin-authorised bulk re-key** path is built (requested on [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) §4/§5 — Stuart's option 2, pending Kam's sizing), extend with: re-key over a named `externalRef` set requires admin auth (connector key → 403) · refs outside the caller's tenant refused · read-back survives the batch for **every** ref in it · the refused-attempt path emits its audit record.

## Out of scope

* **The human approval process itself.** Two-approver authorisation, out-of-band verification and approver-initiated recovery are runbook and rehearsal matters, not automated tests. Covered by the demo rehearsal proposed on [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) (lose a key → re-key → confirm read-back survives on documents anchored before the loss), which is [KS-532](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-532>) territory.
* **All Platform-K implementation work** arising from [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) — per-person platform-admin identities, append-only recovery audit held outside the recovered estate, `register-connector` audit/alerting/rate-limit, refused-re-key correlation, and the bulk re-key path. Separate K-side tickets; this one only proves what exists.

## References

[KS-480](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480>) contract + sign-off · [KS-516](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-516>) seeded key (blocking) · [KS-492](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492>) parent work-stream · [KS-485](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-485>) security review umbrella · [KS-533](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-533>) data-loss register · [KS-532](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-532>) K-side DR · [PS-287 ](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-287>)`@k-live` suite · [PS-473](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-473>) S-side GUID mapping / key store · contract doc `Blockchain/Dev/docs/S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md`.
