title: Review F — Edge, WAF, DDoS & anti-automation
description:
> ## ✅ F-9 RESOLVED — added 2026-08-17. **The row is FALSE at the live edge: all three portals already serve their own CSP. Do NOT add one at the gateway — it would break them.**
>
> **F-9 is closed on this ticket. KS-491 itself stays OPEN** for the two rows that are still live: the **strategic WAF gap** and the **absent Caddyfile**.
>
> ### 1. The claim, tested at the internet-facing edge
>
> Three read-only GETs against `https://secuura02-demo.southeastasia.cloudapp.azure.com`:
>
> | Path | CSP served? | Distinguishing directive |
> | -- | -- | -- |
> | `/` (issuer) | **yes** | `script-src … 'unsafe-eval'` — issuer only |
> | `/admin/` | **yes** | `connect-src … wss://*.secuura.io` — admin only |
> | `/verify/` | **yes** | `frame-ancestors 'self' https://*.secuura.io https://secuura.io` |
>
> **They differ from one another, and that difference is the discriminator.** A single `add_header` at the gateway would make all three byte-identical. Control: `/api/health` returns a **fourth, different** CSP from the API service — so a CSP on this host is not a gateway-wide artefact.
>
> Source side agrees: **8** `Content-Security-Policy` occurrences across `frontend/{issuer,verifier,admin,outlook-addin}/nginx.conf`, and the gateway does **not** `proxy_hide_header Content-Security-Policy`, so downstream policies pass through untouched. It *does* hide-and-re-add `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy` and HSTS — which is why those five are gateway-owned and CSP is not. The file is internally consistent.
>
> ### 2. The gateway's abstention is a decision, and it is NEWER than this row
>
> `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf:240-245`, immediately above the live header block:
>
> > *"CSP is DELIBERATELY NOT SET HERE. It is app-specific — issuer, admin and verifier each ship their own — and a single generic policy at the gateway would either be too loose to be worth having or would break a portal. Owning it here would also silently override a tighter downstream policy. That stays with the apps; tracked as its own decision, not smuggled in."*
>
> `git log -S"DELIBERATELY NOT SET HERE"` attributes it to exactly one commit — `045c658ec`**, 2026-08-13, "KS-613/KS-615: harden the live gateway edge…" (#678)** — the same hardening pass that fixed F-2, F-6 and F-7. Sentinel control returns empty. **The missing gateway CSP is not an oversight this review caught; it is a decision the F-remediation took afterwards, in writing.**
>
> ### 3. Why "just add one" is actively harmful, not merely redundant
>
> Two `Content-Security-Policy` headers are **not merged**. Each policy is enforced independently, so a resource must satisfy **both** — the effective policy is the **intersection**. Intersecting the commented-out `:595` policy against what admin actually serves:
>
> | directive | `:595` policy | admin's live policy | effective | consequence |
> | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
> | `connect-src` | `'self' https://*.blockfrost.io` | `'self' http://localhost:* https://*.secuura.io wss://*.secuura.io` | `'self'` | **admin's XHR/WebSocket blocked** |
> | `script-src` | `'self' 'unsafe-inline'` | `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` | `'self'` | **wasm blocked, all three portals** |
> | `img-src` | `'self' data: https:` | `'self' data: https: blob:` | loses `blob:` | **blob images blocked** |
> | `worker-src` | absent → falls back to `script-src` | `'self' blob:` | loses `blob:` | **blob workers blocked** |
>
> That is the portal-breaking outcome the in-file comment predicts, arrived at independently.
>
> ### 4. Recorded so it is not re-derived
>
> Two things stated explicitly because a later reader will otherwise repeat the work:
>
> * `frame-ancestors` **is NOT part of the breakage.** It does not fall back to `default-src`, so an unspecified `frame-ancestors` in a gateway policy leaves each portal's own value governing. An earlier note of mine claimed otherwise; it was wrong and the four rows above stand without it.
> * `outlook-addin` **is not routed through this gateway** (0 matches for `outlook` in `nginx-demo.conf`), so its policy is unaffected either way.
>
> ### 5. The real question this surfaced → **KS-648**
>
> The policies exist and are well-formed, but two directives are weak: `'unsafe-eval'` **on the issuer alone** (the other two manage on `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`) and `'unsafe-inline'` **styles on all three**. That is an app-level quality question, exactly as the in-file comment says — filed as [KS-648](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-648), Low, in the Security Review project. **Not** part of F-9.
>
> *Established read-only: three GETs,* `git log -S`*, and greps over the tree. No code changed, nothing deployed, no probe whose success path writes. F-9's deploy authorisation was retired rather than released.*

---

> ## ⚠️ STATUS BANNER — added 2026-08-16. **The table below says "0** `limit_req`**, 0** `client_max_body_size`**". That is now FALSE, and the fix is CONFIRMED LIVE ON THE VM.**
>
> **This resolves the open question of whether F's edge hardening was merged-but-undeployed. It is deployed.** Established read-only, with no rate-limit or body-cap probe against the live demo.
>
> ### F-2 / F-7 — fixed in code **and live**
>
> | Measure | Register says | Repo today | **Running container** |
> | -- | -- | -- | -- |
> | `limit_req` | **0** | **9** | **9** |
> | `limit_conn` | 0 | **4** | — |
> | `client_max_body_size` | **0** | **12m** (`:215`) | — |
>
> **The proof that it is live, rather than merely merged:**
>
> * `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf` on the VM is **byte-identical to the repo copy** — md5 `8be17f5b075d51a170269cd404dc6a87` on both.
> * The **running** `secuura-nginx-gateway` **container** serves `/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf` at the **same md5**, so this is the config nginx actually loaded, not just a file sitting on the host disk.
> * Ordering closes it: conf mtime `2026-08-13T00:09:07Z`, container start `2026-08-14T05:06:57Z` — **the container started after the file's last modification**, so it cannot be serving an older copy. `nginx -t` passes.
>
> This matters because **the conf is bind-mounted, not baked into the image** — an image rebuild proves nothing about it either way, which is exactly why the merge alone was not evidence. Shipped by KS-613/#678 and KS-616/#679.
>
> ### Why the earlier "unestablished" reading was right at the time
>
> A single GET returns HSTS, CSP and `X-Frame-Options`, and **none of those discriminate**: the CSP cannot come from this conf (its own is commented out — see below), and Caddy terminates TLS in front, making HSTS unattributable. **Reading the mounted file was the check that discriminates**; the header response was not.
>
> ### Still open
>
> * **F-9 partial — CSP is still commented out at** `nginx-demo.conf:595`**.** `X-Frame-Options` and HSTS are active; the CSP line is inert. Verified today.
> * The **strategic Crit row (no WAF anywhere)** stands unchanged — it is a greenfield gap, not a stale row.
> * **Caddyfile still absent from the repo**, so the TLS edge remains unversioned.
>
> *Banner added during the session-38 closure sweep. Ticket left **open** for F-9's CSP, the WAF row, and the Caddyfile.*

---

Work-stream **F** of the [Platform K security review](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-485>). Forward-looking edge & resilience posture for a millions-of-users, continuously-attacked target. Largely a **gap analysis** — what's ABSENT matters as much as what's present. Recon complete on `develop` @ `fcf2d878c`.

**Scope / checklist**

* WAF: is any WAF present (nginx ModSecurity / Front Door / App Gateway WAF / Cloudflare)? Where would it integrate? (Product owner explicitly wants WAF.)
* Edge config: nginx gateway + Caddy — security headers, request-size limits, timeouts, TLS.
* Rate limiting / DDoS: edge + app tier; connection/request caps; Slowloris/large-body.
* Bot / anti-automation: CAPTCHA on signup/login/verify.
* Secret manager (runtime) & observability/alerting; network segmentation of infra services.

## Findings / recommendations (develop @ fcf2d878c)

| Sev | Evidence | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Crit (strategic) | repo-wide absent; `deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md:50` | **No WAF** anywhere — no ModSecurity, no Front Door/App Gateway WAF; Cloudflare is DNS-only (grey-cloud), so no Cloudflare WAF. Greenfield. Integration point: in front of Caddy (Front Door WAF) or a ModSecurity sidecar at the gateway. |
| High | `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf` (0 `limit_req`, 0 `client_max_body_size`) | The **live** gateway conf has no edge rate-limit and no request-body cap. The hardened `nginx-production.conf:21-22,216` (10r/s, 2r/s auth, `client_max_body_size 10m`) is for the **decommissioned** Container Apps path only — never runs today. Port these to the live conf. |
| High | Caddyfile absent from repo | The actual TLS edge (Caddy on the VM) is **not version-controlled** → TLS ciphers/protocols, HSTS, timeouts, body limits unauditable and drift-prone. Commit the Caddyfile. |
| High | `docker-compose.yml:63-64` (`6432:5432`), `:118-119` (`6379:6379`) | Postgres + Redis publish to host `0.0.0.0` ("remove in production" comments, but active). On the VM these are internet-reachable unless the NSG/ufw blocks them — relies on an external firewall, not config. Bind to the internal network. |
| High | repo-wide absent | **No** CAPTCHA/reCAPTCHA/hCaptcha/Turnstile on signup, login, or public verify. Only IP/velocity limits stand between a botnet and account/verify abuse. |
| Med | `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/rateLimitEnforce.ts:135-137` | App-tier limiters fail **open** on error; if Redis is down the per-client counter degrades to per-replica in-memory (inflated ceiling — [KS-170](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-170/enforceclientratelimit-runs-in-memory-per-replica-wire-the-redis)). |
| Med | `nginx-demo.conf` (no `limit_conn`/`client_body_timeout`/`client_header_timeout`) | No Slowloris/large-body/slow-request protection at the live edge. |
| Low | `nginx-demo.conf` (no active HSTS/CSP `add_header`) | Gateway emits no security headers of its own; relies wholly on downstream helmet + Caddy. Single point of omission if a service skips helmet. |

**GREEN (verified):** app-tier defence is real and layered — `express-rate-limit` global limiter (`api-gateway/src/index.ts:448`, 300/min prod), per-route login (15/15min, `:849`), register (`:861`), verification (`:469`) limiters; per-API-key distributed Redis limiter (`rateLimitEnforce.ts`); **application-level account lockout** on login (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:285-303`). Helmet provides per-service CSP + HSTS + nosniff. A standalone `observability/` module exists. The pen-tested `nginx-production.conf` is a strong hardening template — it just isn't the config in production.

**Acceptance:** WAF introduced at the edge; live gateway/Caddy config carries rate-limits/body-caps/headers; pg/redis bound internal; bot protection on public auth/verify; each with a verification test where feasible (Review G). Several items here are **new-build recommendations**, not code defects — track as remediation issues with owners.

title: Security review — plan, methodology & handover (Platform K)
description:
> **This issue is the coordination hub and living plan for the Platform K security review.** It holds the scope, threat model, methodology, the index of review work-streams, the evidence-cited findings register, remediation sequencing, and full handover context so anyone can pick this up cold. Modelled on the Platform S plan [PS-175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-175).
>
> **v1 — grounded 2026-07-21 against** `develop` **@** `fcf2d878c` (161 commits since 2026-07-01). Register built from a 6-stream parallel recon (A–F); each finding cites `file:line` under `Blockchain/Dev/` on develop.

## 1. Target & threat context

* **System:** platform-k = the Secuura Cardano/blockchain anchoring platform. Node.js microservices monorepo (28 backend services: api-gateway, auth, originate, anchoring, timestamping, kyc, billing, analytics, m365-integration, tenant-provisioning, wallet-connector, nft-certificate, vc-issuer, security, governance, guardian, etc.), PostgreSQL/Prisma + RLS, Redis, Aiken smart contracts on Cardano, three React frontends (Issuer/Verifier/Admin) + Outlook/Gmail add-ins.
* **Code:** `Distributed_Secuura`, remote `github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura.git`, branch `develop`. Platform under `Blockchain/Dev/`.
* **Live env (2026-07-08,** [KS-414](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-414/demo-env-cost-pivot-replace-container-apps-with-a-single-vm-running)): single Azure VM — Caddy auto-TLS → compose nginx gateway (`nginx-demo.conf`) at `https://demo-pk.secuura.net`. The Container Apps template + hardened `nginx-production.conf` are **decommissioned/unused**. **⚠ v1 claimed** `SIMULATE_ANCHORING=true` **in the demo. That is FALSE (corrected 2026-08-13).** The demo does **real** Cardano `preview`-testnet anchoring: `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` is unset, `BLOCKFROST_API_KEY` is set, anchoring boots `cardanoMode: REAL (Blockfrost)`, and a funded **platform wallet mnemonic is present on the VM**. Treat the anchoring path on the live target as a live chain-submission path with key material, not a simulation — see the re-grounding comment (2026-08-13) and KS-535 / KS-607.
* **Integrations:** platform-s (SSD document platform, the S↔K channel — K is the server), Stripe (billing), Microsoft 365 / Entra Verified-ID (KYC/IDV), M365 Graph (Outlook/Gmail add-ins), Cardano (Blockfrost).
* **Protects:** legally-significant artefacts (on-chain anchors, timestamps, VCs/NFTs, document hashes), PII, org/tenant data, payment flows, per-tenant connector credentials.
* **Threat assumptions:** millions of users, high public profile, under continuous attack. Treat availability, tenant isolation, and **anchor/signature integrity** as first-order.

## 2. Objectives

1. Evidence-cited findings register (`file:line`, severity) across the whole attack surface — kept current with develop.
2. Prioritised, **sequenced** remediation issues with owners and acceptance criteria (see §5).
3. Strategic hardening for scale — WAF, bot/anti-automation, edge rate-limits/body-caps, secret manager at runtime, DDoS protection, observability/alerting.
4. Repeatable security gates (make the report-only CI scans blocking; keep the [KS-470](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-470/npm-audit-25-transitive-advisories-on-the-develop-lockfile) audit-gate + lockfile clean-room green) so posture doesn't regress.
5. A **security regression test** for every confirmed finding, in the right harness (systemTest — schemathesis / Akto / cross-tenant-isolation / Playwright).

## 3. Scope & review work-streams

Recon streams A–F are **complete** (this v1 pass). Work-stream owners: **Kamil** for A–F + H; **Peter** for G (systemTest).

> **Table amended 2026-08-13** — the v1 table showed six streams all reading "Recon done", which had drifted from the board in both directions and **omitted Review H entirely** (created by comment on 2026-07-21, closed 2026-08-02). A wrong index costs every future reader. `Status` below is the live Linear state; `Recon` records whether the v1 recon pass covered it.

| \# | Work-stream | Issue | Owner | Recon | Status (live 2026-08-13) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| A | AuthN / AuthZ / tenancy & IDOR | [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486) | Kamil | done | **In Review** |
| B | Input validation, injection, upload, XSS/SSRF & crypto | [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487) | Kamil | done | Todo |
| C | S↔K channel, payments/webhooks & integrations (M365 / KYC / wallet / email) | [KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488) | Kamil | done | Todo |
| D | Blockchain / anchoring / smart-contract integrity | [KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489) | Kamil | done | **In Review** |
| E | Deployment, containers & CI/CD supply chain | [KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490) | Kamil | done | Todo |
| F | Edge, WAF, DDoS & anti-automation | [KS-491](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-491) | Kamil | done | **Todo — IN PROGRESS 2026-08-13** (untouched 07-21 → 08-13) |
| **G** | **systemTest security regression coverage** | [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492) | **Peter** | n/a | Standing (Todo) |
| **H** | **Dependency currency & known-vuln package upgrades** | [KS-493](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-493) | Kamil | done (pass-2) | ✅ **Done 2026-08-02** |

**Deferred as its own sequenced pass:** re-recon of streams A–F against the 168 commits / 202 changed files landed since v1's baseline `fcf2d878c`. Tracked as [KS-612](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-612) (child of this issue) — this re-grounding refreshed the *plan*, not the findings.

## 4. Methodology

Recon → findings register (severity-rated, evidence-cited, mapped loosely to OWASP ASVS / Top 10) → triage (severity × exploitability × blast-radius-at-scale) → sequenced remediation issues with acceptance criteria → verification (reproduce pre-fix, confirm blocked post-fix, add a systemTest regression). **Re-ground the register against develop whenever the branch has materially moved** (the [PS-175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-175/security-review-plan-methodology-and-handover-platform-s) v2 pass is the template).

## 5. Findings register + remediation sequencing

**Legend:** Sev = severity as found on develop @ `fcf2d878c`. All rows cite `Blockchain/Dev/…`. Full evidence + GREEN notes live on each work-stream issue.

### A — AuthN / AuthZ / tenancy & IDOR — [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Med | `services/api-gateway/src/routes/notifications.ts:242-272` | `POST /api/notifications` takes `userId` from body, no self/admin check → spoofed `security`/`system` notifications w/ `actionUrl` to anyone (in-app phishing / BOLA). |
| Med | `services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts:173-205`; transfer `routes/documents.ts:1318` | Documents scoped by `tenant_id` only, never `owner_user_id` — any user in a tenant can read/mutate/transfer another user's doc. Confirm intended tenant==org boundary. |
| Med | `services/originate/src/index.ts:220-227`; `routes/documents.ts:131-133` | Tenant scope derived from inbound `x-tenant-id`; originate JWT has no `tenantId` to cross-check → pure header trust. Safe only via gateway strip + RLS; header-forwarding/SSRF re-opens [KS-4](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-4/critical-cross-tenant-document-leak-via-x-tenant-override-bug)-class cross-tenant read. |
| Low | `services/auth/src/routes/mfa.ts:225-236` | `mfa/verify` validates TOTP with no proof factor-1 passed (standalone TOTP oracle; issues no tokens). |
| Low | gateway `middleware/auth.ts:106-150` vs auth `middleware/authenticate.ts:19-65` | `test_token_*` backdoor guarded asymmetrically — one mis-set env = role/tenant spoof. |

### B — Input validation, injection, upload, XSS/SSRF & crypto — [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| High | `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:1072,1202` | Teams `webhookUrl` validated only by `z.string().url()` — no SSRF guard; `fetch()` to `169.254.169.254`/RFC1918/localhost. |
| Med | `services/originate/src/routes/webhooks.ts:153-205,455-490` | `validateWebhookUrl` blocks only IP literals (no DNS resolution → DNS-rebind) and only at registration, not send time. |
| Med | `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:1769-1773` (+`:36`) | `POST /api/admin/seed-demo-users` mints ORG_ADMIN/OWNER w/ hardcoded `admin123`; no `NODE_ENV`/`ENABLE_DEMO_SEED` gate. |
| Med | `services/kyc/src/index.ts:251` | ID images stored from caller-supplied `mimeType`, no magic-byte verification. |
| Low | `frontend/outlook-addin/src/taskpane/index.tsx:60` | `el.innerHTML` interpolates `${e.message}` — unescaped sink (error path). |

### C — S↔K channel, payments/webhooks & integrations — [KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| High | `services/kyc/src/routes/microsoft-verification.ts:201` | Callback authed by static `api-key` w/ hardcoded default `'secuura-kyc-callback'` → forge Entra Verified-ID results. |
| High | `services/wallet-connector/src/server.ts:246-259` | `POST /api/wallets/verify` is a stub — always `verified:true`. Wallet-ownership proof fully bypassable. |
| Med | `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:138-161,235-243` | Graph access+refresh tokens persisted to Postgres in plaintext. |
| Med | `services/billing/src/routes/webhooks.ts:34-37` | `isEventProcessed` fails **open** on DB-unavailable → redelivered Stripe event re-adds credits. |
| Low | `services/auth/src/services/email.ts:40-45,148-149` | No CRLF sanitisation on `documentTitle`→`subject`; no recipient-domain allow-list. |
| Low | `frontend/gmail-addon/Code.gs:17-18` | Hardcoded to decommissioned Container Apps URLs (stale). |

### D — Blockchain / anchoring / smart-contract integrity — [KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| High | `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:582-593` | On anchoring-POST failure with `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` unset (**default**), fabricates `tx_sim_…` + `status:'anchored'` — outage → fake anchored doc. No `NODE_ENV` guard. |
| Med | `services/timestamping/src/tsa/qualified-tsa.ts:305-325` | TSA error/timeout → `success:true` self-generated `mock:true` token for eIDAS/UETA artefacts. |
| Med | `services/anchoring/src/cardano/confirmation.ts:38-50` | First non-null Blockfrost `getTransaction` → `confirmed:true`; no finality threshold. |

### E — Deployment, containers & CI/CD supply chain — [KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| High | `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:61` (repeated) | 32-char `APP_DB_PASSWORD` literal committed as `:-default` across **51** conn strings — `grep -c 'APP_DB_PASSWORD:-' Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` at the grounding SHA `fcf2d878c` **and** at develop `87384a8ba` (2026-09-06); the original "\~20" was wrong when written, not drifted. See comment `ef553d29`. |
| High | `.github/workflows/security-scan.yml:99,112,134,138,272,298` | Trivy/Gitleaks/Semgrep/Checkov all `continue-on-error` → report-only, can't block a merge. |
| Med | `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml:365-366,369,377` | KV secrets → `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` unmasked + inlined into `DATABASE_URL`. |
| Med | `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:64,119` | Postgres (`:6432`) + Redis (`:6379`) publish to host by default. |
| Med | root `package-lock.json` axios 1.16.1; kyc 1.15.2; mobile 1.13.2 | Stale-lock axios drift vs 1.18.1 (other advisories already patched — axios is the only live drift). [KS-420](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-420/dependency-and-tooling-version-hygiene-audit-from-clean-rebuild) #6. |
| Low | all `services/*/Dockerfile`, `frontend/*` | Base images tag- not digest-pinned; `auth/Dockerfile:46` ships build tooling in runtime layer. |

### F — Edge, WAF, DDoS & anti-automation — [KS-491](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-491)

| Sev | Evidence | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Crit (strategic) | repo-wide absent; `deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md:50` | **No WAF** anywhere (Cloudflare DNS-only). Product owner wants WAF — greenfield. |
| High | `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf` | Live gateway has no `limit_req`/`client_max_body_size`; hardened `nginx-production.conf` is decommissioned-path only. |
| High | Caddyfile absent from repo | Real TLS edge (Caddy on VM) not version-controlled. |
| High | repo-wide absent | No CAPTCHA/Turnstile on signup/login/verify. |
| Med | `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/rateLimitEnforce.ts:135-137` | App-tier limiters fail **open** on Redis error ([KS-170](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-170/enforceclientratelimit-runs-in-memory-per-replica-wire-the-redis)). |
| Med | `nginx-demo.conf` | No Slowloris/large-body/slow-request protection at the live edge. |

### Remediation sequencing (amplifier-first)

* **Wave 1 — active exposure + one-liners:** ungated `seed-demo-users` (B), KYC callback default-secret (C), wallet-verify stub (C), committed `APP_DB_PASSWORD` + lock pg/redis to internal (E/F), make CI scan gates blocking (E).
* **Wave 2 — integrity criticals (K's crown jewels):** anchor-fabrication-on-outage + `NODE_ENV` guard (D), qualified-TSA mock fallback (D), verify-against-chain not DB (D), finality threshold (D), m365 SSRF + originate webhook DNS-rebind/send-time revalidation (B).
* **Wave 3 — authz/tenancy hardening:** notification BOLA (A), document owner-scoping decision + fix (A), close header-trust tenancy path / add JWT `tenantId` cross-check (A), M365 token encryption at rest (C), billing idempotency fail-closed (C).

title: Akto CI scan throughput: ~21 s local vs ~10 min in the isolated pr-akto stack (~28×) — investigate worker starvation / run-pickup latency (KS-435 durable fix)
description:
[akto-2187-findings.md](https://uploads.linear.app/ee72b345-5a75-4c1a-9bbb-09a6955f4499/12359f7f-c7d7-4777-aa45-e997d8acaf8d/dc8d8d55-c175-422c-b4ed-85b2faed7c2f)

## Problem (split out of [KS-435](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-435/akto-suite-pr-full-scan-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling-in-the-isolated) — the durable-fix track)

KS-435's immediate unblock raised the poll ceilings (`PR_TIMEOUT_MS` 660s→1200s, `PRE_MERGE_TIMEOUT_MS` 720s→1260s). But the underlying anomaly is untouched: **the same all-endpoint** `test:pr` **scan completes in \~21 s on a local host and takes \~10 min in the isolated** `pr-akto` **CI stack** — a ~28× gap that is too large to be plain CPU starvation of a co-scheduled stack.

## Evidence

* Local ([KS-433](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-433/akto-bolabflabroken-auth-finding-on-a-write-path-unmasked-by-the-ks) triage, 2026-07-11): `npm run test:pr` → COMPLETED ~21 s, 316 endpoints, 7902 results, 0 vulnerable.
* CI: three runs died at the ~594 s poll ceiling (PR #480 ×2 attempts, PR #488, develop post-merge run on `9a1ade224`); green runs (#481, #489) finished just under it — so real CI wall-clock is ~9–10 min.

## Suspects ([KS-435](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-435/akto-suite-pr-full-scan-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling-in-the-isolated) options 2/3)

1. `akto-testing` worker CPU/IO starvation — the runner co-schedules the 31-service platform stack + Akto's dashboard/mongo/testing/puppeteer.
2. Scheduled-run pickup latency — the testing worker polls for queued runs; check `LAST_TEST_RUN_EXECUTION_DELTA` / pickup-interval behaviour under load.
3. Runner resources — larger GitHub runner class, or trim what boots in the akto job.

## Direction — right-size the runner, keep coverage intact (consolidated from [KS-446](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-446/akto-suite-pr-durable-ci-throughput-fix-stop-the-full-scan-sitting-at), closed as duplicate)

Having weighed the two levers, the clear preference is to **increase the runner's resources (CPU/RAM)** — the isolated stack's runner is simply under-provisioned for co-hosting the full platform + full Akto stack. That is the root cause and the honest fix. In order of preference:

1. **Right-size the runner** — move the `pr-akto` job to a larger runner (more vCPU/RAM), or split the platform stack and the Akto stack onto separate runners so the akto-testing worker isn't starved. Expected to be the whole fix.
2. **Confirm it's genuinely resource starvation** vs. a stall on scheduled-run pickup (~21s local vs >594s CI) — verify (1) is the right lever before spending on it.
3. **Coverage/scope trim — avoid.** The full all-endpoint BOLA/BFLA/Broken-Auth scan is the value of the gate; narrowing it to win on runtime would quietly reduce security coverage rather than fix the real constraint. Last resort only, flagged explicitly, never silent.

## Done means

CI `Akto suite (PR)` wall-clock understood + brought down to low single-digit minutes — achieved by **more runner capacity**, not a further ceiling raise and not by reducing coverage. (Or an explicit, documented decision that ~10 min is accepted and the raised ceiling is the permanent posture — then tighten the ceilings to the measured runtime.)

Consolidates [KS-446](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-446/akto-suite-pr-durable-ci-throughput-fix-stop-the-full-scan-sitting-at) (durable CI-throughput fix), closed as a duplicate of this ticket. Related: [KS-435](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-435/akto-suite-pr-full-scan-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling-in-the-isolated) (parent, Done, #490), [KS-413](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-413/akto-pr-gate-scan-is-endpoint-bound-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling) (prior poll-ceiling class).

title: systemTest (all tools): enable nightly platform test suites after full AWS migration
description:
## Reminder: re-enable the nightly system-test suites once we have fully migrated to AWS

The nightly platform test suites (Schemathesis, Playwright, Performance, Akto) are currently **disabled** — the workflow only runs on manual `workflow_dispatch`. They were prepared to run on a daily schedule but the `schedule:` cron is commented out pending the AWS migration.

### What to do when AWS migration is complete

1. In `.github/workflows/nightly-platform-suites.yml`, **uncomment the** `schedule:` **block** to re-enable the daily trigger:

   ```yaml
   schedule:
     - cron: '0 14 * * *'   # 14:00 UTC — ~midnight Sydney, 22:00 Singapore
   ```
2. Re-point any `--env`/base-URL config from the local isolated stacks to the AWS targets if the nightly is meant to hit AWS rather than a fresh ghcr build.
3. Flip the STATUS header comment in the workflow back to **LIVE**.
4. Confirm the four suite check-runs appear and the shared `build` → fan-out topology still holds.

### Context

* Start time chosen: **14:00 UTC** (≈ midnight Sydney AEST/AEDT year-round, 22:00 Singapore SGT).
* All four suites already start **simultaneously** off the single schedule (each `needs: [prep, build]`), so enabling the one cron enables all four together.
* The Performance job runs a single isolated stack with all scenarios **serial**: smoke → auth-spike → (15m 429 cooldown) → smoke → spike → (15m) → smoke → stress → (15m) → smoke → scalability → (15m) → smoke → nightly soak (~4h4m). ⚠ ~5.9–6.1h total — near GitHub's 6h/job cap; re-check headroom on the AWS runners.
* Everything stays **report-only** (`continue-on-error`); no merge gating.
* Prepared on branch `feature/nightly-schedule-perf-sequence`.

title: CI: require all systemTest (all tools) PR suites + pre-merge to block merges on failure (branch protection + sign-off)
description:
## Goal

Make **every** systemTest PR suite **and** the pre-merge tests actually **block a merge on failure**. The workflow YAML already runs each suite to completion and then hard-fails its check (complete-then-block); what's missing is the **settings half** — a red check only prevents merge when branch protection marks it **Required**, and a check is matched by its **check-run display name**, not its job id. The pre-merge gate specifically must be a **manual human approval** (not an auto-pass).

## Background (already in place, code side)

`.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml` (build-once → isolated per-suite stacks) runs each suite `continue-on-error` then an Enforce step fails the required check on any failure:

* **Schemathesis** — blocking spec-auth ([KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight)) + pytest ([KS-126](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-126/schemathesis-pytest-suite-runs-only-ad-hoc-locally-wire-it-into-ci-dev)) + offline quality/unit gate; [KS-270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-270/featschemathesis-add-low-frequency-auth-profile-to-reduce-429s-on) auth sweep stays informational by design.
* **Playwright** — blocking `quality:check` + `npm run ci`.
* **Performance** — quality/unit gate + k6 smoke, complete-then-block.
* **Akto** — quality/unit gate + PR-gate scan, complete-then-block via step-outcome (emits Allure, not JUnit).

## Tasks (settings — cannot be code)

1. **Branch protection ruleset — mark these check-run display names Required** (match by display name, not job id):
   * `build`
   * `Schemathesis suite`
   * `Playwright suite`
   * `Performance suite (k6 smoke)`
   * `Akto suite (PR-gate subset)`
     Require `build` too — in the build-once topology a `build` failure **skips** the suite jobs, so confirm a required-but-skipped check does not wedge the PR (skipped ≠ stuck).
2. **Pre-merge must be a MANUAL human-approval gate — no auto-pass.** The comprehensive `run.py pre-merge` sweep (`pre-merge-platform-suites.yml`) must require a designated human to **manually click Approve** before the PR can merge; it must never pass on its own.
   * Implement via the GitHub `pre-merge-signoff` **Environment** with **required reviewers** (an Environment reviewer *is* a manual Approve/Reject gate): pin the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` job to that Environment so the run **pauses and waits** for a human decision, and no merge proceeds until a reviewer manually approves. GitHub → Settings → Environments → `pre-merge-signoff` → add required reviewers (start with @peter).
   * Mark the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` check **Required** in the branch-protection ruleset so the manual approval is enforced, not advisory.
   * Per CLAUDE.md, "PR checks green" is **not** the pre-merge sign-off — a human must have run/confirmed the comprehensive pre-merge sweep and then manually approved.

## Notes / carve-outs

* Two deliberate non-blocking exceptions stay as-is: the rate-limited [KS-270](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-270/featschemathesis-add-low-frequency-auth-profile-to-reduce-429s-on) Schemathesis auth sweep (429 back-off would flap the gate) and **all nightly** runs (report-only soak).
* This ticket is GitHub **settings** work; no systemTest code change is required (the YAML is already complete-then-block, and the sign-off job already targets the `pre-merge-signoff` Environment — it just needs reviewers + to be Required). Verify on a draft PR: all five suite checks Required and red-on-failure blocks merge, and the merge stays blocked until a human manually approves the `Pre-merge sign-off (human)` gate.

---

## Precondition: the pre-merge ack checkboxes have no not-applicable path (added 2026-09-09)

**Close this before** `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK` **is set to** `true`**, or turning enforcement on will require a false attestation on any PR that legitimately needs neither suite.**

`.github/pull_request_template.md` seeds two boxes under the heading **"Pre-merge acknowledgment (author)"**, instructing: *"Tick each box **only after** you have run that suite's pre-merge tier and it passed"*. `.github/workflows/pr-premerge-ack.yml` ([KS-413](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-413/akto-pr-gate-scan-is-endpoint-bound-times-out-at-the-poll-ceiling)) matches **only**:

```
^- \[[xX]\][[:space:]]*<!--ack:schemathesis-->
^- \[[xX]\][[:space:]]*<!--ack:akto-->
```

A tick, or nothing. No N/A marker, no label escape, no "suite not applicable" branch. So for an offline shell gate, a docs change or a workflow tweak, the only ways to satisfy the check are to tick a box asserting a sweep that did not happen, or to leave a box that reads as an omission.

**The exemption pattern already exists in that workflow** — drafts pass green unconditionally (`if [ "${DRAFT}" = "true" ]`). And the template models the right affordance one section down, in the PII block: *"Not applicable? Say so explicitly rather than leaving the boxes blank — a blank box reads as 'not checked', which is the state this section exists to make visible."* The ack section has no equivalent.

**How it surfaced.** PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#921](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-778-the-pin-label-gate-could-not-see-two-legal-shapes-and-its-guard-0ba71ba302a2) ([KS-778](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-778/preflight-leg-10s-pin-label-parser-is-blind-to-a-quoted-uses-and-an)) changes exactly one file — `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/action-pins-labelled.sh`, an offline shell gate that reads `.github/` with `git grep` and prints to stdout. Measured: **0 of 1** changed files fall under `services/`, `frontend/`, `packages/`, `migrations/`, `contracts/`, `systemTest/`, any compose file or any `.env`, so neither pre-merge suite exercises anything in it. Both boxes were left unticked with the reason stated inline, following the PII section's pattern — a workaround, not a fix; the workflow still counts it as un-acknowledged.

**Not urgent today:** enforcement is soft by default (the repository Variable `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK` is unset ⇒ warn + pass), and the workflow has not executed since 2026-08-17. It becomes live the moment task 2 above is actioned.

### Fix — one of these, not all

1. **An N/A marker** the workflow recognises, e.g. `<!--ack:schemathesis:na-->`, requiring a stated reason on the same line. Smallest, keeps the human in the loop, and mirrors the PII section so the template gains one convention rather than two. The assertion becomes "I considered this suite and it does not apply" — a true statement, still auditable.
2. **A label escape**, e.g. a `no-premerge-suites` PR label that passes both ack checks, reviewable in itself.
3. **A path-based skip** — passes when the diff touches nothing the suites cover. Most automatic, but duplicates suite-scope knowledge into the workflow and will drift.

### Done means

* A PR that legitimately needs neither suite passes both ack checks **without** anyone ticking a box that asserts an unrun sweep.
* The escape requires a stated reason — an acknowledgment, not a bypass. A blank body still fails.
* Red→green with `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK=true`: a PR using the new form passes; the same PR with the reason removed fails. Proven both ways.
* Template instruction text updated to describe the not-applicable path, in the shape the PII block already uses.
* Ticking a box still means what it says today — this must not weaken the positive assertion.

*Provenance: template and workflow read at* `dbe7ba6b3` *(PR* [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#921](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-778-the-pin-label-gate-could-not-see-two-legal-shapes-and-its-guard-0ba71ba302a2) *head), 2026-09-09; last workflow execution 2026-08-17 via* `gh run list --workflow=pr-premerge-ack.yml`*; surfaced at [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/921#issuecomment-5602690418](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/921#issuecomment-5602690418>)*

title: Base-image refresh routine + track postgres CVE-2025-68121 (redis leg already done in triage)
description:
## Context — KS-363 follow-up (residual criticals after the base-image refresh)

After KS-363 (all built images → `node:22-alpine` / `nginx:1.29-alpine`, **0 critical across the 31 built images**), residual criticals appeared only against the two pinned third-party infra images. Investigated before assuming "major bump needed" — **major bumps buy nothing for either**, and the redis finding turned out to be a stale local scan cache, not a platform exposure.

## 1. redis — RESOLVED during triage (was a stale local image, demo never affected)

* The 6 crit / 59 high initially flagged were in a **stale local Docker cache** of `redis:7-alpine` (pre-pull digest).
* The current upstream digest `sha256:6ab0b6e7…` scans **0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH** — and it is exactly what the ACR mirror holds and what `secuura02-demo-redis` runs. Verified via `az acr import --force` (digest unchanged → ACR already current).
* `redis:8-alpine` is identical (0/0) — no major bump warranted.
* Done: local image re-pulled + container recreated; demo redis app restarted (idempotent) and Running; portals/API re-verified 200.

## 2. postgres — CVE-2025-68121, unfixable by us today (local-only surface) — the one real residual

* `postgres:15-alpine`: 1 critical = **CVE-2025-68121** (Go stdlib `crypto/tls` incorrect certificate validation, in the image's Go helper binary; fixed in Go 1.24.13 / 1.25.7).
* Present **identically in** `postgres:16-alpine` **and** `postgres:17-alpine` — a major bump does not clear it. It clears when Docker Hub rebuilds the image against a patched Go toolchain.
* Demo uses managed `secuura02-demo-pg` (PG 15 flexible server), so this container image is **local dev only**.
* **Action:** periodically re-pull `postgres:15-alpine` and re-scan; close when the upstream rebuild lands.

## 3. Systemic: pinned-tag digests go stale silently

The ACR `node:22-alpine` mirror WAS genuinely stale during KS-363 (needed `--force` re-import before the demo build), and the redis false alarm came from the same mechanism on a local cache. Alpine-based images republish the same tag with fixes; mirrors/local caches keep old digests and quietly re-accumulate CVEs — and stale caches also produce misleading scan results.

**Proposal:** a lightweight refresh routine — periodically (e.g. monthly or per deploy): `az acr import --force` for the mirrored bases (`node:22-alpine`, `nginx:1.29-alpine`, `edoburu/pgbouncer:1.22.1-p0`, `redis:7-alpine`) + `docker compose pull` locally, then re-scan. Could live in `deploy.sh` or a small script + reminder.

## Scanner note

Trivy v0.58.1; the KS-363 Docker Scout baseline rated redis 0 critical — consistent with the stale-local-cache explanation (Scout scanned a fresh rebuild).

title: Phase 2 — JWT RS256 → hybrid (RS256 + ML-DSA-65)
description:
> **⚠ RE-MEASURED 2026-08-12 (session 19) — the shim blocker below is DEAD, and the real blocker is different. Kam's ruling needed on a design change; see the pinned comment for the measurements.**
>
> `jose` 6.2.8 signs and verifies ML-DSA JWTs on Node 24 today — **no liboqs, no WASM shim**. Measured: RS256 435 B / ML-DSA-44 3326 B / **ML-DSA-65 4511 B** / ML-DSA-87 6269 B, and ML-DSA **verifies faster than RS256** (0.3 ms vs 0.5 ms), so performance is not the constraint.
>
> **The real blocker is token size against the refresh-token COOKIE.** `generateRefreshToken` (`services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts`) returns a *signed JWT* which `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:367,534,613` sets as the `refresh_token` cookie; browsers cap one cookie at **4096 bytes**. ML-DSA-65 measured 4511 B on a *three-field* payload — the real refresh payload is larger. It does not fit. That forces a design change (opaque refresh token + server-side session lookup — the pattern already exists at `services/auth/src/services/session.ts:133`, cookie chunking, or access-token-only migration) — **Kam's ruling, not an implementation detail.**
>
> Residual risk from the original refusal, still real: Node reports `ExperimentalWarning: The ML-DSA-65 Web Crypto API algorithm is an experimental feature and might change at any time`. Available ≠ production-hardened.
>
> Also: auth signs with `jsonwebtoken` 9.0.2, which has no ML-DSA support — any rollout starts by moving auth's signing path to `jose`.

Migrate JWT signing to hybrid via the Phase-0 registry.

- [X] `~~jsonwebtoken~~`~~ / ~~`~~jose~~`~~ don't yet ship ML-DSA — add a COSE/JOSE PQC shim (liboqs-node or a vetted WASM ML-DSA lib) behind the crypto abstraction.~~ **OBSOLETE 2026-08-12:** `jose` **6.2.8 ships ML-DSA; no shim required. Replaced by: migrate auth's signing from** `jsonwebtoken` **to** `jose`**.**
- [ ] Roll out **verifier-first** (api-gateway, originate accept both), then signer (auth), then drop classical.
- [ ] Entra ID / CIAM (RS256) is **Microsoft-owned** — only ensure `obeden-ssd` doesn't hard-fail on their token-alg rotation; track their PQC timeline.

Blocked by Phase 0. Ref: plan §5 Phase 2.

title: State the M365 source-document controller boundary in the customer DPA
description:
## Action

Add wording to the customer **DPA** stating the M365 source-document controller boundary.

## Why

From KS-234 §5.3: Secuura's m365 integration holds only an **org-scoped OAuth connection** (`svc_m365_connections`), not a per-user copy of source documents. The source documents live in the **customer's own M365 / SharePoint tenant**, where the **customer is the data controller**. On a Secuura erasure, the customer's M365 source is therefore the **customer's** erasure responsibility, not Secuura's.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Customer DPA explicitly states the customer is controller of their own M365 source documents and is responsible for erasing them in their own tenant.

Refs: KS-234 §5.3. (Belongs in the DPA legal doc, not the platform repo.)

title: Tokenise personal/identifying data — mint a privacy token (Platform S/K by journey origin) and thread it through the APIs
description:
## Context

GDPR data-minimisation / privacy. Spun out of the KS-234 DPIA work: today an individual/sole-trader **issuer name can land in plaintext on the immutable Cardano chain** (KS-234 §5.1, accepted as a disclosed residual *pending this ticket*). Tokenising identifying data also complements KS-291 (per-subject DEK / crypto-shred) by keeping plaintext PII out of immutable artefacts in the first place.

## Goal

Replace plaintext personal / identifying data with a generated **token**, so the token (not the plaintext) is what flows through the system and onto the chain.

## Requirements

* **Token generation owned by the platform where the client journey starts** — generated by **Platform S or Platform K** depending on origin. A journey beginning on Platform S mints the token there; one beginning on Platform K mints it there.
* **Incorporate the token into the APIs** — request/response contracts on both platforms carry the token (in place of, or alongside, the plaintext identifier); downstream services + the on-chain anchor consume the token.
* **Initial implementation on Platform S** (Platform K to follow once the S contract is proven).
* Define the token scheme: stable per-subject/per-identity, non-reversible without the mapping, and the mapping store + its lifecycle (incl. erasure interaction).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Token scheme + ownership defined (which platform mints, by journey origin).
- [ ] Platform S generates and threads the token through its APIs.
- [ ] On-chain anchor uses the token, not the plaintext issuer/personal name (closes the KS-234 §5.1 residual for new anchors).
- [ ] Platform K follow-up scoped (separate sub-task/ticket).

Refs: KS-234 (origin), KS-291 (per-subject DEK / crypto-shred).

title: Enable Code Security / GHAS so security scans populate the Security tab (currently artifact-only)
description:
## Source

Surfaced fixing [KS-237](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-237>) (repair Gitleaks + Semgrep on PRs). When the repaired Semgrep job first ran on a PR, `upload-sarif` failed with `Resource not accessible by integration` **(403)**. Root cause confirmed via the API:

```
GET /repos/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura  → security_and_analysis:
  code_security: disabled
  secret_scanning: disabled
  dependabot_security_updates: disabled
GET /repos/.../code-scanning/analyses    → 403 "Code Security must be enabled for this repository to use code scanning."
```

## Problem

**Code Security / GitHub Advanced Security is disabled on the repo**, so `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` can't write to the **Security → Code scanning** tab. This affects **every SARIF-based scan**, not just Semgrep:

* Gitleaks ([KS-237](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-237/repair-gitleaks-semgrep-security-scan-actions-invalid-sha-pins-semgrep)) and Semgrep ([KS-237](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-237/repair-gitleaks-semgrep-security-scan-actions-invalid-sha-pins-semgrep))
* Container Security Scan (Trivy) — uploads SARIF
* the CodeQL upload steps

[KS-237](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-237/repair-gitleaks-semgrep-security-scan-actions-invalid-sha-pins-semgrep) worked around it: SARIF upload is now best-effort (`continue-on-error`) and findings are published as **workflow artifacts** (`gitleaks-sarif`, `semgrep-sarif`) so they're accessible. But the Security-tab integration (de-duped findings, PR annotations, dismissal workflow, trend view) is dark until GHAS is enabled.

## Decision needed (Kam / Peter)

GitHub Advanced Security is a **paid** add-on for private repos. Options:

1. **Enable GHAS / Code Security** — the upload-sarif paths light up with no further code change; findings land in the Security tab with PR annotations + dismissal workflow. Cost per active committer.
2. **Stay artifact-only** — keep the current best-effort uploads + artifacts; findings are in the run artifacts, no Security-tab UX. Free.
3. **Make the repo public** — GHAS/code-scanning is free for public repos (not in scope / a product decision of its own).

## Acceptance (if option 1 chosen)

- [ ] Code Security enabled on `Secuura/Distributed_Secuura`
- [ ] (optional) Secret scanning + push protection enabled — overlaps with the gitleaks job
- [ ] A PR's Semgrep/Gitleaks/Trivy SARIF appears under Security → Code scanning
- [ ] The `continue-on-error` on the SARIF-upload steps can then be removed (so a genuine upload failure is visible again)

## Related

* [KS-237](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-237>) — the workaround (artifact fallback) lives here
* [KS-230](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-230>) — wired the scanners onto PRs
* [KS-231](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-231>) — Dependabot activation (same "security feature not actually on" class)
* [KS-229](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-229>) — assurance tracker

title: Add OpenAPI inline examples to all 329 operations — eliminate coverage-phase no-test-cases skips
description:
> ### ✅ 2026-08-12 — branch current with `develop`, ready for review
>
> Head `72c33c20a`. Merged develop (#666/#667/#669/#670/#671/#672) and regenerated the spec — the
> regenerated output was byte-identical to the auto-merged YAML, so there was no drift to reconcile.
> The spec now carries **319 operationIds** ([KS-62](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-62/openapi-specification-compliance-optional-features) / #670, was 0) alongside **355 example blocks**;
> the two workstreams compose without contention. `check:openapi` PASS (drift + E1–E9, 0 findings) ·
> `packages/shared` 279/279 · full preflight PASS on push including the new `audit:locks` gate.
>
> **Remaining is not authoring** — it is Kam's sign-off and review pass, then the pre-merge suites.
>
> **PII key question (C1/C2) — CLOSED.** Kam answered 2026-07-29 (he holds the pair locally); with A3
> settled as option (c) the captures have no remaining purpose, so no re-supply is needed. The two raw
> capture directories are confirmed deleted, retiring the 233 live JWTs. The obsolete red banner that
> stood here has been removed as it invited.

> ### 📎 One plan attachment — "[KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage) *implementation plan — the only current version"*
>
> Its `OUTSTANDING ACTIONS` section (groups A–G) is the authoritative pick-up list, mirrored in the
> consolidated comment. **Critical path: B1 → A1 → E1.** Earlier revisions have been deleted rather
> than left alongside it — two files each claiming to be current is how someone picks up a stale plan.

---

## Goal

Give every OpenAPI operation at least one realistic, **runnable** example, so Schemathesis and Akto can generate meaningful test cases instead of falling back to unconstrained fuzz.

This is the prerequisite annotation work for [KS-227](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-227/schemathesis-gate-cicd-on-no-test-cases-skips-once-schema-annotation) (CI gate on coverage skips).

> **⚠ Approach changed 2026-07.** This ticket originally proposed hand-editing `example:` blocks into `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`. **That is not possible** — the spec is *generated* from Zod schemas by `scripts/generate-openapi.ts`, and `npm run check:openapi` fails the build on any hand-edit. Examples must land in the Zod source. The original approach is preserved in the issue's description history.

---

## Where examples actually live

```
services/<svc>/src/<svc>.openapi.ts     ← .openapi({ description, example }) — EDIT HERE
        │  npm run generate-openapi
        ▼
docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml           ← GENERATED. Never hand-edit.
```

The `api-gateway` image bundles the generated spec — but **how you pick a spec change up differs by target** (corrected 2026-08-19, Kamil's review §9):

* **Deployed targets** (Container Apps / the VM's built images) — the spec is baked in, so **rebuild api-gateway**.
* **Local compose** — the spec is **bind-mounted**, not baked (`docker-compose.yml:434`), and since [KS-656](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-656/api-gateway-apidocsopenapiyaml-500s-on-a-dead-spec-bind-mount-while) the gateway reads it into memory **once at boot**, so `docker restart secuura-api-gateway` is what picks it up. A rebuild works only incidentally, by recreating the container.
* **Verify by checksum, not by a 200.** The dev `fs.watch` hot-reload does not fire in the container ([KS-659](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-659/api-gateway-spec-hot-reload-never-fires-in-the-container-a-spec-regen)), and after a `git checkout` the single-file bind mount points at a dead inode — the route keeps answering **200 with the previous branch's spec**.

## Measured baseline vs current (2026-08-05)

| Metric | develop | branch |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Operations in spec | **318** | 318 |
| Named component schemas | **350** | 350 |
| …carrying an example | **14** | **344** |
| Example blocks | 23 | **354** |
| — request only | 6 | **113** |
| — response only | 4 | **172** |

**Examples-phase skips: 303 → 196.** All −107 came from the request-body examples; the 168 response examples moved it by **exactly zero**, because that phase seeds from what a caller *sends*. Detail in the 2026-08-05 comment.

### Superseded 2026-07-20 baseline (for the record)

| Metric | Value |
| -- | -- |
| Operations in spec | **310** (not 329) |
| Named component schemas | **335** |
| …carrying an example | **14** |
| Typed properties | **1,817** |
| …carrying an example | **4** |
| …carrying *any* constraint (`format`/`pattern`/`enum`/`min`/`max`) | **425 (23.4%)** |

**The last row is the real constraint on this ticket.** 76.6% of properties are declared bare `type: string`, so anything generating from the schema — example synthesis, Schemathesis, Akto — has nothing to work with. `createdAt` is a bare string.

## Correction to the original premise

`no_test_cases_generated` **does not appear anywhere in this codebase**, and is not the skip reason the report emits — our HTML report reads a free-text `skip_reason` (`src/html_report/panels/operations.py:51`). The original acceptance criterion was written against a term that does not exist in Schemathesis 4.22.4. Any criterion phrased in terms of it needs restating against the actual skip vocabulary.

---

## The approach: harvest → redact → triage → synthesise → codemod

Built as a self-contained harness in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/openapi-examples/` (see its README). **Default OFF** behind `HARVEST_EXAMPLES`, four independent guards, zero runs in CI — the condition of Kamil's approval.

**1. Harvest.** A capture proxy sits transparently in front of the API on `:6882` while the existing test suites run, recording real request/response pairs. **platform-k only** — `config.tiers` defaults to `['platform-k']`; platform-s moved to [PS-348](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-348/harvest-openapi-example-values-from-the-platform-s-test-suite-ks-256) with its machinery retained. Reach is ~13 of 310 operations (~4%) — real traffic simply does not exercise most endpoints.

**2. Redact — in memory, before any write (R15b).** No raw capture artifact is ever written to disk. Credentials become named placeholders (`<password>`, `<accessToken>`) so a reader knows what to supply. Identifiers normalise to seed fixtures so examples stay runnable after a DB reset (R7).

**3. Triage (Gate 5a) — human, mandatory.** Unrecognised fields land as `REDACTED_UNREVIEWED` and are ineligible to publish. Only fields a human explicitly moves to `ALLOWED_FIELDS` may appear as observed. **Enforced in code**, not by convention.

**4. Synthesise.** Everything harvest cannot reach is generated deterministically from the schema — ~96% of output.

**5. Codemod (Gate 5b) — ✅ WRITTEN AND RUN (2026-08-05).** `scripts/spec-examples/apply-spec-examples.ts` — absent-only, AST-derived text splice, masking before shape-fitting, `--regenerate` round-trips byte-identical. 330 examples landed. [KS-481](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-481/published-openapi-examples-embed-a-volatile-document-id-that-404s-no) no longer gates it (merged #603, 07-29). Superseded text follows: The step that writes `.openapi({ example })` into the Zod files. **Nothing ships until this exists, and** [KS-481](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-481/published-openapi-examples-embed-a-volatile-document-id-that-404s-no) **gates it.**

## Status

| Piece | State |
| -- | -- |
| Capture proxy | working |
| Harvest | **platform-k only**; platform-s deferred to [PS-348](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-348/harvest-openapi-example-values-from-the-platform-s-test-suite-ks-256) |
| `pipeline.ts` | **built** — 335 merged (14 tier-0 untouched + 321 synthesised, 0 harvested) |
| Triage (Gate 5a) | **done** — 18 `ALLOWED_FIELDS` entries. **Dormant**: redaction is in-memory, so they apply only to a *future* harvest |
| PII store | built, empty; lives outside the repo, guarded by a build-failing check |
| **Codemod (Gate 5b)** | **✅ WRITTEN + RUN 2026-08-05** — 330 examples landed, 14 curated untouched. Guards: `check-spec-examples` E1–E9 **blocking**; `verify-spec-examples` V1–V5 **advisory** (non-deterministic). Was: **not written — this is what remains, and** [KS-481](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-481/published-openapi-examples-embed-a-volatile-document-id-that-404s-no) **gates it** |
| Kamil's review (2026-07) | **10 of \~12 fixed**. Each fix carries a `KAMIL-REVIEW` tag and his stated reason, quoted, at the point of change |
| **Kamil's review (2026-08-19)** | **8 of 10 addressed** — §1 build fix, §2 E8/E9 coverage bound, §3 the 16 `address` examples, §4 the 26x400 correction, §5 ack wording, §6 the false `MIN_OBSERVATIONS` comment, §7 PII checkbox, §8 perf gate split to PR #723, §9 restart-not-rebuild, §10 recorded in a commit. **The 2 remaining were deferred by him**, not missed: the `verify/` sub-threshold count ("not for this PR") and the baseline ticket. **Both his stated blockers are cleared** and verified on the pushed head |
| **Pre-merge ack** | **GRANTED for this PR by Kamil, 2026-08-19** — he re-ran the sweep independently, 91 failures, every class mapping to an open ticket. His condition for a *standing* rule (a `schemathesis-baseline.json` keyed by check+operation with ticket + expiry) is now **built and enforced** on this branch: 97 pairs, gate fails on any untriaged pair |

PR: [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#568](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-256-openapi-examples-14-344-schemas-gate-5b-codemod-e1-e9-guard-709ed550b02d) — OPEN, ready for review, head `72c33c20a` (squashed to `c7f55881d` 2026-08-05, then merged current with `develop` 2026-08-12). Review requested from @kamil.kreiser and @stuart.jamieson.

**Local verification is green** — `check:openapi` PASS (drift + E1-E9) · `tsc` 22/22 services · 279/279 shared · 160/160 performance · Playwright 12/12 on generated actors · GDPR IDOR 6/6. The **Schemathesis sweep still FAILS** on fuzz-phase findings (a different set each run — it reseeds); none are example-driven. Akto has not been re-run.

## Open decisions — ✅ ALL THREE RESOLVED 2026-07-29 by @kamil.kreiser (kept for the record)

1. **publish-vs-enrich (BLOCKING).** Peter's. The 321 synthesised proposals are structurally valid but mostly `example-<fieldname>`, because of the 76.6% figure above. Either publish as-is (real coverage, low value), or enrich the Zod schemas with `.datetime()`/`.uuid()`/`.regex()` first. An enrichment codemod was written and reverted: 131 evidence-backed rewrites, 23.4% → 28.5%. These modules are documentation-only — nothing calls `.parse()` on them — so added formats **cannot reject a request**. Plan §7.0-G. ⚠ Interacts with #2.
2. **R3 amendment.** Kamil's. Whether Schemathesis 2xx *responses* become an admissible value source — **166 operations versus harvest's 13**. Highest-leverage open item; if admitted, #1 may resolve itself.
3. `Accept-Encoding`**.** Kamil's. He asked for it to be stripped; we decode instead. Declared and argued on PR #568 and in plan §7.0-F.

*(The former item 4 — the seven volatile-id examples — is now* [KS-481](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-481/published-openapi-examples-embed-a-volatile-document-id-that-404s-no), which **blocks this ticket**. It could not be fixed by substitution: no document is seeded, so every candidate replacement still 404s.)

## Acceptance

**No fixed number** — per Peter, the target is "how many we can get", measured and reported rather than gated on. Ceiling is 335/335 schemas, since synthesis reaches every named schema; the open question is example *quality*, not reach.

- [X] **DONE** Codemod written, and examples landed in `services/*/src/*.openapi.ts` (330 examples, 14 -> 344 schemas). No longer gated by [KS-481](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-481/published-openapi-examples-embed-a-volatile-document-id-that-404s-no)
- [X] **DONE** `npm run generate-openapi` re-run; `npm run check:openapi` passes — now also runs the blocking E1-E9 guard, 0 findings across 354 example blocks
- [ ] Every published example is **runnable** — no volatile ids, no `null` standing in for a value. **No longer gated:** [KS-481](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-481/published-openapi-examples-embed-a-volatile-document-id-that-404s-no) is **Done + archived** (2026-08-12, PR #603), and this branch already carries the seeded canonical document it added. Remaining gap is the long tail, not the blocker
- [X] **DONE** No secrets or PII — E1-E9 green. The sign-off is a build-failing check rather than a signature, which is what @stuart.jamieson asked for. It caught 113 person-shaped violations, a seeded account id in 4 places, and a published credential pair that authenticated
- [ ] Schemathesis + Akto pre-merge suites run and green
- [ ] `api-gateway` rebuilt on both targets
- [X] **DONE** Coverage delta reported — see the 2026-08-05 comments and PR #568
- [ ] ⚠ **NEW, not in the original list:** triage the 26 x 400 (the API rejecting examples we publish). **Corrected 2026-08-19 by Kamil's review §4 — the "at most 4" below was low.** His independent triage (`pre-merge-2026-08-18T23-04-02Z`, seed 2407760562, 20x400 across 19 ops, each decoded from its own response body) puts it at **5 strictly example-fixable** — 4 placeholders violating a documented constraint + 1 example pinning two mutually exclusive fields (`transfer-custody` sending `newHolderId` *and* `newHolderEmail`) — and **8 if parameter examples count**, which §7 already argues they should. The rest are not example-fixable: 6 `onBehalfOf` connector-only, 2 `TENANT_REQUIRED` persona config, 3 state-dependent. Separately unresolved: `POST /api/webhooks` publishes a URL the API refuses because the host cannot be resolved, and fixing it collides with rule E1's reserved-domain requirement
- [ ] ⚠ **NEW:** `verify-spec-examples` is non-deterministic (2/6/6/10 across four cassettes) and ships ADVISORY. Needs an accumulated evidence model before it can gate anything

> ⚠ **CI cannot go green today — now tracked as** [KS-660](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-660/ci-every-needs-build-suite-job-dies-in-3s-with-zero-steps-develop-is) **(Urgent, Blocked).** Since **2026-08-17 08:27Z** every `needs: build` suite job dies in ~3s with **zero steps** and no log blob; cause is the org Actions spend, and it is Kam's call. **Do not read** `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN` **as green** — an unstarted run reports no required check, so a PR looks CLEAN having run nothing. Verified 2026-08-19 on PR #568/#723/#724: **3 runs each, every one** `startup_failure`. Check `gh api "repos/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/actions/runs?head_sha=<sha>"` instead. (The previous note here said "since 2026-07-19", which predates this outage.)

title: [Decision] Erasure: multi-step to trigger, but irreversible + complete once executed — confirm no recoverable off-chain link survives (incl. backups)
description:
Decision/confirmation for **Stuart** (split out of [KS-234](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-234/document-the-gdpr-art-17-erasure-vs-on-chain-immutability-position)). This is the foundation of the whole GDPR Art.17 position, so it needs an explicit sign-off.

## Requirement (Kam)

Erasing a data subject should take **multiple deliberate steps** (guard against accidental deletion), but **once executed it must be gone for good — irreversible and complete.**

## Why it's the crux

Our Art.17 position is "anonymisation by destruction": the permanent on-chain record (a hash + opaque tokens) becomes anonymous because the orphaned token **marries to nothing recoverable by anyone**. That only holds if **every** off-chain link is genuinely destroyed — not just the live DB row, but the M365 source documents, KYC images, search indexes, logs, the PII vault (`vault_entries`), and crucially **immutable backups** (you cannot delete a row from a 7-year immutable backup).

## The mechanism that makes "gone for good" true even in backups

**Crypto-shredding.** All PII is AES-256-GCM encrypted (per-tenant DEKs already exist). On erasure, **destroy the key** → the ciphertext sitting in backups becomes permanently unrecoverable. Today `gdprService.executeErasure` does row anonymise/soft-delete + a `USER_ERASED` fan-out, but does **not** destroy encryption keys — so a backup may still hold recoverable ciphertext. Closing that is what turns "deleted from the live DB" into "gone for good everywhere."

## For Stuart to confirm / decide

1. **Multi-step trigger** — e.g. request → admin approval → typed confirmation. Confirm the controls/UX (no one-click irreversible deletes).
2. **"Gone for good" = key-destruction (crypto-shred) on erasure**, not just row-delete. Confirm we adopt this as the guarantee.
3. **Full-surface coverage** — confirm the destruction reaches every off-chain place a recoverable link could survive: live DB, `vault_entries`, M365 source docs, KYC images, search indexes, application logs, **backups** (via key-destruction). Enumerate + confirm none retains a recoverable link. Anything that does → file as an implementation gap.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Erasure model confirmed: multi-step trigger + irreversible + crypto-shred + full off-chain surface coverage.
- [ ] Residual-link gaps (if any) filed as implementation tickets.

Related: [KS-234](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-234/document-the-gdpr-art-17-erasure-vs-on-chain-immutability-position) (DPIA note), tracker [KS-229](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-229/tracker-2026-06-10-platform-assurance-review-gap-analysis-remediation).

title: [Tracker] 2026-06-10 platform assurance review — gap-analysis + remediation
description:
Umbrella tracker for the 2026-06-10 assurance review (SDLC/supply-chain, OWASP, SOC 2 Type II / ISO 27001, GDPR/privacy) + full e2e across local/dev/demo. Modelled on [KS-169](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-169/tracker-2026-05-29-security-review-findings-remediation)/[KS-79](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-79/tracker-2026-05-14-audit-follow-ups-security-review-test-infra-rot). Full write-up: `Notes (MASTER)/Secuura/platform-k-assurance-gap-analysis-2026-06-10.md`.

## Headline

App-layer security is strong (argon2id+HIBP, AES-256-GCM field encryption w/ AAD, trust-header stripping, parameterised SQL, RS256 migration, CSRF). **No data-subject PII on-chain** (hashes+IDs+org-name only, with an active `@`-in-issuerName guard). Material risk clusters: a live IDOR, inert tenant RLS, CI security gates not on PR, no data-tier resilience, GDPR program architecture-ready not operational.

## E2E (all envs)

* **Local** Tier 1 API: 113 pass (2 "fails" both non-defects — 429 limiter artifact + local single-tenant `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=false` artifact); Tier 2 smoke: 35 pass; Tier 3: see thread.
* **Dev**: live-runner dispatched (run `12a05762…`) — tenant isolation is the real test here (MT on).
* **Demo (prod)**: read-only health/verify only — healthy.
* Test-infra: tenant-isolation specs should skip when `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=false`; e2e-v2 tier1 hits the login limiter (cf [KS-191](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-191/schemathesis-gate-rank-2-disable-login-limiter-in-cilocal-to-stop)).

## Findings

### 🔴 Urgent

* [KS-228](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-228/urgent-idor-gdpr-exportconsentdsr-routes-lack-ownership-check-any) — IDOR on GDPR export/consent/DSR routes (any authed user reads any user's PII). *Fixed.*
  * [KS-258](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-258/testschemathesis-add-gdpr-idor-ownership-guard-regression-tests-ks-228) — Schemathesis regression test suite for [KS-228](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-228/urgent-idor-gdpr-exportconsentdsr-routes-lack-ownership-check-any) fix. Closes `idor_rbac: coverage: PARTIAL` noted in `schemathesis_tests.yaml`. *Backlog.*

### 🟠 High — new tickets

* **CI security gates not enforced on PR** — [KS-105](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-105/ks-49-phase-01-ci-orchestrator-typescript-aggregator-canonical-finding) contract gate + Trivy/Semgrep/Gitleaks/SCA(npm-audit) are `workflow_dispatch`-only. → see linked ticket.
* **Dependabot inactive** — config at dead `Blockchain/Dev/.github/` path, none at repo root. → linked.
* **No DB HA / geo-redundant backups** — HA disabled, 7-day retention, single region/pgbouncer. → linked.
* **No tested DB restore / DR runbook.** → linked.
* **Document the GDPR Art. 17 erasure-vs-on-chain-immutability position** (DPIA note). → linked.

### 🟠 High — already tracked

* RLS fail-open / per-tenant-DB isolation — [KS-160](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-160/tenant-rls-fail-open-when-appcurrent-tenant-id-is-unset-migration) ([KS-172](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-172/ks-160-step-1-inventory-tenant-scoped-vs-cross-tenant-query-paths-rls)/173/174).
* JWT HS256→RS256 cutover — [KS-167](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-167/jwt-symmetric-asymmetric-signing-for-production-rs256eddsa-key-vault) ([KS-183](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-183/jwt-asym-step-e-verifiers-verify-rs256-via-public-key-gateway)/184).

### 🟡 Medium (promote to tickets as picked up)

* Per-route rate limiters use in-memory store (per-replica) → ×replica-count (extends [KS-170](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-170/enforceclientratelimit-runs-in-memory-per-replica-wire-the-redis)).
* Audit log: login `user_id` null + reads unaudited + not tamper-resistant (no hash-chain/WORM).
* Log Analytics retention 30d → raise to ≥90d/1yr (SOC2 window / ISO).
* MFA not mandatory for admin/privileged roles.
* Two divergent MFA-enable flows; `users.ts:707` persists secret pre-verification (cf [KS-158](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-158/mfa-totp-secrets-stored-plaintext-in-mfa-pending-setups-and-likely-in)/171).
* App ships no CSP (relies entirely on nginx) — add gateway-level fallback.
* `requireScope()` is a no-op for human users — no central deny-by-default for function-level authz.
* Cookie consent banner not wired to server-side consent API + bundled/implied consent (GDPR Art. 7).
* No KYC document-image retention policy (Art. 5(1)(e)).
* No Article 30 ROPA / sub-processor register; `Secuura-Compliance-Report.md` overstates posture (do not show customers as-is).
* Breach response not operationalised (no IR runbook / 72h trigger).
* Verify PII keys are Key-Vault-sourced in demo/prod (Art. 32).
* Silent migration-failure handling (log-and-skip → drift).
* Dead duplicate workflow tree `Blockchain/Dev/.github/`; no [SECURITY.md/disclosure/patch-SLA](<http://SECURITY.md/disclosure/patch-SLA>); no CODEOWNERS; base images not digest-pinned + version drift.

### 🟢 Low

* argon2→bcrypt silent fallback (no prod hard-fail); webhook SSRF allowlist unverified; CSRF fails-open on missing Origin (non-prod, documented); strip unused `metadata.ownerId` from anchoring schema; document issuer-org-name-on-chain decision; fix stale `encryptedField.ts` header (says not-live, is live); aggregate auth fail-open on Redis outage.

## Note

`Secuura-Compliance-Report.md` self-certifies "Compliant" vs GDPR/HIPAA/PCI-DSS/SOC2 while unreviewed — flag for downgrade to "design-intent" before any customer/auditor sees it.
